children.translated_text: Now then, we shall expound the chapter on the desire for long life.
Thus, indeed, spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.
Desiring long life, <s>Bharadvāja</s> approached
<s>Indra</s>, lord of the immortals, knowing him to be powerful in austerity and a refuge.
For, just as it had been taught by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s> first received <s>āyurveda</s> (the science of life) in its entirety,

children.text: jagrāha nikhilenādāv aśvinau tu punas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then the two <s>Aśvins</s> received it after him.
From the two <s>Aśvins</s>, the blessed <s>Śakra</s> obtained it complete;
and, instructed by the seers, <s>Bharadvāja</s> therefore approached <s>Śakra</s>.
When diseases, becoming obstacles, arose among embodied beings,
among those whose lives were devoted to austerity, fasting, study, celibacy, and vows,
then the great seers, placing compassion for beings foremost,
assembled on the auspicious side of <s>Himavat</s>.
<s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Jamadagni</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, and <s>Bhṛgu</s>,
<s>Ātreya</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, and <s>Asita</s>,
<s>Agastya</s> and <s>Vāmadeva</s>, and <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> and <s>Āśvalāyana</s>,
<s>Pārikṣi</s>, the mendicant <s>Ātreya</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, and <s>Kapiñjala</s>,
<s>Viśvāmitra</s> and <s>Aśmarathya</s>, <s>Bhārgava</s>, <s>Cyavana</s>, and <s>Abhijit</s>,
<s>Gārgya</s>, <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, <s>Vārkṣi</s>, <s>Devala</s>, and <s>Gālava</s>,
<s>Sāṃkṛtya</s>, <s>Baijavāpi</s>, <s>Kuśika</s>, and <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>,
<s>Baḍiśa</s> and <s>Śaraloman</s>, and both <s>Kāpya</s> and <s>Kātyāyana</s>,
<s>Kāṅkāyana</s>, <s>Kaikaśeya</s>, <s>Dhaumya</s>, and <s>Mārīca Kāśyapa</s>,
<s>Śarkarākṣa</s>, <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, <s>Lokākṣa</s>, and <s>Paiṅgi</s> as well,
<s>Śaunaka</s>, <s>Śākuneya</s>, <s>Maitreya</s>, and <s>Maimatāyani</s>,
the <s>Vaikhānasas</s>, the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, and likewise other great seers,
treasuries of knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> and of self-restraint and discipline,
shining with the brilliance of austerity like sacrificial fires being kindled.
Seated comfortably there, those holy ones held this discussion:
Health is the highest root of <s>dharma</s> (right order), <s>artha</s> (prosperity), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).
Diseases are the destroyers of that, and of excellence and life itself;
this great obstacle has arisen among human beings.
What might be the means of pacifying them? Having said this, they entered meditation.
Then, with the eye of meditation, they saw <s>Śakra</s> as their refuge.
The lord of the immortals will tell the means of pacification as it truly is;
who will go to the abode of the thousand-eyed one to ask <s>Śacīpati</s>?
'Let me be appointed to this matter here' was the first statement
that <s>Bharadvāja</s> spoke; therefore he was appointed by the seers.
He went to the abode of <s>Śakra</s>, who was in the midst of hosts of divine seers,
and saw the slayer of <s>Bala</s>, blazing like fire.
Approaching him and greeting the lord of the gods with blessings of victory,
the wise one, out of humility, spoke the excellent words of the seers:
Diseases have arisen, bringing fear to all living beings;
therefore tell me the means of pacification as it truly is, lord of the immortals.
To him the blessed <s>Śatakratu</s> proclaimed <s>āyurveda</s> (the science of life),
knowing the supreme seer's vast understanding, in few words:
knowledge of causes, signs, and remedies, directed toward the healthy and the ill,

children.text: trisūtraṃ śāśvataṃ puṇyaṃ bubudhe yaṃ pitāmahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the eternal, holy threefold teaching which the grandsire had understood.
That very wise sage, his mind fixed on it, understood in due form
the whole boundless <s>āyurveda</s> (science of life), with its three branches, in a short time.
Through it <s>Bharadvāja</s> obtained immeasurable life joined with happiness,
and he proclaimed it to the seers without addition and without omission.
The seers received from <s>Bharadvāja</s> that teaching beneficial to creatures,
the <s>veda</s> that increases life, wishing to make life long.
Those great seers saw, as it truly is, with the eye of knowledge,

children.text: sāmānyaṃ ca viśeṣaṃ ca guṇān dravyāṇi karma ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>sāmānya</s> (generality), <s>viśeṣa</s> (particularity), qualities, substances, and action,
and inherence; knowing that, they followed the procedure stated in the treatise,
and obtained supreme well-being and life that was not transient.
Then <s>Punarvasu</s>, intent on friendliness, gave the holy <s>āyurveda</s> (science of life)
to six disciples, out of compassion for all beings.
<s>Agniveśa</s>, <s>Bhela</s>, <s>Jatūkarṇa</s>, <s>Parāśara</s>,
<s>Hārīta</s>, and <s>Kṣārapāṇi</s> received that sage's teaching.
In that matter there was a distinction in understanding, not a difference in the sage's instruction,
because <s>Agniveśa</s> became the first author of the treatise.

children.text: atha bhelādayaś cakruḥ svaṃ svaṃ tantraṃ kṛtāni ca
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bhela</s> and the others made their own respective treatises, and when they had been composed,
those wise men recited them to <s>Ātreya</s> together with the assembly of seers.
Hearing the arrangement of the topics into aphoristic form by those of holy deeds,
the seers, delighted, approved them, saying, 'It has been properly arranged in aphorisms.'
All of them praised those seekers of the welfare of all beings,
and together they cried aloud, 'Good! This is compassion for beings.'

children.text: taṃ puṇyaṃ śuśruvuḥ śabdaṃ divi devarṣayaḥ sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: The divine seers standing in heaven heard that holy sound,
and, together with the immortals, rejoiced greatly on hearing the words of the supreme seers.

children.text: aho sādhviti nirghoṣo lokāṃs trīn anvavādayat
children.translated_text: The cry, 'Ah, good!' echoed through the three worlds,
deep and resonant in the sky, uttered by beings out of joy.

children.text: śivo vāyur vavau sarvā bhābhir unmīlitā diśaḥ
children.translated_text: An auspicious wind blew; all the directions opened with radiance;
and divine showers of flowers, moist with water, fell down.
Then the deities of knowledge entered <s>Agniveśa</s> and the others:

children.text: buddhiḥ siddhiḥ smṛtir medhā dhṛtiḥ kīrtiḥ kṣamādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: understanding, accomplishment, memory, intelligence, firmness, fame, patience, and the rest.
And those treatises of theirs, approved by the supreme seers,
They obtained a foundation on earth for the welfare of the multitude of beings.

children.text: hitāhitaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkham āyus tasya hitāhitam
children.translated_text: Wholesome and unwholesome, happiness and suffering, life, and what is wholesome and unwholesome for that life,

children.text: mānaṃ ca tacca yatroktam āyurvedaḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and its measure: that in which this is taught is called <s>āyurveda</s>.
The conjunction of body, senses, mind, and self, which sustains, is life;

children.text: nityagaś cānubandhaś ca paryāyair āyur ucyate ||
children.translated_text: by synonyms it is called <s>āyus</s>, the enduring, the living state, the ever-moving, and the continuing connection.
The knowledge of that life is regarded by knowers of knowledge as most meritorious,

children.text: vakṣyate yan manuṣyāṇāṃ lokayor ubhayor hitam ||
children.translated_text: for it will be explained as beneficial to human beings in both worlds.
In every case, for all entities, similarity is the cause of increase,
and difference is the cause of decrease; activity is concerned with both.
Similarity produces unity, while difference produces separateness;
for similarity means having the same purpose or nature, and difference is the opposite.
Mind, self, and body: this triad, like a tripod,
stands as the world through their conjunction; in it everything is established.
That is the person, the conscious entity, and it is remembered as the locus of that consciousness;
for its sake this knowledge has been revealed, as the subject matter of this <s>Veda</s>.
Space and the elements beginning with it, self, mind, time, and the directions are the collection of substances.
A substance endowed with senses is conscious; one without senses is unconscious.
The qualities are said to be those beginning with heaviness, along with their objects, cognition and those ending with effort, and those beginning with superiority;
action beginning with effort is called activity.
Inherence is understood as the inseparable relation of earth and the other substances with their qualities;

children.text: sa nityo yatra hi dravyaṃ na tatrāniyato guṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is permanent, for where there is a substance, there a quality is not indeterminate or stray.
That in which actions and qualities are based, and which is an inherent cause,

children.text: taddravyaṃ samavāyī tu niśceṣṭaḥ kāraṇaṃ guṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is substance; but an inherent, inactive cause is quality.

children.text: saṃyoge ca vibhāge ca kāraṇaṃ dravyamāśritam
children.translated_text: What depends on substance and is the cause of conjunction and separation
is action, the operation of what is to be done; action depends on nothing else.
Thus cause and effect have been stated; here equilibrium of the bodily constituents is now declared.
The operation that brings about equilibrium of the constituents is said to be the purpose of this treatise.

children.text: kālabuddhīndriyārthānāṃ yogo mithyā na cāti ca
children.translated_text: Wrong use, non-use, and excessive use of time, intellect, and sense objects
are the threefold aggregate of causes for diseases that rest on the two supports.
The body and what is called mind are regarded as the seats of diseases,

children.text: tathā sukhānāṃ yogastu sukhānāṃ kāraṇaṃ samaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also of pleasures; balanced conjunction is the cause of pleasures.
The self, however, is changeless and supreme; through mind, elements, qualities, and senses,

children.text: caitanye kāraṇaṃ nityo draṣṭā paśyati hi kriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as the eternal cause of consciousness and as the seer, it observes actions.
Wind, bile, and phlegm are said to be the aggregate of bodily doṣas;

children.text: mānasaḥ punaruddiṣṭo rajaśca tama eva ca ||
children.translated_text: the mental aggregate, again, is stated to be only passion and darkness.
The former is pacified by medicines, through therapies based on divine and rational means;
the mental one is pacified by knowledge, discriminative understanding, firmness, memory, and concentration.

children.text: rūkṣaḥ śīto laghuḥ sūkṣmaścalo 'tha viśadaḥ kharaḥ
children.translated_text: Dry, cold, light, subtle, mobile, clear, and rough:
<s>māruta</s>, the wind doṣa, is pacified by substances with opposite qualities.

children.text: sasnehamuṣṇaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca dravamamlaṃ saraṃ kaṭu
children.translated_text: Slightly oily, hot, sharp, liquid, sour, flowing, and pungent:
bile is quickly pacified by substances with opposite qualities.
Heavy, cold, soft, oily, sweet, stable, and slimy:
the qualities of phlegm are pacified by opposite qualities.
By medicines possessing opposite qualities, prepared with regard to place, quantity, and time,
disorders that are considered curable are made to cease.
No means of treatment is prescribed for incurable diseases;
therefore, next the qualities and actions will be explained according to each substance.
Taste is the object of the tongue; its substances are water and earth,

children.text: nirvṛttau ca viśeṣe ca pratyayāḥ khādayastrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: while the three beginning with space are conditions in its production and in its differentiation.
Sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter,
and astringent: this is remembered as the sixfold collection of tastes.
Sweet, sour, and salty tastes overcome wind; astringent, sweet, and bitter tastes overcome bile;
astringent, pungent, and bitter tastes overcome phlegm.
Pungent, sour, and salty tastes aggravate bile; sweet, sour, and salty tastes aggravate phlegm;
and pungent, bitter, and astringent tastes aggravate wind.
Some substance pacifies doṣas, some corrupts the bodily constituents,
and some is regarded as useful in the regimen of health; substance is said to be threefold.
That, again, is declared to be of three kinds: animal, plant-derived, and earthy.
Honeys, products of the cow, bile, fat, marrow, blood, and flesh,
feces, urine, skin, semen, bone, sinew, horn, nails, and hooves,
as well as head-hair, body-hair, and <s>rocanā</s>, are used from animals.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ samalāḥ pañca lohāḥ sasikatāḥ sudhā
children.translated_text: Gold, the five metals together with their impurities, sands, and lime,
<s>manaḥśilā</s>, <s>ala</s>, gems, salt, red ochre, and collyrium are earthy medicines.
The earthy medicine has been stated; the plant-derived is of four kinds:
<s>vanaspati</s>, creeper, <s>vānaspatya</s>, and herb.
A <s>vanaspati</s> is known by fruits; a <s>vānaspatya</s> by flowers and also by fruits;
herbs end with the ripening of their fruit, and creepers are remembered as spreading by shoots or tendrils.
Roots, bark, heartwood, exudations, stalks, fresh juices, and shoots,

children.text: kṣārāḥ kṣīraṃ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ bhasma tailāni kaṇṭakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: alkalis, latex, fruit, flowers, ash, oils, and thorns,
leaves, sprouts, tubers, and new growths are the plant-derived group.
Fifteen root-bearing plants and twenty fruit-bearing plants are remembered.
There are also the four great fats, and exactly five salts,
eight urines are enumerated, and likewise eight milks.
And six trees for the purpose of purification have been pointed out by <s>Punarvasu</s>;

children.text: ya etān vetti saṃyoktuṃ vikāreṣu sa vedavit ||
children.translated_text: whoever knows how to combine these in disorders is a knower of the <s>Veda</s>.
<s>Hastidantī</s>, <s>Haimavatī</s>, <s>Śyāmā</s>, <s>Trivṛt</s>, and <s>Adhoguḍā</s>.
Saptalā, that which is called śvetanāmā, pratyakśreṇī, and also gavākṣī;

children.text: jyotiṣmatī ca bimbī ca śaṇapuṣpī viṣāṇikā
children.translated_text: jyotiṣmatī, bimbī, śaṇapuṣpī, and viṣāṇikā;

children.text: ajagandhā dravantī ca kṣīriṇī cātra ṣoḍaśī ||
children.translated_text: ajagandhā, dravantī, and kṣīriṇī: here these make the sixteenth.

children.text: śaṇapuṣpī ca bimbī ca chardane haimavatyapi
children.translated_text: Śaṇapuṣpī, bimbī, and haimavatī too are to be used for <s>chardana</s> (emesis);
and śvetā and jyotiṣmatī are to be employed for purgation of the head.
The eleven that remain are to be employed for <s>virecana</s> (purgation).
Thus the root-drugs have been stated by name and action; now hear the fruit-drugs.
Śaṅkhinī, then viḍaṅga, trapuṣa, and madana;
dhāmārgava, then ikṣvāku, jīmūta, and kṛtavedhana;

children.text: ānūpaṃ sthalajaṃ caiva klītakaṃ dvividhaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: ānūpa and sthalaja; klītaka is remembered as being of two kinds.
Prakīryā and udakīryā, pratyakpuṣpā, likewise abhayā;
antaḥkoṭarapuṣpī, and the autumnal fruit of hastiparṇī;
and the fruit of kampillaka and āragvadha, and that of kuṭaja;
dhāmārgava, then ikṣvāku, jīmūta, and kṛtavedhana.
Madana and kuṭaja, trapuṣa, and hastiparṇinī:
these are to be used both in <s>vamana</s> (emesis) and in <s>āsthāpana</s> (decoction enemas).
Pratyakpuṣpā is prescribed for nasal administration and for inducing vomiting.
The ten that remain are said to be for <s>virecana</s> (purgation).
The fruits, stated by their names and actions, are nineteen less one.
Ghee, oil, fat, and marrow: <s>sneha</s> (unctuous substance) is taught as fourfold.
It is for drinking, anointing, and enema, and also for nasal therapy, according to proper application.
The oleating substances promote unction, vitality, complexion, strength, and increase of bodily substance.
These prescribed <s>sneha</s>s remove <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>.
Sauvarcala, saindhava, viḍa, and audbhida;
together with sea-salt, these are the five salts.
They are unctuous, hot, sharp, and among the very best digestives.
They are used for application, and likewise in the procedure of oleation and fomentation;
in therapies for the lower and upper channels, in <s>nirūha</s> and <s>anuvāsana</s> enemas;
in anointing, for food, and for purgation of the head;
in surgical procedures, for wicks, and in collyrium and rubbing treatments.
They are prescribed for indigestion, abdominal distension from wind, <s>gulma</s>, colic, and abdominal disease.
The salts have been stated above; now learn from me the eight urines,
the principal ones that are taught in their entirety in the instruction of <s>Ātreya</s>.
Sheep's urine, goat's urine, cow's urine, and that of a buffalo;
elephant's urine, then that of a camel, a horse, and a donkey.
Urine is hot, sharp, not dry, pungent, and accompanied by saltiness.
Urine is suitable for rubbing treatments, and suitable in applications too;
urine is suitable in <s>āsthāpana</s> enemas, and suitable also in purgation;
it is also suitable in fomentations, in abdominal distension, and in antidotal preparations;
in abdominal diseases, piles, <s>gulma</s>, skin disease, and <s>kilāsa</s> (leucoderma);
it is suitable in poultices and likewise in sprinkling treatments.
It is taught to stimulate digestion, counteract poison, and destroy worms.
For those afflicted by <s>pāṇḍu</s> disease, it is said to be an excellent source of relief.
When drunk it pacifies <s>śleṣman</s> (kapha) and sets <s>māruta</s> (vāta) in its proper downward course;
it draws <s>pitta</s> to the lower region: this is the summary of its qualities.
I have stated this generally; it will be explained individually.

children.text: avimūtraṃ satiktaṃ syāt snigdhaṃ pittāvirodhi ca
children.translated_text: Sheep's urine is somewhat bitter, unctuous, and not antagonistic to <s>pitta</s>.
Goat's urine is astringent and sweet, wholesome, and destroys the <s>doṣa</s>s.
Cow's urine is somewhat sweet, destroys <s>doṣa</s>s, worms, and skin disease;

children.text: kaṇḍūṃ ca śamayet pītaṃ samyagdoṣodare hitam ||
children.translated_text: when drunk properly it also calms itching and is beneficial in abdominal disease caused by <s>doṣa</s>s.
Buffalo urine, containing alkali, is fluid and destroys piles, swelling, and abdominal disease.

children.text: hāstikaṃ lavaṇaṃ mūtraṃ hitaṃ tu krimikuṣṭhinām ||
children.translated_text: Elephant urine is salty and beneficial for those with worms and skin disease.
It is commended for constipation of feces and urine, poison, phlegmatic disorders, and piles.
Camel urine is called somewhat bitter, destroying dyspnea, cough, and piles.
Horse urine is bitter and pungent, removing skin disease, wounds, and poison.
Donkey urine destroys epilepsy, insanity, and afflictions by seizing spirits.
Thus the urines have been stated here according to their respective capacities and uses.

children.text: ataḥ kṣīrāṇi vakṣyante karma caiṣāṃ guṇāśca ye ||
children.translated_text: Next the milks will be described, along with their actions and qualities.
Sheep's milk, goat's milk, cow's milk, and that of a buffalo;
then that of she-camels, female elephants, mares, and women.

children.text: prāyaśo madhuraṃ snigdhaṃ śītaṃ stanyaṃ payo matam
children.translated_text: Milk, including breast milk, is generally held to be sweet, unctuous, and cooling.

children.text: prīṇanaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ vṛṣyaṃ medhyaṃ balyaṃ manaskaram ||
children.translated_text: It satisfies, nourishes, is aphrodisiac, intellect-promoting, strengthening, and beneficial to the mind.
It sustains life, removes fatigue, and dispels dyspnea and cough.

children.text: hanti śoṇitapittaṃ ca sandhānaṃ vihatasya ca ||
children.translated_text: It also checks hemorrhagic <s>pitta</s> and brings union to what has been broken.
It is wholesome for all living beings, pacifying and also cleansing.

children.text: tṛṣṇāghnaṃ dīpanīyaṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ kṣīṇakṣateṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: It removes thirst, stimulates digestion, and is best in wasting and injury.
It is especially wholesome in <s>pāṇḍu</s> disease, acid <s>pitta</s>, consumption, <s>gulma</s>, abdominal disease,

children.text: atīsāre jvare dāhe śvayathau ca viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: diarrhea, fever, burning, and swelling;
in disorders of the womb and semen, and when urine is scanty;
when feces are hard, it is wholesome for those afflicted by disorders of <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
Milk is used everywhere in nasal therapy, applications, immersions, emesis, and <s>āsthāpana</s> enemas;

children.text: virecane snehane ca payaḥ sarvatra yujyate ||
children.translated_text: and in purgation and oleation as well.
The qualities of each milk separately and in due order
I shall again state completely in the chapter on food and drink and related matters.
Now there are three other trees, distinct because of their fruits and roots;
they are snuhī, arka, and aśmantaka; their separate actions are as follows.
One should know aśmantaka for emesis, and the milk-latex of snuhī for purgation.
The latex of arka should be understood as useful for emesis together with purgation.
They speak of these three further trees, whose barks are beneficial:

children.text: pūtīkaḥ kṛṣṇagandhā ca tilvakaśca tathā taruḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pūtīka</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇagandhā</s>, and likewise the tree <s>Tilvaka</s>.
<s>Pūtīka</s> and <s>Tilvaka</s> should be employed for purgation,
while <s>Kṛṣṇagandhā</s> is taught for erysipelas, swellings, and piles,
and also for ringworm, abscesses, glandular swellings, skin diseases, and <s>alajī</s>.
The discerning person should know these six trees as purifying agents.
Thus have been stated the fruit-bearing and root-bearing plants, the fats, and the salts,

children.text: mūtraṃ kṣīrāṇi vṛkṣāśca ṣaḍ ye diṣṭapayastvacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the urines, milks, and the six trees whose milky sap and barks were prescribed.
Goat-herds know medicinal plants in the forest by name and form,
as do shepherds, cowherds, and other forest-dwellers.
Yet by knowledge of name alone, or again by knowledge of form alone,
no one can attain supreme mastery of medicinal plants.
Rather, one who knows their application, even if not acquainted with their appearance, is said to know their reality;
how much more the physician who knows medicinal plants in every respect.
But one who knows their application as suited to place and time,

children.text: puruṣaṃ puruṣaṃ vīkṣya sa jñeyo bhiṣaguttamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and who observes each patient individually, should be known as the best physician.
As with poison, as with a weapon, as with fire, and as with a thunderbolt,
so too is medicine when it is not understood; when understood, it is like nectar.
For a medicine not known in the three respects of name, form, and qualities,
and even when known, wrongly applied, becomes a cause of harm.
Through proper application even sharp poison may become an excellent medicine,

children.text: bheṣajaṃ cāpi duryuktaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ saṃpadyate viṣam ||
children.translated_text: and a medicine wrongly applied may become a sharp poison.
Therefore no medicine should be accepted from a physician who is outside proper reasoning,
by a wise person who desires life and health.
<s>Vāsava</s>'s thunderbolt, when it falls on the head, may leave something remaining,
but a medicine prescribed by an ignorant man leaves no patient remaining.
To a suffering, bedridden, trusting patient,
one who, considering himself wise, gives medicine without knowing it,
is a wicked, evil-minded man who has abandoned <s>dharma</s>, and has become death itself;
a person would fall into hell even by conversing with him.
Better to drink the poison of a venomous snake, or molten copper,
or to swallow iron balls heated in an intense fire,
than to take, from one wearing the guise of the learned,

children.text: gṛhītamannaṃ pānaṃ vā vittaṃ vā rogapīḍitāt ||
children.translated_text: food, drink, or wealth from a disease-afflicted person who has come for refuge.
Therefore an intelligent man who wishes to become a physician should make supreme effort
toward the excellence of his own qualities, so that he may be a giver of life to people.
That alone is proper medicine which is fit to bring about health,

children.text: sa caiva bhiṣajāṃ śreṣṭho rogebhyo yaḥ pramocayet ||
children.translated_text: and he alone is the best of physicians who frees people from diseases.
Success proclaims the correct application of all actions,
and success, together with all the virtues, proclaims the best physician.
Here are the summary verses:
The transmission of <s>Āyurveda</s>, the cause of that transmission, its promulgation,
the authorization for composing the sūtra, and the determination of <s>Āyurveda</s>;
the complete cause, the effect, and the purpose of <s>Āyurveda</s>,
and, in brief, the causes, the doṣas, and medicine;
the tastes together with their causal substances, the threefold grouping of substances,
the root-bearing and fruit-bearing plants, the fats, and the salts;

children.text: mūtraṃ kṣīrāṇi vṛkṣāśca ṣaḍ ye kṣīratvagāśrayāḥ
children.translated_text: the urines, the milks, and the six trees characterized by milky sap and bark,
the actions of all these, and the merits and faults of proper and improper application;

children.text: vaidyāpavādo yatrasthāḥ sarve ca bhiṣajāṃ guṇāḥ
children.translated_text: the denunciation of bad physicians, and all the qualities on which physicians depend:;
all this was explained by the great seer in the preceding chapter.

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte sūtrasthāne dīrghañjīvitīyo nāma prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s> and redacted by <s>Caraka</s>, in the Sūtrasthāna, the first chapter, named <s>Dīrghañjīvitīya</s>, is completed.
Now then we shall expound the chapter called <s>Apāmārgataṇḍulīya</s>.
Thus spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>.
The seeds of <s>Apāmārga</s>, <s>Pippalī</s>, and <s>Marica</s>,
<s>Viḍaṅga</s>, then <s>Śigru</s>, mustard seeds, and <s>Tumburu</s>,
<s>Ajājī</s> and <s>Ajagandhā</s>, <s>Pīlu</s>, <s>Elā</s>, and <s>Hareṇukā</s>,
<s>Pṛthvīkā</s>, <s>Surasā</s>, <s>Śvetā</s>, <s>Kuṭheraka</s>, and <s>Phaṇijjhaka</s>,
<s>Śirīṣa</s> seed, garlic, the two kinds of <s>Haridrā</s>, and the two salts,
<s>Jyotiṣmatī</s> and <s>Nāgara</s> should be administered for evacuation of the head.
They are used in heaviness of the head, headache, chronic nasal catarrh, and hemicrania,
in worm disease, epilepsy, loss of smell, and stupefying disorders.
<s>Madana</s>, <s>Madhuka</s>, <s>Nimba</s>, <s>Jīmūta</s>, and <s>Kṛtavedhana</s>,
<s>Pippalī</s>, <s>Kuṭaja</s>, <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, <s>Elā</s>, and <s>Dhāmārgava</s>,
when a disease involving <s>Śleṣman</s> and <s>Pitta</s> has arisen and is located in the stomach,
the physician should employ for emesis, without injuring the body.

children.text: trivṛtāṃ triphalāṃ dantīṃ nīlinīṃ saptalāṃ vacām
children.translated_text: <s>Trivṛt</s>, <s>Triphalā</s>, <s>Dantī</s>, <s>Nīlinī</s>, <s>Saptalā</s>, and <s>Vacā</s>,
<s>Kampillaka</s>, <s>Gavākṣī</s>, <s>Kṣīriṇī</s>, and <s>Udakīryakā</s>,
<s>Pīlu</s>, <s>Āragvadha</s>, grapes, <s>Dravantī</s>, and <s>Nicula</s>,
should be employed for purgation when the doṣa has gone to the large intestine.

children.text: pāṭalāṃ cāgnimanthaṃ ca bilvaṃ śyonākameva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Pāṭalā</s>, <s>Agnimantha</s>, <s>Bilva</s>, and <s>Śyonāka</s>,
<s>Kāśmarya</s>, <s>Śālaparṇī</s>, <s>Pṛśniparṇī</s>, and <s>Nidigdhikā</s>,
<s>Balā</s>, <s>Śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, castor, together with <s>Punarnavā</s>,

children.text: yavān kulatthān kolāni guḍūcīṃ madanāni ca ||
children.translated_text: barley, horse gram, jujubes, <s>Guḍūcī</s>, and <s>Madana</s>,

children.text: palāśaṃ kattṛṇaṃ caiva snehāṃśca lavaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: <s>Palāśa</s>, <s>Kattṛṇa</s>, and also fats and salts,
one should use in evacuative enemas for upward movement of wind and constipation.
From this very group of medicines one should also prepare an unctuous retention enema,
which counteracts <s>Māruta</s>; thus the collection relating to pañcakarma has been stated.
For those whose <s>doṣas</s> have presented themselves, after applying oleation and sudation,
one should perform the five <s>pañcakarma</s> procedures, considering the proper dose and time.
Correct procedure depends on dose and time; success is established in correct procedure.
One who knows correct procedure always stands above those who merely know the substances.
From here onward I shall declare medicated <s>yavāgū</s>s made with various drugs,
for the removal of the various disorders that are curable by them.
A <s>yavāgū</s> prepared with <s>pippalī</s>, <s>pippalīmūla</s>, <s>cavya</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>nāgara</s>
is stimulating to digestion and destroys colic pain.
Prepared with <s>dadhittha</s>, <s>bilva</s>, <s>cāṅgerī</s>, buttermilk, and pomegranate,
and, when wind is involved, with <s>pañcamūla</s>, the drinkable gruel is digestive and constipating.
Cooked with <s>śālaparṇī</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>bilva</s>, and <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>,
and soured with pomegranate, the drinkable gruel is beneficial for those with diarrhea caused by pitta and phlegm.
In goat's milk mixed with half water, with <s>hrīvera</s>, <s>utpala</s>, and <s>nāgara</s>,
a drinkable gruel cooked also with <s>pṛśniparṇī</s> removes bloody diarrhea.

children.text: dadyāt sātiviṣāṃ peyāṃ sāme sāmlāṃ sanāgarām
children.translated_text: In a condition with <s>āma</s>, one should give a drinkable gruel containing <s>ativiṣā</s>, made sour and with <s>nāgara</s>;
with <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s> and <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>, and with <s>phāṇita</s>, it is given for dysuria.
With <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>pippalīmūla</s>, <s>śigru</s>, and also black pepper,
a <s>yavāgū</s> cooked in buttermilk, with <s>suvarcikā</s>, destroys worms.
With raisins, <s>sārivā</s>, parched grain, <s>pippalī</s>, honey, and <s>nāgara</s>,
and cooked with <s>somarājī</s>, it removes thirst and counteracts poison.
A <s>yavāgū</s> cooked in boar broth is regarded as nourishing,
while one made from roasted <s>gavedhukā</s> grains and mixed with honey is reducing.
One containing ghee, much sesame, and salt is oleating;
one made from <s>śyāmāka</s> grains in a decoction of <s>kuśa</s> and <s>āmalaka</s> is drying.
Cooked in <s>daśamūla</s> decoction, it removes cough, hiccup, dyspnea, and phlegm;
cooked in a mixture of fats and wine, it removes pain of the lower bowel.
Cooked with vegetables, meat, sesame, and <s>māṣa</s> beans, it drives out feces;
with the stones of jambu and mango, sour <s>dadhittha</s>, and <s>bilva</s>, it is considered astringent and checking.
With alkali, <s>citraka</s>, asafoetida, and sour <s>vetasa</s>, it is considered purgative;
with <s>abhayā</s>, <s>pippalīmūla</s>, and <s>viśva</s>, it directs wind downward.
A <s>yavāgū</s> cooked in buttermilk removes disorders caused by improper use of ghee;
for disorders caused by oil, one cooked with buttermilk and oil-cake is recommended.
Made sour with broths of bovine meat, it destroys irregular fever;
for the throat, barley gruel cooked in a mixture of fats with <s>pippalī</s> and <s>āmalaka</s> is beneficial.
Cooked in the broth of a rooster, it removes pain in the seminal passage;
prepared with equal <s>māṣa</s> and split pulse, and with ghee and milk, it is aphrodisiac.
Cooked with <s>upodikā</s> and curd, it removes intoxication;
cooked with <s>apāmārga</s> milk and iguana broth, it overcomes hunger.
On this there is a summary verse:
Thus these twenty-eight <s>yavāgū</s>s have been set forth.
And, with reference to the five <s>pañcakarma</s> procedures, a collection of medicines has been stated.
The medicine that was previously taught for the sake of knowledge of roots and fruits
has now been recited again for the sake of knowledge connected with <s>pañcakarma</s>.
A physician who is mindful, knows causes and reasoning, has mastered himself, and is skilled in decision
is fit to carry out treatment through combinations of medicines.
Now then, we shall expound the chapter called <s>Āragvadhīya</s>.
Thus spoke the Blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: āragvadhaḥ saiḍagajaḥ karañjo vāsā guḍūcī madanaṃ haridre
children.translated_text: <s>Āragvadha</s>, together with <s>eḍagaja</s>, <s>karañja</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>madana</s>, and the two <s>haridrā</s>s;

children.text: śryāhvaḥ surāhvaḥ khadiro dhavaśca nimbo viḍaṅgaṃ karavīrakatvak ||
children.translated_text: <s>śryāhva</s>, <s>surāhva</s>, <s>khadira</s>, <s>dhava</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, and bark of <s>karavīraka</s>;

children.text: granthiśca bhaurjo laśunaḥ śirīṣaḥ salomaśo guggulukṛṣṇagandhe
children.translated_text: <s>granthi</s>, birch, garlic, <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>salomaśa</s>, <s>guggulu</s>, and <s>kṛṣṇagandhā</s>;
<s>phaṇijjhaka</s>, <s>vatsaka</s>, <s>saptaparṇa</s>, <s>pīlu</s> fruits, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and shoots of <s>sumanas</s>;

children.text: vacā hareṇustrivṛtā nikumbho bhallātakaṃ gairikamañjanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: <s>vacā</s>, <s>hareṇu</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>nikumbha</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s>, red ochre, and collyrium;
<s>manaḥśilā</s> and <s>ālaka</s>, house soot, <s>elā</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, <s>musta</s>, and <s>sarja</s>;
these six formulations, prescribed in half-pala measures, are drunk with cow's bile and then pounded again.
Prepared with excellent mustard oil, these powders and pastes are to be applied by the physician.

children.text: kuṣṭhāni kṛcchrāṇi navaṃ kilāsaṃ sureśaluptaṃ kiṭibhaṃ sadadru
children.translated_text: When applied, they quickly destroy difficult skin diseases, recent <s>kilāsa</s>, <s>indralupta</s>, <s>kiṭibha</s> together with ringworm,
as well as fistula, piles, scrofulous swellings, and scabies in human beings.

children.text: kuṣṭhaṃ haridre surasaṃ paṭolaṃ nimbāśvagandhe suradāruśigrū
children.translated_text: One should make equal powders of <s>kuṣṭha</s>, the two <s>haridrā</s>s, <s>surasa</s>, <s>paṭola</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>suradāru</s>, <s>śigru</s>,

children.text: sasarṣapaṃ tumburudhānyavanyaṃ caṇḍāṃ ca cūrṇāni samāni kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: mustard, <s>tumburu</s>, <s>dhānyaka</s>, wild <s>dhānyaka</s>, and <s>caṇḍā</s>.
With these, ground in buttermilk, one should first rub the body after it has been anointed with oil.

children.text: tenāsyakaṇḍūḥ piḍakāḥ sakoṭhāḥ kuṣṭhāni śophāśca śamaṃ vrajanti ||
children.translated_text: By that, itching, pustules, wheals, skin diseases, and swellings on his body subside.
<s>Kuṣṭha</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>saṅga</s>, <s>kaṭaṅkaṭerī</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>kampillaka</s>, <s>musta</s>, and <s>lodhra</s>;
<s>saugandhika</s>, resin of <s>sarja</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>manaḥśilā</s> and <s>ālaka</s>, and bark of <s>karavīraka</s>;
these powders should be applied for dusting on the body of one whose limbs have been anointed with oil.

children.text: dadrūḥ sakaṇḍūḥ kiṭibhāni pāmā vicarcikā caiva tathaiti śāntim ||
children.translated_text: Ringworm with itching, <s>kiṭibha</s>, scabies, and eczema likewise become pacified.

children.text: manaḥśilāle maricāni tailamārkaṃ payaḥ kuṣṭhaharaḥ pradehaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Manaḥśilā</s> and <s>ālaka</s>, black pepper, oil, and the latex of <s>arka</s> form a paste that removes skin disease;

children.text: tutthaṃ viḍaṅgaṃ maricāni kuṣṭhaṃ lodhraṃ ca tadvat samanaḥśilaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: blue vitriol, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, black pepper, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and <s>lodhra</s>, similarly with <s>manaḥśilā</s>, make another such paste.

children.text: rasāñjanaṃ saprapunāḍabījaṃ yuktaṃ kapitthasya rasena lepaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rasāñjana</s> with <s>prapunāḍa</s> seed, mixed with the juice of <s>kapittha</s>, is a plaster.

children.text: karañjabījaiḍagajaṃ sakuṣṭhaṃ gomūtrapiṣṭaṃ ca paraḥ pradehaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Eḍagaja</s> with <s>karañja</s> seeds and <s>kuṣṭha</s>, ground in cow's urine, is another excellent paste.

children.text: ubhe haridre kuṭajasya bījaṃ karañjabījaṃ sumanaḥpravālān
children.translated_text: Both <s>haridrā</s>s, seed of <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>karañja</s> seed, and shoots of <s>sumanas</s>,

children.text: tvacaṃ samadhyāṃ hayamārakasya lepaṃ tilakṣārayutaṃ vidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: together with the bark and pith of <s>hayamāraka</s>, should be made into a paste with sesame alkali.

children.text: manaḥśilā tvak kuṭajāt sakuṣṭhāt salomaśaḥ saiḍagajaḥ karañjaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Manaḥśilā</s>, bark, <s>Kuṭaja</s>, with <s>Kuṣṭha</s>, <s>Salomaśa</s>, <s>Iḍagaja</s>, and <s>Karañja</s>,

children.text: granthiśca bhaurjaḥ karavīramūlaṃ cūrṇāni sādhyāni tuṣodakena ||
children.translated_text: <s>Granthi</s>, <s>Bhaurja</s>, and the root of <s>Karavīra</s>: their powders are to be prepared with husk-water.
Or else, after taking one karṣa of each, with an āḍhaka measure of the juice from burning <s>Palāśa</s>,
they prescribe this paste, thick enough to coat a ladle, as supreme for destroying <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease).

children.text: parṇāni piṣṭvā caturaṅgulasya takreṇa parṇānyatha kākamācyāḥ
children.translated_text: Having ground the leaves of <s>Caturaṅgula</s> with buttermilk, and then the leaves of <s>Kākamācī</s>,
one should rub away the skin diseases of a man whose body has been anointed with oil, also using leaves of <s>Aśvahana</s>.
<s>Kola</s>, horse gram, <s>Suradāru</s>, <s>Rāsnā</s>, black gram, flaxseed oil, and <s>Kuṣṭha</s>,
<s>Vacā</s>, <s>Śatāhvā</s>, barley flour, sour substances, and hot substances form a poultice for those afflicted by vāta disorders.
A warm poultice with meat-preparations of marsh animals and fish should remove <s>Pavana</s> (vāta);
and a poultice with the four fats, mixed with <s>Daśamūla</s> and fragrant herbs, removes <s>Anila</s> (vāta).

children.text: takreṇa yuktaṃ yavacūrṇamuṣṇaṃ sakṣāramartiṃ jaṭhare nihanyāt
children.translated_text: Warm barley flour mixed with buttermilk and alkali destroys pain in the abdomen;

children.text: kuṣṭhaṃ śatāhvāṃ savacāṃ yavānāṃ cūrṇaṃ satailāmlamuśanti vāte ||
children.translated_text: for vāta they recommend a powder of <s>Kuṣṭha</s>, <s>Śatāhvā</s>, <s>Vacā</s>, and barley, with oil and sour liquid.

children.text: ubhe śatāhve madhukaṃ madhūkaṃ balāṃ priyālaṃ ca kaśerukaṃ ca
children.translated_text: The two kinds of <s>Śatāhvā</s>, <s>Madhuka</s>, <s>Madhūka</s>, <s>Balā</s>, <s>Priyāla</s>, and <s>Kaśeruka</s>,

children.text: ghṛtaṃ vidārīṃ ca sitopalāṃ ca kuryāt pradehaṃ pavane sarakte ||
children.translated_text: together with ghee, <s>Vidārī</s>, and sugar candy, should be made into a poultice when vāta is accompanied by blood.

children.text: rāsnā guḍūcī madhukaṃ bale dve sajīvakaṃ sarṣabhakaṃ payaśca
children.translated_text: <s>Rāsnā</s>, <s>Guḍūcī</s>, <s>Madhuka</s>, the two <s>Balā</s>s, with <s>Jīvaka</s>, <s>Sarṣabhaka</s>, and milk,

children.text: ghṛtaṃ ca siddhaṃ madhuśeṣayuktaṃ raktānilārtiṃ praṇudet pradehaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and ghee cooked with these and mixed with a remainder of honey: as a poultice it drives away pain from blood and vāta.

children.text: vāte sarakte saghṛtaṃ pradeho godhūmacūrṇaṃ chagalīpayaśca
children.translated_text: When vāta is accompanied by blood, wheat flour and goat's milk with ghee are a poultice;
<s>Nata</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, and sandalwood mixed with <s>Kuṣṭha</s> and ghee are a poultice for headache.

children.text: prapauṇḍarīkaṃ suradāru kuṣṭhaṃ yaṣṭyāhvamelā kamalotpale ca
children.translated_text: <s>Prapauṇḍarīka</s>, <s>Suradāru</s>, <s>Kuṣṭha</s>, <s>Yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>Elā</s>, lotus, and water-lily,
with ghee, form a poultice for headache, as do <s>Lohairaka</s>, <s>Padmaka</s>, and <s>Coraka</s>.

children.text: rāsnā haridre naladaṃ śatāhve dve devadārūṇi sitopalā ca
children.translated_text: <s>Rāsnā</s>, the two <s>Haridrā</s>s, <s>Nalada</s>, the two <s>Śatāhvā</s>s, the two <s>Devadāru</s>s, and sugar candy,
with <s>Jīvantī</s> root, ghee, and oil, make a lukewarm application for pains in the sides.
<s>Śaivāla</s>, lotus, water-lily, <s>Vetratuṅga</s>, <s>Prapauṇḍarīka</s>, lotus-fiber, and <s>Lodhra</s>,
<s>Priyaṅgu</s>, <s>Kāleyaka</s>, and sandalwood make a cooling poultice when combined with ghee.
Sugar, <s>Latā</s>, cane, <s>Padmaka</s>, <s>Yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>Aindrī</s>, lotuses, and <s>Dūrvā</s>,
the root of <s>Yavāsa</s>, the roots of <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Kāśa</s>, and <s>Jalameraka</s> make a cooling application.

children.text: śaileyamelāguruṇī sakuṣṭhe caṇḍā nataṃ tvak suradāru rāsnā
children.translated_text: <s>Śaileya</s>, <s>Elā</s>, <s>Aguru</s>, with <s>Kuṣṭha</s>, <s>Caṇḍā</s>, <s>Nata</s>, bark, <s>Suradāru</s>, and <s>Rāsnā</s>:

children.text: śītaṃ nihanyādacirāt pradeho viṣaṃ śirīṣastu sasindhuvāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: this poultice quickly destroys coldness; but <s>Śirīṣa</s> with <s>Sindhuvāra</s> destroys poison.
A rubbing with <s>Śirīṣa</s>, <s>Lāmajjaka</s>, <s>Hema</s>, and <s>Lodhra</s> removes disorders of the skin and sweating;
a poultice of leaf, water, <s>Lodhra</s>, <s>Abhayā</s>, and sandalwood removes bad body odor.
Here is the summary verse:
Here the son of <s>Atri</s>, the perfected one praised by accomplished great seers, has stated thirty-two most effective
powders and poultices in the <s>Āragvadhīya</s> chapter, destroying various diseases, for the welfare of the world.
Now then we shall expound the chapter entitled <s>Ṣaḍvirecanaśatāśritīya</s>, 'Based on the Six Hundred Purgatives.'
Thus spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: iha khalu ṣaḍ virecanaśatāni bhavanti ṣaḍ virecanāśrayāḥ pañca kaṣāyayonayaḥ pañcavidhaṃ kaṣāyakalpanaṃ pañcāśanmahākaṣāyāḥ pañca kaṣāyaśatāni iti saṃgrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, in brief, there are six hundreds of purgatives, six supports for purgation, five sources of medicinal preparations, a fivefold preparation of decoctions, fifty great decoctions, and five hundred decoctions.

children.text: ṣaḍ virecanaśatāni iti yaduktaṃ tadiha saṃgraheṇodāhṛtya vistareṇa kalpopaniṣadi vyākhyāsyāmaḥ tatra trayastriṃśadyogaśataṃ praṇītaṃ phaleṣu ekonacatvāriṃśajjīmūtakeṣu yogāḥ pañcacatvāriṃśadikṣvākuṣu dhāmārgavaḥ ṣaṣṭidhā bhavati yogayuktaḥ kuṭajastvaṣṭādaśadhā yogameti kṛtavedhanaṃ ṣaṣṭidhā bhavati yogayuktaṃ śyāmātrivṛdyogaśataṃ praṇītaṃ daśāpare cātra bhavanti yogāḥ caturaṅgulo dvādaśadhā yogameti lodhraṃ vidhau ṣoḍaśayogayuktaṃ mahāvṛkṣo bhavati viṃśatiyogayuktaḥ ekonacatvāriṃśat saptalāśaṅkhinyoryogāḥ aṣṭacatvāriṃśaddantīdravantyoḥ iti ṣaḍvirecanaśatāni ||
children.translated_text: What was called the six hundreds of purgatives will be cited here in summary and explained in detail in the <s>Kalpopaniṣad</s>: one hundred and thirty-three formulations are taught among fruits; there are thirty-nine formulations with <s>Jīmūtaka</s>, forty-five with <s>Ikṣvāku</s>; <s>Dhāmārgava</s> becomes equipped with sixty formulations; <s>Kuṭaja</s> enters eighteen formulations; <s>Kṛtavedhana</s> becomes equipped with sixty formulations; a hundred formulations of <s>Śyāmā</s> and <s>Trivṛt</s> are taught, and ten further formulations occur here; <s>Caturaṅgula</s> enters twelve forms; <s>Lodhra</s>, in its proper method, is joined with sixteen formulations; <s>Mahāvṛkṣa</s> is joined with twenty formulations; there are thirty-nine formulations of <s>Saptalā</s> and <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>, and forty-eight of <s>Dantī</s> and <s>Dravantī</s>. These are the six hundreds of purgatives.
The six supports for purgation are milk, root, bark, leaf, flower, and fruit.

children.text: pañca kaṣāyayonaya iti madhurakaṣāyo 'mlakaṣāyaḥ kaṭukaṣāyastiktakaṣāyaḥ kaṣāyakaṣāyaśceti tantre saṃjñā ||
children.translated_text: The five sources of medicinal preparations are the sweet preparation, sour preparation, pungent preparation, bitter preparation, and astringent preparation; these are the technical names in the treatise.

children.text: pañcavidhaṃ kaṣāyakalpanamiti tadyathā svarasaḥ kalkaḥ śṛtaḥ śītaḥ phāṇṭaḥ kaṣāya iti
children.translated_text: The fivefold preparation of medicinal decoction is as follows: expressed juice, paste, boiled decoction, cold infusion, and hot infusion.
The liquid pressed out from a substance by a press is called expressed juice.

children.text: yaḥ piṇḍo rasapiṣṭānāṃ sa kalkaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: The lump made of substances ground with liquid is termed paste.
Physicians call a substance boiled over fire a boiled decoction.

children.text: dravyād āpothitāt toye pratapte niśi saṃsthitāt
children.translated_text: From a pounded substance placed overnight in heated water,
the decoction that comes forth is called a cold infusion.
What is put into hot water and rubbed is termed a hot infusion.

children.text: teṣāṃ yathāpūrvaṃ balādhikyam ataḥ kaṣāyakalpanā vyādhyāturabalāpekṣiṇī na tvevaṃ khalu sarvāṇi sarvatropayogīni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Of these, strength is greater in the preceding order; therefore the preparation of decoctions depends on the disease and the strength of the patient, but certainly not all of them are useful in every case.

children.text: pañcāśanmahākaṣāyā iti yaduktaṃ tadanuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ tadyathā jīvanīyo bṛṃhaṇīyo lekhanīyo bhedanīyaḥ saṃdhānīyo dīpanīya iti ṣaṭkaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ balyo varṇyaḥ kaṇṭhyo hṛdya iti catuṣkaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ tṛptighno 'rśoghnaḥ kuṣṭhaghnaḥ kaṇḍūghnaḥ krimighno viṣaghna iti ṣaṭkaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ stanyajananaḥ stanyaśodhanaḥ śukrajananaḥ śukraśodhana iti catuṣkaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ snehopagaḥ svedopago vamanopago virecanopaga āsthāpanopago 'nuvāsanopagaḥ śirovirecanopaga iti saptakaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ chardinigrahaṇastṛṣṇānigrahaṇo hikkānigrahaṇa iti trikaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ purīṣasaṃgrahaṇīyaḥ purīṣavirajanīyo mūtrasaṃgrahaṇīyo mūtravirajanīyo mūtravirecanīya iti pañcakaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ kāsaharaḥ śvāsaharaḥ śothaharo jvaraharaḥ śramahara iti pañcakaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ dāhapraśamanaḥ śītapraśamana udardapraśamano 'ṅgamardapraśamanaḥ śūlapraśamana iti pañcakaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ śoṇitasthāpano vedanāsthāpanaḥ saṃjñāsthāpanaḥ prajāsthāpano vayaḥsthāpana iti pañcakaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ iti pañcāśanmahākaṣāyā mahatāṃ ca kaṣāyāṇāṃ lakṣaṇodāharaṇārthaṃ vyākhyātā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Now we shall explain in detail what was called the fifty great <s>kaṣāyas</s> (medicinal decoction groups). They are as follows: life-promoting, bulk-promoting, scraping, breaking open, healing, and digestive: this is a group of six <s>kaṣāya</s> classes. Strengthening, complexion-promoting, beneficial to the throat, and beneficial to the heart: this is a group of four <s>kaṣāya</s> classes. Destroying satiety, destroying hemorrhoids, destroying skin disease, destroying itching, destroying worms, and destroying poison: this is a group of six <s>kaṣāya</s> classes. Producing breast milk, purifying breast milk, producing semen, and purifying semen: this is a group of four <s>kaṣāya</s> classes. Adjunctive to oleation, adjunctive to sweating, adjunctive to emesis, adjunctive to purgation, adjunctive to evacuative enema, adjunctive to unctuous enema, and adjunctive to head-purgation: this is a group of seven <s>kaṣāya</s> classes. Restraining vomiting, restraining thirst, and restraining hiccup: this is a group of three <s>kaṣāya</s> classes. Collecting the feces, correcting discoloration of the feces, collecting the urine, correcting discoloration of the urine, and promoting urinary evacuation: this is a group of five <s>kaṣāya</s> classes. Removing cough, removing dyspnea, removing swelling, removing fever, and removing fatigue: this is a group of five <s>kaṣāya</s> classes. Pacifying burning, pacifying cold, pacifying urticaria, pacifying bodily aching, and pacifying colic pain: this is a group of five <s>kaṣāya</s> classes. Stabilizing blood, stabilizing sensation, stabilizing consciousness, stabilizing progeny, and stabilizing age: this is a group of five <s>kaṣāya</s> classes. Thus the fifty great <s>kaṣāyas</s> have been explained for the purpose of defining and exemplifying the major <s>kaṣāyas</s>.

children.text: teṣāmekaikasmin mahākaṣāye daśa daśāvayavikān kaṣāyānanuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ tānyeva pañca kaṣāyaśatāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: For each one of these great <s>kaṣāyas</s> we shall explain ten component <s>kaṣāyas</s>; these make five hundred <s>kaṣāyas</s> in all.

children.text: tadyathā jīvakarṣabhakau medā mahāmedā kākolī kṣīrakākolī mudgaparṇīmāṣaparṇyau jīvantī madhukamiti daśemāni jīvanīyāni bhavanti kṣīriṇī rājakṣavakāśvagandhākākolīkṣīrakākolīvāṭyāyanībhadraudanībhāradvājīpayasyarṣyagandhā iti daśemāni bṛṃhaṇīyāni bhavanti mustakuṣṭhaharidrādāruharidrāvacātiviṣākaṭurohiṇīcitrakacirabilvahaimavatya iti daśemāni lekhanīyāni bhavanti suvahārkorubukāgnimukhīcitrācitrakacirabilvaśaṅkhinīśakulādanīsvarṇakṣīriṇya iti daśemāni bhedanīyāni bhavanti madhukamadhuparṇīpṛśniparṇyambaṣṭhakīsamaṅgāmocarasadhātakīlodhrapriyaṅgukaṭphalānīti daśemāni saṃdhānīyāni bhavanti pippalīpippalīmūlacavyacitrakaśṛṅgaverāmlavetasamaricājamodābhallātakāsthihiṅguniryāsā iti daśemāni dīpanīyāni bhavanti iti ṣaṭkaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are as follows. <s>Jīvaka</s> and <s>Ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>Medā</s>, <s>Mahāmedā</s>, <s>Kākolī</s>, <s>Kṣīrakākolī</s>, <s>Mudgaparṇī</s> and <s>Māṣaparṇī</s>, <s>Jīvantī</s>, and <s>Madhuka</s>: these ten are life-promoting. <s>Kṣīriṇī</s>, <s>Rājakṣavaka</s>, <s>Aśvagandhā</s>, <s>Kākolī</s>, <s>Kṣīrakākolī</s>, <s>Vāṭyāyanī</s>, <s>Bhadraudanī</s>, <s>Bhāradvājī</s>, <s>Payasyā</s>, and <s>Ṛṣyagandhā</s>: these ten are bulk-promoting. <s>Musta</s>, <s>Kuṣṭha</s>, <s>Haridrā</s>, <s>Dāruharidrā</s>, <s>Vacā</s>, <s>Ativiṣā</s>, <s>Kaṭurohiṇī</s>, <s>Citraka</s>, <s>Cirabilva</s>, and <s>Haimavatī</s>: these ten are scraping. <s>Suvahā</s>, <s>Arka</s>, <s>Urubuka</s>, <s>Agnimukhī</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Citraka</s>, <s>Cirabilva</s>, <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>, <s>Śakulādanī</s>, and <s>Svarṇakṣīriṇī</s>: these ten are breaking open. <s>Madhuka</s>, <s>Madhuparṇī</s>, <s>Pṛśniparṇī</s>, <s>Ambaṣṭhakī</s>, <s>Samaṅgā</s>, <s>Mocarasa</s>, <s>Dhātakī</s>, <s>Lodhra</s>, <s>Priyaṅgu</s>, and <s>Kaṭphala</s>: these ten are healing. <s>Pippalī</s>, <s>Pippalīmūla</s>, <s>Cavya</s>, <s>Citraka</s>, <s>Śṛṅgavera</s>, <s>Amlavetasa</s>, <s>Marica</s>, <s>Ajamodā</s>, <s>Bhallātakāsthi</s>, and <s>Hiṅguniryāsa</s>: these ten are digestive. Thus ends the group of six <s>kaṣāya</s> classes.

children.text: aindryṛṣabhyatirasarṣyaproktāpayasyāśvagandhāsthirārohiṇībalātibalā iti daśemāni balyāni bhavanti candanatuṅgapadmakośīramadhukamañjiṣṭhāsārivāpayasyāsitālatā iti daśemāni varṇyāni bhavanti sārivekṣumūlamadhukapippalīdrākṣāvidārīkaiṭaryahaṃsapādībṛhatīkaṇṭakārikā iti daśemāni kaṇṭhyāni bhavanti āmrāmrātakalikucakaramardavṛkṣāmlāmlavetasakuvalabadaradāḍimamātuluṅgānīti daśemāni hṛdyāni bhavanti iti catuṣkaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aindrī</s>, <s>Ṛṣabhī</s>, <s>Atirasā</s>, <s>Ṛṣyaproktā</s>, <s>Payasyā</s>, <s>Aśvagandhā</s>, <s>Sthirā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Balā</s>, and <s>Atibalā</s>: these ten are strengthening. <s>Candana</s>, <s>Tuṅga</s>, <s>Padmaka</s>, <s>Uśīra</s>, <s>Madhuka</s>, <s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>Sārivā</s>, <s>Payasyā</s>, <s>Sitā</s>, and <s>Latā</s>: these ten promote complexion. <s>Sārivā</s>, <s>Ikṣumūla</s>, <s>Madhuka</s>, <s>Pippalī</s>, <s>Drākṣā</s>, <s>Vidārī</s>, <s>Kaiṭarya</s>, <s>Haṃsapādī</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, and <s>Kaṇṭakārikā</s>: these ten are beneficial to the throat. <s>Āmra</s>, <s>Āmrātaka</s>, <s>Likuca</s>, <s>Karamarda</s>, <s>Vṛkṣāmla</s>, <s>Amlavetasa</s>, <s>Kuvala</s>, <s>Badara</s>, <s>Dāḍima</s>, and <s>Mātuluṅga</s>: these ten are beneficial to the heart. Thus ends the group of four <s>kaṣāya</s> classes.

children.text: nāgaracavyacitrakaviḍaṅgamūrvāguḍūcīvacāmustapippalīpaṭolānīti daśemāni tṛptighnāni bhavanti kuṭajabilvacitrakanāgarātiviṣābhayādhanvayāsakadāruharidrāvacācavyānīti daśemānyarśoghnāni bhavanti khadirābhayāmalakaharidrāruṣkarasaptaparṇāragvadhakaravīraviḍaṅgajātīpravālā iti daśemāni kuṣṭhaghnāni bhavanti candananaladakṛtamālanaktamālanimbakuṭajasarṣapamadhukadāruharidrāmustānīti daśemāni kaṇḍūghnāni bhavanti akṣīvamaricagaṇḍīrakebukaviḍaṅganirguṇḍīkiṇihīśvadaṃṣṭrāvṛṣaparṇikākhuparṇikā iti daśemāni krimighnāni bhavanti haridrāmañjiṣṭhāsuvahāsūkṣmailāpālindīcandanakatakaśirīṣasindhuvāraśleṣmātakā iti daśemāni viṣaghnāni bhavanti iti ṣaṭkaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nāgara</s>, <s>Cavya</s>, <s>Citraka</s>, <s>Viḍaṅga</s>, <s>Mūrvā</s>, <s>Guḍūcī</s>, <s>Vacā</s>, <s>Musta</s>, <s>Pippalī</s>, and <s>Paṭola</s>: these ten destroy satiety. <s>Kuṭaja</s>, <s>Bilva</s>, <s>Citraka</s>, <s>Nāgara</s>, <s>Ativiṣā</s>, <s>Abhayā</s>, <s>Dhanvayāsaka</s>, <s>Dāruharidrā</s>, <s>Vacā</s>, and <s>Cavya</s>: these ten destroy hemorrhoids. <s>Khadira</s>, <s>Abhayā</s>, <s>Āmalaka</s>, <s>Haridrā</s>, <s>Aruṣkara</s>, <s>Saptaparṇa</s>, <s>Āragvadha</s>, <s>Karavīra</s>, <s>Viḍaṅga</s>, and <s>Jātīpravāla</s>: these ten destroy skin disease. <s>Candana</s>, <s>Nalada</s>, <s>Kṛtamāla</s>, <s>Naktamāla</s>, <s>Nimba</s>, <s>Kuṭaja</s>, <s>Sarṣapa</s>, <s>Madhuka</s>, <s>Dāruharidrā</s>, and <s>Musta</s>: these ten destroy itching. <s>Akṣīva</s>, <s>Marica</s>, <s>Gaṇḍīraka</s>, <s>Ebuka</s>, <s>Viḍaṅga</s>, <s>Nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>Kiṇihī</s>, <s>Śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, <s>Vṛṣaparṇikā</s>, and <s>Ākhuparṇikā</s>: these ten destroy worms. <s>Haridrā</s>, <s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>Suvahā</s>, <s>Sūkṣmailā</s>, <s>Pālindī</s>, <s>Candana</s>, <s>Kataka</s>, <s>Śirīṣa</s>, <s>Sindhuvāra</s>, and <s>Śleṣmātaka</s>: these ten destroy poison. Thus ends the group of six <s>kaṣāya</s> classes.

children.text: vīraṇaśāliṣaṣṭikekṣuvālikādarbhakuśakāśagundretkaṭakattṛṇamūlānīti daśemāni stanyajananāni bhavanti pāṭhāmahauṣadhasuradārumustamūrvāguḍūcīvatsakaphalakirātatiktakakaṭurohiṇīsārivā iti daśemāni stanyaśodhanāni bhavanti jīvakarṣabhakakākolīkṣīrakākolīmudgaparṇīmāṣaparṇīmedāvṛddharuhājaṭilākuliṅgā iti daśemāni śukrajananāni bhavanti kuṣṭhailavālukakaṭphalasamudraphenakadambaniryāsekṣukāṇḍekṣvikṣurakavasukośīrāṇīti daśemāni śukraśodhanāni bhavanti iti catuṣkaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The roots of <s>Vīraṇa</s>, <s>Śāli</s>, <s>Ṣaṣṭika</s>, <s>Ikṣuvālikā</s>, <s>Darbha</s>, <s>Kuśa</s>, <s>Kāśa</s>, <s>Gundrā</s>, <s>Itkaṭa</s>, and <s>Kattṛṇa</s>: these ten are breast-milk-producing. <s>Pāṭhā</s>, <s>Mahauṣadha</s>, <s>Suradāru</s>, <s>Musta</s>, <s>Mūrvā</s>, <s>Guḍūcī</s>, <s>Vatsakaphala</s>, <s>Kirātatiktaka</s>, <s>Kaṭurohiṇī</s>, and <s>Sārivā</s>: these ten purify breast milk. <s>Jīvaka</s>, <s>Ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>Kākolī</s>, <s>Kṣīrakākolī</s>, <s>Mudgaparṇī</s>, <s>Māṣaparṇī</s>, <s>Medā</s>, <s>Vṛddharuhā</s>, <s>Jaṭilā</s>, and <s>Kuliṅgā</s>: these ten produce semen. <s>Kuṣṭha</s>, <s>Elavāluka</s>, <s>Kaṭphala</s>, <s>Samudraphena</s>, <s>Kadambaniryāsa</s>, <s>Ikṣukāṇḍa</s>, <s>Ikṣu</s>, <s>Ikṣuraka</s>, <s>Vasuka</s>, and <s>Uśīra</s>: these ten purify semen. Thus ends the group of four <s>kaṣāya</s> classes.

children.text: mṛdvīkāmadhukamadhuparṇīmedāvidārīkākolīkṣīrakākolījīvakajīvantīśālaparṇya iti daśemāni snehopagāni bhavanti śobhāñjanakairaṇḍārkavṛścīrapunarnavāyavatilakulatthamāṣabadarāṇīti daśemāni svedopagāni bhavanti madhumadhukakovidārakarbudāranīpavidulabimbīśaṇapuṣpīsadāpuṣpāpratyakpuṣpā iti daśemāni vamanopagāni bhavanti drākṣākāśmaryaparūṣakābhayāmalakabibhītakakuvalabadarakarkandhupīlūnīti daśemāni virecanopagāni bhavanti trivṛdbilvapippalīkuṣṭhasarṣapavacāvatsakaphalaśatapuṣpāmadhukamadanaphalānīti daśemānyāsthāpanopagāni bhavanti rāsnāsuradārubilvamadanaśatapuṣpāvṛścīrapunarnavāśvadaṃṣṭrāgnimanthaśyonākā iti daśemānyanuvāsanopagāni bhavanti jyotiṣmatīkṣavakamaricapippalīviḍaṅgaśigrusarṣapāpāmārgataṇḍulaśvetāmahāśvetā iti daśemāni śirovirecanopagāni bhavanti iti saptakaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛdvīkā</s>, <s>Madhuka</s>, <s>Madhuparṇī</s>, <s>Medā</s>, <s>Vidārī</s>, <s>Kākolī</s>, <s>Kṣīrakākolī</s>, <s>Jīvaka</s>, <s>Jīvantī</s>, and <s>Śālaparṇī</s>: these ten are aids to oleation. <s>Śobhāñjana</s>, <s>Kairaṇḍa</s>, <s>Arka</s>, <s>Vṛścīra</s>, <s>Punarnavā</s>, barley, sesame, horse gram, black gram, and <s>Badara</s>: these ten are aids to sweating. Honey, <s>Madhuka</s>, <s>Kovidāra</s>, <s>Karbudāra</s>, <s>Nīpa</s>, <s>Vidula</s>, <s>Bimbī</s>, <s>Śaṇapuṣpī</s>, <s>Sadāpuṣpā</s>, and <s>Pratyakpuṣpā</s>: these ten are aids to emesis. <s>Drākṣā</s>, <s>Kāśmarya</s>, <s>Parūṣaka</s>, <s>Abhayā</s>, <s>Āmalaka</s>, <s>Bibhītaka</s>, <s>Kuvala</s>, <s>Badara</s>, <s>Karkandhu</s>, and <s>Pīlu</s>: these ten are aids to purgation. <s>Trivṛt</s>, <s>Bilva</s>, <s>Pippalī</s>, <s>Kuṣṭha</s>, mustard, <s>Vacā</s>, <s>Vatsakaphala</s>, <s>Śatapuṣpā</s>, <s>Madhuka</s>, and <s>Madanaphala</s>: these ten are aids to evacuative enema. <s>Rāsnā</s>, <s>Suradāru</s>, <s>Bilva</s>, <s>Madana</s>, <s>Śatapuṣpā</s>, <s>Vṛścīra</s>, <s>Punarnavā</s>, <s>Śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, <s>Agnimantha</s>, and <s>Śyonāka</s>: these ten are aids to unctuous enema. <s>Jyotiṣmatī</s>, <s>Kṣavaka</s>, pepper, <s>Pippalī</s>, <s>Viḍaṅga</s>, <s>Śigru</s>, mustard, <s>Apāmārgataṇḍula</s>, <s>Śvetā</s>, and <s>Mahāśvetā</s>: these ten are aids to evacuation of the head. Thus this is a sevenfold kaṣāya (decoction) class.

children.text: jambvāmrapallavamātuluṅgāmlabadaradāḍimayavayaṣṭikośīramṛllājā iti daśemāni chardinigrahaṇāni bhavanti nāgaradhanvayavāsakamustaparpaṭakacandanakirātatiktakaguḍūcīhrīveradhānyakapaṭolānīti daśemāni tṛṣṇānigrahaṇāni bhavanti śaṭīpuṣkaramūlabadarabījakaṇṭakārikābṛhatīvṛkṣaruhābhayāpippalīdurālabhākulīraśṛṅgya iti daśemāni hikkānigrahaṇāni bhavantīti trikaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jambu</s> and mango shoots, <s>Mātuluṅga</s>, sour <s>Badara</s>, pomegranate, barley, <s>Yaṣṭika</s>, <s>Uśīra</s>, clay, and parched grain: these ten check vomiting. <s>Nāgara</s>, <s>Dhanvayavāsaka</s>, <s>Musta</s>, <s>Parpaṭaka</s>, sandalwood, <s>Kirātatiktaka</s>, <s>Guḍūcī</s>, <s>Hrīvera</s>, coriander, and <s>Paṭola</s>: these ten check thirst. <s>Śaṭī</s>, <s>Puṣkaramūla</s>, <s>Badara</s> seed, <s>Kaṇṭakārikā</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, <s>Vṛkṣaruhā</s>, <s>Abhayā</s>, <s>Pippalī</s>, <s>Durālabhā</s>, and <s>Kulīraśṛṅgī</s>: these ten check hiccup. Thus this is a threefold kaṣāya class.

children.text: priyaṅgvanantāmrāsthikaṭvaṅgalodhramocarasasamaṅgādhātakīpuṣpapadmāpadmakesarāṇīti daśemāni purīṣasaṃgrahaṇīyāni bhavanti jambuśallakītvakkacchurāmadhūkaśālmalīśrīveṣṭakabhṛṣṭamṛtpayasyotpalatilakaṇā iti daśemāni purīṣavirajanīyāni bhavanti ambvāmraplakṣavaṭakapītanoḍumbarāśvatthabhallātakāśmantakasomavalkā iti daśemāni mūtrasaṃgrahaṇīyāni bhavanti padmotpalanalinakumudasaugandhikapuṇḍarīkaśatapatramadhukapriyaṅgudhātakīpuṣpāṇīti daśemāni mūtravirajanīyāni bhavanti vṛkṣādanīśvadaṃṣṭrāvasukavaśirapāṣāṇabhedadarbhakuśakāśagundretkaṭamūlānīti daśemāni mūtravirecanīyāni bhavantīti pañcakaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṅgu</s>, <s>Anantā</s>, mango stone, <s>Kaṭvaṅga</s>, <s>Lodhra</s>, <s>Mocarasa</s>, <s>Samaṅgā</s>, <s>Dhātakī</s> flowers, lotus, and lotus filaments: these ten are stool-binding substances. <s>Jambu</s>, <s>Śallakī</s> bark, <s>Kacchurā</s>, <s>Madhūka</s>, <s>Śālmalī</s>, <s>Śrīveṣṭaka</s>, roasted clay, <s>Payasyā</s>, blue lotus, and sesame: these ten restore the proper color of feces. Water, mango, <s>Plakṣa</s>, <s>Vaṭaka</s>, <s>Pītana</s>, <s>Udumbara</s>, <s>Aśvattha</s>, <s>Bhallātaka</s>, <s>Aśmantaka</s>, and <s>Somavalka</s>: these ten restrain urine. Lotus, blue lotus, <s>Nalina</s>, water lily, fragrant water lily, white lotus, hundred-petaled lotus, <s>Madhuka</s>, <s>Priyaṅgu</s>, and <s>Dhātakī</s> flowers: these ten restore the proper color of urine. <s>Vṛkṣādanī</s>, <s>Śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, <s>Vasuka</s>, <s>Vaśira</s>, <s>Pāṣāṇabheda</s>, <s>Darbha</s>, <s>Kuśa</s>, <s>Kāśa</s>, <s>Gundrā</s>, and <s>Itkaṭa</s> roots: these ten promote urination. Thus this is a fivefold kaṣāya class.

children.text: drākṣābhayāmalakapippalīdurālabhāśṛṅgīkaṇṭakārikāvṛścīrapunarnavātāmalakya iti daśemāni kāsaharāṇi bhavanti śaṭīpuṣkaramūlāmlavetasailāhiṅgvagurusurasātāmalakījīvantīcaṇḍā iti daśemāni śvāsaharāṇi bhavanti pāṭalāgnimanthaśyonākabilvakāśmaryakaṇṭakārikābṛhatīśālaparṇīpṛśniparṇīgokṣurakā iti daśemāni śvayathuharāṇi bhavanti sārivāśarkarāpāṭhāmañjiṣṭhādrākṣāpīluparūṣakābhayāmalakabibhītakānīti daśemāni jvaraharāṇi bhavanti drākṣākharjūrapriyālabadaradāḍimaphalguparuṣakekṣuyavaṣaṣṭikā iti daśemāni śramaharāṇi bhavanti iti pañcakaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Drākṣā</s>, <s>Abhayā</s>, <s>Āmalaka</s>, <s>Pippalī</s>, <s>Durālabhā</s>, <s>Śṛṅgī</s>, <s>Kaṇṭakārikā</s>, <s>Vṛścīra</s>, <s>Punarnavā</s>, and <s>Tāmalakī</s>: these ten remove cough. <s>Śaṭī</s>, <s>Puṣkaramūla</s>, sour <s>Vetasa</s>, cardamom, asafoetida, aloe-wood, <s>Surasā</s>, <s>Tāmalakī</s>, <s>Jīvantī</s>, and <s>Caṇḍā</s>: these ten remove dyspnea. <s>Pāṭalā</s>, <s>Agnimantha</s>, <s>Śyonāka</s>, <s>Bilva</s>, <s>Kāśmarya</s>, <s>Kaṇṭakārikā</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, <s>Śālaparṇī</s>, <s>Pṛśniparṇī</s>, and <s>Gokṣuraka</s>: these ten remove swelling. <s>Sārivā</s>, sugar, <s>Pāṭhā</s>, <s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>Drākṣā</s>, <s>Pīlu</s>, <s>Parūṣaka</s>, <s>Abhayā</s>, <s>Āmalaka</s>, and <s>Bibhītaka</s>: these ten remove fever. <s>Drākṣā</s>, dates, <s>Priyāla</s>, <s>Badara</s>, pomegranate, <s>Phalgu</s>, <s>Parūṣaka</s>, sugarcane, barley, and sixty-day rice: these ten remove fatigue. Thus this is a fivefold kaṣāya class.

children.text: lājācandanakāśmaryaphalamadhūkaśarkarānīlotpalośīrasārivāguḍūcīhrīverāṇīti daśemāni dāhapraśamanāni bhavanti tagarāgurudhānyakaśṛṅgaverabhūtīkavacākaṇṭakāryagnimanthaśyonākapippalya iti daśemāni śītapraśamanāni bhavanti tindukapriyālabadarakhadirakadarasaptaparṇāśvakarṇārjunāsanārimedā iti daśemānyudardapraśamanāni bhavanti vidārīgandhāpṛśniparṇībṛhatīkaṇṭakārikairaṇḍakākolīcandanośīrailāmadhukānīti daśemānyaṅgamardapraśamanāni bhavanti pippalīpippalīmūlacavyacitrakaśṛṅgaveramaricājamodājagandhājājīgaṇḍīrāṇīti daśemāni śūlapraśamanāni bhavanti iti pañcakaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Parched grain, sandalwood, <s>Kāśmarya</s> fruit, <s>Madhūka</s>, sugar, blue lotus, <s>Uśīra</s>, <s>Sārivā</s>, <s>Guḍūcī</s>, and <s>Hrīvera</s>: these ten pacify burning. <s>Tagara</s>, aloe-wood, coriander, dry ginger, <s>Bhūtīka</s>, <s>Vacā</s>, <s>Kaṇṭakārī</s>, <s>Agnimantha</s>, <s>Śyonāka</s>, and <s>Pippalī</s>: these ten pacify cold. <s>Tinduka</s>, <s>Priyāla</s>, <s>Badara</s>, <s>Khadira</s>, <s>Kadara</s>, <s>Saptaparṇa</s>, <s>Aśvakarṇa</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Asana</s>, and <s>Arimeda</s>: these ten pacify urticarial eruptions. <s>Vidārīgandhā</s>, <s>Pṛśniparṇī</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, <s>Kaṇṭakārī</s>, castor, <s>Kākolī</s>, sandalwood, <s>Uśīra</s>, cardamom, and <s>Madhuka</s>: these ten pacify aching of the limbs. <s>Pippalī</s>, <s>Pippalīmūla</s>, <s>Cavya</s>, <s>Citraka</s>, dry ginger, pepper, <s>Ajamodā</s>, <s>Ajagandhā</s>, cumin, and <s>Gaṇḍīra</s>: these ten pacify colic pain. Thus this is a fivefold kaṣāya class.

children.text: madhumadhukarudhiramocarasamṛtkapālalodhragairikapriyaṅguśarkarālājā iti daśemāni śoṇitasthāpanāni bhavanti śālakaṭphalakadambapadmakatumbamocarasaśirīṣavañjulailavālukāśokā iti daśemāni vedanāsthāpanāni bhavanti hiṅgukaiṭaryārimedāvacācorakavayasthāgolomījaṭilāpalaṅkaṣāśokarohiṇya iti daśemāni saṃjñāsthāpanāni bhavanti aindrībrāhmīśatavīryāsahasravīryāmoghāvyathāśivāriṣṭāvāṭyapuṣpīviṣvaksenakāntā iti daśemāni prajāsthāpanāni bhavanti amṛtābhayādhātrīmuktāśvetājīvantyatirasāmaṇḍūkaparṇīsthirāpunarnavā iti daśemāni vayaḥsthāpanāni bhavanti iti pañcakaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Honey, <s>Madhuka</s>, blood, <s>Mocarasa</s>, potsherd clay, <s>Lodhra</s>, red ochre, <s>Priyaṅgu</s>, sugar, and parched grain: these ten stabilize blood. <s>Śāla</s>, <s>Kaṭphala</s>, <s>Kadamba</s>, <s>Padmaka</s>, <s>Tumba</s>, <s>Mocarasa</s>, <s>Śirīṣa</s>, <s>Vañjula</s>, <s>Elavāluka</s>, and <s>Aśoka</s>: these ten stabilize pain. Asafoetida, <s>Kaiṭarya</s>, <s>Arimeda</s>, <s>Vacā</s>, <s>Coraka</s>, <s>Vayasthā</s>, <s>Golomī</s>, <s>Jaṭilā</s>, <s>Palaṅkaṣā</s>, and <s>Aśokarohiṇī</s>: these ten restore consciousness. <s>Aindrī</s>, <s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Śatavīryā</s>, <s>Sahasravīryā</s>, <s>Amoghā</s>, <s>Avyathā</s>, <s>Śivā</s>, <s>Ariṣṭā</s>, <s>Vāṭyapuṣpī</s>, and <s>Viṣvaksenakāntā</s>: these ten sustain offspring. <s>Amṛtā</s>, <s>Abhayā</s>, <s>Dhātrī</s>, pearl, <s>Śvetā</s>, <s>Jīvantī</s>, <s>Atirasā</s>, <s>Maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, <s>Sthirā</s>, and <s>Punarnavā</s>: these ten sustain age. Thus this is a fivefold kaṣāya class.

children.text: iti pañcakaṣāyaśatānyabhisamasya pañcāśanmahākaṣāyā mahatāṃ ca kaṣāyāṇāṃ lakṣaṇodāharaṇārthaṃ vyākhyātā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, after bringing together the five hundreds of <s>kaṣāya</s> preparations, the fifty <s>mahākaṣāyas</s>, and the explanation of the definitions and examples of the great <s>kaṣāyas</s>, have been set forth.

children.text: nahi vistarasya pramāṇamasti na cāpyatisaṃkṣepo 'lpabuddhīnāṃ sāmarthyāyopakalpate tasmādanatisaṃkṣepeṇānativistareṇa copadiṣṭāḥ
children.translated_text: For there is no fixed measure of expansiveness; nor does excessive brevity serve the capacity of those of slight understanding. Therefore they have been taught neither too briefly nor too extensively.

children.text: etāvanto hyalamalpabuddhīnāṃ vyavahārāya buddhimatāṃ ca svālakṣaṇyānumānayuktikuśalānām anuktārthajñānāyeti ||
children.translated_text: For these many are sufficient for practical use by those of slight understanding, and for intelligent persons skilled in inference from specific characteristics and in reasoning, they are sufficient for knowing meanings not explicitly stated.

children.text: evaṃvādinaṃ bhagavantamātreyamagniveśa uvāca naitāni bhagavan pañca kaṣāyaśatāni pūryante tāni tāni hyevāṅgānyupaplavante teṣu teṣu mahākaṣāyeṣviti ||
children.translated_text: When the venerable <s>Ātreya</s> had spoken thus, <s>Agniveśa</s> said, 'Venerable sir, these five hundred <s>kaṣāyas</s> are not completed, for the very same constituent parts recur in those various <s>mahākaṣāyas</s>.'
The venerable <s>Ātreya</s> said to him, 'This is not how an intelligent person should see it, <s>Agniveśa</s>.

children.text: eko 'pi hyanekāṃ saṃjñāṃ labhate kāryāntarāṇi kurvan tadyathā puruṣo bahūnāṃ karmaṇāṃ karaṇe samartho bhavati sa yadyat karma karoti tasya tasya karmaṇaḥ kartṛkaraṇakāryasamprayuktaṃ tattadgauṇaṃ nāmaviśeṣaṃ prāpnoti tadvadauṣadhadravyamapi draṣṭavyam
children.translated_text: For even a single thing receives many designations when it performs different functions. Just as a man may be capable of performing many tasks, and whichever task he performs, he receives, in connection with that task, a particular secondary name joined with the agent, instrument, and result of that action, so too should a medicinal substance be understood.

children.text: yadi caikameva kiṃcid dravyam āsādayāmastathāguṇayuktaṃ yat sarvakarmaṇāṃ karaṇe samarthaṃ syāt kastato 'nyadicchedupadhārayitumupadeṣṭuṃ vā śiṣyebhya iti ||
children.translated_text: And if we were to obtain even one substance endowed with such qualities that it could perform all actions, who would then wish to consider or teach any other substance to his pupils?'
Here are the verses:
From what source, how many, and by which substances the six hundreds of purgative preparations
have been stated here in summary, and likewise their six supports;
the tastes, excluding salt, are designated as <s>kaṣāyas</s>,
and therefore a fivefold source of <s>kaṣāyas</s> has been declared.
Likewise their preparation too has again been stated as fivefold,
and the fifty great <s>kaṣāyas</s> have been enumerated.
Also five hundreds of <s>kaṣāyas</s> have been taught by division,

children.text: lakṣaṇārthaṃ pramāṇaṃ hi vistarasya na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: for the sake of definition; there is no measure for expansiveness.
Nor is excessive brevity adequate or useful for capacity,
for one of slight understanding; therefore this is neither too brief nor too extensive.
For the practical use of the dull and for the increase of understanding among the wise,
this group of fifty <s>kaṣāyas</s> has been declared.
He who knows their combination and application in external actions

children.text: saṃyogaṃ ca prayogaṃ ca yo veda sa bhiṣagvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in internal ones is the best of physicians.
Now then we shall expound the chapter called <s>Mātrāśitīya</s>, 'On Eating in Measure.'
Thus spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>.
One should be a measured eater.
The measure of food, moreover, depends on the strength of <s>agni</s> (digestive fire).

children.text: yāvaddhyasyāśanamaśitamanupahatya prakṛtiṃ yathākālaṃ jarāṃ gacchati tāvadasya mātrāpramāṇaṃ veditavyaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For as much food as, when eaten, proceeds to digestion at the proper time without impairing one's natural condition, that much is to be known as the proper measure for him.

In this regard, food substances such as <s>śāli</s> rice, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, <s>mudga</s>, <s>āvaka</s>, <s>piñjala</s>, antelope, hare, <s>śarabha</s>, <s>śambara</s>, and the like, though naturally light, still depend on measure.

Likewise food substances such as preparations of flour, sugarcane products, milk products, sesame, <s>māṣa</s>, and the flesh of marsh-dwelling and aquatic animals, though naturally heavy, still depend on measure alone.

children.text: na caivamukte dravye gurulāghavamakāraṇaṃ manyeta laghūni hi dravyāṇi vāyvagniguṇabahulāni bhavanti pṛthvīsomaguṇabahulānītarāṇi tasmāt svaguṇādapi laghūnyagnisaṃdhukṣaṇasvabhāvānyalpadoṣāṇi cocyante 'pi sauhityopayuktāni gurūṇi punar nāgnisaṃdhukṣaṇasvabhāvānyasāmānyāt ataścātimātraṃ doṣavanti sauhityopayuktānyanyatra vyāyāmāgnibalāt saiṣā bhavatyagnibalāpekṣiṇī mātrā ||
children.translated_text: Nor, when this has been said, should one think that heaviness and lightness in substances are causeless. Light substances are rich in the qualities of <s>vāyu</s> and <s>agni</s>, while the others are rich in the qualities of earth and water. Therefore, because of their own qualities, light substances are by nature kindlers of <s>agni</s> and are said to produce little <s>doṣa</s>, even when eaten to satiety. Heavy substances, however, are not by nature kindlers of <s>agni</s>, because they are dissimilar to it; therefore, when eaten in excessive measure and to satiety, they produce <s>doṣas</s>, except where there is exercise and strength of <s>agni</s>. Thus this measure depends on the strength of <s>agni</s>.

children.text: na ca nāpekṣate dravyaṃ dravyāpekṣayā ca tribhāgasauhityamardhasauhityaṃ vā gurūṇāmupadiśyate laghūnāmapi ca nātisauhityamagneryuktyartham ||
children.translated_text: And substance is not irrelevant; with regard to the substance, one-third satiety or half satiety is prescribed for heavy foods, while even with light foods there should be no excessive satiety, for the proper management of <s>agni</s>.
For food eaten in proper measure, without impairing one's natural condition, surely connects the user with strength, complexion, comfort, and longevity.
And here there are verses:
Therefore, because flour-based food is heavy, and even flattened rice made from grain is heavy,
one who has already eaten should never eat it; one who is hungry should eat it in proper measure.
Dried meat, dried vegetables, water-lily roots, and lotus fibers,
because of their heaviness, should not be used habitually; lean meat too should not be consumed.

children.text: matsyān dadhi ca māṣāṃśca yavakāṃśca na śīlayet ||
children.translated_text: One should not make a habit of fish, curds, <s>māṣa</s> beans, or <s>yavaka</s>.
One should make regular use of <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, <s>śāli</s> rice, <s>mudga</s>, rock salt, <s>āmalaka</s>, barley,
rainwater, milk, ghee, meat from dry-land animals, and honey.
And one should use daily that by which health is maintained,
and that which prevents the arising of disorders not yet arisen.
From here onward, the regimen for the body, beginning with eye-salve and anointing,
will be explained according to its qualities, with healthy conduct in view.
One should regularly apply <s>sauvīra</s> collyrium, beneficial for the eyes,
and every fifth or eighth night <s>rasāñjana</s>, for the purpose of causing discharge.
The eye is made of light; for that reason it has special fear of <s>śleṣman</s>.

children.text: tataḥ śleṣmaharaṃ karma hitaṃ dṛṣṭeḥ prasādanam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore an action that removes <s>śleṣman</s> and clears the sight is beneficial.
That sharp collyrium should not be applied to the eyes by day,
for sight, weakened by purgation, fails when it meets the sun.
Therefore the discharge-inducing collyrium is certainly prescribed at night.
For just as gold and other things, when dirty and of various kinds,
after being washed with oil, cloth, hair, and the like, have stainless purity,
so too, in the eyes of mortals, by collyria and eye-drops,
the sight shines untroubled, like the moon in a clear sky.

children.text: hareṇukāṃ priyaṅguṃ ca pṛthvīkāṃ keśaraṃ nakham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hareṇukā</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>pṛthvīkā</s>, saffron, and <s>nakha</s>,
<s>hrīvera</s>, sandalwood, leaf, bark, cardamom, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>padmaka</s>,
<s>dhyāmaka</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>māṃsī</s>, <s>guggulu</s>, <s>aguru</s>, and sugar,
the good barks of banyan, udumbara, aśvattha, plakṣa, and lodhra,
wild resin, <s>sarjarasa</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>śaileya</s>, lotus, and blue lotus,

children.text: śrīveṣṭakaṃ śallakīṃ ca śukabarham athāpi ca
children.translated_text: <s>śrīveṣṭaka</s>, <s>śallakī</s>, and also a parrot's feather:
having ground these, he should smear them on reed-pith; the physician should make that wick barley-shaped,
as thick as the thumb and eight finger-breadths in length.

children.text: śuṣkāṃ nigarbhāṃ tāṃ vartiṃ dhūmanetrārpitāṃ naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it is dry and hollowed out, a person should place that wick in the smoking tube,
anoint it with unctuous substance, kindle it with fire, and inhale the pleasant practical smoke.
With fat, ghee, beeswax, and excellent medicines properly combined,
one should make a wick with sweet substances and practice <s>snaihika</s> (unctuous) smoking.
White <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, <s>haritāla</s>, <s>manaḥśilā</s>,
and fragrances such as <s>aguru</s> and leaf are used for smoke in head-purgation.
Heaviness of the head, pain, chronic nasal catarrh, hemicrania,
pain of the ears and eyes, cough, hiccup, dyspnea, and obstruction of the throat,
weakness of the teeth and discharge produced by disorders of the ear, nose, and eye,
foul odor of the nose and mouth, toothache, and anorexia,
stiffness of the jaw and neck, itching, worms, and pallor of the face,
excess salivation from <s>śleṣman</s>, hoarseness, swelling of the uvula, and <s>upajihvikā</s>,

children.text: khālityaṃ piñjaratvaṃ ca keśānāṃ patanaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: baldness, tawny discoloration, and also falling of the hair,
sneezing, excessive torpor, confusion of the intellect, and oversleeping:
these are pacified by smoke-drinking, and greater strength arises
for the hair of the head, the skull, the senses, and the voice.
And diseases above the clavicle, composed of <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, even if strong,
do not become head diseases for one whose mouth and nose drink smoke.
For its practical drinking, eight occasions are fully declared.
For an agitation of <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> is observed at these times:

children.text: snātvā bhuktvā samullikhya kṣutvā dantānnighṛṣya ca ||
children.translated_text: after bathing, after eating, after scraping or cleansing, after sneezing, and after rubbing the teeth,
and after nasal therapy, collyrium, and sleep, the self-possessed person should be a drinker of smoke.
Thus diseases above the clavicle that are of the nature of <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s> do not arise.

children.text: rogāstasya tu peyāḥ syur āpānās tristrayastrayaḥ
children.translated_text: For him the draughts to be drunk should be three sets of three inhalations.
The wise person should drink it at most twice a day, at the proper times of the day.

children.text: prayoge snaihike tvekaṃ vairecyaṃ tricatuḥ pibet
children.translated_text: In practical and unctuous use he should drink once, but for evacuative smoking he should drink three or four times.
Purification of the heart, throat, and senses, lightness of the head, and calming
of the <s>doṣas</s> mentioned above are the signs of smoke properly drunk.
Deafness, blindness, muteness, <s>raktapitta</s>, and dizziness of the head:
smoke drunk at the wrong time or in excess causes these complications.
In that case, drinking ghee, nasal therapy, collyrium, and eye-nourishing treatment are desired.

children.text: snaihikaṃ dhūmaje doṣe vāyuḥ pittānugo yadi
children.translated_text: For a disorder caused by smoke, unctuous treatment is desired if <s>vāyu</s> is accompanied by <s>pitta</s>.
But in <s>raktapitta</s> there should be cooling treatment, and in <s>śleṣma-pitta</s>, drying treatment.

children.text: paraṃ tvataḥ pravakṣyāmi dhūmo yeṣāṃ vigarhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Beyond this, I shall now explain those for whom smoke is censured.

children.text: na viriktaḥ pibeddhūmaṃ na kṛte bastikarmaṇi ||
children.translated_text: One who has been purged should not drink smoke, nor one after enema therapy has been performed.

children.text: na raktī na viṣeṇārto na śocanna ca garbhiṇī
children.translated_text: Not one with bleeding, not one afflicted by poison, not one grieving, and not a pregnant woman;

children.text: na śrame na made nāme na pitte na prajāgare ||
children.translated_text: not in fatigue, not in intoxication, not in <s>āma</s>, not in a <s>pitta</s> condition, and not after keeping awake;

children.text: na mūrcchābhramatṛṣṇāsu na kṣīṇe nāpi ca kṣate
children.translated_text: not during fainting, dizziness, or thirst, not when emaciated, and not when wounded;

children.text: na madyadugdhe pītvā ca na snehaṃ na ca mākṣikam ||
children.translated_text: not after drinking liquor or milk, nor after taking unctuous substance or honey;

children.text: dhūmaṃ na bhuktvā dadhnā ca na rūkṣaḥ kruddha eva ca
children.translated_text: one should not smoke after eating curds, nor when dry, nor when angry;

children.text: na tāluśoṣe timire śirasyabhihite na ca ||
children.translated_text: not with dryness of the palate, in <s>timira</s>, or when the head has been injured;

children.text: na śaṅkhake na rohiṇyāṃ na mehe na madātyaye
children.translated_text: not in <s>śaṅkhaka</s>, not in <s>rohiṇī</s>, not in urinary disorder, and not in the after-effect of intoxication.

children.text: eṣu dhūmamakāleṣu mohāt pibati yo naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The person who, out of delusion, drinks smoke in these improper times
has his diseases increase terribly because of deranged use of smoke.
One fit for smoke should drink it when the <s>doṣa</s> is lodged in the head, nose, or eyes.
He should take it by the nose; when it is in the throat, by the mouth. One who drinks through the nose should expel it by the mouth.
Drinking mouthfuls of smoke through the mouth, he should not expel it through the nose.

children.text: pratilomaṃ gato hyāśu dhūmo hiṃsyāddhi cakṣuṣī
children.translated_text: For smoke that has gone in the reverse direction quickly harms the eyes.
With body, eyes, and attention straight, well seated, in three rounds,
