children.translated_text: Then he should procure attendants endowed with good conduct, purity, proper practice, devotion, skill, and courteousness, skilled in service, accomplished in every task: cooks of soup and rice, bathers, massagers, lifters, bed-makers, and grinders of medicines, attendants who are not averse to any work; likewise people skilled in singing, instrumental music, cheerful conversation, verses, gāthās, tales, <s>itihāsa</s> and <s>purāṇa</s>, who understand intentions, are approved, know place and time, and are fit for company. He should also procure lāva birds, partridges, hares, deer, antelopes, black-tailed deer, young deer, sheep, and a milch cow, good-natured, healthy, with a living calf, and well supplied with grass, shelter, and water; vessels, rinsing water, mortars, jars, pitchers, basins, pots, tubs, bowls, ladles, wicker baskets, dipping vessels, cooking vessels, churners, leather, cloth, thread, cotton, wool, and the like; beds, seats, and so on, provided with water-jugs and receptacles, with well-arranged bedding, upper covers, and pillows, with supports, comfortable for lying down, sitting, oleation, sudation, massage, poulticing, sprinkling, anointing, emesis, purgation, evacuative enema, unctuous enema, head-purgation, urination, and defecation; well-washed cushions, and smooth, medium-sized grinding stones; instruments for use as tools, a smoking tube, an enema nozzle, an upper-enema nozzle, a handful of <s>kuśa</s> grass, scales, measuring vessels, ghee, oil, fat, marrow, honey, phāṇita, salt, fuel, water, madhu, sīdhu, surā, sauvīraka, tuṣodaka, maireya, medaka, curd, the liquid part of curd, mastu, dhānyāmla, urine, and also śāli rice, ṣaṣṭika rice, green gram, black gram, barley, sesame, horse gram, jujube, raisins, kāśmarya, parūṣaka, harītakī, āmalaka, and vibhītaka; many kinds of equipment and substances for oleation and sudation; and medicines described as upward-moving, downward-moving, acting in both directions, saṃgrahaṇīya, dīpanīya, pācanīya, upaśamanīya, vāta-removing, and so forth. Whatever other equipment he knows to be needed for countermeasures after reckoning possible complications, and whatever is needed for enjoyment, all that he should arrange.

children.text: tatastaṃ puruṣaṃ yathoktābhyāṃ snehasvedābhyāṃ yathārhamupapādayet taṃ cedasminnantare mānasaḥ śārīro vā vyādhiḥ kaścittīvrataraḥ sahasābhyāgacchet tameva tāvadasyopāvartayituṃ yateta tatastamupāvartya tāvantamevainaṃ kālaṃ tathāvidhenaiva karmaṇopācaret ||
children.translated_text: After that, he should prepare that person as appropriate with the oleation and sudation just described. If in the meantime some rather severe mental or bodily disease should suddenly come upon him, he should first try to turn back that very condition. Then, after turning it back, he should tend him for that same length of time with the same kind of procedure.

children.text: tatastaṃ puruṣaṃ snehasvedopapannamanupahatamanasamabhisamīkṣya sukhoṣitaṃ suprajīrṇabhaktaṃ śiraḥsnātamanuliptagātraṃ sragviṇamanupahatavastrasaṃvītaṃ devatāgnidvijaguruvṛddhavaidyānarcitavantamiṣṭe nakṣatratithikaraṇamuhūrte kārayitvā brāhmaṇān svastivācanaṃ prayuktābhir āśīrbhir abhimantritāṃ madhumadhukasaindhavaphāṇitopahitāṃ madanaphalakaṣāyamātrāṃ pāyayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having examined that person, prepared with oleation and sudation, with his mind uninjured, after he has slept comfortably and his food has been well digested, with his head bathed, his body anointed, wearing a garland and clothed in undamaged garments, and after he has worshipped the deities, fire, twice-born men, teachers, elders, and physicians, at a desired lunar mansion, lunar day, karaṇa, and muhūrta, he should have brāhmaṇas pronounce blessings. With the prescribed benedictions, he should make him drink a measured dose of madanaphala decoction, consecrated and mixed with honey, madhuka, rock salt, and phāṇita.

children.text: madanaphalakaṣāyamātrāpramāṇaṃ tu khalu sarvasaṃśodhanamātrāpramāṇāni ca pratipuruṣamapekṣitavyāni bhavanti yāvaddhi yasya saṃśodhanaṃ pītaṃ vaikārikadoṣaharaṇāyopapadyate na cātiyogāyogāya tāvadasya mātrāpramāṇaṃ veditavyaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The measure of the dose of madanaphala decoction, and indeed the measures of all purificatory doses, must be determined with regard to each person. For whatever amount of purification, when drunk by someone, is suitable for removing morbid doṣas and does not lead to excessive or insufficient application, that should be known as the proper measure of his dose.

children.text: pītavantaṃ tu khalvenaṃ muhūrtam anukāṅkṣeta tasya yadā jānīyāt svedaprādurbhāveṇa doṣaṃ pravilayanamāpadyamānaṃ lomaharṣeṇa ca sthānebhyaḥ pracalitaṃ kukṣisamādhmāpanena ca kukṣimanugataṃ hṛllāsāsyasravaṇābhyāmapi cordhvamukhībhūtām athāsmai jānusamam asaṃbādhaṃ suprayuktāstaraṇottarapracchadopadhānaṃ sopāśrayamāsanamupaveṣṭuṃ prayacchet pratigrahāṃścopacārayet lālāṭapratigrahe pārśvopagrahaṇe nābhiprapīḍane pṛṣṭhonmardane cānapatrapaṇīyāḥ suhṛdo 'numatāḥ prayateran ||
children.translated_text: After he has drunk it, one should wait for a muhūrta. When one knows that the doṣa is becoming liquefied from the appearance of sweat, that it has moved from its places from horripilation, that it has entered the abdomen from distension of the belly, and that it has turned upward from nausea and salivation, then one should give him a seat to sit on, knee-high, uncramped, with well-arranged bedding, upper cover, and pillow, and with support. One should also attend to the receptacles. Approved friends, free from embarrassment, should exert themselves in holding the spittoon, supporting his sides, pressing the navel, and rubbing his back.

children.text: athainamanuśiṣyāt vivṛtoṣṭhatālukaṇṭho nātimahatā vyāyāmena vegānudīrṇānudīrayan kiṃcid avanamya grīvāmūrdhvaśarīram upavegam apravṛttān pravartayan suparilikhitanakhābhyām aṅgulibhyām utpalakumudasaugandhikanālair vā kaṇṭham abhispṛśan sukhaṃ pravartayasveti sa tathāvidhaṃ kuryāt tato 'sya vegān pratigrahagatānavekṣetāvahitaḥ vegaviśeṣadarśanāddhi kuśalo yogāyogātiyogaviśeṣān upalabheta vegaviśeṣānupalabheta vegaviśeṣadarśī punaḥ kṛtyaṃ yathārhamavabudhyeta lakṣaṇena tasmādvegānavekṣetāvahitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he should instruct him: 'With the lips, palate, and throat open, without excessive effort, rousing the urges that have arisen, bringing on those that have not yet begun, bending the neck and upper body slightly forward, and touching the throat with two fingers whose nails are well trimmed, or with stalks of blue lotus, white water-lily, or fragrant water-lily, set it comfortably in motion.' He should act in that way. Then the physician should attentively inspect the urges that have gone into the receptacle. For by seeing the specific character of the urges, a skilled physician recognizes the distinctions between proper application, insufficient application, and excessive application; seeing the specific character of the urges, he again understands what is to be done as appropriate from the signs. Therefore he should inspect the urges attentively.

children.text: tatrāmūnyayogayogātiyogaviśeṣajñānāni bhavanti tadyathā apravṛttiḥ kutaścit kevalasya vāpyauṣadhasya vibhraṃśo vibandho vegānāmayogalakṣaṇāni bhavanti kāle pravṛttiranatimahatī vyathā yathākramaṃ doṣaharaṇaṃ svayaṃ cāvasthānamiti yogalakṣaṇāni bhavanti yogena tu doṣapramāṇaviśeṣeṇa tīkṣṇamṛdumadhyavibhāgo jñeyaḥ yogādhikyena tu phenilaraktacandrikopagamanam ityatiyogalakṣaṇāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: In this matter these are the distinctions by which deficient application, proper application, and excessive application are known. They are as follows. Non-activity from any cause, or the ejection of only the medicine, failure of the procedure, and obstruction of the urges are the signs of deficient application. Activity at the proper time, not very great pain, elimination of the <s>doṣas</s> in due order, and cessation by itself are the signs of proper application. With proper application, the division into sharp, mild, and moderate should be known from the particular measure of the <s>doṣas</s>; with excessive application, the appearance of froth, blood, and shining mucus is the sign of excess.

children.text: tatrātiyogāyoganimittān imān upadravān vidyāt ādhmānaṃ parikartikā parisrāvo hṛdayogasaraṇamaṅgagraho jīvādānaṃ vibhraṃśaḥ stambhaḥ klamaścetyupadravāḥ ||
children.translated_text: From excessive and deficient application one should know these complications: distension, cutting pain, oozing discharge, movement toward the heart, rigidity of the limbs, loss of vital fluid, displacement, stiffness, and exhaustion. These are the complications.

children.text: yogena tu khalvenaṃ charditavantamabhisamīkṣya suprakṣālitapāṇipādāsyaṃ muhūrtamāśvāsya snaihikavairecanikopaśamanīyānāṃ dhūmānāmanyatamaṃ sāmarthyataḥ pāyayitvā punarevodakam upasparśayet ||
children.translated_text: When, after examining him, one sees that he has vomited with proper application, one should have his hands, feet, and mouth well washed, let him recover for a moment, make him inhale, according to his strength, one of the unctuous, purgative, or pacifying smokes, and then have him rinse with water again.

children.text: upaspṛṣṭodakaṃ cainaṃ nivātamāgāramanupraveśya saṃveśya cānuśiṣyāt uccairbhāṣyam atyāśanam atisthānam aticaṅkramaṇaṃ krodhaśokahimātapāvaśyāyātipravātān yānayānaṃ grāmyadharmam asvapanaṃ niśi divā svapnaṃ viruddhājīrṇāsātmyākālapramitātihīnaguruviṣamabhojanavegasaṃdhāraṇodīraṇam iti bhāvān etān manasāpyasevamānaḥ sarvamaho gamayasveti
children.translated_text: After he has rinsed with water, one should lead him into a room sheltered from wind, have him lie down, and instruct him: "Pass the whole day without indulging even mentally in these things: loud speech, overeating, standing too long, walking too much, anger, grief, cold, heat, dew, excessive wind, riding in vehicles, sexual intercourse, staying awake at night, sleeping by day, incompatible food, undigested food, unsuitable food, food at the wrong time, excessively measured, too little, heavy, or irregular food, and the suppression or forcible initiation of natural urges."
He should do accordingly.

children.text: athainaṃ sāyāhne pare vāhni sukhodakapariṣiktaṃ purāṇānāṃ lohitaśālitaṇḍulānāṃ svavaklinnāṃ maṇḍapūrvāṃ sukhoṣṇāṃ yavāgūṃ pāyayedagnibalamabhisamīkṣya evaṃ dvitīye tṛtīye cānnakāle caturthe tvannakāle tathāvidhānāmeva śālitaṇḍulānām utsvinnāṃ vilepīm uṣṇodakadvitīyām asnehalavaṇām alpasnehalavaṇāṃ vā bhojayet evaṃ pañcame ṣaṣṭhe cānnakāle saptame tvannakāle tathāvidhānāmeva śālīnāṃ dviprasṛtaṃ susvinnam odanam uṣṇodakānupānaṃ tanunā tanusnehalavaṇopapannena mudgayūṣeṇa bhojayet evamaṣṭame navame cānnakāle daśame tvannakāle lāvakapiñjalādīnāmanyatamasya māṃsarasenaudakalāvaṇikena nātisāravatā bhojayed uṣṇodakānupānam evamekādaśe dvādaśe cānnakāle ata ūrdhvamannaguṇān krameṇopabhuñjānaḥ saptarātreṇa prakṛtibhojanamāgacchet ||
children.translated_text: Then in the evening, or on the following day, after he has been bathed with warm water, one should give him to drink a comfortably warm <s>yavāgū</s> gruel, preceded by thin rice-water, made from old red <s>śāli</s> rice grains well softened, after considering the strength of his digestive fire. In the second and third meal-times the same should be done. At the fourth meal-time one should feed him a boiled thick gruel made from the same kind of <s>śāli</s> rice grains, with hot water as the second accompaniment, without ghee and salt or with only a little ghee and salt. The same should be done at the fifth and sixth meal-times. At the seventh meal-time one should feed him two <s>prasṛtas</s> of well-cooked rice of the same <s>śāli</s> grains, with hot water as an after-drink, together with a thin mung-bean soup containing a little ghee and salt. The same should be done at the eighth and ninth meal-times. At the tenth meal-time one should feed him with the meat broth of one among quail, partridge, and the like, prepared with water and salt and not too thin, with hot water as an after-drink. The same should be done at the eleventh and twelfth meal-times. After that, gradually taking on the qualities of ordinary food, he returns to his normal diet in seven nights.

children.text: athainaṃ punareva snehasvedābhyām upapādyānupahatamanasam abhisamīkṣya sukhoṣitaṃ suprajīrṇabhaktaṃ kṛtahomabalimaṅgalajapaprāyaścittamiṣṭe tithinakṣatrakaraṇamuhūrte brāhmaṇān svasti vācayitvā trivṛtkalkamakṣamātraṃ yathārhāloḍanaprativinītaṃ pāyayet prasamīkṣya doṣabheṣajadeśakālabalaśarīrāhārasātmyasattvaprakṛtivayasām avasthāntarāṇi vikārāṃśca samyak viriktaṃ cainaṃ vamanoktena dhūmavarjena vidhinopapādayed ā balavarṇaprakṛtilābhāt balavarṇopapannaṃ cainamanupahatamanasamabhisamīkṣya sukhoṣitaṃ suprajīrṇabhaktaṃ śiraḥsnātamanuliptagātraṃ sragviṇam anupahatavastrasaṃvītam anurūpālaṅkārālaṃkṛtaṃ suhṛdāṃ darśayitvā jñātīnāṃ darśayet athainaṃ kāmeṣvavasṛjet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after again preparing him with oleation and fomentation, examining him to be sure that his mind is unimpaired, that he has slept comfortably, and that his meal has been well digested, after he has performed oblations, offerings, auspicious rites, recitation, and expiation, at a desired lunar day, constellation, lunar division, and moment, and after having Brahmins pronounce blessings, one should give him to drink a paste of <s>trivṛt</s> the size of an <s>akṣa</s>, diluted and corrected with a suitable mixing substance, after carefully considering the varying states of <s>doṣa</s>, medicine, place, time, strength, body, diet, habituation, mind, constitution, and age, and also the disorders. When he has been properly purged, one should care for him by the procedure stated for emesis, except for smoking, until he regains strength, complexion, and his natural condition. When he is endowed with strength and complexion, one should examine him to be sure his mind is unimpaired, that he has slept comfortably and digested his meal well, then have him bathe his head, anoint his body, wear a garland, put on undamaged garments, and adorn himself with suitable ornaments. Having shown him to his friends, one should show him to his relatives; then one may release him to his desired activities.
And here there are verses:
By this procedure a king, or again a royal officer,

children.text: yasya vā vipulaṃ dravyaṃ sa saṃśodhanamarhati ||
children.translated_text: or one who possesses abundant wealth, is fit for cleansing therapy.
But a poor man, when he has fallen into distress and cleansing has become timely,
may drink it as needed, even without having gathered supplies that are hard to obtain.

children.text: na hi sarvamanuṣyāṇāṃ santi sarve paricchadāḥ
children.translated_text: For not all human beings possess all requisites,

children.text: na ca rogā na bādhante daridrānapi dāruṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and terrible diseases do afflict the poor as well.
Whatever medicine a person can prepare in an emergency,
that should be used according to his ability, and so too clothing and foods.
Having properly drunk cleansing therapy, which removes impurities, cures disease, and clarifies strength and complexion,
one is joined with life for a long time.
Here are the summary verses:
For lords and wealthy men, emesis together with purgation;

children.text: saṃbhārā ye yadarthaṃ ca samānīya prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: the supplies that should be assembled and used, and for what purpose;

children.text: yathā prayojyā mātrā yā yadayogasya lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: how the therapy is to be applied, what the dose is, and what is the sign of deficient application;
what belongs to proper and excessive application, and what faults and complications there are;
what is to be avoided by one who has been purified, and what the sequence of dietary restoration is:
all this <s>Punarvasu</s> declared in the chapter on preparation.
Now then, we shall explain the chapter called <s>Cikitsāprābhṛtīya</s>, "On the Equipment for Treatment."
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.
A wise man equipped for treatment, learned in the treatise and intent on practice,

children.text: naraṃ virecayati yaṃ sa yogāt sukhamaśnute ||
children.translated_text: purges a person; that person, through proper application, obtains ease.
But the ignorant man who merely thinks himself a physician and purges a human being:
that human being suffers from excessive application and deficient application.
Weakness, lightness, lassitude, the minuteness or lessening of diseases, and relish for food,
purity of the heart and complexion, hunger and thirst, and the timely movement of the urges,
clarity of intellect, senses, and mind, the downward course of <s>māruta</s> (vāta),
and the proper functioning of the bodily fire: these are the signs of one properly purged.
Spitting, impurity of the heart, excitement of <s>śleṣman</s> (kapha) and <s>pitta</s>,
distension, loss of relish, vomiting, absence of weakness, and absence of lightness,
sinking of the calves and thighs, drowsiness, stiffness, and the onset of coryza:
these are the signs of those not properly purged, along with obstruction of <s>māruta</s> (vāta).
When feces, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s> have come forth in due order,
and after that blood flows, resembling fat, flesh, or water,
or watery blood without <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, or blood that is simply black,
in a satiated person afflicted by <s>māruta</s> (vāta) and fainting, that is over-application.
When emesis has been overdone, these very signs occur,
and diseases of <s>vāta</s> moving upward, and especially obstruction of speech, may arise.
Therefore a man should resort to the protection afforded by the provision for treatment,

children.text: yuñjyād ya enamatyantamāyuṣā ca sukhena ca ||
children.translated_text: which links him most fully with life and with happiness.
Indigestion, loss of relish, corpulence, pallor, heaviness, fatigue,
the occurrence of pimples, urticaria, and itching, and also discontent,
laziness, weariness, weakness, foul odor, depression,
agitation of <s>śleṣman</s> (kapha) and <s>pitta</s>, sleeplessness or excessive sleep,
drowsiness, impotence, dullness of intellect, seeing inauspicious dreams,
and loss of strength and complexion, even while being nourished with strengthening therapies:
these are the signs of one with many <s>doṣa</s>s; for him purification is beneficial,
both upward and downward, according to the <s>doṣa</s> and according to strength.
Thus, when the bowel has been purified, the bodily fire increases,
diseases subside, and the natural constitution follows its course.
His senses, mind, intellect, and complexion become clear,

children.text: balaṃ puṣṭirapatyaṃ ca vṛṣatā cāsya jāyate ||
children.translated_text: and strength, nourishment, offspring, and virility arise for him.
He reaches old age only with difficulty, and he lives long, free from illness;
therefore a man should drink a properly reasoned purification at the proper time.
<s>Doṣa</s>s that have been subdued by fasting and digestive measures sometimes become aggravated again,

children.text: jitāḥ saṃśodhanairye tu na teṣāṃ punarudbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but for those subdued by purifications there is no further arising.

children.text: doṣāṇāṃ ca drumāṇāṃ ca mūle'nupahate sati
children.translated_text: When the root of <s>doṣa</s>s, like that of trees, remains unharmed,
the return of diseases, once gone, and of shoots, once cut, is certain.
After medicines have reduced the body, nourishment should be by wholesome foods,
combined with ghee, meat broth, milk, and pleasing soups,
with oil massage, rubbing, baths, non-unctuous enemas, and also unctuous enemas;

children.text: tathā sa labhate śarma yujyate cāyuṣā ciram ||
children.translated_text: in this way he obtains comfort and is joined with long life.
For those afflicted by over-application, drinking ghee is recommended,
or oil cooked with sweet substances, or else an unctuous enema.
But the person in whom there has been under-application should again be purified after unction,
with regard for dose, time, and strength, remembering the previous sequence.

children.text: snehane svedane śuddhau rogāḥ saṃsarjane ca ye
children.translated_text: The diseases that arise in unction, fomentation, purification,
and the post-purification dietary regimen, when the method has not been properly followed, are treated in the chapters on successful treatment.
Through inequality of causes, the bodily constituents become unequal;
through equality of causes, they become equal. Their natural cessation is constant.
There is a cause for the arising of entities; for their cessation there is no cause.
Some, even in that matter, suppose a cause: the non-continuance of the cause.
When the teacher had spoken this meaning, <s>Agniveśa</s> addressed him:
'If cessation is natural, what is the action of the provision for treatment?
Which unequal bodily constituents does the physician make equal by medicines?

children.text: kā vā cikitsā bhagavan kimarthaṃ vā prayujyate ||
children.translated_text: What, lord, is treatment, and for what purpose is it applied?'
Having heard that speech of his pupil, <s>Punarvasu</s> replied:
'Listen here, gentle one, to the reasoning seen by the great seers.
Because there is no cause of destruction, no cause that destroys entities
is known, just as no cause is known for the passing of time, which is ever moving.
As a thing that has come into being perishes through swift passage, so an entity comes to destruction;
there is no cause for its cessation, nor is there any making it otherwise.
Those actions by which the bodily constituents become balanced in the body

children.text: sā cikitsā vikārāṇāṃ karma tadbhiṣajāṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: are treatment for disorders; that is remembered as the work of physicians.

children.text: kathaṃ śarīre dhātūnāṃ vaiṣamyaṃ na bhavediti
children.translated_text: Action is undertaken so that inequality of the bodily constituents may not occur in the body,
and so that the continuity of those that are balanced may remain.
Through abandonment of unequal causes and through resorting to equal ones,
unequal constituents do not continue, and balanced bodily constituents arise.
Since by balanced causes one produces balanced bodily constituents,
the provision for treatment is therefore the giver of bodily happiness and life.
For <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>, and for this human world and the other,
the physician becomes the giver by giving bodily happiness and life.
Here are the verses:
The merit of the provision for treatment, and the defect that depends on what is other than it,
the signs of proper application, under-application, and over-application, with reference to purification,
the signs of one with many <s>doṣa</s>s, and the qualities of purification,
the mere principle of treatment, and its relation to successful treatment and complications,

children.text: yā ca yuktiścikitsāyāṃ yaṃ cārthaṃ kurute bhiṣak
children.translated_text: the reasoning in treatment, and the purpose that the physician accomplishes:
all this the sage declared in the chapter on the provision for treatment.
Now then, we shall explain the chapter called <s>Kiyantaḥśirasīya</s>, 'How Many in the Head.'
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: kiyantaḥ śirasi proktā rogā hṛdi ca dehinām
children.translated_text: How many diseases are stated to be in the head, and how many in the heart of embodied beings?
And how many diseases, from <s>anila</s> and the other <s>doṣa</s>s, are born of mental constructions?

children.text: kṣayāḥ kati samākhyātāḥ piḍakāḥ kati cānagha
children.translated_text: How many <s>kṣayas</s> (wasting conditions) are described, and how many pimples, O blameless one?
And how many kinds of movement of the <s>doṣas</s> are stated, O destroyer of <s>doṣas</s>?
Having heard the words of <s>Hutāśaveśa</s>, the teacher replied:

children.text: pṛṣṭavānasi yat saumya tanme śṛṇu savistaram ||
children.translated_text: What you have asked, gentle one, hear that from me in detail.
Five head diseases are observed, and likewise five disorders of the heart;
there are sixty-two diseases produced by variations in the measure of the <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: daśāṣṭau ca kṣayāḥ sapta piḍakā mādhumehikāḥ
children.translated_text: There are eighteen <s>kṣayas</s> and seven <s>mādhumehika</s> (diabetic) pimples;
and the movement of the <s>doṣas</s> is said to be threefold. Hear it in detail.
From suppressing urges, sleeping by day, staying awake at night, intoxication,
speaking loudly, dew, easterly wind, and excessive sexual intercourse;
from smelling unsuitable odors, from dust, smoke, cold, and sun-heat;
from taking heavy, sour, and green foods, and from using very cold water;
from injury to the head, corrupted undigested matter, weeping, and holding back tears;
from the coming of clouds, mental distress, and inversion of place and season;
<s>Vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣas</s> become aggravated in the head, and the blood is vitiated.
From that, diseases with various symptoms arise in the head.

children.text: prāṇāḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ yatra śritāḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Where the vital breaths of living beings and all the sense faculties are lodged,
that which is the highest limb among the limbs is called the head.

children.text: ardhāvabhedako vā syāt sarvaṃ vā rujyate śiraḥ
children.translated_text: There may be <s>ardhāvabhedaka</s> (one-sided splitting headache), or the whole head may hurt;
coryza, diseases of the mouth, nose, eyes, and ears, and dizziness of the head;
facial paralysis, trembling of the head, and seizure of the throat, nape, and jaw;
and various other diseases arise from <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣas</s>, and from worms.
But those five head disorders that were separately taught in the compendium by the great seers,
hear them from me, each with its own causes and symptoms.
From loud speech and excessive speech, from strong drink and staying awake,
from contact with cold wind, intercourse, and suppression of natural urges;
from fasting, injury, excessive purgation, and excessive vomiting;
from tears, grief, fear, terror, carrying burdens, too much walking, and emaciation;
the increased <s>vāyu</s>, entering the vessels located in the head, becomes aggravated.
Then, because of <s>vāta</s>, a great pain arises there.

children.text: nistudyete bhṛśaṃ śaṅkhau ghāṭā saṃbhidyate tathā
children.translated_text: The temples are pierced severely, and the back of the head seems to split apart;
the middle of the brows and the forehead burn, and there is extreme pain.
The ears are tormented with ringing, and the eyes seem as if they are being pulled out.

children.text: ghūrṇatīva śiraḥ sarvaṃ saṃdhibhya iva mucyate ||
children.translated_text: The whole head seems to whirl, as if it were being loosened from its joints.
The network of vessels throbs intensely, and the neck becomes stiff.
In a head disease of the <s>anila</s> (<s>vāta</s>) type, unctuous and warm treatment gives relief.
By pungent, sour, salty, and alkaline substances, by wine, anger, sunlight, and fire,
<s>pitta</s>, vitiated in the head, becomes the cause of head disease.

children.text: dahyate rujyate tena śiraḥ śītaṃ suṣūyate
children.translated_text: Because of it the head burns and hurts, and cold is strongly desired.

children.text: dahyete cakṣuṣī tṛṣṇā bhramaḥ svedaśca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: The eyes burn; thirst, dizziness, and sweating arise.
By comfort in sitting, comfort in sleep, and excessive heavy and unctuous eating,
<s>śleṣman</s> (<s>kapha</s>), vitiated in the head, becomes the cause of head disease.
Because of it, the head has dull pain and is numb, inert, and heavy.
Drowsiness arises, as do lassitude and loss of appetite.
In head disease caused by all three <s>doṣas</s>, pain, dizziness, and trembling come from <s>vāta</s>; burning, intoxication, and thirst from <s>pitta</s>;
and heaviness and drowsiness from <s>kapha</s>.
From sesame, milk, jaggery, undigested food, putrid food, and mixed foods,
morbid moisture arises in the blood, <s>kapha</s>, and flesh, together with the <s>doṣas</s>.
Then, from the dampness in the head, evil worms
come into being and generate a head disease with repulsive symptoms.
One should know a patient to be afflicted by a worm disease when he suffers from piercing and cutting pains, itching, swelling, foulness, and distress,
and also from the sight of the worms.
By grief, fasting, exercise, and rough, dry, scanty food,
<s>vāyu</s>, entering the heart, produces the highest degree of pain.
Trembling, constriction, rigidity, stupor, emptiness, and fear
are the features in one whose heart is afflicted by <s>vāta</s>; and when food is digested, the pain is extremely severe.
By hot, sour, salty, alkaline, pungent, and undigested foods,
and by wine, anger, and sunlight, <s>pitta</s> is quickly aggravated in the heart.
Burning in the heart, bitterness in the mouth, bitter and sour eructation, and fatigue,
thirst, fainting, dizziness, and sweating characterize <s>pitta</s>-type heart disease.
Overeating heavy and unctuous food, lack of thought, inactivity,
and excessive pleasure in sleep are the causes of <s>kapha</s>-type heart disease.
In <s>kapha</s>-type heart disease the heart is numb, inert, and heavy.
For one overcome by drowsiness and aversion to food, it is as if covered by a stone.
Because of the combination of causes and symptoms, it is called <s>sānnipātika</s>.

children.text: tridoṣaje tu hṛdroge yo durātmā niṣevate ||
children.translated_text: But in heart disease caused by all three <s>doṣas</s>, if a corrupt man consumes
sesame, milk, jaggery, and the like, a knot develops in him.
And his nutritive fluid reaches morbid dampness in one part of the vital organ.
From that dampness worms arise in this damaged person.

children.text: marmaikadeśe te jātāḥ sarpanto bhakṣayanti ca ||
children.translated_text: Born in one part of the vital organ, they crawl and devour it.
He thinks his heart is being pierced as if by needles,
and cut as if by knives, with itching and great pain.
Having recognized worm-born heart disease by these signs as extremely terrible,

children.text: tvareta jetuṃ taṃ vidvān vikāraṃ śīghrakāriṇam ||
children.translated_text: the wise man should hasten to overcome that disorder, for it acts quickly.
With two predominant or one predominant <s>doṣa</s> there are six forms; and with lesser, middling, and greater degrees there are six more.
With the <s>doṣas</s> equal there is one; thus those <s>sannipāta</s> disorders are thirteen.

children.text: saṃsarge nava ṣaṭ tebhya ekavṛddhyā samaistrayaḥ
children.translated_text: In <s>saṃsarga</s> (combined disorder) there are nine: from them, by single increase, six, and with equal <s>doṣas</s>, three.
And there are three separate ones; together with those in which the <s>doṣas</s> are increased, the diseases number twenty-five.
Just as there are twenty-five conditions when the <s>doṣas</s> are increased, so also when they are depleted,
another variation caused by increase and decrease will now be taught.
The increase of one, the normal state of one, and the depletion of one;
the increase of two together and the depletion of one; the increase of one and the depletion of two:

children.text: prakṛtisthaṃ yadā pittaṃ mārutaḥ śleṣmaṇaḥ kṣaye
children.translated_text: when <s>pitta</s> remains in its natural state and, as <s>śleṣman</s> is depleted, <s>māruta</s> (vāta),
taking it from its place, spreads through the limbs here and there,
then piercing pain and burning, unstable from place to place,
arise in the regions of his body, and also fatigue and weakness.

children.text: prakṛtisthaṃ kaphaṃ vāyuḥ kṣīṇe pitte yadā balī
children.translated_text: Or when <s>pitta</s> is depleted and strong <s>vāyu</s>
drags <s>kapha</s>, though it is in its natural state, then it produces pain, with coldness, stiffness, and heaviness.
When, through the complete depletion of <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>
obstructs <s>anila</s> (vāta) that is in its natural condition, then burning and pain arise in him.

children.text: śleṣmāṇaṃ hi samaṃ pittaṃ yadā vātaparikṣaye
children.translated_text: When, through the complete depletion of <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>
obstructs <s>śleṣman</s> which is normal, then it produces fever with drowsiness and heaviness.

children.text: pravṛddho hi yadā śleṣmā pitte kṣīṇe samīraṇam
children.translated_text: When greatly increased <s>śleṣman</s>, while <s>pitta</s> is depleted,
obstructs <s>samīraṇa</s> (vāta), then it produces chill, heaviness, and pain.
When <s>samīraṇa</s> is completely depleted, <s>kapha</s>
obstructing <s>pitta</s> that has gone to a normal state, produces weak digestive fire and heaviness in the head,

children.text: nidrāṃ tandrām pralāpaṃ ca hṛdrogaṃ gātragauravam
children.translated_text: sleep, drowsiness, delirious speech, heart disease, and heaviness of the limbs,
yellowness of the nails and the like, and spitting caused by <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
When <s>śleṣman</s>, together with <s>pitta</s>, moves in a person whose <s>vāta</s> is deficient,
it causes anorexia, indigestion, prostration, and heaviness as well,
nausea, salivation from the mouth, pallor, burning distress, and intoxication,
as well as irregularity of purgation and irregularity of digestive fire.
But in one whose <s>pitta</s> is deficient, <s>śleṣman</s>, associated with <s>māruta</s> (vāta),

children.text: stambhaṃ śaityaṃ ca todaṃ ca janayatyanavasthitam ||
children.translated_text: generates shifting stiffness, coldness, and pricking pain,
heaviness, mildness of digestive fire, lack of desire for food, trembling,
whiteness of the nails and the like, and roughness of the body.

children.text: mārutastu kaphe hīne pittaṃ ca kupitaṃ dvayam
children.translated_text: When <s>kapha</s> is deficient, <s>māruta</s> and aggravated <s>pitta</s>, the two together,

children.text: karoti yāni liṅgāni śṛṇu tāni samāsataḥ ||
children.translated_text: produce the signs which I shall tell you briefly.
Dizziness, twisting pain, pricking pain, burning, cracking, tremor,
aching of the limbs, extreme drying, burning distress, and heat:
when <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> are depleted, <s>śleṣman</s>, strongly blocking the channels,

children.text: ceṣṭāpraṇāśaṃ mūrcchāṃ ca vāksaṅgaṃ ca karoti hi ||
children.translated_text: causes loss of movement, fainting, and obstruction of speech.
When <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> are depleted, <s>pitta</s> moves, causing the body's <s>ojas</s> to slip away,
and produces lassitude, weakness of the senses, thirst, fainting, and loss of activity.
When <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> are depleted, <s>vāyu</s>, excessively pressing the vital points,
destroys consciousness, or else makes the person tremble.

children.text: doṣāḥ pravṛddhāḥ svaṃ liṅgaṃ darśayanti yathābalam
children.translated_text: Increased <s>doṣas</s> display their own signs according to their strength;

children.text: kṣīṇā jahati liṅgaṃ svaṃ samāḥ svaṃ karma kurvate ||
children.translated_text: depleted ones abandon their own signs; those in balance perform their own function.
Of <s>vāta</s> and the others, of rasa and the other tissues, of the wastes, and likewise of <s>ojas</s>,
the depletions are as follows; among them, the symptoms of depleted <s>anila</s> and the others have been stated.
The heart is jarred, it cannot bear sound, it does not run loudly, and it is pained;
the heart faints even with slight exertion when rasa is depleted.
When blood is depleted, the skin is rough, cracked, faded, and dry;
when flesh is depleted, there is especially dryness of the buttocks, neck, and abdomen.

children.text: sandhīnāṃ sphuṭanaṃ glānir akṣṇor āyāsa eva ca
children.translated_text: Cracking of the joints, lassitude, and fatigue of the eyes

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ medasi kṣīṇe tanutvaṃ codarasya ca ||
children.translated_text: are the signs when fat is depleted, along with thinness of the abdomen.
Falling of the hair, body hair, nails, beard, and teeth, and fatigue
should be known as signs when bone is depleted, as well as looseness of the joints.

children.text: śīryanta iva cāsthīni durbalāni laghūni ca
children.translated_text: When marrow is depleted in embodied beings, the bones seem to crumble,
and become weak, light, and constantly afflicted by disorders of <s>vāta</s>.
Weakness, dryness of the mouth, pallor, prostration, fatigue,
impotence, and non-emission of semen are the symptoms of depleted semen.
When feces are depleted, <s>māruta</s>, as if pressing the intestines,
raises the abdomen of the dry person and moves sideways and upward.
When urine is depleted there is painful urination and discoloration of the urine;

children.text: pipāsā bādhate cāsya mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati ||
children.translated_text: thirst afflicts him, and his mouth dries up completely.

children.text: malāyanāni cānyāni śūnyāni ca laghūni ca
children.translated_text: When the other channels of waste are depleted, they are observed, each according to its own nature,
to be empty, light, and dried out.
When <s>ojas</s> is depleted, he is weak and often fearful, brooding, with disturbed senses,
of bad complexion, dejected, dry, and emaciated.
That pure blood, slightly tinged with yellow, which remains in the heart
is reckoned as <s>ojas</s> in the body; by its destruction one does not continue to live.
For <s>ojas</s> arises first in this body of embodied beings;
it is produced with the color of ghee, a sweet taste, and the scent of parched grain.
Exercise, fasting, anxiety, dry, scanty, and measured food,
wind and sun, fear, grief, dry drink, and keeping awake;
excessive discharge of <s>kapha</s>, blood, semen, and wastes,
time and injury by beings should be known as causes of depletion.
For those who eat in excess heavy, unctuous, sour, and salty things,

children.text: navamannaṃ ca pānaṃ ca nidrām āsyāsukhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: new grain and drink, and who indulge in sleep and the comforts of sitting at ease,
who have abandoned exercise and worry and do not perform purificatory therapy,

children.text: śleṣmā pittaṃ ca medaśca māṃsaṃ cātipravardhate ||
children.translated_text: <s>śleṣman</s>, <s>pitta</s>, fat, and flesh become excessively increased.
When <s>vāyu</s>, its movement obstructed by them, takes hold of <s>ojas</s> and goes

children.text: yadā bastiṃ tadā kṛcchro madhumehaḥ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: to the bladder, then difficult <s>madhumeha</s> begins.

children.text: sa mārutasya pittasya kaphasya ca muhurmuhuḥ
children.translated_text: It repeatedly displays the form of <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>;
after passing into wasting, it becomes filled out again.
Through neglect, seven terrible <s>piḍakā</s> lesions arise in him,
in fleshy spaces, in vital spots, and also in the joints.
They are <s>śarāvikā</s>, <s>kacchapikā</s>, <s>jālinī</s>, and likewise <s>sarṣapī</s>,

children.text: alajī vinatākhyā ca vidradhī ceti saptamī ||
children.translated_text: <s>alajī</s>, the one called <s>vinatā</s>, and <s>vidradhī</s> as the seventh.
Raised at the edges, depressed in the middle, dark, and accompanied by moisture and pain,
the <s>śarāvikā</s> is a lesion situated in the shape of a shallow dish.
With deep pain and stabbing, occupying a large site,
smooth and resembling the back of a tortoise, the lesion is regarded as <s>kacchapī</s>.
Rigid, furnished with a net of veins, with oily discharge, and having a large seat,
abounding in pain and stabbing and having tiny openings, it is <s>jālinī</s>.
A lesion that is not very large, ripens quickly, and has great pain
is <s>sarṣapī</s>, covered with lesions resembling mustard seeds.
At its arising it burns the skin and produces thirst, delusion, and fever;
creeping continually and painful, <s>alajī</s> burns like fire.
With deep pain and moisture, whether on the back or even on the abdomen,

children.text: mahatī vinatā nīlā piḍakā vinatā matā ||
children.translated_text: large, bent down, and blue-black, the lesion is considered <s>vinatā</s>.

children.text: vidradhiṃ dvividhām āhur bāhyām ābhyantarīṃ tathā
children.translated_text: They say that <s>vidradhi</s> (abscess) is of two kinds, external and internal.
The external one arises from skin, sinew, and flesh, resembles a tendon, and is very painful.
From cold food, burning-hot food, dry food, desiccated food, and excessive eating,
from incompatible, undigested, polluted, irregular, and unsuitable food,
from corrupted and excessive liquor, suppression of urges, and fatigue,
from improper exercise or lying down, excessive carrying of loads, travel, and sexual intercourse,
when the impurities enter the flesh and blood inside the body,
then a very terrible swelling arises, situated deep within.

children.text: hṛdaye klomni yakṛti plīhni kukṣau ca vṛkkayoḥ
children.translated_text: In the heart, kloman, liver, spleen, abdomen, kidneys,
navel, groins, or bladder, it has intense pain.
Because of the excessive amount of vitiated blood, it quickly suppurates;
therefore, from its rapid suppuration, it is called <s>vidradhī</s>.
One knows the <s>vātika</s> type by piercing, cutting, dizziness, distension, sound, throbbing, and creeping sensations;
the <s>paittika</s> type by thirst, burning, delusion, intoxication, and fever;
and the <s>śleṣmika</s> type by yawning, nausea, loss of appetite, stiffness, and chills.
In all <s>vidradhi</s> abscesses, great colic-like pain arises.
It is as though being split by knives and missiles, and as though being burned by firebrands;
when the abscess has reached a sharp corrosive state, it is as though being bitten by scorpions.
The <s>vāta</s>-type abscess discharges a thin, dry, reddish, dark, frothy fluid;
the <s>pitta</s>-type abscess discharges fluid resembling water from sesame, black gram, or horse gram.

children.text: ślaiṣmikī sravati śvetaṃ picchilaṃ bahalaṃ bahu
children.translated_text: The <s>śleṣmika</s> type discharges white, slimy, thick, abundant fluid;
the <s>sānnipātika</s> type partakes of all these signs together.

children.text: athāsāṃ vidradhīnāṃ sādhyāsādhyatvaviśeṣajñānārthaṃ sthānakṛtaṃ liṅgaviśeṣamupadekṣyāmaḥ tatra pradhānamarmajāyāṃ vidradhyāṃ hṛdghaṭṭanatamakapramohakāsaśvāsāḥ klomajāyāṃ pipāsāmukhaśoṣagalagrahāḥ yakṛjjāyāṃ śvāsaḥ plīhajāyāmucchvāsoparodhaḥ kukṣijāyāṃ kukṣipārśvāntarāṃsaśūlaṃ vṛkkajāyāṃ pṛṣṭhakaṭigrahaḥ nābhijāyāṃ hikkā vaṅkṣaṇajāyāṃ sakthisādaḥ bastijāyāṃ kṛcchrapūtimūtravarcastvaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: Now, in order to know the specific distinction between curability and incurability among these abscesses, we shall teach the particular signs caused by location. In an abscess arising in a principal vital spot there are heart-striking pain, asthmatic oppression, fainting, cough, and dyspnea; in one arising in the kloman there are thirst, dryness of the mouth, and constriction of the throat; in one arising in the liver, dyspnea; in one arising in the spleen, obstruction of breathing out; in one arising in the abdomen, pain in the abdomen, flanks, inner region, and shoulders; in one arising in the kidneys, stiffness of the back and waist; in one arising in the navel, hiccup; in one arising in the groin, weakness of the thighs; and in one arising in the bladder, difficult, foul urine and feces.

children.text: pakvaprabhinnāsūrdhvajāsu mukhāt srāvaḥ sravati adhojāsu gudāt ubhayatastu nābhijāsu ||
children.translated_text: When they have ripened and burst, in upward abscesses discharge flows from the mouth, in downward ones from the anus, and in navel-born ones from both.

children.text: āsāṃ hṛnnābhibastijāḥ paripakvāḥ sānnipātikī ca maraṇāya śeṣāḥ punaḥ kuśalam āśupratikāriṇaṃ cikitsakamāsādyopaśāmyanti
children.translated_text: Among these, those arising in the heart, navel, and bladder, once fully ripened, and the <s>sānnipātika</s> type lead to death; the rest subside if they obtain a skilled physician who acts quickly.

children.text: tasmādacirotthitāṃ vidradhīṃ śastrasarpavidyudagnitulyāṃ snehavirecanairāśvevopakramet sarvaśo gulmavacceti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore a newly arisen <s>vidradhi</s>, comparable to a knife, snake, lightning, or fire, should be treated very quickly in every way with oleation and purgation, as in the case of <s>gulma</s>.
And here there are verses:
Even without <s>prameha</s>, these arise in persons whose fat is vitiated;
and they are not recognized until they have occupied their site.
<s>Śarāvikā</s>, <s>kacchapikā</s>, and <s>jālinī</s> are hard to endure;
for they arise with great strength in those with abundant <s>śleṣman</s> and fat.

children.text: sarṣapī cālajī caiva vinatā vidradhī ca yāḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>sarṣapī</s>, <s>alajī</s>, <s>vinatā</s>, and <s>vidradhī</s>
are curable; they are dominated by <s>pitta</s> and occur in those with little fat.

children.text: marmasvaṃse gude pāṇyoḥ stane sandhiṣu pādayoḥ
children.translated_text: When lesions arise in a diabetic patient in the vital spots, the shoulder, the anus, the hands, the breast, the joints, or the feet,

children.text: jāyante yasya piḍakāḥ sa pramehī na jīvati ||
children.translated_text: that person with <s>prameha</s> does not live.
There are also other lesions, red, yellow, black, and reddish-brown,
pale, pallid in color, ash-like, and having a dark luster;
some are soft and others hard, some large and others small,
some slow in force and others violent, some with little pain and others with great pain.
Recognizing them according to the respective causes and signs of <s>māruta</s> and the other <s>doṣas</s>,
one should diagnose them and treat them quickly, before complications appear.
Thirst, dyspnea, putrefaction of the flesh, delusion, hiccup, intoxication, fever,
spreading inflammation, and obstruction of vital spots are the complications of the lesions.

children.text: kṣayaḥ sthānaṃ ca vṛddhiśca doṣāṇāṃ trividhā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: Decrease, remaining in place, and increase are the threefold course of the <s>doṣas</s>;
and another threefold course is to be known as upward, downward, and sideways.
A further threefold course is in the bowel, the branches, and the vital spots, bones, and joints;
thus the threefold course of the <s>doṣas</s> has been stated according to distinctions of rule.
Accumulation, provocation, and pacification of <s>pitta</s> and the others, in due order,
occur one by one in the six seasons beginning with the rainy season.
This course, beginning with accumulation and so on, is again said to be produced by time.

children.text: gatiśca dvividhā dṛṣṭā prākṛtī vaikṛtī ca yā ||
children.translated_text: And that course is seen to be twofold: natural and pathological.
The digestive cooking by heat in human beings arises from <s>pitta</s> alone.

children.text: tacca pittaṃ prakupitaṃ vikārān kurute bahūn ||
children.translated_text: And that <s>pitta</s>, when aggravated, produces many disorders.

children.text: prākṛtastu balaṃ śleṣmā vikṛto mala ucyate
children.translated_text: In its normal state <s>śleṣman</s> is strength; when altered, it is called a waste product.

children.text: sa caivaujaḥ smṛtaḥ kāye sa ca pāpmopadiśyate ||
children.translated_text: That very same thing is remembered as <s>ojas</s> in the body, and it is also taught as an evil when corrupted.

children.text: sarvā hi ceṣṭā vātena sa prāṇaḥ prāṇināṃ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: For every activity is due to <s>vāta</s>; it is remembered as the life-breath of living beings.
By it diseases arise, and by it life itself is obstructed.
Considering himself as always having an enemy close at hand, the self-possessed man,
always attentive, should care for himself if he desires unfailing life.
On this there are two verses.
Diseases of the head, together with diseases of the heart, diseases arising from mental formations,
wasting conditions with eruptions, and the movement of the <s>doṣas</s> have been stated.
In this chapter called Kiyantaḥśirasīya, for the sake of knowledge,
they have been taught by the truth-seeing physician who desires the welfare of people.
Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter on the three kinds of swelling.
Thus spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: trayaḥ śothā bhavanti vātapittaśleṣmanimittāḥ te punardvividhā nijāgantubhedena ||
children.translated_text: There are three swellings, caused by <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s>; again, they are twofold by the distinction between endogenous and exogenous.

children.text: tatrāgantavaś chedanabhedanakṣaṇanabhañjanapicchanotpeṣaṇaprahāravadhabandhanaveṣṭanavyadhanapīḍanādibhir vā bhallātakapuṣpaphalarasātmaguptāśūkakrimiśūkāhitapatralatāgulmasaṃsparśanair vā svedanaparisarpaṇāvamūtraṇairvā viṣiṇāṃ saviṣaprāṇidaṃṣṭrādantaviṣāṇanakhanipātair vā sāgaraviṣavātahimadahanasaṃsparśanairvā śothāḥ samupajāyante ||
children.translated_text: Among them, exogenous swellings arise from cutting, splitting, wounding, breaking, crushing, pounding, blows, injury, binding, wrapping, piercing, pressure, and the like; or from contact with the flowers, fruits, or sap of <s>bhallātaka</s>, with <s>ātmagupta</s> pods, insect bristles, and harmful leaves, creepers, and shrubs; or from the sweat, crawling, or urination of poisonous creatures; or from the fall of poisonous fangs, teeth, horns, or nails of venomous animals; or from contact with sea-poison, wind, cold, or fire.

children.text: te punaryathāsvaṃ hetuvyañjanair ādāvupalabhyante nijavyañjanaikadeśaviparītaiḥ bandham antrāgadapralepapratāpanirvāpaṇādibhiś copakramair upakramyamāṇāḥ praśāntimāpadyante ||
children.translated_text: These are first recognized by their respective causes and signs, by symptoms partly contrary to those of endogenous swellings, and, when treated with measures such as bandaging, internal antidotes, poultices, heating, and cooling, they become pacified.

children.text: nijāḥ punaḥ snehasvedavamanavirecanāsthāpanānuvāsanaśirovirecanānām ayathāvatprayogānmithyāsaṃsarjanād vā chardyalasakavisūcikāśvāsakāsātisāraśoṣapāṇḍurogodarajvarapradarabhagandarārśovikārātikarśanairvā kuṣṭhakaṇḍūpiḍakādibhirvā chardikṣavathūdgāraśukravātamūtrapurīṣavegadhāraṇairvā karmarogopavāsādhvakarśitasya vā sahasātigurvamlalavaṇapiṣṭānnaphalaśākarāgadadhiharitakamadyamandakavirūḍhanavaśūkaśamīdhānyānūpaudakapiśitopayogān mṛtpaṅkaloṣṭabhakṣaṇāllavaṇātibhakṣaṇād garbhasampīḍanād āmagarbhaprapatanāt prajātānāṃ ca mithyopacārād udīrṇadoṣatvācca śophāḥ prādurbhavanti ityuktaḥ sāmānyo hetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Endogenous swellings, however, appear from improper use of oleation, sweating, emesis, purgation, evacuative enema, unctuous enema, and head-cleansing; from faulty convalescent diet; from excessive emaciation through vomiting, <s>alasaka</s>, <s>visūcikā</s>, dyspnea, cough, diarrhea, consumption, anemia, abdominal disease, fever, gynecological discharge, fistula, piles, and disorders; from skin disease, itching, eruptions, and the like; from suppressing the urges to vomit, sneeze, belch, and pass semen, flatus, urine, or feces; or, in one emaciated by work, illness, fasting, or travel, from sudden excessive use of very heavy, sour, salty, flour-based foods, fruits, vegetables, relishes, curds, greens, wine, thin gruel, sprouts, fresh awned and leguminous grains, and the meat of marsh and aquatic animals; from eating earth, mud, and clods; from excessive eating of salt; from compression of the fetus, miscarriage of an immature fetus, wrong care of women after delivery, and from the <s>doṣas</s> being aroused. This has been stated as the general cause.

children.text: ayaṃ tvatra viśeṣaḥ śītarūkṣalaghuviśadaśramopavāsātikarśanakṣapaṇādibhir vāyuḥ prakupitastvaṅmāṃsaśoṇitādīnyabhibhūya śophaṃ janayati sa kṣiprotthānapraśamo bhavati tathā śyāmāruṇavarṇaḥ prakṛtivarṇo vā calaḥ spandanaḥ kharaparuṣabhinnatvagromā chidyata iva bhidyata iva pīḍyata iva sūcībhiriva tudyata iva pipīlikābhiriva saṃsṛpyate sarṣapakalkāvalipta iva cimicimāyate saṃkucyata āyamyata iveti vātaśothaḥ
children.translated_text: Here is the specific distinction: <s>vāyu</s>, aggravated by cold, dry, light, and clear things, by exertion, fasting, excessive emaciation, depletion, and the like, overwhelms the skin, flesh, blood, and so on and produces swelling. It arises and subsides quickly; it is dark, reddish, or of the natural color, mobile, throbbing, with rough, harsh, and cracked skin and hair; it feels as if it is being cut, split, pressed, pricked with needles, crawled over by ants, smeared with mustard paste, tingling, contracted, or stretched. This is <s>vāta</s>-swelling.

children.text: uṣṇatīkṣṇakaṭukakṣāralavaṇāmlājīrṇabhojanair agnyātapapratāpaiśca pittaṃ prakupitaṃ tvaṅmāṃsaśoṇitānyabhibhūya śothaṃ janayati sa kṣiprotthānapraśamo bhavati kṛṣṇapītanīlatāmrāvabhāsa uṣṇo mṛduḥ kapilatāmraromā uṣyate dūyate dhūpyate ūṣmāyate svidyate klidyate na ca sparśamuṣṇaṃ ca suṣūyata iti pittaśothaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Pitta</s>, aggravated by hot, sharp, pungent, alkaline, salty, sour, and undigested foods and by the heat of fire and sun, overwhelms the skin, flesh, and blood and produces swelling. It arises and subsides quickly; it has a black, yellow, blue, or coppery appearance, is hot and soft, with tawny or coppery hair; it burns, aches, smokes, gives off heat, sweats, becomes moist, does not tolerate touch, and suppurates with heat. This is <s>pitta</s>-swelling.

children.text: gurumadhuraśītasnigdhair atisvapnāvyāyāmādibhiśca śleṣmā prakupitastvaṅmāṃsaśoṇitādīnyabhibhūya śothaṃ janayati sa kṛcchrotthānapraśamo bhavati pāṇḍuśvetāvabhāso guruḥ snigdhaḥ ślakṣṇaḥ sthiraḥ styānaḥ śuklāgraromā sparśoṣṇasahaśceti śleṣmaśothaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣman</s>, aggravated by heavy, sweet, cold, and unctuous things, by excessive sleep, lack of exercise, and the like, overwhelms the skin, flesh, blood, and so on and produces swelling. It arises and subsides with difficulty; it appears pale or white, is heavy, unctuous, smooth, fixed, compact, with white-tipped hairs, and tolerates warm touch. This is <s>śleṣma</s>-swelling.

children.text: yathāsvakāraṇākṛtisaṃsargāddvidoṣajāstrayaḥ śothā bhavanti yathāsvakāraṇākṛtisannipātāt sānnipātika ekaḥ evaṃ saptavidho bhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From the combination of the respective causes and forms, there are three swellings produced by two <s>doṣas</s>; from the concurrence of the respective causes and forms, there is one <s>sānnipātika</s> swelling. Thus the division is sevenfold.

children.text: prakṛtibhistābhistābhir bhidyamāno dvividhastrividhaścaturvidhā saptavidho 'ṣṭavidhaśca śotha upalabhyate punaścaika evotsedhasāmānyāt ||
children.translated_text: When differentiated by those various natures, swelling is observed as twofold, threefold, fourfold, sevenfold, and eightfold; again, because of the common feature of elevation, it is only one.
And here there are verses:

children.text: śūyante yasya gātrāṇi svapantīva rujanti ca
children.translated_text: When a person's limbs swell, feel as if asleep, and hurt,
and when pressed quickly rise again, one should identify that as <s>vāta</s>-swelling.
And a swelling that has a reddish color and disappears at night,

children.text: snehoṣṇamardanābhyāṃ ca praṇaśyet sa ca vātikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and disappears with oleation, heat, and massage, is also <s>vātika</s>.
A swelling of one afflicted by thirst and fever, which aches and burns,

children.text: svidyati klidyate gandhī sa paittaḥ śvayathuḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: which sweats, becomes moist, and has an odor, is remembered as a <s>paitta</s> swelling.
That in which the eyes, face, and skin are yellow, and which first swells from the middle...

children.text: tanutvak cātisārī ca pittaśothaḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Thinness of the skin and diarrhea: that is called a swelling due to <s>pitta</s>.
But a swelling that is cold, whose movement is impeded, itchy, and pale,
and which, when pressed down, does not rise up, is a swelling whose nature is <s>kapha</s>.
When, from a cut made by a knife or by kuśa grass, blood does not flow

children.text: kṛcchreṇa picchā sravati sa cāpi kaphasaṃbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but a slimy fluid oozes with difficulty, that also is produced from <s>kapha</s>.
From a combination of causes and forms a swelling may be due to two <s>doṣas</s>;
from the conjunction of all, a swelling has all forms and has mixed causes.
The swelling which, having arisen from the feet, spreads to the whole body

children.text: jantoḥ sa ca sukaṣṭaḥ syāt prasṛtaḥ strīmukhācca yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: of a creature is very difficult, as is that which has spread from a woman's face.

children.text: yaścāpi guhyaprabhavaḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā
children.translated_text: And that which arises from the private parts, whether of a woman or a man,

children.text: sa ca kaṣṭatamo jñeyo yasya ca syurupadravāḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be known as the most difficult, as also that which has complications.
Vomiting, dyspnea, anorexia, thirst, fever, and diarrhea:
this group of seven, together with constant weakness, is the collection of complications of swelling.
When aggravated <s>śleṣman</s> settles at the root of a person's tongue,
it quickly produces swelling, and an <s>upajihvikā</s> arises in him.
When aggravated <s>śleṣman</s> settles in the <s>kākala</s>,
it quickly produces swelling and creates <s>galaśuṇḍikā</s>.
When aggravated <s>śleṣman</s> settles outside the throat,
it slowly produces swelling, and <s>galagaṇḍa</s> arises in him.
When aggravated <s>śleṣman</s> stands firmly inside the throat,
it quickly produces swelling, and <s>galagraha</s> arises in him.

children.text: yasya pittaṃ prakupitaṃ saraktaṃ tvaci sarpati
children.translated_text: When aggravated <s>pitta</s>, together with blood, creeps through the skin,
it produces swelling accompanied by redness, and <s>visarpa</s> arises in him.
When aggravated <s>pitta</s> settles in the skin and blood,

children.text: śothaṃ sarāgaṃ janayet piḍakā tasya jāyate ||
children.translated_text: it produces swelling accompanied by redness, and eruptions arise in him.

children.text: yasya prakupitaṃ pittaṃ śoṇitaṃ prāpya śuṣyati
children.translated_text: When aggravated <s>pitta</s>, having reached the blood, dries up,

children.text: tilakā piplavo vyaṅgā nīlikā tasya jāyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>tilakā</s>, <s>piplava</s>, <s>vyaṅga</s>, and <s>nīlikā</s> arise in him.
When aggravated <s>pitta</s> settles at the temples,
a dreadful swelling called <s>śaṅkhaka</s> arises in him.
When aggravated <s>pitta</s> settles at the root of the ear,
after fever a swelling arises in him, hard to conquer and leading to death.
When aggravated <s>vāta</s>, having distended the spleen, remains there,
the spleen increases in him, slowly pricking the side.
When aggravated <s>vāyu</s> settles in the place of <s>gulma</s>,
it produces swelling with pain, and <s>gulma</s> arises in him.
When aggravated <s>vāyu</s>, moving about and causing swelling and pain,
goes from the groin to the testicles, <s>vṛddhi</s> arises in him.
When aggravated <s>vāta</s> has taken refuge between the skin and flesh,
it produces swelling in the abdomen, and <s>udara</s> arises in him.
When aggravated <s>vāta</s> takes refuge in the abdomen and remains there,
going neither downward nor upward, <s>ānāha</s> arises in him.
Diseases such as <s>adhimāṃsa</s>, <s>arbuda</s>, and the rest, because of their common feature of elevation,
are to be specified in the collection of swellings, though distinguished by name and form.
When the three, <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>, are aggravated simultaneously
and settle at the root of the tongue, burning and raised up,
they produce severe swelling and pains of various kinds;
one should designate that disease, which acts quickly, as <s>rohiṇī</s>.
For that creature, life lasts at most three nights,
but when it is treated by a skilled physician, he quickly becomes well.
There are indeed such diseases, regarded as dreadful, which are curable,

children.text: ye hanyur anupakrāntā mithyācāreṇa vā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but which kill if not treated, or again if treated by a wrong regimen.
And there are other diseases, regarded as mild, which are curable,
in which treatment, whether done with effort or without effort, succeeds without doubt.
And there are other incurable diseases, called manageable,

children.text: susādhvapi kṛtaṃ yeṣu karma yātrākaraṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: in which even treatment performed very well only supports the course of life.

children.text: santi cāpyapare rogā yeṣu karma na sidhyati
children.translated_text: And there are still other diseases in which treatment does not succeed;
even if fools undertake treatment with effort, a learned physician should not treat them.
Diseases are remembered as of two kinds, curable and incurable;
by the division into mild and dreadful, they become fourfold.
And those very diseases become innumerable as they are divided
by pain, color, origin, site, configuration, and names.
Their determination is made as a summary according to broad categories;
in the same way, the common nature of the constitutions is taught among disorders.
One who is not skilled in the names of disorders should never be ashamed,

children.text: na hi sarvavikārāṇāṃ nāmato 'sti dhruvā sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for there is no fixed establishment of all disorders by name.
The very same aggravated <s>doṣa</s>, because of a specific mode of arising,
and because it has gone to another site, produces many diseases.
Therefore, after understanding the natures of disorders, the different seats,
and the specific modes of arising, one should undertake treatment.
For the physician who, knowing this triad, begins treatments

children.text: jñānapūrvaṃ yathānyāyaṃ sa karmasu na muhyati ||
children.translated_text: with prior knowledge and according to rule, is not bewildered in his actions.
The three, <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>, are always present in the bodies of living beings;

children.text: vikṛtāḥ prakṛtisthā vā tān bubhutseta paṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether disturbed or standing in their natural state, the wise person should seek to understand them.
Exertion, inhalation, exhalation, activity, the movement of tissues, and regularity,
and the proper release of things that move are the actions of <s>vāyu</s> when it is not disordered.
Vision, digestion, heat, hunger, thirst, and softness of the body
Luster, clarity, and intelligence are normal functions of <s>pitta</s>, not born of disorder.

children.text: sneho bandhaḥ sthiratvaṃ ca gauravaṃ vṛṣatā balam
children.translated_text: Unctuousness, binding, steadiness, heaviness, virility, and strength,
forbearance, firmness, and freedom from greed are normal functions of <s>kapha</s>, not born of disorder.

children.text: vāte pitte kaphe caiva kṣīṇe lakṣaṇamucyate
children.translated_text: Now the symptoms when <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s> are depleted are stated:
there is loss of their natural activity, or increase of contrary factors.
The specific nature of the <s>doṣa</s> is the fixed sign of increase;
in this way the nature, depletion, and increase of the <s>doṣas</s> are to be examined.
There are these verses:

children.text: saṃkhyāṃ nimittaṃ rūpāṇi śothānāṃ sādhyatāṃ na ca
children.translated_text: The number, cause, forms, and curability or incurability of swellings,
the particular swellings belonging to each disorder, and those arising beforehand,
the distinctions in method for disorders, and the threefold concise teaching to be understood,
as well as the natural function of the <s>doṣas</s> and the symptoms in their depletion and increase:
<s>Punarvasu</s>, free from delusion, passion, faulty greed, pride, intoxication, and longing,
explained these in the chapter on diseases called Triśothīya.
Now, then, we shall expound the chapter called Aṣṭodarīya.
Thus spoke the Blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: iha khalvaṣṭāvudarāṇi aṣṭau mūtrāghātaḥ aṣṭau kṣīradoṣāḥ aṣṭau retodoṣāḥ sapta kuṣṭhāni sapta piḍakāḥ sapta visarpāḥ ṣaḍatīsārāḥ ṣaḍudāvartāḥ pañca gulmāḥ pañca plīhadoṣāḥ pañca kāsāḥ pañca śvāsāḥ pañca hikkāḥ pañca tṛṣṇāḥ pañca chardayaḥ pañca bhaktasyānaśanasthānāni pañca śirorogāḥ pañca hṛdrogāḥ pañca pāṇḍurogāḥ pañconmādāḥ catvāro 'pasmārāḥ catvāro 'kṣirogāḥ catvāraḥ karṇarogāḥ catvāraḥ pratiśyāyāḥ catvāro mukharogāḥ catvāro grahaṇīdoṣāḥ catvāro madāḥ catvāro mūrcchāyāḥ catvāraḥ śoṣāḥ catvāri klaibyāni trayaḥ śophāḥ trīṇi kilāsāni trividhaṃ lohitapittaṃ dvau jvarau dvau vraṇau dvāvāyāmau dve gṛdhrasyau dve kāmale dvividham āmaṃ dvividhaṃ vātaraktaṃ dvividhānyarśāṃsi eka ūrustambhaḥ ekaḥ saṃnyāsaḥ eko mahāgadaḥ viṃśatiḥ krimijātayaḥ viṃśatiḥ pramehāḥ viṃśatiryonivyāpadaḥ ityaṣṭacatvāriṃśadrogādhikaraṇānyasmin saṃgrahe samuddiṣṭāni ||
children.translated_text: Here, indeed, eight abdominal diseases, eight forms of urinary obstruction, eight defects of milk, eight defects of semen, seven kinds of skin disease, seven pustules, seven spreading eruptions, six diarrheas, six upward movements, five <s>gulmas</s>, five disorders of the spleen, five coughs, five dyspneas, five hiccups, five thirsts, five vomitings, five states in which food is not eaten, five diseases of the head, five heart diseases, five cases of pallor disease, five insanities, four epilepsies, four eye diseases, four ear diseases, four coryzas, four diseases of the mouth, four defects of <s>grahaṇī</s>, four intoxications, four fainting fits, four wasting diseases, four kinds of impotence, three swellings, three kinds of <s>kilāsa</s>, threefold <s>lohitapitta</s>, two fevers, two wounds, two contractions, two cases of sciatica, two jaundices, twofold <s>āma</s>, twofold <s>vātarakta</s>, two kinds of hemorrhoids, one stiffness of the thighs, one coma, one great disease, twenty classes of worms, twenty urinary disorders, and twenty disorders of the female genital tract: these forty-eight disease topics are briefly indicated in this compendium.
We shall specify these according to the order of their statement.

children.text: aṣṭāvudarāṇīti vātapittakaphasannipātaplīhabaddhacchidradakodarāṇi aṣṭau mūtrāghātā iti vātapittakaphasannipātāśmarīśarkarāśukraśoṇitajāḥ aṣṭau kṣīradoṣā iti vaivarṇyaṃ vaigandhyaṃ vairasyaṃ paicchilyaṃ phenasaṅghāto raukṣyaṃ gauravamatisnehaśca aṣṭau retodoṣā iti tanu śuṣkaṃ phenilam aśvetaṃ pūtyatipicchalamanyadhātūpahitamavasādi ca
children.translated_text: The eight abdominal diseases are those due to <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, their combination, the spleen, obstruction, perforation, and water. The eight urinary obstructions are those produced by <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, their combination, stone, gravel, semen, and blood. The eight defects of milk are discoloration, bad smell, bad taste, sliminess, accumulation of foam, dryness, heaviness, and excessive unctuousness. The eight defects of semen are thinness, dryness, foaminess, absence of whiteness, foulness, excessive sliminess, admixture with another tissue, and settling down.

children.text: sapta kuṣṭhānīti kapālodumbaramaṇḍalarṣyajihvapuṇḍarīkasidhmakākaṇāni sapta piḍakā iti śarāvikā kacchapikā jālinī sarṣapyalajī vinatā vidradhī ca sapta visarpā iti vātapittakaphāgnikardamakagranthisannipātākhyāḥ
children.translated_text: The seven skin diseases are named Kapāla, Udumbara, Maṇḍala, Ṛṣyajihva, Puṇḍarīka, Sidhmaka, and Kākaṇa. The seven pustules are Śarāvikā, Kacchapikā, Jālinī, Sarṣapī, Alajī, Vinatā, and Vidradhī. The seven spreading eruptions are called those of <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, fire, mud, knot, and the combined type.

children.text: ṣaḍatīsārā iti vātapittakaphasannipātabhayaśokajāḥ ṣaḍudāvartā iti vātamūtrapurīṣaśukracchardikṣavathujāḥ
children.translated_text: The six diarrheas are produced by <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, their combination, fear, and grief. The six upward movements are produced by <s>vāta</s>, urine, feces, semen, vomiting, and sneezing.

children.text: pañca gulmā iti vātapittakaphasannipātaśoṇitajāḥ pañca plīhadoṣā iti gulmairvyākhyātāḥ pañca kāsā iti vātapittakaphakṣatakṣayajāḥ pañca śvāsā iti mahordhvacchinnatamakakṣudrāḥ pañca hikkā iti mahatī gambhīrā vyapetā kṣudrānnajā ca pañca tṛṣṇā iti vātapittāmakṣayopasargātmikāḥ pañca chardaya iti dviṣṭārthasaṃyogajā vātapittakaphasannipātodrekotthāśca pañca bhaktasyānaśanasthānānīti vātapittakaphasannipātadveṣāḥ pañca śirorogā iti pūrvoddeśamabhisamasya vātapittakaphasannipātakrimijāḥ pañca hṛdrogā iti śirorogairvyākhyātāḥ pañca pāṇḍurogā iti vātapittakaphasannipātamṛdbhakṣaṇajāḥ pañconmādā iti vātapittakaphasannipātāgantunimittāḥ
children.translated_text: The five <s>gulmas</s> are produced by <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, their combination, and blood. The five spleen disorders are explained by the <s>gulmas</s>. The five coughs are produced by <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, injury, and wasting. The five dyspneas are great, upward, interrupted, tamaka, and minor. The five hiccups are great, deep, displaced, minor, and food-born. The five thirsts have the nature of <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>āma</s>, wasting, and complication. The five vomitings are produced by contact with something repugnant and by aggravation of <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and their combination. The five states in which food is not eaten are caused by <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, their combination, and aversion. The five diseases of the head, combining the earlier statement, are produced by <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, their combination, and worms. The five heart diseases are explained by the diseases of the head. The five pallor diseases are produced by <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, their combination, and eating clay. The five insanities have as their causes <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, their combination, and an external factor.

children.text: catvāro 'pasmārā iti vātapittakaphasannipātanimittāḥ catvāro 'kṣirogāścatvāraḥ karṇarogāścatvāraḥ pratiśyāyāścatvāro mukharogāścatvāro grahaṇīdoṣāścatvāro madāścatvāro mūrcchāyā ityapasmārairvyākhyātāḥ catvāraḥ śoṣā iti sāhasasaṃdhāraṇakṣayaviṣamāśanajāḥ catvāri klaibyānīti bījopaghātāddhvajabhaṅgājjarāyāḥ śukrakṣayācca
children.translated_text: The four epilepsies have <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and their combination as causes. The four eye diseases, four ear diseases, four coryzas, four mouth diseases, four defects of <s>grahaṇī</s>, four intoxications, and four fainting fits are explained by the epilepsies. The four wasting diseases are produced by overexertion, suppression of urges, depletion, and irregular eating. The four kinds of impotence arise from injury to the seed, collapse of the organ, old age, and depletion of semen.

children.text: trayaḥ śothā iti vātapittaśleṣmanimittāḥ trīṇi kilāsānīti raktatāmraśuklāni trividhaṃ lohitapittamiti ūrdhvabhāgam adhobhāgam ubhayabhāgaṃ ca
children.translated_text: The three swellings have <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s> as causes. The three kinds of <s>kilāsa</s> are red, coppery, and white. The threefold <s>lohitapitta</s> is upward, downward, and both upward and downward.

children.text: dvau jvarāviti uṣṇābhiprāyaḥ śītasamutthaśca śītābhiprāyaścoṣṇasamutthaḥ dvau vraṇāviti nijaścāgantujaśca dvāvāyāmāviti bāhyaścābhyantaraśca dve gṛdhrasyāviti vātād vātakaphācca dve kāmale iti koṣṭhāśrayā śākhāśrayā ca dvividhamāmamiti alasako visūcikā ca dvividhaṃ vātaraktamiti gambhīramuttānaṃ ca dvividhānyarśāṃsīti śuṣkāṇyārdrāṇi ca
children.translated_text: The two fevers are: one inclined toward heat and arising from cold, and one inclined toward cold and arising from heat. The two wounds are endogenous and external. The two <s>āyāmas</s> (contractures) are external and internal. The two cases of <s>gṛdhrasī</s> (sciatica) arise from <s>vāta</s> and from <s>vāta</s> with <s>kapha</s>. The two jaundices are located in the bowel and located in the branches. The twofold <s>āma</s> is <s>alasaka</s> and <s>visūcikā</s>. The twofold <s>vātarakta</s> is deep and superficial. The two kinds of hemorrhoids are dry and moist.

children.text: eka ūrustambha ityāmatridoṣasamutthaḥ ekaḥ saṃnyāsa iti tridoṣātmako manaḥśarīrādhiṣṭhānaḥ eko mahāgada iti atattvābhiniveśaḥ
children.translated_text: The single stiffness of the thighs arises from <s>āma</s> and the three <s>doṣas</s>. The single <s>saṃnyāsa</s> is of the nature of all three <s>doṣas</s> and has mind and body as its seat. The single great disease is fixation on what is not real.

children.text: viṃśatiḥ kṛmijātaya iti yūkā pipīlikāśceti dvividhā bahirmalajāḥ keśādā lomādā lomadvīpāḥ saurasā audumbarā jantumātaraśceti ṣaṭ śoṇitajāḥ antrādā udarāveṣṭā hṛdayādāścuravo darbhapuṣpāḥ saugandhikā mahāgudāśceti sapta kaphajāḥ kakerukā makerukā lelihāḥ saśūlakāḥ sausurādāśceti pañca purīṣajāḥ viṃśatiḥ pramehā ityudakamehaś cekṣubālikārasamehaśca sāndramehaśca sāndraprasādamehaśca śuklamehaśca śukramehaśca śītamehaśca śanairmehaśca sikatāmehaśca lālāmehaśceti daśa śleṣmanimittāḥ kṣāramehaśca kālamehaśca nīlamehaśca lohitamehaśca mañjiṣṭhāmehaśca haridrāmehaśca hastimehaśca madhumehaśceti catvāro vātanimittāḥ iti viṃśatiḥ pramehāḥ viṃśatiryonivyāpada iti vātikī paittikī ślaiṣmikī sānnipātikī ceti catasro doṣajāḥ doṣadūṣyasaṃsargaprakṛtinirdeśairavaśiṣṭāḥ ṣoḍaśa nirdiśyante tadyathā raktayoniścārajaskā cācaraṇā cāticaraṇā ca prākcaraṇā copaplutā ca pariplutā codāvartinī ca karṇinī ca putraghnī cāntarmukhī ca sūcīmukhī ca śuṣkā ca vāminī ca ṣaṇḍhayoniśca mahāyoniśceti viṃśatiryonivyāpado bhavanti
children.translated_text: The twenty classes of worms are as follows: lice and ants are the two kinds born from external impurity; the hair-eaters, body-hair-eaters, <s>lomadvīpas</s>, <s>saurasas</s>, <s>audumbaras</s>, and <s>jantumātṛs</s> are the six born from blood; the intestine-eaters, belly-coilers, heart-eaters, <s>curavas</s>, <s>darbhapuṣpas</s>, <s>saugandhikas</s>, and <s>mahāgudas</s> are the seven born from <s>kapha</s>; the <s>kakerukas</s>, <s>makerukas</s>, <s>lelihās</s>, <s>saśūlakas</s>, and <s>sausurādas</s> are the five born from feces. The twenty <s>pramehas</s> (urinary disorders) are: <s>udakameha</s>, <s>ikṣubālikārasameha</s>, <s>sāndrameha</s>, <s>sāndraprasādameha</s>, <s>śuklameha</s>, <s>śukrameha</s>, <s>śītameha</s>, <s>śanairmeha</s>, <s>sikatāmeha</s>, and <s>lālāmeha</s>, these ten being caused by <s>śleṣman</s>; <s>kṣārameha</s>, <s>kālameha</s>, <s>nīlameha</s>, <s>lohitameha</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhāmeha</s>, <s>haridrāmeha</s>, <s>hastimeha</s>, and <s>madhumeha</s>, these being included in the enumeration that ends with four caused by <s>vāta</s>. Thus there are twenty <s>pramehas</s>. The twenty disorders of the female genital tract are: those due to <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>śleṣman</s>, and the combined type, these four being produced by the <s>doṣas</s>; the remaining sixteen are specified by indications of the conjunction of <s>doṣa</s>, affected tissue, and constitution, namely <s>raktayoni</s>, <s>arajaskā</s>, <s>acaraṇā</s>, <s>aticaraṇā</s>, <s>prākcaraṇā</s>, <s>upaplutā</s>, <s>pariplutā</s>, <s>udāvartinī</s>, <s>karṇinī</s>, <s>putraghnī</s>, <s>antarmukhī</s>, <s>sūcīmukhī</s>, <s>śuṣkā</s>, <s>vāminī</s>, <s>ṣaṇḍhayoni</s>, and <s>mahāyoni</s>. These are the twenty disorders of the female genital tract.
This is only the summary statement, and it has been specified according to the order of that summary.

children.text: sarva eva nijā vikārā nānyatra vātapittakaphebhyo nirvartante yathāhi śakuniḥ sarvaṃ divasamapi paripatan svāṃ chāyāṃ nātivartate tathā svadhātuvaiṣamyanimittāḥ sarve vikārā vātapittakaphānnātivartante
children.translated_text: All endogenous disorders arise from nowhere other than <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>. For just as a bird, though it flies about all day, does not pass beyond its own shadow, so all disorders caused by imbalance of one's own bodily constituents do not pass beyond <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: vātapittaśleṣmaṇāṃ punaḥ sthānasaṃsthānaprakṛtiviśeṣānabhisamīkṣya tadātmakānapi ca sarvavikārāṃstānevopadiśanti buddhimantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, after considering the distinctions of place, configuration, and nature belonging to <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s>, the wise teach all disorders that have their nature as precisely those same entities.
And here there are verses:
The many groups of disorders in the body that are born from imbalance of one's own bodily constituents

children.text: na te pṛthak pittakaphānilebhya āgantavastveva tato viśiṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are not separate from <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>anila</s>; external disorders, however, are distinct from them.
An external disorder follows upon an endogenous disorder, and an endogenous disorder, when increased, likewise follows upon an external one.

children.text: tatrānubandhaṃ prakṛtiṃ ca samyag jñātvā tataḥ karma samārabheta ||
children.translated_text: In such a case, after correctly knowing the secondary connection and the primary nature, one should then begin treatment.
Here are two verses:
The groups of twenty and the single diseases, and three triads have been stated;
also eight pairs, twelve tetrads, and ten pentads.
There are four groups of eight, two groups of six, and three groups of seven;
these diseases have been set forth in the chapter on diseases called Aṣṭodarīya.
Now, then, we shall expound the chapter on great diseases.
Thus spoke the Blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: catvāro rogā bhavanti āgantuvātapittaśleṣmanimittāḥ teṣāṃ caturṇāmapi rogāṇāṃ rogatvamekavidhaṃ bhavati ruksāmānyāt dvividhā punaḥ prakṛtireṣām āgantunijavibhāgāt dvividhaṃ caiṣāmadhiṣṭhānaṃ manaḥśarīraviśeṣāt vikārāḥ punaraparisaṃkhyeyāḥ prakṛtyadhiṣṭhānaliṅgāyatanavikalpaviśeṣāparisaṃkhyeyatvāt ||
children.translated_text: There are four diseases: those caused by an external factor, by <s>vāta</s>, by <s>pitta</s>, and by <s>śleṣman</s>. The diseased condition of all four of these diseases is of one kind, because pain is common to them. Their nature, however, is twofold because of the division into external and endogenous. Their seat is twofold because of the distinction between mind and body. Their specific disorders, again, are innumerable, because the distinctions of nature, seat, sign, abode, and variant are innumerable.

children.text: mukhāni tu khalvāgantor nakhadaśanapatanābhicārābhiśāpābhiṣaṅgābhighātavyadhabandhanaveṣṭanapīḍanarajjudahanaśastrāśanibhūtopasargādīni nijasya tu mukhaṃ vātapittaśleṣmaṇāṃ vaiṣamyam ||
children.translated_text: The sources of an external disorder are, for example, nails, teeth, falling, sorcery, curses, harmful contact or possession, blows, piercing, binding, wrapping, pressure, rope, burning, weapons, lightning, and attacks by beings. The source of an endogenous disorder, however, is the imbalance of <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s>.
The incitement of both external and endogenous disorders is unsuitable contact between the senses and their objects, an offense of judgment, and temporal transformation.

children.text: sarve'pi tu khalvete 'bhipravṛddhāś catvāro rogāḥ parasparamanubadhnanti na cānyonyena saha saṃdehamāpadyante ||
children.translated_text: All these four diseases, when greatly increased, attach themselves to one another, yet they do not become confused with one another.
