children.text: atha khalvaṣṭābhyaḥ kāraṇebhyo jvaraḥ saṃjāyate manuṣyāṇāṃ tadyathā vātāt pittāt kaphāt vātapittābhyāṃ vātakaphābhyāṃ pittakaphābhyāṃ vātapittakaphebhyaḥ āgantoraṣṭamāt kāraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: Now fever arises in human beings from eight causes, namely: from <s>vāta</s>, from <s>pitta</s>, from <s>kapha</s>, from <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, from <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, from <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, from <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>, and, as the eighth cause, from an adventitious cause.
We shall explain its particular etiologies, prodromal signs, symptoms, and alleviating factors.

<s>Vāyu</s> becomes aggravated by excessive use of dry, light, and cold things, emesis, purgation, evacuative enema, evacuation of the head, exercise, suppression of urges, fasting, injury, sexual intercourse, anxiety, grief, excessive bloodletting, staying awake, and irregular bodily posture.

children.text: sa yadā prakupitaḥ praviśyāmāśayam ūṣmaṇā saha miśrībhūyād yam āhārapariṇāmadhātuṃ rasanāmānam anvavetya rasasvedavahāni srotāṃsi pidhāyāgnim upahatya paktisthānād ūṣmāṇaṃ bahirnirasya kevalaṃ śarīramanuprapadyate tadā jvaramabhinirvartayati ||
children.translated_text: When that aggravated <s>vāyu</s> enters the stomach, becomes mixed with heat, follows the first product of food-transformation called <s>rasa</s>, blocks the channels carrying <s>rasa</s> and sweat, impairs the digestive fire, drives the heat out from the place of digestion, and then pervades the entire body by itself, it produces fever.

children.text: tasyemāni liṅgāni bhavanti tadyathā viṣamārambhavisargitvam ūṣmaṇo vaiṣamyaṃ tīvratanubhāvānavasthānāni jvarasya jaraṇānte divasānte niśānte gharmānte vā jvarasyābhyāgamanam abhivṛddhir vā viśeṣeṇa paruṣāruṇavarṇatvaṃ nakhanayanavadanamūtrapurīṣatvacām atyarthaṃ kﾱptībhāvaśca anekavidhopamāś calācalāśca vedanāsteṣāṃ teṣām aṅgāvayavānāṃ tadyathā pādayoḥ suptatā piṇḍikayor udveṣṭanaṃ jānunoḥ kevalānāṃ ca sandhīnāṃ viśleṣaṇam ūrvoḥ sādaḥ kaṭīpārśvapṛṣṭhaskandhabāhvaṃsorasāṃ ca bhagnarugṇamṛditamathitacaṭitāvapāṭitāvanunnatvam iva hanvoścāprasiddhiḥ svanaśca karṇayoḥ śaṅkhayornistodaḥ kaṣāyāsyatā āsyavairasyaṃ vā mukhatālukaṇṭhaśoṣaḥ pipāsā hṛdayagrahaḥ śuṣkacchardiḥ śuṣkakāsaḥ kṣavathūdgāravinigrahaḥ annarasakhedaḥ prasekārocakāvipākāḥ viṣādajṛmbhāvināmavepathuśramabhramapralāpaprajāgararomaharṣadantaharṣāḥ uṣṇābhiprāyatā nidānoktānām anupaśayo viparītopaśayaśceti vātajvarasya liṅgāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Its signs are these: irregular onset and cessation, irregularity of heat, instability of the fever as intense or slight, the coming or increase of fever at the end of digestion, at the end of the day, at the end of the night, or at the end of the hot period; especially rough and reddish color, and an extreme roughened condition of the nails, eyes, face, urine, feces, and skin; many kinds of pains, both moving and fixed, in various limbs and parts, such as numbness in the feet, twisting in the calves, looseness of the knees and of the individual joints, weakness in the thighs, and a feeling as though the hips, flanks, back, shoulders, arms, shoulder-joints, and chest were broken, pained, crushed, churned, split, torn open, and struck down; impairment of the jaws, ringing in the ears, piercing pain in the temples, astringency or bad taste in the mouth, dryness of the mouth, palate, and throat, thirst, constriction in the heart, dry vomiting, dry cough, obstruction of sneezing and belching, distress at the taste of food, salivation, anorexia, and indigestion; dejection, yawning, bending of the body, tremor, fatigue, dizziness, delirium, sleeplessness, horripilation, and sensitivity of the teeth; desire for heat, non-alleviation by the causes stated in the etiology, and alleviation by their opposites. These are the signs of <s>vāta</s>-fever.
<s>Pitta</s> becomes aggravated by excessive use of hot, sour, salty, alkaline, pungent, and undigested foods, and also by sharp heat from the sun or fire, exertion, anger, and irregular diet.

children.text: tadyadā prakupitam āmāśayād ūṣmāṇam upasṛjyādyamāhārapariṇāmadhātuṃ rasanāmānam anvavetya rasasvedavahāni srotāṃsi pidhāya dravatvād agnim upahatya paktisthānād ūṣmāṇaṃ bahirnirasya prapīḍayat kevalaṃ śarīram anuprapadyate tadā jvaram abhinirvartayati ||
children.translated_text: When that aggravated <s>pitta</s>, from the stomach, joins with heat, follows the first product of food-transformation called <s>rasa</s>, blocks the channels carrying <s>rasa</s> and sweat, impairs the digestive fire because of its fluidity, drives the heat out from the place of digestion, and pervades the entire body while pressing upon it, it produces fever.

children.text: tasyemāni liṅgāni bhavanti tadyathā yugapadeva kevale śarīre jvarasyābhyāgamanam abhivṛddhirvā bhuktasya vidāhakāle madhyaṃdine 'rdharātre śaradi vā viśeṣeṇa kaṭukāsyatā ghrāṇamukhakaṇṭhauṣṭhatālupākaḥ tṛṣṇā mado bhramo mūrchā pittacchardanam atīsāraḥ annadveṣaḥ sadanaṃ khedaḥ pralāpaḥ raktakoṭhābhinirvṛttiḥ śarīre haritahāridratvaṃ nakhanayanavadanamūtrapurīṣatvacām atyartham ūṣmaṇastīvrabhāvaḥ atimātraṃ dāhaḥ śītābhiprāyatā nidānoktānupaśayo viparītopaśayaśceti pittajvaraliṅgāni bhavati ||
children.translated_text: These are its signs, namely: the onset of fever throughout the whole body all at once, or its increase, especially at the time when eaten food is being digested, at midday, at midnight, or in autumn; a pungent taste in the mouth; burning of the nose, mouth, throat, lips, and palate; thirst, intoxicated feeling, dizziness, fainting, vomiting of pitta, diarrhea, aversion to food, exhaustion, distress, delirious speech, the appearance of red wheals, a greenish-yellow coloration of the body, nails, eyes, face, urine, feces, and skin, extreme intensity of heat, excessive burning, a desire for cold, non-relief by the causes stated in the etiology, and relief by their opposites. These are the signs of pitta fever.
From excessive indulgence in things oily, heavy, sweet, slimy, cold, sour, and salty, and from day-sleep, pleasure, and lack of exercise, śleṣman becomes aggravated.

children.text: sa yadā prakupitaḥ praviśyāmāśayam ūṣmaṇā saha miśrībhūyādyam āhārapariṇāmadhātuṃ rasanāmānam anvavetya rasasvedavahāni srotāṃsi pidhāyāgnimupahatya paktisthānād ūṣmāṇaṃ bahirnirasya prapīḍayan kevalaṃ śarīramanuprapadyate tadā jvaramabhinirvartayati ||
children.translated_text: When it is aggravated, enters the stomach, combines with heat, follows the first product of food transformation called rasa, blocks the channels that carry rasa and sweat, impairs the digestive fire, drives the heat outward from the place of digestion, and passes through the whole body while oppressing it, then it produces fever.

children.text: tasyemāni liṅgāni bhavanti tadyathā yugapadeva kevale śarīre jvarasyābhyāgamanam abhivṛddhirvā bhuktamātre pūrvāhṇe pūrvarātre vasantakāle vā viśeṣeṇa gurugātratvam anannābhilāṣaḥ śleṣmaprasekaḥ mukhamādhuryaṃ hṛllāsaḥ hṛdayopalepaḥ stimitatvaṃ chardiḥ mṛdvagnitā nidrādhikyaṃ stambhaḥ tandrā kāsaḥ śvāsaḥ pratiśyāyaḥ śaityaṃ śvaityaṃ ca nakhanayanavadanamūtrapurīṣatvacām atyarthaṃ ca śītapiḍakā bhṛśamaṅgebhya uttiṣṭhanti uṣṇābhiprāyatā nidānoktānupaśayo viparītopaśayaśca iti śleṣmajvaraliṅgāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: These are its signs, namely: the onset of fever throughout the whole body all at once, or its increase, especially immediately after eating, in the forenoon, in the first part of the night, or in spring; heaviness of the limbs, lack of desire for food, discharge of phlegm, sweetness in the mouth, nausea, a coating sensation in the heart, torpor, vomiting, weak digestive fire, excessive sleep, stiffness, drowsiness, cough, dyspnea, catarrh, coldness, whiteness of the nails, eyes, face, urine, feces, and skin, and very cold eruptions rising strongly from the limbs; a desire for warmth, non-relief by the causes stated in the etiology, and relief by their opposites. These are the signs of śleṣman fever.

children.text: viṣamāśanād anaśanād annaparivartād ṛtuvyāpatter asātmyagandhopaghrāṇād viṣopahatasya codakasyopayogād garebhyo girīṇāṃ copaśleṣāt snehasvedavamanavirecanāsthāpanānuvāsanaśirovirecanānām ayathāvatprayogāt mithyāsaṃsarjanādvā strīṇāṃ ca viṣamaprajananāt prajātānāṃ ca mithyopacārād yathoktānāṃ ca hetūnāṃ miśrībhāvād yathānidānaṃ dvandvānām anyatamaḥ sarve vā trayo doṣā yugapat prakopam āpadyante te prakupitās tayaivānupūrvyā jvaram abhinirvartayanti ||
children.translated_text: Because of irregular eating, fasting, change of food, disturbance of the seasons, smelling unsuitable odors, the use of water affected by poison, artificial poisons, contact with mountains, improper application of oleation, sweating, emesis, purgation, evacuative enema, unctuous enema, and head-purgation, or from wrong post-therapy diet, and because of difficult delivery in women and wrong care of women who have given birth, or from the combination of the causes stated above, according to the cause one or another pair of doṣas, or all three doṣas at once, become aggravated. Once aggravated, they produce fever in that very sequence.

children.text: tatra tathoktānāṃ jvaraliṅgānāṃ miśrībhāvaviśeṣadarśanād dvāṃdvikam anyatamaṃ jvaraṃ sānnipātikaṃ vā vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: In such cases, from observing the particular mixture of the fever signs just described, one should recognize either one of the paired fevers or a sannipātika fever involving all the doṣas.
The external, eighth fever arises from traumatic injury, afflicting attachment or possession, hostile ritual, and curse, and is preceded by pain.

children.text: sa kiṃcitkālam āgantuḥ kevalo bhūtvā paścāddoṣairanubadhyate
children.translated_text: For some time it remains purely external, and afterward it becomes connected with the doṣas.

children.text: tatrābhighātajo vāyunā duṣṭaśoṇitādhiṣṭhānena abhiṣaṅgajaḥ punarvātapittābhyām abhicārābhiśāpajau tu saṃnipātenānubadhyete ||
children.translated_text: Among these, the fever born of traumatic injury is connected with vāta, with vitiated blood as its seat; the one born of afflicting attachment or possession is connected with vāta and pitta; and those born of hostile ritual and curse are connected with the conjunction of all three doṣas.

children.text: sa saptavidhājjvarād viśiṣṭaliṅgopakramasamutthānatvād viśiṣṭo veditavyaḥ karmaṇā sādhāraṇena copacaryate
children.translated_text: It should be known as distinct from the sevenfold fever because its signs, treatment, and onset are distinct; it is treated both by the special procedure and by the common treatment.
Thus the eightfold nature of fever has been stated.
Fever, however, is one alone, characterized by heat and burning.
That very fever is described as twofold because of a difference in standpoint, and because of the distinction between endogenous and external fever.

children.text: tatra nijaṃ dvividhaṃ trividhaṃ caturvidhaṃ saptavidhaṃ cāhurbhiṣajo vātādivikalpāt ||
children.translated_text: In the case of endogenous fever, physicians call it twofold, threefold, fourfold, and sevenfold according to the divisions beginning with vāta.

children.text: tasyemāni pūrvarūpāṇi bhavanti tadyathā mukhavairasyaṃ gurugātratvam anannābhilāṣaḥ cakṣuṣorākulatvam aśrvāgamanaṃ nidrādhikyam aratiḥ jṛmbhā vināmaḥ vepathuḥ śramabhramapralāpajāgaraṇaromaharṣadantaharṣāḥ śabdaśītavātātapasahatvāsahatvam arocakāvipākau daurbalyam aṅgamardaḥ sadanam alpaprāṇatā dīrghasūtratā ālasyam ucitasya karmaṇo hāniḥ pratīpatā svakāryeṣu gurūṇāṃ vākyeṣvabhyasūyā bālebhyaḥ pradveṣaḥ svadharmeṣvacintā mālyānulepanabhojanaparikleśanaṃ madhurebhyaśca bhakṣebhyaḥ pradveṣaḥ amlalavaṇakaṭukapriyatā ca iti jvarasya pūrvarūpāṇi bhavanti prāksaṃtāpāt api cainaṃ saṃtāpārtam anubadhnanti ||
children.translated_text: These are its prodromal signs, namely: bad taste in the mouth, heaviness of the limbs, lack of desire for food, disturbance of the eyes, flow of tears, excessive sleep, discontent, yawning, bending of the body, trembling, fatigue, dizziness, delirium, wakefulness, horripilation, sensitivity of the teeth, tolerance or intolerance of sound, cold, wind, and sun, anorexia and indigestion, weakness, aching of the limbs, exhaustion, slight vitality, slowness in acting, laziness, neglect of customary work, contrariness in one's own affairs, fault-finding toward the words of elders, hatred toward children, lack of thought for one's own duties, distress at garlands, unguents, and food, aversion to sweet foods, and liking for sour, salty, and pungent things. These are the prodromal signs of fever; they occur before the heat and also accompany one who is afflicted by that heat.
Thus the signs of each fever have been explained both in detail and in summary.

children.text: jvarastu khalu maheśvarakopaprabhavaḥ sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ prāṇaharo dehendriyamanastāpakaraḥ prajñābalavarṇaharṣotsāhahrāsakaraḥ śramaklamamohāhāroparodhasaṃjananaḥ jvarayati śarīrāṇīti jvaraḥ nānye vyādhayastathā dāruṇā bahūpadravā duścikitsyāśca yathāyam
children.translated_text: Now fever arises from the anger of <s>Maheśvara</s>; it takes away the life of all living beings, torments the body, senses, and mind, diminishes understanding, strength, complexion, joy, and vigor, and brings about fatigue, exhaustion, delusion, and obstruction of food. Because it makes bodies fevered, it is called fever. No other diseases are so terrible, attended by many complications, and difficult to treat as this one.

children.text: sa sarvarogādhipatiḥ nānātiryagyoniṣu ca bahuvidhaiḥ śabdairabhidhīyate
children.translated_text: It, the lord over all diseases, is also designated among the various animal species by many kinds of names.

children.text: sarve prāṇabhṛtaḥ sajvarā eva jāyante sajvarā eva mriyante ca sa mahāmohaḥ tenābhibhūtāḥ prāgdaihikaṃ dehinaḥ karma kiṃcidapi na smaranti sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ ca jvara evānte prāṇān ādatte ||
children.translated_text: All living beings are born with <s>jvara</s> (fever) and die with <s>jvara</s> as well. It is the great delusion; when embodied beings are overpowered by it, they remember nothing at all of the actions belonging to a former body, and at the end <s>jvara</s> alone takes away the lives of all living beings.

children.text: tatra pūrvarūpadarśane jvarādau vā hitaṃ laghvaśanam apatarpaṇaṃ vā jvarasyāmāśayasamutthatvāt tataḥ kaṣāyapānābhyaṅgasnehasvedapradehapariṣekānulepanavamanavirecanāsthāpanānuvāsanopaśamananastaḥkarmadhūpadhūmapānāñjanakṣīrabhojanavidhānaṃ ca yathāsvaṃ yuktyā prayojyam ||
children.translated_text: When the prodromal signs appear, or at the beginning of fever, light food or depletion is beneficial, because fever originates from the stomach. Thereafter drinking decoctions, massage, oiling, fomentation, poultices, sprinkling, anointing, emesis, purgation, non-unctuous and unctuous enemas, pacifying measures, nasal therapy, fumigation, smoke inhalation, collyrium, and a regimen of milk and food should each be applied according to reasoning as appropriate.

children.text: jīrṇajvareṣu tu sarveṣveva sarpiṣaḥ pānaṃ praśasyate yathāsvauṣadhasiddhasya sarpirhi snehādvātaṃ śamayati saṃskārāt kaphaṃ śaityātpittamūṣmāṇaṃ ca tasmāj jīrṇajvareṣu sarveṣveva sarpirhitam udakam ivāgnipluṣṭeṣu dravyeṣviti ||
children.translated_text: But in all chronic fevers the drinking of ghee prepared with the appropriate medicines is praised. For ghee, by its unctuousness, pacifies <s>vāta</s>; by its preparation it pacifies <s>kapha</s>; by its coolness it pacifies <s>pitta</s> and heat. Therefore in all chronic fevers ghee is beneficial, like water for things scorched by fire.
And here there are these verses:
As men sprinkle a blazing house with water,
seeking its quenching, so ghee is used in chronic fever.
By unctuousness it pacifies <s>vāta</s>; by coolness it restrains <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ tulyaguṇaṃ doṣaṃ saṃskārāttu jayet kapham ||
children.translated_text: Ghee, having qualities similar to the disorder, conquers <s>kapha</s> through its preparation.
No other unctuous substance follows preparation
as ghee does; therefore ghee is considered the best of all unctuous substances.
When a meaning that has been stated in prose is again sung in verses,
that repetition is not blameworthy, since it serves the determination and clarification of that meaning.
On this there are verses:
The threefold disease under its names and synonyms, its fivefold cause,
the synonyms of the disease's symptoms, and the fivefold seizure of the illness,
the eightfold fever, its remote and immediate causes,

children.text: pūrvarūpaṃ ca rūpaṃ ca bheṣajaṃ saṃgraheṇa ca ||
children.translated_text: its prodromal signs and manifest symptoms, and its treatment in summary:
these, concerning fever, were declared first in the section on diagnosis by the one free from fever,
the venerable <s>Punarvasu</s>, to the reverent <s>Agniveśa</s>.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the diagnosis of <s>raktapitta</s> (hemorrhagic pitta disorder).
Thus spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: pittaṃ yathābhūtaṃ lohitapittamiti saṃjñāṃ labhate tad vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We shall explain how <s>pitta</s>, in accordance with the actual condition, obtains the designation <s>lohitapitta</s>.

children.text: yadā janturyavakoddālakakoradūṣaprāyāṇyannāni bhuṅkte bhṛśoṣṇatīkṣṇamapi cānyadannajātaṃ niṣpāvamāṣakulatthasūpakṣāropasaṃhitaṃ dadhidadhimaṇḍodaśvitkaṭvarāmlakāñjikopasekaṃ vā vārāhamāhiṣāvikamātsyagavyapiśitaṃ piṇyākapiṇḍāluśuṣkaśākopahitaṃ mūlakasarṣapalaśunakarañjaśigrumadhuśigrukhaḍayūṣabhūstṛṇasumukhasurasakuṭherakagaṇḍīrakālamālakaparṇāsakṣavakaphaṇijjhakopadaṃśaṃ surāsauvīratuṣodakamaireyamedakamadhūlakaśuktakuvalabadarāmlaprāyānupānaṃ vā piṣṭānnottarabhūyiṣṭham uṣṇābhitapto vātimātramativelaṃ vāmaṃ payaḥ pibati payasā samaśnāti rauhiṇīkaṃ kāṇakapotaṃ vā sarṣapatailakṣārasiddhaṃ kulatthapiṇyākajāmbavalakucapakvaiḥ śauktikairvā saha kṣīraṃ pibatyuṣṇābhitaptaḥ tasyaivamācarataḥ pittaṃ prakopamāpadyate lohitaṃ ca svapramāṇamativartate
children.translated_text: When a person eats foods consisting chiefly of barley, kodrava-like grains, and koradūṣa, and also other very hot and sharp kinds of food, soups of niṣpāva beans, black gram, and horse gram mixed with alkali, foods sprinkled with curd, whey, sour gruel, or other sharp sour liquids, meat of pig, buffalo, sheep, fish, or cow, preparations accompanied by oil-cake, piṇḍālu, and dried vegetables, side dishes of radish, mustard, garlic, karañja, śigru, madhuśigru, khaḍayūṣa, bhūstṛṇa, sumukha, surasa, kuṭheraka, gaṇḍīra, kālamālaka, parṇāsa, kṣavaka, and phaṇijjhaka, or when he takes as drink mostly liquor, sauvīra, tuṣodaka, maireya, medaka, madhūlaka, vinegar, or sour drinks of jujube and similar fruits; when, overheated by heat, he drinks unsuitable milk in excessive quantity or at an improper time, or eats milk together with rauhiṇīka or kāṇakapota prepared with mustard oil and alkali, or drinks milk together with horse gram, oil-cake, jambu, lakuca, and ripened sour ferments while overheated: in one acting thus, <s>pitta</s> becomes aggravated, and the blood exceeds its proper measure.

children.text: tasmin pramāṇātivṛtte pittaṃ prakupitaṃ śarīramanusarpad yad eva yakṛtplīhaprabhavāṇāṃ lohitavahānāṃ ca srotasāṃ lohitābhiṣyandagurūṇi mukhānyāsādya pratirundhyāt tadeva lohitaṃ dūṣayati ||
children.translated_text: When the blood has exceeded its measure, the aggravated <s>pitta</s>, moving through the body, obstructs precisely those openings of the channels that arise from the liver and spleen and carry blood, openings made heavy by the congestion of blood; and there it corrupts the blood.
Because of its admixture, its corruption of the blood, and its conformity to the smell and color of blood, they call this <s>pitta</s> <s>lohitapitta</s>.

children.text: tasyemāni pūrvarūpāṇi bhavanti tadyathāanannābhilāṣaḥ bhuktasya vidāhaḥ śuktāmlagandharasa udgāraḥ charderabhīkṣṇamāgamanaṃ charditasya bībhatsatā svarabhedo gātrāṇāṃ sadanaṃ paridāhaḥ mukhāddhūmāgama iva lohalohitamatsyāmagandhitvamiva cāsyasya raktaharitahāridratvam aṅgāvayavaśakṛnmūtrasvedalālāsiṅghāṇakāsyakarṇamalapiḍakolikāpiḍakānām aṅgavedanā lohitanīlapītaśyāvānāmarciṣmatāṃ ca rūpāṇāṃ svapne darśanamabhīkṣṇamiti lohitapittapūrvarūpāṇi bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Its prodromal signs are these: lack of desire for food; burning after eating; eructation with a sour-vinegar smell and taste; frequent occurrence of vomiting; repulsiveness of the vomited matter; alteration of the voice; weakness of the limbs; burning all over; a sensation as if smoke were coming from the mouth; the mouth smelling like metal, blood, or raw fish; redness, greenness, or yellowness of the mouth; pain in the limbs and in the parts of the body, feces, urine, sweat, saliva, nasal mucus, phlegm, earwax, pimples, and boils; and frequent seeing in dreams of forms that are red, blue, yellow, or dark and flame-like. These are the prodromal signs of <s>lohitapitta</s>.
Its complications, however, are weakness, anorexia, indigestion, dyspnea, cough, fever, diarrhea, swelling, wasting, pallor disease, and alteration of the voice.
Its routes, again, are two: upward and downward.

children.text: tadbahuśleṣmaṇi śarīre śleṣmasaṃsargādūrdhvaṃ pratipadyamānaṃ karṇanāsikānetrāsyebhyaḥ pracyavate bahuvāte tu śarīre vātasaṃsargādadhaḥ pratipadyamānaṃ mūtrapurīṣamārgābhyāṃ pracyavate bahuśleṣmavāte tu śarīre śleṣmavātasaṃsargāddvāvapi mārgau pratipadyate tau mārgau pratipadyamānaṃ sarvebhya eva yathoktebhyaḥ khebhyaḥ pracyavate śarīrasya ||
children.translated_text: In a body with much <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), because of association with <s>śleṣman</s>, it proceeds upward and flows out from the ears, nose, eyes, and mouth. But in a body with much <s>vāta</s> (wind), because of association with <s>vāta</s>, it proceeds downward and flows out through the urinary and fecal passages. In a body with much <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>vāta</s>, because of association with <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>vāta</s>, it enters both paths; entering those paths, it flows out from all the openings of the body just mentioned.

children.text: tatra yadūrdhvabhāgaṃ tat sādhyaṃ virecanopakramaṇīyatvād bahvauṣadhatvācca yadadhobhāgaṃ tad yāpyaṃ vamanopakramaṇīyatvād alpauṣadhatvācca yadubhayabhāgaṃ tadasādhyaṃ vamanavirecanāyogitvād anauṣadhatvācceti ||
children.translated_text: Of these, what has the upper part as its path is curable, because purgation is the appropriate treatment and because there are many medicines. What has the lower part as its path is manageable, because emesis is the appropriate treatment and because there are few medicines. What has both parts as its path is incurable, because neither emesis nor purgation is suitable and because there is no medicine for it.

children.text: raktapittaprakopastu khalu purā dakṣayajñoddhvaṃse rudrakopāmarṣāgninā prāṇināṃ parigataśarīraprāṇānām abhavajjvaram anu ||
children.translated_text: Now the aggravation of <s>raktapitta</s> (hemorrhagic disorder) first occurred after the destruction of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice, following fever, among living beings whose bodies and vital breaths had been seized by the fire of <s>Rudra</s>'s anger and wrath.

children.text: tasyāśukāriṇo dāvāgnerivāpatitasyātyayikasyāśu praśāntyai prayatitavyaṃ mātrāṃ deśaṃ kālaṃ cābhisamīkṣya saṃtarpaṇenāpatarpaṇena vā mṛdumadhuraśiśiratiktakaṣāyairabhyavahāryaiḥ pradehapariṣekāvagāhasaṃsparśanair vamanādyair vā tatrāvahiteneti ||
children.translated_text: Since it acts quickly, like a forest fire that has fallen upon one, and is urgent, one must strive for its rapid pacification after considering measure, place, and time, either by nourishing or depleting treatment, by foods that are mild, sweet, cooling, bitter, and astringent, by applications, sprinklings, immersions, and contacts, or by emesis and the like, with careful attention in that case.
And here there are these verses:
That <s>lohitapitta</s> is curable which proceeds upward,
because purgation is suitable and because medicine is abundant.
Purgation is the supreme medicine for conquering <s>pitta</s>,

children.text: yaśca tatrānvayaḥ śleṣmā tasya cānadhamaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and it is remembered as not inferior for the <s>śleṣman</s> that accompanies it there.
There a sweet medicine, too, becomes suitable for the therapy;

children.text: tasmāt sādhyaṃ mataṃ raktaṃ yadūrdhvaṃ pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: therefore the blood that proceeds upward is considered curable.
But the blood that has the lower part as its path is certainly manageable,
because emesis has little suitability and because medicine is scant.

children.text: vamanaṃ hi na pittasya haraṇe śreṣṭhamucyate
children.translated_text: For emesis is not said to be best for removing <s>pitta</s>,
and the <s>vāyu</s> that accompanies it there is remembered as inferior with respect to its pacification.
Astringent and bitter medicines are not suitable for the therapy there;
therefore what is said to move downward is declared manageable.
But the <s>raktapitta</s> that enters both paths
should be known as incurable for the very reason stated before.
For there is no purificatory treatment for it that moves against its path,
and in <s>raktapitta</s> removal is prescribed along the opposing path.
Likewise, there is no complete pacification for it in every respect,
for when the <s>doṣas</s> are mixed, a pacifying treatment that conquers all is approved.
Thus blood has been described as having three kinds of outcome according to the distinction of path;

children.text: ebhyastu khalu hetubhyaḥ kiṃcitsādhyaṃ na sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: but for these reasons even something curable may not be cured:
from lack of attendants and equipment, from bad character, from the physician's fault,
and from failure to act, some disease passes beyond curability.
In that case there may be a single state of incurability, because the curable and the manageable have not been treated in due course.
This knowledge of <s>raktapitta</s> is taught for that condition.
What is black or else blue, or what has the appearance of a rainbow,
that <s>raktapitta</s> is incurable, as is that which stains cloth.
What is very fetid, excessive, and accompanied by all complications,
and what occurs with wasting of strength and flesh, that blood is unsuccessful in treatment.
And when a person afflicted with blood through <s>raktapitta</s>
sees visible objects and even the sky as blood, that is incurable, without doubt.
There the incurable should be abandoned; the manageable should be managed with effort;
and the physician, attentive, should cure the curable with proven medicines.
On this there are two verses:
The cause, the derivation of the name, the premonitory signs, the complications,

children.text: mārgau doṣānubandhaṃ ca sādhyatvaṃ na ca hetumat ||
children.translated_text: the paths, the associated <s>doṣas</s>, curability and incurability with their causes:
in the diagnosis of <s>raktapitta</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s> declared these things,
free from delusion, the fault of passion, greed, pride, intoxication, and craving.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the diagnosis of <s>gulma</s>.
Thus spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: iha khalu pañca gulmā bhavanti tadyathāvātagulmaḥ pittagulmaḥ śleṣmagulmo nicayagulmaḥ śoṇitagulma iti ||
children.translated_text: Here, indeed, there are five kinds of <s>gulma</s>: namely, <s>vātagulma</s>, <s>pittagulma</s>, <s>śleṣmagulma</s>, <s>nicayagulma</s>, and <s>śoṇitagulma</s>.

children.text: evaṃvādinaṃ bhagavantamātreyamagniveśa uvāca kathamiha bhagavan pañcānāṃ gulmānāṃ viśeṣamabhijānīmahe nahyaviśeṣavidrogāṇāmauṣadhavidapi bhiṣak praśamanasamartho bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: When the venerable <s>Ātreya</s> had spoken thus, <s>Agniveśa</s> said: How, venerable sir, may we here recognize the distinction among the five kinds of <s>gulma</s>? For a physician, even if he knows medicines, is not able to pacify diseases if he does not know their distinctions.

children.text: tamuvāca bhagavānātreyaḥ samutthānapūrvarūpaliṅgavedanopaśayaviśeṣebhyo viśeṣavijñānaṃ gulmānāṃ bhavatyanyeṣāṃ ca rogāṇāmagniveśa tattu khalu gulmeṣūcyamānaṃ nibodha ||
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Ātreya</s> said to him: <s>Agniveśa</s>, knowledge of the distinction among <s>gulmas</s>, and among other diseases as well, arises from distinctions in origin, premonitory signs, marks, pain, and what gives relief. Now listen as that is being explained with respect to <s>gulmas</s>.

children.text: yadā puruṣo vātalo viśeṣeṇa jvaravamanavirecanātīsārāṇāmanyatamena darśanena karśito vātalamāhāramāharati śītaṃ vā viśeṣeṇātimātram asnehapūrve vā vamanavirecane pibati anudīrṇāṃ vā chardimudīrayati udīrṇān vātamūtrapurīṣavegānniruṇaddhi atyaśito vā pibati navodakamatimātram atisaṃkṣobhiṇā vā yānena yāti ativyavāyavyāyāmamadyaśokarucirvā abhighātamṛcchati vā viṣamāsanaśayanasthānacaṅkramaṇasevī vā bhavati anyadvā kiṃcidevaṃvidhaṃ viṣamamatimātraṃ vyāyāmajātamārabhate tasyāpacārādvātaḥ prakopamāpadyate ||
children.translated_text: When a person of <s>vāta</s> constitution, especially one emaciated by fever, emesis, purgation, diarrhea, or any one such manifestation, takes food that increases <s>vāta</s>, or especially cold food, or an excessive quantity; or drinks emetic or purgative preparations without first having taken unctuous substance; or forcibly brings on vomiting that has not arisen; or suppresses arisen urges of flatus, urine, and feces; or drinks an excessive quantity of fresh water after overeating; or travels in a vehicle that causes excessive jolting; or is given to excessive intercourse, exercise, liquor, grief, or distaste for food; or suffers injury; or habitually uses irregular sitting, sleeping, standing, or walking; or undertakes any other such irregular and excessive kind of exertion, then because of his misconduct <s>vāta</s> becomes aggravated.

children.text: sa prakupito vāyurmahāsroto 'nupraviśya raukṣyāt kaṭhinībhūtam āplutya piṇḍito 'vasthānaṃ karoti hṛdi bastau pārśvayornābhyāṃ vā sa śūlamupajanayati granthīṃścānekavidhān piṇḍitaścāvatiṣṭhate sa piṇḍitatvād gulma ityabhidhīyate sa muhurādhamati muhuralpatvamāpadyate aniyatavipulāṇuvedanaśca bhavati calatvādvāyoḥ muhuḥ pipīlikāsampracāra ivāṅgeṣu todabhedasphuraṇāyāmasaṅkocasuptiharṣapralayodayabahulaḥ tadāturaḥ sūcyeva śaṅkuneva cābhisaṃviddham ātmānaṃ manyate api ca divasānte jvaryate śuṣyati cāsyāsyam ucchvāsaścoparudhyate hṛṣyanti cāsya romāṇi vedanāyāḥ prādurbhāve plīhāṭopāntrakūjanāvipākodāvartāṅgamardamanyāśiraḥśaṅkhaśūlabradhnarogāś cainamupadravanti kṛṣṇāruṇaparuṣatvaṅnakhanayanavadanamūtrapurīṣaśca bhavati nidānoktāni cāsya nopaśerate viparītāni copaśerata iti vātagulmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That aggravated <s>vāyu</s>, entering the great channel, because of its dryness, gathers into a hard mass after flooding it and makes a fixed lodging in the heart, bladder, flanks, or navel. It produces pain and various kinds of nodules, and remains there as a compact mass. Because it is massed together it is called <s>gulma</s>. It swells up at one moment and becomes small at another; its pains are irregular, broad, and minute, because of the mobility of <s>vāyu</s>. There are frequent sensations as if ants were moving over the limbs, with pricking, splitting pain, throbbing, extension, contraction, numbness, horripilation, and repeated loss and return of sensation. The patient thinks himself pierced as if by a needle and by a stake. Moreover, at the end of the day he becomes feverish, his mouth dries up, his breathing is obstructed, and his body hairs stand erect when pain appears. Distention of the spleen, rumbling of the intestines, indigestion, upward movement of wind, pain in the limbs, pain in the neck, head, and temples, and diseases of the groin also afflict him. His skin, nails, eyes, face, urine, and feces become blackish, reddish, and rough. The causes mentioned in the diagnosis do not relieve him, while their opposites do relieve him. This is <s>vātagulma</s>.

children.text: tair eva tu karśanaiḥ karśitasyāmlalavaṇakaṭukakṣāroṣṇatīkṣṇaśuktavyāpannamadyaharitakaphalāmlānāṃ vidāhināṃ ca śākadhānyamāṃsādīnām upayogād ajīrṇādhyaśanād raukṣyānugate cāmāśaye vamanam ativelaṃ saṃdhāraṇaṃ vātātapau cātisevamānasya pittaṃ saha mārutena prakopam āpadyate ||
children.translated_text: But when a person emaciated by those very depleting factors uses sour, salty, pungent, alkaline, hot, sharp, fermented, spoiled-liquor, green-vegetable, and sour-fruit substances, and also burning foods such as vegetables, grains, and meats; when he eats during indigestion or over a prior meal; when emesis is performed too late in the stomach that is associated with dryness, and when he excessively suppresses urges and overuses wind and sun, <s>pitta</s> becomes aggravated together with <s>māruta</s>.

children.text: tat prakupitaṃ māruta āmāśayaikadeśe saṃvartya tāneva vedanāprakārānupajanayati ya uktā vātagulme pittaṃ tvenaṃ vidahati kukṣau hṛdyurasi kaṇṭhe ca sa vidahyamānaḥ sadhūmamivodgāramudgiratyamlānvitaṃ gulmāvakāśaścāsya dahyate dūyate dhūpyate ūṣmāyate svidyati klidyati śithila iva sparśāsaho 'lparomāñcaśca bhavati jvarabhramadavathupipāsāgalatālumukhaśoṣapramohaviḍbhedāś cainam upadravanti haritahāridratvaṅnakhanayanavadanamūtrapurīṣaśca bhavati nidānoktāni cāsya nopaśerate viparītānyupaśerata iti pittagulmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it is aggravated, <s>māruta</s> gathers it into one part of the stomach and produces the same kinds of pains as were stated for <s>vātagulma</s>. But <s>pitta</s> burns it in the abdomen, heart, chest, and throat. As it is being burned, the patient belches out an acidic eructation as if accompanied by smoke, and the region of the <s>gulma</s> burns, aches, smokes, heats up, sweats, becomes moist, seems slack, cannot bear touch, and has little horripilation. Fever, dizziness, burning, thirst, dryness of the throat, palate, and mouth, confusion, and looseness of stool also afflict him. His skin, nails, eyes, face, urine, and feces become green and yellow. The causes mentioned in the diagnosis do not relieve him, while their opposites do relieve him. This is <s>pittagulma</s>.

children.text: taireva tu karśanaiḥ karśitasyātyaśanād atisnigdhagurumadhuraśītāśanāt piṣṭekṣukṣīratilamāṣaguḍavikṛtisevanān mandakamadyātipānāddharitakātipraṇayanād ānūpaudakagrāmyamāṃsātibhakṣaṇāt saṃdhāraṇād abubhukṣasya cātipragāḍhamudapānāt saṃkṣobhaṇādvā śarīrasya śleṣmā saha mārutena prakopamāpadyate ||
children.translated_text: But when a person emaciated by those same depleting factors overeats; eats excessively unctuous, heavy, sweet, and cold food; uses preparations of flour, sugarcane, milk, sesame, black gram, and jaggery; drinks too much weak liquor; is overly attached to green vegetables; eats too much meat from marshy, aquatic, and domesticated animals; suppresses urges; drinks water very deeply when not hungry; or has his body shaken, <s>śleṣman</s> becomes aggravated together with <s>māruta</s>.

children.text: taṃ prakupitaṃ māruta āmāśayaikadeśe saṃvartya tāneva vedanāprakārānupajanayati ya uktā vātagulme śleṣmā tvasya śītajvarārocakāvipākāṅgamardaharṣahṛdrogacchardinidrālasyastaimityagauravaśirobhitāpānupajanayati api ca gulmasya sthairyagauravakāṭhinyāvagāḍhasuptatāḥ tathā kāsaśvāsapratiśyāyān rājayakṣmāṇaṃ cātipravṛddhaḥ śvaityaṃ tvaṅnakhanayanavadanamūtrapurīṣeṣūpajanayati nidānoktāni cāsya nopaśerate viparītāni copaśerata iti śleṣmagulmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it is aggravated, <s>māruta</s> gathers it into one part of the stomach and produces the same kinds of pains as were stated for <s>vātagulma</s>. But <s>śleṣman</s> produces in him cold fever, anorexia, indigestion, pain in the limbs, horripilation, heart disease, vomiting, sleepiness, lassitude, stiffness, heaviness, and headache. Moreover, the <s>gulma</s> has stability, heaviness, hardness, deep-seatedness, and numbness. When greatly increased, it also produces cough, dyspnea, catarrh, wasting disease, and whiteness in the skin, nails, eyes, face, urine, and feces. The causes mentioned in the diagnosis do not relieve him, while their opposites do relieve him. This is <s>śleṣmagulma</s>.
When there is a conjunction of the causes and signs of all three <s>doṣas</s>, the skilled teach it as a <s>sānnipātika gulma</s>.
Because its treatments are mutually opposed, this cumulative <s>gulma</s> is incurable.

children.text: śoṇitagulmastu khalu striyā eva bhavati na puruṣasya garbhakoṣṭhārtavāgamanavaiśeṣyāt
children.translated_text: But <s>śoṇitagulma</s> occurs only in a woman, not in a man, because of the special character of the womb and the occurrence of menstruation.

children.text: pāratantryād avaiśāradyāt satatamupacārānurodhādvā vegān udīrṇān uparundhatyā āmagarbhe vāpyacirapatite 'thavāpyaciraprajātāyā ṛtau vā vātaprakopaṇānyāsevamānāyāḥ kṣipraṃ vātaḥ prakopamāpadyate ||
children.translated_text: For a woman who, through dependence, lack of confidence, or constant compliance with attendance upon others, suppresses arisen urges; or whose immature fetus has recently miscarried; or who has recently given birth; or who during the menstrual season uses things that aggravate <s>vāta</s>, <s>vāta</s> quickly becomes aggravated.

children.text: sa prakupito yonimukhamanupraviśyārtavamuparuṇaddhi māsi māsi tadārtavamuparudhyamānaṃ kukṣimabhivardhayati
children.translated_text: That aggravated <s>vāta</s>, entering the vaginal opening, obstructs the menstrual blood. Month by month, as that menstrual blood is obstructed, it enlarges the abdomen.

children.text: tasyāḥ śūlakāsātīsāracchardyarocakāvipākāṅgamardanidrālasyastaimityakaphaprasekāḥ samupajāyante stanayośca stanyam oṣṭhayoḥ stanamaṇḍalayośca kārṣṇyam atyarthaṃ glāniścakṣuṣoḥ mūrcchā hṛllāsaḥ dohadaḥ śvayathuśca pādayoḥ īṣaccodgamo romarājyāḥ yonyāś cāṭālatvam api ca yonyā daurgandhyamāsrāvaścopajāyate kevalaścāsyā gulmaḥ piṇḍita eva spandate tāmagarbhāṃ garbhiṇīmityāhur mūḍhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In her there arise colic, cough, diarrhea, vomiting, anorexia, indigestion, aching of the limbs, sleepiness, lassitude, stiffness, and discharge of <s>kapha</s> (phlegm); and in the breasts there is milk, while the lips and the areolae of the breasts become very dark. There is extreme fatigue of the eyes, fainting, nausea, craving, and swelling of the feet, a slight rising of the line of body hair, and looseness of the vagina; moreover, fetor and discharge from the vagina arise. This woman's <s>gulma</s> (abdominal mass) alone, formed into a lump, throbs; the deluded call her, though not pregnant, a pregnant woman.

children.text: eṣāṃ tu khalu pañcānāṃ gulmānāṃ prāg abhinivṛtter imāni pūrvarūpāṇi bhavanti tadyathānannābhilaṣaṇam arocakāvipākau agnivaiṣamyaṃ vidāho bhuktasya pākakāle cāyuktyā chardyudgārau vātamūtrapurīṣavegānāṃ cāprādurbhāvaḥ prādurbhūtānāṃ cāpravṛttirīṣadāgamanaṃ vā vātaśūlāṭopāntrakūjanāpariharṣaṇātivṛttapurīṣatāḥ abubhukṣā daurbalyaṃ sauhityasya cāsahatvamiti ||
children.translated_text: Now, before the full manifestation of these five <s>gulmas</s>, these are the prodromal signs: namely, lack of desire for food, anorexia and indigestion, irregularity of digestive fire, burning of what has been eaten at the time of digestion, improper vomiting and eructation, failure of the urges for wind, urine, and feces to appear, or, when they have appeared, their non-operation or only slight passage, pains from wind, distention, rumbling in the intestines, horripilation, excessive evacuation of feces, lack of hunger, weakness, and inability to tolerate satiety.

children.text: sarveṣvapi khalveteṣu gulmeṣu na kaścidvātādṛte sambhavati gulmaḥ
children.translated_text: Indeed, in all these <s>gulmas</s>, no <s>gulma</s> arises apart from <s>vāta</s> (wind).

children.text: teṣāṃ sānnipātikamasādhyaṃ jñātvā naivopakrameta ekadoṣaje tu yathāsvamārambhaṃ praṇayet saṃsṛṣṭāṃstu sādhāraṇena karmaṇopacaret
children.translated_text: Knowing the <s>sānnipātika</s> (tridoṣic) one among them to be incurable, one should not undertake treatment at all. In a single-doṣa case, one should apply the proper treatment according to that doṣa; but mixed cases should be treated with a common course of therapy.

And whatever else one considers not incompatible should also be administered, after distinguishing the heaviness and lightness of the complications. The physician should treat the serious complications urgently, and the others afterward.

children.text: tvaramāṇastu viśeṣam anupalabhamāno gulmeṣvātyayike karmaṇi vātacikitsitaṃ praṇayet snehasvedau vātaharau snehopasaṃhitaṃ ca mṛdu virecanaṃ bastīṃśca amlalavaṇamadhurāṃśca rasān yuktyāvacārayet
children.translated_text: But when acting urgently, if he does not perceive a specific distinction among <s>gulmas</s>, he should apply treatment for <s>vāta</s> in the emergency: oleation and fomentation that remove <s>vāta</s>, mild purgation accompanied by oiliness, enemas, and sour, salty, and sweet tastes, administering them with proper judgment.

children.text: mārute hyupaśānte svalpenāpi prayatnena śakyo 'nyo 'pi doṣo niyantuṃ gulmeṣviti ||
children.translated_text: For when <s>māruta</s> (wind) has been pacified, even another <s>doṣa</s>, with little effort, can be controlled in cases of <s>gulma</s>.
And here there is this verse:
For those afflicted with <s>gulma</s>, pacification of <s>anila</s> (wind) should be carried out in every way by the proper means, according to rule.
For when <s>māruta</s> has not been conquered, even a slightly aggravated other <s>doṣa</s> destroys the treatment.
On this there is a verse:
The number, the cause, the signs, and also the prodromal signs,
the prognosis in the diagnosis of <s>gulmas</s>, and one portion of the treatments, have been taught.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the diagnosis of <s>prameha</s>.
Thus spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>.
There are twenty disorders called <s>prameha</s>, caused by the aggravation of the three <s>doṣas</s>, and other disorders are beyond enumeration.
Now we shall explain in sequence how aggravation of the three <s>doṣas</s> brings about the <s>pramehas</s>.

Here, indeed, from specific differences in causes, <s>doṣas</s>, and affected substrates, there are corresponding specific differences in whether disorders are obstructed or not obstructed in their manifestation.

children.text: yadā hyete trayo nidānādiviśeṣāḥ parasparaṃ nānubadhnantyathavā kālaprakarṣādabalīyāṃso 'thavānubadhnanti na tadā vikārābhinirvṛttiḥ cirādvāpyabhinirvartante tanavo vā bhavantyayathoktasarvaliṅgā vā viparyaye viparītāḥ iti sarvavikāravighātabhāvābhāvaprativiśeṣābhinirvṛttihetur bhavatyuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For when these three specific factors, beginning with causes, do not mutually connect with one another, or when, because of a long lapse of time, they are weak, or when they do connect but not strongly, then the disorder does not arise; or it arises only after a long time, or is slight, or lacks all the signs described. In the opposite case the opposite results occur. Thus the cause has been stated for the specific production of the presence or absence of obstruction to all disorders.

children.text: tatreme trayo nidānādiviśeṣāḥ śleṣmanimittānāṃ pramehāṇāmāśvabhinirvṛttikarā bhavanti tad yathā hāyanakayavakacīnakoddālakanaiṣadhetkaṭamukundakamahāvrīhipramodakasugandhakānāṃ navānāmativelamatipramāṇena copayogaḥ tathā sarpiṣmatāṃ navahareṇumāṣasūpyānāṃ grāmyānūpaudakānāṃ ca māṃsānāṃ śākatilapalalapiṣṭānnapāyasakṛśarāvilepīkṣuvikārāṇāṃ kṣīranavamadyamandakadadhidravamadhurataruṇaprāyāṇāṃ copayogaḥ mṛjāvyāyāmavarjanaṃ svapnaśayanāsanaprasaṅgaḥ yaśca kaścidvidhiranyo 'pi śleṣmamedomūtrasaṃjananaḥ sa sarvo nidānaviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among these, the following three specific factors beginning with causes bring about the rapid manifestation of <s>pramehas</s> caused by <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm): namely, excessive use, both too often and in too great a quantity, of new grains such as <s>hāyanaka</s>, <s>yavaka</s>, <s>cīnaka</s>, <s>uddālaka</s>, <s>naiṣadha</s>, <s>etkaṭa</s>, <s>mukundaka</s>, <s>mahāvrīhi</s>, <s>pramodaka</s>, and <s>sugandhaka</s>; likewise, the use of fresh legume dishes of <s>hareṇu</s> and <s>māṣa</s> prepared with ghee, meats of domestic, marshy, and aquatic animals, vegetables, sesame, gruels and flour preparations, boiled rice, milk-rice, <s>kṛśara</s>, thick gruel, sugarcane products, milk, fresh wine, weak liquor, the liquid part of curds, and substances that are very sweet and mostly fresh; avoidance of cleansing and exercise; indulgence in sleep, lying down, and sitting; and any other regimen whatsoever that generates <s>śleṣman</s>, fat, and urine. All this is the specific cause.
Abundant fluid <s>śleṣman</s> is the specific <s>doṣa</s>.

children.text: bahvabaddhaṃ medo māṃsaṃ śarīrajakledaḥ śukraṃ śoṇitaṃ vasā majjā lasīkā rasaścaujaḥsaṃkhyāta iti dūṣyaviśeṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Abundant, unbound fat, flesh, bodily moisture, semen, blood, muscle fat, marrow, lymph, <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid), and what is counted as <s>ojas</s> are the specific affected substrates.

children.text: trayāṇāmeṣāṃ nidānādiviśeṣāṇāṃ sannipāte kṣipraṃ śleṣmā prakopamāpadyate prāg atibhūyastvāt sa prakupitaḥ kṣiprameva śarīre visṛptiṃ labhate śarīraśaithilyāt sa visarpañ śarīre medasaivādito miśrībhāvaṃ gacchati medasaścaiva bahvabaddhatvānmedasaśca guṇaiḥ samānaguṇabhūyiṣṭhatvāt sa medasā miśrībhavan dūṣayatyenat vikṛtatvāt sa vikṛto duṣṭena medasopahitaḥ śarīrakledamāṃsābhyāṃ saṃsargaṃ gacchati kledamāṃsayor atipramāṇābhivṛddhatvāt sa māṃse māṃsapradoṣāt pūtimāṃsapiḍakāḥ śarāvikākacchapikādyāḥ saṃjanayati aprakṛtibhūtatvāt śarīrakledaṃ punardūṣayan mūtratvena pariṇamayati mūtravahānāṃ ca srotasāṃ vaṅkṣaṇabastiprabhavāṇāṃ medaḥkledopahitāni gurūṇi mukhānyāsādya pratirudhyate tataḥ pramehāṃsteṣāṃ sthairyamasādhyatāṃ vā janayati prakṛtivikṛtibhūtatvāt ||
children.translated_text: When these three specific factors beginning with causes come together, <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm) quickly becomes aggravated, because at first they are especially abundant. Once aggravated, it very quickly obtains diffusion through the body because the body is lax. As it spreads through the body, it first enters into mixture with <s>medas</s> (fat), because <s>medas</s> is abundant and unbound, and because it has a predominance of qualities similar to those of <s>śleṣman</s>. Mingling with <s>medas</s>, it vitiates it, since it has itself become altered. Altered and joined with vitiated <s>medas</s>, it comes into contact with bodily moisture and flesh, because moisture and flesh have increased beyond measure. In the flesh, because of vitiation of the flesh, it produces putrid fleshy pustules, <s>śarāvikā</s>, <s>kacchapikā</s>, and the like, since it is no longer in its natural state. Again vitiating the bodily moisture, it transforms it into urine. And, reaching the heavy openings of the urine-carrying channels that arise from the groins and bladder, openings loaded with fat and moisture, it is obstructed. From this it produces <s>pramehas</s> (urinary disorders), or their firmness and incurability, because it has the nature both of what is normal and what is abnormal.

children.text: śarīrakledastu śleṣmamedomiśraḥ praviśan mūtrāśayaṃ mūtratvamāpadyamānaḥ ślaiṣmikairebhirdaśabhirguṇairupasṛjyate vaiṣamyayuktaiḥ tadyathāśvetaśītamūrtapicchilācchasnigdhagurumadhurasāndraprasādamandaiḥ tatra yena guṇenaikenānekena vā bhūyastaramupasṛjyate tatsamākhyaṃ gauṇaṃ nāmaviśeṣaṃ prāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: Bodily moisture, mixed with <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>medas</s>, enters the urinary bladder and, while becoming urine, is affected by these ten <s>ślaiṣmika</s> qualities in uneven combinations, namely: white, cold, formed, slimy, clear, unctuous, heavy, sweet, dense-and-clear, and slow. There, according to whichever one quality, or several qualities, affects it most strongly, it receives a corresponding secondary specific name.

children.text: te tu khalvime daśa pramehā nāmaviśeṣeṇa bhavanti tadyathāudakamehaśca ikṣuvālikārasamehaśca sāndramehaśca sāndraprasādamehaśca śuklamehaśca śukramehaśca śītamehaśca sikatāmehaśca śanairmehaśca ālālamehaśceti ||
children.translated_text: These, then, are the ten <s>pramehas</s> according to their specific names: <s>udakameha</s>, <s>ikṣuvālikārasameha</s>, <s>sāndrameha</s>, <s>sāndraprasādameha</s>, <s>śuklameha</s>, <s>śukrameha</s>, <s>śītameha</s>, <s>sikatāmeha</s>, <s>śanairmeha</s>, and <s>ālālameha</s>.

children.text: te daśa pramehāḥ sādhyāḥ samānaguṇamedaḥsthānakatvāt kaphasya prādhānyāt samakriyatvācca ||
children.translated_text: Those ten <s>pramehas</s> are curable, because they have the same qualities and the same seat, <s>medas</s>, because <s>kapha</s> is predominant, and because their treatment is uniform.
Here there are verses for understanding the distinctions of <s>śleṣma-prameha</s>.
Clear, abundant, white, cold, odorless, and resembling water:
because of aggravation of <s>śleṣman</s>, a man with <s>udameha</s> passes such urine.
Exceedingly sweet, cold, slightly slimy, and turbid,
like the juice of sugarcane stalk: because of aggravation of <s>śleṣman</s>, he passes such urine.
When a man's urine, after standing, becomes dense in the vessel,
because of aggravation of <s>kapha</s>, they call that man a <s>sāndramehin</s>.

children.text: yasya saṃhanyate mūtraṃ kiṃcit kiṃcit prasīdati
children.translated_text: When a man's urine coagulates, while becoming clear little by little,
because of aggravation of <s>śleṣman</s>, they call him one with <s>sāndraprasādameha</s>.
When someone frequently passes white urine resembling flour,
because of aggravation of <s>kapha</s>, they call that man a <s>śuklamehin</s>.

children.text: śukrābhaṃ śukramiśraṃ vā mururmehati yo naraḥ
children.translated_text: When a man frequently passes urine resembling semen, or mixed with semen,
because of aggravation of <s>śleṣman</s>, they call that man a <s>śukramehin</s>.

children.text: atyarthamadhuraṃ śītaṃ mūtraṃ mehati yo bhṛśam
children.translated_text: When someone passes very copious urine that is exceedingly sweet and cold,
because of aggravation of <s>śleṣman</s>, they call that man a <s>śītamehin</s>.
When a man passes small, solidified <s>doṣas</s> contained in the urine,
because of aggravation of <s>śleṣman</s>, one should know that man as a <s>sikatāmehin</s>.

children.text: mandaṃ mandamavegaṃ tu kṛcchraṃ yo mūtrayecchanaiḥ
children.translated_text: When someone urinates slowly, slowly, without force and with difficulty,
because of aggravation of <s>śleṣman</s>, they call that man a <s>śanairmehin</s>.
When someone passes slimy <s>ālāla</s>, as if bound together by threads,
because of aggravation of <s>śleṣman</s>, one should know that man as an <s>ālālamehin</s>.

children.text: ityete daśa pramehāḥ śleṣmaprakopanimittā vyākhyātā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Thus these ten <s>pramehas</s>, caused by aggravation of <s>śleṣman</s>, have been explained.

children.text: uṣṇāmlalavaṇakṣārakaṭukājīrṇabhojanopasevinas tathātitīkṣṇātapāgnisaṃtāpaśramakrodhaviṣamāhāropasevinaśca tathāvidhaśarīrasyaiva kṣipraṃ pittaṃ prakopamāpadyate tattu prakupitaṃ tayaivānupūrvyā pramehānimān ṣaṭ kṣiprataramabhinirvartayati ||
children.translated_text: In one who takes food that is hot, sour, salty, alkaline, pungent, or undigested, and likewise in one who exposes himself to excessively sharp sun, fire, heat, exertion, anger, and irregular diet, if the body is of that kind, <s>pitta</s> quickly becomes aggravated. Once aggravated, following that same sequence, it very rapidly produces these six <s>pramehas</s>.

children.text: teṣāmapi tu khalu pittaguṇaviśeṣeṇaiva nāmaviśeṣā bhavanti tadyathākṣāramehaśca kālamehaśca nīlamehaśca lohitamehaśca māñjiṣṭhamehaśca hāridramehaśceti ||
children.translated_text: Their specific names too arise precisely from particular qualities of <s>pitta</s>: <s>kṣārameha</s>, <s>kālameha</s>, <s>nīlameha</s>, <s>lohitameha</s>, <s>māñjiṣṭhameha</s>, and <s>hāridrameha</s>.

children.text: te ṣaḍbhireva kṣārāmlalavaṇakaṭukavisroṣṇaiḥ pittaguṇaiḥ pūrvavadyuktā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: They are connected, as before, with just the six qualities of <s>pitta</s>: alkaline, sour, salty, pungent, fetid, and hot.
All of them are manageable, because their seat is <s>medas</s> together with mixed <s>doṣas</s>, and because their therapeutic procedures are mutually opposed.
Here there are verses for understanding the distinctions of <s>pitta-prameha</s>.
Like alkali in smell, color, taste, and touch,
because of aggravation of <s>pitta</s>, a man with <s>kṣārameha</s> passes such urine.
When someone constantly passes hot urine that is the color of ink,
one should know him, through the great aggravation of <s>pitta</s>, as a <s>kālamehin</s>.
When a man passes sour urine resembling the wing of a <s>cāṣa</s> bird,
one should know him, through the great aggravation of <s>pitta</s>, as a <s>nīlamehin</s>.

children.text: visraṃ lavaṇamuṣṇaṃ ca raktaṃ mehati yo naraḥ
children.translated_text: When a man passes urine that is fetid, salty, hot, and red,
one should know him, through the great aggravation of <s>pitta</s>, as a <s>raktamehin</s>.
When someone passes urine resembling water colored with madder and very fetid,
one should know him, through the great aggravation of <s>pitta</s>, as a <s>māñjiṣṭhamehin</s>.
When someone passes pungent urine resembling water colored with turmeric,
Because of the aggravation of <s>pitta</s> (bile), one should know him as suffering from <s>hāridrameha</s>.

children.text: ityete ṣaṭ pramehāḥ pittaprakopanimittā vyākhyātā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Thus these six <s>pramehas</s> caused by aggravation of <s>pitta</s> have been explained.

In one who resorts excessively to astringent, pungent, bitter, dry, light, cold things, sexual intercourse, exercise, emesis, purgation, decoction enemas, errhines, suppression of urges, fasting, injury, sun exposure, anxiety, grief, excessive loss of blood, wakefulness, and irregular bodily postures, and whose body is of that sort, <s>vāta</s> quickly becomes aggravated.

children.text: sa prakupitastathāvidhe śarīre visarpan yadā vasāmādāya mūtravahāni srotāṃsi pratipadyate tadā vasāmehamabhinirvartayati yadā punarmajjānaṃ mūtrabastāvākarṣati tadā majjameham abhinirvartayati yadā tu lasīkāṃ mūtrāśaye 'bhivahanmūtramanubandhaṃ cyotayati lasīkātibahutvād vikṣepaṇācca vāyoḥ khalvasyātimūtrapravṛttisaṅgaṃ karoti tadā sa matta iva gajaḥ kṣaratyajasraṃ mūtramavegaṃ taṃ hastimehinamācakṣate ojaḥ punarmadhurasvabhāvaṃ tad yadā raukṣyādvāyuḥ kaṣāyatvenābhisaṃsṛjya mūtrāśaye 'bhivahati tadā madhumehaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: When that aggravated <s>vāta</s>, spreading through such a body, takes up fat and enters the urine-carrying channels, it produces <s>vasāmeha</s>. When again it draws marrow into the urinary bladder, it produces <s>majjameha</s>. But when, carrying lymph into the urinary receptacle, it makes urine drip continuously, then, because of the great abundance of lymph and because of the scattering action of <s>vāyu</s>, it causes excessive urinary flow without proper urge; then he passes urine constantly and without control like a rutting elephant, and they call him one with <s>hastimeha</s>. Again, <s>ojas</s> is naturally sweet; when, because of dryness, <s>vāyu</s> mixes it with astringency and carries it into the urinary bladder, it produces <s>madhumeha</s>.
Physicians call these four <s>pramehas</s>, born of <s>vāta</s>, incurable, because they are very dangerous and because the therapeutic procedure is contrary.

children.text: teṣāmapi pūrvavadguṇaviśeṣeṇa nāmaviśeṣā bhavanti tadyathāvasāmehaśca majjamehaśca hastimehaśca madhumehaśceti ||
children.translated_text: For them too, as before, particular names arise from particular qualities, namely <s>vasāmeha</s>, <s>majjameha</s>, <s>hastimeha</s>, and <s>madhumeha</s>.
On this there are verses for recognizing the particular forms of <s>vātaja prameha</s>.

children.text: vasāmiśraṃ vasābhaṃ vā muhurmehati yo naraḥ
children.translated_text: The man who repeatedly passes urine mixed with fat or resembling fat
they call one with <s>vasāmeha</s>, incurable from aggravation of <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: majjānaṃ saha mūtreṇa muhurmehati yo naraḥ
children.translated_text: The man who repeatedly passes marrow together with urine
they call one with <s>majjameha</s>, incurable from aggravation of <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: hastī matta ivājasraṃ mūtraṃ kṣarati yo bhṛśam
children.translated_text: The man who, like a rutting elephant, constantly lets urine flow in great quantity
they call one with <s>hastimeha</s>, incurable from aggravation of <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: kaṣāyamadhuraṃ pāṇḍu rūkṣaṃ mehati yo naraḥ
children.translated_text: The man who passes urine that is astringent-sweet, pale, and dry
one should understand him, from aggravation of <s>vāta</s>, to be an incurable sufferer from <s>madhumeha</s>.

children.text: ityete catvāraḥ pramehā vātaprakopanimittā vyākhyātā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Thus these four <s>pramehas</s> caused by aggravation of <s>vāta</s> have been explained.

children.text: evaṃ tridoṣaprakopanimittā viṃśatiḥ pramehā vyākhyātā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: In this way the twenty <s>pramehas</s> caused by aggravation of the three <s>doṣas</s> have been explained.

children.text: trayastu khalu doṣāḥ prakupitāḥ pramehānabhinirvartayiṣyanta imāni pūrvarūpāṇi darśayanti tadyathājaṭilībhāvaṃ keśeṣu mādhuryamāsyasya karapādayoḥ suptatādāhau mukhatālukaṇṭhaśoṣaṃ pipāsām ālasyaṃ malaṃ kāye kāyacchidreṣūpadehaṃ paridāhaṃ suptatāṃ cāṅgeṣu ṣaṭpadapipīlikābhiśca śarīramūtrābhisaraṇaṃ mūtre ca mūtradoṣān visraṃ śarīragandhaṃ nidrāṃ tandrāṃ ca sarvakālamiti ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, the three <s>doṣas</s>, when aggravated and about to produce <s>pramehas</s>, show these prodromal signs: matting of the hair; sweetness of the mouth; numbness and burning in the hands and feet; dryness of the mouth, palate, and throat; thirst; lassitude; grime on the body; coating in the bodily openings; burning; numbness in the limbs; the swarming of bees and ants over the body and urine; defects of the urine in the urine; a raw or fetid smell of the body; and sleepiness and drowsiness at all times.

The complications of those with <s>prameha</s> are thirst, diarrhea, fever, burning, weakness, anorexia, and indigestion, and, in consequence of it, putrid-flesh pustules, <s>alajī</s>, abscesses, and the like.
Among these, one should treat the curable <s>pramehas</s> appropriately with purificatory and pacifying measures.
And here there are these verses:
A man greedy for foods, a hater of bathing and walking,
<s>prameha</s> quickly approaches, like a bird approaching its nesting tree.
A man of weak initiative, excessively stout, excessively unctuous, and a great eater,
death quickly takes away in the form of <s>prameha</s>.
But the man who follows a diet that brings the body's <s>dhātus</s> into equilibrium
and various other activities as well, he enjoys happiness.
On this there are verses:
The cause of particular diseases, the cause of the <s>pramehas</s>,
the combination of <s>doṣas</s> and <s>dhātus</s>, and the manifold symptomatology;

children.text: daśa śleṣmakṛtā yasmāt pramehāḥ ṣaṭ ca pittajāḥ
children.translated_text: why ten <s>pramehas</s> are produced by <s>śleṣman</s> and six by <s>pitta</s>,

children.text: yathā ca vāyuścaturaḥ pramehān kurute balī ||
children.translated_text: and how powerful <s>vāyu</s> produces four <s>pramehas</s>;
the distinctions of curable and incurable, the prodromal signs and complications,
and the principle of treatment: these have been stated in this diagnosis of <s>prameha</s>.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the diagnosis of <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
Thus spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>.
Seven substances, when their normal condition has become pathological, are the material basis of <s>kuṣṭhas</s>.

children.text: tadyathātrayo doṣā vātapittaśleṣmāṇaḥ prakopaṇavikṛtāḥ dūṣyāśca śarīradhātavas tvaṅmāṃsaśoṇitalasīkāś caturdhā doṣopaghātavikṛtā iti
children.translated_text: They are as follows: the three <s>doṣas</s>, <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s>, altered by aggravation; and the bodily <s>dhātus</s> that are affected, namely skin, flesh, blood, and lymph, altered in four ways by injury from the <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: etat saptānāṃ saptadhātukam evaṃgatamājananaṃ kuṣṭhānām ataḥprabhavāṇyabhinirvartamānāni kevalaṃ śarīramupatapanti ||
children.translated_text: This, then, is the generation of <s>kuṣṭhas</s> as having these seven constituents. Arising from these, they afflict the whole body.

children.text: na ca kiṃcid asti kuṣṭhamekadoṣaprakopanimittam asti tu khalu samānaprakṛtīnāmapi kuṣṭhānāṃ doṣāṃśāṃśavikalpānubandhasthānavibhāgena vedanāvarṇasaṃsthānaprabhāvanāmacikitsitaviśeṣaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no <s>kuṣṭha</s> caused by the aggravation of only one <s>doṣa</s>. But even among <s>kuṣṭhas</s> of the same basic nature, because of differences in the portions of the <s>doṣas</s>, in their associations, and in their locations, there is distinction in pain, color, shape, effect, name, and treatment.
It may be sevenfold, eighteenfold, or innumerable.

children.text: doṣā hi vikalpanairvikalpyamānā vikalpayanti vikārān anyatrāsādhyabhāvāt
children.translated_text: For the <s>doṣas</s>, when differentiated through variations, make the disorders varied, apart from the condition of incurability.
Considering that there would be excessive extension in enumerating their variants and disorders, we shall teach only a sevenfold special classification of <s>kuṣṭha</s>.

children.text: iha vātādiṣu triṣu prakupiteṣu tvagādīṃścaturaḥ pradūṣayatsu vāte 'dhikatare kapālakuṣṭhamabhinirvartate pitte tvaudumbaraṃ śleṣmaṇi maṇḍalakuṣṭhaṃ vātapittayorṛṣyajihvaṃ pittaśleṣmaṇoḥ puṇḍarīkaṃ śleṣmamārutayoḥ sidhmakuṣṭhaṃ sarvadoṣābhivṛddhau kākaṇakamabhinirvartate evameṣa saptavidhaḥ kuṣṭhaviśeṣo bhavati
children.translated_text: Here, when the three beginning with <s>vāta</s> are aggravated and vitiate the four beginning with the skin, <s>kapālakuṣṭha</s> arises when <s>vāta</s> is predominant, <s>audumbarakuṣṭha</s> when <s>pitta</s> is predominant, <s>maṇḍalakuṣṭha</s> when <s>śleṣman</s> is predominant, <s>ṛṣyajihvā</s> from <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, <s>puṇḍarīka</s> from <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, <s>sidhmakuṣṭha</s> from <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>māruta</s>, and <s>kākaṇaka</s> when all the <s>doṣas</s> are increased. Thus this special classification of <s>kuṣṭha</s> is sevenfold.

children.text: sa caiṣa bhūyastaratamataḥ prakṛtau vikalpyamānāyāṃ bhūyasīṃ vikāravikalpasaṃkhyāmāpadyate ||
children.translated_text: And this, when its nature is differentiated according to greater and lesser degrees, comes to have a still larger number of variant disorders.

children.text: tatredaṃ sarvakuṣṭhanidānaṃ samāsenopadekṣyāmaḥ śītoṣṇavyatyāsam anānupūrvyopasevamānasya tathā saṃtarpaṇāpatarpaṇābhyavahāryavyatyāsaṃ madhuphāṇitamatsyalakucamūlakakākamācīḥ satatamatimātramajīrṇe ca samaśnataḥ cilicimaṃ ca payasā hāyanakayavakacīnakoddālakakoradūṣaprāyāṇi cānnāni kṣīradadhitakrakolakulatthamāṣātasīkusumbhasnehavanti etairevātimātraṃ suhitasya ca vyavāyavyāyāmasaṃtāpānatyupasevamānasya bhayaśramasaṃtāpopahatasya ca sahasā śītodakamavatarataḥ vidagdhaṃ cāhārajātam anullikhya vidāhīnyabhyavaharataḥ chardiṃ ca pratighnataḥ snehāṃścāticarataḥ trayo doṣāḥ yugapat prakopamāpadyante tvagādayaścatvāraḥ śaithilyamāpadyante teṣu śithileṣu doṣāḥ prakupitāḥ sthānamadhigamya saṃtiṣṭhamānāstāneva tvagādīn dūṣayantaḥ kuṣṭhānyabhinirvartayanti ||
children.translated_text: Now we shall briefly teach this general cause of all <s>kuṣṭha</s>. When a person uses cold and hot things in alternation without proper sequence, and likewise alternates nourishing and depleting foods; when he constantly and excessively eats honey, <s>phāṇita</s>, fish, <s>lakuca</s>, radish, and <s>kākamācī</s>, and does so when food is undigested; when he eats <s>cilicima</s> together with milk, and foods consisting chiefly of <s>hāyanaka</s>, <s>yavaka</s>, <s>cīnaka</s>, <s>uddālaka</s>, and <s>koradūṣa</s>, along with milk, curds, buttermilk, jujube, horse gram, black gram, linseed, and safflower fats; when, having become excessively satisfied by these very things, he overuses intercourse, exercise, and heat; when, overcome by fear, fatigue, and heat, he suddenly enters cold water; when, without vomiting up a spoiled mass of food, he eats burning foods; when he suppresses vomiting and overdoes unctuous substances: then the three <s>doṣas</s> become aggravated simultaneously, and the four beginning with the skin become slackened. When these are slackened, the aggravated <s>doṣas</s>, finding a place and remaining there, vitiate those very tissues beginning with the skin and produce <s>kuṣṭhas</s>.

children.text: teṣāmimāni pūrvarūpāṇi bhavanti tadyathā asvedanam atisvedanaṃ pāruṣyamatiślakṣṇatā vaivarṇyaṃ kaṇḍūrnistodaḥ suptatā paridāhaḥ pariharṣo lomaharṣaḥ kharatvamūṣmāyaṇaṃ gauravaṃ śvayathur vīsarpāgamanam abhīkṣṇaṃ ca kāye kāyacchidreṣūpadehaḥ pakvadagdhadaṣṭabhagnakṣatopaskhaliteṣvatimātraṃ vedanā svalpānāmapi ca vraṇānāṃ duṣṭir asaṃrohaṇaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: Their premonitory signs are these: absence of sweating, excessive sweating, roughness, excessive smoothness, discoloration, itching, pricking pain, numbness, burning all around, tingling, horripilation, harshness, heat, heaviness, swelling, the onset of <s>vīsarpa</s>, frequent coating on the body and in the body openings, excessive pain in places that are suppurated, burned, bitten, broken, wounded, or bruised, and the corruption and failure to heal of even small wounds.

children.text: tato 'nantaraṃ kuṣṭhānyabhinirvartante teṣāmidaṃ vedanāvarṇasaṃsthānaprabhāvanāmaviśeṣavijñānaṃ bhavati tadyathā rūkṣāruṇaparuṣāṇi viṣamavisṛtāni kharaparyantāni tanūnyudvṛttabahistanūni suptavatsuptāni hṛṣitalomācitāni nistodabahulāny alpakaṇḍūdāhapūyalasīkāny āśugatisamutthānāny āśubhedīni jantumanti kṛṣṇāruṇakapālavarṇāni ca kapālakuṣṭhānīti vidyāt tāmrāṇi tāmrakhararomarājībhiravanaddhāni bahalāni bahubahalapūyaraktalasīkāni kaṇḍūkledakothadāhapākavantyāśugatisamutthānabhedīni sasaṃtāpakrimīṇi pakvodumbaraphalavarṇānyaudumbarakuṣṭhānīti vidyāt snigdhāni gurūṇyutsedhavanti ślakṣṇasthirapītaparyantāni śuklaraktāvabhāsāni śuklaromarājīsantānāni bahubahalaśuklapicchilasrāvīṇi bahukledakaṇḍūkrimīṇi saktagatisamutthānabhedīni parimaṇḍalāni maṇḍalakuṣṭhāni vidyāt paruṣāṇyaruṇavarṇāni bahirantaḥśyāvāni nīlapītatāmrāvabhāsānyāśugatisamutthānānyalpakaṇḍūkledakrimīṇi dāhabhedanistodapākabahulāni śūkopahatopamavedanānyutsannamadhyāni tanuparyantāni karkaśapiḍakācitāni dīrghaparimaṇḍalānyṛṣyajihvākṛtīni ṛṣyajihvānīti vidyāt śuklaraktāvabhāsāni raktaparyantāni raktarājīsirāsaṃtatāny utsedhavanti bahubahalaraktapūyalasīkāni kaṇḍūkrimidāhapākavantyāśugatisamutthānabhedīni puṇḍarīkapalāśasaṃkāśāni puṇḍarīkāṇīti vidyāt paruṣāruṇāni viśīrṇabahistanūnyantaḥsnigdhāni śuklaraktāvabhāsāni bahūnyalpavedanānyalpakaṇḍūdāhapūyalasīkāni laghusamutthānānyalpabhedakrimīṇyalābupuṣpasaṅkāśāni sidhmakuṣṭhānīti vidyāt kākaṇantikāvarṇānyādau paścāttu sarvakuṣṭhaliṅgasamanvitāni pāpīyasā sarvakuṣṭhaliṅgasaṃbhavenānekavarṇāni kākaṇānīti vidyāt
children.translated_text: After that the <s>kuṣṭhas</s> arise. This is the knowledge of their specific differences in pain, color, shape, and effect: one should know as <s>kapālakuṣṭha</s> those lesions that are dry, reddish, rough, irregularly spreading, rough-edged, thin, raised and outwardly thin, numb as if insensible, covered with bristling hairs, full of pricking pain, with little itching, burning, pus, or serum, rapid in course and onset, quick to split, worm-infested, and blackish-red like the color of a potsherd. One should know as <s>audumbarakuṣṭha</s> those that are coppery, covered with lines of coppery rough hairs, thick, with abundant thick pus, blood, and serum, having itching, moisture, sloughing, burning, and suppuration, rapid in course, onset, and splitting, accompanied by heat and worms, and colored like a ripe <s>udumbara</s> fruit. One should know as <s>maṇḍalakuṣṭha</s> those that are unctuous, heavy, raised, smooth, firm, yellow-edged, white and red in appearance, covered with stretches of white hairs, discharging much thick white slimy fluid, having much moisture, itching, and worms, slow in course, onset, and splitting, and circular in form. One should know as <s>ṛṣyajihvā</s> those that are rough, reddish, dark both outside and inside, with blue, yellow, and coppery appearance, rapid in course and onset, with little itching, moisture, and worms, full of burning, splitting, pricking, and suppuration, painful as if struck by bristles, raised in the middle, thin-edged, covered with hard pustules, long and rounded, and shaped like a deer's tongue. One should know as <s>puṇḍarīka</s> those that are white and red in appearance, red-edged, spread with red lines and veins, raised, with abundant thick blood, pus, and serum, having itching, worms, burning, and suppuration, rapid in course, onset, and splitting, and resembling lotus petals. One should know as <s>sidhmakuṣṭha</s> those that are rough and reddish, externally cracked and thin, internally unctuous, white and red in appearance, numerous, with little pain, little itching, burning, pus, and serum, slight in onset, with little splitting and few worms, and resembling bottle-gourd flowers. One should know as <s>kākaṇaka</s> those that at first have the color of <s>kākaṇantikā</s>, but afterwards are furnished with the marks of all <s>kuṣṭhas</s>, being especially bad because they combine all the marks of <s>kuṣṭha</s> and have many colors.
Those are incurable; the others, however, are curable.

children.text: tatra yadasādhyaṃ tadasādhyatāṃ nātivartate sādhyaṃ punaḥ kiṃcit sādhyatām ativartate kadācidapacārāt
children.translated_text: In this matter, what is incurable does not pass beyond its incurability; but what is curable sometimes passes beyond curability because of improper conduct.

children.text: sādhyāni hi ṣaṭ kākaṇakavarjyāny acikitsyamānānyapacārato vā doṣair abhiṣyandamānānyasādhyatām upayānti ||
children.translated_text: For the six curable forms, excepting <s>kākaṇaka</s>, if they are not treated, or if through improper conduct they are flooded by the <s>doṣas</s>, become incurable.

children.text: sādhyānāmapi hyupekṣyamāṇānāṃ tvaṅmāṃsaśoṇitalasīkākothakledasaṃsvedajāḥ krimayo 'bhimūrchanti te bhakṣayantastvagādīn doṣāḥ punardūṣayanta imānupadravān pṛthak pṛthag utpādayanti tatra vātaḥ śyāvāruṇavarṇaṃ paruṣatāmapi ca raukṣyaśūlaśoṣatodavepathuharṣasaṅkocāyāsastambhasuptibhedabhaṅgān pittaṃ dāhasvedakledakothasrāvapākarāgān śleṣmā tvasya śvaityaśaityakaṇḍūsthairyagauravotsedhopasnehopalepān krimayastu tvagādīṃścaturaḥ sirāḥ snāyūścāsthīnyapi taruṇānyādadate ||
children.translated_text: For even in those cases that are curable, if they are neglected, worms born from putrefaction, moisture, and sweating in the skin, flesh, blood, lymph, and slough overwhelm the patient. As they consume the skin and the rest, the <s>doṣas</s> again vitiate them and separately produce these complications. There <s>vāta</s> produces a dark reddish color and roughness, and also dryness, pain, wasting, pricking, trembling, horripilation, contraction, exhaustion, stiffness, numbness, splitting, and breaking. <s>pitta</s> produces burning, sweating, moisture, putrefaction, discharge, suppuration, and redness. <s>śleṣman</s> produces whiteness, coldness, itching, fixity, heaviness, swelling, oiliness, and coating. But the worms consume the four beginning with the skin, and also the vessels, sinews, and even tender bones.

children.text: asyāṃ caivāvasthāyāmupadravāḥ kuṣṭhinaṃ spṛśanti tadyathā prasravaṇam aṅgabhedaḥ patanānyaṅgāvayavānāṃ tṛṣṇājvarātīsāradāhadaurbalyārocakāvipākāśca tathāvidhamasādhyaṃ vidyāditi ||
children.translated_text: And in this very condition complications affect the person with <s>kuṣṭha</s>: namely, oozing, breaking pain in the limbs, falling away of bodily parts, thirst, fever, diarrhea, burning, weakness, anorexia, and indigestion. One should know such a case to be incurable.
And here there are these verses:
The man who at first neglects a disease, thinking, "This is curable,"
after some time has passed, realizes that he is as good as dead.

children.text: yastu prāgeva rogebhyo rogeṣu taruṇeṣu vā
children.translated_text: But one who applies medicine properly before diseases arise, or while diseases are still recent,

children.text: bheṣajaṃ kurute samyak sa ciraṃ sukhamaśnute ||
children.translated_text: enjoys happiness for a long time.
For just as a young tree is cut down with little effort,
but that same tree, when greatly grown, is cut down only with very great effort,
so too a disorder, when recent, is easily cured;
when it has grown, it is cured with difficulty, or it may become incurable.
On this there is a verse:
The number, substances, <s>doṣas</s>, causes, prodromal signs,
manifest signs, and complications of the <s>kuṣṭhas</s> have each been stated in the chapter on <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the diagnosis of <s>śoṣa</s>.
Thus spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: iha khalu catvāri śoṣasyāyatanāni bhavanti tadyathāsāhasaṃ saṃdhāraṇaṃ kṣayo viṣamāśanamiti ||
children.translated_text: Here, indeed, there are four bases of <s>śoṣa</s>: namely, rash overexertion, suppression, wasting, and irregular eating.

children.text: tatra sāhasaṃ śoṣasyāyatanamiti yaduktaṃ tadanuvyākhyāsyāmaḥyadā puruṣo durbalo hi san balavatā saha vigṛhṇāti atimahatā vā dhanuṣā vyāyacchati jalpati vāpyatimātram atimātraṃ vā bhāramudvahati apsu vā plavate cātidūram utsādanapadāghātane vātipragāḍhamāsevate atiprakṛṣṭaṃ vādhvānaṃ drutamabhipatati abhihanyate vā anyadvā kiṃcidevaṃvidhaṃ viṣamamatimātraṃ vā vyāyāmajātamārabhate tasyātimātreṇa karmaṇoraḥ kṣaṇyate
children.translated_text: There, what was said as "rash overexertion is a basis of <s>śoṣa</s>" will be explained in detail. When a man, though weak, wrestles with someone strong; or strains with a bow that is too great; or talks excessively; or carries an excessive burden; or swims too far in water; or practices rubbing and trampling too forcefully; or quickly rushes along a very long road; or is struck; or undertakes any other such irregular or excessive kind of exertion, then through that excessive action his chest is injured.
<s>Vāyu</s> attacks that injured chest.

children.text: sa tatrāvasthitaḥ śleṣmāṇamuraḥsthamupasaṃgṛhya pittaṃ ca dūṣayan viharatyūrdhvam adhastiryak ca
children.translated_text: Remaining there, it takes hold of the <s>śleṣman</s> lodged in the chest, vitiates <s>pitta</s>, and moves upward, downward, and crosswise.

children.text: tasya yo 'ṃśaḥ śarīrasandhīnāviśati tenāsya jṛmbhāṅgamardo jvaraścopajāyate yastvāmāśayamabhyupaiti tena rogā bhavanti urasyā arocakaśca yaḥ kaṇṭhamabhiprapadyate kaṇṭhastenoddhvaṃsyate svaraścāvasīdati yaḥ prāṇavahāni srotāṃsyanveti tena śvāsaḥ pratiśyāyaśca jāyate yaḥ śirasyavatiṣṭhate śirastenopahanyate tataḥ kṣaṇanāccaivoraso viṣamagatitvācca vāyoḥ kaṇṭhasya coddhvaṃsanāt kāsaḥ satatamasya saṃjāyate sa kāsaprasaṅgādurasi kṣate śoṇitaṃ ṣṭhīvati śoṇitāgamanāccāsya daurbalyamupajāyate evamete sāhasaprabhavāḥ sāhasikamupadravāḥ spṛśanti
children.translated_text: Of it, the portion that enters the joints of the body causes yawning, aching of the limbs, and fever. The portion that reaches the stomach causes disorders in the chest and anorexia. The portion that reaches the throat irritates the throat, and the voice sinks. The portion that follows the channels carrying breath causes dyspnea and catarrh. The portion that settles in the head injures the head. Then, from the injury to the chest, from the irregular movement of <s>vāyu</s>, and from the irritation of the throat, a constant cough arises in him. Because of the persistence of coughing, when there is injury in the chest, he spits blood; and from the appearance of blood, weakness arises in him. Thus these complications born of rash overexertion affect the rashly overexerted man.
Then, afflicted by these wasting complications, he dries up little by little.

children.text: tasmāt puruṣo matimān balamātmanaḥ samīkṣya tadanurūpāṇi karmāṇyārabheta kartuṃ balasamādhānaṃ hi śarīraṃ śarīramūlaśca puruṣa iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore a wise man, after considering his own strength, should undertake actions suited to it. For the body depends on the establishment of strength, and the person has the body as his root.
And here there is this verse:
Guarding his own life, one should avoid rash action,
for only while living does a man enjoy the desired fruit of action.

children.text: saṃdhāraṇaṃ śoṣasyāyatanamiti yaduktaṃ tadanuvyākhyāsyāmaḥyadā puruṣo rājasamīpe bhartuḥ samīpe vā gurorvā pādamūle dyūtasabhamanyaṃ vā satāṃ samājaṃ strīmadhyaṃ vā samanupraviśya yānairvāpyuccāvacair abhiyān bhayāt prasaṅgāddhrīmattvādghṛṇitvād vā niruṇaddhyāgatān vātamūtrapurīṣavegān tadā tasya saṃdhāraṇādvāyuḥ prakopamāpadyate sa prakupitaḥ pittaśleṣmāṇau samudīryordhvamadhastiryak ca viharati tataścāṃśaviśeṣeṇa pūrvavaccharīrāvayavaviśeṣaṃ praviśya śūlamupajanayati bhinatti purīṣamucchoṣayati vā pārśve cātirujati aṃsāvavamṛdnāti kaṇṭhamuraścāvadhamati śiraścopahanti kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ jvaraṃ svarabhedaṃ pratiśyāyaṃ copajanayati tataḥ sa upaśoṣaṇair etair upadravair upadrutaḥ śanaiḥ śanairupaśuṣyati
children.translated_text: What was said as "suppression is a basis of <s>śoṣa</s>" will be explained in detail. When a man, having entered the presence of a king, the presence of a master, the feet of a teacher, a gambling hall, another assembly of respectable people, or the company of women, or while traveling in high and low vehicles, suppresses arisen urges of flatus, urine, and feces out of fear, attachment to the occasion, modesty, or disgust, then because of that suppression his <s>vāyu</s> becomes aggravated. Once aggravated, it stirs up <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> and moves upward, downward, and crosswise. Then, by a particular portion, as before, entering a particular bodily part, it produces colic, breaks up or dries up the feces, causes severe pain in the flank, crushes the shoulders, distends the throat and chest, injures the head, and produces cough, dyspnea, fever, alteration of the voice, and catarrh. Then, afflicted by these wasting complications, he dries up little by little.

children.text: tasmāt puruṣo matimānātmanaḥ śārīreṣveva yogakṣemakareṣu prayateta viśeṣeṇa śarīraṃ hyasya mūlaṃ śarīramūlaśca puruṣo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore a wise person should make special effort precisely with respect to those bodily means that secure his own acquisition and preservation, for the body is his root, and the person has the body as his root.
And here there is this verse:
Abandoning everything else, one should protect the body.
For when it is absent, all states of embodied beings are absent.

children.text: kṣayaḥ śoṣasyāyatanamiti yaduktaṃ tadanuvyākhyāsyāmaḥyadā puruṣo 'timātraṃ śokacintāparigatahṛdayo bhavati īrṣyotkaṇṭhābhayakrodhādibhirvā samāviśyate kṛśo vā san rūkṣānnapānasevī bhavati durbalaprakṛtiranāhāro 'lpāhāro vā bhavati tadā tasya hṛdayasthāyī rasaḥ kṣayamupaiti sa tasyopakṣayācchoṣaṃ prāpnoti apratīkārāccānubadhyate yakṣmaṇā yathopadekṣyamāṇarūpeṇa yadā vā puruṣo 'tiharṣādatiprasaktabhāvaḥ strīṣvatiprasaṅgamārabhate tasyātimātraprasaṅgādretaḥ kṣayameti
