children.text: dṛśyante hi khalu saumya nakṣatragrahagaṇacandrasūryānilānalānāṃ diśāṃ cāprakṛtibhūtānāmṛtuvaikārikā bhāvāḥ acirādito bhūr api ca na yathāvad rasavīryavipākaprabhāvam oṣadhīnāṃ pratividhāsyati tadviyogāccātaṅkaprāyatā niyatā
children.translated_text: "Indeed, my gentle one, abnormal seasonal states are seen among the constellations, planets, groups of stars, moon, sun, wind, fire, and directions when they have become unnatural. And before long the earth too will not duly supply the taste, potency, post-digestive effect, and specific action of medicinal plants; and because of the loss of these, a prevalence of disease is certain.

children.text: tasmāt prāguddhvaṃsāt prāk ca bhūmer virasībhāvād uddharadhvaṃ saumya bhaiṣajyāni yāvan nopahatarasavīryavipākaprabhāvāṇi bhavanti
children.translated_text: Therefore, before the destruction, and before the earth becomes devoid of taste, gather the medicines, my gentle one, while their taste, potency, post-digestive effect, and specific action have not yet been impaired.

children.text: vayaṃ caiṣāṃ rasavīryavipākaprabhāvān upayokṣyāmahe ye cāsmān anukāṅkṣanti yāṃśca vayam anukāṅkṣāmaḥ
children.translated_text: We shall make use of their taste, potency, post-digestive effect, and specific action, as will those who look to us and those whom we look to.

children.text: na hi samyaguddhṛteṣu saumya bhaiṣajyeṣu samyagvihiteṣu samyak cāvacāriteṣu janapadoddhvaṃsakarāṇāṃ vikārāṇāṃ kiṃcit pratīkāragauravaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For when medicines have been properly gathered, properly prepared, and properly administered, there is no great difficulty in counteracting disorders that bring about the destruction of communities."

children.text: evaṃvādinaṃ bhagavantamātreyamagniveśa uvāca uddhṛtāni khalu bhagavan bhaiṣajyāni samyagvihitāni samyagavacāritāni ca api tu khalu janapadoddhvaṃsanam ekenaiva vyādhinā yugapad asamānaprakṛtyāhāradehabalasātmyasattvavayasāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ kasmādbhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: When the venerable <s>Ātreya</s> had spoken thus, <s>Agniveśa</s> said, "Venerable sir, the medicines have been gathered, properly prepared, and properly administered. But why does the destruction of communities occur at the same time through one and the same disease among people whose constitutions, diets, bodies, strength, suitability, minds, and ages are unlike?"

children.text: tamuvāca bhagavānātreyaḥ evam asāmānyāvatām apyebhir agniveśa prakṛtyādibhir bhāvair manuṣyāṇāṃ ye'nye bhāvāḥ sāmānyāstadvaiguṇyāt samānakālāḥ samānaliṅgāśca vyādhayo 'bhinirvartamānā janapadam uddhvaṃsayanti
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Ātreya</s> said to him, "Even though people are dissimilar with respect to constitution and the other factors, <s>Agniveśa</s>, there are other factors common to them. Through the impairment of those common factors, diseases arise at the same time and with the same symptoms, and they destroy a community.

children.text: te tu khalvime bhāvāḥ sāmānyā janapadeṣu bhavanti tadyathā vāyur udakaṃ deśaḥ kāla iti ||
children.translated_text: Now these are the common factors among communities: wind, water, place, and season.

children.text: tatra vātam evaṃvidham anārogyakaraṃ vidyāt tadyathā yathartuviṣamam atistimitam aticalam atiparuṣam atiśītam atyuṣṇam atirūkṣam atyabhiṣyandinam atibhairavārāvam atipratihataparasparagatim atikuṇḍalinam asātmyagandhabāṣpasikatāpāṃśudhūmopahatam iti udakaṃ tu khalvatyarthavikṛtagandhavarṇarasasparśaṃ kledabahulam apakrāntajalacaravihaṅgam upakṣīṇajaleśayam aprītikaram apagataguṇaṃ vidyāt deśaṃ punaḥ prakṛtivikṛtavarṇagandharasasparśaṃ kledabahulam upasṛṣṭaṃ sarīsṛpavyālamaśakaśalabhamakṣikāmūṣakolūkaśmāśānikaśakunijambūkādibhis tṛṇolūpopavanavantaṃ pratānādibahulam apūrvavadavapatitaśuṣkanaṣṭaśasyaṃ dhūmrapavanaṃ pradhmātapatatrigaṇam utkruṣṭaśvagaṇam udbhrāntavyathitavividhamṛgapakṣisaṅgham utsṛṣṭanaṣṭadharmasatyalajjācāraśīlaguṇajanapadaṃ śaśvatkṣubhitodīrṇasalilāśayaṃ pratatolkāpātanirghātabhūmikampam atibhayārāvarūpaṃ rūkṣatāmrāruṇasitābhrajālasaṃvṛtārkacandratārakam abhīkṣṇaṃ sasaṃbhramodvegam iva satrāsaruditamiva satamaskam iva guhyakācaritam ivākranditaśabdabahulaṃ cāhitaṃ vidyāt kālaṃ tu khalu yathartuliṅgādviparītaliṅgam atiliṅgaṃ hīnaliṅgaṃ cāhitaṃ vyavasyet imān evaṃdoṣayuktāṃścaturo bhāvāñjanapadoddhvaṃsakarān vadanti kuśalāḥ ato'nyathābhūtāṃstu hitān ācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: In that regard, one should know wind of the following kind to be injurious to health: wind contrary to the season, excessively still, excessively violent, excessively harsh, excessively cold, excessively hot, excessively dry, excessively moist and obstructive, making an extremely terrifying sound, having motions that strike against one another, excessively whirling, and spoiled by unsuitable smells, vapors, gravel, dust, and smoke. Water, in turn, should be known as having excessively altered smell, color, taste, and touch, being full of slime, abandoned by aquatic creatures and birds, with its reservoirs diminished, unpleasant, and bereft of its qualities. Place, again, should be known as harmful when its natural color, smell, taste, and touch are altered; when it is full of slime, overrun with reptiles, beasts, mosquitoes, moths, flies, mice, owls, cremation-ground birds, jackals, and the like; when it has grasses, creepers, and groves, many spreading plants and the like; when its crops have fallen, dried up, or been destroyed as never before; when its winds are smoky, flocks of birds are blown about, packs of dogs howl, and various herds of animals and birds are bewildered and distressed; when its people have abandoned or lost <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), truth, modesty, conduct, character, and virtue; when its bodies of water are constantly agitated and swollen; when meteors, thunderbolts, and earthquakes are frequent; when its sounds and forms are extremely terrifying; when the sun, moon, and stars are covered by networks of dry, coppery, reddish, white clouds; when it seems continually filled with confusion and agitation, as if frightened and weeping, as if full of darkness, as if haunted by guhyakas, and full of cries. Season, moreover, should be judged harmful when it has signs opposite to the proper marks of the season, excessive signs, or deficient signs. The skilled call these four factors, when endowed with such faults, causes of the destruction of communities; those that are otherwise they declare to be beneficial.

children.text: viguṇeṣvapi khalveteṣu janapadoddhvaṃsakareṣu bhāveṣu bheṣajenopapādyamānānām abhayaṃ bhavati rogebhya iti ||
children.translated_text: Even when these factors that cause the destruction of communities are impaired, those who are properly supplied with medicine have freedom from fear of diseases."
And here there are verses:
The relative gravity of place, season, wind, and water
when they have become impaired will be explained in particular, along with its cause.
One who understands the matter should know water to be naturally weightier than wind, place than water,
and season weightier than place, because each is harder to avoid.
But one who knows the particulars of the faults described in wind and the other factors
should recognize relative lightness by the ease of counteraction.

children.text: caturṣvapi tu duṣṭeṣu kālānteṣu yadā narāḥ
children.translated_text: Yet when all four are corrupted, and at the end of a season people
are properly supplied with medicine, then they do not become afflicted.

children.text: yeṣāṃ na mṛtyusāmānyaṃ sāmānyaṃ na ca karmaṇām
children.translated_text: For those who do not share a common death, and whose actions are not common,
the fivefold action is said to be the supreme medicine.
The proper use of <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative therapy) is commended,
and the maintenance of the body is recommended with medicines gathered beforehand.

children.text: sasyaṃ bhūte dayā dānaṃ balayo devatārcanam
children.translated_text: Also what is beneficial among crops, compassion for beings, giving, offerings, worship of deities,
following good conduct, pacification, and guarding oneself;
what is wholesome for communities, association with auspicious persons,
the practice of celibacy, and likewise service to celibate students;
conversation on treatises of <s>dharma</s> with great seers who have mastered themselves,
and constant sitting together with righteous, sattvic people approved by elders."
Thus this medicine for the preservation of life has been taught
for those whose death is not fixed in that very dreadful time.

children.text: iti śrutvā janapadoddhvaṃsane kāraṇāni punarapi bhagavantamātreyam agniveśa uvācātha khalu bhagavan kutomūlam eṣāṃ vāyvādīnāṃ vaiguṇyam utpadyate yenopapannā janapadamuddhvaṃsayantīti ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this concerning the causes in the destruction of communities, <s>Agniveśa</s> again addressed the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>: "Now then, venerable sir, from what root does this defectiveness of wind and the other factors arise, by which, when affected, they destroy a community?"

children.text: tamuvāca bhagavānātreyaḥ sarveṣām apyagniveśa vāyvādīnāṃ yadvaiguṇyamutpadyate tasya mūlamadharmaḥ tanmūlaṃ vāsatkarma pūrvakṛtaṃ tayoryoniḥ prajñāparādha eva
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Ātreya</s> said to him: "<s>Agniveśa</s>, the root of whatever defectiveness arises in all these, wind and the others, is <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness); and its root is bad action done previously. The source of both of these is precisely <s>prajñāparādha</s> (error of judgment).

children.text: tadyathā yadā vai deśanagaranigamajanapadapradhānā dharmam utkramyādharmeṇa prajāṃ vartayanti tadāśritopāśritāḥ paurajanapadā vyavahāropajīvinaśca tamadharmam abhivardhayanti tataḥ so'dharmaḥ prasabhaṃ dharmam antardhatte tataste 'ntarhitadharmāṇo devatābhirapi tyajyante teṣāṃ tathāntarhitadharmaṇām adharmapradhānānām apakrāntadevatānām ṛtavo vyāpadyante tena nāpo yathākālaṃ devo varṣati na vā varṣati vikṛtaṃ vā varṣati vātā na samyagabhivānti kṣitirvyāpadyate salilānyupaśuṣyanti oṣadhayaḥ svabhāvaṃ parihāyāpadyante vikṛtiṃ tata uddhvaṃsante janapadāḥ spṛśyābhyavahāryadoṣāt ||
children.translated_text: For example, when the leaders of a country, city, market-town, and community, having transgressed <s>dharma</s>, direct the people by <s>adharma</s>, then the townspeople, country people, dependents, subdependents, and those who live by dealings increase that <s>adharma</s>. Then that <s>adharma</s> forcibly obscures <s>dharma</s>. Then, when <s>dharma</s> has been obscured, even the deities abandon them. For those whose <s>dharma</s> is thus obscured, who are dominated by <s>adharma</s>, and from whom the deities have departed, the seasons become disturbed. Because of this the god of rain does not rain waters at the proper time, or he does not rain, or he rains in a distorted way; the winds do not blow properly; the earth is disturbed; the waters dry up; plants, abandoning their own nature, undergo distortion. From this, communities are destroyed because of defects in what is touched and eaten.
Likewise, in the destruction of communities that arises from weapons too, <s>adharma</s> alone is the cause.

children.text: ye 'tipravṛddhalobhakrodhamohamānās te durbalān avamatyātmasvajanaparopaghātāya śastreṇa parasparam abhikrāmanti parān vābhikrāmanti parair vābhikrāmyante ||
children.translated_text: Those whose greed, anger, delusion, and pride have become excessive, disregarding the weak, attack one another with weapons for the injury of themselves, their own people, and others; or they attack others, or are attacked by others.

children.text: rakṣogaṇādibhirvā vividhair bhūtasaṅghais tamadharmam anyad vāpyapacārāntaram upalabhyābhihanyante ||
children.translated_text: Or, when that <s>adharma</s> or some other improper conduct has been perceived, they are struck down by groups of <s>rakṣases</s> and other various hosts of beings.
Likewise, in the destruction that arises from curses too, <s>adharma</s> alone is the cause.

children.text: ye luptadharmāṇo dharmād apetāste guruvṛddhasiddharṣipūjyān avamatyāhitānyācaranti tatastāḥ prajā gurvādibhirabhiśaptā bhasmatām upayānti prāgevānekapuruṣakulavināśāya niyatapratyayopalambhād aniyatāś cāpare ||
children.translated_text: Those whose <s>dharma</s> has been lost and who have fallen away from <s>dharma</s>, disregarding teachers, elders, perfected beings, seers, and venerable persons, do what is unwholesome. Then those people, cursed by teachers and the others, are reduced to ashes. Some are destined beforehand for the destruction of many men and families, because a determinate causal condition is observed; others are indeterminate.
And even formerly, apart from <s>adharma</s>, no arising of misfortune occurred from anything else.

children.text: ādikāle hyaditisutasamaujaso 'tivimalavipulaprabhāvāḥ pratyakṣadevadevarṣidharmayajñavidhividhānāḥ śailasārasaṃhatasthiraśarīrāḥ prasannavarṇendriyāḥ pavanasamabalajavaparākramāścārusphico 'bhirūpapramāṇākṛtiprasādopacayavantaḥ satyārjavānṛśaṃsyadānadamaniyamatapa'upavāsabrahmacaryavrataparā vyapagatabhayarāgadveṣamohalobhakrodhaśokamānaroganidrātandrāśramaklamālasyaparigrahāśca puruṣā babhūvur amitāyuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: For in the beginning age, men were equal in strength to the sons of <s>Aditi</s>, possessed of extremely pure and vast power, directly connected with deities, divine seers, <s>dharma</s>, and sacrificial rites, with bodies firm and compact like the substance of mountains, with clear complexion and senses, with strength, speed, and valor equal to the wind, with lovely buttocks, handsome, endowed with proper measure, form, clarity, and bodily increase, devoted to truth, straightforwardness, non-cruelty, giving, restraint, observance, austerity, fasting, celibacy, and vows, free from fear, passion, hatred, delusion, greed, anger, grief, pride, disease, sleep, drowsiness, fatigue, exhaustion, laziness, and possessiveness, and having immeasurable lifespans.

children.text: teṣām udārasattvaguṇakarmaṇām acintyarasavīryavipākaprabhāvaguṇasamuditāni prādurbabhūvuḥ śasyāni sarvaguṇasamuditatvāt pṛthivyādīnāṃ kṛtayugasyādau
children.translated_text: For those whose mental quality, virtues, and actions were noble, grains appeared endowed with inconceivable qualities of taste, potency, postdigestive effect, power, and influence, because earth and the other elements were endowed with all qualities at the beginning of the <s>kṛtayuga</s>.

children.text: bhraśyati tu kṛtayuge keṣāṃcid atyādānāt sāṃpannikānāṃ sattvānāṃ śarīragauravam āsīt śarīragauravācchramaḥ śramādālasyam ālasyāt saṃcayaḥ saṃcayāt parigrahaḥ parigrahāllobhaḥ prādurāsīt kṛte
children.translated_text: But as the <s>kṛtayuga</s> declined, through excessive taking by certain affluent beings, heaviness of the body arose. From bodily heaviness came fatigue; from fatigue, laziness; from laziness, accumulation; from accumulation, possession; and from possession, greed appeared in the <s>kṛta</s> age.

children.text: tatastretāyāṃ lobhād abhidrohaḥ abhidrohānṛtavacanam anṛtavacanāt kāmakrodhamānadveṣapāruṣyābhighātabhayatāpaśokacintodvegādayaḥ pravṛttāḥ
children.translated_text: Then in the <s>tretā</s>, from greed came hostility; from hostility, false speech; and from false speech there proceeded desire, anger, pride, hatred, harshness, assault, fear, heat, grief, worry, anxiety, and the like.
Then in the <s>tretā</s>, one quarter of <s>dharma</s> disappeared.
With its disappearance there occurred a loss of one quarter in the measure of the years of the age, and the destruction of one quarter of the qualities of earth and the other elements.
And because of that destruction, there was a fall of one quarter in the unctuousness, purity, taste, potency, postdigestive effect, power, and qualities of grains.

children.text: tatastāni prajāśarīrāṇi hīyamānaguṇapādair āhāravihārair ayathāpūrvam upaṣṭabhyamānānyagnimārutaparītāni prāgvyādhibhir jvarādibhir ākrāntāni
children.translated_text: Then those bodies of creatures, being supported in a manner unlike before by foods and conduct whose qualities were diminished by one quarter, afflicted by fire and wind, were first attacked by diseases beginning with fever.

children.text: ataḥ prāṇino hrāsam avāpur āyuṣaḥ kramaśa iti ||
children.translated_text: From this, living beings gradually underwent a decrease of lifespan."
And here there are verses:
In each age, one quarter of <s>dharma</s> diminishes in this sequence,
and one quarter of the qualities of beings; in this way the world dissolves.
When a hundred years are complete, a year undergoes decline
from the lifespan of embodied beings, at the time when whatever measure is accepted for them.
Thus the cause for the first arising of disorders has been stated.

children.text: evaṃvādinaṃ bhagavantamagniveśa uvāca kiṃnu khalu bhagavan niyatakālapramāṇamāyuḥ sarvaṃ na veti ||
children.translated_text: When the venerable one had spoken thus, <s>Agniveśa</s> said: "Venerable sir, is the whole lifespan fixed in measure by time, or not?"
The venerable one said to him:
"Here, <s>Agniveśa</s>, the lifespan of beings depends upon rational application;

children.text: daive puruṣakāre ca sthitaṃ hyasya balābalam ||
children.translated_text: for its strength and weakness rest in both fate and human effort.

children.text: daivam ātmakṛtaṃ vidyāt karma yat paurvadaihikam
children.translated_text: One should know fate as action done by oneself, belonging to a former body;
but human effort is remembered as the further action that is done here.
There is a distinction of strength and weakness in both of those actions also."

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ hi trividhaṃ karma hīnaṃ madhyamam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: For action is indeed observed to be threefold: deficient, middling, and excellent.

children.text: tayor udārayor yuktir dīrghasya ca sukhasya ca
children.translated_text: The conjunction of the two excellent ones is the cause of a life that is long and happy,
and fixed in its term; the contrary conjunction is the cause of the contrary.
The middling one is held to be the cause of a middling life. And hear another cause:
for weak fate is overcome by human exertion.
And the other action is overcome by a superior fate.
Seeing this, some people think that the measure of life is fixed.

children.text: karma kiṃcit kvacit kāle vipāke niyataṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Some action, in a certain place and at a certain time, being great, is fixed in its fruition;
but some is not fixed as to time and is awakened by causal conditions.
Therefore, since both cases are observed, the adoption of an absolute position is unsound.

children.text: nidarśanam api cātrodāhariṣyāmaḥ yadi hi niyatakālapramāṇam āyuḥ sarvaṃ syāt tadāyuṣkāmāṇāṃ na mantrauṣadhimaṇimaṅgalabalyupahārahomaniyamaprāyaścittopavāsasvastyayanapraṇipātagamanādyāḥ kriyā iṣṭayaśca prayojyeran nodbhrāntacaṇḍacapalagogajoṣṭrakharaturagamahiṣādayaḥ pavanādayaśca duṣṭāḥ parihāryāḥ syuḥ na prapātagiriviṣamadurgāmbuvegāḥ tathā na pramattonmattodbhrāntacaṇḍacapalamohalobhākulamatayaḥ nārayaḥ na pravṛddho'gniḥ ca vividhaviṣāśrayāḥ sarīsṛporagādayaḥ na sāhasaṃ nādeśakālacaryā na narendraprakopa iti evamādayo hi bhāvā nābhāvakarāḥ syuḥ āyuṣaḥ sarvasya niyatakālapramāṇatvāt
children.translated_text: And here too we shall give an illustration. If every life had a fixed measure of time, then for those who desire long life, practices such as mantras, medicines, jewels, auspicious rites, offerings, gifts, oblations, observances, expiations, fasts, rites for welfare, bowing down, and going to holy places, as well as sacrifices, would not be employed. Nor would one have to avoid deranged, fierce, and restless cattle, elephants, camels, donkeys, horses, buffaloes, and the like, nor harmful winds, nor precipices, mountains, difficult terrain, and rushing waters. Likewise one would not have to avoid negligent, mad, deranged, fierce, restless, deluded, greedy, and confused-minded men or enemies, nor a raging fire, nor various venomous creatures such as creeping things and snakes, nor rash action, nor conduct unsuitable to place and time, nor the anger of a king. For such things and the like would not be destroyers of life, since the measure of time for every life would be fixed.

children.text: na cānabhyastākālamaraṇabhayanivārakāṇām akālamaraṇabhayam āgacchet prāṇināṃ vyarthāścārambhakathāprayogabuddhayaḥ syurmaharṣīṇāṃ rasāyanādhikāre nāpīndro niyatāyuṣaṃ śatruṃ vajreṇābhihanyāt nāśvināvārtaṃ bheṣajenopapādayetāṃ na maharṣayo yatheṣṭam āyus tapasā prāpnuyuḥ na ca viditaveditavyā maharṣayaḥ sasureśāḥ samyak paśyeyur upadiśeyurācareyurvā
children.translated_text: Nor would fear of untimely death come upon living beings who had not practiced measures that avert the danger of untimely death. The activities, teachings, applications, and reasoning of the great seers in the section on <s>rasāyana</s> would be useless. Nor would <s>Indra</s> strike down an enemy of fixed lifespan with his thunderbolt; nor would the <s>Aśvins</s> restore one who was afflicted by means of medicine; nor would great seers obtain life as they wished through austerity. Nor would the great seers, together with the lord of the gods, knowing what is to be known, rightly see, teach, or practice.

children.text: api ca sarvacakṣuṣāmetat paraṃ yadaindraṃ cakṣuḥ idaṃ cāpyasmākaṃ tena pratyakṣaṃ yathā puruṣasahasrāṇām utthāyotthāyāhavaṃ kurvatām akurvatāṃ cātulyāyuṣṭvaṃ tathā jātamātrāṇām apratīkārāt pratīkārācca aviṣaviṣaprāśināṃ cāpyatulyāyuṣṭvameva na ca tulyo yogakṣema udapānaghaṭānāṃ citraghaṭānāṃ cotsīdatāṃ tasmāddhitopacāramūlaṃ jīvitam ato viparyayānmṛtyuḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, among all eyes, the eye belonging to <s>Indra</s> is supreme; and even to our eye this is directly evident: just as thousands of men who rise again and again to fight in battle and those who do not fight have unequal lifespans, so too newborn infants, depending on whether treatment is absent or present, and those who ingest poison and those who do not, have unequal lifespans. The preservation of water-pots and painted pots is not the same when they are sinking. Therefore life is rooted in wholesome care, and death in the opposite.

children.text: api ca deśakālātmaguṇaviparītānāṃ karmaṇām āhāravikārāṇāṃ ca kramopayogaḥ samyak tyāgaḥ sarvasya cātiyogāyogamithyāyogānāṃ sarvātiyogasaṃdhāraṇam asaṃdhāraṇam udīrṇānāṃ ca gatimatāṃ sāhasānāṃ ca varjanam ārogyānuvṛttau hetum upalabhāmahe samyagupadiśāmaḥ samyak paśyāmaśceti ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, we recognize, teach correctly, and see correctly that the sequential use of actions and changes of diet contrary to place, time, and one's own qualities, and the proper abandonment of all such things; the abandonment of every overuse, non-use, and wrong use; restraint from every excessive indulgence; non-suppression of arisen urges that are moving; and avoidance of rash acts are causes for the continuance of health.

children.text: ataḥ paramagniveśa uvāca evaṃ satyaniyatakālapramāṇāyuṣāṃ bhagavan kathaṃ kālamṛtyurakālamṛtyurvā bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: After this <s>Agniveśa</s> said: "If this is so, venerable sir, how can there be death in due time or death out of due time for those whose lifespans do not have a fixed measure of time?"

children.text: tamuvāca bhagavānātreyaḥ śrūyatāmagniveśa yathā yānasamāyukto'kṣaḥ prakṛtyaivākṣaguṇairupetaḥ sa ca sarvaguṇopapanno vāhyamāno yathākālaṃ svapramāṇakṣayād evāvasānaṃ gacchet tathāyuḥ śarīropagataṃ balavatprakṛtyā yathāvadupacaryamāṇaṃ svapramāṇakṣayād evāvasānaṃ gacchati sa mṛtyuḥ kāle
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Ātreya</s> said to him: "Listen, <s>Agniveśa</s>. Just as an axle joined to a vehicle, naturally endowed with the qualities of an axle, and possessing all its qualities while being driven, reaches its end in due time solely through the exhaustion of its own measure, so life, lodged in the body, strong by nature and properly cared for, reaches its end solely through the exhaustion of its own measure. That is death in due time.

children.text: yathā ca sa evākṣo 'tibhārādhiṣṭhitatvād viṣamapathād apathād akṣacakrabhaṅgād vāhyavāhakadoṣād aṇimokṣād anupāṅgāt paryasanāccāntarāvasānam āpadyate tathāyurapyayathābalam ārambhād ayathāgnyabhyavaharaṇād viṣamābhyavaharaṇād viṣamaśarīranyāsād atimaithunād asatsaṃśrayād udīrṇavegavinigrahād vidhāryavegāvidhāraṇād bhūtaviṣavāyvagnyupatāpād abhighātād āhārapratīkāravivarjanāccāntarāvasānam āpadyate sa mṛtyurakāle tathā jvarādīn apyātaṅkān mithyopacaritān akālamṛtyūn paśyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: And just as that same axle, because it is burdened with too much weight, because of uneven or bad roads, because of the breaking of the axle or wheel, because of faults in the draught animal or driver, because the pin is loosened, because an accessory is missing, or because of overturning, comes to an end in the middle of its course, so life too comes to an end in the middle through undertakings beyond one's strength, eating in a way unsuitable to the digestive fire, irregular eating, improper placement of the body, excessive sexual intercourse, association with bad people, suppression of arisen urges, failure to restrain urges that should be restrained, injury from beings, poison, wind, or fire, trauma, and neglect of diet and countermeasures. That is death out of due time. Thus we also observe illnesses such as <s>jvara</s> (fever), when wrongly treated, to be causes of untimely death."

children.text: athāgniveśaḥ papraccha kiṃnu khalu bhagavan jvaritebhyaḥ pānīyamuṣṇaṃ prayacchanti bhiṣajo bhūyiṣṭhaṃ na tathā śītam asti ca śītasādhyo'pi dhāturjvarakara iti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Agniveśa</s> asked: "Venerable sir, why do physicians mostly give warm water to fever patients, and not cold water in the same way, although there is also a fever-producing bodily factor curable by cold?"

children.text: tamuvāca bhagavānātreyaḥ jvaritasya kāyasamutthānadeśakālān abhisamīkṣya pācanārthaṃ pānīyamuṣṇaṃ prayacchanti bhiṣajaḥ
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Ātreya</s> said to him: "After considering the fever patient's body, origin of the disease, place, and time, physicians give warm water as a drink for the purpose of digestion.

children.text: jvaro hyāmāśayasamutthaḥ prāyo bheṣajāni cāmāśayasamutthānāṃ vikārāṇāṃ pācanavamanāpatarpaṇasamarthāni bhavanti pācanārthaṃ ca pānīyamuṣṇaṃ tasmād etajjvaritebhyaḥ prayacchanti bhiṣajo bhūyiṣṭham
children.translated_text: For <s>jvara</s> (fever) most often arises from the <s>āmāśaya</s> (stomach), and medicines for disorders arising from the <s>āmāśaya</s> are capable of digestion, emesis, and depletion. Warm water as a drink is for the purpose of digestion; therefore physicians mostly give it to fever patients."

children.text: taddhi teṣāṃ pītaṃ vātam anulomayati agniṃ codaryam udīrayati kṣipraṃ jarāṃ gacchati śleṣmāṇaṃ pariśoṣayati svalpamapi ca pītaṃ tṛṣṇāpraśamanāyopakalpate tathā yuktam api caitannātyarthotsannapitte jvare sadāhabhramapralāpātisāre vā pradeyam uṣṇena hi dāhabhramapralāpātisārā bhūyo'bhivardhante śīte na copaśāmyantīti ||
children.translated_text: For when that has been drunk by them, it makes <s>vāta</s> move in its proper downward course, stimulates the digestive fire in the abdomen, goes quickly to digestion, dries up <s>śleṣman</s>, and even when drunk in a small amount is useful for quenching thirst. Yet even though it is appropriate in this way, it should not be given in fever when <s>pitta</s> is excessively increased, or when there is burning, dizziness, delirious speech, or diarrhea; for burning, dizziness, delirious speech, and diarrhea increase further with heat, and with cold they do not subside.
And here there is a verse:
Physicians who know medicine pacify diseases caused by heat with cold;
but diseases caused by cold are conquered by physicians with heat.

children.text: evamitareṣāmapi vyādhīnāṃ nidānaviparītaṃ bheṣajaṃ bhavati yathāpatarpaṇanimittānāṃ vyādhīnāṃ nāntareṇa pūraṇamasti śāntiḥ tathā pūraṇanimittānāṃ vyādhīnāṃ nāntareṇāpatarpaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Thus for other diseases also, the medicine is opposite to the cause. For example, diseases caused by depletion have no pacification without replenishment, and likewise diseases caused by replenishment have none without depletion.

children.text: apatarpaṇamapi ca trividhaṃ laṅghanaṃ laṅghanapācanaṃ doṣāvasecanaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: Depletion too is threefold: <s>laṅghana</s> (lightening), <s>laṅghana-pācana</s> (lightening with digestive treatment), and <s>doṣāvasecana</s> (evacuation of the doṣas).

children.text: tatra laṅghanam alpabaladoṣāṇāṃ laṅghanena hyagnimārutavṛddhyā vātātapaparītam ivālpam udakamalpo doṣaḥ praśoṣamāpadyate laṅghanapācane tu madhyabaladoṣāṇāṃ laṅghanapācanābhyāṃ hi sūryasaṃtāpamārutābhyāṃ pāṃśubhasmāvakiraṇairiva cānatibahūdakaṃ madhyabalo doṣaḥ praśoṣam āpadyate bahudoṣāṇāṃ punardoṣāvasecanameva kāryaṃ na hyabhinne kedārasetau palvalāpraseko'sti tadvad doṣāvasecanam ||
children.translated_text: There, <s>laṅghana</s> is for doṣas of slight strength; for by <s>laṅghana</s>, through the increase of digestive fire and wind, a small doṣa becomes dried up like a small amount of water surrounded by wind and sun. <s>Laṅghana-pācana</s>, however, is for doṣas of middling strength; for by <s>laṅghana</s> and digestive treatment a doṣa of middling strength becomes dried up like a not very large amount of water by the heat of the sun and by wind, with dust and ash strewn over it. But for abundant doṣas, evacuation of the doṣas alone should be done; for when the bank of a field has not been breached, there is no draining of a pond. So it is with evacuation of the doṣas.
One should not administer evacuation of the doṣas, or any other medicine, to such a patient, even if the proper time has arrived:

namely, one for whom no remedy is possible against criticism, one who is poor, one without attendants, one who thinks himself a physician, one who is violent, one who is envious, one who has a sharp dislike for dharma and artha, one whose strength, flesh, and blood are extremely wasted, one afflicted by an incurable disease, and one marked by signs of impending death.

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ hyāturam upacaran bhiṣak pāpīyasāyaśasā yogam ṛcchatīti ||
children.translated_text: For a physician treating such a patient comes into association with very bad disrepute.
And here there is a verse:

children.text: tadātve cānubandhe vā yasya syādaśubhaṃ phalam
children.translated_text: An action whose result would be inauspicious, either immediately or in consequence,
should not be done. This is the opinion of the wise.
A region that has little water and few trees, is windy, and has abundant sun

children.text: jñeyaḥ sa jāṅgalo deśaḥ svalparogatamo'pi ca ||
children.translated_text: should be known as <s>jāṅgala</s> land, and also as having the least disease.
One that has abundant water and trees, is sheltered from wind, and has little sun
is <s>anūpa</s>, having many doṣas; the intermediate is regarded as <s>sādhāraṇa</s>.
Here are the summary verses:
The preliminary signs, the general causes together with their particular marks,
the medicine for the destruction of communities, and the very root of the causes;
the arising of disorder before disease, the process of the waning of life,
and the determination of timely and untimely death among living beings;
how untimely death occurs, how medicine succeeds when properly applied,

children.text: siddhiṃ yātyauṣadhaṃ yeṣāṃ na kuryādyena hetunā ||
children.translated_text: for whom a remedy succeeds, and for what reason one should not treat;
all this, wholly and completely, <s>Ātreya</s>, the best of sages,
declared to <s>Agniveśa</s> in the <s>vimāna</s> called <s>Janapadoddhvaṃsanīya</s>.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the <s>vimāna</s> on the knowledge of the threefold distinction of diseases.
Thus spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: trividhaṃ khalu rogaviśeṣavijñānaṃ bhavati tadyathā āptopadeśaḥ pratyakṣam anumānaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: There is indeed a threefold knowledge of the distinction of diseases, namely: authoritative instruction, perception, and inference.
There, authoritative instruction means the statement of authoritative persons.
For authoritative persons are those who know without error the divisions of reflection and memory, and who see without attachment or distress.
Because they are endowed with such qualities, whatever statement is theirs is a valid means of knowledge.

children.text: apramāṇaṃ punarmattonmattamūrkharaktaduṣṭāduṣṭavacanamiti pratyakṣaṃ tu khalu tadyat svayamindriyairmanasā copalabhyate
children.translated_text: Invalid, however, is speech from the intoxicated, the insane, the foolish, the attached, the corrupted, and the hostile. Perception, in turn, is what is apprehended by one's own senses and also by the mind.
Inference is reasoning that depends on logical connection.

children.text: trividhena khalvanena jñānasamudāyena pūrvaṃ parīkṣya rogaṃ sarvathā sarvamathottarakālam adhyavasānamadoṣaṃ bhavati na hi jñānāvayavena kṛtsne jñeye jñānamutpadyate
children.translated_text: Having first examined a disease by this threefold aggregate of knowledge, and afterward making a decision about the disease in every respect and in its entirety, there is no error. For knowledge of a complete object of knowledge does not arise from only one part of knowledge.

children.text: trividhe tvasmin jñānasamudaye pūrvam āptopadeśājjñānaṃ tataḥ pratyakṣānumānābhyāṃ parīkṣopapadyate
children.translated_text: But when this threefold aggregate of knowledge is present, knowledge first arises from authoritative instruction; then examination is established through perception and inference.

children.text: kiṃ hyanupadiṣṭaṃ pūrvaṃ yattat pratyakṣānumānābhyāṃ parīkṣamāṇo vidyāt
children.translated_text: For what previously untaught thing could one know by examining it through perception and inference?

children.text: tasmād dvividhā parīkṣā jñānavatāṃ pratyakṣam anumānaṃ ca trividhā vā sahopadeśena ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, for those who possess knowledge, examination is twofold, perception and inference, or threefold when instruction is included.

children.text: tatredamupadiśanti buddhimantaḥ rogam ekaikam evaṃprakopaṇam evaṃyonim evamutthānam evamātmānam evamadhiṣṭhānam evaṃvedanam evaṃsaṃsthānam evaṃśabdasparśarūparasagandham evamupadravam evaṃvṛddhisthānakṣayasamanvitam evamudarkam evaṃnāmānam evaṃyogaṃ vidyāt tasminniyaṃ pratīkārārthā pravṛttirathavā nivṛttirityupadeśājjñāyate ||
children.translated_text: In this matter the intelligent give this instruction: one should know each disease as having this kind of aggravation, this kind of source, this kind of arising, this kind of nature, this kind of seat, this kind of sensation, this kind of configuration, this kind of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, this kind of complication, this kind of increase, stability, decrease, and pacification, this kind of outcome, this kind of name, and this kind of therapeutic application. From instruction one knows, 'In this case there is this activity for the sake of treatment, or else abstention from activity.'

children.text: pratyakṣatastu khalu rogatattvaṃ bubhutsuḥ sarvairindriyaiḥ sarvānindriyārthān āturaśarīragatān parīkṣeta anyatra rasajñānāt tadyathā antrakūjanaṃ sandhisphuṭanam aṅgulīparvaṇāṃ ca svaraviśeṣāṃśca ye cānye'pi keciccharīropagatāḥ śabdāḥ syustāñchrotreṇa parīkṣeta varṇasaṃsthānapramāṇacchāyāḥ śarīraprakṛtivikārau cakṣurvaiṣayikāṇi yāni cānyānyanuktāni tāni cakṣuṣā parīkṣeta rasaṃ tu khalvāturaśarīragatam indriyavaiṣayikam apyanumānād avagacchet na hyasya pratyakṣeṇa grahaṇam upapadyate tasmādāturaparipraśnenaivāturamukharasaṃ vidyāt yūkāpasarpaṇena tvasya śarīravairasyaṃ makṣikopasarpaṇena śarīramādhuryaṃ lohitapittasaṃdehe tu kiṃ dhārilohitaṃ lohitapittaṃ veti śvakākabhakṣaṇāddhārilohitam abhakṣaṇāllohitapittam ityanumātavyam evam anyān apyāturaśarīragatān rasānanumimīta gandhāṃstu khalu sarvaśarīragatānāturasya prakṛtivaikārikān ghrāṇena parīkṣeta sparśaṃ ca pāṇinā prakṛtivikṛtiyuktam
children.translated_text: But one who wishes to know the true nature of disease by direct perception should examine, with all the sense faculties, all sense-objects present in the patient's body, except for knowing taste. Thus he should examine by the ear intestinal rumbling, cracking of the joints and of the finger-knuckles, special variations of voice, and whatever other sounds may be present in the body. By the eye he should examine color, shape, size, complexion, the normal and abnormal conditions of the body, and whatever other visible matters have not been mentioned. Taste, however, though it is a sense-object present in the patient's body, should be understood by inference, for apprehending it by direct perception is not possible. Therefore, from questioning the patient one should know the taste in the patient's mouth. From lice moving away one should infer the disagreeable taste of his body, and from flies coming near, the sweetness of the body. When there is doubt about blood, whether it is ordinary blood or <s>lohitapitta</s> (hemorrhagic pitta), it should be inferred to be ordinary blood if dogs and crows eat it, and <s>lohitapitta</s> if they do not eat it. In this same way one should infer other tastes present in the patient's body. The smells throughout the patient's whole body, whether natural or altered, should be examined by the nose, and touch, whether natural or altered, by the hand.
Thus examination by direct perception, by inference, and by authoritative instruction has been stated.

children.text: ime tu khalvanye'pyevameva bhūyo'numānajñeyā bhavanti bhāvāḥ
children.translated_text: Now these other states too are, in just this way, mostly to be known by inference.

children.text: tadyathāgnijaraṇaśaktyā parīkṣeta balaṃ vyāyāmaśaktyā śrotrādīni śabdādyarthagrahaṇena mano'rthāvyabhicaraṇena vijñānaṃ vyavasāyena rajaḥ saṅgena mohamavijñānena krodhamabhidroheṇa śokaṃ dainyena harṣamāmodena prītiṃ toṣeṇa bhayaṃ viṣādena dhairyamaviṣādena vīryamutthānena avasthānamavibhrameṇa śraddhāmabhiprāyeṇa medhāṃ grahaṇena saṃjñāṃ nāmagrahaṇena smṛtiṃ smaraṇena hriyamapatrapaṇena śīlamanuśīlanena dveṣaṃ pratiṣedhena upadhimanubandhena dhṛtim alaulyena vaśyatāṃ vidheyatayā vayobhaktisātmyavyādhisamutthānāni kāladeśopaśayavedanāviśeṣeṇa gūḍhaliṅgaṃ vyādhimupaśayānupaśayābhyāṃ doṣapramāṇaviśeṣam apacāraviśeṣeṇa āyuṣaḥ kṣayamariṣṭaiḥ upasthitaśreyastvaṃ kalyāṇābhiniveśena amalaṃ sattvamavikāreṇa grahaṇyāstu mṛdudāruṇatvaṃ svapnadarśanamabhiprāyaṃ dviṣṭeṣṭasukhaduḥkhāni cāturaparipraśnenaiva vidyāditi ||
children.translated_text: For example, one should examine <s>agni</s> (digestive fire) by the power of digestion, strength by the capacity for exercise, the senses beginning with hearing by their apprehension of sound and the other objects, the mind by its non-deviation from its objects, understanding by determination, <s>rajas</s> by attachment, delusion by lack of understanding, anger by hostility, grief by dejection, joy by delight, affection by satisfaction, fear by despondency, courage by absence of despondency, vigor by initiative, steadiness by absence of bewilderment, faith by intention, intelligence by grasping, recognition by grasping a name, memory by remembering, shame by bashfulness, character by habitual conduct, hatred by rejection, secondary motive by continued attachment, firmness by lack of fickleness, compliance by obedience, and age, diet, suitability, and disease-origin by particular differences in time, place, relief, and pain. A disease with hidden signs should be known by relief or non-relief, a particular measure of the <s>doṣas</s> by a particular offense against regimen, the wasting of life by fatal signs, the presence of future welfare by inclination toward the auspicious, and a stainless <s>sattva</s> by absence of alteration. The softness or harshness of the <s>grahaṇī</s>, dreams seen, intention, and disliked and liked pleasures and pains should be known only by questioning the patient.
And here there are verses: By instruction from authoritative persons, by the instrument of direct perception,
and also by inference, the discerning man should correctly know diseases.
Having considered everything in every way, as far as possible, one who understands the matter

children.text: athādhyavasyet tattve ca kārye ca tadanantaram ||
children.translated_text: should then make a determination both about the reality of the case and, after that, about the action to be done.
One who knows the specific nature of the action and of the reality is not confused in practice.
Unconfused, he obtains the result that arises from absence of delusion.
One who, though knowing the truth, does not enter by the lamp of knowledge and intelligence
into the patient's inner self, does not treat the diseases.
There are two summary verses on this point:
The threefold collection of knowledge concerning all particular diseases,
how authoritative persons teach, and how direct perception is grasped,
and which states are to be known by inference and how: these too the sage of noble understanding
has stated in the <s>Vimāna</s> on the threefold knowledge of disease.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the <s>Srotasāṃ Vimāna</s>, the section on the channels.
Thus spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: yāvantaḥ puruṣe mūrtimanto bhāvaviśeṣāstāvanta evāsmin srotasāṃ prakāraviśeṣāḥ
children.translated_text: As many distinct embodied entities as there are in the person, exactly that many distinct kinds of <s>srotas</s> (channels) are in him.

children.text: sarve hi bhāvāḥ puruṣe nāntareṇa srotāṃsyabhinirvartante kṣayaṃ vāpyabhigacchanti
children.translated_text: For all entities in the person are neither produced nor undergo depletion apart from the <s>srotas</s>.
The <s>srotas</s>, by serving as pathways, convey the <s>dhātus</s> (bodily constituents) as they undergo transformation.

children.text: api caike srotasāmeva samudayaṃ puruṣamicchanti sarvagatatvāt sarvasaratvācca doṣaprakopaṇapraśamanānām
children.translated_text: Moreover, some hold that the person is nothing but the aggregate of the <s>srotas</s>, because the processes that aggravate and pacify the <s>doṣas</s> are all-pervading and move everywhere.

children.text: na tvetadevaṃ yasya hi srotāṃsi yacca vahanti yaccāvahanti yatra cāvasthitāni sarvaṃ tadanyattebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: But this is not so. For that which possesses the <s>srotas</s>, what they carry, what they do not carry, and where they are situated: all of that is different from them.

children.text: atibahutvāt khalu kecid aparisaṃkhyeyānyācakṣate srotāṃsi parisaṅkhyāni punaranye ||
children.translated_text: Because they are exceedingly numerous, some call the <s>srotas</s> innumerable; others, however, say that they can be counted.

children.text: teṣāṃ tu khalu srotasāṃ yathāsthūlaṃ katicitprakārānmūlataśca prakopavijñānataścānuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ ye bhaviṣyantyalamanuktārthajñānāya jñānavatāṃ vijñānāya cājñānavatām
children.translated_text: Of these <s>srotas</s>, then, we shall describe in broad outline some types, according to their roots and according to the knowledge of their aggravation, which will be sufficient for the wise to understand what has not been stated and for the unknowing to gain discernment.

children.text: tadyathā prāṇodakānnarasarudhiramāṃsamedosthimajjaśukramūtrapurīṣasvedavahānīti vātapittaśleṣmaṇāṃ punaḥ sarvaśarīracarāṇāṃ sarvāṇi srotāṃsyayanabhūtāni tadvadatīndriyāṇāṃ punaḥ sattvādīnāṃ kevalaṃ cetanāvaccharīram ayanabhūtam adhiṣṭhānabhūtaṃ ca
children.translated_text: They are those that carry <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), water, food, <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid), blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, semen, urine, feces, and sweat. In the case of <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>śleṣma</s>, since they move throughout the entire body, all the <s>srotas</s> serve as their pathways. Likewise, for supersensible factors such as <s>sattva</s>, only the body endowed with consciousness serves as pathway and support.
When this is the natural condition of the <s>srotas</s>, the body is not afflicted by disorders.

children.text: tatra prāṇavahānāṃ srotasāṃ hṛdayaṃ mūlaṃ mahāsrotaśca praduṣṭānāṃ tu khalveṣāmidaṃ viśeṣavijñānaṃ bhavati tadyathā atisṛṣṭam atibaddhaṃ kupitamalpālpamabhīkṣṇaṃ vā saśabdaśūlam ucchvasantaṃ dṛṣṭvā prāṇavahānyasya srotāṃsi praduṣṭānīti vidyāt
children.translated_text: There, the root of the channels carrying <s>prāṇa</s> is the heart and the great channel. But when these are corrupted, this is the particular recognition of them: if one sees him breathing in a way that is excessively open, excessively obstructed, disturbed, in small repeated breaths, or frequent, with noise and pain, one should know that his <s>prāṇavaha srotas</s>, the channels carrying vital breath, are corrupted.

children.text: udakavahānāṃ srotasāṃ tālumūlaṃ kloma ca praduṣṭānāṃ tu khalveṣāmidaṃ viśeṣavijñānaṃ bhavati tadyathā jihvātālvoṣṭhakaṇṭhaklomaśoṣaṃ pipāsāṃ cātipravṛddhāṃ dṛṣṭvodakavahānyasya srotāṃsi praduṣṭānīti vidyāt
children.translated_text: The root of the channels carrying water is the base of the palate and the <s>kloma</s>. But when these are corrupted, this is the particular recognition of them: if one sees dryness of the tongue, palate, lips, throat, and <s>kloma</s>, and greatly increased thirst, one should know that his water-carrying channels are corrupted.

children.text: annavahānāṃ srotasāmāmāśayo mūlaṃ vāmaṃ ca pārśvaṃ praduṣṭānāṃ tu khalveṣāmidaṃ viśeṣavijñānaṃ bhavati tadyathā anannābhilaṣaṇam arocakavipākau chardiṃ ca dṛṣṭvānnavahānyasya srotāṃsi praduṣṭānīti vidyāt
children.translated_text: The root of the channels carrying food is the stomach and the left side. But when these are corrupted, this is the particular recognition of them: if one sees lack of desire for food, anorexia, indigestion, and vomiting, one should know that his food-carrying channels are corrupted.

children.text: rasavahānāṃ srotasāṃ hṛdayaṃ mūlaṃ daśa ca dhamanyaḥ
children.translated_text: The root of the channels carrying <s>rasa</s> is the heart and the ten vessels.
The root of the channels carrying blood is the liver and the spleen.

children.text: māṃsavahānāṃ ca srotasāṃ snāyurmūlaṃ tvak ca
children.translated_text: The root of the channels carrying flesh is the ligaments and the skin.

children.text: medovahānāṃ srotasāṃ vṛkkau mūlaṃ vapāvahanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: The root of the channels carrying fat is the two kidneys and the fat-bearing omentum.

children.text: asthivahānāṃ srotasāṃ medo mūlaṃ jaghanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: The root of the channels carrying bone is fat and the pelvic region.
The root of the channels carrying marrow is the bones and the joints.
The root of the channels carrying semen is the two testicles and the penis.

children.text: praduṣṭānāṃ tu khalveṣāṃ rasādivahasrotasāṃ vijñānānyuktāni vividhāśitapītīye yānyeva hi dhātūnāṃ pradoṣavijñānāni tānyeva yathāsvaṃ praduṣṭānāṃ dhātusrotasām
children.translated_text: But the signs of these corrupted channels carrying <s>rasa</s> and the other tissues have already been stated in the <s>Vividhāśitapītīya</s> chapter; for the signs of corruption in the tissues themselves are precisely the signs, each in its own case, of the corrupted tissue-channels.

children.text: mūtravahānāṃ srotasāṃ bastirmūlaṃ vaṅkṣaṇau ca praduṣṭānāṃ tu khalveṣāmidaṃ viśeṣavijñānaṃ bhavati tadyathā atisṛṣṭam atibaddhaṃ prakupitam alpālpam abhīkṣṇaṃ vā bahalaṃ saśūlaṃ mūtrayantaṃ dṛṣṭvā mūtravahānyasya srotāṃsi praduṣṭānīti vidyāt
children.translated_text: The root of the channels carrying urine is the bladder and the two groins. But when these are corrupted, this is the particular recognition of them: if one sees him urinating with excessive flow, excessive obstruction, irritation, small amounts, frequent passing, thickness, and pain, one should know that his urine-carrying channels are corrupted.

children.text: purīṣavahānāṃ srotasāṃ pakvāśayo mūlaṃ sthūlagudaṃ ca praduṣṭānāṃ tu khalveṣāmidaṃ viśeṣavijñānaṃ bhavati tadyathā kṛcchreṇālpālpaṃ saśabdaśūlam atidravam atigrathitam atibahu copaviśantaṃ dṛṣṭvā purīṣavahānyasya srotāṃsi praduṣṭānīti vidyāt
children.translated_text: The root of the channels carrying feces is the large intestine and the thick rectum. But when these are corrupted, this is the particular recognition of them: if one sees him evacuating with difficulty, in small amounts, with noise and pain, too liquid, too hard, or too much, one should know that his feces-carrying channels are corrupted.

children.text: svedavahānāṃ srotasāṃ medo mūlaṃ lomakūpāśca praduṣṭānāṃ tu khalveṣāmidaṃ viśeṣavijñānaṃ bhavati tadyathā asvedanam atisvedanaṃ pāruṣyamatiślakṣṇatāmaṅgasya paridāhaṃ lomaharṣaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā svedavahānyasya srotāṃsi praduṣṭānīti vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: The root of the channels carrying sweat is fat and the hair follicles. But when these are corrupted, this is the particular recognition of them: if one sees absence of sweating, excessive sweating, roughness, excessive smoothness of the body, burning over the body, and horripilation, one should know that his sweat-carrying channels are corrupted.

children.text: srotāṃsi sirāḥ dhamanyaḥ rasāyanyaḥ rasavāhinyaḥ nāḍyaḥ panthānaḥ mārgāḥ śarīracchidrāṇi saṃvṛtāsaṃvṛtāni sthānāni āśayāḥ niketāśceti śarīradhātvavakāśānāṃ lakṣyālakṣyāṇāṃ nāmāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: <s>Srotas</s>, veins, arteries, rasa-channels, rasa-carrying channels, tubes, paths, routes, openings in the body, covered and uncovered places, receptacles, and abodes: these are names for the visible and invisible spaces belonging to the bodily tissues.

children.text: teṣāṃ prakopāt sthānasthāścaiva mārgagāśca śarīradhātavaḥ prakopamāpadyante itareṣāṃ prakopāditarāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Through the aggravation of these, the bodily tissues, both those situated in their own places and those moving along the channels, become aggravated; and through the aggravation of other channels, other tissues become aggravated.
When corrupted, channels corrupt channels themselves, and tissues corrupt the tissues themselves.

children.text: teṣāṃ sarveṣāmeva vātapittaśleṣmāṇaḥ praduṣṭā dūṣayitāro bhavanti doṣasvabhāvāditi ||
children.translated_text: For all of them, corrupted <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s> are the corrupting agents, because that is the nature of the <s>doṣas</s>.
And here there are verses:

children.text: kṣayāt saṃdhāraṇād raukṣyād vyāyāmāt kṣudhitasya ca
children.translated_text: From wasting, suppression, dryness, exercise while hungry,
and also from other severe causes, the channels carrying <s>prāṇa</s> become corrupted.
From heat, from <s>āma</s>, from fear, from drinking, from eating excessively dry food,
and from excessive affliction by thirst, the channels carrying water become corrupted.
From eating in excessive quantity, at the wrong time, and what is unwholesome,
and from defect of the digestive fire, the channels carrying food become corrupted.
For those who eat food that is heavy, cold, excessively unctuous, and excessive in quantity,
and from excessive brooding over matters of thought, the channels carrying <s>rasa</s> become corrupted.
For those who resort to burning foods and drinks, unctuous, hot, and liquid things,
and to the sun and fire, the channels carrying blood become corrupted.

children.text: abhiṣyandīni bhojyāni sthūlāni ca gurūṇi ca
children.translated_text: Obstructive foods, and foods that are bulky and heavy,

children.text: māṃsavāhīni duṣyanti bhuktvā ca svapatāṃ divā ||
children.translated_text: and sleeping by day after eating corrupt the channels carrying flesh.
From lack of exercise, sleeping by day, and excessive eating of fattening foods,
and from excessive use of <s>vāruṇī</s> liquor, the channels carrying fat become corrupted.
From exercise, excessive jolting, and excessive striking of the bones,
and from using wind-promoting things, the channels carrying bone become corrupted.
From crushing, excessive obstruction and exudation, injury, and pressure,
and from using incompatible things, the channels carrying marrow become corrupted.
From intercourse at an improper time or with an improper partner, from suppression, and from excessive sexual intercourse,
and likewise from instruments, alkalis, and fire, the channels carrying semen become corrupted.
From resorting to water, foods, and intercourse in a disordered urinary state, and from suppressing urine,
the channels carrying urine become corrupted in one who is depleted or injured.
From suppression, overeating, eating when food is undigested, and eating again on top of a meal,
the channels carrying feces become corrupted in one whose digestive fire is weak and who is emaciated.
From exercise, excessive heat, and irregular use of cold and hot things,
and also from anger, sorrow, and fear, the channels carrying sweat become corrupted.
And diet and regimen that are similar to the qualities of the <s>doṣas</s>...
And when it is also deranged by the bodily constituents, it becomes a polluter of the <s>srotas</s> (channels).

children.text: atipravṛttiḥ saṅgo vā sirāṇāṃ granthayo 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Excessive activity, or obstruction, or knots in the vessels,
and also movement along a wrong path: these are the signs of corruption of the <s>srotas</s>.
The <s>srotas</s> are of the same color as their own bodily constituent; they are round, large, and minute,
long in form, and also resembling branching networks.
For the corrupted channels carrying breath, water, and food, treatment for dyspnea,
treatment that pacifies thirst, and likewise treatment for disorders of <s>āma</s> should be performed.
The medicine for <s>rasa</s> and the others that was taught in the chapter on various foods and drinks
should be applied, each in its proper manner, to the channels of <s>rasa</s> and the rest.
For the channels carrying urine, feces, and sweat, treatment should be that for urinary difficulty,
that for diarrhea, and likewise that for fever.
On this there are verses:
The roots of the thirteen <s>srotas</s>, the signs of their corruption,
their general account, synonyms, and mutual provoking factors;
the cause of disorder, taken separately, and the indication of medicine:
these have been taught in the <s>Srotovimāna</s>, and also the determination at the beginning.
One who knows the body alone in all its aspects,

children.text: śārīrāḥ sarvarogāśca sa karmasu na muhyati ||
children.translated_text: and all bodily diseases, is not bewildered in his actions.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the <s>vimāna</s> on groups of diseases.
Thus spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: dve rogānīke bhavataḥ prabhāvabhedena sādhyam asādhyaṃ ca dve rogānīke balabhedena mṛdu dāruṇaṃ ca dve rogānīke adhiṣṭhānabhedena mano'dhiṣṭhānaṃ śarīrādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca dve rogānīke nimittabhedena svadhātuvaiṣamyanimittam āgantunimittaṃ ca dve rogānīke āśayabhedena āmāśayasamutthaṃ pakvāśayasamutthaṃ ceti
children.translated_text: There are two groups of diseases according to difference of effect: curable and incurable; two groups of diseases according to difference of strength: mild and severe; two groups of diseases according to difference of seat: seated in the mind and seated in the body; two groups of diseases according to difference of cause: caused by imbalance of one's own bodily constituents and caused by an external agent; and two groups of diseases according to difference of receptacle: arising from the <s>āmāśaya</s> and arising from the <s>pakvāśaya</s>.

children.text: evametat prabhāvabalādhiṣṭhānanimittāśayabhedāddvaidhaṃ sadbhedaprakṛtyantareṇa bhidyamānam athavāpi saṃdhīyamānaṃ syādekatvaṃ bahutvaṃ vā
children.translated_text: Thus, through the distinctions of effect, strength, seat, cause, and receptacle, this twofold classification, while being divided according to another principle of division or else being joined together, may become unity or multiplicity.

children.text: ekatvaṃ tāvad ekameva rogānīkaṃ duḥkhasāmānyāt bahutvaṃ tu daśa rogānīkāni prabhāvabhedādinā bhavanti bahutvam api saṃkhyeyaṃ syādasaṃkhyeyaṃ vā
children.translated_text: As for unity, there is just one group of diseases, because suffering is common to all. But multiplicity consists of ten groups of diseases through distinctions such as effect; and multiplicity too may be countable or uncountable.

children.text: tatra saṃkhyeyaṃ tāvad yathoktam aṣṭodarīye aparisaṃkhyeyaṃ punaryathā mahārogādhyāye rugvarṇasamutthānādīnām asaṃkhyeyatvāt ||
children.translated_text: There the countable is as stated in the chapter on the eight abdominal diseases; the uncountable, however, is as in the chapter on major diseases, because pains, colors, modes of arising, and so forth are uncountable.

children.text: na ca saṃkhyeyāgreṣu bhedaprakṛtyantarīyeṣu vigītirityato doṣavatī syādatra kācitpratijñā na cāvigītir ityataḥ syādadoṣavatī
children.translated_text: And because there is no contradiction among the foremost countable classifications that arise from different principles of division, some proposition here would not be faulty on that account; nor, because there is no contradiction, would it be free from fault on that account alone.

children.text: bhettā hi bhedyamanyathā bhinatti anyathā purastādbhinnaṃ bhedaprakṛtyantareṇa bhindan bhedasaṃkhyāviśeṣam āpādayatyanekadhā na ca pūrvaṃ bhedāgramupahanti
children.translated_text: For a classifier divides the thing to be classified in one way, and in another way, dividing what has previously been divided according to a different principle of division, he produces a particular number of divisions in many ways, without impairing the earlier chief division.
Even when the principle of division is the same, one must take into account a different application of the matter under discussion.

children.text: santi hyarthāntarāṇi samānaśabdābhihitāni santi cānarthāntarāṇi paryāyaśabdābhihitāni
children.translated_text: For there are different meanings denoted by the same word, and there are non-different meanings denoted by synonymous words.

children.text: samāno hi rogaśabdo doṣeṣu ca vyādhiṣu ca doṣā hyapi rogaśabdamātaṅkaśabdaṃ yakṣmaśabdaṃ doṣaprakṛtiśabdaṃ vikāraśabdaṃ ca labhante vyādhayaśca rogaśabdam ātaṅkaśabdaṃ yakṣmaśabdaṃ doṣaprakṛtiśabdaṃ vikāraśabdaṃ ca labhante
children.translated_text: For the same word <s>roga</s> is used both for <s>doṣas</s> and for diseases. Indeed <s>doṣas</s> receive the terms <s>roga</s>, <s>ātaṅka</s>, <s>yakṣma</s>, <s>doṣaprakṛti</s>, and <s>vikāra</s>; and diseases too receive the terms <s>roga</s>, <s>ātaṅka</s>, <s>yakṣma</s>, <s>doṣaprakṛti</s>, and <s>vikāra</s>.

children.text: tatra doṣeṣu caiva vyādhiṣu ca rogaśabdaḥ samānaḥ śeṣeṣu tu viśeṣavān ||
children.translated_text: Thus the word <s>roga</s> is common to both <s>doṣas</s> and diseases, while in the remaining terms there is a distinction of usage.

children.text: tatra vyādhayo'parisaṃkhyeyā bhavanti atibahutvāt doṣāstu khalu parisaṃkhyeyā bhavanti anatibahutvāt tasmādyathācitraṃ vikārānudāharaṇārtham anavaśeṣeṇa ca doṣān vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: There diseases are uncountable because they are extremely numerous; but <s>doṣas</s> are countable because they are not extremely numerous. Therefore, in order to illustrate disorders as they occur, and to explain the <s>doṣas</s> exhaustively, we shall describe the <s>doṣas</s>.
<s>Rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> are the mental <s>doṣas</s>.
Their disorders are desire, anger, greed, delusion, envy, pride, intoxication, grief, anxiety of mind, fear, joy, and the like.
But <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s> are the bodily <s>doṣas</s>.
Their disorders too are fever, diarrhea, swelling, wasting, dyspnea, urinary disease, skin disease, and the like.
Thus the <s>doṣas</s> alone have been explained, and one portion of their disorders.

children.text: tatra khalveṣāṃ dvayānāmapi doṣāṇāṃ trividhaṃ prakopaṇaṃ tadyathā asātmyendriyārthasaṃyogaḥ prajñāparādhaḥ pariṇāmaśceti ||
children.translated_text: Now, for both of these two kinds of <s>doṣas</s>, there are three causes of aggravation, namely: unsuitable contact between sense organs and their objects, error of judgment, and transformation over time.

children.text: prakupitāstu khalu te prakopaṇaviśeṣād dūṣyaviśeṣācca vikāraviśeṣān abhinirvartayantyaparisaṃkhyeyān ||
children.translated_text: When aggravated, they produce uncountable particular disorders because of the particular aggravating factor and the particular vulnerable substrate.

children.text: te ca vikārāḥ parasparamanuvartamānāḥ kadācidanubadhnanti kāmādayo jvarādayaśca ||
children.translated_text: And those disorders, following one another, sometimes become connected: desire and the like with fever and the like.

children.text: niyatastvanubandho rajastamasoḥ parasparaṃ na hyarajaskaṃ tamaḥ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: But the mutual connection of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> is fixed, for <s>tamas</s> does not proceed without <s>rajas</s>.

children.text: prāyaḥ śārīradoṣāṇām ekādhiṣṭhānīyānāṃ sannipātaḥ saṃsargo vā samānaguṇatvāt doṣā hi dūṣaṇaiḥ samānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Generally, among bodily <s>doṣas</s> sharing one seat, there is either combination or conjunction because of their similar qualities; for <s>doṣas</s> are similar in their acts of vitiation.

children.text: tatrānubandhyānubandhakṛto viśeṣaḥ svatantro vyaktaliṅgo yathoktasamutthānapraśamo bhavatyanubandhyaḥ tadviparītalakṣaṇas tvanubandhaḥ
children.translated_text: There the distinction made by the connected and the connector is this: the connected, or principal factor, is independent, has manifest signs, and has the mode of arising and pacification stated for it; the connector, or secondary factor, has the opposite characteristics.

children.text: anubandhyalakṣaṇasamanvitāstatra yadi doṣā bhavanti tattrikaṃ sannipātam ācakṣate dvayaṃ vā saṃsargam
children.translated_text: If the <s>doṣas</s> there are endowed with the marks of the principal connected factor, they call the triad a <s>sannipāta</s>, or the pair a <s>saṃsarga</s>.
But because of the distinction between principal connected factor and secondary connector, the division of <s>doṣas</s> is manifold.

children.text: evameṣa saṃjñāprakṛto bhiṣajāṃ doṣeṣu vyādhiṣu ca nānāprakṛtiviśeṣavyūhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus this varied arrangement of particular differences, arising from terminology, has been stated by physicians with regard to <s>doṣas</s> and diseases.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the <s>vimāna</s> called <s>Vyādhitarūpīya</s>, concerning diseased persons whose appearance is misleading.
Thus spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: iha khalu dvau puruṣau vyādhitarūpau bhavataḥ guruvyādhitaḥ laghuvyādhitaśca
children.translated_text: Here indeed there are two kinds of persons with misleading disease-appearance: one who is gravely diseased and one who is lightly diseased.

children.text: tatraguruvyādhita ekaḥ sattvabalaśarīrasampadupetatvāllaghuvyādhita iva dṛśyate laghuvyādhito 'paraḥ sattvādīnāmadhamatvādguruvyādhita iva dṛśyate
children.translated_text: Of these, one who is gravely diseased appears as if lightly diseased because he is endowed with strength of mind and bodily excellence; another, though lightly diseased, appears as if gravely diseased because of the inferiority of mental strength and the like.

children.text: tayorakuśalāḥ kevalaṃ cakṣuṣaiva rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvādhyavasyanto vyādhigurulāghave vipratipadyante ||
children.translated_text: In those two cases, the unskilled, deciding the matter after seeing the form only with the eye, go wrong about the heaviness or lightness of the disease.
For knowledge of a complete object of knowledge does not arise from a single component of knowledge.

children.text: vipratipannāstu khalu rogajñāne upakramayuktijñāne cāpi vipratipadyante
children.translated_text: And those who are mistaken in the knowledge of disease are also mistaken in the knowledge of the proper reasoning for treatment.

children.text: te yadā guruvyādhitaṃ laghuvyādhitarūpamāsādayanti tadā tamalpadoṣaṃ matvā saṃśodhanakāle 'smai mṛdu saṃśodhanaṃ prayacchanto bhūya evāsya doṣānudīrayanti
children.translated_text: When they encounter a gravely diseased person who has the appearance of one lightly diseased, then, thinking him to have little <s>doṣa</s>, they administer mild <s>saṃśodhana</s> (cleansing therapy) to him at the time for cleansing, and thereby stir up his <s>doṣas</s> still further.

children.text: yadā tu laghuvyādhitaṃ guruvyādhitarūpamāsādayanti tadā taṃ mahādoṣaṃ matvā saṃśodhanakāle 'smai tīkṣṇaṃ saṃśodhanaṃ prayacchanto doṣānatinirhṛtya śarīramasya kṣiṇvanti
children.translated_text: But when they encounter a lightly diseased person who has the appearance of one gravely diseased, then, thinking him to have great <s>doṣa</s>, they administer sharp <s>saṃśodhana</s> to him at the time for cleansing, and, by over-expelling the <s>doṣas</s>, they weaken his body.

children.text: evamavayavena jñānasya kṛtsne jñeye jñānamabhimanyamānāḥ pariskhalanti
children.translated_text: In this way, supposing that knowledge of a complete object of knowledge is obtained through only a part, they stumble.

children.text: viditaveditavyāstu bhiṣajaḥ sarvaṃ sarvathā yathāsaṃbhavaṃ parīkṣyaṃ parīkṣyādhyavasyanto na kvacidapi vipratipadyante yatheṣṭamarthamabhinirvartayanti ceti ||
children.translated_text: But physicians who know what is to be known, after examining everything in every way as far as possible and making a decision only after examination, are never mistaken anywhere, and they accomplish the intended result.
And here there are verses:
When fools see the appearance of disease in a patient as varying because of differences in mental strength and the like,
they are mistaken about the strength or weakness of the disease.
Deluded by ignorance, through improper use of medicine they bring about
the destruction of the sick, or at least their great suffering.
But the wise, having fully understood everything here that is to be examined in every way,
never stumble in the application of medicines.

children.text: iti vyādhitarūpādhikāre vyādhitarūpasaṃkhyāgrasaṃbhavaṃ vyādhitarūpahetuvipratipattau kāraṇaṃ sāpavādaṃ saṃpratipattikāraṇaṃ cānapavādaṃ niśamya bhagavantamātreyamagniveśo 'taḥ paraṃ sarvakrimīṇāṃ purīṣasaṃśrayāṇāṃ samutthānasthānasaṃsthānavarṇanāmaprabhāvacikitsitaviśeṣān papracchopasaṃgṛhya pādau ||
children.translated_text: In the discussion of misleading disease-appearance, after hearing the enumeration and occurrence of such appearances, the reason for error in determining them, with its exception, and the flawless reason for correct understanding, <s>Agniveśa</s> then clasped the feet of the venerable <s>Ātreya</s> and asked about the specific causes, locations, forms, colors, names, effects, and treatments of all <s>krimis</s> (worms or parasites) that reside in feces.

children.text: athāsmai provāca bhagavānātreyaḥiha khalvagniveśa viṃśatividhāḥ krimayaḥ pūrvamuddiṣṭā nānāvidhena pravibhāgenānyatra sahajebhyaḥ te punaḥ prakṛtibhirvibhajyamānāścaturvidhā bhavanti tadyathāpurīṣajāḥ śleṣmajāḥ śoṇitajā malajāśceti ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ātreya</s> said to him: "Here indeed, <s>Agniveśa</s>, twenty kinds of <s>krimis</s> have previously been mentioned elsewhere under various divisions, apart from those that are congenital. When divided according to their natures, they are again of four kinds: those born from feces, those born from <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), those born from blood, and those born from filth."
There, filth is both external and internal.
Those born from external filth we call filth-born.

children.text: teṣāṃ samutthānaṃ mṛjāvarjanaṃ sthānaṃ keśaśmaśrulomapakṣmavāsāṃsi saṃsthānamaṇavastilākṛtayo bahupādāśca varṇaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ śuklaśca nāmāni yūkāḥ pipīlikāśca prabhāvaḥ kaṇḍūjananaṃ koṭhapiḍakābhinirvartanaṃ ca cikitsitaṃ tu khalveṣāmapakarṣaṇaṃ malopaghātaḥ malakarāṇāṃ ca bhāvānāmanupasevanamiti ||
children.translated_text: Their cause is the avoidance of cleansing. Their locations are the hair of the head, beard, body hair, eyelashes, and garments. Their form is minute, sesame-shaped, and many-footed. Their color is black and white. Their names are lice and <s>pipīlikās</s>. Their effect is the production of itching and the formation of eruptions and pustules. Their treatment, however, is removal, destruction of filth, and avoidance of conditions that produce filth.

children.text: śoṇitajānāṃ tu khalu kuṣṭhaiḥ samānaṃ samutthānaṃ sthānaṃ raktavāhinyo dhamanyaḥ saṃsthānamaṇavo vṛttāścāpādāśca sūkṣmatvāccaike bhavantyadṛśyāḥ varṇaḥ tāmraḥ nāmāni keśādā lomādā lomadvīpāḥ saurasā auḍumbarā jantumātaraśceti prabhāvaḥ keśaśmaśrunakhalomapakṣmāpadhvaṃsaḥ vraṇagatānāṃ ca harṣakaṇḍūtodasaṃsarpaṇāni ativṛddhānāṃ ca tvaksirāsnāyumāṃsataruṇāsthibhakṣaṇamiti cikitsitamapyeṣāṃ kuṣṭhaiḥ samānaṃ taduttarakālamupadekṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those born from blood have the same cause as <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease). Their location is the blood-carrying arteries. Their form is minute, round, and footless; because of their subtlety some are invisible. Their color is coppery. Their names are <s>Keśādās</s>, <s>Lomādās</s>, <s>Lomadvīpas</s>, <s>Saurasas</s>, <s>Auḍumbaras</s>, and <s>Jantumātṛs</s>. Their effect is the destruction of head-hair, beard, nails, body hair, and eyelashes; and, when they have entered wounds, horripilation, itching, piercing pain, and creeping sensations. When excessively increased, they eat the skin, vessels, sinews, flesh, cartilage, and bone. Their treatment too is the same as for <s>kuṣṭha</s>; we shall teach that later.

children.text: śleṣmajāḥ kṣīraguḍatilamatsyānūpamāṃsapiṣṭānnaparamānnakusumbhasnehājīrṇapūtiklinnasaṃkīrṇaviruddhāsātmyabhojanasamutthānāḥ teṣāmāmāśayaḥ sthānaṃ te pravardhamānāstūrdhvamadho vā visarpantyubhayato vā saṃsthānavarṇaviśeṣāstu śvetāḥ pṛthubradhnasaṃsthānāḥ kecit kecidvṛttapariṇāhā gaṇḍūpadākṛtayaḥ śvetāstāmrāvabhāsāśca kecidaṇavo dīrghāstantvākṛtayaḥ śvetāḥ teṣāṃ trividhānāṃ śleṣmanimittānāṃ krimīṇāṃ nāmāni antrādāḥ udarādāḥ hṛdayacarāḥ curavaḥ darbhapuṣpāḥ saugandhikāḥ mahāgudāśceti prabhāvo hṛllāsaḥ āsyasaṃsravaṇam arocakāvipākau jvaraḥ mūrcchā jṛmbhā kṣavathuḥ ānāhaḥ aṅgamardaḥ chardiḥ kārśyaṃ pāruṣyaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: Those born from <s>śleṣman</s> arise from milk, molasses, sesame, fish, meat of marshy animals, flour preparations, cooked rice delicacies, safflower oil, indigestion, and putrid, moist, mixed, incompatible, and unsuitable foods. Their location is the <s>āmāśaya</s> (stomach). As they grow, they spread upward, downward, or in both directions. As for their particular forms and colors: some are white and broad-bodied, some have a round girth and the shape of earthworms, some are white with a coppery sheen, and some are minute, long, thread-shaped, and white. The names of these three kinds of phlegm-caused <s>krimis</s> are <s>Antrādās</s>, <s>Udarādās</s>, <s>Hṛdayacaras</s>, <s>Curavas</s>, <s>Darbhapuṣpas</s>, <s>Saugandhikas</s>, and <s>Mahāgudas</s>. Their effect is nausea, salivation from the mouth, anorexia, indigestion, fever, fainting, yawning, sneezing, abdominal distension, aching of the limbs, vomiting, emaciation, and roughness.

children.text: purīṣajāstulyasamutthānāḥ śleṣmajaiḥ teṣāṃ sthānaṃ pakvāśayaḥ te pravardhamānāstvadho visarpanti yasya punarāmāśayābhimukhāḥ syuryadantaraṃ tadantaraṃ tasyodgāraniḥśvāsāḥ purīṣagandhinaḥ syuḥ saṃsthānavarṇaviśeṣāstu sūkṣmavṛttaparīṇāhāḥ śvetā dīrghā ūrṇāṃśusaṃkāśāḥ kecit kecit punaḥ sthūlavṛttaparīṇāhāḥ śyāvanīlaharitapītāḥ teṣāṃ nāmāni kakerukāḥ makerukāḥ lelihāḥ saśūlakāḥ sausurādāśceti prabhāvaḥ purīṣabhedaḥ kārśyaṃ pāruṣyaṃ lomaharṣābhinirvartanaṃ ca ta eva cāsya gudamukhaṃ paritudantaḥ kaṇḍūṃ copajanayanto gudamukhaṃ paryāsate ta eva jātaharṣā gudaniṣkramaṇamativelaṃ kurvanti ityeṣa śleṣmajānāṃ purīṣajānāṃ ca krimīṇāṃ samutthānādiviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those born from feces have origins like those born from <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm). Their seat is the <s>pakvāśaya</s> (large intestine). As they increase, they spread downward. But when they turn toward the <s>āmāśaya</s> (stomach), then the patient's belchings and breaths smell of feces. As for their special shapes and colors: some are thin, round in circumference, white, long, and like fibers of wool; others again are thick and round in circumference, dark, blue, green, or yellow. Their names are <s>Kakeruka</s>, <s>Makeruka</s>, <s>Lelihā</s>, <s>Saśūlaka</s>, and <s>Sausurāda</s>. Their effect is looseness of stool, emaciation, roughness, and the production of horripilation. These same worms, piercing the opening of the anus and producing itching, gather around the anal opening. And these same ones, when excited, cause excessive emergence from the anus. This is the distinction, beginning with origin, of the worms born from <s>śleṣman</s> and from feces.
Now we shall first teach their treatment in summary and afterward teach it in detail.

children.text: tatra sarvakrimīṇāmapakarṣaṇamevāditaḥ kāryaṃ tataḥ prakṛtivighātaḥ anantaraṃ nidānoktānāṃ bhāvānāmanupasevanamiti ||
children.translated_text: In that regard, for all worms, extraction should be done first; then the disruption of their natural conditions; and after that, non-use of the things stated among the causes.

children.text: tatrāpakarṣaṇaṃhastenābhigṛhya vimṛśyopakaraṇavatāpanayanamanupakaraṇena vā sthānagatānāṃ tu krimīṇāṃ bheṣajenāpakarṣaṇaṃ nyāyataḥ taccaturvidhaṃ tadyathā śirovirecanaṃ vamanaṃ virecanam āsthāpanaṃ ca ityapakarṣaṇavidhiḥ
children.translated_text: There, extraction means removal by grasping with the hand, examining, and using an instrument, or without an instrument. But for worms lodged in internal seats, extraction is properly done by medicine. This is fourfold, namely: purgation of the head, emesis, purgation, and evacuative enema. This is the method of extraction.

children.text: prakṛtivighātastveṣāṃ kaṭutiktakaṣāyakṣāroṣṇānāṃ dravyāṇāmupayogaḥ yaccānyadapi kiṃcicchleṣmapurīṣapratyanīkabhūtaṃ tat syāt iti prakṛtivighātaḥ
children.translated_text: The disruption of their natural conditions is the use of substances that are pungent, bitter, astringent, alkaline, and hot, and anything else that is opposed to <s>śleṣman</s> and feces. This is disruption of their natural conditions.

children.text: anantaraṃ nidānoktānāṃ bhāvānāmanupasevanaṃ yaduktaṃ nidānavidhau tasya vivarjanaṃ tathāprāyāṇāṃ cāpareṣāṃ dravyāṇām
children.translated_text: After that comes non-use of the things mentioned among the causes: the avoidance of what was stated in the section on etiology, and also of other substances of a similar kind.
Thus the treatment has been explained in terms of its defining features.
Now this same treatment will be taught in detail.

children.text: athainaṃ krimikoṣṭhamāturamagre ṣaḍrātraṃ saptarātraṃ vā snehasvedābhyāmupapādya śvobhūte enaṃ saṃśodhanaṃ pāyayitāsmīti kṣīraguḍadadhitilamatsyānūpamāṃsapiṣṭānnaparamānnakusumbhasnehasamprayuktair bhojyaiḥ sāyaṃ prātaścopapādayet samudīraṇārthaṃ krimīṇāṃ koṣṭhābhisaraṇārthaṃ ca bhiṣak
children.translated_text: First the physician should prepare this patient whose bowels contain worms for six or seven nights with oleation and fomentation. Thinking, 'Tomorrow I shall give him purificatory treatment,' he should provide him, evening and morning, with foods mixed with milk, jaggery, curds, sesame, fish, meat from marshy animals, cakes, sweet rice, and safflower oil, for the purpose of exciting the worms and making them move into the bowels.

children.text: atha vyuṣṭāyāṃ rātryāṃ sukhoṣitaṃ suprajīrṇabhaktaṃ ca vijñāyāsthāpanavamanavirecanais tadahar evopapādayed upapādanīyaścet syāt sarvān parīkṣyaviśeṣān parīkṣya samyak ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the night has passed, after knowing that he has slept comfortably and that his meal is well digested, on that very day the physician should prepare him with evacuative enema, emesis, and purgation, if he is fit to be so prepared, after properly examining all particular factors.

children.text: athāhareti brūyāt mūlakasarṣapalaśunakarañjaśigrumadhuśigrukharapuṣpābhūstṛṇasumukhasurasakuṭherakagaṇḍīrakālamālakaparṇāsakṣavakaphaṇijjhakāni sarvāṇyathavā yathālābhaṃ tānyāhṛtānyabhisamīkṣya khaṇḍaśaśchedayitvā prakṣālya pānīyena suprakṣālitāyāṃ sthālyāṃ samāvāpya gomūtreṇārdhodakenābhiṣicya sādhayet satatamavaghaṭṭayan darvyā tamupayuktabhūyiṣṭhe 'mbhasi gataraseṣvauṣadheṣu sthālīmavatārya suparipūtaṃ kaṣāyaṃ sukhoṣṇaṃ madanaphalapippalīviḍaṅgakalkatailopahitaṃ svarjikālavaṇitamabhyāsicya bastau vidhivadāsthāpayedenaṃ tathārkālarkakuṭajāḍhakīkuṣṭhakaiḍaryakaṣāyeṇa vā tathā śigrupīlukustumburukaṭukāsarṣapakaṣāyeṇa tathā āmalakaśṛṅgaveradāruharidrāpicumardakaṣāyeṇa madanaphalādisaṃyogasampāditena trivāraṃ saptarātraṃ vāsthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Then he should say, 'Bring these': <s>mūlaka</s>, <s>sarṣapa</s>, <s>laśuna</s>, <s>karañja</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>madhuśigru</s>, <s>kharapuṣpā</s>, <s>bhūstṛṇa</s>, <s>sumukha</s>, <s>surasā</s>, <s>kuṭheraka</s>, <s>gaṇḍīra</s>, <s>kālamālaka</s>, <s>parṇāsa</s>, <s>kṣavaka</s>, and <s>phaṇijjhaka</s>, all of them or as many as are available. Having inspected them when brought, he should cut them into pieces, wash them with water, place them together in a well-washed pot, pour over them cow's urine mixed with half water, and cook them, constantly stirring with a ladle. When most of the water has been consumed and the medicines have lost their taste, he should take the pot down, strain the decoction well, and, while it is pleasantly warm, mix it with a paste of <s>madanaphala</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s>, with oil added, salt it with <s>svarjikā</s> salt, and administer it to him properly as an evacuative enema. Or he should administer in the same way a decoction of <s>arka</s>, <s>alarka</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>āḍhakī</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and <s>kaiḍarya</s>; likewise a decoction of <s>śigru</s>, <s>pīlu</s>, <s>kustumburu</s>, pungent substances, and mustard; or a decoction of <s>āmalaka</s>, <s>śṛṅgavera</s>, <s>dāruharidrā</s>, and <s>picumarda</s>, prepared with the combination beginning with <s>madanaphala</s>. He should administer the enema three times, or for seven nights.

children.text: pratyāgate ca paścime bastau pratyāśvastaṃ tadaharevobhayatobhāgaharaṃ saṃśodhanaṃ pāyayedyuktyā tasya vidhir upadekṣyate madanaphalapippalīkaṣāyasyārdhāñjalimātreṇa trivṛtkalkākṣamātramāloḍya pātum asmai prayacchet tadasya doṣamubhayato nirharati sādhu evameva kalpoktāni vamanavirecanāni pratisaṃsṛjya pāyayedenaṃ buddhyā sarvaviśeṣānavekṣamāṇo bhiṣak ||
children.translated_text: And when the last enema has returned and the patient has recovered, on that very day he should judiciously give him a purificatory medicine that acts in both directions. Its procedure will be taught: he should stir one <s>akṣa</s> measure of <s>trivṛt</s> paste into half an <s>añjali</s> measure of a decoction of <s>madanaphala</s> and <s>pippalī</s>, and give it to him to drink. This properly expels his <s>doṣa</s> in both directions. In just this way, the physician, thoughtfully considering all particulars, should mix and give him the emetics and purgatives stated in the <s>kalpa</s> section.

children.text: athainaṃ samyagviriktaṃ vijñāyāparāhṇe śaikharikakaṣāyeṇa sukhoṣṇena pariṣecayet
children.translated_text: Then, after knowing that he has been properly purged, in the afternoon he should sprinkle him with a pleasantly warm decoction of <s>śaikharika</s>.
