or that a house is made by clay, grass, and wood without a house-builder,

children.text: yo vadet sa vadeddehaṃ sambhūya karaṇaiḥ kṛtam
children.translated_text: then that person would be saying that the body is made by the instruments after they have come together,
without an agent; through ignorance he would be excluded from reasoning and authoritative tradition.
The <s>puruṣa</s> is apprehended as the cause by all means of valid knowledge,
and is measured by all the authoritative traditions from which all that is to be known is measured.
Those other things that arise through succession are not exactly like it;

children.text: sārūpyādye ta eveti nirdiśyante navā navāḥ ||
children.translated_text: because of similarity they are pointed out as these very same ones, though they are ever new.
Some have settled on the view that those states, their aggregate, being without a lord and called <s>sattva</s>,

children.text: kartā bhoktā na sa pumāniti kecidvyavasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are not a person who is agent and experiencer.
For those by whom no self is taught, other new states,
similar to the earlier states, experience the obtained fruit of what was done by other states.

children.text: karaṇānyānyatā dṛṣṭā kartuḥ kartā sa eva tu
children.translated_text: A difference among instruments is observed, but the agent of the agent is that same one.
For the agent, joined with instruments, is the cause of all actions.
Because states perish in less than the time of a blink,

children.text: bhagnānāṃ na punarbhāvaḥ kṛtaṃ nānyamupaiti ca ||
children.translated_text: what has been broken does not come into being again, and what has been done does not pass to another.

children.text: mataṃ tattvavidāmetad yasmāt tasmāt sa kāraṇam
children.translated_text: This is the opinion of those who know reality; for this reason he is the cause,
the eternal one called <s>puruṣa</s>, in the activity and experience of beings.
Ego-sense, fruit, action, movement to another body, and memory
exist when there is a cause of beings apart from the body.
Because it is beginningless, no origination of the supreme self is found;
but the <s>puruṣa</s> called the aggregate is born from delusion, desire, hatred, and action.
The self is a knower; through conjunction with the instruments, its knowledge proceeds,
but because of impurity of the instruments, or because of non-conjunction, it does not function.
Just as, even for one who sees, there is no seeing in a soiled mirror,

children.text: tattvaṃ jale vā kaluṣe cetasyupahate tathā ||
children.translated_text: or of a thing in turbid water, so too there is no seeing of reality when the mind is impaired.
The instruments are mind, intellect, and the cognitive and action senses;

children.text: kartuḥ saṃyogajaṃ karma vedanā buddhireva ca ||
children.translated_text: action, sensation, and cognition arise from the agent's conjunction.

children.text: naikaḥ pravartate kartuṃ bhūtātmā nāśnute phalam
children.translated_text: The elemental self does not proceed alone to act, nor does it enjoy the fruit;
everything proceeds from conjunction; without it there is nothing.

children.text: na hyeko vartate bhāvo vartate nāpyahetukaḥ
children.translated_text: For no single state functions, nor does it function without a cause;
because of its swift passing, by nature disappearance does not fail to occur.
The <s>puruṣa</s> is beginningless and eternal, while the contrary is causally produced;
that which exists without a cause is seen as eternal; what is cause-born is otherwise.
That very thing, because of its existence, is not graspable; its eternity is not from anything else.
That unmanifest is to be known from its existence; it is unthinkable, while the manifest is otherwise.
The unmanifest, the self, the knower of the field, is everlasting, all-pervading, and undecaying;
therefore whatever is other than that is manifest, and the remaining pair will be explained.
The manifest is also sense-accessible, and what is grasped by the senses is that;
what is other than this is again unmanifest, grasped by a sign and beyond the senses.
Ether and the other elements, intellect, the unmanifest, and ego as the eighth
are declared to be the material nature of beings; and the evolutes are sixteen.
The five cognitive senses and the five action senses,
together with mind and the five objects, are called the evolutes.
Thus the field has been fully stated, all of it except the unmanifest;
the seers know the unmanifest of this field as the knower of the field.
Intellect is born from the unmanifest; through intellect one thinks, I.
Then ether and the other elements arise from ego in due order.
Thereafter, born complete in all limbs, he is said to have arisen;
at dissolution the <s>puruṣa</s> is again separated from activities and states.

children.text: avyaktād vyaktatāṃ yāti vyaktād avyaktatāṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: From the unmanifest it goes to manifestation, and from the manifest back again to the unmanifest.
Possessed by <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, he revolves like a wheel.
Those whose supreme attachment is to the pairs of opposites, and those who are devoted to egoism,

children.text: udayapralayau teṣāṃ na teṣāṃ ye tvato'nyathā ||
children.translated_text: for them there are arising and dissolution; not for those who are otherwise than that.
<s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, blinking and the like, life, the movement of the mind,
passing from one sense faculty to another, and whatever is impulsion and retention,
movement to another place in dream, and likewise the assumption of the fivefold state,
and also the apprehension by the left eye of what has been seen with the right eye,

children.text: icchā dveṣaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ prayatnaścetanā dhṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: desire, hatred, pleasure, pain, effort, consciousness, firmness,
intellect, memory, and egoism are signs of the <s>paramātman</s> (supreme self).
Because these signs are perceived in a living person,
and the signs of the self are not perceived in one who is dead, therefore the great seers say this.
For when that one has gone, the body is like an empty house, unconscious;
because only the five elements remain, it is said to have gone to the fivefold state.
The mind is unconscious, though active; the higher one is the one who causes consciousness.

children.text: yuktasya manasā tasya nirdiśyante vibhoḥ kriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When that all-pervading one is joined with the mind, actions are ascribed to him.
Because the self possesses consciousness, it is therefore defined as the agent;
and because the mind is unconscious, though active, it is not so called.
By means of his own self, each living being, in all wombs,
maintains himself with the breaths; for there is no other controller of him.
Being master, he performs the action whose fruit he enjoys after performing it;

children.text: vaśī cetaḥ samādhatte vaśī sarvaṃ nirasyati ||
children.translated_text: being master, he composes the mind; being master, he casts everything away.
Though the embodied self is all-pervading, in each particular organ of touch,
the self does not thereby know all sensations that are situated in every support.
For this reason his pervasiveness is established, since he is all-pervading and great;
and by concentration of the mind the self sees what is concealed.
One should know him as constantly connected with the mind, which follows the body's karma,
and as having entered all wombs, even while established in a single womb.
There is no beginning of the self, and the succession of fields is beginningless;
therefore, because both of these are beginningless, it cannot be said which is prior.

children.text: jñaḥ sākṣītyucyate nājñaḥ sākṣī tvātmā yataḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: He is called knowing and a witness, not unknowing; for the self is remembered as witness,
since all states of all beings have the self as their witness.
A single elemental self is never characterized by marks;
for no distinction of singleness exists for that which is not perceived.
A distinction is accepted for the person formed by conjunction, produced by sensation;
where sensation is determinate, there the distinction is produced by that.
Some say that the physician treats all sensations of the three times;
the reasoning by which they say this should be considered.
Again that headache, that fever, has returned;

children.text: punaḥ sa kāso balavāṃśchardiḥ sā punarāgatā ||
children.translated_text: again that powerful cough, that vomiting, has returned.
By familiar expressions such as these, the return of what is past is accepted;
and this is the time of the past afflictions when they have returned.
The medicine that is applied with reference to that time of affliction
is said to be the pacification of past sensations.

children.text: āpastāḥ punarāgurmā yābhiḥ śasyaṃ purā hatam
children.translated_text: May those waters by which the crop was formerly destroyed not come again;
just as an embankment is built, so also a countermeasure is applied to the support.
Seeing the premonitory form of disorders that are about to appear,

children.text: yā kriyā kriyate sā ca vedanāṃ hantyanāgatām ||
children.translated_text: the action that is performed also destroys future sensation.
But the continuous succession of sufferings ceases,
and happiness also arises, through treatment with the causes of happiness.

children.text: na samā yānti vaiṣamyaṃ viṣamāḥ samatāṃ na ca
children.translated_text: Balanced states do not pass into imbalance, nor do imbalanced states pass into balance;
the bodily <s>dhātus</s> (constituents) are always produced in conformity with their causes.
Putting this reasoning in front, the physician

children.text: hantītyuktaṃ cikitsā tu naiṣṭhikī yā vinopadhām ||
children.translated_text: is said to destroy sensation in the three times; but the final treatment is that without <s>upadhā</s> (substrate or attachment).
For <s>upadhā</s> is the supreme cause, giving pain and a support for pain;
and the abandonment of all <s>upadhās</s> removes every suffering.
Just as the maker of a cocoon takes up threads that bring death,
so the ignorant person, always afflicted, takes up craving from objects.
But the wise person, knowing harmful objects to be like fire, turns away from them;
because he does not begin and does not connect with them, that suffering does not approach him.
Derangement of intellect, firmness, and memory; the arrival of time and deeds;
and contact with unsuitable objects: these should be known as causes of suffering.
The wrong fixation concerning what is eternal and non-eternal, beneficial and harmful,

children.text: jñeyaḥ sa buddhivibhraṃśaḥ samaṃ buddhirhi paśyati ||
children.translated_text: should be known as derangement of intellect, for intellect sees evenly.
A mind inclined toward sense objects, because of derangement of firmness, cannot
be restrained from harmful objects; for firmness is of the nature of restraint.
When the memory of one whose self is covered by <s>rajas</s> and delusion falls away

children.text: bhraśyate sa smṛtibhraṃśaḥ smartavyaṃ hi smṛtau sthitam ||
children.translated_text: with regard to knowledge of reality, that is derangement of memory; for what is to be remembered is established in memory.
The unwholesome action that one bereft of intellect, firmness, and memory performs,
know that as <s>prajñāparādha</s> (offense against wisdom), which aggravates all the <s>doṣas</s>.
The provocation of natural urges that should move, and the suppression of those that have arisen,
the practice of rash acts, and excessive indulgence in women,
missing the proper time for actions, and wrong undertaking of actions,
loss of humility and proper conduct, and assault against those worthy of honor,
the personal practice of things known to be harmful,
and resorting to conditions that are extremely maddening,
moving about at improper times and places, friendship with those whose actions are polluted,
and abandonment of the good conduct taught as the proper approach to the senses,
envy, pride, fear, anger, greed, delusion, intoxication, and confusion

children.text: tajjaṃ vā karma yatkliṣṭaṃ kliṣṭaṃ yaddehakarma ca ||
children.translated_text: Or any action born from that which is afflicted, and any afflicted bodily action,
and whatever other action of this kind arises from <s>rajas</s> and delusion,
the learned call that <s>prajñāparādha</s> (offense against understanding), a cause of disease.
Incorrect discernment by the intellect, and incorrect engagement as well,
one should know to be <s>prajñāparādha</s>; for that is within the sphere of the mind.
The arrival at the proper time of diseases has been indicated in the compendium of diseases,
as also, previously, the accumulation, aggravation, and pacification of <s>pitta</s> and the others.
The causes of disease at the end of the rains have improper, excessive, and deficient signs,
as do the conditions of digested food, eaten food, and food being digested, occurring at the right or wrong time.
Morning, midday, and afternoon, and the three watches of the night,

children.text: eṣu kāleṣu niyatā ye rogāste ca kālajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the diseases fixed in these times are themselves born from time.
The fever of the following day, the one that takes hold after two days, and the tertian and quartan fevers

children.text: sve sve kāle pravartante kāle hyeṣāṃ balāgamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: arise at their own respective times, for the onset of their strength occurs in time.

children.text: ete cānye ca ye kecit kālajā vividhā gadāḥ
children.translated_text: These and whatever other various illnesses are born from time
should be treated before they arrive by one who knows their strength and time.
Diseases arising from old age and death, through the transformation of time,
are seen to be natural; nature is not subject to counteraction.
The action of a former body has been indicated by the word <s>daiva</s> (fate).
That too is found, in time, to be a cause of diseases.

children.text: na hi karma mahatkiṃcit phalaṃ yasya na bhujyate
children.translated_text: For there is no action of great force whose fruit is not experienced.

children.text: kriyāghnāḥ karmajā rogāḥ praśamaṃ yānti tatkṣayāt ||
children.translated_text: Diseases born of action and resistant to treatment come to pacification when that action is exhausted.
From hearing sounds that are excessively harsh, and from not hearing sounds at all,
and from hearing sounds that are excessively weak, people become impaired in hearing.
Contact of the auditory sense with sounds that are harsh, terrifying, inauspicious, unpleasant, or indicative of misfortune
is called improper conjunction.
Non-contact, excessive contact, and also deficient contact
with tangible objects, stated in summary, are harmful to the organ of touch.
Contact that comes out of season, whether from living beings, poisons, or winds,
and contact with unctuousness, cold, or heat, is called improper use.
The sight of brilliant forms is destroyed by seeing them too much,
and by seeing things that are too subtle, and also by not seeing at all.
Seeing hated, frightful, disgusting things, or things too distant or too close,
and seeing dark forms, is called improper conjunction.
Excessive intake, non-intake, and intake involving habituation and suitability,
as well as irregular intake, little intake, and vitiation of tastes, are faults.
The use of odors that are excessively mild or excessively sharp,
and total non-use of odors, destroy the olfactory sense.
Odors that are putrid, from living beings or poisons, hated,
or out of season: conjunction of the nose with those odors is called improper use.
Thus unsuitable contact with objects is threefold and aggravates the <s>doṣas</s>.
One should know as unsuitable that which does not enter into compatibility with oneself.
The disease that arises from wrong, excessive, or deficient conjunction

children.text: śabdādīnāṃ sa vijñeyo vyādhir aindriyako budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: of sound and the other sense objects is to be understood by the wise as a disease of the senses.
These are remembered as the causes of unpacified sensations.
There is only one cause of happiness: balanced conjunction, which is very hard to attain.
Neither the senses nor their objects are the causes of pleasure and pain.
Rather, the cause of pleasure and pain is seen to be conjunction, which is fourfold.

children.text: santīndriyāṇi santyarthā yogo na ca na cāsti ruk
children.translated_text: The senses exist and the objects exist; if there is no conjunction, there is no pain.

children.text: na sukhaṃ kāraṇaṃ tasmād yoga eva caturvidhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the cause is not happiness itself; conjunction alone is fourfold.

children.text: nātmendriyaṃ mano buddhiṃ gocaraṃ karma vā vinā
children.translated_text: Without the self, the sense, the mind, the intellect, the object, or action,
pleasure and pain, in whatever form and manner they occur, should be understood; that is now stated.
Contact with the tactile sense and mental contact
are the two kinds of touch that set in motion sensations of pleasure and pain.
Craving, whose nature is desire and aversion, arises from pleasure and pain,
and craving is again said to be the cause of pleasure and pain.
For craving appropriates states that are called supports of sensation.
When there is no appropriation, there is no contact; and one who is not contacted does not experience sensations.
The seat of sensations is the mind and the body together with the senses,
excepting the hair of the head, body hair, the tips of the nails, food, impurities, fluids, and qualities.

children.text: yoge mokṣe ca sarvāsāṃ vedanānām avartanam
children.translated_text: In yoga and in liberation there is non-occurrence of all sensations.
In liberation there is complete cessation; yoga sets liberation in motion.
Pleasure and pain arise from the conjunction of self, senses, mind, and objects.
When the mind is steady and rests in the self, because there is no initiation of activity,
both of these cease, and mastery arises.
The knowers of yoga, the seers, know that state, while one is still embodied, as yoga.
Entrance into another's mind, knowledge, action upon objects at will,
vision, hearing, memory, beauty, and also becoming invisible at will:
this eightfold sovereign power of yogins has been taught.
All of that arises from the concentration of purified <s>sattva</s>.
Mokṣa, because of the absence of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> and because of the exhaustion of powerful action,
is called separation from all conjunctions and non-rebirth.
Proper attendance upon good people, avoidance of bad people,
the observance of vows and fasts, and various kinds of restraints,
retention of the <s>dharmaśāstras</s>, knowledge, delight in solitude,
dispassion toward sense objects, resolve toward mokṣa, and supreme firmness,
non-initiation of actions, exhaustion of actions already done,
renunciation, absence of egoism, seeing danger in conjunction,
concentration of mind and intellect, and examination of the truth of things
All this proceeds from the presence of recollection of reality.
Recollection arises through service to good people and the other means, ending with steadfastness.
Remembering the nature of things, one is freed from suffering through that recollection.
The eight causes by which recollection arises will now be stated:
from grasping the cause and form, from similarity, and from contrast,
from connection with the mind, from practice, from the discipline of knowledge, and again from what has been heard.
Recollection is said to be the remembering of things seen, heard, and experienced.
This is that single path to liberation shown by those who are liberated,
the power of recollection of reality, by which they have gone and have not returned.
This path has again been called the path of <s>yoga</s> by the <s>yogin</s>s,
and by those sharing the doctrine of enumeration and by the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s it is also called the path to liberation.
Everything that has a cause is suffering, is not one's own, and is indeed impermanent.

children.text: na cātmakṛtakaṃ taddhi tatra cotpadyate svatā ||
children.translated_text: It is not made by the self; and yet a sense of selfhood arises with regard to it.
So long as true understanding does not arise, by which one knows, "This is not I,"
and, knowing, "This is not mine," the knower passes beyond everything.
In that final renunciation, all sensations, root and all,
together with perception, cognition, and discernment, come to complete cessation.
Beyond this, having become <s>brahman</s>, the <s>bhūtātman</s> is not apprehended.
He has gone out from all states, and no mark of him exists.
This is the knowledge of the knowers of <s>brahman</s>; an ignorant person is not fit to know it.
The twenty-three excellent questions concerning the <s>puruṣa</s>,
have been decided in this <s>Katidhāpuruṣīya</s> chapter by the seer of reality.
Now then, we shall explain the chapter called <s>Atulyagotrīya</s>.
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.
When, at the end of menstruation, a man of a different lineage has had intercourse and privately emitted seed,

children.text: kiṃ syāccatuṣpātprabhavaṃ ca ṣaḍbhyo yat strīṣu garbhatvamupaiti puṃsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: what is it that has four quarters, arises from the six, and from the man attains the state of an embryo in women?

children.text: śukraṃ tadasya pravadanti dhīrā yaddhīyate garbhasamudbhavāya
children.translated_text: The wise call that his semen, which is discharged for the arising of an embryo.
It has quarters consisting of the qualities of wind, fire, earth, and water, and its source is from the six tastes.

children.text: sampūrṇadehaḥ samaye sukhaṃ ca garbhaḥ kathaṃ kena ca jāyate strī
children.translated_text: How, by what, and at what time does a woman bear an embryo that is complete in body and happy?

children.text: garbhaṃ cirādvindati saprajāpi bhūtvāthavā naśyati kena garbhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why does a woman, though already having offspring, conceive only after a long time, or why does the embryo perish?
When semen, blood, self, womb, and season are in excellent condition, and when treatment is likewise wholesome, with suitable foods,

children.text: garbhaśca kāle ca sukhī sukhaṃ ca saṃjāyate saṃparipūrṇadehaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then in due time the embryo is happy, and is happily born with a completely developed body.
Because of defects of the womb, distress of the mind, defects of semen, blood, diet, and regimen,
because of improper timing and loss of strength, even a woman who has had offspring conceives only after a long time.

children.text: asṛṅniruddhaṃ pavanena nāryā garbhaṃ vyavasyantyabudhāḥ kadācit
children.translated_text: Sometimes the ignorant suppose blood obstructed by wind in a woman to be an embryo.

children.text: garbhasya rūpaṃ hi karoti tasyās tadasṛg asrāvi vivardhamānam ||
children.translated_text: For that blood, as it increases, takes on for her the appearance of an embryo, and then is discharged.
When it is set in motion by fire, sun, exertion, grief, or disease, or by hot foods and drinks,

children.text: dṛṣṭvāsṛgekaṃ na ca garbhasaṃjñaṃ kecin narā bhūtahṛtaṃ vadanti ||
children.translated_text: some people, seeing only blood and not anything called an embryo, say that the embryo has been seized by beings.
For night-wanderers who feed on vital essence, the body is not desired as food;

children.text: garbhaṃ hareyuryadi te na mātur labdhāvakāśā na hareyurojaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if they could seize the embryo, then, having found an opportunity, they would not fail to seize the mother's vital essence.

children.text: kanyāṃ sutaṃ vā sahitau pṛthagvā sutau sute vā tanayān bahūn vā
children.translated_text: Why does a woman give birth to a girl or a son, to two sons together or separately, to two daughters, or to many children?

children.text: kasmāt prasūte sucireṇa garbham eko'bhivṛddhiṃ ca yame'bhyupaiti ||
children.translated_text: Why does she carry an embryo for a very long time, and why does one in a pair of twins attain greater growth?

children.text: raktena kanyām adhikena putraṃ śukreṇa tena dvividhīkṛtena
children.translated_text: By an excess of blood she bears a girl; by an excess of semen, a son. When that seed is divided in two,

children.text: bījena kanyāṃ ca sutaṃ ca sūte yathāsvabījānyatarādhikena ||
children.translated_text: she bears a girl and a son, according to the predominance of one or the other seed.

children.text: śukrādhikaṃ dvaidhamupaiti bījaṃ yasyāḥ sutau sā sahitau prasūte
children.translated_text: When seed in which semen predominates divides in two, she gives birth to two sons together.

children.text: raktādhikaṃ vā yadi bhedameti dvidhā sute sā sahite prasūte ||
children.translated_text: Or if seed in which blood predominates divides in two, she gives birth to two daughters together.
As greatly active wind divides the semen and menstrual blood into many parts,
so many offspring, apportioned accordingly, does she bear, constituted by karma and not by her own will.

children.text: āhāramāpnoti yadā na garbhaḥ śoṣaṃ samāpnoti parisrutiṃ vā
children.translated_text: When an embryo does not obtain nourishment and undergoes drying up or discharge,

children.text: taṃ strī prasūte sucireṇa garbhaṃ puṣṭo yadā varṣagaṇairapi syāt ||
children.translated_text: a woman bears that embryo only after a long time, when it becomes nourished even after a number of years.
Because twins are constituted by karma, and because of unequal division of the semen and blood, growth occurs in the womb:

children.text: eko'dhiko nyūnataro dvitīya evaṃ yame'pyabhyadhiko viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one is greater and the other less; thus even among twins there is a marked difference.
Why does a <s>dviretāḥ</s>, a <s>pavanendriya</s>, a <s>saṃskāravāhin</s>, a male or female <s>ṣaṇḍa</s>,

children.text: vakrī tatherṣyābhiratiḥ kathaṃ vā saṃjāyate vātikaṣaṇḍako vā ||
children.translated_text: a <s>vakrī</s>, one whose delight is in jealousy, or a <s>vātikaṣaṇḍaka</s> come into being?

children.text: bījāt samāṃśād upataptabījāt strīpuṃsaliṅgī bhavati dviretāḥ
children.translated_text: From seed with equal portions, or from seed that has been afflicted, there arises a <s>dviretāḥ</s>, bearing both female and male signs.

children.text: śukrāśayaṃ garbhagatasya hatvā karoti vāyuḥ pavanendriyatvam ||
children.translated_text: By injuring the semen-receptacle of the fetus in the womb, wind produces the condition called <s>pavanendriya</s>.
And by disrupting the opening of the semen-receptacle, wind makes one a <s>saṃskāravāhin</s>.
Sluggish and scanty seed, lack of strength, and absence of arousal are the cause of the two <s>klība</s> abnormalities.
A <s>vakrī</s> arises from obstruction to intercourse on the mother's part and from weakness of the father's seed.

children.text: īrṣyābhibhūtāvapi mandaharṣāv īrṣyārater eva vadanti hetum ||
children.translated_text: Those who are overcome by jealousy and have weak arousal are said to be the cause of the condition of delighting in jealousy.

children.text: vāyvagnidoṣād vṛṣaṇau tu yasya nāśaṃ gatau vātikaṣaṇḍakaḥ saḥ
children.translated_text: He whose testicles have been destroyed by a disorder of wind and fire is a <s>vātikaṣaṇḍaka</s>.
Thus these eight kinds of abnormality, constituted by karma, are to be recognized.
Of an embryo that has just entered the womb, of female, male, and neuter fetuses situated in the belly...

children.text: kiṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kāraṇamiṣyate kiṃ sarūpatāṃ yena ca yātyapatyam ||
children.translated_text: what is its characteristic? what is regarded as its cause? and by what does the offspring attain resemblance?

children.text: niṣṭhīvikā gauravabhaṅgasādas tandrāpraharṣau hṛdaye vyathā ca
children.translated_text: Spitting, heaviness, breaking pain in the body, lassitude, drowsiness, lack of exhilaration, pain in the heart,

children.text: tṛptiśca bījagrahaṇaṃ ca yonyāṃ garbhasya sadyo'nugatasya liṅgam ||
children.translated_text: satisfaction, and the womb's reception of the seed are the immediate signs of a conceived embryo.
A woman desiring a male child, whose bodily movements are on the left side, and whose dreams, drinks, food, habits, and activities are feminine,

children.text: savyāttagarbhā na ca vṛttagarbhā savyapradugdhā striyameva sūte ||
children.translated_text: who has conceived from the left side and whose pregnancy is not displaced, and whose milk appears first on the left, gives birth to a female.

children.text: putraṃ tvato liṅgaviparyayeṇa vyāmiśraliṅgā prakṛtiṃ tṛtīyām
children.translated_text: But by the reversal of these signs she gives birth to a son; with mixed signs, to a third nature.

children.text: garbhopapattau tu manaḥ striyā yaṃ jantuṃ vrajettatsadṛśaṃ prasūte ||
children.translated_text: At the arising of pregnancy, whatever creature the woman's mind approaches, she gives birth to one resembling that.
Four sets of four elements of the embryo, arising from mother and father,

children.text: āhārajānyātmakṛtāni caiva sarvasya sarvāṇi bhavanti dehe ||
children.translated_text: from food, and from the self's own action, all exist in the body of everyone.

children.text: teṣāṃ viśeṣād balavanti yāni bhavanti mātāpitṛkarmajāni
children.translated_text: Among these, whichever are especially strong, born from mother, father, or action,

children.text: tāni vyavasyet sadṛśatvahetuṃ sattvaṃ yathāmūlamapi vyavasyet ||
children.translated_text: one should determine them to be the cause of resemblance; and one should also determine <s>sattva</s> according to its source.

children.text: kasmāt prajāṃ strī vikṛtāṃ prasūte hīnādhikāṅgīṃ vikalendriyāṃ vā
children.translated_text: Why does a woman give birth to deformed offspring, deficient or excessive in limbs, or with impaired senses?

children.text: dehāt kathaṃ dehamupaiti cānyam ātmā sadā kairanubadhyate ca ||
children.translated_text: And how does the <s>ātman</s> go from one body to another, and by what is it always accompanied?
Through faults of the seed, the <s>ātman</s>'s action, the latent store, time, and the mother's food and conduct,
the vitiated <s>doṣas</s> produce various deformities of bodily structure, color, and sense faculties.
Just as in the rainy season currents of wood, stones, thick water, and floods

children.text: yathaiva kuryurvikṛtiṃ tathaiva garbhasya kukṣau niyatasya doṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: would deform a tree standing in the stream of a river, so the <s>doṣas</s> deform an embryo fixed in the womb.

children.text: bhūtaiścaturbhiḥ sahitaḥ susūkṣmair manojavo dehamupaiti dehāt
children.translated_text: Together with the four very subtle elements, swift as the mind, it goes from body to body.

children.text: karmātmakatvānna tu tasya dṛśyaṃ divyaṃ vinā darśanamasti rūpam ||
children.translated_text: Because it has action as its nature, its form is not visible without divine sight.

children.text: sa sarvagaḥ sarvaśarīrabhṛcca sa viśvakarmā sa ca viśvarūpaḥ
children.translated_text: It is all-pervading and bears all bodies; it is the maker of all and has all forms.

children.text: sa cetanādhāturatīndriyaśca sa nityayuk sānuśayaḥ sa eva ||
children.translated_text: It is the conscious element, beyond the senses, eternally connected, accompanied by latent residues; it is just that same one.

children.text: rasātmamātāpitṛsaṃbhavāni bhūtāni vidyāddaśa ṣaṭ ca dehe
children.translated_text: One should know that there are sixteen elements in the body, arising from rasa, the self, mother, and father.

children.text: catvāri tatrātmani saṃśritāni sthitastathātmā ca caturṣu teṣu ||
children.translated_text: Among them four are lodged in the self, and the self is likewise situated in those four.

children.text: bhūtāni mātāpitṛsaṃbhavāni rajaśca śukraṃ ca vadanti garbhe
children.translated_text: The elements arising from mother and father in the embryo are said to be menstrual blood and semen.

children.text: āpyāyyate śukramasṛk ca bhūtair yaistāni bhūtāni rasodbhavāni ||
children.translated_text: The semen and blood are nourished by the elements; those elements are born from rasa.

children.text: bhūtāni catvāri tu karmajāni yānyātmalīnāni viśanti garbham
children.translated_text: The four elements born from action, which are merged in the self, enter the embryo.

children.text: sa bījadharmā hyaparāparāṇi dehāntarāṇyātmani yāti yāti ||
children.translated_text: For, having the nature of a seed, it passes again and again into successive other bodies within the self.

children.text: rūpāddhi rūpaprabhavaḥ prasiddhaḥ karmātmakānāṃ manaso manastaḥ
children.translated_text: It is established that form comes from form; from mind, the mind of those whose nature is action.

children.text: bhavanti ye tvākṛtibuddhibhedā rajastamastatra ca karma hetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The distinctions of shape and intellect that arise have action as their cause there, together with <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: atīndriyais tair atisūkṣmarūpair ātmā kadācin na viyuktarūpaḥ
children.translated_text: The self is never at any time separated from those imperceptible, extremely subtle forms,

children.text: na karmaṇā naiva manomatibhyāṃ na cāpyahaṅkāravikāradoṣaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor from action, nor from mind and intellect, nor from the faults of modifications of egoity.

children.text: rajastamobhyāṃ hi mano'nubaddhaṃ jñānaṃ vinā tatra hi sarvadoṣāḥ
children.translated_text: For the mind is bound by <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>; without knowledge, all faults are there.

children.text: gatipravṛttyostu nimittamuktaṃ manaḥ sadoṣaṃ balavacca karma ||
children.translated_text: For movement and activity, the stated cause is a faulty mind and powerful action.

children.text: rogāḥ kutaḥ saṃśamanaṃ kimeṣāṃ harṣasya śokasya ca kiṃ nimittam
children.translated_text: Whence come diseases? What is their pacification? What is the cause of joy and grief?

children.text: śarīrasattvaprabhavā vikārāḥ kathaṃ na śāntāḥ punarāpateyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: How do disorders arising from body and <s>sattva</s>, once pacified, not return again?
Intellectual error, unsuitable objects, and the third cause, the time of transformation,

children.text: sarvāmayānāṃ trividhā ca śāntir jñānārthakālāḥ samayogayuktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are the causes of all diseases; and the threefold pacification is knowledge, objects, and time when properly joined.

children.text: dharmyāḥ kriyā harṣanimittamuktās tato'nyathā śokavaśaṃ nayanti
children.translated_text: Righteous actions are stated to be the cause of joy; actions otherwise lead one under the power of grief.
Diseases arising from body and <s>sattva</s> do not occur again when those two do not recur.

children.text: rūpasya sattvasya ca santatiryā noktastadādirnahi so'sti kaścit
children.translated_text: As for the continuity of bodily form and <s>sattva</s>, its beginning has not been stated, for there is no such beginning.

children.text: tayoravṛttiḥ kriyate parābhyāṃ dhṛtismṛtibhyāṃ parayā dhiyā ca ||
children.translated_text: Their non-recurrence is brought about by supreme steadiness, memory, and supreme understanding.

children.text: satyāśraye vā dvividhe yathokte pūrvaṃ gadebhyaḥ pratikarma nityam
children.translated_text: Or, grounded in truth in the twofold way stated before, one should always undertake counteraction against diseases.

children.text: jitendriyaṃ nānupatanti rogās tatkālayuktaṃ yadi nāsti daivam ||
children.translated_text: Diseases do not afflict one who has conquered the senses, if the measure is suited to the time and if <s>daiva</s> does not intervene.

children.text: daivaṃ purā yat kṛtamucyate tat tat pauruṣaṃ yattviha karma dṛṣṭam
children.translated_text: What was done formerly is called <s>daiva</s>; what action is seen here is <s>pauruṣa</s>.

children.text: pravṛttiheturviṣamaḥ sa dṛṣṭo nivṛttiheturhi samaḥ sa eva ||
children.translated_text: When it is unequal it is seen as the cause of activity; the same, when equal, is the cause of cessation.

children.text: haimantikaṃ doṣacayaṃ vasante pravāhayan graiṣmikam abhrakāle
children.translated_text: By expelling the winter accumulation of <s>doṣas</s> in spring, the summer accumulation in the cloudy season,

children.text: ghanātyaye vārṣikamāśu samyak prāpnoti rogānṛtujānna jātu ||
children.translated_text: and the rainy-season accumulation properly and promptly at the end of the rains, a person never incurs seasonal diseases.
A person who follows wholesome food and conduct, acts after careful consideration, is unattached to sense objects,

children.text: dātā samaḥ satyaparaḥ kṣamāvān āptopasevī ca bhavatyarogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is generous, even-minded, devoted to truth, patient, and attends upon trustworthy authorities becomes free from disease.

children.text: matirvacaḥ karma sukhānubandhaṃ sattvaṃ vidheyaṃ viśadā ca buddhiḥ
children.translated_text: He whose thought, speech, and action are followed by happiness, whose <s>sattva</s> is disciplined, whose intellect is clear,

children.text: jñānaṃ tapastatparatā ca yoge yasyāsti taṃ nānupatanti rogāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and who has knowledge, austerity, and devotion to yoga: diseases do not afflict him.
Here is the verse:
The blessed great seer, in the section of thirty-six questions of <s>Agniveśa</s>, filled with great meaning,
properly resolved them in the unequalled lineage, for the increase of knowledge.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the brief śārīra section on the descent of the embryo.
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: puruṣasyānupahataretasaḥ striyāścāpraduṣṭayoniśoṇitagarbhāśayāyā yadā bhavati saṃsargaḥ ṛtukāle yadā cānayostathāyukte saṃsarge śukraśoṇitasaṃsargamantargarbhāśayagataṃ jīvo 'vakrāmati sattvasaṃprayogāttadā garbho 'bhinirvartate sa sātmyarasopayogādarogo 'bhivardhate samyagupacāraiścopacaryamāṇaḥ tataḥ prāptakālaḥ sarvendriyopapannaḥ paripūrṇaśarīro balavarṇasattvasaṃhananasaṃpadupetaḥ sukhena jāyate samudayādeṣāṃ bhāvānāṃ mātṛjaścāyaṃ garbhaḥ pitṛjaścātmajaśca sātmyajaśca rasajaśca asti ca khalu sattvamaupapādukamiti hovāca bhagavānātreyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When there is intercourse, in the fertile season, between a man whose semen is unimpaired and a woman whose vagina, blood, and womb are unvitiated, and when, in intercourse so properly conditioned, the mingling of semen and blood has entered within the womb and the <s>jīva</s> enters it through conjunction with <s>sattva</s>, then the embryo is formed. Through the use of wholesome nutritive essence it grows without disease, and, being tended with proper care, then, at the right time, endowed with all the senses, with a fully developed body, furnished with strength, complexion, <s>sattva</s>, and compactness, it is born easily. From the conjunction of these factors this embryo is maternal, paternal, self-derived, born of suitability, and born of nutritive essence; and there is also an adventitious <s>sattva</s>. Thus said the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: neti bharadvājaḥ kiṃ kāraṇaṃ na hi mātā na pitā nātmā na sātmyaṃ na pānāśanabhakṣyalehyopayogā garbhaṃ janayanti na ca paralokādetya garbhaṃ sattvamavakrāmati
children.translated_text: "No," said <s>Bharadvāja</s>. "For what reason? For neither mother, nor father, nor self, nor suitability, nor the use of drinks, foods, chewables, and lickables produces the embryo; nor does a <s>sattva</s> come from the other world and enter the embryo.

children.text: yadi hi mātāpitarau garbhaṃ janayetāṃ bhūyasyaḥ striyaḥ pumāṃsaśca bhūyāṃsaḥ putrakāmāḥ te sarve putrajanmābhisaṃdhāya maithunadharmamāpadyamānāḥ putrāneva janayeyur duhitṝr vā duhitṛkāmāḥ na tu kāścit striyaḥ kecidvā puruṣā nirapatyāḥ syurapatyakāmā vā parideveran
children.translated_text: For if mother and father produced the embryo, then the many women and the many men who desire sons would all, entering into sexual union with the intention of producing sons, produce sons alone; or, desiring daughters, they would produce daughters. No women or men would be childless, nor would those desiring offspring lament.
Nor does the self produce itself.

children.text: yadi hyātmātmānaṃ janayejjāto vā janayed ātmānam ajāto vā taccobhayathāpyayuktam
children.translated_text: For if the self produced itself, it would produce itself either already born or unborn, and in both ways that is unsuitable.

children.text: na hi jāto janayati sattvāt na cājāto janayatyasattvāt tasmādubhayathāpyanupapattiḥ
children.translated_text: For what is born does not produce, because it already exists; and what is unborn does not produce, because it does not exist. Therefore in both ways there is no logical possibility.
Let this matter stand for the moment.

children.text: yadyayam ātmātmānaṃ śakto janayituṃ syāt na tvenamiṣṭāsveva kathaṃ yoniṣu janayedvaśinamapratihatagatiṃ kāmarūpiṇaṃ tejobalajavavarṇasattvasaṃhananasamuditam ajaram arujam amaram evaṃvidhaṃ hyātmātmānam icchatyato vā bhūyaḥ
children.translated_text: If this self were capable of producing itself, why then would it not produce itself only in desired wombs, independent, with unobstructed movement, able to take whatever form it wished, endowed with brilliance, strength, speed, complexion, <s>sattva</s>, and compactness, free from old age, free from disease, and immortal? For the self wishes itself to be of such a kind, or even greater.
And this embryo is not born of suitability.

children.text: yadi hi sātmyajaḥ syāt tarhi sātmyasevināmevaikāntena prajā syāt asātmyasevinaśca nikhilenānapatyāḥ syuḥ taccobhayamubhayatraiva dṛśyate
children.translated_text: For if it were born of suitability, then only those who practice what is suitable would invariably have offspring, and those who practice what is unsuitable would all be childless. But both cases are seen in both groups.
And this embryo is not born of nutritive essence.

children.text: yadi hi rasajaḥ syāt na kecit strīpuruṣeṣvanapatyāḥ syuḥ na hi kaścidastyeṣāṃ yo rasānnopayuṅkte śreṣṭharasopayogināṃ cedgarbhā jāyanta ityabhipretamiti evaṃ saty ājaurabhramārgamāyūragokṣīradadhighṛtamadhutailasaindhavekṣurasamudgaśālibhṛtānām evaikāntena prajā syāt śyāmākavarakoddālakakoradūṣakakandamūlabhakṣāśca nikhilenānapatyāḥ syuḥ taccobhayamubhayatra dṛśyate
children.translated_text: For if it were born of nutritive essence, there would be no childless women or men, since there is none among them who does not make use of nutritive essence. If it is maintained that embryos are born among those who use the best nutritive essences, then, this being so, offspring would invariably belong only to those who are supported by goat's, sheep's, deer's, peacock's, and cow's milk, curds, ghee, honey, oil, rock salt, sugarcane juice, mung beans, and śāli rice; while those who eat śyāmāka, varaka, uddālaka, koradūṣaka, bulbs, roots, and fruits would all be childless. But both cases are seen in both groups.

children.text: na khalvapi paralokādetya sattvaṃ garbhamavakrāmati yadi hyenamavakrāmet nāsya kiṃcit paurvadehikaṃ syādaviditamaśrutamadṛṣṭaṃ vā sa ca tacca na kiṃcidapi smarati
children.translated_text: Nor indeed does a <s>sattva</s> come from the other world and enter the embryo. For if it entered it, nothing belonging to its former body would be unknown, unheard, or unseen by it; yet that person remembers nothing at all of that.

children.text: tasmād etad brūmahe amātṛjaścāyaṃ garbho 'pitṛjaś cānātmajaś cāsātmyajaś cārasajaśca na cāsti sattvamaupapādukamiti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore we say this: this embryo is not maternal, not paternal, not self-derived, not born of suitability, and not born of nutritive essence; and there is no adventitious <s>sattva</s>."

children.text: neti bhagavānātreyaḥ sarvebhya ebhyo bhāvebhyaḥ samuditebhyo garbho 'bhinirvartate ||
children.translated_text: "No," said the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>. "The embryo is produced from all these factors when they have come together."
This embryo is maternal.

children.text: na hi māturvinā garbhotpattiḥ syāt na ca janma jarāyujānām
children.translated_text: For without the mother there would be no production of an embryo, nor any birth among creatures born from the womb.

children.text: yāni khalvasya garbhasya mātṛjāni yāni cāsya mātṛtaḥ sambhavataḥ sambhavanti tānyanuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ tad yathā tvak ca lohitaṃ ca māṃsaṃ ca medaśca nābhiśca hṛdayaṃ ca kloma ca yakṛcca plīhā ca vṛkkau ca bastiśca purīṣādhānaṃ cāmāśayaśca pakvāśayaścottaragudaṃ cādharagudaṃ ca kṣudrāntraṃ ca sthūlāntraṃ ca vapā ca vapāvahanaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: Now we shall explain those parts of this embryo that are maternal, and those that arise in it from the mother: namely, the skin, blood, flesh, fat, navel, heart, kloman, liver, spleen, the two kidneys, bladder, receptacle of feces, stomach, colon, upper rectum, lower rectum, small intestine, large intestine, omentum, and the channel that carries the omentum.
This embryo is paternal.

children.text: nahi piturṛte garbhotpattiḥ syāt na ca janma jarāyujānām
children.translated_text: For without the father there would be no production of an embryo, nor any birth among creatures born from the womb.

children.text: yāni khalvasya garbhasya pitṛjāni yāni cāsya pitṛtaḥ sambhavataḥ sambhavanti tānyanuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ tad yathā keśaśmaśrunakhalomadantāsthisirāsnāyudhamanyaḥ śukraṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: Now we shall explain those parts of this embryo that are paternal, and those that arise in it from the father: namely, hair of the head, beard, nails, body hair, teeth, bones, veins, ligaments, arteries, and semen.
This embryo is self-derived.

children.text: garbhātmā hyantarātmā yaḥ taṃ jīva ityācakṣate śāśvatam arujam ajaram amaram akṣayam abhedyam achedyam aloḍyaṃ viśvarūpaṃ viśvakarmāṇam avyaktam anādim anidhanam akṣaram api
children.translated_text: For the inner self that belongs to the embryo is what they call the <s>jīva</s>: eternal, free from disease, free from old age, immortal, imperishable, unbreakable, uncuttable, unshakable, of universal form, maker of all, unmanifest, without beginning, without end, and imperishable.

children.text: sa garbhāśayamanupraviśya śukraśoṇitābhyāṃ saṃyogametya garbhatvena janayatyātmanātmānam ātmasaṃjñā hi garbhe
children.translated_text: Having entered the womb, it comes into conjunction with semen and blood and, as an embryo, produces itself by itself; for the designation "self" applies to the embryo.

children.text: tasya punarātmano janmānāditvānnopapadyate tasmānna jāta evāyamajātaṃ garbhaṃ janayati ajāto hyayamajātaṃ garbhaṃ janayati sa caiva garbhaḥ kālāntareṇa bālayuvasthavirabhāvān prāpnoti sa yasyāṃ yasyāmavasthāyāṃ vartate tasyāṃ tasyāṃ jāto bhavati yā tvasya puraskṛtā tasyāṃ janiṣyamāṇaśca tasmāt sa eva jātaścājātaśca yugapadbhavati yasmiṃścaitadubhayaṃ sambhavati jātatvaṃ janiṣyamāṇatvaṃ ca sa jāto janyate sa caivānāgateṣvavasthāntareṣvajāto janayaty ātmanātmānam
children.translated_text: Again, because the birth of this <s>ātman</s> (self) is beginningless, that objection does not hold. Therefore this one, though unborn, generates the unborn <s>garbha</s> (embryo). For this one, unborn, generates an unborn embryo; and that same embryo, in the course of time, reaches the states of child, youth, and elder. In whatever state it exists, in that state it is born; but with respect to the state placed before it, it is still to be born. Therefore the same one is both born and unborn at the same time. In one in whom both are possible, being born and being about to be born, that one, born, is generated; and in future different states, unborn, it generates itself by itself.

children.text: sato hyavasthāntaragamanamātrameva hi janma cocyate tatra tatra vayasi tasyāṃ tasyāmavasthāyāṃ yathā satāmeva śukraśoṇitajīvānāṃ prāk saṃyogādgarbhatvaṃ na bhavati tacca saṃyogādbhavati yathā satastasyaiva puruṣasya prāgapatyāt pitṛtvaṃ na bhavati taccāpatyādbhavati tathā satastasyaiva garbhasya tasyāṃ tasyāmavasthāyāṃ jātatvam ajātatvaṃ cocyate ||
children.translated_text: For birth is indeed said to be merely the passage of an existing thing into another state, in each age and in each condition. Just as existing semen, blood, and living principle are not an embryo before conjunction, and become one through conjunction; just as that same existing man does not have fatherhood before offspring, and comes to have it through offspring; so too, of that same existing embryo, in each state, being born and being unborn are spoken of.

children.text: na khalu garbhasya na ca māturna piturna cātmanaḥ sarvabhāveṣu yatheṣṭakāritvamasti te kiṃcit svavaśāt kurvanti kiṃcit karmavaśāt kvaciccaiṣāṃ karaṇaśaktirbhavati kvacinna bhavati
children.translated_text: Certainly neither the embryo, nor the mother, nor the father, nor the <s>ātman</s> has the capacity to act exactly as desired in all states. They do something by their own power, something under the power of <s>karma</s>; in some cases they have the capacity of an instrument, and in some cases they do not.

children.text: yatra sattvādikaraṇasaṃpattatra yathābalameva yatheṣṭakāritvam ato 'nyathā viparyayaḥ
children.translated_text: Where there is completeness of <s>sattva</s> and the other instruments, there is action as desired only according to one's strength; otherwise the reverse occurs.

children.text: na ca karaṇadoṣādakaraṇamātmā sambhavati garbhajanane dṛṣṭaṃ ceṣṭā yoniraiśvaryaṃ mokṣaścātmavidbhirātmāyattam
children.translated_text: And the <s>ātman</s> does not become a non-agent in the generation of the embryo because of a defect in the instruments. Activity is observed in the generation of an embryo; source of birth, sovereignty, and mokṣa are held by knowers of the self to depend on the self.
For no one else is the maker of pleasure and pain.

children.text: na cānyato garbho jāyate jāyamānaḥ nāṅkurotpattirabījāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor is an embryo, when it is being born, born from something other than this; there is no production of a sprout from a non-seed.

children.text: yāni tu khalvasya garbhasyātmajāni yāni cāsyātmataḥ sambhavataḥ sambhavanti tānyanuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ tadyathā tāsu tāsu yoniṣūtpattirāyurātmajñānaṃ mana indriyāṇi prāṇāpānau preraṇaṃ dhāraṇamākṛtisvaravarṇaviśeṣāḥ sukhaduḥkhe icchādveṣau cetanā dhṛtirbuddhiḥ smṛtirahaṅkāraḥ prayatnaśceti ||
children.translated_text: But those things of this embryo that are born from the <s>ātman</s>, and that arise in it from the <s>ātman</s> as it comes into being, we shall explain. They are as follows: birth in various wombs, lifespan, knowledge of the self, mind, the senses, <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, impulse, support, particularities of form, voice, and complexion, pleasure and pain, desire and aversion, consciousness, firmness, intellect, memory, egoity, and effort.
And this embryo is born from <s>sātmya</s> (suitability or habituated compatibility).

children.text: na hyasātmyasevitvam antareṇa strīpuruṣayorvandhyatvamasti garbheṣu vāpyaniṣṭo bhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: For, apart from the use of what is unsuitable, there is no infertility of woman and man, nor any undesirable condition among embryos.

children.text: yāvat khalvasātmyasevināṃ strīpuruṣāṇāṃ trayo doṣāḥ prakupitāḥ śarīramupasarpanto na śukraśoṇitagarbhāśayopaghātāyopapadyante tāvat samarthā garbhajananāya bhavanti
children.translated_text: So long as, in women and men who use unsuitable things, the three <s>doṣas</s>, aggravated and entering the body, are not capable of injuring the semen, blood, and womb, so long they remain able to generate an embryo.

children.text: sātmyasevināṃ punaḥ strīpuruṣāṇāmanupahataśukraśoṇitagarbhāśayānāmṛtukāle saṃnipatitānāṃ jīvasyānavakramaṇād garbhā na prādurbhavanti
children.translated_text: Again, for women and men who use what is suitable, whose semen, blood, and womb are unimpaired, and who come together at the proper season, embryos do not appear if the <s>jīva</s> has not entered.

children.text: na hi kevalaṃ sātmyaja evāyaṃ garbhaḥ samudayo 'tra kāraṇamucyate
children.translated_text: For this embryo is not born from <s>sātmya</s> alone; an aggregate is stated here as the cause.

children.text: yāni khalvasya garbhasya sātmyajāni yāni cāsya sātmyataḥ sambhavataḥ sambhavanti tānyanuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ tad yathārogyam anālasyam alolupatvam indriyaprasādaḥ svaravarṇabījasaṃpat praharṣabhūyastvaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: Those things of this embryo that are born from <s>sātmya</s>, and that arise in it from <s>sātmya</s> as it comes into being, we shall explain. They are as follows: health, absence of laziness, freedom from greed, clarity of the senses, excellence of voice, complexion, and seed, and abundance of joy.
And this embryo is born from <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid).

children.text: na hi rasādṛte mātuḥ prāṇayātrāpi syāt kiṃ punargarbhajanma
children.translated_text: For without <s>rasa</s>, even the mother's maintenance of life would not occur, much less the birth of an embryo.

children.text: na caivāsamyagupayujyamānā rasā garbhamabhinirvartayanti na ca kevalaṃ samyagupayogādeva rasānāṃ garbhābhinirvṛttirbhavati samudāyo 'pyatra kāraṇamucyate
children.translated_text: And <s>rasas</s>, when not used properly, do not bring the embryo to completion; nor does the formation of the embryo from <s>rasas</s> occur from proper use alone. Here too an aggregate is stated as the cause.

children.text: yāni tu khalvasya garbhasya rasajāni yāni cāsya rasataḥ sambhavataḥ sambhavanti tānyanuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ tad yathā śarīrasyābhinirvṛttirabhivṛddhiḥ prāṇānubandhastṛptiḥ puṣṭirutsāhaśceti ||
children.translated_text: But those things of this embryo that are born from <s>rasa</s>, and that arise in it from <s>rasa</s> as it comes into being, we shall explain. They are as follows: formation of the body, growth, connection with life, satisfaction, nourishment, and energy.

children.text: asti khalu sattvamaupapādukaṃ yajjīvaṃ spṛkśarīreṇābhisaṃbadhnāti yasminnapagamanapuraskṛte śīlamasya vyāvartate bhaktir viparyasyate sarvendriyāṇyupatapyante balaṃ hīyate vyādhaya āpyāyyante yasmāddhīnaḥ prāṇāñjahāti yad indriyāṇām abhigrāhakaṃ ca mana ityabhidhīyate tattrividham ākhyāyate śuddhaṃ rājasaṃ tāmasamiti
children.translated_text: There is indeed an adventitious <s>sattva</s> (mind-principle) that connects the <s>jīva</s> with the tangible body. When its departure is impending, a person's character changes, inclination is reversed, all the senses are afflicted, strength declines, diseases increase, and, deprived of it, one gives up the life-breaths. That which apprehends the senses is called <s>manas</s> (mind), and it is described as threefold: pure, <s>rājasa</s>, and <s>tāmasa</s>.

children.text: yenāsya khalu mano bhūyiṣṭhaṃ tena dvitīyāyām ā jātau saṃprayogo bhavati yadā tu tenaiva śuddhena saṃyujyate tadā jāteratikrāntāyā api smarati
children.translated_text: According to whichever of these his mind is predominant, with that there is conjunction in his next birth. But when he is joined with that same pure mind, then he remembers even after the former birth has passed.

children.text: smārtaṃ hi jñānamātmanastasyaiva manaso 'nubandhādanuvartate yasyānuvṛttiṃ puraskṛtya puruṣo jātismara ityucyate
children.translated_text: For remembered knowledge belonging to the <s>ātman</s> continues because of the continuity of that very mind; with reference to the continuance of that mind, a person is called a rememberer of former births.

children.text: yāni khalvasya garbhasya sattvajāni yānyasya sattvataḥ sambhavataḥ sambhavanti tānyanuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ tad yathā bhaktiḥ śīlaṃ śaucaṃ dveṣaḥ smṛtirmohastyāgo mātsaryaṃ śauryaṃ bhayaṃ krodhastandrotsāhastaikṣṇyaṃ mārdavaṃ gāmbhīryamanavasthitatvamityevamādayaścānye te sattvavikārā yānuttarakālaṃ sattvabhedamadhikṛtyopadekṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Now we shall explain those factors of this embryo which are born from <s>sattva</s> and which arise from its coming into being through <s>sattva</s>. They are, for example: attachment, conduct, purity, hatred, memory, delusion, renunciation, envy, courage, fear, anger, torpor, energy, sharpness, gentleness, depth, instability, and other such things. These are modifications of <s>sattva</s>, which we shall teach later when treating the divisions of <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: nānāvidhāni khalu sattvāni tāni sarvāṇyekapuruṣe bhavanti na ca bhavantyekakālam ekaṃ tu prāyovṛttyāha ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, <s>sattvas</s> are of many kinds. All of them exist in a single person, but they do not occur at one and the same time; rather, one is spoken of according to what is predominant.

children.text: evamayaṃ nānāvidhānāmeṣāṃ garbhakarāṇāṃ bhāvānāṃ samudāyādabhinirvartate garbhaḥ yathā kūṭāgāraṃ nānādravyasamudāyāt yathā vā ratho nānārathāṅgasamudāyāt tasmād etad avocāma mātṛjaścāyaṃ garbhaḥ pitṛjaśca ātmajaśca sātmyajaśca rasajaśca asti ca sattvamaupapādukamiti ||
children.translated_text: Thus this embryo comes into being from the aggregate of these many kinds of embryo-producing factors, just as a house with an upper chamber comes from an aggregate of many materials, or as a chariot comes from an aggregate of many chariot-parts. Therefore we said this: this embryo is derived from the mother, derived from the father, derived from the self, derived from habituation, derived from nutritive fluid, and there is also the <s>sattva</s> that arises adventitiously.

children.text: bharadvāja uvāca yadyayam eṣāṃ nānāvidhānāṃ garbhakarāṇāṃ bhāvānāṃ samudāyādabhinirvartate garbhaḥ kathamayaṃ saṃdhīyate yadi cāpi saṃdhīyate kasmāt samudāyaprabhavaḥ san garbho manuṣyavigraheṇa jāyate manuṣyaśca manuṣyaprabhava ucyate tatra cediṣṭametadyasmānmanuṣyo manuṣyaprabhavastasmādeva manuṣyavigraheṇa jāyate yathā gaur goprabhavaḥ yathā cāśvo 'śvaprabhava iti evaṃ sati yaduktamagre samudayātmaka iti tadayuktam
children.translated_text: <s>Bharadvāja</s> said: If this embryo comes into being from the aggregate of these many kinds of embryo-producing factors, how is it joined together? And if it is joined together, why is the embryo, though produced from an aggregate, born with a human form, and why is a human being said to be produced from a human being? If it is accepted here that, because a human being is produced from a human being, therefore it is born with a human form, just as a cow is produced from a cow and a horse from a horse, then, this being so, what was said before, that it is aggregate in nature, is inappropriate.

children.text: yadi ca manuṣyo manuṣyaprabhavaḥ kasmāj jaḍāndhakubjamūkavāmanaminminavyaṅgonmattakuṣṭhikilāsibhyo jātāḥ pitṛsadṛśarūpā na bhavanti
children.translated_text: And if a human being is produced from a human being, why are those born from dull, blind, hunchbacked, mute, dwarf, stammering, deformed, insane, leprous, or vitiliginous fathers not similar in form to their fathers?

children.text: athātrāpi buddhirevaṃ syātsvenaivāyamātmā cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi vetti śrotreṇa śabdān ghrāṇena gandhān rasanena rasān sparśanena sparśān buddhyā boddhavyamityanena hetunā na jaḍādibhyo jātāḥ pitṛsadṛśā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Now if here too the thought should be this: 'This self knows forms by its own eye, sounds by the ear, odors by the nose, tastes by the tongue, touches by the tactile sense, and what is to be known by the intellect; for this reason those born from dull persons and the like are not similar to their fathers,'

children.text: atrāpi pratijñāhānidoṣaḥ syāt evamukte hyātmā satsvindriyeṣu jñaḥ syādasatsvajñaḥ yatra caitadubhayaṃ sambhavati jñatvam ajñatvaṃ ca savikāraścātmā
children.translated_text: even here there would be the fault of abandoning the thesis. For when it is stated in this way, the self would be knowing when the senses exist and unknowing when they do not exist. And where both of these are possible, knowing and not knowing, the self is subject to modification.

children.text: yadi ca darśanādibhirātmā viṣayān vetti nirindriyo darśanādivirahādajñaḥ syāt ajñatvādakāraṇam akāraṇatvācca nātmeti vāgvastumātram etad vacanamanarthaṃ syāditi ||
children.translated_text: And if the self knows objects by seeing and the like, then when it is without the senses, because it lacks seeing and the like, it would be unknowing; because it is unknowing it would not be a cause, and because it is not a cause it would not be the self. Such a statement would be merely a verbal object and would be meaningless.

children.text: ātreya uvāca purastādetat pratijñātaṃ sattvaṃ jīvaṃ spṛkśarīreṇābhisaṃbadhnātīti
children.translated_text: <s>Ātreya</s> said: This has been stated previously: <s>sattva</s> connects the living being with the body that experiences contact.

children.text: yasmāttu samudāyaprabhavaḥ san sa garbho manuṣyavigraheṇa jāyate manuṣyo manuṣyaprabhava ityucyate tadvakṣyāmaḥ bhūtānāṃ caturvidhā yonir bhavati jarāyvaṇḍasvedodbhidaḥ
children.translated_text: But as to why that embryo, though produced from an aggregate, is born with a human form and why a human being is said to be produced from a human being, we shall explain that. There are four kinds of birth-sources for living beings: placental, egg-born, sweat-born, and sprout-born.

children.text: tāsāṃ khalu catasṛṇāmapi yonīnāmekaikā yoniraparisaṃkhyeyabhedā bhavati bhūtānām ākṛtiviśeṣāparisaṃkhyeyatvāt
children.translated_text: Of these four birth-sources, each single birth-source has innumerable divisions, because the particular forms of living beings are innumerable.

children.text: tatra jarāyujānām aṇḍajānāṃ ca prāṇināmete garbhakarā bhāvā yāṃ yāṃ yonimāpadyante tasyāṃ tasyāṃ yonau tathātathārūpā bhavanti yathā kanakarajatatāmratrapusīsakānyāsicyamānāni teṣu teṣu madhūcchiṣṭavigraheṣu tāni yadā manuṣyabimbamāpadyante tadā manuṣyavigraheṇa jāyante tasmāt samudāyaprabhavaḥ san garbho manuṣyavigraheṇa jāyate manuṣyaśca manuṣyaprabhava ucyate tadyonitvāt ||
children.translated_text: Among placental and egg-born creatures, these embryo-producing factors, whichever birth-source they enter, become of a corresponding form in that particular birth-source, just as gold, silver, copper, tin, and lead, when poured into various wax molds, take those forms. When they enter a human mold, they are born with a human form. Therefore the embryo, though produced from an aggregate, is born with a human form, and a human being is said to be produced from a human being because that is its birth-source.

children.text: yaccoktaṃ yadi ca manuṣyo manuṣyaprabhavaḥ kasmānna jaḍādibhyo jātāḥ pitṛsadṛśarūpā bhavantīti tatrocyate yasya yasya hyaṅgāvayavasya bīje bījabhāga upatapto bhavati tasya tasyāṅgāvayavasya vikṛtirupajāyate nopajāyate cānupatāpāt tasmādubhayopapattirapyatra
children.translated_text: As for what was said, 'If a human being is produced from a human being, why are those born from dull persons and the like not similar in form to their fathers?' To this the answer is: in whatever limb or part the seed-portion in the seed is afflicted, a deformity arises in that very limb or part; and it does not arise when there is no affliction. Therefore both alternatives are admissible here.

children.text: sarvasya cātmajānīndriyāṇi teṣāṃ bhāvābhāvaheturdaivaṃ tasmānnaikāntato jaḍādibhyo jātāḥ pitṛsadṛśarūpā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: And all the senses are born from the self; fate is the cause of their presence or absence. Therefore those born from dull persons and the like are not in every case similar in form to their fathers.

children.text: na cātmā satsvindriyeṣu jñaḥ asatsu vā bhavatyajñaḥ na hyasattvaḥ kadācidātmā sattvaviśeṣāccopalabhyate jñānaviśeṣa iti ||
children.translated_text: Nor is the self knowing when the senses exist and unknowing when they do not exist. For the self is never without <s>sattva</s>, and a particular kind of knowledge is apprehended because of a particular condition of <s>sattva</s>.
And here there are verses:
Because the instruments are absent, knowledge of the work does not proceed for the agent;

children.text: yā kriyā vartate bhāvaiḥ sā vinā tairna vartate ||
children.translated_text: the activity that proceeds by means of factors does not proceed without them.
Even though he knows, the potter does not set to work when clay is absent.
Hear also this great spiritual power, the strength of knowledge of the self:

children.text: indriyāṇi ca saṃkṣipya manaḥ saṃkṣipya cañcalam
children.translated_text: having drawn in the senses and having drawn in the restless mind,
the knower of the self, entering inwardly, remains established in his own knowledge.
With knowledge attentive everywhere, he examines all states.
And grasp this further conclusion, <s>Bharadvāja</s>:
when, with the activity of the senses, speech, and bodily movement ceased, he is asleep and has entered dream,

children.text: viṣayān sukhaduḥkhe ca vetti nājño 'pyataḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he knows objects, pleasure, and pain; therefore, even then, he is not regarded as unknowing.
And apart from knowledge of the <s>ātman</s> (self), no knowledge of anything at all proceeds.

children.text: na hyeko vartate bhāvo vartate nāpyahetukaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For no entity exists alone, nor does it exist without a cause.
Therefore the self is the knower, <s>prakṛti</s> (nature), the seer, and indeed also the cause.
All this, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, has been determined; abandon doubt.
On this there are two verses.

children.text: heturgarbhasya nirvṛttau vṛddhau janmani caiva yaḥ
children.translated_text: The cause that operates in the formation of the embryo, in its growth, and also in its birth,
and the view of <s>Punarvasu</s> and the view of <s>Bharadvāja</s>,
the thesis and its rejection, and the clear determination of the self,
all this has been set forth in the brief section concerning the descent of the embryo.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the great <s>śārīra</s> section on the descent of the embryo.
Thus spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: yataśca garbhaḥ sambhavati yasmiṃśca garbhasaṃjñā yadvikāraśca garbhaḥ yayā cānupūrvyābhinirvartate kukṣau yaścāsya vṛddhihetuḥ yataścāsyājanma bhavati yataśca jāyamānaḥ kukṣau vināśaṃ prāpnoti yataśca kārtsnyenāvinaśyan vikṛtimāpadyate tadanuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From what the embryo arises, in what the designation "embryo" applies, what modification the embryo is, by what sequence it develops in the womb, what the cause of its growth is, from what its birth occurs, from what one being born undergoes destruction in the womb, and from what, without being entirely destroyed, it becomes deformed: this we shall explain in detail.

children.text: mātṛtaḥ pitṛta ātmataḥ sātmyato rasataḥ sattvata ityetebhyo bhāvebhyaḥ samuditebhyo garbhaḥ sambhavati
children.translated_text: The embryo arises from these factors when they have come together: from the mother, from the father, from the self, from <s>sātmya</s> (suitable habituation), from <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid), and from <s>sattva</s> (mind-principle).

children.text: tasya ye ye 'vayavā yato yataḥ sambhavataḥ sambhavanti tān vibhajya mātṛjādīnavayavān pṛthak pṛthaguktamagre ||
children.translated_text: Those parts of it that arise from each respective source, and from wherever they arise, have been stated before separately, after dividing the parts born from the mother and the others.

children.text: śukraśoṇitajīvasaṃyoge tu khalu kukṣigate garbhasaṃjñā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: But when semen, blood, and the <s>jīva</s> (living principle) come together within the womb, the designation <s>garbha</s> (embryo) applies.
The embryo is a modification of space, air, fire, water, and earth, and it has consciousness as its foundation.

children.text: evamanayā yuktyā pañcamahābhūtavikārasamudāyātmako garbhaścetanādhiṣṭhānabhūtaḥ sa hyasya ṣaṣṭho dhāturuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by this reasoning, the embryo consists of an aggregate of modifications of the five great elements and has consciousness as its foundation; for consciousness is said to be its sixth <s>dhātu</s> (constituent).

children.text: yayā cānupūrvyābhinirvartate kukṣau tāṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ gate purāṇe rajasi nave cāvasthite śuddhasnātāṃ striyamavyāpannayoniśoṇitagarbhāśayāmṛtumatīmācakṣmahe
children.translated_text: We shall explain the sequence by which it develops in the womb. When the old menstrual blood has passed and the new has become established, we call a woman in season when she has bathed after purification and when her vagina, blood, and uterus are unimpaired.

children.text: tayā saha tathābhūtayā yadā pumānavyāpannabījo miśrībhāvaṃ gacchati tadā tasya harṣodīritaḥ paraḥ śarīradhātvātmā śukrabhūto 'ṅgādaṅgāt sambhavati
children.translated_text: When a man whose seed is unimpaired enters into union with such a woman, then his highest bodily constituent, impelled by joy and having become semen, arises from limb to limb.

children.text: sa tathā harṣabhūtenātmanodīritaścādhiṣṭhitaśca bījarūpo dhātuḥ puruṣaśarīrād abhiniṣpattyocitena pathā garbhāśayam anupraviśyārtavenābhisaṃsargam eti ||
children.translated_text: That seed-form constituent, impelled and governed by the self in that state of joy, issues from the man's body by the proper channel, enters the uterus, and comes into contact with the menstrual blood.

children.text: tatra pūrvaṃ cetanādhātuḥ sattvakaraṇo guṇagrahaṇāya pravartate sa hi hetuḥ kāraṇaṃ nimittamakṣaraṃ kartā mantā veditā boddhā draṣṭā dhātā brahmā viśvakarmā viśvarūpaḥ puruṣaḥ prabhavo 'vyayo nityo guṇī grahaṇaṃ pradhānamavyaktaṃ jīvo jñaḥ pudgalaścetanāvān vibhurbhūtātmā cendriyātmā cāntarātmā ceti
children.translated_text: There the consciousness-constituent, using <s>sattva</s> as its instrument, first acts for the apprehension of qualities. It is indeed the motive, the cause, the occasion, the imperishable, the agent, the thinker, the knower, the understander, the seer, the supporter, <s>Brahmā</s>, the maker of all, the one of universal form, the person, the source, the undecaying, the eternal, the possessor of qualities, apprehension, the principal, the unmanifest, the <s>jīva</s>, the knower, the person, the conscious one, the all-pervading, the elemental self, the sensory self, and the inner self.

children.text: sa guṇopādānakāle 'ntarikṣaṃ pūrvamanyebhyo guṇebhya upādatte yathā pralayātyaye sisṛkṣurbhūtānyakṣarabhūta ātmā sattvopādānaḥ pūrvataramākāśaṃ sṛjati tataḥ krameṇa vyaktataraguṇān dhātūn vāyvādikāṃścaturaḥ tathā dehagrahaṇe 'pi pravartamānaḥ pūrvataramākāśamevopādatte tataḥ krameṇa vyaktataraguṇān dhātūn vāyvādikāṃścaturaḥ
children.translated_text: At the time of taking up qualities, it first takes up space before the other qualities, just as, at the end of dissolution, the imperishable self, desiring to create beings and taking up <s>sattva</s>, first creates space and then, in sequence, the four constituents beginning with air, whose qualities are progressively more manifest. So too, when proceeding to assume a body, it first takes up space itself, and then, in sequence, the four constituents beginning with air, whose qualities are progressively more manifest.
All this taking up of qualities occurs in an exceedingly minute time.

children.text: sa sarvaguṇavān garbhatvamāpannaḥ prathame māsi saṃmūrchitaḥ sarvadhātukaluṣīkṛtaḥ kheṭabhūto bhavatyavyaktavigrahaḥ sadasadbhūtāṅgāvayavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Possessing all qualities and having assumed the state of an embryo, in the first month it is congealed, made turbid by all the constituents, slime-like, indistinct in form, with limbs and parts as though both existent and nonexistent.

children.text: dvitīye māsi ghanaḥ sampadyate piṇḍaḥ peśyarbudaṃ vā
children.translated_text: In the second month it becomes a solid mass, a lump, a <s>peśī</s>, or an <s>arbuda</s>.

children.text: tatra ghanaḥ puruṣaḥ peśī strī arbudaṃ napuṃsakam ||
children.translated_text: Among these, a solid mass is male, a <s>peśī</s> is female, and an <s>arbuda</s> is neuter.
In the third month all the senses and all the limbs and parts develop simultaneously.

children.text: tatrāsya kecidaṅgāvayavā mātṛjādīnavayavān vibhajya pūrvamuktā yathāvat
children.translated_text: Some of its limbs and parts, after being divided into parts born from the mother and the others, have already been stated previously as they are.
But now, by dividing them according to modifications of the great elements, we shall further explain these same limbs and parts, some in another way and others in addition.
Even the maternal and other parts of it are themselves simply modifications of the great elements.

children.text: tatrāsyākāśātmakaṃ śabdaḥ śrotraṃ lāghavaṃ saukṣmyaṃ vivekaśca vāyvātmakaṃ sparśaḥ sparśanaṃ raukṣyaṃ preraṇaṃ dhātuvyūhanaṃ ceṣṭāśca śārīryaḥ agnyātmakaṃ rūpaṃ darśanaṃ prakāśaḥ paktirauṣṇyaṃ ca abātmakaṃ raso rasanaṃ śaityaṃ mārdavaṃ snehaḥ kledaśca pṛthivyātmakaṃ gandho ghrāṇaṃ gauravaṃ sthairyaṃ mūrtiśceti ||
children.translated_text: Of it, what consists of space is sound, hearing, lightness, subtlety, and separation; what consists of air is touch, the tactile faculty, dryness, propulsion, arrangement of the constituents, and bodily movements; what consists of fire is form, sight, illumination, digestion, and heat; what consists of water is taste, tasting, coldness, softness, unctuousness, and moisture; and what consists of earth is odor, smelling, heaviness, stability, and formed shape.
Thus this person is commensurate with the world.

children.text: yāvanto hi loke mūrtimanto bhāvaviśeṣāstāvantaḥ puruṣe yāvantaḥ puruṣe tāvanto loke iti budhāstvevaṃ draṣṭumicchanti ||
children.translated_text: For as many particular entities possessed of form as there are in the world, so many are in the person; and as many as there are in the person, so many are in the world. The wise wish to see it in this way.

children.text: evam asyendriyāṇyaṅgāvayavāśca yaugapadyenābhinirvartante 'nyatra tebhyo bhāvebhyo ye 'sya jātasyottarakālaṃ jāyante tad yathā dantā vyañjanāni vyaktībhāvastathāyuktāni cāparāṇi
children.translated_text: Thus his senses and limbs and parts develop simultaneously, apart from those features that arise after he is born, such as teeth, distinguishing marks, manifest appearance, and other things of that sort.
This is <s>prakṛti</s> (normal condition); <s>vikṛti</s> (abnormality), on the other hand, is what is otherwise than this.

children.text: santi khalvasmin garbhe kecinnityā bhāvāḥ santi cānityāḥ kecit
children.translated_text: Indeed, in this <s>garbha</s> (embryo) some states are permanent, and some are impermanent.

children.text: tasya ya evāṅgāvayavāḥ saṃtiṣṭhante ta eva strīliṅgaṃ puruṣaliṅgaṃ napuṃsakaliṅgaṃ vā bibhrati
children.translated_text: Whatever limbs and parts of it are formed, those very same bear the female mark, the male mark, or the neuter mark.

children.text: tatra strīpuruṣayorye vaiśeṣikā bhāvāḥ pradhānasaṃśrayā guṇasaṃśrayāśca teṣāṃ yato bhūyastvaṃ tato 'nyatarabhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: Among these, the particular states of woman and man, those based on the principal organ and those based on qualities, whichever of them predominate, from that there is the state of one or the other.

children.text: tadyathāklaibyaṃ bhīrutvamavaiśāradyaṃ moho 'navasthānamadhogurutvamasahanaṃ śaithilyaṃ mārdavaṃ garbhāśayabījabhāgastathāyuktāni cāparāṇi strīkarāṇi ato viparītāni puruṣakarāṇi ubhayabhāgāvayavā napuṃsakakarāṇi bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: For example, lack of virility, timidity, want of confidence, delusion, instability, downward heaviness, inability to endure, looseness, softness, the womb and the seed-portion when so conditioned, and other such factors produce femaleness; the opposites of these produce maleness; and parts and limbs belonging to both sides produce neuterness.

children.text: tasya yatkālamevendriyāṇi saṃtiṣṭhante tatkālameva cetasi vedanā nirbandhaṃ prāpnoti tasmāt tadā prabhṛti garbhaḥ spandate prārthayate ca janmāntarānubhūtaṃ yat kiṃcit tad dvaihṛdayyam ācakṣate vṛddhāḥ
children.translated_text: At the very time when its senses are formed, at that same time sensation becomes fixed in its mind. Therefore from then onward the <s>garbha</s> moves and desires whatever it has experienced in previous births; the elders call this <s>dvaihṛdayya</s> (the two-hearted state).

children.text: mātṛjaṃ cāsya hṛdayaṃ mātṛhṛdayenābhisaṃbaddhaṃ bhavati rasavāhinībhiḥ saṃvāhinībhiḥ tasmāttayostābhirbhaktiḥ saṃspandate
children.translated_text: Its heart, being maternal in origin, is connected with the mother's heart by channels that carry <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid). Therefore the inclination of the two pulses through those channels.

children.text: taccaiva kāraṇamavekṣamāṇā na dvaihṛdayyasya vimānitaṃ garbhamicchanti kartum
children.translated_text: Considering this very cause, they do not wish to make a <s>garbha</s> whose two-hearted state has been disregarded.
For when it is disregarded, destruction or deformity of it is observed.

children.text: samānayogakṣemā hi tadā bhavati garbheṇa keṣucidartheṣu mātā
children.translated_text: At that time, in certain matters, the mother has the same welfare and danger as the <s>garbha</s>.
Therefore skilled physicians treat a pregnant woman especially with what is pleasing and beneficial.

children.text: tasyā garbhāpatter dvaihṛdayyasya ca vijñānārthaṃ liṅgāni samāsenopadekṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: For the sake of recognizing her conception and the two-hearted state, we shall briefly teach the signs.

children.text: upacārasādhanaṃ hyasya jñāne jñānaṃ ca liṅgataḥ tasmādiṣṭo liṅgopadeśaḥ
children.translated_text: For treatment is made possible by knowing it, and knowledge comes from signs; therefore the instruction on signs is desired.

children.text: tadyathā ārtavādarśanam āsyasaṃsravaṇam anannābhilāṣaśchardir arocako 'mlakāmatā ca viśeṣeṇa śraddhāpraṇayanamuccāvaceṣu bhāveṣu gurugātratvaṃ cakṣuṣorglāniḥ stanayoḥ stanyamoṣṭhayoḥ stanamaṇḍalayośca kārṣṇyamatyarthaṃ śvayathuḥ pādayor īṣallomarājyudgamo yonyāścāṭālatvamiti garbhe paryāgate rūpāṇi bhavati ||
children.translated_text: They are as follows: absence of menstruation, salivation in the mouth, lack of desire for food, vomiting, distaste, a special desire for sour things, a marked attraction and affection for various sorts of objects, heaviness of the body, weariness of the eyes, milk in the breasts, extreme darkening of the lips and of the areolae of the breasts, swelling of the feet, a slight appearance of a line of hair, and dilation of the vagina. These are the forms when the <s>garbha</s> has arrived.
Whatever she desires, that should be given to her, except for things that injure the <s>garbha</s>.

children.text: garbhopaghātakarāstvime bhāvā bhavanti tad yathā sarvam atigurūṣṇatīkṣṇaṃ dāruṇāśca ceṣṭāḥ imāṃścānyānupadiśanti vṛddhāḥ devatārakṣo'nucaraparirakṣaṇārthaṃ na raktāni vāsāṃsi bibhṛyānna madakarāṇi madyānyabhyavaharenna yānamadhirohenna māṃsamaśnīyāt sarvendriyapratikūlāṃśca bhāvān dūrataḥ parivarjayet yaccānyadapi kiṃcit striyo vidyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The factors that injure the <s>garbha</s> are these: everything excessively heavy, hot, or sharp, and violent activities. The elders also prescribe these and other things for protection against attendants of deities and demons: she should not wear red garments, should not consume intoxicating liquors, should not mount a vehicle, should not eat meat, and should avoid from afar all things hostile to the senses, and anything else that women know of.

children.text: tīvrāyāṃ tu khalu prārthanāyāṃ kāmamahitamapyasyai hitenopahitaṃ dadyāt prārthanāvinayanārtham
