children.translated_text: But when the craving is intense, even what is unwholesome to her desire should be given to her, combined with what is wholesome, in order to pacify the craving.

children.text: prārthanāsaṃdhāraṇāddhi vāyuḥ prakupito 'ntaḥśarīramanucaran garbhasyāpadyamānasya vināśaṃ vairūpyaṃ vā kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: For from the restraint of craving, <s>vāyu</s> (wind), becoming aggravated and moving within the body, may cause destruction or deformity of the <s>garbha</s> as it is developing.

children.text: caturthe māsi sthiratvamāpadyate garbhaḥ tasmāttadā garbhiṇī gurugātratvamadhikamāpadyate viśeṣeṇa ||
children.translated_text: In the fourth month the <s>garbha</s> attains stability; therefore at that time the pregnant woman especially experiences increased heaviness of body.

children.text: pañcame māsi garbhasya māṃsaśoṇitopacayo bhavatyadhikamanyebhyo māsebhyaḥ tasmāttadā garbhiṇī kārśyamāpadyate viśeṣeṇa ||
children.translated_text: In the fifth month there is greater increase of the <s>garbha</s>'s flesh and blood than in the other months; therefore at that time the pregnant woman especially becomes thin.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe māsi garbhasya balavarṇopacayo bhavatyadhikamanyebhyo māsebhyaḥ tasmāttadā garbhiṇī balavarṇahānimāpadyate viśeṣeṇa ||
children.translated_text: In the sixth month there is greater increase of the <s>garbha</s>'s strength and complexion than in the other months; therefore at that time the pregnant woman especially suffers loss of strength and complexion.

children.text: saptame māsi garbhaḥ sarvairbhāvairāpyāyyate tasmāttadā garbhiṇī sarvākāraiḥ klāntatamā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In the seventh month the <s>garbha</s> is nourished in all respects; therefore at that time the pregnant woman becomes most exhausted in every way.

children.text: aṣṭame māsi garbhaśca mātṛto garbhataśca mātā rasahāriṇībhiḥ saṃvāhinībhirmuhurmuhurojaḥ parasparata ādadāte garbhasya ā sampūrṇatvāt
children.translated_text: In the eighth month, the <s>garbha</s> from the mother and the mother from the <s>garbha</s> repeatedly take <s>ojas</s> (vital essence) from one another through the channels that convey and carry <s>rasa</s>, because the <s>garbha</s> is not yet complete.

children.text: tasmāttadā garbhiṇī muhurmuhurmudā yuktā bhavati muhurmuhuśca mlānā tathā garbhaḥ tasmāttadā garbhasya janma vyāpattimad bhavatyojaso 'navasthitatvāt
children.translated_text: Therefore at that time the pregnant woman is repeatedly joyful and repeatedly faded, and so too is the <s>garbha</s>. Therefore at that time the birth of the <s>garbha</s> is attended with danger, because <s>ojas</s> is not settled.
Considering precisely this matter, skilled physicians say that the eighth month is not to be counted.

children.text: tasminnekadivasātikrānte 'pi navamaṃ māsamupādāya prasavakālam ityāhur ā daśamānmāsāt
children.translated_text: When even one day has passed beyond it, beginning with the ninth month they call it the time of delivery, up to the tenth month.

children.text: etāvān prasavakālaḥ vaikārikamataḥ paraṃ kukṣāvavasthānaṃ garbhasya ||
children.translated_text: This much is the time of delivery; beyond this, the stay of the <s>garbha</s> in the womb is pathological.
Thus it develops in the womb in this sequence.

children.text: mātrādīnāṃ khalu garbhakarāṇāṃ bhāvānāṃ saṃpadastathā vṛttasya sauṣṭhavānmātṛtaścaivopasnehopasvedābhyāṃ kālapariṇāmāt svabhāvasaṃsiddheśca kukṣau vṛddhiṃ prāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: Through the excellence of the embryo-producing factors such as those from the mother and the rest, and likewise through good conduct, through nourishment and warmth from the mother, through the maturation of time, and through natural accomplishment, it attains growth in the womb.

children.text: mātrādīnāmeva tu khalu garbhakarāṇāṃ bhāvānāṃ vyāpattinimittam asya ā janma bhavati ||
children.translated_text: But because of impairment of those very embryo-producing factors such as those from the mother and the rest, its condition from birth becomes defective.

children.text: ye hyasya kukṣau vṛddhihetusamākhyātā bhāvāsteṣāṃ viparyayādudare vināśamāpadyate athavāpyacirajātaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: For those factors that have been described as causes of growth for him in the womb: from the opposite of them he perishes in the abdomen, or else he may be born prematurely.

children.text: yatastu kārtsnyenāvinaśyan vikṛtimāpadyate tad anuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ yadā striyā doṣaprakopaṇoktānyāsevamānāyā doṣāḥ prakupitāḥ śarīramupasarpantaḥ śoṇitagarbhāśayāvupapadyante na ca kārtsnyena śoṇitagarbhāśayau dūṣayanti tadeyaṃ garbhaṃ labhate strī tadā tasya garbhasya mātṛjānāmavayavānāmanyatamo 'vayavo vikṛtimāpadyata eko 'thavāneke yasya yasya hyavayavasya bīje bījabhāge vā doṣāḥ prakopamāpadyante taṃ tamavayavaṃ vikṛtirāviśati
children.translated_text: But when, without perishing completely, he undergoes deformity, we shall explain that in detail. When, in a woman who is using the things said to aggravate the <s>doṣas</s>, the aggravated <s>doṣas</s>, spreading through the body, reach the blood and the womb, but do not corrupt the blood and womb completely, then that woman conceives an embryo. At that time, of the maternal parts of that embryo, one part, or more than one, undergoes deformity. For whichever part has its seed or seed-portion affected by the aggravated <s>doṣas</s>, deformity enters that very part.

children.text: yadā hyasyāḥ śoṇite garbhāśayabījabhāgaḥ pradoṣamāpadyate tadā vandhyāṃ janayati yadā punarasyāḥ śoṇite garbhāśayabījabhāgāvayavaḥ pradoṣamāpadyate tadā pūtiprajāṃ janayati yadā tvasyāḥ śoṇite garbhāśayabījabhāgāvayavaḥ strīkarāṇāṃ ca śarīrabījabhāgānāmekadeśaḥ pradoṣamāpadyate tadā stryākṛtibhūyiṣṭhāmastriyaṃ vārtāṃ nāma janayati tāṃ strīvyāpadamācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: For when, in her blood, the seed-portion belonging to the womb is impaired, then she gives birth to a barren woman. But when, in her blood, a constituent part of the seed-portion belonging to the womb is impaired, then she gives birth to one whose offspring perish. And when, in her blood, a constituent part of the seed-portion belonging to the womb, and one part of the bodily seed-portions that produce femaleness, are impaired, then she gives birth to a non-woman, mostly female in form, called <s>vārtā</s>. That is called a female disorder.

children.text: evameva puruṣasya yadā bīje bījabhāgaḥ pradoṣamāpadyate tadā vandhyaṃ janayati yadā punarasya bīje bījabhāgāvayavaḥ pradoṣamāpadyate tadā pūtiprajaṃ janayati yadā tvasya bīje bījabhāgāvayavaḥ puruṣakarāṇāṃ ca śarīrabījabhāgānāmekadeśaḥ pradoṣamāpadyate tadā puruṣākṛtibhūyiṣṭhamapuruṣaṃ tṛṇaputrikaṃ nāma janayati tāṃ puruṣavyāpadamācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: In just the same way, when in a man the seed-portion in the semen is impaired, then he begets a sterile male. But when a constituent part of the seed-portion in his semen is impaired, then he begets one whose offspring perish. And when a constituent part of the seed-portion in his semen, and one part of the bodily seed-portions that produce maleness, are impaired, then he begets a non-male, mostly male in form, called <s>tṛṇaputrika</s>. That is called a male disorder.

children.text: etena mātṛjānāṃ pitṛjānāṃ cāvayavānāṃ vikṛtivyākhyānena sātmyajānāṃ rasajānāṃ sattvajānāṃ cāvayavānāṃ vikṛtirvyākhyātā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By this explanation of deformity in the parts derived from the mother and those derived from the father, deformity in the parts derived from <s>sātmya</s> (habituated compatibility), from <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid), and from <s>sattva</s> (mind-principle) has also been explained.

children.text: nirvikāraḥ parastvātmā sarvabhūtānāṃ nirviśeṣaḥ sattvaśarīrayostu viśeṣādviśeṣopalabdhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the supreme <s>ātman</s> (self) is free from modification and without distinction in all beings; particular distinction is apprehended because of the distinction of <s>sattva</s> and body.

children.text: tatra trayaḥ śarīradoṣā vātapittaśleṣmāṇaḥ te śarīraṃ dūṣayanti dvau punaḥ sattvadoṣau rajastamaśca tau sattvaṃ dūṣayataḥ
children.translated_text: Here there are three bodily <s>doṣas</s>: <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s>. They corrupt the body. Again there are two mental <s>doṣas</s>, <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>; they corrupt <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: tābhyāṃ ca sattvaśarīrābhyāṃ duṣṭābhyāṃ vikṛtirupajāyate nopajāyate cāpraduṣṭābhyām ||
children.translated_text: And when those two, <s>sattva</s> and body, are corrupted, deformity arises; when they are not corrupted, it does not arise.
Here the body has previously been stated to be fourfold according to the particular kind of birth-source.

children.text: trividhaṃ khalu sattvaṃ śuddhaṃ rājasaṃ tāmasamiti
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s>, however, is threefold: pure, <s>rājasa</s>, and <s>tāmasa</s>.

children.text: tatra śuddhamadoṣamākhyātaṃ kalyāṇāṃśatvāt rājasaṃ sadoṣamākhyātaṃ roṣāṃśatvāt tāmasamapi sadoṣamākhyātaṃ mohāṃśatvāt
children.translated_text: Among these, the pure is said to be free from defect because it has a share of the auspicious. The <s>rājasa</s> is said to be defective because it has a share of anger. The <s>tāmasa</s> too is said to be defective because it has a share of delusion.

children.text: teṣāṃ tu trayāṇāmapi sattvānāmekaikasya bhedāgram aparisaṃkhyeyaṃ taratamayogāccharīrayoniviśeṣebhyaś cānyonyānuvidhānatvācca
children.translated_text: But the range of divisions of each one of these three kinds of <s>sattva</s> is not to be counted, because of gradation, because of the particular kinds of bodily birth-source, and because each follows the other.

children.text: śarīraṃ hyapi sattvamanuvidhīyate sattvaṃ ca śarīram
children.translated_text: For the body also conforms to <s>sattva</s>, and <s>sattva</s> conforms to the body.
Therefore, for the sake of illustration, we shall explain some divisions of <s>sattva</s> by indicative designation.

children.text: tad yathā śuciṃ satyābhisaṃdhaṃ jitātmānaṃ saṃvibhāginaṃ jñānavijñānavacanaprativacanasampannaṃ smṛtimantaṃ kāmakrodhalobhamānamoherṣyāharṣāmarṣāpetaṃ samaṃ sarvabhūteṣu brāhmaṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: One should know as <s>brāhma</s> the person who is pure, intent on truth, self-controlled, sharing, endowed with knowledge, discernment, speech, and reply, mindful, free from desire, anger, greed, pride, delusion, envy, elation, and impatience, and equal toward all beings.

One should know as <s>ārṣa</s> the person who is devoted to sacrifice, study, vows, oblation, and chastity, who observes hospitality as a vow, whose intoxication, pride, passion, hatred, delusion, greed, and anger are pacified, and who is endowed with brilliance, speech, understanding, retention, and power.

children.text: aiśvaryavantamādeyavākyaṃ yajvānaṃ śūramojasvinaṃ tejasopetamakliṣṭakarmāṇaṃ dīrghadarśinaṃ dharmārthakāmābhiratamaindraṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: One should know as <s>aindra</s> the person who possesses lordly power, whose word is accepted, who sacrifices, is heroic, vigorous, endowed with splendor, whose action is unwearied, who sees far ahead, and who is devoted to <s>dharma</s>, wealth, and pleasure.

children.text: lekhāsthavṛttaṃ prāptakāriṇam asaṃprahāryam utthānavantaṃ smṛtimantam aiśvaryalambhinaṃ vyapagatarāgerṣyādveṣamohaṃ yāmyaṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: One should know as <s>yāmya</s> the person whose conduct is orderly, who acts at the proper time, is not to be shaken, is energetic, mindful, obtains lordly power, and is free from passion, envy, hatred, and delusion.

children.text: śūraṃ dhīraṃ śucimaśucidveṣiṇaṃ yajvānamambhovihāraratimakliṣṭakarmāṇaṃ sthānakopaprasādaṃ vāruṇaṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: One should know as <s>vāruṇa</s> the person who is heroic, firm, pure, a hater of impurity, a sacrificer, fond of sport in water, unwearied in action, and whose anger and favor arise in due place.

children.text: sthānamānopabhogaparivārasampannaṃ dharmārthakāmanityaṃ śuciṃ sukhavihāraṃ vyaktakopaprasādaṃ kauberaṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: One should know as <s>kaubera</s> the person who is endowed with position, honor, enjoyment, and retinue, who is constantly devoted to <s>dharma</s>, wealth, and pleasure, is pure, lives comfortably, and whose anger and favor are manifest.

One should know as <s>gāndharva</s> the person who loves dancing, singing, instrumental music, jests, verses, tales, histories, and purāṇas, who is skilled in them, who is constantly fond of perfumes, garlands, unguents, clothing, women, and pleasure, and who is not envious.

children.text: ityenaṃ śuddhasya sattvasya saptavidhaṃ bhedāṃśaṃ vidyāt kalyāṇāṃśatvāt tatsaṃyogāttu brāhmamatyantaśuddhaṃ vyavasyet ||
children.translated_text: Thus one should know this sevenfold division of pure <s>sattva</s>, because it has a share of the auspicious. But from their combination, one should determine the <s>brāhma</s> type to be supremely pure.

children.text: śūraṃ caṇḍam asūyakam aiśvaryavantam aupadhikaṃ raudram ananukrośamātmapūjakam āsuraṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: One should know as <s>āsura</s> the person who is heroic, fierce, envious, powerful, deceitful, harsh, without compassion, and self-worshipping.

children.text: amarṣiṇamanubandhakopaṃ chidraprahāriṇaṃ krūramāhārātimātrarucimāmiṣapriyatamaṃ svapnāyāsabahulamīrṣyuṃ rākṣasaṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: One should know as <s>rākṣasa</s> the person who is intolerant, whose anger is persistent, who strikes at weaknesses, who is cruel, who has excessive liking for food, who is especially fond of meat, who has much sleep and fatigue, and who is envious.

children.text: mahāśanaṃ straiṇaṃ strīrahaskāmamaśuciṃ śucidveṣiṇaṃ bhīruṃ bhīṣayitāraṃ vikṛtavihārāhāraśīlaṃ paiśācaṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: One should know the <s>paiśāca</s> type as gluttonous, devoted to women, desiring secret intercourse with women, impure, hating purity, timid, frightening others, and habituated to distorted conduct and diet.

children.text: kruddhaśūramakruddhabhīruṃ tīkṣṇamāyāsabahulaṃ saṃtrastagocaram āhāravihāraparaṃ sārpaṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: One should know the <s>sārpa</s> type as brave when angry but timid when not angry, sharp, full of strain, moving in a field of fear, and devoted to food and recreation.

children.text: āhārakāmam atiduḥkhaśīlācāropacāram asūyakam asaṃvibhāginam atilolupam akarmaśīlaṃ praitaṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: One should know the <s>preta</s> type as craving food, extremely miserable in habit, conduct, and treatment, envious, unwilling to share, excessively greedy, and inactive.

children.text: anuṣaktakāmam ajasram āhāravihāraparam anavasthitam amarṣaṇam asaṃcayaṃ śākunaṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: One should know the <s>śākuna</s> type as constantly attached to desire, always devoted to food and recreation, unstable, intolerant, and without accumulation.

children.text: ityevaṃ khalu rājasasya sattvasya ṣaḍvidhaṃ bhedāṃśaṃ vidyāt roṣāṃśatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed one should know the sixfold partial division of the <s>rājasa</s> <s>sattva</s>, because anger is its component.

children.text: nirākariṣṇumamedhasaṃ jugupsitācārāhāraṃ maithunaparaṃ svapnaśīlaṃ pāśavaṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: One should know the <s>pāśava</s> type as rejecting others, unintelligent, disgusting in conduct and diet, intent on intercourse, and given to sleep.

children.text: bhīrum abudham āhāralubdham anavasthitam anuṣaktakāmakrodhaṃ saraṇaśīlaṃ toyakāmaṃ mātsyaṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: One should know the <s>mātsya</s> type as timid, foolish, greedy for food, unstable, attached to desire and anger, prone to fleeing, and fond of water.
One should know the <s>vānaspatya</s> type as lazy, solely absorbed in food, and devoid of every faculty of intelligence.

children.text: ityevaṃ tāmasasya sattvasya trividhaṃ bhedāṃśaṃ vidyānmohāṃśatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Thus one should know the threefold partial division of the <s>tāmasa</s> <s>sattva</s>, because delusion is its component.

children.text: ityaparisaṃkhyeyabhedānāṃ trayāṇāmapi sattvānāṃ bhedaikadeśo vyākhyātaḥ śuddhasya sattvasya saptavidho brahmarṣiśakrayamavaruṇakuberagandharvasattvānukāreṇa rājasasya ṣaḍvidho daityapiśācarākṣasasarpapretaśakunisattvānukāreṇa tāmasasya trividhaḥ paśumatsyavanaspatisattvānukāreṇa kathaṃca yathāsattvamupacāraḥ syāditi ||
children.translated_text: Thus, among the innumerably divided three kinds of <s>sattva</s>, a portion of their divisions has been explained: the pure <s>sattva</s> as sevenfold, in imitation of the <s>Brahmarṣi</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, and <s>Gandharva</s> types of being; the <s>rājasa</s> as sixfold, in imitation of the <s>Daitya</s>, <s>Piśāca</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, serpent, <s>Preta</s>, and bird types of being; and the <s>tāmasa</s> as threefold, in imitation of the animal, fish, and plant types of being, so that, in some way, treatment may be according to the person's <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: kevalaścāyamuddeśo yathoddeśamabhinirdiṣṭo bhavati garbhāvakrāntisamprayuktaḥ tasya cārthasya vijñāne sāmarthyaṃ garbhakarāṇāṃ ca bhāvānām anusamādhiḥ vighātaśca vighātakarāṇāṃ bhāvānāmiti ||
children.translated_text: And this is only a summary; what was set out has been indicated according to that outline, in connection with the descent of the embryo. From knowing its meaning there comes capacity: the proper observance of the embryo-producing factors, and the prevention of the factors that obstruct them.
On this there are verses:
The cause, the self, the nature, and the growth in the womb in sequence,
and the cause of the embryo's growth: these five factors are designated auspicious.
The cause of non-birth, and also the cause of destruction and deformity,
these three inauspicious factors they call obstructive to the embryo.
The physician who knows in every way all these eight factors,

children.text: sarvathā veda yaḥ sarvān sa rājñaḥ kartumarhati ||
children.translated_text: described as auspicious and inauspicious, is fit to treat a king.
Such a wise man is able to know the means for obtaining an embryo,
and also those factors that have been stated to obstruct the embryo.
Now then we shall explain the bodily section called the analysis of the <s>puruṣa</s>.
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.
"This <s>puruṣa</s> is commensurate with the world," said the blessed <s>Punarvasu Ātreya</s>.

children.text: yāvanto hi loke mūrtimanto bhāvaviśeṣāstāvantaḥ puruṣe yāvantaḥ puruṣe tāvanto loke ityevaṃvādinaṃ bhagavantamātreyamagniveśa uvāca naitāvatā vākyenoktaṃ vākyārthamavagāhāmahe bhagavatā buddhyā bhūyastaramato 'nuvyākhyāyamānaṃ śuśrūṣāmaha iti ||
children.translated_text: When the blessed <s>Ātreya</s> had spoken in this way, <s>Agniveśa</s> said: "By this much speech we do not comprehend the meaning of the statement uttered by the blessed one. With our understanding we wish to hear it explained further and more fully."

children.text: tamuvāca bhagavānātreyaḥ aparisaṃkhyeyā lokāvayavaviśeṣāḥ puruṣāvayavaviśeṣā apyaparisaṃkhyeyāḥ teṣāṃ yathāsthūlaṃ katicidbhāvān sāmānyamabhipretyodāhariṣyāmaḥ tānekamanā nibodha samyagupavarṇyamānānagniveśa
children.translated_text: The blessed <s>Ātreya</s> said to him: "The particular components of the world are innumerable, and the particular components of the <s>puruṣa</s> too are innumerable. With reference to their general correspondence, I shall state some of them in a gross way. Listen to them with one-pointed mind, <s>Agniveśa</s>, as they are properly described.

children.text: ṣaḍdhātavaḥ samuditāḥ puruṣa iti śabdaṃ labhante tadyathā pṛthivyāpastejo vāyurākāśaṃ brahma cāvyaktamiti eta eva ca ṣaḍdhātavaḥ samuditāḥ puruṣa iti śabdaṃ labhante ||
children.translated_text: The six elements, when combined, receive the designation <s>puruṣa</s>: namely earth, waters, fire, wind, space, and <s>Brahman</s>, the unmanifest. These very six elements, when combined, receive the designation <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: tasya puruṣasya pṛthivī mūrtiḥ āpaḥ kledaḥ tejo 'bhisaṃtāpaḥ vāyuḥ prāṇaḥ viyat suṣirāṇi brahma antarātmā
children.translated_text: In that <s>puruṣa</s>, earth is solid form, waters are moisture, fire is heat, wind is <s>prāṇa</s>, space is the cavities, and <s>Brahman</s> is the inner self.

children.text: yathā khalu brāhmī vibhūtirloke tathā puruṣe 'pyāntarātmikī vibhūtiḥ brahmaṇo vibhūtirloke prajāpatirantarātmano vibhūtiḥ puruṣe sattvaṃ yastvindro loke sa puruṣe 'haṅkāraḥ ādityastvādānaṃ rudro roṣaḥ somaḥ prasādaḥ vasavaḥ sukham aśvinau kāntiḥ marudutsāhaḥ viśvedevāḥ sarvendriyāṇi sarvendriyārthāśca tamo mohaḥ jyotirjñānaṃ yathā lokasya sargādistathā puruṣasya garbhādhānaṃ yathā kṛtayugamevaṃ bālyaṃ yathā tretā tathā yauvanaṃ yathā dvāparastathā sthāviryaṃ yathā kalirevamāturyaṃ yathā yugāntastathā maraṇamiti
children.translated_text: Just as the power of <s>Brahman</s> exists in the world, so in the <s>puruṣa</s> there is the power belonging to the inner self. The manifestation of <s>Brahman</s> in the world is <s>Prajāpati</s>; the manifestation of the inner self in the <s>puruṣa</s> is <s>sattva</s>. What <s>Indra</s> is in the world, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> is in the <s>puruṣa</s>; <s>Āditya</s> is taking in, <s>Rudra</s> is anger, <s>Soma</s> is serenity, the <s>Vasus</s> are pleasure, the <s>Aśvins</s> are beauty, the <s>Maruts</s> are energy, and the <s>Viśvedevas</s> are all the senses and all the sense-objects. Darkness is delusion; light is knowledge. As the creation is the beginning of the world, so conception is the beginning of the <s>puruṣa</s>. As the <s>Kṛta</s> age is, so is childhood; as the <s>Tretā</s>, so is youth; as the <s>Dvāpara</s>, so is old age; as the <s>Kali</s>, so is illness; and as the end of an age is, so is death.
By this inference, <s>Agniveśa</s>, one should know the correspondence even of particular components of the world and the <s>puruṣa</s> that have not been stated.

children.text: evaṃvādinaṃ bhagavantamātreyamagniveśa uvāca evam etat sarvamanapavādaṃ yathoktaṃ bhagavatā lokapuruṣayoḥ sāmānyam
children.translated_text: When the blessed <s>Ātreya</s> had spoken in this way, <s>Agniveśa</s> said: "All this is without exception just as the blessed one has stated, concerning the correspondence of the world and the <s>puruṣa</s>.
But what is the purpose of this teaching on correspondence?"

children.text: bhagavān uvāca śṛṇvagniveśa sarvalokamātmanyātmānaṃ ca sarvaloke samamanupaśyataḥ satyā buddhiḥ samutpadyate
children.translated_text: The blessed one said: "Listen, <s>Agniveśa</s>. For one who sees the whole world equally in himself and himself in the whole world, true understanding arises.

children.text: sarvalokaṃ hyātmani paśyato bhavatyātmaiva sukhaduḥkhayoḥ kartā nānya iti
children.translated_text: For one who sees the whole world in himself comes to know that the self alone is the maker of pleasure and pain, and no one else."

children.text: karmātmakatvācca hetvādibhiryuktaḥ sarvaloko 'hamiti viditvā jñānaṃ pūrvamutthāpyate 'pavargāyeti
children.translated_text: And because it has the nature of <s>karma</s> (action), the whole world, furnished with causes and the rest, is understood as "I"; therefore knowledge is first brought forth for the sake of <s>apavarga</s> (release).
In this matter, the word "world" depends on conjunction.
For, in general, the whole world is the aggregate of the six constituents.

children.text: tasya hetuḥ utpattiḥ vṛddhiḥ upaplavaḥ viyogaśca
children.translated_text: Its cause consists of origination, growth, disturbance, and separation.

children.text: tatra heturutpattikāraṇaṃ utpattirjanma vṛddhirāpyāyanam upaplavo duḥkhāgamaḥ ṣaḍdhātuvibhāgo viyogaḥ sajīvāpagamaḥ sa prāṇanirodhaḥ sa bhaṅgaḥ sa lokasvabhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: There, cause is the reason for origination; origination is birth; growth is increase; disturbance is the arrival of suffering; the division of the six constituents is separation; the departure of the living principle is the cessation of life-breath, that is dissolution, that is the nature of the world.

children.text: pravṛttirduḥkhaṃ nivṛttiḥ sukhamiti yaj jñānamutpadyate tat satyam
children.translated_text: The knowledge that activity is suffering and cessation is happiness is true.
Its cause is knowledge of what is common to the whole world.
This is the purpose of the general instruction.

children.text: athāgniveśa uvāca kiṃmūlā bhagavan pravṛttiḥ nivṛttau ca ka upāya iti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Agniveśa</s> said: Blessed one, what is the root of activity, and what is the means to cessation?
The Blessed One said: Activity is rooted in delusion, desire, hatred, and action.

children.text: tajjā hyahaṅkārasaṅgasaṃśayābhisaṃplavābhyavapātavipratyayāviśeṣānupāyās taruṇamiva drumamativipulaśākhāstaravo 'bhibhūya puruṣamavatatyaivottiṣṭhante yairabhibhūto na sattāmativartate
children.translated_text: For the egoism, attachment, doubt, over-identification, falling into possessiveness, false conviction, failure to distinguish, and wrong methods born from these rise up, spreading over a person, like trees with excessively broad branches overwhelming a young tree; overcome by them, he does not pass beyond existence.

children.text: tatraivaṃjātirūpavittavṛttabuddhiśīlavidyābhijanavayovīryaprabhāvasaṃpanno 'hamityahaṅkāraḥ yan manovākkāyakarma nāpavargāya sa saṅgaḥ karmaphalamokṣapuruṣapretyabhāvādayaḥ santi vā neti saṃśayaḥ sarvāvasthāsvananyo 'hamahaṃ sraṣṭā svabhāvasaṃsiddho 'hamahaṃ śarīrendriyabuddhismṛtiviśeṣarāśiriti grahaṇamabhisaṃplavaḥ mama mātṛpitṛbhrātṛdārāpatyabandhumitrabhṛtyagaṇo gaṇasya cāham ityabhyavapātaḥ kāryākāryahitāhitaśubhāśubheṣu viparītābhiniveśo vipratyayaḥ jñājñayoḥ prakṛtivikārayoḥ pravṛttinivṛttyośca sāmānyadarśanamaviśeṣaḥ prokṣaṇānaśanāgnihotratriṣavaṇābhyukṣaṇāvāhanayājanayajanayācanasalilahutāśanapraveśādayaḥ samārambhāḥ procyante hyanupāyāḥ
children.translated_text: Here, the thought "I am endowed with such birth, form, wealth, conduct, intelligence, character, learning, family, age, strength, and influence" is egoism. Whatever action of mind, speech, or body does not lead to <s>apavarga</s> is attachment. Doubt is uncertainty as to whether the fruit of action, liberation, the person, existence after death, and the like exist or not. The grasping, "I am the same in all states; I am the creator; I am established by my own nature; I am the aggregate of the body, senses, intellect, memory, and particular qualities," is over-identification. The notion "mother, father, brother, wife, child, kinsman, friend, and servants are mine, and I belong to the group" is falling into possessiveness. Reverse adherence concerning what is to be done and not done, beneficial and harmful, auspicious and inauspicious, is false conviction. Seeing no distinction between the knower and the unknowing, between primal nature and modification, and between activity and cessation is failure to distinguish. Undertakings such as sprinkling, fasting, fire-offering, the three daily ablutions, ritual sprinkling, invocation, causing sacrifice, sacrificing, begging, and entering water or fire are called wrong methods.

children.text: evam ayam adhīdhṛtismṛtirahaṅkārābhiniviṣṭaḥ saktaḥ sasaṃśayo 'bhisaṃplutabuddhir abhyavapatito 'nyathādṛṣṭiraviśeṣagrāhī vimārgagatirnivāsavṛkṣaḥ sattvaśarīradoṣamūlānāṃ sarvaduḥkhānāṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: Thus this person, whose intelligence, firmness, and memory are overcome, who is possessed by egoism, attached, full of doubt, whose understanding is over-identified, fallen into possessiveness, seeing wrongly, grasping without distinctions, and following a wrong path, becomes the dwelling tree of all sufferings rooted in <s>sattva</s> (mind-principle), body, and <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: evamahaṅkārādibhirdoṣairbhrāmyamāṇo nātivartate pravṛttiṃ sā ca mūlamaghasya ||
children.translated_text: Thus, being made to wander by faults such as egoism and the rest, he does not pass beyond activity; and that activity is the root of evil.

children.text: nivṛttirapavargaḥ tat paraṃ praśāntaṃ tattadakṣaraṃ tadbrahma sa mokṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nivṛtti</s> (cessation) is <s>apavarga</s>; that is supreme, peaceful, real, imperishable; that is <s>brahman</s>; that is <s>mokṣa</s>.
Now we shall explain the means of advancement for those who desire liberation.

children.text: tatra lokadoṣadarśino mumukṣorādita evācāryābhigamanaṃ tasyopadeśānuṣṭhānam agnerevopacaryā dharmaśāstrānugamanaṃ tadārthāvabodhaḥ tenāvaṣṭambhaḥ tatra yathoktāḥ kriyāḥ satāmupāsanam asatāṃ parivarjanam asaṃgatirjanena satyaṃ sarvabhūtahitam aparuṣam anatikāle parīkṣya vacanaṃ sarvaprāṇiṣu cātmanīvāvekṣā sarvāsām asmaraṇam asaṃkalpanam aprārthanam anabhibhāṣaṇaṃ ca strīṇāṃ sarvaparigrahatyāgaḥ kaupīnaṃ pracchādanārthaṃ dhāturāganivasanaṃ kanthāsīvanahetoḥ sūcīpippalakaṃ śaucādhānahetorjalakuṇḍikā daṇḍadhāraṇaṃ bhaikṣacaryārthaṃ pātraṃ prāṇadhāraṇārthamekakālamagrāmyo yathopapanno 'bhyavahāraḥ śramāpanayanārthaṃ śīrṇaśuṣkaparṇatṛṇāstaraṇopadhānaṃ dhyānahetoḥ kāyanibandhanaṃ vaneṣvaniketavāsaḥ tandrānidrālasyādikarmavarjanaṃ indriyārtheṣvanurāgopatāpanigrahaḥ suptasthitagataprekṣitāhāravihārapratyaṅgaceṣṭādikeṣvārambheṣu smṛtipūrvikā pravṛttiḥ satkārastutigarhāvamānakṣamatvaṃ kṣutpipāsāyāsaśramaśītoṣṇavātavarṣāsukhaduḥkhasaṃsparśasahatvaṃ śokadainyamānodvegamadalobharāgerṣyābhayakrodhādibhir asaṃcalanam ahaṅkārādiṣūpasargasaṃjñā lokapuruṣayoḥ sargādisāmānyāvekṣaṇaṃ kāryakālātyayabhayaṃ yogārambhe satatamanirvedaḥ sattvotsāhaḥ apavargāya dhīdhṛtismṛtibalādhānaṃ niyamanamindriyāṇāṃ cetasi cetasa ātmani ātmanaśca dhātubhedena śarīrāvayavasaṃkhyānamabhīkṣṇaṃ sarvaṃ kāraṇavadduḥkhamasvamanityamityabhyupagamaḥ sarvapravṛttiṣvaghasaṃjñā sarvasaṃnyāse sukhamityabhiniveśaḥ eṣa mārgo 'pavargāya ato 'nyathā badhyate ityudayanāni vyākhyātāni ||
children.translated_text: For a seeker of liberation who sees the faults of the world, first there is approach to a teacher, practice of his instruction, service of the sacred fire, following the <s>dharmaśāstras</s>, understanding their meaning, support from that, the acts prescribed there, association with the good, avoidance of the bad, non-attachment to people, speech that is true, beneficial to all beings, not harsh, not untimely, and examined beforehand, regarding all living beings as oneself, complete non-recollection, non-conception, non-desire, and non-address of women, abandonment of all possessions, a loincloth for covering, a garment dyed with mineral color, a needle and pin for sewing a patched cloak, a water pot for maintaining purity, carrying a staff, a bowl for the practice of begging, one non-vulgar meal obtained as it happens at a single time for sustaining life, a bed and pillow of fallen dry leaves and grass for removing fatigue, restraint of the body for meditation, dwelling without a fixed house in forests, avoidance of torpor, sleep, laziness, and similar activities, restraint of attachment and distress with respect to the objects of the senses, activity preceded by mindfulness in undertakings such as sleeping, standing, walking, looking, eating, recreation, and the movements of each limb, endurance of honor, praise, blame, and insult, endurance of contact with hunger, thirst, exertion, fatigue, cold, heat, wind, rain, pleasure, and pain, not being shaken by grief, wretchedness, pride, agitation, intoxication, greed, passion, envy, fear, anger, and the like, recognizing egoism and the rest as afflictions, considering the common features of creation and the rest in the world and the person, fear of delay at the proper time for action, constant freedom from despondency at the beginning of yoga, energy of <s>sattva</s>, strengthening of intellect, firmness, and memory for <s>apavarga</s>, restraining the senses in the mind, the mind in the self, and the self, by distinguishing the constituents, frequent enumeration of the bodily parts, accepting that everything has a cause, is suffering, is not one's own, and is impermanent, regarding all activity as evil, and firm conviction that happiness lies in complete renunciation. This is the path to <s>apavarga</s>; otherwise one is bound. Thus the means of advancement have been explained.
And here there are verses:
By these means of purification, impure <s>sattva</s> is purified,
like a mirror being wiped with oil, cloth, hair, and the like.
As the disk of the sun shines when it is not covered by planets, clouds, dust, smoke, or mist,
so too stainless <s>sattva</s> shines.
that <s>sattva</s>, restrained within itself when its channels are closed off, blazes
like a pure, steady lamp with a clear flame in the lamp-vessel.
By it one splits apart the very powerful darkness made of great delusion.
By it one becomes free from craving, knowing the own nature of all things.

children.text: yogaṃ yayā sādhayate sāṃkhyaḥ sampadyate yayā ||
children.translated_text: By it the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> practitioner accomplishes <s>yoga</s>; by it he attains perfection.
By it one does not come to egoism; by it one does not worship a cause.

children.text: yayā nālambate kiṃcit sarvaṃ saṃnyasyate yayā ||
children.translated_text: By it one depends on nothing at all; by it everything is renounced.

children.text: yāti brahma yayā nityamajaraṃ śāntam avyayam
children.translated_text: By it one always goes to <s>brahman</s>, ageless, peaceful, and imperishable.

children.text: vidyā siddhirmatirmedhā prajñā jñānaṃ ca sā matā ||
children.translated_text: That is considered <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), accomplishment, intelligence, insight, wisdom, and knowledge.
For one who sees the self spread throughout the world, and the world within the self,
who sees what is higher and lower, the peace rooted in knowledge does not perish.
For one who sees all beings, in all states, at all times,
and who has become <s>brahman</s>, conjunction does not befit one who is pure.
Because there are no instruments belonging to the self, even its mark is not perceived.
Because of its disjunction from all instruments, it is called liberated.
Sinless, stainless, peaceful, supreme, imperishable, and undecaying,
immortal, <s>brahman</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s>: by these synonyms it is called peace.
This, gentle one, is that understanding; having known it, and freed from doubt,
the sages, with delusion, passion, and craving gone, reached tranquility.
On this there are two verses:
With its purpose, the commonality of the world and of the <s>puruṣa</s>

children.text: sāmānyaṃ mūlamutpattau nivṛttau mārga eva ca ||
children.translated_text: has been explained with respect to origination, to cessation, and precisely to the path.
The settling of purified <s>sattva</s>, true understanding, and final intelligence
have been stated by the supreme seer in the analysis of the <s>puruṣa</s>, as has the final state.
Now then we shall explain the bodily section called the analysis of the body.
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.
Analysis of the body is desired for the sake of benefiting the body.

children.text: jñātvā hi śarīratattvaṃ śarīropakārakareṣu bhāveṣu jñānamutpadyate
children.translated_text: For, when the truth of the body is known, knowledge arises concerning the factors that bring benefit to the body.
Therefore skilled physicians praise analysis of the body.

children.text: tatra śarīraṃ nāma cetanādhiṣṭhānabhūtaṃ pañcamahābhūtavikārasamudāyātmakaṃ samayogavāhi
children.translated_text: There, the body is what is called the seat of consciousness, an aggregate made up of modifications of the five great elements, and the bearer of balanced conjunction.

children.text: yadā hyasmiñśarīre dhātavo vaiṣamyamāpadyante tadā kleśaṃ vināśaṃ vā prāpnoti
children.translated_text: For when the <s>dhātus</s> in this body fall into imbalance, it reaches distress or destruction.

children.text: vaiṣamyagamanaṃ hi punardhātūnāṃ vṛddhihrāsagamanam akārtsnyena prakṛtyā ca ||
children.translated_text: The movement of the <s>dhātus</s> into imbalance is, again, their movement into increase or decrease, either partially or by their nature.

children.text: yaugapadyena tu virodhināṃ dhātūnāṃ vṛddhihrāsau bhavataḥ
children.translated_text: But increase and decrease occur simultaneously among mutually opposed <s>dhātus</s>.

children.text: yaddhi yasya dhātorvṛddhikaraṃ tattato viparītaguṇasya dhātoḥ pratyavāyakaraṃ sampadyate ||
children.translated_text: For whatever causes increase of a given <s>dhātu</s> becomes, for that reason, injurious to the <s>dhātu</s> whose qualities are opposite.

children.text: tadeva tasmādbheṣajaṃ samyagavacāryamāṇaṃ yugapan nyūnātiriktānāṃ dhātūnāṃ sāmyakaraṃ bhavati adhikam apakarṣati nyūnamāpyāyayati ||
children.translated_text: That same remedy, when properly considered, simultaneously brings into balance <s>dhātus</s> that are deficient and excessive: it draws down the excessive and nourishes the deficient.

children.text: etāvadeva hi bhaiṣajyaprayoge phalamiṣṭaṃ svasthavṛttānuṣṭhāne ca yāvaddhātūnāṃ sāmyaṃ syāt
children.translated_text: For this much alone is desired as the result in the use of medicine and in the practice of the regimen for the healthy: that there should be equilibrium of the <s>dhātus</s>.

children.text: svasthā hyapi dhātūnāṃ sāmyānugrahārthameva kuśalā rasaguṇānāhāravikārāṃśca paryāyeṇecchantyupayoktuṃ sātmyasamājñātān ekaprakārabhūyiṣṭhāṃś copayuñjānās tadviparītakarasamājñātayā ceṣṭayā samamicchanti kartum ||
children.translated_text: For even those who are healthy wish to use tastes and qualities, and transformations of food, only for supporting the equilibrium of the <s>dhātus</s>, in alternation, as known to be wholesome; and when they use items mostly of a single type, they wish to make them balanced by activity known to produce the opposite taste and effect.

children.text: deśakālātmaguṇaviparītānāṃ hi karmaṇām āhāravikārāṇāṃ ca kriyopayogaḥ samyak sarvātiyogasaṃdhāraṇam asaṃdhāraṇam udīrṇānāṃ ca gatimatāṃ sāhasānāṃ ca varjanaṃ svasthavṛttametāvaddhātūnāṃ sāmyānugrahārthamupadiśyate ||
children.translated_text: The proper performance and use of actions and transformations of food that are opposite to place, time, and one's own qualities; restraint from every excess, non-restraint of urges that have arisen and are moving, and avoidance of rash actions: this much is taught as the regimen for the healthy, for the purpose of supporting the equilibrium of the <s>dhātus</s>.

children.text: dhātavaḥ punaḥ śārīrāḥ samānaguṇaiḥ samānaguṇabhūyiṣṭhair vāpyāhāravikārair abhyasyamānair vṛddhiṃ prāpnuvanti hrāsaṃ tu viparītaguṇair viparītaguṇabhūyiṣṭhair vāpyāhārairabhyasyamānaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, bodily <s>dhātus</s> increase through transformations of food that are practiced habitually and have similar qualities, or mostly similar qualities; but they decrease through foods of opposite qualities, or mostly opposite qualities, when practiced habitually.

In this matter, these qualities of the bodily <s>dhātus</s> are what determine number and capacity, namely: heavy, light, cold, hot, unctuous, dry, dull, sharp, stable, mobile, soft, hard, clear, slimy, smooth, rough, subtle, gross, dense, and fluid.

children.text: teṣu ye guravaste gurubhirāhāravikāraguṇair abhyasyamānair āpyāyyante laghavaśca hrasanti laghavastu laghubhir āpyāyyante guravaśca hrasanti
children.translated_text: Among these, those that are heavy are nourished by habitual use of heavy qualities in transformations of food, while the light ones decrease; but the light ones are nourished by light qualities, while the heavy ones decrease.
In just this way, for all qualities of the <s>dhātus</s>, increase comes from conjunction with what is similar, and decrease from the opposite.

children.text: tasmānmāṃsamāpyāyyate māṃsena bhūyastaram anyebhyaḥ śarīradhātubhyaḥ tathā lohitaṃ lohitena medo medasā vasā vasayā asthi taruṇāsthnā majjā majjñā śukraṃ śukreṇa garbhastvāmagarbheṇa ||
children.translated_text: Therefore flesh is nourished by flesh more than by the other bodily <s>dhātus</s>; likewise blood by blood, fat by fat, muscle-fat by muscle-fat, bone by young bone, marrow by marrow, semen by semen, and the embryo by an unripe embryo.

children.text: yatra tvevaṃlakṣaṇena sāmānyena sāmānyavatām āhāravikārāṇām asānnidhyaṃ syāt saṃnihitānāṃ vāpy ayuktatvān nopayogo ghṛṇitvād anyasmādvā kāraṇāt sa ca dhāturabhivardhayitavyaḥ syāt tasya ye samānaguṇāḥ syurāhāravikārā asevyāśca tatra samānaguṇabhūyiṣṭhānām anyaprakṛtīnām apyāhāravikārāṇām upayogaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: But where there is no availability of foods and transformations of food having similar properties through such commonality, or where available ones are not used because they are unsuitable, disgusting, or for some other reason, and that <s>dhātu</s> must be increased, then foods and transformations of food that have similar qualities, even though of another nature, and are mostly endowed with similar qualities, should be used there.

children.text: tadyathā śukrakṣaye kṣīrasarpiṣorupayogo madhurasnigdhaśītasamākhyātānāṃ cāpareṣāṃ dravyāṇāṃ mūtrakṣaye punar ikṣurasavāruṇīmaṇḍadravamadhurāmlalavaṇopakledināṃ purīṣakṣaye kulmāṣamāṣakuṣkuṇḍājamadhyayavaśākadhānyāmlānāṃ vātakṣaye kaṭukatiktakaṣāyarūkṣalaghuśītānāṃ pittakṣaye'mlalavaṇakaṭukakṣāroṣṇatīkṣṇānāṃ śleṣmakṣaye snigdhagurumadhurasāndrapicchilānāṃ dravyāṇām
children.translated_text: For example: when <s>śukra</s> is deficient, there is the use of milk and ghee, and of other substances described as sweet, unctuous, and cold; when urine is deficient, there is the use of sugarcane juice, <s>vāruṇī</s>, gruel-liquid, fluids, and substances that are sweet, sour, salty, and moistening; when feces are deficient, there is the use of <s>kulmāṣa</s>, black gram, <s>kuṣkuṇḍa</s>, goat products, barley, greens, and sour grain preparations; when <s>vāta</s> is deficient, there is the use of substances that are pungent, bitter, astringent, dry, light, and cold; when <s>pitta</s> is deficient, of substances that are sour, salty, pungent, alkaline, hot, and sharp; and when <s>śleṣman</s> is deficient, of substances that are unctuous, heavy, sweet, dense, and slimy.
And whatever action increases a given <s>dhātu</s> should be practiced for that one.

children.text: evamanyeṣām api śarīradhātūnāṃ sāmānyaviparyayābhyāṃ vṛddhihrāsau yathākālaṃ kāryau
children.translated_text: In this way, for the other bodily <s>dhātus</s> too, increase and decrease should be brought about at the proper time by similarity and by opposition.
Thus the agents that cause increase and decrease of all the <s>dhātus</s>, both individually and by extension, have been explained.

children.text: kārtsnyena śarīravṛddhikarāstvime bhāvā bhavanti tadyathā kālayogaḥ svabhāvasaṃsiddhiḥ āhārasauṣṭhavam avighātaśceti ||
children.translated_text: Now the factors that increase the body as a whole are these: suitable timing, natural accomplishment, excellence of food, and absence of obstruction.
The factors that increase strength are these:

children.text: tadyathā balavatpuruṣe deśe janma balavatpuruṣe kāle ca sukhaśca kālayogaḥ bījakṣetraguṇasaṃpac ca āhārasaṃpac ca śarīrasaṃpac ca sātmyasaṃpac ca sattvasaṃpac ca svabhāvasaṃsiddhiśca yauvanaṃ ca karma ca saṃharṣaśceti ||
children.translated_text: namely, birth in a region where people are strong, and at a time when people are strong; a favorable conjunction of time; excellence of seed and field; excellence of food; excellence of the body; excellence of habituation; excellence of <s>sattva</s>; natural accomplishment; youth; action; and exhilaration.
The factors that bring about the transformation of food are these:

children.text: tadyathoṣmā vāyuḥ kledaḥ snehaḥ kālaḥ samayogaśceti ||
children.translated_text: namely, heat, wind, moisture, unctuousness, time, and proper combination.

children.text: tatra tu khalveṣāmūtrādīnām āhārapariṇāmakarāṇāṃ bhāvānāmime karmaviśeṣā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Among these, the particular actions of heat and the rest, the factors that bring about the transformation of food, are as follows:

children.text: tadyathā ūṣmā pacati vāyurapakarṣati kledaḥ śaithilyamāpādayati sneho mārdavaṃ janayati kālaḥ paryāptim abhinirvartayati samayogastveṣāṃ pariṇāmadhātusāmyakaraḥ sampadyate ||
children.translated_text: heat cooks; wind draws away; moisture produces looseness; unctuousness generates softness; time brings completion to fullness; and the proper combination of these becomes the cause of transformation and equilibrium of the <s>dhātus</s>.

children.text: pariṇamatastvāhārasya guṇāḥ śarīraguṇabhāvam āpadyante yathāsvamaviruddhāḥ viruddhāśca vihanyurvihatāśca virodhibhiḥ śarīram ||
children.translated_text: As food is being transformed, its qualities, so far as they are not incompatible, become qualities of the body according to their own nature; incompatible ones harm the body, and those that are checked by opposing factors do harm as well.
The qualities of the body, again, are twofold in summary: those that are waste products and those that are clear, beneficial products.
Among them, the waste products are those that cause trouble for the body.

children.text: tadyathā śarīracchidreṣūpadehāḥ pṛthagjanmāno bahirmukhāḥ paripakvāśca dhātavaḥ prakupitāśca vātapittaśleṣmāṇaḥ ye cānye'pi keciccharīre tiṣṭhanto bhāvāḥ śarīrasyopaghātāyopapadyante sarvāṃstān male saṃcakṣmahe itarāṃstu prasāde gurvādīṃśca dravāntān guṇabhedena rasādīṃśca śukrāntān dravyabhedena ||
children.translated_text: For example, deposits in the body's openings, bodily constituents separately produced, turned outward, and fully matured, and also aggravated <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s>, and whatever other conditions remain in the body and come to injure it: all these we call waste. The others we call clear beneficial products: the qualities from heaviness through fluidity, according to distinction of quality, and the substances from <s>rasa</s> through <s>śukra</s>, according to distinction of substance.

children.text: teṣāṃ sarveṣāmeva vātapittaśleṣmāṇo duṣṭā dūṣayitāro bhavanti doṣasvabhāvāt
children.translated_text: Of all of these, <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s>, when deranged, become corruptors, because that is the nature of <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: vātādīnāṃ punardhātvantare kālāntare praduṣṭānāṃ vividhāśitapītīye'dhyāye vijñānānyuktāni
children.translated_text: The indications of <s>vāta</s> and the others when they are vitiated in another <s>dhātu</s> and at another time have been stated in the chapter on various foods and drinks.
The course of the deranged <s>doṣas</s> extends only so far as their contact with the bodily <s>dhātus</s>.
But the fruit of <s>vāta</s> and the others when they are in their natural state is health.
Therefore intelligent people should strive to keep them in their natural condition.

children.text: śarīraṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ sarvadā veda yo bhiṣak
children.translated_text: The physician who always knows the whole body completely in every way
knows <s>āyurveda</s> in its entirety, which bestows happiness on the world.

children.text: evaṃvādinaṃ bhagavantamātreyamagniveśa uvāca śrutametadyaduktaṃ bhagavatā śarīrādhikāre vacaḥ
children.translated_text: When the blessed <s>Ātreya</s> had spoken in this way, <s>Agniveśa</s> said: "I have heard this statement concerning the body, as spoken by the blessed one.

children.text: kiṃnu khalu garbhasyāṅgaṃ pūrvamabhinirvartate kukṣau kathaṃ cāntargatastiṣṭhati kimāhāraśca vartayati kathaṃbhūtaśca niṣkrāmati kaiścāyamāhāropacārair jātaḥ sadyo hanyate kair avyādhirabhivardhate kiṃ cāsya devādiprakopanimittā vikārāḥ sambhavanti āhosvinna kiṃ cāsya kālākālamṛtyvor bhāvābhāvayor bhagavān adhyavasyati kiṃ cāsya paramāyuḥ kāni cāsya paramāyuṣo nimittānīti ||
children.translated_text: But which part of the embryo is formed first in the womb? How does it remain while inside? By what food is it sustained? In what condition does it come forth? By what regimens of food and care is it killed immediately after birth, and by which does it grow without disease? Do disorders caused by the provocation of gods and the like arise in it, or not? What does the blessed one determine about the existence or nonexistence of death in due time and untimely death? What is its maximum lifespan, and what are the causes of that maximum lifespan?"

children.text: tamevamuktavantamagniveśaṃ bhagavān punarvasurātreya uvāca pūrvam uktam etadgarbhāvakrāntau yathāyamabhinivartate kukṣau yāsya yadā saṃtiṣṭhate'ṅgajātam
children.translated_text: To <s>Agniveśa</s>, who had spoken thus, the blessed <s>Punarvasu Ātreya</s> replied: "This has been stated before, in the discussion of the descent of the embryo: how it comes into being in the womb, and when its full set of limbs becomes established.

children.text: viprativādāstvatra bahuvidhāḥ sūtrakṛtāmṛṣīṇāṃ santi sarveṣāṃ tānapi nibodhocyamānān śiraḥpūrvam abhinirvartate kukṣāviti kumāraśirā bharadvājaḥ paśyati sarvendriyāṇāṃ tadadhiṣṭhānamiti kṛtvā hṛdayamiti kāṅkāyano bāhlīkabhiṣak cetanādhiṣṭhānatvāt nābhiriti bhadrakāpyaḥ āhārāgama itikṛtvā pakvāśayagudam iti bhadraśaunakaḥ mārutādhiṣṭhānatvāt hastapādamiti baḍiśaḥ tatkaraṇatvātpuruṣasya indriyāṇīti janako vaidehaḥ tānyasya buddhyadhiṣṭhānānīti kṛtvā parokṣatvād acintyamiti mārīciḥ kaśyapaḥ sarvāṅgābhinirvṛttiryugapad iti dhanvantariḥ tadupapannaṃ sarvāṅgānāṃ tulyakālābhinirvṛttatvāddhṛdayaprabhṛtīnām
children.translated_text: But on this matter there are many disagreements among the sages who composed the treatises. Listen also to all of those as they are being stated. <s>Kumāraśiras Bhāradvāja</s> holds that the head is formed first in the womb, because it is the seat of all the senses. <s>Kāṅkāyana</s>, the physician from <s>Bāhlīka</s>, says the heart, because it is the seat of consciousness. <s>Bhadrakāpya</s> says the navel, because food arrives there. <s>Bhadraśaunaka</s> says the colon and anus, because they are the seat of wind. <s>Baḍiśa</s> says the hands and feet, because they are the person's instruments. <s>Janaka Vaideha</s> says the sense faculties, because they are the seats of its intelligence. <s>Mārīci Kaśyapa</s> says it is inconceivable because it is beyond perception. <s>Dhanvantari</s> says that all the limbs are formed simultaneously. That is reasonable, because all the limbs, beginning with the heart, are formed at the same time."

children.text: sarvāṅgānāṃ hyasya hṛdayaṃ mūlam adhiṣṭhānaṃ ca keṣāṃcid bhāvānām na ca tasmāt pūrvābhinirvṛttireṣāṃ tasmāddhṛdayaprabhṛtīnāṃ sarvāṅgānāṃ tulyakālābhinirvṛttiḥ sarve bhāvā hyanyonyapratibaddhāḥ tasmād yathābhūtadarśanaṃ sādhu ||
children.translated_text: For its heart is the root of all the limbs and the seat of certain states; these do not come into being before it. Therefore the heart and the other limbs all arise at the same time. For all states are mutually connected with one another; therefore seeing things as they really are is proper.

children.text: garbhastu khalu mātuḥ pṛṣṭhābhimukha ūrdhvaśirāḥ saṃkucyāṅgānyāste 'ntaḥkukṣau ||
children.translated_text: But the embryo, facing the mother's back, with its head upward and its limbs contracted, remains inside the womb.

children.text: vyapagatapipāsābubhukṣastu khalu garbhaḥ paratantravṛttir mātaramāśritya vartayatyupasnehopasvedābhyāṃ garbhāśaye sadasadbhūtāṅgāvayavaḥ tadanantaraṃ hyasya kaścil lomakūpāyanair upasnehaḥ kaścin nābhināḍyayanaiḥ
children.translated_text: The embryo, free from thirst and hunger, lives dependently, relying on the mother, in the uterus by moistening and warming, with the parts of its limbs partly manifest and partly not yet manifest. Immediately thereafter some nourishment reaches it through channels in the hair-pores, and some through the channels of the umbilical cord.

children.text: nābhyāṃ hyasya nāḍī prasaktā nāḍyāṃ cāparā aparā cāsya mātuḥ prasaktā hṛdaye mātṛhṛdayaṃ hyasya tām aparām abhisaṃplavate sirābhiḥ syandamānābhiḥ sa tasya raso balavarṇakaraḥ sampadyate sa ca sarvarasavān āhāraḥ
children.translated_text: For a cord is attached to its navel, and the placenta is attached to the cord; and its placenta is attached to the mother's heart. The mother's heart floods that placenta through flowing vessels. That <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid) becomes productive of its strength and complexion, and that food contains all tastes.

children.text: striyā hyāpannagarbhāyāstridhā rasaḥ pratipadyate svaśarīrapuṣṭaye stanyāya garbhavṛddhaye ca
children.translated_text: For in a pregnant woman the <s>rasa</s> goes in three directions: for the nourishment of her own body, for breast milk, and for the growth of the embryo.
Supported by that food, living dependently and contained within, it remains relying on the mother.

children.text: sa copasthitakāle janmani prasūtimārutayogāt parivṛttyāvākśirā niṣkrāmatyapatyapathena eṣā prakṛtiḥ vikṛtiḥ punarato'nyathā
children.translated_text: And when the time of birth has arrived, through the action of the birth-wind, it turns with its head downward and comes out by the path for offspring. This is the normal condition; what is otherwise than this is abnormal.
After this, however, it lives independently.
Its diet and regimen, taught in the section on birth-rules, are non-disordering and growth-promoting.

children.text: tābhyāmeva ca viṣamasevitābhyāṃ jātaḥ sadya upahanyate tarurivāciravyaparopito vātātapābhyām apratiṣṭhitamūlaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when those very two are used improperly, the newborn is harmed at once, like a tree newly transplanted, with its roots not yet established, by wind and heat.

children.text: āptopadeśād adbhutarūpadarśanāt samutthānaliṅgacikitsitaviśeṣāc cādoṣaprakopānurūpā devādiprakopanimittā vikārāḥ samupalabhyante ||
children.translated_text: From trustworthy instruction, from the sight of extraordinary forms, and from specific differences in origin, signs, and treatment, disorders are observed that do not correspond to aggravation of the <s>doṣas</s> and are caused by the provocation of deities and the like.

children.text: kālākālamṛtyvostu khalu bhāvābhāvayor idam adhyavasitaṃ naḥ yaḥ kaścin mriyate sa kāla eva mriyate na hi kālacchidramastītyeke bhāṣante
children.translated_text: As for the existence and nonexistence of death in due time and out of due time, this is our settled view. Some say: Whoever dies, dies only at the proper time, for there is no gap in time.
But that is not correct.

children.text: na hyachidratā sachidratā vā kālasyopapadyate kālasvalakṣaṇasvabhāvāt
children.translated_text: For it is not possible that time should either have no gaps or have gaps, since time has its own defining nature.

children.text: tatrāhurapare yo yadā mriyate sa tasya niyato mṛtyukālaḥ sa sarvabhūtānāṃ satyaḥ samakriyatvāditi
children.translated_text: On this point others say: Whenever a person dies, that is his fixed time of death; this is true for all beings, because it applies equally to all.
This too is a misunderstanding of the matter.

children.text: na hi kaścin na mriyata iti samakriyaḥ
children.translated_text: For the fact that no one does not die is not what makes the case the same.
Time is spoken of with reference to the measure of lifespan.

children.text: yasya ceṣṭaṃ yo yadā mriyate sa tasya mṛtyukāla iti tasya sarve bhāvā yathāsvaṃ niyatakālā bhaviṣyanti tacca nopapadyate pratyakṣaṃ hyakālāhāravacanakarmaṇāṃ phalamaniṣṭaṃ viparyaye ceṣṭaṃ pratyakṣataścopalabhyate khalu kālākālavyaktistāsu tāsvavasthāsu taṃ tamartham abhisamīkṣya tadyathā kālo'yamasya vyādherāhārasyauṣadhasya pratikarmaṇo visargasya akālo veti
children.translated_text: And if one's intended meaning is that whenever someone dies, that is his time of death, then all states will have their own fixed times; and that is not tenable. For the unwanted result of improper time in food, speech, and action is directly observed, and the desired result in the opposite case. The distinction between proper and improper time is also directly observed in each particular condition with regard to each particular purpose, as when one says, 'This is the proper time for this disease, this food, this medicine, this countermeasure, this purgation,' or 'this is not the proper time.'

children.text: loke 'pyetadbhavati kāle devo varṣatyakāle devo varṣati kāle śītamakāle śītaṃ kāle tapatyakāle tapati kāle puṣpaphalamakāle ca puṣpaphalamiti
children.translated_text: This also occurs in ordinary life: the god rains in season, and the god rains out of season; there is cold in season and cold out of season; there is heat in season and heat out of season; flowers and fruits appear in season, and flowers and fruits appear out of season.
Therefore both exist: death in due time and death out of due time. There is no absolute rule here.

children.text: yadi hyakāle mṛtyurna syānniyatakālapramāṇam āyuḥ sarvaṃ syāt evaṃgate hitāhitajñānamakāraṇaṃ syāt pratyakṣānumānopadeśāścāpramāṇāni syurye pramāṇabhūtāḥ sarvatantreṣu yairāyuṣyāṇyanāyuṣyāṇi copalabhyante
children.translated_text: For if there were no death out of due time, every lifespan would have a fixed measure of time. In that case knowledge of what is beneficial and harmful would be causeless, and perception, inference, and authoritative teaching, which are accepted as valid means in all systems and by which life-promoting and life-diminishing factors are known, would not be means of knowledge.

children.text: vāgvastumātram etadvādam ṛṣayo manyante nākāle mṛtyurastīti ||
children.translated_text: The seers consider this doctrine, that there is no death out of due time, to be mere verbal assertion.
In this age, the measure of lifespan is one hundred years.
Its causes are excellence of constitution, qualities, and self, and the practice of what is wholesome.
On this there are verses:
The body, just as it is, and how it functions when afflicted by diseases,

children.text: yathā kleśaṃ vināśaṃ ca yāti ye cāsya dhātavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how it comes to suffering and destruction, and what its <s>dhātus</s> are,

children.text: vṛddhihrāsau yathā teṣāṃ kṣīṇānām auṣadhaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: how their increase and decrease occur, and what medicine is for them when depleted,
what factors increase the body and what factors increase strength,

children.text: pariṇāmakarā bhāvā yā ca teṣāṃ pṛthak kriyā
children.translated_text: what factors produce transformation, and what the separate action of these factors is,

children.text: malākhyāḥ samprasādākhyā dhātavaḥ praśna eva ca ||
children.translated_text: the <s>dhātus</s> called wastes and those called clear essences, and also the question itself,
and its ninefold determination have been duly explained
truthfully in the bodily section on the analysis of the body by the supreme seer.
Now then we shall explain the bodily section called the enumeration of the body.
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: śarīrasaṃkhyāmavayavaśaḥ kṛtsnaṃ śarīraṃ pravibhajya sarvaśarīrasaṃkhyānapramāṇajñānahetor bhagavantam ātreyam agniveśaḥ papraccha ||
children.translated_text: Having divided the whole body according to its parts, <s>Agniveśa</s> asked the blessed <s>Ātreya</s> about the enumeration of the body, for the sake of knowing the number and measure of the whole body.

children.text: tamuvāca bhagavānātreyaḥ śṛṇu matto'gniveśa sarvaśarīram ācakṣāṇasya yathāpraśnamekamanā yathāvat
children.translated_text: The blessed <s>Ātreya</s> said to him: Listen to me, <s>Agniveśa</s>, with one-pointed mind, as I describe the whole body properly, according to the question.

children.text: śarīre ṣaṭ tvacaḥ tadyathā udakadharā tvagbāhyā dvitīyā tvasṛgdharā tṛtīyā sidhmakilāsasaṃbhavādhiṣṭhānā caturthī dadrūkuṣṭhasaṃbhavādhiṣṭhānā pañcamī tvalajīvidradhisaṃbhavādhiṣṭhānā ṣaṣṭhī tu yasyāṃ chinnāyāṃ tāmyatyandha iva ca tamaḥ praviśati yāṃ cāpyadhiṣṭhāyārūṃṣi jāyante parvasu kṛṣṇaraktāni sthūlamūlāni duścikitsyatamāni ca iti ṣaṭ tvacaḥ
children.translated_text: There are six layers of skin in the body, namely: the outer skin, which holds water; the second, which holds blood; the third, which is the seat where <s>sidhmā</s> and <s>kilāsa</s> arise; the fourth, which is the seat where <s>dadrū</s> and <s>kuṣṭha</s> arise; the fifth, which is the seat where <s>alajī</s> and <s>vidradhi</s> arise; and the sixth, when cut, makes one faint and enter darkness as if blind, and on which, when it is affected, wounds arise in the joints, black and red, with thick roots, and most difficult to treat. Thus there are six layers of skin.
These six extend over and cover the six-limbed body.

children.text: tatrāyaṃ śarīrasyāṅgavibhāgaḥ tadyathā dvau bāhū dve sakthinī śirogrīvam antarādhiḥ iti ṣaḍaṅgamaṅgam ||
children.translated_text: Here is the division of the body's limbs: namely, the two arms, the two legs, the head and neck, and the middle trunk. Thus the limb is six-limbed.
There are three hundred and sixty bones, together with the tooth-sockets and nails.

children.text: tadyathā dvātriṃśaddantāḥ dvātriṃśaddantolūkhalāni viṃśatirnakhāḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ pāṇipādāṅgulyasthīni viṃśatiḥ pāṇipādaśalākāḥ catvāri pāṇipādaśalākādhiṣṭhānāni dve pārṣṇyorasthinī catvāraḥ pādayor gulphāḥ dvau maṇikau hastayoḥ catvāryaratnyorasthīni catvāri jaṅghayoḥ dve jānunī dve jānukapālike dvāvūrunalakau dvau bāhunalakau dvāvaṃsau dve aṃsaphalake dvāvakṣakau ekaṃ jatru dve tāluke dve śroṇiphalake ekaṃ bhagāsthi pañcacatvāriṃśat pṛṣṭhagatānyasthīni pañcadaśa grīvāyāṃ caturdaśorasi dvayoḥ pārśvayoścaturviṃśatiḥ parśukāḥ tāvanti sthālakāni tāvanti caiva sthālakārbudāni ekaṃ hanvasthi dve hanumūlabandhane ekāsthi nāsikāgaṇḍakūṭalalāṭaṃ dvau śaṅkhau catvāri śiraḥkapālānīti evaṃ trīṇi saṣaṣṭīni śatāny asthnāṃ saha dantolūkhalanakheneti ||
children.translated_text: They are as follows: thirty-two teeth, thirty-two tooth-sockets, twenty nails, sixty bones of the fingers and toes, twenty long bones of the hands and feet, four bases of those hand and foot bones, two heel bones, four ankles in the feet, two wrist bones in the hands, four forearm bones, four bones in the shanks, two knees, two kneecaps, two thigh shafts, two arm shafts, two shoulders, two shoulder blades, two collarbones, one breast-bone, two palatal bones, two pelvic plates, one pubic bone, forty-five bones situated in the back, fifteen in the neck, fourteen in the chest, twenty-four ribs on the two sides, as many supporting plates, and as many raised knobs of the supporting plates, one jaw bone, two bindings at the roots of the jaws, one bone comprising the nose, cheeks, prominences, and forehead, two temples, and four skull bones. Thus there are three hundred and sixty bones, together with the tooth-sockets and nails.

children.text: pañcendriyādhiṣṭhānāni tadyathā tvag jihvā nāsikā akṣiṇī karṇau ca
children.translated_text: There are five seats of the sense organs, namely skin, tongue, nose, the two eyes, and the two ears.

children.text: pañca buddhīndriyāṇi tadyathā sparśanaṃ rasanaṃ ghrāṇaṃ darśanaṃ śrotramiti
children.translated_text: There are five cognitive sense faculties, namely touch, taste, smell, sight, and hearing.

children.text: pañca karmendriyāṇi tadyathā hastau pādau pāyuḥ upasthaḥ jihvā ceti ||
children.translated_text: There are five organs of action, namely the two hands, the two feet, the anus, the generative organ, and the tongue.
The heart is the single seat of consciousness.

children.text: daśa prāṇāyatanāni tadyathā mūrdhā kaṇṭhaḥ hṛdayaṃ nābhiḥ gudaṃ vastiḥ ojaḥ śukraṃ śoṇitaṃ māṃsamiti
children.translated_text: There are ten abodes of <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath), namely the head, throat, heart, navel, anus, bladder, <s>ojaḥ</s> (vital essence), <s>śukra</s> (semen), blood, and flesh.
Among these, the first six are counted as <s>marman</s> (vital spots).

children.text: pañcadaśa koṣṭhāṅgāni tadyathā nābhiśca hṛdayaṃ ca kloma ca yakṛcca plīhā ca vṛkkau ca vastiśca purīṣādhāraśca āmāśayaśca pakvāśayaśca uttaragudaṃ ca adharagudaṃ ca kṣudrāntraṃ ca sthūlāntraṃ ca vapāvahanaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: There are fifteen organs of the <s>koṣṭha</s> (visceral cavity), namely the navel, the heart, the <s>kloma</s>, the liver, the spleen, the two kidneys, the bladder, the receptacle of feces, the stomach, the cooked-food bowel, the upper rectum, the lower rectum, the small intestine, the large intestine, and the <s>vapāvahana</s>.

children.text: ṣaṭpañcāśat pratyaṅgāni ṣaṭsvaṅgeṣūpanibaddhāni yānyaparisaṃkhyātāni pūrvamaṅgeṣu parisaṃkhyāyamāneṣu tānyanyaiḥ paryāyairiha prakāśyāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: There are fifty-six subsidiary parts attached to the six limbs. Since they were not enumerated earlier when the limbs were being counted, they are to be set out here by other terms.

children.text: tadyathā dve jaṅghāpiṇḍike dve ūrupiṇḍike dvau sphicau dvau vṛṣaṇau ekaṃ śephaḥ dve ukhe dvau vaṅghaṇau dvau kukundarau ekaṃ vastiśīrṣam ekamudaraṃ dvau stanau dvau śleṣmabhuvau dve bāhupiṇḍike cibukamekaṃ dvāvoṣṭhau dve sṛkkaṇyau dvau dantaveṣṭakau ekaṃ tālu ekā galaśuṇḍikā dve upajihvike ekā gojihvikā dvau gaṇḍau dve karṇaśaṣkulike dvau karṇaputrakau dve akṣikūṭe catvāryakṣivartmāni dve akṣikanīnike dve bhruvau ekāvaṭuḥ catvāri pāṇipādahṛdayāni ||
children.translated_text: They are as follows: two calf masses, two thigh masses, two buttocks, two testicles, one penis, two <s>ukhā</s>, two groins, two haunches, one head of the bladder, one abdomen, two breasts, two seats of phlegm, two upper-arm masses, one chin, two lips, two corners of the mouth, two gums, one palate, one uvula, two sublingual parts, one <s>gojihvikā</s>, two cheeks, two outer ears, two ear openings, two eye sockets, four eyelids, two pupils, two eyebrows, one forehead, and the four centers of the hands and feet.

children.text: nava mahānti chidrāṇi sapta śirasi dve cādhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There are nine great openings: seven in the head and two below.
Only this much, being visible, can be specified.
What lies beyond this cannot be specified; it is only to be inferred.

children.text: tadyathā nava snāyuśatāni sapta sirāśatāni dve dhamanīśate catvāri peśīśatāni saptottaraṃ marmaśataṃ dve sandhiśate ekonatriṃśatsahasrāṇi nava ca śatāni ṣaṭpañcāśatkāni sirādhamanīnām aṇuśaḥ pravibhajyamānānāṃ mukhāgraparimāṇaṃ tāvanti caiva keśaśmaśrulomānīti
children.translated_text: For example: nine hundred sinews, seven hundred veins, two hundred arteries, four hundred muscles, one hundred and seven <s>marman</s> (vital spots), two hundred joints, and twenty-nine thousand nine hundred and fifty-six minute openings at the tips of the veins and arteries when they are subdivided finely; and there are just as many hairs of the head, beard hairs, and body hairs.
This, from the skin onward, has been counted as it really is: what is visible, and beyond that what is inferable.
Neither of these two admits variation, because this is the natural state of the body.

children.text: yattvañjalisaṃkhyeyaṃ tadupadekṣyāmaḥ tat paraṃ pramāṇam abhijñeyaṃ tacca vṛddhihrāsayogi tarkyameva
children.translated_text: But what is countable by <s>añjali</s> (handful measure), that we shall teach. That should be understood as the further measure, and since it is subject to increase and decrease, it too is only inferable.

children.text: tadyathā daśodakasyāñjalayaḥ śarīre svenāñjalipramāṇena yattu pracyavamānaṃ purīṣamanubadhnātyatiyogena tathā mūtraṃ rudhiramanyāṃśca śarīradhātūn yattu sarvaśarīracaraṃ bāhyā tvagbibharti yattu tvagantare vraṇagataṃ lasīkāśabdaṃ labhate yaccoṣmaṇānubaddhaṃ lomakūpebhyo niṣpatat svedaśabdam avāpnoti tadudakaṃ daśāñjalipramāṇaṃ navāñjalayaḥ pūrvasyāhārapariṇāmadhātoḥ yaṃ rasa ityācakṣate aṣṭau śoṇitasya sapta purīṣasya ṣaṭ śleṣmaṇaḥ pañca pittasya catvāro mūtrasya trayo vasāyāḥ dvau medasaḥ eko majjāyāḥ mastiṣkasyārdhāñjaliḥ śukrasya tāvadeva pramāṇaṃ tāvadeva ślaiṣmikasyaujasa iti
children.translated_text: For example: in the body, according to its own <s>añjali</s> measure, there are ten <s>añjalis</s> of water. That water is what, when flowing out, accompanies feces in excessive discharge, and similarly urine, blood, and the other bodily <s>dhātus</s>; it is what moves through the whole body and is held by the outer skin; what, when located within the skin in a wound, receives the name <s>lasīkā</s> (serous fluid); and what, accompanied by heat and issuing from the hair-pores, obtains the name sweat. That water measures ten <s>añjalis</s>. There are nine <s>añjalis</s> of the preceding product of digested food, which they call <s>rasa</s>; eight of <s>śoṇita</s> (blood); seven of feces; six of <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm); five of <s>pitta</s> (bile); four of urine; three of <s>vasā</s> (muscle-fat); two of <s>medas</s> (fat); one of marrow; half an <s>añjali</s> of brain; the measure of semen is just that much, and just that much is the <s>ojas</s> of the <s>śleṣman</s> type.
This has been stated as the reality of the body.

children.text: tatra yad viśeṣataḥ sthūlaṃ sthiraṃ mūrtimadgurukharakaṭhinam aṅgaṃ nakhāsthidantamāṃsacarmavarcaḥkeśaśmaśrulomakaṇḍarādi tat pārthivaṃ gandho ghrāṇaṃ ca yad dravasaramandasnigdhamṛdupicchilaṃ rasarudhiravasākaphapittamūtrasvedādi tadāpyaṃ raso rasanaṃ ca yat pittam ūṣmā ca yo yā ca bhāḥ śarīre tat sarvamāgneyaṃ rūpaṃ darśanaṃ ca yad ucchvāsapraśvāsonmeṣanimeṣākuñcanaprasāraṇagamanapreraṇadhāraṇādi tad vāyavīyaṃ sparśaḥ sparśanaṃ ca yadviviktaṃ yaducyate mahānti cāṇūni srotāṃsi tadāntarīkṣaṃ śabdaḥ śrotraṃ ca yat prayoktṛ tat pradhānaṃ buddhirmanaśca
children.translated_text: In it, whatever bodily part is especially gross, stable, embodied, heavy, rough, and hard, such as nails, bones, teeth, flesh, skin, feces, hair of the head, beard, body hair, sinews, and the like, is earthy; smell and the organ of smell also belong to it. Whatever is liquid, flowing, dull, unctuous, soft, and slimy, such as <s>rasa</s>, blood, <s>vasā</s>, <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, urine, sweat, and the like, is watery; taste and the organ of taste also belong to it. Whatever is <s>pitta</s>, heat, and the radiance that exists in the body is all fiery; form and sight also belong to it. Whatever is inhalation, exhalation, opening and closing the eyes, contraction, extension, movement, impulse, support, and the like is airy; touch and the organ of touch also belong to it. Whatever is empty space, and what are called the large and minute channels, is spatial; sound and hearing also belong to it. Whatever is the directing agent is the principal factor: intellect and mind.
Thus the enumeration of the bodily parts has been taught according to the gross division of the parts.
But the bodily parts are innumerable when divided into atoms, because they are extremely many, extremely subtle, and beyond the senses.

children.text: teṣāṃ saṃyogavibhāge paramāṇūṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ vāyuḥ karmasvabhāvaśca ||
children.translated_text: Wind, together with the nature of action, is the cause of the conjunction and separation of those atoms.
This body, thus enumerated, is seen as a unity though it has many parts; conjunction is bondage, and separateness is <s>apavarga</s> (release).

children.text: tatra pradhānam asaktaṃ sarvasattānivṛttau nivartate iti ||
children.translated_text: In this matter the principal factor, being unattached, ceases when all states of being have ceased.
On this there are two verses:
The physician who knows the enumeration of the body in all its parts
is not joined to the delusion that arises from ignorance of it.
Undeluded, he is not overpowered by the <s>doṣas</s> rooted in delusion;
free from <s>doṣas</s>, without craving, and peaceful, he becomes pacified, without rebirth.
Now then we shall explain the bodily section called <s>Jātisūtrīya</s>.
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: strīpuṃsayor avyāpannaśukraśoṇitagarbhāśayayoḥ śreyasīṃ prajāmicchatos tadarthābhinirvṛttikaraṃ karmopadekṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a woman and a man whose semen, blood, and womb are unimpaired and who desire excellent offspring, we shall teach the procedure that brings that aim to accomplishment.

children.text: athāpyetau strīpuṃsau snehasvedābhyām upapādya vamanavirecanābhyāṃ saṃśodhya krameṇa prakṛtimāpādayet
children.translated_text: Then, having prepared this woman and man with oleation and sweating, one should purify them with emesis and purgation and gradually bring them back to their natural condition.

children.text: saṃśuddhau cāsthāpanānuvāsanābhyām upācared upācarecca madhurauṣadhasaṃskṛtābhyāṃ ghṛtakṣīrābhyāṃ puruṣaṃ striyaṃ tu tailamāṣābhyām ||
children.translated_text: When they have been purified, one should treat them with decoction and unctuous enemas; and one should treat the man with ghee and milk prepared with sweet medicines, but the woman with oil and black gram.

children.text: tataḥ puṣpāt prabhṛti trirātramāsīta brahmacāriṇyadhaḥśāyinī pāṇibhyāmannam ajarjarapātrād bhuñjānā na ca kāṃcin mṛjāmāpadyeta
children.translated_text: Then, from the onset of menstruation, she should remain for three nights celibate, sleeping below on the ground, eating food with her hands from an unbroken vessel, and she should not undertake any cleansing or adornment.

children.text: tataścaturthe'hanyenām utsādya saśiraskaṃ snāpayitvā śuklāni vāsāṃsyācchādayet puruṣaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Then, on the fourth day, after having her anointed and bathed including the head, one should clothe her in white garments, and the man as well.

children.text: tataḥ śuklavāsasau sragviṇau subhanasāvanyonyamabhikāmau saṃvaseyātāṃ snānāt prabhṛti yugmeṣvahaḥsu putrakāmau ayugmeṣu duhitṛkāmau ||
children.translated_text: Then the two, dressed in white, wearing garlands, well-disposed, and desiring one another, should have intercourse. From the bath onward, they should do so on even days if they desire a son, and on odd days if they desire a daughter.

children.text: na ca nyubjāṃ pārśvagatāṃ vā saṃseveta
children.translated_text: And he should not have intercourse with her when she is lying face down or on her side.

children.text: nyubjāyā vāto balavān sa yoniṃ pīḍayati pārśvagatāyā dakṣiṇe pārśve śleṣmā sa cyutaḥ pidadhāti garbhāśayaṃ vāme pārśve pittaṃ tadasyāḥ pīḍitaṃ vidahati raktaṃ śukraṃ ca tasmāduttānā bījaṃ gṛhṇīyāt tathāhi yathāsthānam avatiṣṭhante doṣāḥ
children.translated_text: In a woman lying face down, <s>vāta</s> is strong and presses upon the vagina. In one lying on her right side, <s>śleṣman</s>, displaced, blocks the womb. In one lying on her left side, <s>pitta</s>, compressed there, burns her blood and the semen. Therefore she should receive the seed while lying on her back, for then the <s>doṣas</s> remain in their proper places.
When the act is complete, he should sprinkle her with cold water.

children.text: tatrātyaśitā kṣudhitā pipāsitā bhītā vimanāḥ śokārtā kruddhānyaṃ ca pumāṃsam icchantī maithune cātikāmā vā na garbhaṃ dhatte viguṇāṃ vā prajāṃ janayati
children.translated_text: In that matter, a woman who has overeaten, is hungry, thirsty, frightened, dejected, afflicted by grief, angry, desiring another man, or excessively eager for intercourse does not conceive, or else gives birth to defective offspring.
One should avoid a woman who is too young, too old, chronically ill, or afflicted by some other disorder.
These same defects apply also in the man.
Therefore the woman and man should come together when both are free from all defects.

children.text: saṃjātaharṣau maithune cānukūlāviṣṭagandhaṃ svāstīrṇaṃ sukhaṃ śayanamupakalpya manojñaṃ hitamaśanamaśitvā nātyaśitau dakṣiṇapādena pumānārohed vāmapādena strī ||
children.translated_text: With joy arisen, favorably disposed toward intercourse, having prepared a bed that is fragrant, well spread, and comfortable, and having eaten pleasing and wholesome food, but without overeating, the man should mount with the right foot and the woman with the left foot.
There he should employ the mantra:

children.text: ahirasi āyurasi sarvataḥ pratiṣṭhāsi dhātā tvā dadatu vidhātā tvā dadhātu brahmavarcasā bhava
children.translated_text: "You are a serpent; you are life; you are established on every side. Let <s>Dhātṛ</s> give you; let <s>Vidhātṛ</s> place you. Be endowed with brahmanic radiance."
Thus.
May <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, and likewise the <s>Aśvins</s>,

children.text: bhago'tha mitrāvaruṇā vīraṃ dadatu me sutam
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaga</s> and <s>Mitra-Varuṇa</s>, give me a heroic son.
Having said this, the two should have intercourse.

children.text: sā ced evamāśāsīta bṛhantam avadātaṃ haryakṣam ojasvinaṃ śuciṃ sattvasampannaṃ putramiccheyamiti śuddhasnānāt prabhṛtyasyai manthamavadātayavānāṃ madhusarpirbhyāṃ saṃmṛjya śvetāyā goḥ sarūpavatsāyāḥ payasāloḍya rājate kāṃsye vā pātre kāle kāle saptāhaṃ satataṃ prayacchet pānāya
children.translated_text: If she should desire thus, 'I wish for a tall, fair, tawny-eyed, vigorous, pure son endowed with <s>sattva</s> (mental strength),' then from the time of the purificatory bath onward one should prepare for her a gruel of white barley, mixing it with honey and ghee, stir it with the milk of a white cow with a calf of the same color, and give it to her to drink at the proper times, continuously for seven days, in a silver or bronze vessel.

children.text: prātaśca śāliyavānnavikārān dadhimadhusarpirbhiḥ payobhirvā saṃmṛjya bhuñjīta tathā sāyam avadātaśaraṇaśayanāsanapānavasanabhūṣaṇā ca syāt
children.translated_text: And in the morning she should eat preparations of rice and barley, mixed with curds, honey, and ghee, or with milk; likewise in the evening. Her dwelling, bed, seat, drink, clothing, and ornaments should be white.

children.text: sāyaṃ prātaśca śaśvacchvetaṃ mahāntaṃ vṛṣabhamājāneyaṃ vā haricandanāṅgadaṃ paśyet
children.translated_text: Evening and morning she should constantly look at a white, large bull or a well-bred horse adorned with yellow sandalwood and bracelets.
And one should attend upon her with gentle stories agreeable to her mind.
She should see women and men, and also other objects of the senses, that are white and have gentle appearance, speech, service, and movements.
Her companions should continually attend upon her with what is pleasant and beneficial, and so too should her husband.
And the two should not come together sexually.

children.text: anena vidhinā saptarātraṃ sthitvāṣṭame 'hany āplutyādbhiḥ saśiraskaṃ saha bhartrā ahatāni vastrāṇyācchādayed avadātāni avadātāśca srajo bhūṣaṇāni ca bibhṛyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having remained in this manner for seven nights, on the eighth day, after bathing with water including the head, she together with her husband should put on unworn white garments and wear white garlands and ornaments.

children.text: tata ṛtvik prāguttarasyāṃ diśyagārasya prākpravaṇam udakpravaṇaṃ vā pradeśamabhisamīkṣya gomayodakābhyāṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya prokṣya codakena vedīm asmin sthāpayet
children.translated_text: Then the officiating priest, having examined a place in the northeastern direction of the house, sloping eastward or northward, should smear a <s>sthaṇḍila</s> (sacrificial ground) with cow-dung and water, sprinkle it with water, and set up the altar there.

children.text: tāṃ paścimenāhatavastrasaṃcaye śvetārṣabhe vāpyajina upaviśed brāhmaṇaprayuktaḥ rājanyaprayuktastu vaiyāghre carmaṇyānaḍuhe vā vaiśyaprayuktastu raurave bāste vā
children.translated_text: To the west of it, if the rite is for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he should sit on a pile of unworn cloth or on the hide of a white bull; if it is for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, on a tiger skin or an ox hide; and if it is for a <s>Vaiśya</s>, on the hide of a <s>ruru</s> deer or a goat.
