children.text: tatropaviṣṭaḥ pālāśībhir aiṅgudībhir audumbarībhir mādhūkībhir vā samidbhir agnim upasamādhāya kuśaiḥ paristīrya paridhibhiśca paridhāya lājaiḥ śuklābhiśca gandhavatībhiḥ sumanobhirupakiret
children.translated_text: Seated there, he should establish the fire with fuel sticks of <s>palāśa</s>, <s>iṅgudī</s>, <s>udumbara</s>, or <s>madhūka</s>; spread <s>kuśa</s> grass around it; enclose it with enclosing sticks; and scatter parched grain and white, fragrant flowers over it.

children.text: tatra praṇīyodapātraṃ pavitrapūtamupasaṃskṛtya sarpirājyārthaṃ yathoktavarṇān ājāneyādīn samantataḥ sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: There he should bring forward a water vessel, purify it with a strainer, consecrate it, and set ghee apart for the oblation; and he should place all around the well-bred animals and the like of the colors previously stated.

children.text: tataḥ putrakāmā paścimato'gniṃ dakṣiṇato brāhmaṇam upaviśyānvālabheta saha bhartrā yatheṣṭaṃ putram āśāsānā
children.translated_text: Then the woman desiring a son should sit to the west of the fire and to the south of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; together with her husband, wishing for whatever son she desires, she should touch him from behind.

children.text: tatastasyā āśāsānāyā ṛtvik prajāpatim abhinirdiśya yonau tasyāḥ kāmaparipūraṇārthaṃ kāmyāmiṣṭiṃ nirvartayed viṣṇuryoniṃ kalpayatu ityanayarcā
children.translated_text: Then, while she is making her wish, the officiating priest should perform the optional sacrifice, with <s>Prajāpati</s> as the deity, for the fulfillment of her desire in her womb, using the verse 'May <s>Viṣṇu</s> prepare the womb.'
Then, having sprinkled the cooked oblation in the pot with ghee, he should offer it three times according to the sacred prescription.
He should give her the water vessel, empowered by the mantra, saying, 'Use it for all water-related purposes.'

children.text: tataḥ samāpte karmaṇi pūrvaṃ dakṣiṇapādamabhiharantī pradakṣiṇamagnim anuparikrāmet saha bhartrā
children.translated_text: Then, when the rite is completed, stepping first with the right foot, she should circumambulate the fire clockwise together with her husband.

children.text: tato brāhmaṇān svasti vācayitvājyaśeṣaṃ prāśnīyāt pūrvaṃ pumān paścāt strī na cocchiṣṭamavaśeṣayet
children.translated_text: Then, after causing the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> to pronounce blessings, he should eat the remaining ghee, the man first and the woman afterward; and they should leave no remainder from what has been tasted.

children.text: tatastau saha saṃvaseyātām aṣṭarātraṃ tathāvidhaparicchadāveva ca syātāṃ tatheṣṭaputraṃ janayetām ||
children.translated_text: Then the two should live together for eight nights, furnished with the same kind of accessories, and in that way they would beget the desired son.

children.text: yā tu strī śyāmaṃ lohitākṣaṃ vyūḍhoraskaṃ mahābāhuṃ ca putramāśāsīta yā vā kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇamṛdudīrghakeśaṃ śuklākṣaṃ śukladantaṃ tejasvinam ātmavantam eṣa evānayorapi homavidhiḥ
children.translated_text: But if a woman desires a son who is dark, red-eyed, broad-chested, and long-armed, or one who is black, with black, soft, long hair, white eyes, white teeth, radiant, and self-possessed, the same fire ritual applies for both of these also.
Only the equipment should be the same except with regard to color.

children.text: putravarṇānurūpastu yathāśīreva tayoḥ paribarho'nyaḥ kāryaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: For each of the two, however, the other equipment should be arranged according to the blessing desired and in conformity with the son's color.
A <s>Śūdra</s> woman, however, should only make obeisance to the gods, fire, twice-born, teachers, ascetics, and accomplished beings.

children.text: yā yā ca yathāvidhaṃ putram āśāsīta tasyāstasyāstāṃ tāṃ putrāśiṣam anuniśamya tāṃstāñjanapadān manasānuparikrāmayet
children.translated_text: And whatever kind of son each woman desires according to rule, after listening to that particular blessing for a son in each case, one should mentally lead her through those various countries.

children.text: tato yā yā yeṣāṃ yeṣāṃ janapadānāṃ manuṣyāṇāmanurūpaṃ putramāśāsīta sā sā teṣāṃ teṣāṃ janapadānāṃ manuṣyāṇām āhāravihāropacāraparicchadān anuvidhatsveti vācyā syāt
children.translated_text: Then whichever woman desires a son corresponding to the people of such and such countries, she should be told, 'Conform yourself to the food, behavior, service, and accessories of the people of those countries.'

children.text: ityetat sarvaṃ putrāśiṣāṃ samṛddhikaraṃ karma vyākhyātaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus this whole rite that brings success to blessings for sons has been explained.

children.text: na khalu kevalametadeva karma varṇavaiśeṣyakaraṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: Indeed, this rite alone is not what produces distinctions of color.

children.text: api tu tejodhātur apyudakāntarikṣadhātuprāyo 'vadātavarṇakaro bhavati pṛthivīvāyudhātuprāyaḥ kṛṣṇavarṇakaraḥ samasarvadhātuprāyaḥ śyāmavarṇakaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Rather, the <s>tejas</s> element too, when predominating together with the water and space elements, produces a fair color; predominance of the earth and wind elements produces a black color; and predominance of all the elements in equal measure produces a dark-brown color.

children.text: sattvavaiśeṣyakarāṇi punasteṣāṃ teṣāṃ prāṇināṃ mātāpitṛsattvānyantarvatnyāḥ śrutayaścābhīkṣṇaṃ svocitaṃ ca karma sattvaviśeṣābhyāsaśceti ||
children.translated_text: Again, what produces distinctions of <s>sattva</s> in these various living beings are the <s>sattvas</s> of the mother and father, the things repeatedly heard by the pregnant woman, conduct proper to oneself, and the repeated cultivation of particular mental dispositions.

children.text: yathoktena vidhinopasaṃskṛtaśarīrayoḥ strīpuruṣayor miśrībhāvam āpannayoḥ śukraṃ śoṇitena saha saṃyogaṃ sametyāvyāpannam avyāpannena yonāvanupahatāyām apraduṣṭe garbhāśaye garbham abhinirvartayatyekāntena
children.translated_text: When a woman and man, whose bodies have been prepared by the procedure described, come together sexually, the semen, joining with the blood, if it is unimpaired and united with what is unimpaired, in an uninjured vagina and an untainted womb, unfailingly brings about an embryo.

children.text: yathā nirmale vāsasi suparikalpite rañjanaṃ samuditaguṇam upanipātādeva rāgam abhinirvartayati tadvat yathā vā kṣīraṃ dadhnābhiṣutam abhiṣavaṇād vihāya svabhāvam āpadyate dadhibhāvaṃ śukraṃ tadvat ||
children.translated_text: Just as, on a clean and well-prepared cloth, a dye endowed with all its proper qualities produces color simply by contact, so too; or just as milk inoculated with curd, through that inoculation, abandons its own nature and assumes the state of curd, so too does <s>śukra</s> (semen).

children.text: evam abhinirvartamānasya garbhasya strīpuruṣatve hetuḥ pūrvamuktaḥ
children.translated_text: The cause of femaleness and maleness in the embryo as it is thus being formed has been stated earlier.

children.text: yathā hi bījam anupataptam uptaṃ svāṃ svāṃ prakṛtimanuvidhīyate vrīhirvā vrīhitvaṃ yavo vā yavatvaṃ tathā strīpuruṣāvapi yathoktaṃ hetuvibhāgamanuvidhīyete ||
children.translated_text: For just as a seed that has not been damaged, when sown, follows its own particular nature, rice becoming rice and barley becoming barley, so too a woman and a man follow the division of causes as stated.

children.text: tayoḥ karmaṇā vedoktena vivartanamupadiśyate prāgvyaktībhāvāt prayuktena samyak
children.translated_text: For the two of them, a transformation is taught by a Veda-prescribed rite, when it is properly applied before manifest differentiation.

children.text: karmaṇāṃ hi deśakālasaṃpadupetānāṃ niyatam iṣṭaphalatvaṃ tathetareṣām itaratvam
children.translated_text: For actions endowed with the right place and time certainly have the desired result; actions otherwise performed have the opposite result.

children.text: tasmādāpannagarbhāṃ striyam abhisamīkṣya prāgvyaktībhāvādgarbhasya puṃsavanamasyai dadyāt
children.translated_text: Therefore, after examining a woman who has conceived, before the embryo has become manifest one should give her <s>puṃsavana</s> (the rite for obtaining a male child).

children.text: goṣṭhe jātasya nyagrodhasya prāguttarābhyāṃ śākhābhyāṃ śuṅge anupahate ādāya dvābhyāṃ dhānyamāṣābhyāṃ saṃpadupetābhyāṃ gaurasarṣapābhyāṃ vā saha dadhni prakṣipya puṣyeṇa pibet tathaivāparāñ jīvakarṣabhakāpāmārgasahacarakalkāṃśca yugapadekaikaśo yatheṣṭaṃ vāpyupasaṃskṛtya payasā kuḍyakīṭakaṃ matsyakaṃ vodakāñjalau prakṣipya puṣyeṇa pibet tathā kanakamayān rājatān āyasāṃśca puruṣakān agnivarṇān aṇuprabhāṇān dadhni payasyudakāñjalau vā prakṣipya pibed anavaśeṣataḥ puṣyeṇa puṣyeṇaiva ca śālipiṣṭasya pacyamānasyoṣmāṇam upāghrāya tasyaiva ca piṣṭasyodakasaṃsṛṣṭasya rasaṃ dehalyām upanidhāya dakṣiṇe nāsāpuṭe svayamāsiñcet picunā
children.translated_text: From a <s>nyagrodha</s> tree born in a cowshed, one should take two uninjured shoots from the eastern and northern branches, put them in curds together with two excellent grains and black grams, or with white mustard seeds, and she should drink this under <s>Puṣya</s>. Likewise, other pastes of <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, and <s>sahacara</s>, prepared all together, singly, or as desired with milk, may be used; or she should put a wall-insect or a small fish into a handful of water and drink it under <s>Puṣya</s>. Likewise, she should put little male figures made of gold, silver, and iron, heated to a fire-like color and minute in brightness, into curds, milk, or a handful of water, and drink it completely under <s>Puṣya</s>. Also under <s>Puṣya</s>, after smelling the steam of rice-flour while it is cooking, she herself should place the juice of that same flour mixed with water on the threshold and instill it into the right nostril with a cotton swab.

children.text: yaccānyadapi brāhmaṇā brūyurāptā vā striyaḥ puṃsavanamiṣṭaṃ taccānuṣṭheyam
children.translated_text: And whatever else trustworthy Brahmins or reliable women say is a desired <s>puṃsavana</s> should also be performed.
Thus the <s>puṃsavana</s> procedures are stated.

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ garbhasthāpanāni vyākhyāsyāmaḥ aindrī brāhmī śatavīryā sahasravīryāmoghāvyathā śivāriṣṭā vāṭyapuṣpī viṣvaksenakāntā cetyāsām oṣadhīnāṃ śirasā dakṣiṇena vā pāṇinā dhāraṇam etābhiścaiva siddhasya payasaḥ sarpiṣo vā pānam etābhiścaiva puṣye puṣye snānaṃ sadā ca tāḥ samālabheta
children.translated_text: From here onward we shall explain the measures for stabilizing the fetus. One should wear on the head or in the right hand these herbs: <s>aindrī</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, <s>śatavīryā</s>, <s>sahasravīryā</s>, <s>amoghā</s>, <s>avyathā</s>, <s>śivā</s>, <s>ariṣṭā</s>, <s>vāṭyapuṣpī</s>, and <s>viṣvaksenakāntā</s>. One should drink milk or ghee prepared with these same herbs, bathe with them at every <s>Puṣya</s>, and always anoint oneself with them.

children.text: tathā sarvāsāṃ jīvanīyoktānām oṣadhīnāṃ sadopayogas taistair upayogavidhibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise there should be constant use of all the herbs mentioned among the life-promoting remedies, according to their respective modes of use.
Thus the measures for stabilizing the fetus have been explained.

children.text: garbhopaghātakarāstvime bhāvā bhavanti tadyathā utkaṭaviṣamakaṭhināsanasevinyā vātamūtrapurīṣavegān uparundhatyā dāruṇānucitavyāyāmasevinyās tīkṣṇoṣṇātimātrasevinyāḥ pramitāśanasevinyā garbho mriyate'ntaḥ kukṣeḥ akāle vā sraṃsate śoṣī vā bhavati tathābhighātaprapīḍanaiḥ śvabhrakūpaprapātadeśāvalokanair vābhīkṣṇaṃ mātuḥ prapatatyakāle garbhaḥ tathātimātrasaṃkṣobhibhir yānair yānena apriyātimātraśravaṇairvā
children.translated_text: These, however, are factors that harm the fetus. For example, in a woman who makes use of high, uneven, and hard seats, suppresses the urges for flatus, urine, and feces, undertakes harsh and unsuitable exercise, consumes excessively sharp and hot substances, or lives on measured and scanty food, the fetus dies inside the womb, is discharged prematurely, or becomes wasted. Likewise, because of blows and pressure, or because the mother repeatedly looks down into places such as ravines, wells, and precipices, the fetus falls prematurely; likewise because of vehicles that cause excessive jolting, or from hearing things that are extremely unpleasant.

children.text: pratatottānaśāyinyāḥ punargarbhasya nābhyāśrayā nāḍī kaṇṭhamanuveṣṭayati vivṛtaśāyinī naktaṃcāriṇī conmattaṃ janayati apasmāriṇaṃ punaḥ kalikalahaśīlā vyavāyaśīlā durvapuṣam ahrīkaṃ straiṇaṃ vā śokanityā bhītam apacitam alpāyuṣaṃ vā abhidhyātrī paropatāpinam īrṣyuṃ straiṇaṃ vā stenā tvāyāsabahulam atidrohiṇam akarmaśīlaṃ vā amarṣiṇī caṇḍamaupadhikam asūyakaṃ vā svapnanityā tandrālumabudham alpāgniṃ vā madyanityā pipāsālum alpasmṛtim anavasthitacittaṃ vā godhāmāṃsaprāyā śārkariṇam aśmariṇaṃ śanairmehiṇaṃ vā varāhamāṃsaprāyā raktākṣaṃ krathanam atiparuṣaromāṇaṃ vā matsyamāṃsanityā ciranimeṣaṃ stabdhākṣaṃ vā madhuranityā pramehiṇaṃ mūkamatisthūlaṃ vā amlanityā raktapittinaṃ tvagakṣirogiṇaṃ vā lavaṇanityā śīghravalīpalitaṃ khālityarogiṇaṃ vā kaṭukanityā durbalam alpaśukram anapatyaṃ vā tiktanityā śoṣiṇamabalamanupacitaṃ vā kaṣāyanityā śyāvam ānāhinam udāvartinaṃ vā yadyacca yasya yasya vyādher nidānamuktaṃ tattadāsevamānāntarvatnī tannimittavikārabahulam apatyaṃ janayati
children.translated_text: Again, in a woman who constantly lies on her back, the cord attached to the fetus's navel wraps around its neck. A woman who sleeps exposed and wanders at night gives birth to an insane child. A woman disposed to quarrels and disputes gives birth to one afflicted with epilepsy; one devoted to sexual intercourse, to one ugly, shameless, or woman-obsessed; one constantly grieving, to one fearful, emaciated, or short-lived; one who covets, to one who harms others, is envious, or woman-obsessed; a thief, to one full of hardship, very hostile, or inactive; one who is intolerant, to one fierce, deceitful, or jealous; one constantly sleeping, to one drowsy, unintelligent, or weak in digestion; one constantly drinking liquor, to one thirsty, poor in memory, or unsteady in mind. A woman whose diet is mostly monitor-lizard meat gives birth to one with gravel, urinary stones, or slow urination; one whose diet is mostly pork, to one red-eyed, grunting, or with very coarse hair; one who habitually eats fish meat, to one who blinks slowly or has fixed eyes; one constantly taking sweet foods, to one with <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorder), mute, or excessively fat; one constantly taking sour foods, to one with <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorder) or disease of the skin and eyes; one constantly taking salty foods, to one quickly affected by wrinkles, gray hair, or baldness; one constantly taking pungent foods, to one weak, scant in semen, or childless; one constantly taking bitter foods, to one wasted, weak, or undeveloped; and one constantly taking astringent foods, to one dark, distended with gas, or suffering from upward-moving wind. Whatever is stated as the cause of any particular disease, when a pregnant woman habitually follows that, she gives birth to offspring abounding in disorders caused by that very factor.
Defects of semen arising from the father are explained by the misconducts arising from the mother.
Thus the factors that harm the fetus have been stated.

children.text: tasmādahitān āhāravihārān prajāsaṃpadam icchantī strī viśeṣeṇa varjayet
children.translated_text: Therefore a woman who desires excellence in offspring should especially avoid harmful foods and modes of conduct.
Living with good conduct, she should care for herself with beneficial food and regimen. Thus.

children.text: vyādhīṃścāsyā mṛdumadhuraśiśirasukhasukumāraprāyair auṣadhāhāropacārair upacaret na cāsyā vamanavirecanaśirovirecanāni prayojayet na raktamavasecayet sarvakālaṃ ca nāsthāpanamanuvāsanaṃ vā kuryād anyatrātyayikād vyādheḥ
children.translated_text: One should treat her diseases with medicines, foods, and procedures that are mostly mild, sweet, cooling, pleasant, and delicate. One should not employ emesis, purgation, or evacuation of the head for her; one should not let blood from her; and at no time should one administer either a decoction enema or an unctuous enema, except in a disease that is urgent.

children.text: aṣṭamaṃ māsamupādāya vamanādisādhyeṣu punarvikāreṣvātyayikeṣu mṛdubhir vamanādibhis tadarthakāribhir vopacāraḥ syāt
children.translated_text: But from the eighth month onward, in urgent disorders that are curable by emesis and the like, treatment may be given by mild emesis and similar measures, or by procedures that accomplish the same purpose.
A pregnant woman should be tended without disturbing her, like a vessel filled to the brim with oil.

children.text: sā cedapacārād dvayostriṣu vā māseṣu puṣpaṃ paśyennāsyā garbhaḥ sthāsyatīti vidyāt ajātasāro hi tasmin kāle bhavati garbhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, through improper conduct, she sees menstrual blood in the second or third month, one should know that her fetus will not remain; for at that time the fetus has not yet developed its essence.

children.text: sā cec catuṣprabhṛtiṣu māseṣu krodhaśokāsūyerṣyābhayatrāsavyavāyavyāyāmasaṃkṣobhasaṃdhāraṇaviṣamāśanaśayanasthānakṣutpipāsātiyogāt kadāhārād vā puṣpaṃ paśyet tasyā garbhasthāpanavidhim upadekṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: But if, from the fourth month onward, she sees blood because of anger, grief, resentment, jealousy, fear, terror, intercourse, exercise, agitation, suppression of urges, irregular eating, lying or standing improperly, excessive hunger or thirst, or from too little food, we shall teach the procedure for stabilizing her fetus.

children.text: puṣpadarśanādevaināṃ brūyāt śayanaṃ tāvanmṛdusukhaśiśirāstaraṇasaṃstīrṇam īṣadavanataśiraskaṃ pratipadyasveti
children.translated_text: As soon as blood is seen, one should tell her, 'For now, take to a bed that is soft, pleasant, cool, and spread with bedding, with the head slightly lowered.'

children.text: tato yaṣṭīmadhukasarpirbhyāṃ paramaśiśiravāriṇi saṃsthitābhyāṃ picum āplāvyopasthasamīpe sthāpayet tasyāḥ tathā śatadhautasahasradhautābhyāṃ sarpirbhyāmadhonābheḥ sarvataḥ pradihyāt sarvataśca gavyena caināṃ payasā suśītena madhukāmbunā vā nyagrodhādikaṣāyeṇa vā pariṣecayedadho nābheḥ udakaṃ vā suśītam avagāhayet kṣīriṇāṃ kaṣāyadrumāṇāṃ ca svarasaparipītāni celāni grāhayet nyagrodhādiśuṅgāsiddhayor vā kṣīrasarpiṣoḥ picuṃ grāhayet ataścaivākṣamātraṃ prāśayet prāśayedvā kevalaṃ kṣīrasarpiḥ padmotpalakumudakiñjalkāṃścāsyai samadhuśarkarān lehārthaṃ dadyāt śṛṅgāṭakapuṣkarabījakaśerukān bhakṣaṇārthaṃ gandhapriyaṅgvasitotpalaśālūkodumbaraśalāṭunyagrodhaśuṅgāni vā pāyayedenāmājena payasā payasā caināṃ balātibalāśāliṣaṣṭikekṣumūlakākolīśṛtena samadhuśarkaraṃ raktaśālīnāmodanaṃ mṛdusurabhiśītalaṃ bhojayet lāvakapiñjalakuraṅgaśambaraśaśahariṇaiṇakālapucchakarasena vā ghṛtasusaṃskṛtena sukhaśiśiropavātadeśasthāṃ bhojayet krodhaśokāyāsavyavāyavyāyāmebhyaś cābhirakṣet saumyābhiścaināṃ kathābhir mano'nukūlābhir upāsīta tathāsyā garbhastiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Then one should soak a cotton plug in <s>yaṣṭīmadhuka</s> and ghee that have been kept in very cold water, and place it near her vagina. Likewise, with ghee washed a hundred times or a thousand times, one should anoint her everywhere below the navel. One should also sprinkle her everywhere below the navel with very cold cow's milk, or with <s>madhuka</s> water, or with a decoction beginning with <s>nyagrodha</s>; or one should have her immerse herself in very cold water. One should have her hold cloths thoroughly soaked in the fresh juices of milky trees and astringent trees; or have her hold a plug soaked in milk or ghee cooked with shoots beginning with <s>nyagrodha</s>. From this one should also make her drink a quantity of one <s>akṣa</s>, or else make her drink only milk and ghee. One should give her filaments of lotus, blue lotus, and water-lily with honey and sugar as a linctus; and <s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s>, lotus seeds, and <s>kaśeruka</s> for eating. Or one should make her drink goat's milk with fragrant <s>priyaṅgu</s>, white lotus, <s>śālūka</s>, <s>udumbara</s> fruit, and shoots of <s>nyagrodha</s>. With milk boiled with <s>balā</s>, <s>atibalā</s>, <s>śāli</s>, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s>, sugarcane root, and <s>kākolī</s>, and with honey and sugar, one should feed her soft, fragrant, cooling rice of red <s>śāli</s>; or feed her with the meat broth of quail, partridge, antelope, <s>śambara</s> deer, hare, deer, black antelope, or <s>kālapucchaka</s>, well prepared with ghee, while she stays in a place that is comfortable, cool, and sheltered from wind. One should protect her from anger, grief, fatigue, intercourse, and exercise, and attend upon her with gentle stories pleasing to her mind. In this way her fetus remains.

children.text: yasyāḥ punarāmānvayāt puṣpadarśanaṃ syāt prāyastasyāstadgarbhopaghātakaraṃ bhavati viruddhopakramatvāttayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when a woman sees blood because of association with <s>āma</s> (undigested pathogenic matter), that mostly brings injury to her fetus, because the therapeutic approaches for the two are opposed.

children.text: yasyāḥ punar uṣṇatīkṣṇopayogād garbhiṇyā mahati saṃjātasāre garbhe puṣpadarśanaṃ syādanyo vā yonisrāvastasyā garbho vṛddhiṃ na prāpnoti niḥsrutatvāt sa kālamavatiṣṭhate'timātraṃ tamupaviṣṭakamityācakṣate kecit
children.translated_text: Again, when a pregnant woman has used hot and sharp substances, and blood is seen, or some other vaginal discharge occurs, while the fetus is large and has developed its essence, her fetus does not attain growth, because it has been depleted. It remains for an excessive length of time; some call this an <s>upaviṣṭaka</s> fetus.

children.text: upavāsavratakarmaparāyāḥ punaḥ kadāhārāyāḥ snehadveṣiṇyā vātaprakopaṇoktānyāsevamānāyā garbho vṛddhiṃ na prāpnoti pariśuṣkatvāt sa cāpi kālamavatiṣṭhate'timātram aspandanaśca bhavati taṃ tu nāgodaram ityācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: Again, for a woman devoted to fasting and vows, eating too little, averse to unctuous substances, and using the things said to aggravate <s>vāta</s>, the fetus does not attain growth because it is dried out. It too remains for an excessive length of time and is motionless; this they call <s>nāgodara</s>.

children.text: nāryostayor ubhayorapi cikitsitaviśeṣam upadekṣyāmaḥ bhautikajīvanīyabṛṃhaṇīyamadhuravātaharasiddhānāṃ sarpiṣāṃ payasāmāmagarbhāṇāṃ copayogo garbhavṛddhikaraḥ tathā sambhojanametaireva siddhaiśca ghṛtādibhiḥ subhikṣāyāḥ abhīkṣṇaṃ yānavāhanāpamārjanāvajṛmbhaṇair upapādanam iti ||
children.translated_text: We shall teach the special treatment for both of those women. The use of ghee, milk, and meat juices prepared with drugs of the elemental, life-promoting, nourishing, sweet, and <s>vāta</s>-pacifying groups promotes fetal growth; so too does feeding her with foods prepared with these same substances and with ghee and the like. When food is plentiful, she should also often be provided with conveyances, rides, cleansing and rubbing, and relaxing bodily measures.

children.text: yasyāḥ punargarbhaḥ supto na spandate tāṃ śyenamatsyagavayaśikhitāmracūḍatittirīṇām anyatamasya sarpiṣmatā rasena māṣayūṣeṇa vā prabhūtasarpiṣā mūlakayūṣeṇa vā raktaśālīnām odanaṃ mṛdumadhuśītalaṃ bhojayet
children.translated_text: When a woman's fetus is asleep and does not move, one should feed her soft, sweet, cooling rice of red <s>śāli</s> with the ghee-rich meat broth of any one of hawk, fish, wild ox, peacock, rooster, or partridge; or with black-gram soup; or with radish soup containing abundant ghee.
And by oil massage one should frequently treat the regions of her abdomen, bladder, groins, thighs, hips, sides, and back with slightly warm oil.

children.text: yasyāḥ punarudāvartavibandhaḥ syādaṣṭame māse na cānuvāsanasādhyaṃ manyeta tatastasyās tadvikārapraśamanam upakalpayennirūham
children.translated_text: Again, if in the eighth month she has upward movement of wind and constipation, and one does not consider it treatable by an unctuous enema, then one should prepare for her a decoction enema that pacifies that disorder.

children.text: udāvarto hyupekṣitaḥ sahasā sagarbhāṃ garbhiṇīṃ garbham athavātipātayet
children.translated_text: For upward-moving wind, if neglected, may suddenly destroy the pregnant woman together with the fetus, or else the fetus alone.

children.text: tatra vīraṇaśāliṣaṣṭikakuśakāśekṣuvālikāvetasaparivyādhamūlānāṃ bhūtīkānantākāśmaryaparūṣakamadhukamṛdvīkānāṃ ca payasārdhodakenodgamayya rasaṃ priyālavibhītakamajjatilakalkasamprayuktam īṣallavaṇam anatyuṣṇaṃ ca nirūhaṃ dadyāt
children.translated_text: In that case, one should boil the roots of <s>vīraṇa</s>, <s>śāli</s>, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s>, <s>kuśa</s>, <s>kāśa</s>, sugarcane, <s>vālikā</s>, <s>vetasa</s>, and <s>parivyādha</s>, and also <s>bhūtīka</s>, <s>anantā</s>, <s>kāśmaryā</s>, <s>parūṣaka</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and raisins, in half milk and half water. One should give the resulting liquid as a decoction enema, mixed with a paste of <s>priyāla</s> kernels, <s>vibhītaka</s> kernels, and sesame, slightly salted and not too hot.

children.text: vyapagatavibandhāṃ caināṃ sukhasalilapariṣiktāṅgīṃ sthairyakaram avidāhinam āhāraṃ bhuktavatīṃ sāyaṃ madhurakasiddhena tailenānuvāsayet
children.translated_text: And when the obstruction has passed away, after her limbs have been sprinkled with pleasant water and she has eaten food that gives firmness and does not cause burning, in the evening one should give her an unctuous enema with oil prepared with sweet drugs.
But if she is bent or turned downward, one should treat her with both evacuative and unctuous enemas.

children.text: yasyāḥ punar atimātradoṣopacayād vā tīkṣṇoṣṇātimātrasevanād vā vātamūtrapurīṣavegavidhāraṇair vā viṣamāśanaśayanasthānasampīḍanābhighātair vā krodhaśokerṣyābhayatrāsādibhir vā sāhasairvāparaiḥ karmabhirantaḥ kukṣergarbho mriyate tasyāḥ stimitaṃ stabdhamudaram ātataṃ śītamaśmāntargatamiva bhavatyaspandano garbhaḥ śūlam adhikamupajāyate na cāvyaḥ prādurbhavanti yonirna prasravati akṣiṇī cāsyāḥ sraste bhavataḥ tāmyati vyathate bhramate śvasiti aratibahulā ca bhavati na cāsyā vegaprādurbhāvo yathāvadupalabhyate ityevaṃlakṣaṇāṃ striyam mṛtagarbheyamiti vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: Again, when in a woman the fetus dies within the abdomen because of excessive accumulation of the <s>doṣas</s>, or because of excessive use of sharp and hot things, or through suppression of the urges for flatus, urine, and feces, or through irregular eating, sleeping, posture, pressure, and blows, or through anger, grief, jealousy, fear, terror, and the like, or through other rash acts and deeds, her abdomen becomes still, rigid, distended, and cold, as if a stone were inside; the fetus does not move; severe pain arises; the signs of delivery do not appear; the vagina does not discharge; her eyes become sunken; she faints, is distressed, becomes dizzy, breathes heavily, and is full of restlessness; and the proper manifestation of her urges is not observed. A woman with these signs should be known as having a dead fetus.

children.text: tasya garbhaśalyasya jarāyuprapātanaṃ karma saṃśamanamityāhureke mantrādikam atharvavedavihitam ityeke paridṛṣṭakarmaṇā śalyahartrā haraṇam ityeke
children.translated_text: Concerning that fetal foreign body, some say that the treatment is to make the placenta fall and to pacify the condition; others say that it is the use of mantras and the like prescribed in the <s>Atharvaveda</s>; others say that it is removal by a surgeon who has observed the procedure.

children.text: vyapagatagarbhaśalyāṃ tu striyam āmagarbhāṃ surāsīdhvariṣṭamadhumadirāsavānām anyatamam agre sāmarthyataḥ pāyayed garbhakoṣṭhaśuddhyartham artivismaraṇārthaṃ praharṣaṇārthaṃ ca ataḥ paraṃ samprīṇanair balānurakṣibhir asnehasamprayuktair yavāgvādibhirvā tatkālayogibhir āhārair upacared doṣadhātukledaviśoṣaṇamātraṃ kālam
children.translated_text: But when the fetal foreign body has passed out, if the woman has an unripe fetus, one should first have her drink, according to her capacity, any one of surā, sīdhu, ariṣṭa, madhu, madirā, or āsava, for the cleansing of the uterine cavity, for forgetting the pain, and for exhilaration. After that one should treat her for just so long as is needed to dry up the moisture of the <s>doṣas</s> and <s>dhātus</s>, with nourishing foods that protect strength and are not combined with fat, such as gruels and other foods appropriate to the time.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ snehapānair vastibhir āhāravidhibhiśca dīpanīyajīvanīyabṛṃhaṇīyamadhuravātaharasamākhyātair upacaret
children.translated_text: After that one should treat her with intake of fats, enemas, and dietary regimens described as kindling digestion, life-promoting, bulk-promoting, sweet, and pacifying <s>vāta</s>.
But in the case of a woman whose fetal foreign body was mature and has then been released, oleating treatment should begin on that very day.

children.text: paramato nirvikāramāpyāyyamānasya garbhasya māse māse karmopadekṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Next we shall teach, month by month, the regimen for a fetus that is free from disorder and is being nourished.

children.text: prathame māse śaṅkitā cedgarbhamāpannā kṣīramanupaskṛtaṃ mātrāvacchītaṃ kāle kāle pibet sātmyameva ca bhojanaṃ sāyaṃ prātaśca bhuñjīta dvitīye māse kṣīrameva ca madhurauṣadhasiddhaṃ tṛtīye māse kṣīraṃ madhusarpirbhyām upasaṃsṛjya caturthe māse kṣīranavanītam akṣamātramaśnīyāt pañcame māse kṣīrasarpiḥ ṣaṣṭhe māse kṣīrasarpirmadhurauṣadhasiddhaṃ tadeva saptame māse
children.translated_text: In the first month, if she suspects that she has conceived, she should drink plain milk, cooled and in proper measure, from time to time, and should eat only wholesome food in the evening and morning. In the second month she should take that same milk prepared with sweet drugs. In the third month she should take milk mixed with honey and ghee. In the fourth month she should eat milk with fresh butter in the amount of one akṣa. In the fifth month she should take milk with ghee. In the sixth month she should take milk and ghee prepared with sweet drugs, and the same in the seventh month.

children.text: tatra garbhasya keśā jāyamānā māturvidāhaṃ janayantīti striyo bhāṣante tanneti bhagavān ātreyaḥ kiṃtu garbhotpīḍanād vātapittaśleṣmāṇa uraḥ prāpya vidāhaṃ janayanti tataḥ kaṇḍūrupajāyate kaṇḍūmūlā ca kikkisāvāptir bhavati
children.translated_text: On this point women say, 'The hairs of the fetus as they arise produce burning in the mother.' 'That is not so,' says the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>; rather, because of pressure from the fetus, <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s> reach the chest and produce burning; from that itching arises, and from itching as its root there is the occurrence of kikkisā, stretch marks.

children.text: tatra kolodakena navanītamadhurauṣadhasiddhasya pāṇitalamātraṃ kāle kāle'syai pānārthaṃ dadyāt candanamṛṇālakalkaiścāsyāḥ stanodaraṃ vimṛdnīyāt śirīṣadhātakīsarṣapamadhukacūrṇair vā kuṭajārjakabījamustaharidrākalkairvā nimbakolasurasamañjiṣṭhākalkair vā pṛṣatahariṇaśaśarudhirayutayā triphalayā vā karavīrapatrasiddhena tailenābhyaṅgaḥ pariṣekaḥ punar mālatīmadhukasiddhenāmbhasā jātakaṇḍūśca kaṇḍūyanaṃ varjayettvagbhedavairūpyaparihārārtham asahyāyāṃ tu kaṇḍvām unmardanoddharṣaṇābhyāṃ parihāraḥ syāt madhuramāhārajātaṃ vātaharamalpamasnehalavaṇam alpodakānupānaṃ ca bhuñjīta
children.translated_text: In that case, from time to time one should give her, for drinking, a palmful of fresh butter prepared with jujube water and sweet drugs. Her breasts and abdomen should be rubbed with pastes of sandalwood and lotus-fiber, or with powders of śirīṣa, dhātakī, mustard, and madhuka, or with pastes of kuṭaja seed, arjaka seed, musta, and haridrā, or with pastes of nimba, kola, surasa, and mañjiṣṭhā, or with triphalā mixed with the blood of the spotted antelope, deer, and hare. Anointing should be done with oil prepared with oleander leaves, and sprinkling again with water prepared with mālatī and madhuka. When itching has arisen, she should avoid scratching, in order to prevent cracking and disfigurement of the skin. But when the itching is unbearable, relief may be obtained by rubbing and friction. She should eat sweet kinds of food that pacify <s>vāta</s>, are small in quantity, contain little fat and salt, and are followed by little water.

children.text: aṣṭame tu māse kṣīrayavāgūṃ sarpiṣmatīṃ kāle kāle pibet tanneti bhadrakāpyaḥ paiṅgalyābādho hyasyā garbhamāgacchediti astvatra paiṅgalyābādha ityāha bhagavān punarvasur ātreyaḥ na tvevaitanna kāryam evaṃ kurvatī hyarogārogyabalavarṇasvarasaṃhananasampadupetaṃ jñātīnāmapi śreṣṭhamapatyaṃ janayati
children.translated_text: In the eighth month she should drink milk-gruel with ghee from time to time. 'That should not be done,' says <s>Bhadrakāpya</s>, 'for the affliction of yellowness may come upon her fetus.' 'Let there be this affliction of yellowness here,' says the blessed <s>Punarvasu Ātreya</s>, 'but this certainly must be done; for a woman acting in this way gives birth to a child endowed with freedom from disease, health, strength, complexion, voice, and compactness, excellent even among its kinsmen.'

children.text: navame tu khalvenāṃ māse madhurauṣadhasiddhena tailenānuvāsayet
children.translated_text: In the ninth month, moreover, one should give her an unctuous enema with oil prepared with sweet drugs.
And from that very oil one should insert a tampon into her vagina, for the purpose of lubricating the place and path of the fetus.

children.text: yadidaṃ karma prathamaṃ māsaṃ samupādāyopadiṣṭam ā navamānmāsāttena garbhiṇyā garbhasamaye garbhadhāriṇīkukṣikaṭīpārśvapṛṣṭhaṃ mṛdūbhavati vātaścānulomaḥ sampadyate mūtrapurīṣe ca prakṛtibhūte sukhena mārgamanupadyete carmanakhāni ca mārdavamupayānti balavarṇau copacīyete putraṃ ceṣṭaṃ saṃpadupetaṃ sukhinaṃ sukhenaiṣā kāle prajāyata iti ||
children.translated_text: By this procedure taught beginning with the first month and extending up to the ninth month, at the time of pregnancy the womb-supporting abdomen, hips, sides, and back of the pregnant woman become soft; <s>vāta</s> moves in its proper downward course; urine and feces, restored to their natural condition, easily follow their channels; the skin and nails become soft; strength and complexion increase; and at the proper time she gives birth easily to a desired son, endowed with excellence and happy.

children.text: prāk caivāsyā navamānmāsāt sūtikāgāraṃ kārayedapahṛtāsthiśarkarākapāle deśe praśastarūparasagandhāyāṃ bhūmau prāgdvāram udagdvāraṃ vā bailvānāṃ kāṣṭhānāṃ taindukaiṅgudakānāṃ bhāllātakānāṃ vāraṇānāṃ khādirāṇāṃ vā yāni cānyānyapi brāhmaṇāḥ śaṃseyur atharvavedavidasteṣāṃ vasanālepanācchādanāpidhānasaṃpadupetaṃ vāstuvidyāhṛdayayogāgnisalilodūkhalavarcaḥsthānasnānabhūmimahānasam ṛtusukhaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Before her ninth month one should also have a birthing room made in a place cleared of bones, gravel, and potsherds, on ground excellent in appearance, taste, and smell, with a door facing east or north, made of wood of bilva, tinduka, inguda, bhallātaka, vāraṇa, khadira, or any other trees that brahmins learned in the <s>Atharvaveda</s> recommend. It should be furnished with clothing, ointments, coverings, and lids, and provided, according to the principles of building science, with hearth, water, mortar, latrine, bathing ground, and kitchen, and it should be comfortable in every season.

children.text: tatra sarpistailamadhusaindhavasauvarcalakālaviḍlavaṇaviḍaṅgakuṣṭhakilimanāgarapippalīpippalīmūlahastipippalīmaṇḍūkaparṇyelālāṅgalīvacācavyacitrakacirabilvahiṅgusarṣapalaśunakatakakaṇakaṇikānīpātasībalvajabhūrjakulatthamaireyasurāsavāḥ saṃnihitāḥ syuḥ tathāśmānau dvau dve kuṇḍamusale dve udūkhale kharavṛṣabhaśca dvau ca tīkṣṇau sūcīpippalakau sauvarṇarājatau śastrāṇi ca tīkṣṇāyasāni dvau ca bilvamayau paryaṅkau taindukaiṅgudāni ca kāṣṭhānyagnisaṃdhukṣaṇāni striyaśca bahvyo bahuśaḥ prajātāḥ sauhārdayuktāḥ satatam anuraktāḥ pradakṣiṇācārāḥ pratipattikuśalāḥ prakṛtivatsalāstyaktaviṣādāḥ kleśasahinyo'bhimatāḥ brāhmaṇāścātharvavedavidaḥ yaccānyadapi tatra samarthaṃ manyeta yaccānyacca brāhmaṇā brūyuḥ striyaśca vṛddhāstat kāryam ||
children.translated_text: There, ghee, oil, honey, rock salt, sauvarchala salt, kālaviḍa salt, viḍaṅga, kuṣṭha, kilima, nāgara, pippalī, pippalī root, hastipippalī, maṇḍūkaparṇī, elā, lāṅgalī, vacā, cavya, citraka, cirabilva, hiṅgu, mustard, garlic, kataka, kaṇakaṇikā, nīpa, flax, balvaja grass, birch bark, horse gram, maireya liquor, surā, and āsava should be kept at hand. Likewise there should be two stones, two pestles, two mortars, two grinding mortars, a donkey and a bull, two sharp needles made of gold and silver, sharp iron instruments, two couches made of bilva, tinduka and inguda wood for kindling the fire, many women who have often given birth, who are friendly, constantly affectionate, auspicious in conduct, skilled in practical response, naturally tender, free from despondency, able to endure hardship, and agreeable, and brahmins learned in the <s>Atharvaveda</s>. Whatever else one thinks useful there, and whatever else the brahmins and elderly women say, should be done.

children.text: tataḥ pravṛtte navame māse puṇye'hani praśastanakṣatrayogamupagate praśaste bhagavati śaśini kalyāṇe kalyāṇe ca karaṇe maitre muhūrte śāntiṃ hutvā gobrāhmaṇam agnimudakaṃ cādau praveśya gobhyas tṛṇodakaṃ madhulājāṃśca pradāya brāhmaṇebhyo'kṣatān sumanaso nāndīmukhāni ca phalānīṣṭāni dattvodakapūrvam āsanasthebhyo 'bhivādya punarācamya svasti vācayet
children.translated_text: Then, when the ninth month has begun, on an auspicious day, when a favorable conjunction of lunar mansion has occurred, when the blessed moon is favorable, when the karaṇa is auspicious, and at a friendly muhūrta, after offering an oblation for pacification, one should first bring in a cow, a brahmin, fire, and water. After giving grass, water, honey, and parched grain to the cows, and after giving unbroken grains, flowers, nāndīmukha offerings, and desired fruits to the brahmins seated on their seats, with water poured before them, one should salute them, sip water again, and have blessings recited.

children.text: tataḥ puṇyāhaśabdena gobrāhmaṇaṃ samanuvartamānā pradakṣiṇaṃ praviśet sūtikāgāram
children.translated_text: Then, while the sound of "this is an auspicious day" is being uttered, and while she follows the cow and the brahmin, she should enter the birthing room clockwise.
Staying there, she should await the time of delivery.

children.text: tasyāstu khalvimāni liṅgāni prajananakālamabhito bhavanti tadyathā klamo gātrāṇāṃ glānir ānanasya akṣṇoḥ śaithilyaṃ vimuktabandhanatvamiva vakṣasaḥ kukṣer avasraṃsanam adhogurutvaṃ vaṅkṣaṇavastikaṭīkukṣipārśvapṛṣṭhanistodaḥ yoneḥ prasravaṇam anannābhilāṣaśceti tato'nantaramāvīnāṃ prādurbhāvaḥ prasekaśca garbhodakasya ||
children.translated_text: These, then, are the signs that appear in her around the time of giving birth: fatigue of the limbs, pallor or languor of the face, slackness of the eyes, a feeling as if the binding of the chest were loosened, descent of the abdomen, heaviness downward, stabbing pain in the groin, bladder, hips, abdomen, sides, and back, discharge from the vagina, and lack of desire for food. Immediately after this comes the arising of the birth-pains and the flowing of the amniotic fluid.
When the birth-pains arise, one should prepare a bed on the ground, furnished with a soft covering.
She should sit down upon it.

children.text: tāṃ tataḥ samantataḥ parivārya yathoktaguṇāḥ striyaḥ paryupāsīrann āśvāsantyo vāgbhir grāhiṇīyābhiḥ sāntvanīyābhiśca ||
children.translated_text: Then women with the qualities already stated should surround her on all sides and attend upon her, encouraging her with words that help her grasp what to do and that console her.

children.text: sā ced āvībhiḥ saṃkliśyamānā na prajāyetāthaināṃ brūyāt uttiṣṭha musalamanyataraṃ gṛhṇīṣva anenaitad ulūkhalaṃ dhānyapūrṇaṃ muhurmuhur abhijahi muhurmuhur avajṛmbhasva caṅkramasva cāntarāntareti evamupadiśantyeke
children.translated_text: If, while being distressed by the pains, she does not give birth, then one should say to her: "Rise. Take one of the pestles. With this strike again and again that mortar full of grain. Yawn again and again, and walk about from time to time." Some teach in this way.
The blessed <s>Ātreya</s> says that this is not so.

children.text: dāruṇavyāyāmavarjanaṃ hi garbhiṇyāḥ satatam upadiśyate viśeṣataśca prajananakāle pracalitasarvadhātudoṣāyāḥ sukumāryā nāryā musalavyāyāmasamīrito vāyurantaraṃ labdhvā prāṇān hiṃsyāt duṣpratīkāratamā hi tasmin kāle viśeṣeṇa bhavati garbhiṇī tasmānmusalagrahaṇaṃ parihāryamṛṣayo manyante jṛmbhaṇaṃ caṅkramaṇaṃ ca punaranuṣṭheyam iti
children.translated_text: For avoidance of harsh exertion is always prescribed for a pregnant woman, and especially at the time of delivery, when all her <s>dhātus</s> and <s>doṣas</s> are disturbed. If <s>vāyu</s>, stirred up by exercise with the pestle in a delicate woman, finds an opening within, it may injure her vital breaths. At that time in particular the pregnant woman is very difficult to treat. Therefore the seers hold that taking up the pestle is to be avoided, while yawning and walking about are still to be practiced.

children.text: athāsyai dadyāt kuṣṭhailālāṅgalikīvacācitrakacirabilvacavyacūrṇam upaghrātuṃ sā tanmuhurmuhurupajighret tathā bhūrjapatradhūmaṃ śiṃśapāsāradhūmaṃ vā
children.translated_text: Then one should give her powder of kuṣṭha, elā, lāṅgalikī, vacā, citraka, cirabilva, and cavya to smell; she should smell it repeatedly. Likewise she may smell the smoke of birch bark or the smoke of the heartwood of śiṃśapā.

children.text: tasyāścāntarāntarā kaṭīpārśvapṛṣṭhasakthideśān īṣad uṣṇena tailenābhyajyānusukham avamṛdnīyāt
children.translated_text: At intervals one should anoint the regions of her hips, sides, back, and thighs with slightly warm oil and gently rub them in a way that is comfortable.
By this procedure the fetus turns downward.

children.text: sa yadā jānīyādvimucya hṛdayamudaramasyāstvāviśati vastiśiro'vagṛhṇāti tvarayantyenāmāvyaḥ parivartate'dho garbha iti asyāmavasthāyāṃ paryaṅkamenām āropya pravāhayitumupakrameta
children.translated_text: When one knows that it has left her heart and abdomen, entered the region of the bladder, taken hold of the bladder-head, is urged on by the pains, and has turned downward, then in this condition one should place her on the couch and begin to make her bear down.
And a woman favorable to her should murmur this mantra in her ear:
Earth, water, space, fire, wind, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Prajāpati</s>,

children.text: sagarbhāṃ tvāṃ sadā pāntu vaiśalyaṃ ca diśantu te
children.translated_text: may they always protect you together with the fetus, and may they grant you freedom from the dart.
Give birth, auspicious-faced one, without distress to an undistressed child,
a son with the brilliance of <s>Kārttikeya</s>, protected by the <s>Kārttikeyas</s>.
Thus.

children.text: tāścaināṃ yathoktaguṇāḥ striyo'nuśiṣyuḥ anāgatāvīr mā pravāhiṣṭhāḥ yā hyanāgatāvīḥ pravāhate vyarthamevāsyāstat karma bhavati prajā cāsyā vikṛtā vikṛtimāpannā ca śvāsakāsaśoṣaplīhaprasaktā vā bhavati
children.translated_text: And women possessing the qualities already described should instruct her: 'Do not bear down before the fetus has come. For a woman who bears down before it has come makes that action of hers entirely fruitless, and her offspring becomes deformed, falls into deformity, or is afflicted with dyspnea, cough, consumption, or enlargement of the spleen.'

children.text: yathā hi kṣavathūdgāravātamūtrapurīṣavegān prayatamāno'pyaprāptakālānna labhate kṛcchreṇa vāpyavāpnoti tathānāgatakālaṃ garbhamapi pravāhamāṇā yathā caiṣāmeva kṣavathvādīnāṃ saṃdhāraṇam upaghātāyopapadyate tathā prāptakālasya garbhasyāpravāhaṇamiti
children.translated_text: For just as, even when one tries, one does not obtain the urges for sneezing, belching, flatus, urine, or feces before their proper time, or obtains them only with difficulty, so too with a fetus whose time has not yet come, if she bears down. And just as the restraint of those very urges beginning with sneezing leads to injury, so too does failure to bear down when the fetus has reached its proper time.
She should be told, 'Do as instructed.'

children.text: tathā ca kurvatī śanaiḥ pūrvaṃ pravāheta tato'nantaraṃ balavattaram
children.translated_text: And doing so, she should first bear down gently, and immediately afterward more forcefully.

children.text: tasyāṃ ca pravāhamāṇāyāṃ striyaḥ śabdaṃ kuryuḥ prajātā prajātā dhanyaṃ dhanyaṃ putram iti
children.translated_text: While she is bearing down, the women should make a cry: 'Born! Born! Blessed, blessed son!'
In that way, through joy, her vital breaths are also nourished.

children.text: yadā ca prajātā syāttadaivainām avekṣeta kācidasyā aparā prapannā na veti
children.translated_text: And when she has given birth, one should at once examine her to see whether some placenta of hers has come down or not.

children.text: tasyāścedaparā prapannā syādathaināmanyatamā strī dakṣiṇena pāṇinā nābherupariṣṭādbalavannipīḍya savyena pāṇinā pṛṣṭhata upasaṃgṛhya tāṃ sunirdhūtaṃ nirdhunuyāt
children.translated_text: If her placenta has not come down, then one of the women should press forcefully above her navel with the right hand, support her from behind with the left hand, and shake her thoroughly.
Then she should strike her hips with her heel.
She should grasp her buttocks and press them with firm pressure.
Then she should rub the woman's throat and palate with a braid of hair.
And she should fumigate her vagina with birch bark, glass, a jewel, and the cast-off skin of a snake.

children.text: kuṣṭhatālīśakalkaṃ balvajayūṣe maireyasurāmaṇḍe tīkṣṇe kaulatthe vā yūṣe maṇḍūkaparṇīpippalīsampāke vā saṃplāvya pāyayedenām
children.translated_text: One should soak a paste of <s>kuṣṭha</s> and <s>tālīśa</s> in a decoction of <s>balvaja</s>, in the sharp sediment of <s>maireya</s> liquor or <s>surā</s>, in horse-gram soup, or in a decoction of <s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s> and <s>pippalī</s>, and make her drink it.

children.text: tathā sūkṣmailākilimakuṣṭhanāgaraviḍaṅgapippalīkālāgurucavyacitrakopakuñcikākalkaṃ kharavṛṣabhasya vā jīvato dakṣiṇaṃ karṇamutkṛtya dṛṣadi jarjarīkṛtya balvajakvāthādīnām āplāvanānām anyatame prakṣipyāplāvya muhūrtasthitam uddhṛtya tadāplāvanaṃ pāyayedenām
children.translated_text: Likewise, one should make a fine paste of <s>elā</s>, <s>kilima</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>nāgara</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, black <s>aguru</s>, <s>cavya</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>upakuñcikā</s>; or else cut off the right ear of a living donkey or bull, crush it on a stone, place it in one of the soaking liquids such as decoction of <s>balvaja</s>, leave it soaked for a <s>muhūrta</s>, remove it, and make her drink that infusion.
And one should have her take a tampon of oil prepared with <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>madana</s>, and <s>hiṅgu</s>.
And with this same oil one should give her an unctuous enema.

With these same soaking liquids, supplemented with <s>phala</s>, <s>jīmūta</s>, <s>ikṣvāku</s>, <s>dhāmārgava</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>kṛtavedhana</s>, and <s>hastipippalī</s>, one should give her a decoction enema.

children.text: tadāsthāpanamasyāḥ saha vātamūtrapurīṣair nirharatyaparāmāsaktāṃ vāyor evāpratilomagatvāt
children.translated_text: That decoction enema draws out her retained placenta together with flatus, urine, and feces, because <s>vāta</s> is moving in its proper, non-reversed direction.
For the placenta obstructs flatus, urine, feces, and the other internal and external pathways.

children.text: tasyāstu khalvaparāyāḥ prapatanārthe karmaṇi kriyamāṇe jātamātrasyaiva kumārasya kāryāṇyetāni karmāṇi bhavanti tadyathā aśmanoḥ saṃghaṭṭanaṃ karṇayor mūle śītodakenoṣṇodakena vā mukhapariṣekaḥ tathā sa kleśavihatān prāṇān punarlabheta
children.translated_text: But while procedures are being performed for that placenta to fall, these procedures are to be done for the child immediately after birth: striking two stones together at the roots of his ears, and sprinkling his face with cold water or warm water, so that he may regain the vital breaths impaired by distress.

children.text: kṛṣṇakapālikāśūrpeṇa cainamabhiniṣpuṇīyur yadyaceṣṭaḥ syād yāvat prāṇānāṃ pratyāgamanam tattat sarvameva kāryam
children.translated_text: And if he is without movement, they should fan him with a black potsherd and a winnowing basket. Whatever is needed until the return of the vital breaths, all of that should be done.

children.text: tataḥ pratyāgataprāṇaṃ prakṛtibhūtam abhisamīkṣya snānodakagrahaṇābhyām upapādayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, when one has observed that his vital breaths have returned and that he is in his natural condition, one should provide for bathing and taking up water.
After that one should begin wiping his palate, lips, throat, and tongue with a finger whose nail has been well pared and which is furnished with a well-washed cotton pad and plug.

children.text: prathamaṃ pramārjitāsyasya cāsya śirastālu kārpāsapicunā snehagarbheṇa pratisaṃchādayet
children.translated_text: When his mouth has first been wiped, one should cover his head and palate with a cotton plug containing an unctuous substance.
Immediately after that, one should cause him to vomit by means of ghee mixed with rock salt.
Then comes the preparation of the umbilical cord.

children.text: atastasyāḥ kalpanavidhim upadekṣyāmaḥ nābhibandhanāt prabhṛtyaṣṭāṅgulam abhijñānaṃ kṛtvā chedanāvakāśasya dvayorantarayoḥ śanairgṛhītvā tīkṣṇena raukmarājatāyasānāṃ chedanānām anyatamenārdhadhāreṇa chedayet
children.translated_text: Next we shall teach the procedure for preparing it. From the tying at the navel one should mark a measure of eight finger-breadths as the place for cutting; gently taking hold of the space between the two points, one should cut it with a sharp half-edged cutting instrument made of gold, silver, or iron.
One should tie its end with a thread and let it hang loosely around his neck.

children.text: tasya cen nābhiḥ pacyeta tāṃ lodhramadhukapriyaṅgusuradāruharidrākalkasiddhena tailenābhyajyāt eṣām eva tailauṣadhānāṃ cūrṇenāvacūrṇayet
children.translated_text: If his navel suppurates, one should anoint it with oil prepared with pastes of <s>lodhra</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>suradāru</s>, and <s>haridrā</s>, and dust it with powder made from these same oil-drugs.
Thus the procedure for preparing the umbilical cord has been properly stated.
For if the umbilical cord is improperly prepared, there is danger from disorders called <s>āyāma</s>, <s>vyāyāma</s>, <s>uttuṇḍitā</s>, <s>piṇḍalikā</s>, <s>vināmikā</s>, and <s>vijṛmbhikā</s>.

In those cases one should treat with non-burning oil massage, rubbing, and sprinkling that pacify <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, and with ghees, after considering whether the condition is heavy or light.
After this, the <s>jātakarma</s>, the birth rite, should be performed for the child.

children.text: tadyathā madhusarpiṣī mantropamantrite yathāmnāyaṃ prathamaṃ prāśituṃ dadyāt
children.translated_text: That is as follows: honey and ghee, consecrated with mantras according to the received teaching, should first be given to him to taste.

children.text: stanamata ūrdhvametenaiva vidhinā dakṣiṇaṃ pātuṃ purastāt prayacchet
children.translated_text: Afterward the right breast, consecrated by this same procedure, should first be offered for him to drink.
Then one should place at his head a water pot consecrated with mantras.

children.text: athāsya rakṣāṃ vidadhyāt ādānīkhadirakarkandhupīluparūṣakaśākhābhirasyā gṛhaṃ samantataḥ parivārayet
children.translated_text: Then one should provide protection for him: with branches of <s>ādānī</s>, <s>khadira</s>, <s>karkandhu</s>, <s>pīlu</s>, and <s>parūṣaka</s>, one should enclose her house on every side.
And on every side of the birthing room one should scatter white mustard, flax seeds, grains of rice, and <s>kaṇakaṇikā</s>.

children.text: tathā taṇḍulabalihomaḥ satatam ubhayakālaṃ kriyeta ā nāmakarmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise, an offering of rice, a <s>bali</s> offering, and a fire-oblation should constantly be performed at both times of day until the naming ceremony.

children.text: dvāre ca musalaṃ dehalīmanu tiraścīnaṃ nyaset
children.translated_text: At the door one should place a pestle crosswise along the threshold.

children.text: vacākuṣṭhakṣaumakahiṅgusarṣapātasīlaśunakaṇakaṇikānāṃ rakṣoghnasamākhyātānāṃ cauṣadhīnāṃ poṭṭalikāṃ baddhvā sūtikāgārasyottaradehalyāmavasṛjet tathā sūtikāyāḥ kaṇṭhe saputrāyāḥ sthālyudakakumbhaparyaṅkeṣvapi tathaiva ca dvayordvārapakṣayoḥ
children.translated_text: One should tie up a small bundle of <s>vacā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>kṣaumaka</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s>, mustard, flax, garlic, and <s>kaṇakaṇikā</s>, herbs known as demon-dispelling, and place it on the northern threshold of the birthing room; likewise on the neck of the puerperal woman together with her son, and also on the cooking vessel, water jar, and bed, and in the same way on the two door leaves.

children.text: kaṇakakaṇṭakendhanavān agnis tindukakāṣṭhendhanaś cāgniḥ sūtikāgārasyābhyantarato nityaṃ syāt
children.translated_text: Within the birthing room there should always be a fire supplied with <s>kaṇaka</s> thorns as fuel, and also a fire supplied with <s>tinduka</s> wood as fuel.

children.text: striyaścaināṃ yathoktaguṇāḥ suhṛdaś cānuścānujāgṛyur daśāhaṃ dvādaśāhaṃ vā
children.translated_text: Women having the qualities already stated, and friends as well, should keep watch over her for ten days or for twelve days.
That house should be made full of uninterrupted gifts, auspicious blessings, praise, songs, and instrumental music, with pure food and drink, and with people who are attached to her and delighted.

children.text: brāhmaṇaścātharvavedavit satatam ubhayakālaṃ śāntiṃ juhuyāt svastyayanārthaṃ kumārasya tathā sūtikāyāḥ
children.translated_text: And a brahmin learned in the <s>Atharvaveda</s> should constantly, at both times of day, offer a pacifying oblation for the welfare of the child and of the puerperal woman.
This protective procedure has been stated.

children.text: sūtikāṃ tu khalu bubhukṣitāṃ viditvā snehaṃ pāyayeta paramayā śaktyā sarpistailaṃ vasāṃ majjānaṃ vā sātmyībhāvam abhisamīkṣya pippalīpippalīmūlacavyacitrakaśṛṅgaveracūrṇasahitam
children.translated_text: But when one knows that the puerperal woman is hungry, one should make her drink a <s>sneha</s> (unctuous substance), to the utmost of her capacity: ghee, oil, fat, or marrow, after considering what has become suitable to her, together with powders of <s>pippalī</s>, <s>pippalīmūla</s>, <s>cavya</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>śṛṅgavera</s>.

children.text: snehaṃ pītavatyāśca sarpistailābhyām abhyajya veṣṭayedudaraṃ mahatācchena vāsasā tathā tasyā na vāyurudare vikṛtim utpādayatyanavakāśatvāt
children.translated_text: After she has drunk the <s>sneha</s>, one should anoint her with ghee and oil and bind her abdomen with a large clean cloth; in that way <s>vāyu</s> does not produce a disorder in her abdomen, because there is no open space.

children.text: jīrṇe tu snehe pippalyādibhireva siddhāṃ yavāgūṃ susnigdhāṃ dravāṃ mātraśaḥ pāyayet
children.translated_text: When the <s>sneha</s> has been digested, one should give her, in measured amounts, a gruel prepared with <s>pippalī</s> and the other drugs, very unctuous and liquid.

children.text: ubhayataḥkālaṃ coṣṇodakena ca pariṣecayet prāk snehayavāgūpānābhyām
children.translated_text: At both times of day one should also pour warm water over her before the drinking of the <s>sneha</s> and the gruel.
Having cared for her in this way for five nights or for seven nights, one should gradually nourish and restore her.
This much is the regimen of healthy conduct for a puerperal woman.

children.text: tasyāstu khalu yo vyādhirutpadyate sa kṛcchrasādhyo bhavatyasādhyo vā garbhavṛddhikṣayitaśithilasarvadhātutvāt pravāhaṇavedanākledanaraktaniḥsrutiviśeṣaśūnyaśarīratvācca tasmāttāṃ yathoktena vidhinopacaret bhautikajīvanīyabṛṃhaṇīyamadhuravātaharasiddhair abhyaṅgotsādanapariṣekāvagāhanānnapānavidhibhir viśeṣataś copacaret viśeṣato hi śūnyaśarīrāḥ striyaḥ prajātā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: But any disease that arises in her is hard to cure or else incurable, because all her <s>dhātus</s> have been depleted and loosened by the growth of the fetus, and because her body has been emptied in a special way by straining, pain, moistening, and the outflow of blood. Therefore one should treat her by the procedure stated, and should treat her especially with methods of massage, rubbing, pouring, bathing, food, and drink prepared with the elemental, life-promoting, nourishing, sweet, and <s>vāta</s>-pacifying groups. For women who have given birth are especially emptied in body.

children.text: daśame tvahani saputrā strī sarvagandhauṣadhair gaurasarṣapalodhraiśca snātā laghvahataśucivastraṃ paridhāya pavitreṣṭalaghuvicitrabhūṣaṇavatī ca saṃspṛśya maṅgalānyucitām arcayitvā ca devatāṃ śikhinaḥ śuklavāsaso 'vyaṅgāṃśca brāhmaṇān svasti vācayitvā kumāramahatānāṃ ca vāsasāṃ saṃcaye prākśirasam udakśirasaṃ vā saṃveśya devatāpūrvaṃ dvijātibhyaḥ praṇamatītyuktvā kumārasya pitā dve nāmanī kārayennākṣatrikaṃ nāmābhiprāyikaṃ ca
children.translated_text: But on the tenth day the woman, together with her son, having bathed with all fragrant herbs, white mustard, and <s>lodhra</s>, wearing light, new, clean clothing, adorned with pure, desired, light, and varied ornaments, having touched auspicious objects, worshipped the appropriate deity, and had auspicious words spoken by brahmins with topknots, dressed in white, and free from deformity, should lay the child with his head toward the east or toward the north on a heap of large new garments. After saying, 'Bow first to the deities and to the twice-born,' the father of the child should have two names made for him: a name according to the lunar mansion and a preferred name.

children.text: tatrābhiprāyikaṃ ghoṣavadādyantasthāntam ūṣmāntaṃ vāvṛddhaṃ tripuruṣānūkam anavapratiṣṭhitaṃ nākṣatrikaṃ tu nakṣatradevatāsamānākhyaṃ dvyakṣaraṃ caturakṣaraṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: Among these, the preferred name should be sonorous, ending in a semivowel or in a sibilant, without <s>vṛddhi</s>, following three generations, and not newly established; but the name according to the lunar mansion should have the same designation as the deity of the lunar mansion, and should be of two syllables or four syllables.

children.text: vṛtte ca nāmakarmaṇi kumāraṃ parīkṣitumupakrametāyuṣaḥ pramāṇajñānahetoḥ
children.translated_text: And when the naming ceremony has been completed, one should begin to examine the child, in order to know the measure of his lifespan.
In this connection, these are the marks of children who possess long life.

children.text: tadyathā ekaikajā mṛdavo'lpāḥ snigdhāḥ subaddhamūlāḥ kṛṣṇāḥ keśāḥ praśasyante sthirā bahalā tvak prakṛtyātisampannam īṣatpramāṇātivṛttam anurūpam ātapatropamaṃ śiraḥ vyūḍhaṃ dṛḍhaṃ samaṃ suśliṣṭaśaṅkhasandhyūrdhvavyañjanasampannam upacitaṃ valibham ardhacandrākṛti lalāṭaṃ bahalau vipulasamapīṭhau samau nīcair vṛddhau pṛṣṭhato'vanatau suśliṣṭakarṇaputrakau mahāchidrau karṇau īṣat pralambinyāvasaṃgate same saṃhate mahatyau bhruvau same samāhitadarśane vyaktabhāgavibhāge balavatī tejasopapanne svaṅgāpāṅge cakṣuṣī ṛjvī mahocchvāsā vaṃśasampanneṣadavanatāgrā nāsikā mahadṛjusuniviṣṭadantam āsyam āyāmavistāropapannā ślakṣṇā tanvī prakṛtivarṇayuktā jihvā ślakṣṇaṃ yuktopacayam ūṣmopapannaṃ raktaṃ tālu mahānadīnaḥ snigdho 'nunādī gambhīrasamuttho dhīraḥ svaraḥ nātisthūlau nātikṛśau vistāropapannāvāsyapracchādanau raktāvoṣṭhau mahatyau hanū vṛttā nātimahatī grīvā vyūḍhamupacitam uraḥ gūḍhaṃ jatru pṛṣṭhavaṃśaśca viprakṛṣṭāntarau stanau asaṃpātinī sthire pārśve vṛttaparipūrṇāyatau bāhū sakthinī aṅgulayaśca mahadupacitaṃ pāṇipādaṃ sthirā vṛttāḥ snigdhāstāmrāstuṅgāḥ kūrmākārāḥ karajāḥ pradakṣiṇāvartā sotsaṅgā ca nābhiḥ urastribhāgahīnā samā samupacitamāṃsā kaṭī vṛttau sthiropacitamāṃsau nātyunnatau nātyavanatau sphicau anupūrvaṃ vṛttāvupacayayuktāvūrū nātyupacite nātyapacite eṇīpade pragūḍhasirāsthisaṃdhī jaṅghe nātyupacitau nātyapacitau gulphau pūrvopadiṣṭaguṇau pādau kūrmākārau prakṛtiyuktāni vātamūtrapurīṣaguhyāni tathā svaprajāgaraṇāyāsasmitaruditastanagrahaṇāni yacca kiṃcid anyad apyanuktam asti tadapi sarvaṃ prakṛtisampannam iṣṭaṃ viparītaṃ punaraniṣṭam
children.translated_text: The marks are as follows. Hairs that grow singly, are soft, few, unctuous, well-rooted, and black are praised. The skin should be firm and thick. The head should be naturally well endowed, slightly beyond the normal measure, proportionate, and like an umbrella. The forehead should be broad, firm, even, with well-joined temporal joints, furnished with upward marks, full, folded, and shaped like a half-moon. The ears should be thick, broad, with equal bases, even, grown low, bent backward, with well-joined lobes, and with large openings. The eyebrows should be slightly hanging, not joined together, even, compact, and large. The eyes should be equal, steady in gaze, with their parts clearly divided, strong, endowed with brilliance, and beautiful in the main and outer corners. The nose should be straight, with ample breathing, with a good bridge, and with its tip slightly bent down. The mouth should have large, straight, well-set teeth. The tongue should have proper length and breadth, be smooth, thin, and of its natural color. The palate should be smooth, properly built up, warm, and red. The voice should be powerful in resonance, unctuous, echoing, arising deep, and steady. The lips should be neither too thick nor too thin, sufficiently broad, covering the mouth, and red. The jaws should be large. The neck should be round and not too large. The chest should be broad and full; the clavicles and spine should be concealed. The breasts should be far apart. The sides should not collapse and should be firm. The arms, thighs, and fingers should be round, full, and long. The hands and feet should be large and full. The nails should be firm, round, unctuous, coppery, raised, and shaped like a tortoise. The navel should turn clockwise and have a depression. The waist should be smaller than the chest by a third, even, and well furnished with flesh. The buttocks should be round, firm, fleshy, neither too high nor too low. The thighs should be gradually rounded and well nourished. The shanks should be neither overdeveloped nor underdeveloped, like those of an antelope, with veins, bones, and joints well hidden. The ankles should be neither overdeveloped nor underdeveloped. The feet should have the qualities stated before. The organs of flatus, urine, feces, and reproduction should be tortoise-like and natural. Likewise sleep, waking, exertion, smiling, crying, taking the breast, and whatever else has not been stated should all be naturally well formed. The opposite is undesirable.
Thus ends the marks of long life.
Now we shall teach the examination of a wet nurse.

children.text: atha brūyāt dhātrīmānaya samānavarṇāṃ yauvanasthāṃ nibhṛtāmanāturām avyaṅgām avyasanām avirūpām ajugupsitāṃ deśajātīyām akṣudrām akṣudrakarmiṇīṃ kule jātāṃ vatsalāmarogāṃ jīvadvatsāṃ puṃvatsāṃ dogdhrīm apramattām anuccāraśāyinīm anantyāvasāyinīṃ kuśalopacārāṃ śucim aśucidveṣiṇīṃ stanastanyasaṃpadupetāmiti ||
children.translated_text: Then he should say: "Bring a wet nurse of the same class and complexion, established in youth, restrained, free from illness, without blemish, without bad habits, not deformed, not repulsive, born in the same region, not low, not engaged in low acts, born in a good family, affectionate toward children, healthy, whose own child is living, who has borne a male child, who gives milk, is not careless, does not sleep in filth, does not dwell among outcastes, is skilled in care, clean, averse to uncleanness, and endowed with good breasts and good milk."

children.text: tatreyaṃ stanasaṃpat nātyūrdhvau nātilambāvanatikṛśāvanatipīnau yuktapippalakau sukhaprapānau ceti stanasaṃpat ||
children.translated_text: In this matter, this is excellence of the breasts: they are not too high, not too pendulous, not too thin, not too full, have suitable nipples, and are easy to drink from. This is excellence of the breasts.

children.text: stanyasaṃpattu prakṛtivarṇagandharasasparśam udapātre ca duhyamānam udakaṃ vyeti prakṛtibhūtatvāt tat puṣṭikaramārogyakaraṃ ceti stanyasaṃpat ||
children.translated_text: Excellence of breast milk is as follows: it has its natural color, smell, taste, and touch; when milked into a vessel of water, it disperses in the water because it is in its natural state. That milk is nourishing and health-giving. This is excellence of breast milk.
Anything otherwise should be known as impaired.

children.text: tasya viśeṣāḥ śyāvāruṇavarṇaṃ kaṣāyānurasaṃ viśadamanālakṣyagandhaṃ rūkṣaṃ dravaṃ phenilaṃ laghvatṛptikaraṃ karśanaṃ vātavikārāṇāṃ kartṛ vātopasṛṣṭaṃ kṣīramabhijñeyaṃ kṛṣṇanīlapītatāmrāvabhāsaṃ tiktāmlakaṭukānurasaṃ kuṇaparudhiragandhi bhṛśoṣṇaṃ pittavikārāṇāṃ kartṛ ca pittopasṛṣṭaṃ kṣīram abhijñeyam atyarthaśuklam atimādhuryopapannaṃ lavaṇānurasaṃ ghṛtatailavasāmajjagandhi picchilaṃ tantumad udakapātre 'vasīdacchleṣmavikārāṇāṃ kartṛ śleṣmopasṛṣṭaṃ kṣīramabhijñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Its specific varieties are these. Milk affected by <s>vāta</s> should be recognized as dusky-red in color, with an astringent aftertaste, clear, without perceptible odor, rough, thin, frothy, light, unsatisfying, wasting, and productive of <s>vāta</s> disorders. Milk affected by <s>pitta</s> should be recognized as having black, blue, yellow, or coppery luster, a bitter, sour, and pungent aftertaste, the smell of a corpse or blood, very hot, and productive of <s>pitta</s> disorders. Milk affected by <s>śleṣman</s> should be recognized as extremely white, endowed with excessive sweetness, with a salty aftertaste, smelling of ghee, oil, fat, and marrow, slimy, stringy, sinking in a vessel of water, and productive of <s>śleṣman</s> disorders.

children.text: teṣāṃ tu trayāṇāmapi kṣīradoṣāṇāṃ prativiśeṣam abhisamīkṣya yathāsvaṃ yathādoṣaṃ ca vamanavirecanāsthāpanānuvāsanāni vibhajya kṛtāni praśamanāya bhavanti
children.translated_text: For all three of these milk defects, emesis, purgation, evacuative enemas, and unctuous enemas, performed separately after examining each particular condition and according to its own <s>doṣa</s>, serve for pacification.

The rule for drink and food for a woman whose milk is vitiated should consist chiefly of barley, wheat, <s>śāli</s> rice, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, mung, <s>hareṇuka</s>, horse gram, <s>surā</s>, <s>sauvīraka</s>, <s>maireya</s>, <s>medaka</s>, garlic, and <s>karañja</s>.
And, after repeatedly considering the specific milk defects, the corresponding regimen should be carried out.

children.text: pāṭhāmahauṣadhasuradārumustamūrvāguḍūcīvatsakaphalakirātatiktakakaṭukarohiṇīsārivākaṣāyāṇāṃ ca pānaṃ praśasyate tathānyeṣāṃ tiktakaṣāyakaṭukamadhurāṇāṃ dravyāṇāṃ prayogaḥ kṣīravikāraviśeṣān abhisamīkṣya mātrāṃ kālaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Drinking decoctions of <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>mahauṣadha</s>, <s>suradāru</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>vatsaka</s> fruit, <s>kirātatiktaka</s>, <s>kaṭukarohiṇī</s>, and <s>sārivā</s> is praised; likewise the use of other bitter, astringent, pungent, and sweet substances, after examining the specific disorders of the milk, along with the proper dose and time.
Thus ends the purifications of milk.

children.text: kṣīrajananāni tu madyāni sīdhuvarjyāni grāmyānūpaudakāni ca śākadhānyamāṃsāni dravamadhurāmlalavaṇabhūyiṣṭhāś cāhārāḥ kṣīriṇyaś cauṣadhayaḥ kṣīrapānam anāyāsaśca vīraṇaṣaṣṭikaśālīkṣuvālikādarbhakuśakāśagundretkaṭamūlakaṣāyāṇāṃ na pānamiti kṣīrajananāni ||
children.translated_text: The producers of milk are liquors other than <s>sīdhu</s>, and foods consisting mostly of vegetable dishes, grains, and meats of domestic, marsh, and aquatic animals, rich in liquid, sweet, sour, and salty qualities; also milky herbs, drinking milk, freedom from exertion, and not drinking decoctions of the roots of <s>vīraṇa</s>, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, <s>śāli</s>, sugarcane, <s>vālikā</s>, <s>darbha</s>, <s>kuśa</s>, <s>kāśa</s>, <s>gundrā</s>, and <s>utkaṭa</s>. These are the producers of milk.

children.text: dhātrī tu yadā svādubahulaśuddhadugdhā syāttadā snātānuliptā śuklavastraṃ paridhāyaindrīṃ brāhmīṃ śatavīryāṃ sahasravīryām amoghām avyathāṃ śivām ariṣṭāṃ vāṭyapuṣpīṃ viṣvaksenakāntāṃ vā bibhratyoṣadhiṃ kumāraṃ prāṅmukhaṃ prathamaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ stanaṃ pāyayet
children.translated_text: But when the nurse has abundant, sweet, pure milk, then, bathed and anointed, wearing a white garment, and carrying the herb <s>Indrī</s>, <s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Śatavīryā</s>, <s>Sahasravīryā</s>, <s>Amoghā</s>, <s>Avyathā</s>, <s>Śivā</s>, <s>Ariṣṭā</s>, <s>Vāṭyapuṣpī</s>, or <s>Viṣvaksenakāntā</s>, she should first give the child, facing east, the right breast to drink.
Thus the duty of the nurse.

children.text: ato'nantaraṃ kumārāgāravidhim anuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ vāstuvidyākuśalaḥ praśastaṃ ramyam atamaskaṃ nivātaṃ pravātaikadeśaṃ dṛḍham apagataśvāpadapaśudaṃṣṭrimūṣikapataṅgaṃ suvibhaktasalilolūkhalamūtravarcaḥsthānasnānabhūmimahānasam ṛtusukhaṃ yathartuśayanāsanāstaraṇasampannaṃ kuryāt tathā suvihitarakṣāvidhānabalimaṅgalahomaprāyaścittaṃ śucivṛddhavaidyānuraktajanasampūrṇam
children.translated_text: After this we shall explain the procedure for the infant's room. A person skilled in building science should make it auspicious, pleasant, free from darkness, sheltered from wind but with one airy part, sturdy, free from beasts, domestic animals, fanged creatures, mice, and insects, and well divided with places for water, mortar, urine and feces, bathing area, and kitchen; comfortable in the seasons and furnished, according to the season, with beds, seats, and coverings. It should likewise have well-arranged provisions for protection, offerings, auspicious rites, oblations, and expiations, and be filled with clean elders, physicians, and affectionate attendants.
Thus the procedure for the infant's room.

children.text: śayanāsanāstaraṇaprāvaraṇāni kumārasya mṛdulaghuśucisugandhīni syuḥ svedamalajantumanti mūtrapurīṣopasṛṣṭāni ca varjyāni syuḥ asati saṃbhave'nyeṣāṃ tānyeva ca suprakṣālitopadhānāni sudhūpitāni śuddhaśuṣkāṇyupayogaṃ gaccheyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The child's beds, seats, bedding, and covers should be soft, light, clean, and fragrant. Those containing sweat, dirt, or vermin, and those soiled with urine or feces, should be avoided. If other ones are not available, those very articles may be used after they have been thoroughly washed, furnished with clean pillows, well fumigated, purified, and dried.

children.text: dhūpanāni punarvāsasāṃ śayanāstaraṇaprāvaraṇānāṃ ca yavasarṣapātasīhiṅgugugguluvacācorakavayaḥsthāgolomījaṭilāpalaṅkaṣāśokarohiṇīsarpanirmokāṇi ghṛtayuktāni syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The fumigants for clothing, beds, bedding, and covers should be barley, mustard, flax, asafoetida, guggulu, <s>vacā</s>, <s>coraka</s>, <s>vayaḥsthā</s>, <s>golomī</s>, <s>jaṭilā</s>, <s>palaṅkaṣā</s>, <s>aśokarohiṇī</s>, and sloughed snakeskin, mixed with ghee.

children.text: maṇayaśca dhāraṇīyāḥ kumārasya khaḍgarurugavayavṛṣabhāṇāṃ jīvatāmeva dakṣiṇebhyo viṣāṇebhyo'grāṇi gṛhītāni syuḥ aindryādyāścauṣadhayo jīvakarṣabhakau ca yāni cānyānyapi brāhmaṇāḥ praśaṃseyur atharvavedavidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The child should also wear jewels and amulets: the tips taken from the right horns of living rhinoceroses, <s>ruru</s> deer, wild oxen, and bulls; the herbs beginning with <s>Aindrī</s>; <s>jīvaka</s> and <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>; and whatever other things brahmins learned in the <s>Atharvaveda</s> recommend.

children.text: krīḍanakāni khalu kumārasya vicitrāṇi ghoṣavantyabhirāmāṇi cāgurūṇi cātīkṣṇāgrāṇi cānāsyapraveśīni cāprāṇaharāṇi cāvitrāsanāni syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The child's toys should be varied, sounding, pleasing, not heavy, without sharp points, unable to enter the mouth, not life-destroying, and not frightening.
For frightening him is not good.

children.text: tasmāttasmin rudatyabhuñjāne vānyatra vidheyatām āgacchati rākṣasapiśācapūtanādyānāṃ nāmānyāhvayatā kumārasya vitrāsanārthaṃ nāmagrahaṇaṃ na kāryaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, when he is crying, not eating, or being brought under control in some other matter, one should not mention names of <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, and the like in order to frighten the child.

children.text: yadi tvāturyaṃ kiṃcit kumāramāgacchet tat prakṛtinimittapūrvarūpaliṅgopaśayaviśeṣais tattvato 'nubudhya sarvaviśeṣān āturauṣadhadeśakālāśrayānavekṣamāṇaś cikitsitum ārabhetainaṃ madhuramṛdulaghusurabhiśītaśaṃkaraṃ karma pravartayan
children.translated_text: But if some illness should come upon the child, then, after understanding it truly by its constitution, cause, prodromal signs, marks, and special response to treatment, one should begin to treat him, not disregarding all the particular factors depending on the patient, medicine, place, and time, while applying measures that are sweet, gentle, light, fragrant, cool, and soothing.
For in this way children become accustomed to what is wholesome.
Thus they obtain well-being for a long time.

children.text: aroge tvarogavṛttam ātiṣṭheddeśakālātmaguṇaviparyayeṇa vartamānaḥ krameṇāsātmyāni parivartyopayuñjānaḥ sarvāṇyahitāni varjayet
children.translated_text: When he is free from disease, one should follow the regimen for health, acting according to changes in place, time, and one's own constitution, gradually replacing unsuitable habituations, and avoiding all harmful things.
In that way he obtains excellence of strength, complexion, body, and life span.
In this way one should care for this child until he reaches youth and until he acquires skill in <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>.
Thus the procedure that brings prosperity to the blessings wished for sons has been explained.

children.text: tadācaran yathoktairvidhibhiḥ pūjāṃ yatheṣṭaṃ labhate 'nasūyaka iti ||
children.translated_text: Practicing it according to the prescribed rules, a person free from envy obtains honor as desired.
On this there are two verses:
This procedure, which has been stated as bringing prosperity to the blessings wished for sons, is joined with a great purpose.

children.text: tadācaran jño vidhibhiryathātathaṃ pūjāṃ yatheṣṭaṃ labhate'nasūyakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Practicing it knowingly and exactly according to the rules, a person free from envy obtains honor as desired.
The body is considered in its entirety, together with divine and human endowments.
Because it is considered through all its states, therefore the section is called the Section on the Body.
Now then we shall explain the prognostic topic called Color and Voice.
Thus indeed spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: iha khalu varṇaśca svaraśca gandhaśca rasaśca sparśaśca cakṣuśca śrotraṃ ca ghrāṇaṃ ca rasanaṃ ca sparśanaṃ ca sattvaṃ ca bhaktiśca śaucaṃ ca śīlaṃ cācāraśca smṛtiścākṛtiśca prakṛtiśca vikṛtiśca balaṃ ca glāniśca medhā ca harṣaśca raukṣyaṃ ca snehaśca tandrā cārambhaśca gauravaṃ ca lāghavaṃ ca guṇāścāhāraśca vihāraścāhārapariṇāmaścopāyaś cāpāyaśca vyādhiśca vyādhipūrvarūpaṃ ca vedanāścopadravāśca chāyā ca praticchāyā ca svapnadarśanaṃ ca dūtādhikāraśca pathi cautpātikaṃ cāturakule bhāvāvasthāntarāṇi ca bheṣajasaṃvṛttiśca bheṣajavikārayuktiśceti parīkṣyāṇi pratyakṣānumānopadeśair āyuṣaḥ pramāṇāvaśeṣaṃ jijñāsamānena bhiṣajā ||
children.translated_text: Here, when a physician wishes to know the measure of remaining life, he should examine, by perception, inference, and authoritative instruction, color, voice, smell, taste, touch, the eye, hearing, smell, taste, touch, mind, devotion, purity, character, conduct, memory, form, constitution, morbid alteration, strength, exhaustion, intelligence, joy, dryness, unctuousness, drowsiness, initiative, heaviness, lightness, qualities, diet, regimen, digestion of food, means of success and failure, disease, prodromal signs of disease, pains, complications, shade, reflected image, dream-visions, the circumstances of messengers, omens on the road, changes of state in the patient's household, the availability of medicines, and the reasoning behind modifications of medicine.

children.text: tatra tu khalveṣāṃ parīkṣyāṇāṃ kānicit puruṣam anāśritāni kānicic ca puruṣasaṃśrayāṇi
children.translated_text: But among these things to be examined, some are independent of the person, and some depend on the person.

children.text: tatra yāni puruṣam anāśritāni tānyupadeśato yuktitaśca parīkṣeta puruṣasaṃśrayāṇi punaḥ prakṛtito vikṛtitaśca ||
children.translated_text: Among them, those that are independent of the person should be examined by authoritative teaching and by reasoning; those that depend on the person, however, should be examined by <s>prakṛti</s> (natural constitution) and <s>vikṛti</s> (morbid alteration).

children.text: tatra prakṛtir jātiprasaktā ca kulaprasaktā ca deśānupātinī ca kālānupātinī ca vayo'nupātinī ca pratyātmaniyatā ceti
children.translated_text: Here <s>prakṛti</s> is connected with birth, connected with family, dependent on region, dependent on time, dependent on age, and fixed for each individual self.

children.text: jātikuladeśakālavayaḥpratyātmaniyatā hi teṣāṃ teṣāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ te te bhāvaviśeṣā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: For according to birth, family, region, time, age, and individual nature, particular states occur in each of those persons.

children.text: vikṛtiḥ punarlakṣaṇanimittā ca lakṣyanimittā ca nimittānurūpā ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vikṛti</s>, on the other hand, is caused by signs, caused by what is to be observed, and corresponding to its cause.

children.text: tatra lakṣaṇanimittā nāma sā yasyāḥ śarīre lakṣaṇānyeva hetubhūtāni bhavanti daivāt lakṣaṇāni hi kānicic charīropanibaddhāni bhavanti yāni hi tasmiṃstasmin kāle tatrādhiṣṭhānamāsādya tāṃ tāṃ vikṛtimutpādayanti
children.translated_text: That which is called caused by signs is the condition in which the signs in the body themselves become causal, by fate; for some signs are bound to the body, and when at a given time they obtain their seat there, they produce this or that morbid alteration.

children.text: lakṣyanimittā tu sā yasyā upalabhyate nimittaṃ yathoktaṃ nidāneṣu
children.translated_text: But that which is caused by what is to be observed is the condition whose cause is found in the way stated in the sections on etiology.

children.text: nimittānurūpā tu nimittārthānukāriṇī yā tām animittāṃ nimittamāyuṣaḥ pramāṇajñānasyecchanti bhiṣajo bhūyaś cāyuṣaḥ kṣayanimittāṃ pretaliṅgānurūpāṃ yām āyuṣo 'ntargatasya jñānārthamupadiśanti dhīrāḥ
children.translated_text: That which corresponds to its cause is the condition that follows the meaning of the cause. Physicians regard that apparently causeless condition as a sign for knowing the measure of life; and the wise teach it, since it is a sign of the waning of life and resembles the marks of the dead, for knowing that life has reached its end.
And it is with reference to this that we shall teach the person-dependent signs of those who are about to die.
This is the enumeration.
We shall explain it in detail.
There, first of all, comes the section on complexion.

children.text: tadyathā kṛṣṇaḥśyāmaḥ śyāmāvadātaḥ avadātaśceti prakṛtivarṇāḥ śarīrasya bhavanti yāṃścāparānupekṣamāṇo vidyād anūkato'nyathā vāpi nirdiśyamānāṃstajjñaiḥ ||
