children.translated_text: one should give him <s>yāvaka</s> for three nights, or else for five days with ghee,
or for seven days with old grain, until the feces are purified.
But when one knows that his bowel has been cleansed, one should administer the <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation therapy),
knowing his age, constitution, and habituation, whichever formulation would be suitable for him.
One should know <s>harītakī</s> to possess five tastes, to be hot, lacking only the salty taste, and auspicious;
it directs the <s>doṣa</s>s downward, is light, and kindles and digests.

children.text: āyuṣyāṃ pauṣṭikīṃ dhanyāṃ vayasaḥ sthāpanīṃ parām
children.translated_text: It promotes life, nourishes, is fortunate, and is supreme for maintaining youth;
it pacifies all diseases and grants strength to the intellect and senses.
<s>Harītakī</s> quickly conquers <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease), <s>gulma</s> (abdominal mass), <s>udāvarta</s> (upward-moving vāta), wasting, pallor disease, intoxication,
hemorrhoids, disorder of the <s>grahaṇī</s>, and long-standing irregular fever;
heart disease together with disease of the head, diarrhea, loss of appetite,
cough, <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorder), abdominal distension, splenic disease, and recent abdominal disease;
excess salivation from kapha, hoarseness, discoloration, jaundice, and worms;
swelling, <s>tamaka</s> asthma, vomiting, impotence, and weakness of the limbs;
various obstructions of the channels, coating in the heart and chest,
and confusion of memory and intellect.
Those who have indigestion, who eat dry food, or who are wasted by women, alcohol, or poison,

children.text: severan nābhayām ete kṣuttṛṣṇoṣṇārditāś ca ye ||
children.translated_text: and those who are afflicted by hunger, thirst, and heat, should not use <s>abhayā</s>.
Those same qualities and actions should be known also in <s>āmalakī</s>,
which have been stated for <s>harītakī</s>, but with the opposite potency.
Therefore, because of such actions, the physician should know these to be like nectar,
namely the excellent fruits of <s>harītakī</s> and <s>āmalaka</s>.
The supreme ground for medicinal plants is <s>Himavān</s>, best of mountains;
therefore one should procure fruits born there, produced in their proper season,
full in taste and potency, at the proper time and according to rule,
and nourished by sun, wind, shade, and water.
Those fruits should be uneaten, unrotted, unwounded, and free from disease.

children.text: teṣāṃ prayogaṃ vakṣyāmi phalānāṃ karma cottamam ||
children.translated_text: I shall explain the use of those fruits and their highest action.
One should take ten-pala portions of each of the five groups of five roots,
as well as one thousand <s>harītakī</s>s and three times as many fresh <s>āmalaka</s>s.
<s>Vidārigandhā</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>, and <s>nidigdhikā</s>
should be known as the group beginning with <s>vidārigandhā</s>, with <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s> as the fifth.
<s>Bilva</s>, <s>agnimantha</s>, <s>śyonāka</s>, <s>kāśmarya</s>, and then <s>pāṭalā</s>;
<s>punarnavā</s>, the two <s>śūrpaparṇī</s>s, <s>balā</s>, and also <s>eraṇḍa</s>;
<s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>jīvantī</s> together with <s>śatāvarī</s>;
and the roots of <s>śara</s>, sugarcane, <s>darbha</s>, <s>kāśa</s>, and <s>śāli</s> rice.
Thus, of these five groups of five roots,
one should prepare the portions as stated; all of that is to be cooked in ten times as much water.
When one tenth remains, it should be strained, and that decoction should be collected,
along with all those <s>harītakī</s>s and all those <s>āmalaka</s>s.
All those fruits, after their stones have been removed, should be crushed with pounders,
and, after placing them in that decoction, one should add these powders:
of <s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, and <s>plava</s>,
of <s>mustā</s> together with <s>viḍaṅga</s>, and likewise of <s>candana</s> and <s>aguru</s>,
of <s>madhuka</s>, <s>haridrā</s>, <s>vacā</s>, and <s>kanaka</s>,

children.text: bhāgāṃś catuṣpalān kṛtvā sūkṣmailāyās tvacas tathā ||
children.translated_text: making four-pala portions, and likewise of fine <s>elā</s> and <s>tvac</s>.
One should also add powdered sugar-candy, a thousand palas and more by one <s>tulā</s>,

children.text: tailasya hy āḍhakaṃ tatra dadyāt trīṇi ca sarpiṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and should put in one <s>āḍhaka</s> of oil and three of ghee.
All that is to be cooked in an <s>udumbara</s> vessel over a gentle fire.

children.text: jñātvā lehyamadagdhaṃ ca śītaṃ kṣaudreṇa saṃsṛjet ||
children.translated_text: When one knows it to be a lickable preparation and unburnt, after it has cooled one should combine it with honey.
The measure of honey is half the measure of the fats; all that should stand in a ghee vessel,

children.text: tiṣṭhet saṃmūrchitaṃ tasya mātrāṃ kāle prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: well blended. Its dose should be administered at the proper time,
as a dose against old age, in such a quantity that it does not block a single meal.
When it has been digested, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk is the food prescribed here.
The <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s, the <s>Vālakhilya</s>s, and other ascetics rich in austerity,
having eaten this <s>rasāyana</s>, became immeasurably long-lived.
Casting off their old bodies, they obtained excellent youthful age,
free from drowsiness, fatigue, and shortness of breath, free from illness, and composed.
Endowed with intelligence, memory, and strength, those ascetics for a long time
practiced brahmanical austerity and celibacy with complete devotion.
One who desires long life should use this <s>brāhma rasāyana</s>.

children.text: dīrgham āyur vayaś cāgryaṃ kāmāṃśceṣṭān samaśnute ||
children.translated_text: He obtains long life, excellent youth, and the desired objects he seeks.

children.text: yathoktaguṇānām āmalakānāṃ sahasraṃ piṣṭasvedanavidhinā payasa ūṣmaṇā susvinnamanātapaśuṣkamanasthi cūrṇayet
children.translated_text: One should take a thousand <s>āmalaka</s>s of the stated qualities, steam them thoroughly by the <s>piṣṭasvedana</s> method with the vapor of milk, dry them without sun, remove their stones, and powder them.

children.text: tadāmalakasahasrasvarasaparipītaṃ sthirāpunarnavājīvantīnāgabalābrahmasuvarcalāmaṇḍūkaparṇīśatāvarīśaṅkhapuṣpīpippalīvacāviḍaṅgasvayaṅguptāmṛtā candanāgurumadhukamadhūkapuṣpotpalapadmamālatīyuvatīyūthikācūrṇāṣṭabhāgasaṃyuktaṃ punar nāgabalāsahasrapalasvarasaparipītam anātapaśuṣkaṃ dviguṇitasarpiṣā kṣaudrasarpiṣā vā kṣudraguḍākṛtiṃ kṛtvā śucau dṛḍhe ghṛtabhāvite kumbhe bhasmarāśer adhaḥ sthāpayed antarbhūmeḥ pakṣaṃ kṛtarakṣāvidhānam atharvavedavidā pakṣātyaye coddhṛtya kanakarajatatāmrapravālakālāyasacūrṇāṣṭabhāgasaṃyuktam ardhakarṣavṛddhyā yathoktena vidhinā prātaḥ prātaḥ prayuñjāno 'gnibalam abhisamīkṣya jīrṇe ca ṣaṣṭikaṃ payasā sasarpiṣkam upasevamāno yathoktān guṇān samaśnuta iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, after it has been thoroughly saturated with the juice of a thousand <s>āmalaka</s>s, and combined with one-eighth part powders of <s>sthirā</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>nāgabalā</s>, <s>brahmasuvarcalā</s>, <s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>svayaṅguptā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, sandalwood, aloe-wood, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>madhūka</s>-flowers, blue lotus, lotus, <s>mālatī</s>, <s>yuvatī</s>, and <s>yūthikā</s>, it should again be saturated with the juice of a thousand palas of <s>nāgabalā</s>, dried out of the sun, and made, with double the quantity of ghee, or with honey and ghee, into pieces shaped like small lumps of jaggery. It should be placed in a clean, firm jar smeared with ghee, beneath a heap of ashes underground, for a fortnight, with protective rites performed by one who knows the <s>Atharvaveda</s>. After the fortnight has passed, it should be taken out and mixed with one-eighth part powders of gold, silver, copper, coral, and black iron. Using it every morning according to the prescribed rule, increasing by half-karṣa measures, after assessing the strength of the digestive fire, and, when it has been digested, taking <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk and ghee, one obtains the qualities already stated.
This is the <s>brāhma rasāyana</s>, attended by companies of great seers.
One who uses it becomes free from disease, long-lived, and very strong.
He becomes dear to people, successful in his aims, and equal in radiance to the moon and sun.
He retains what he has heard, and a seer-like clarity of mind arises in him.
He has the essence of a mountain that bears the earth, and vigor equal to the wind.

children.text: sa bhavatyaviṣaṃ cāsya gātre saṃpadyate viṣam ||
children.translated_text: Poison becomes non-poison for him; poison in his body is rendered harmless.
<s>Bilva</s>, <s>agnimantha</s>, <s>śyonāka</s>, <s>kāśmarya</s>, <s>pāṭali</s>, and <s>balā</s>,
the four <s>parṇī</s>s, <s>pippalī</s>s, <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, and the two <s>bṛhatī</s>s,
<s>śṛṅgī</s>, <s>tāmalakī</s>, grape, <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>puṣkara</s>, aloe-wood,
<s>abhayā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>ṛddhi</s>, <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, and <s>śaṭī</s>,
<s>musta</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>elā</s>, sandalwood, and blue lotus,
<s>vidārī</s>, the roots of <s>vṛṣa</s>, <s>kākolī</s>, and <s>kākanāsikā</s>:
of these, one should take parts measured by a pala, and five hundred <s>āmalaka</s>s,
put them all together, and cook them in a droṇa of water.
When he knows that these herbs have lost their essence, then that decoction,
and those <s>āmalaka</s>s too, should be taken out; the fruits, with their stones removed,
should be fried in twelve palas of oil and ghee, and the physician should add
half a tulā of purified <s>matsyaṇḍikā</s> sugar and cook it well like a linctus.
When it is prepared and cooled, he should add six palas of honey to it,
four palas of <s>tugākṣīrī</s>, and likewise two palas of <s>pippalī</s>.
He should also add one pala each of cinnamon bark, cardamom, leaf, and saffron.
Thus this <s>Cyavanaprāśa</s> is declared to be the highest <s>rasāyana</s>.
It is especially taught as removing cough and dyspnea,
and as increasing the body in those wasted by consumption or injury, in the old, and in children.
It removes loss of voice, disease of the chest, heart disease, <s>vātaśoṇita</s>,
thirst, and also disorders seated in the semen.
One should use such a dose of it as does not obstruct the meal.
By the use of this, <s>Cyavana</s>, though extremely old, became young again.
Through the use of this <s>rasāyana</s>, a person obtains intelligence, memory, beauty, freedom from disease, extension of life, strength of the senses,
delight among women, the highest increase of digestive fire, clearness of complexion, and the proper downward movement of wind.

children.text: rasāyanasyāsya naraḥ prayogāl labheta jīrṇo 'pi kuṭīpraveśāt
children.translated_text: By using this <s>rasāyana</s>, even an aged man, through the hut-entry procedure, obtains these,

children.text: jarākṛtaṃ rūpamapāsya sarvaṃ bibharti rūpaṃ navayauvanasya ||
children.translated_text: and, having cast off every form produced by old age, bears the form of fresh youth.

children.text: athāmalakaharītakīnām āmalakavibhītakānāṃ harītakīvibhītakānām āmalakaharītakīvibhītakānāṃ vā palāśatvagavanaddhānāṃ mṛdāvaliptānāṃ kukūlasvinnānām akulakānāṃ palasahasramulūkhale saṃpothya dadhighṛtamadhupalalatailaśarkarāsaṃyuktaṃ bhakṣayed anannabhug yathoktena vidhinā tasyānte yavāgvādibhiḥ pratyavasthāpanam abhyaṅgotsādanaṃ sarpiṣā yavacūrṇaiśca ayaṃca rasāyanaprayogaprakarṣo dvistāvadagnibalam abhisamīkṣya pratibhojanaṃ yūṣeṇa payasā vā ṣaṣṭikaḥ sasarpiṣkaḥ ataḥ paraṃ yathāsukhavihāraḥ kāmabhakṣyaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: Then one may take a thousand palas of <s>āmalaka</s> and <s>harītakī</s>, or of <s>āmalaka</s> and <s>vibhītaka</s>, or of <s>harītakī</s> and <s>vibhītaka</s>, or of <s>āmalaka</s>, <s>harītakī</s>, and <s>vibhītaka</s> together, wrapped in <s>palāśa</s> bark, smeared with clay, steamed in chaff-heat, and not broken open. After pounding them in a mortar, he should eat them, while taking no other food, combined with curd, ghee, honey, one pala of oil, and sugar, according to the stated rule. At the end of that course, restoration should be done with gruel and the like, with anointing and rubbing by means of ghee and barley flour. This intensification of the <s>rasāyana</s> regimen is twice as great. Assessing the strength of the digestive fire, he should take at each meal <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with ghee, together with soup or milk. After that, he may follow a comfortable way of life and eat what he desires.

children.text: anena prayogeṇarṣayaḥ punar yuvatvam avāpur babhūvuś cānekavarṣaśatajīvino nirvikārāḥ paraśarīrabuddhīndriyabalasamuditāś ceruś cātyantaniṣṭhayā tapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this regimen the seers regained youth, lived for many hundreds of years, were free from disorder, endowed with the highest strength of body, intellect, and senses, and practiced austerity with complete firmness.

children.text: harītakyāmalakavibhītakapañcapañcamūlaniryūhe pippalīmadhukamadhūkakākolīkṣīrakākolyātmaguptājīvakarṣabhakakṣīraśuklākalkasamprayuktena vidārīsvarasena kṣīrāṣṭaguṇasamprayuktena ca sarpiṣaḥ kumbhaṃ sādhayitvā prayuñjāno 'gnibalasamāṃ mātrāṃ jīrṇe ca kṣīrasarpirbhyāṃ śāliṣaṣṭikam uṣṇodakānupānam aśnañjarāvyādhipāpābhicāravyapagatabhayaḥ śarīrendriyabuddhibalam atulam upalabhyāpratihatasarvārambhaḥ paramāyur avāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having prepared a jar of ghee in a decoction of <s>harītakī</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, and the five groups of five roots, with a paste of <s>pippalī</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>madhūka</s>, <s>kākolī</s>, <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>, <s>ātmaguptā</s>, <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, and <s>kṣīraśuklā</s>, together with the juice of <s>vidārī</s> and eight times as much milk, a person should use a dose equal to the strength of his digestive fire. When it has been digested, eating <s>śāli</s> or <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk and ghee, and taking warm water as the after-drink, he becomes free from fear of old age, disease, sin, and hostile rites; he obtains incomparable strength of body, senses, and intellect, has all undertakings unobstructed, and attains the highest lifespan.

children.text: harītakyāmalakavibhītakaharidrāsthirābalāviḍaṅgāmṛtavallīviśvabheṣajamadhukapippalīsomavalkasiddhena kṣīrasarpiṣā madhuśarkarābhyāmapi ca saṃnīyāmalakasvarasaśataparipītam āmalakacūrṇam ayaścūrṇacaturbhāgasamprayuktaṃ pāṇitalamātraṃ prātaḥ prātaḥ prāśya yathoktena vidhinā sāyaṃ mudgayūṣeṇa payasā vā sasarpiṣkaṃ śāliṣaṣṭikānnam aśnīyāt trivarṣaprayogādasya varṣaśatam ajaraṃ vayas tiṣṭhati śrutam avatiṣṭhate sarvāmayāḥ praśāmyanti viṣamaviṣaṃ bhavati gātre gātram aśmavat sthirībhavati adhṛṣyo bhūtānāṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: After mixing powder of <s>āmalaka</s>, soaked a hundred times in the fresh juice of <s>āmalaka</s>, with milk-ghee prepared with <s>harītakī</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>haridrā</s>, <s>sthirā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>amṛtavallī</s>, <s>viśvabheṣaja</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>somavalka</s>, and also with honey and sugar, and after combining it with one quarter part of iron powder, one should swallow every morning a palm-sized quantity. In the evening, according to the stated rule, one should eat <s>śāliṣaṣṭika</s> rice with mung-bean soup or with milk, together with ghee. From using this for three years, his age remains unaged for a hundred years, his learning stays firm, all illnesses are pacified, poison becomes non-poison in his body, his body becomes firm like stone, and he becomes unassailable by beings.
As <s>amṛta</s> is for the immortals, as <s>sudhā</s> is for the <s>Bhogavats</s>,
so in ancient times was the procedure of <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation therapy) for the great seers.

children.text: na jarāṃ na ca daurbalyaṃ nāturyaṃ nidhanaṃ na ca
children.translated_text: They did not come to old age, nor to weakness, illness, or death;
devoted to <s>rasāyana</s> in ancient times, they lived for thousands of years.

children.text: na kevalaṃ dīrghamihāyuraśnute rasāyanaṃ yo vidhivanniṣevate
children.translated_text: One who uses <s>rasāyana</s> properly does not merely obtain long life here;

children.text: gatiṃ sa devarṣiniṣevitāṃ śubhāṃ prapadyate brahma tatheti cākṣayam ||
children.translated_text: he attains the auspicious path followed by divine seers, and likewise the imperishable <s>brahman</s>.
In this <s>Abhayāmalakīya</s> section, six preparations have been taught,
proven <s>rasāyana</s>s by which life is prolonged.

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte cikitsāsthāne rasāyanādhyāye 'bhayāmalakīyo nāma rasāyanapādaḥ prathamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s> and revised by <s>Caraka</s>, in the section on therapeutics, in the chapter on <s>rasāyana</s>, the first <s>rasāyana</s> quarter named <s>Abhayāmalakīya</s> is complete.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the <s>Prāṇakāmīya</s> quarter on <s>rasāyana</s>.
Thus indeed spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: prāṇakāmāḥ śuśrūṣadhvam idam ucyamānam amṛtam ivāparam aditisutahitakaram acintyādbhutaprabhāvam āyuṣyam ārogyakaraṃ vayasaḥ sthāpanaṃ nidrātandrāśramaklamālasyadaurbalyāpaharam anilakaphapittasāmyakaraṃ sthairyakaram abaddhamāṃsaharam antaragnisaṃdhukṣaṇaṃ prabhāvarṇasvarottamakaraṃ rasāyanavidhānam
children.translated_text: O you who desire vitality, listen to this <s>rasāyana</s> procedure as it is being taught: like another nectar, beneficial to the sons of <s>Aditi</s>, of inconceivable and wonderful power, life-promoting, health-giving, sustaining youth, removing sleepiness, torpor, exhaustion, fatigue, laziness, and weakness, balancing <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>pitta</s>, producing firmness, removing loose flesh, kindling the internal fire, and making touch, complexion, and voice excellent.

children.text: anena cyavanādayo maharṣayaḥ punaryuvatvam āpur nārīṇāṃ ceṣṭatamā babhūvuḥ sthirasamasuvibhaktamāṃsāḥ susaṃhatasthiraśarīrāḥ suprasannabalavarṇendriyāḥ sarvatrāpratihataparākramāḥ kleśasahāś ca
children.translated_text: By this, great seers such as <s>Cyavana</s> regained youth; they became most desired by women, with firm, even, and well-divided flesh, with well-knit and stable bodies, with strength, complexion, and senses beautifully clear, with prowess everywhere unobstructed, and able to endure hardship.

children.text: sarve śarīradoṣā bhavanti grāmyāhārād amlatvalavaṇakaṭukakṣāraśukraśākamāṃsatilapalalapiṣṭānnabhojināṃ virūḍhanavaśūkaśamīdhānyaviruddhāsātmyarūkṣakṣārābhiṣyandibhojināṃ klinnagurupūtiparyuṣitabhojināṃ viṣamādhyaśanaprāyāṇāṃ divāsvapnastrīmadyanityānāṃ viṣamātimātravyāyāmasaṃkṣobhitaśarīrāṇāṃ bhayakrodhaśokalobhamohāyāsabahulānām atonimittaṃ hi śithilībhavanti māṃsāni vimucyante saṃdhayaḥ vidahyate raktaṃ viṣyandate cānalpaṃ medaḥ na saṃdhīyate 'sthiṣu majjā śukraṃ na pravartate kṣayamupaityojaḥ sa evaṃbhūte glāyati sīdati nidrātandrālasyasamanvito nirutsāhaḥ śvasiti asamarthaśceṣṭānāṃ śārīramānasīnāṃ naṣṭasmṛtibuddhicchāyo rogāṇām adhiṣṭhānabhūto na sarvamāyuravāpnoti
children.translated_text: All bodily faults arise in those who eat village foods, sour, salty, pungent, alkaline foods, semen-promoting foods, greens, meat, sesame mash, and flour preparations; in those who eat sprouted, new, bristly, leguminous, incompatible, unsuitable, dry, alkaline, and obstructive foods; in those who eat moist, heavy, putrid, and stale foods; in those mostly given to irregular and excessive eating; in those habitually devoted to day-sleep, women, and liquor; in those whose bodies are agitated by irregular and excessive exercise; and in those much affected by fear, anger, grief, greed, delusion, and exertion. For this reason the flesh becomes slack, the joints loosen, the blood is burned, fat flows excessively, marrow does not join properly in the bones, semen does not proceed, and <s>ojas</s> (vital essence) comes to depletion. In such a state a person languishes, sinks down, is accompanied by sleepiness, torpor, and laziness, lacks vigor, breathes with difficulty, is incapable of bodily and mental activities, has lost memory, intellect, and luster, becomes a seat of diseases, and does not attain the full span of life.

children.text: tasmādetāndoṣānavekṣamāṇaḥ sarvān yathoktān ahitān apāsyāhāravihārān rasāyanāni prayoktumarhatītyuktvā bhagavān punarvasur ātreya uvāca ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, having considered all these faults, one should abandon all the harmful diets and modes of conduct as stated and should undertake <s>rasāyana</s>s. Having said this, the blessed <s>Punarvasu Ātreya</s> spoke again.

children.text: āmalakānāṃ subhūmijānāṃ kālajānām anupahatagandhavarṇarasānām āpūrṇasapramāṇavīryāṇāṃ svarasena punarnavākalkapādasamprayuktena sarpiṣaḥ sādhayedāḍhakam ataḥ paraṃ vidārīsvarasena jīvantīkalkasamprayuktena ataḥ paraṃ caturguṇena payasā balātibalākaṣāyeṇa śatāvarīkalkasaṃyuktena anena krameṇaikaikaṃ śatapākaṃ sahasrapākaṃ vā śarkarākṣaudracaturbhāgasamprayuktaṃ sauvarṇe rājate mārttike vā śucau dṛḍhe ghṛtabhāvite kumbhe sthāpayet tadyathoktena vidhinā yathāgni prātaḥ prātaḥ prayojayet jīrṇe ca kṣīrasarpirbhyāṃ śāliṣaṣṭikam aśnīyāt
children.translated_text: From <s>āmalaka</s> fruits grown in good soil, produced in the proper season, whose smell, color, and taste are unimpaired, and whose measure and potency are full, one should prepare one <s>āḍhaka</s> of ghee with their fresh juice, combined with one quarter part paste of <s>punarnavā</s>. After that, one should cook it with fresh juice of <s>vidārī</s>, combined with paste of <s>jīvantī</s>. After that, one should cook it with four times its quantity of milk, with a decoction of <s>balā</s> and <s>atibalā</s>, joined with paste of <s>śatāvarī</s>. In this sequence, cooked a hundred times each, or a thousand times, mixed with one quarter part sugar and honey, it should be kept in a clean, firm, ghee-impregnated jar of gold, silver, or clay. According to the stated rule, one should use it every morning in accordance with digestive fire; when it has been digested, one should eat <s>śāliṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk and ghee.

children.text: asya prayogādvarṣaśataṃ vayo'jaraṃ tiṣṭhati śrutamavatiṣṭhate sarvāmayāḥ praśāmyanti apratihatagatiḥ strīṣu apatyavān bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: From using this, age remains unaged for a hundred years, learning remains firm, all diseases are pacified, one has unobstructed movement among women, and one becomes possessed of offspring.
For the man who consumes this preparation, there comes a large body, solid as the essence of a mountain, with steady senses and senses of exceeding strength,
unassailable by others, of surpassingly lovely form, and sharing in praise, honor, happiness, and a cheerful mind.
Great strength, foremost purity of complexion, and a voice resembling the thunder of a dense mass of clouds

children.text: bhavatyapatyaṃ vipulaṃ sthiraṃ ca samaśnato yogamimaṃ narasya ||
children.translated_text: come to the man who consumes this preparation, and his offspring becomes abundant and stable.

children.text: āmalakasahasraṃ pippalīsahasrasamprayuktaṃ palāśataruṇakṣārodakottaraṃ tiṣṭhet tadanugatakṣārodakam anātapaśuṣkam anasthi cūrṇīkṛtaṃ caturguṇābhyāṃ madhusarpirbhyāṃ saṃnīya śarkarācūrṇacaturbhāgasamprayuktaṃ ghṛtabhājanasthaṃ ṣaṇmāsān sthāpayedantarbhūmeḥ
children.translated_text: A thousand <s>āmalaka</s> fruits, combined with a thousand <s>pippalī</s>s, should remain covered with alkaline water made from young <s>palāśa</s>. When they have been permeated by that alkaline water, dried out of the sun, freed from their stones, powdered, mixed with fourfold honey and ghee, and combined with a quarter part of powdered sugar, they should be kept for six months in a ghee vessel underground.

children.text: tasyottarakālamagnibalasamāṃ mātrāṃ khādet paurvāhṇikaḥ prayogo nāparāhṇikaḥ sātmyāpekṣaścāhāravidhiḥ
children.translated_text: After that time, one should eat a dose proportionate to the strength of one's digestive fire. The administration is in the forenoon, not in the afternoon, and the dietary rule depends on what is suitable to the patient.

children.text: asya prayogād varṣaśatamajaraṃ vayas tiṣṭhatīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa ||
children.translated_text: By the use of this preparation, unaged youth remains for a hundred years; the rest is the same as before.

children.text: āmalakacūrṇāḍhakam ekaviṃśatirātram āmalakasvarasaparipītaṃ madhughṛtāḍhakābhyāṃ dvābhyāmekīkṛtam aṣṭabhāgapippalīkaṃ śarkarācūrṇacaturbhāgasamprayuktaṃ ghṛtabhājanasthaṃ prāvṛṣi bhasmarāśau nidadhyāt tadvarṣānte sātmyapathyāśī prayojayet asya prayogād varṣaśatam ajaram āyus tiṣṭhatīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa ||
children.translated_text: An <s>āḍhaka</s> of powdered <s>āmalaka</s>, soaked for twenty-one nights in <s>āmalaka</s> juice, should be combined with two <s>āḍhaka</s>s of honey and ghee, furnished with one eighth part <s>pippalī</s>, and mixed with a quarter part of powdered sugar. Placed in a ghee vessel during the rainy season in a heap of ashes, it should be used at the end of a year by one who eats suitable and wholesome food. By the use of this preparation, unaged life remains for a hundred years; the rest is the same as before.

children.text: viḍaṅgataṇḍulacūrṇānām āḍhakamāḍhakaṃ pippalītaṇḍulānām adhyardhāḍhakaṃ sitopalāyāḥ sarpistailamadhvāḍhakaiḥ ṣaḍbhir ekīkṛtaṃ ghṛtabhājanasthaṃ prāvṛṣi bhasmarāśāv iti sarvaṃ samānaṃ pūrveṇa yāvad āśīḥ ||
children.translated_text: An <s>āḍhaka</s> each of powdered kernels of <s>viḍaṅga</s>, one and a half <s>āḍhaka</s>s of kernels of <s>pippalī</s>, and sugar candy, combined into one with six <s>āḍhaka</s>s of ghee, oil, and honey, should be placed in a ghee vessel during the rainy season in a heap of ashes. Everything is the same as before, down to the benediction.

children.text: yathoktaguṇānāmāmalakānāṃ sahasramārdrapalāśadroṇyāṃ sapidhānāyāṃ bāṣpam anudvamantyām āraṇyagomayāgnibhir upasvedayet tāni susvinnaśītāny uddhṛtakulakāny āpothyāḍhakena pippalīcūrṇānāmāḍhakena ca viḍaṅgataṇḍulacūrṇānām adhyardhena cāḍhakena śarkarāyā dvābhyāṃ dvābhyām āḍhakābhyāṃ tailasya madhunaḥ sarpiṣaśca saṃyojya śucau dṛḍhe ghṛtabhāvite kumbhe sthāpayed ekaviṃśatirātram ata ūrdhvaṃ prayogaḥ asya prayogādvarṣaśatam ajaram āyus tiṣṭhatīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa ||
children.translated_text: A thousand <s>āmalaka</s>s possessing the qualities already stated should be steamed in a fresh <s>palāśa</s> trough, covered and not letting out steam, with fires of forest cow-dung. When they are well steamed and cooled, their stones should be removed and they should be pounded. They should then be combined with an <s>āḍhaka</s> of <s>pippalī</s> powder, an <s>āḍhaka</s> of powdered <s>viḍaṅga</s> kernels, one and a half <s>āḍhaka</s>s of sugar, and two <s>āḍhaka</s>s each of oil, honey, and ghee, and kept for twenty-one nights in a clean, strong jar treated with ghee. Thereafter comes the administration. By the use of this preparation, unaged life remains for a hundred years; the rest is the same as before.

children.text: dhanvani kuśāstīrṇe snigdhakṛṣṇamadhuramṛttike suvarṇavarṇamṛttike vā vyapagataviṣaśvāpadapavanasalilāgnidoṣe karṣaṇavalmīkaśmaśānacaityoṣarāvasathavarjite deśe yathartusukhapavanasalilādityasevite jātāny anupahatāny anadhyārūḍhāny abālāny ajīrṇāny adhigatavīryāṇi śīrṇapurāṇaparṇāny asaṃjātāny aparṇāni tapasi tapasye vā māse śuciḥ prayataḥ kṛtadevārcanaḥ svasti vācayitvā dvijātīn cale sumuhūrte nāgabalāmūlāny uddharet teṣāṃ suprakṣālitānāṃ tvakpiṇḍam āmramātram akṣamātraṃ vā ślakṣṇapiṣṭamāloḍya payasā prātaḥ prayojayet cūrṇīkṛtāni vā pibet payasā madhusarpirbhyāṃ vā saṃyojya bhakṣayet jīrṇe ca kṣīrasarpirbhyāṃ śāliṣaṣṭikam aśnīyāt
children.translated_text: In an arid tract strewn with <s>kuśa</s> grass, with unctuous, black, sweet soil or with golden-colored soil, free from faults caused by poison, wild animals, wind, water, or fire, and free from ploughing, anthills, cremation grounds, shrines, saline ground, and dwellings; in a place served by seasonally pleasant wind, water, and sunlight, there grow roots of <s>nāgabalā</s> that are unharmed, not overgrown, neither immature nor overmature, endowed with potency, with old leaves fallen, not newly sprouted, and leafless. In the month <s>Tapas</s> or <s>Tapasya</s>, one who is pure, restrained, has worshiped the gods, and has had the twice-born recite blessings should uproot the <s>nāgabalā</s> roots at a moving and auspicious moment. From those well-washed roots, the pulp of the bark, the size of a mango or of an <s>akṣa</s>, should be ground smooth, stirred with milk, and administered in the morning. Or, powdered, they may be drunk with milk, or combined with honey and ghee and eaten. When it has been digested, one should eat <s>śāliṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk and ghee.
By using this for a year, unaged youth remains for a hundred years; the rest is the same as before.

The expressed juices of <s>balā</s>, <s>atibalā</s>, <s>candana</s>, <s>aguru</s>, <s>dhava</s>, <s>tiniśa</s>, <s>khadira</s>, <s>śiṃśapā</s>, <s>asana</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>, ten herbs in all, are explained according to the procedure for <s>nāgabalā</s>.

children.text: svarasānāmalābhe tv ayaṃ svarasavidhiś cūrṇānām āḍhakam āḍhakam udakasyāhorātrāsthitaṃ mṛditapūtaṃ svarasavat prayojyam ||
children.translated_text: But when expressed juices are not obtainable, this is the method for an expressed juice: an <s>āḍhaka</s> each of the powders, left in water for a day and night, kneaded and filtered, is to be used like an expressed juice.

children.text: bhallātakāny anupahatāny anāmayāny āpūrṇarasapramāṇavīryāṇi pakvajāmbavaprakāśāni śucau śukre vā māse saṃgṛhya yavapalle māṣapalle vā nidhāpayet tāni caturmāsasthitāni sahasi sahasye vā māse prayoktum ārabheta śītasnigdhamadhuropaskṛtaśarīraḥ
children.translated_text: Unharmed and sound <s>bhallātaka</s>s, full in juice, measure, and potency, and resembling ripe <s>jāmbava</s> fruits, should be gathered in the month <s>Śuci</s> or <s>Śukra</s> and placed in a heap of barley straw or a heap of black-gram straw. After remaining there for four months, in the month <s>Sahas</s> or <s>Sahasya</s>, one whose body has been prepared with cooling, unctuous, sweet adjuncts should begin to use them.

children.text: pūrvaṃ daśabhallātakānyāpothyāṣṭaguṇenāmbhasā sādhu sādhayet teṣāṃ rasamaṣṭabhāgāvaśeṣaṃ pūtaṃ sapayaskaṃ pibet sarpiṣāntar mukham abhyajya
children.translated_text: First, ten <s>bhallātaka</s>s should be pounded and cooked well with eight times as much water. Their liquid, reduced to one eighth and filtered, should be drunk with milk, after the inside of the mouth has been anointed with ghee.

children.text: tāny ekaikabhallātakotkarṣāpakarṣeṇa daśabhallātakāny ā triṃśataḥ prayojyāni nātaḥ paramutkarṣaḥ
children.translated_text: They are to be administered by increasing and decreasing one <s>bhallātaka</s> at a time, from ten <s>bhallātaka</s>s up to thirty; there is no increase beyond that.
According to this rule of administration, the <s>bhallātaka</s> course has a limit of one thousand.

children.text: jīrṇe ca sasarpiṣā payasā śāliṣaṣṭikāśanam upacāraḥ prayogānte ca dvis tāvat payasaivopacāraḥ
children.translated_text: When it has been digested, the aftercare is a meal of <s>śāliṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk and ghee; and at the end of the course, the aftercare is for twice as long with milk alone.
By the use of that preparation, unaged youth remains for a hundred years; the rest is the same as before.

children.text: bhallātakānāṃ jarjarīkṛtānāṃ piṣṭasvedanaṃ pūrayitvā bhūmāv ākaṇṭhaṃ nikhātasya snehabhāvitasya dṛḍhasyopari kumbhasyāropyoḍupenāpidhāya kṛṣṇamṛttikāvaliptaṃ gomayāgnibhir upasvedayet teṣāṃ yaḥ svarasaḥ kumbhaṃ prapadyeta tam aṣṭabhāgamadhusamprayuktaṃ dviguṇaghṛtam adyāt tatprayogādvarṣaśatamajaraṃ vayastiṣṭhatīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa ||
children.translated_text: A steaming apparatus should be filled with crushed <s>bhallātaka</s>s and set above a strong jar that has been treated with fat and buried in the ground up to its neck. It should be covered with a bowl, plastered with black clay, and heated with cow-dung fires. The expressed juice from them that reaches the jar should be eaten, mixed with one eighth part honey and with double the quantity of ghee. By the use of that preparation, unaged youth remains for a hundred years; the rest is the same as before.

children.text: bhallātakatailapātraṃ sapayaskaṃ madhukena kalkenākṣamātreṇa śatapākaṃ kuryāditi samānaṃ pūrveṇa ||
children.translated_text: A vessel of <s>bhallātaka</s> oil, together with milk and with an <s>akṣa</s>-measure of <s>madhuka</s> paste, should be cooked a hundred times; the rest is the same as before.

children.text: bhallātakasarpiḥ bhallātakakṣīraṃ bhallātakakṣaudraṃ guḍabhallātakaṃ bhallātakayūṣaḥ bhallātakatailaṃ bhallātakapalalaṃ bhallātakasaktavaḥ bhallātakalavaṇaṃ bhallātakatarpaṇam iti bhallātakavidhānamuktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus the procedure for <s>bhallātaka</s> has been stated: <s>bhallātaka</s> ghee, <s>bhallātaka</s> milk, <s>bhallātaka</s> honey, jaggery with <s>bhallātaka</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s> soup, <s>bhallātaka</s> oil, <s>bhallātaka</s> paste, <s>bhallātaka</s> meal, <s>bhallātaka</s> salt, and <s>bhallātaka</s> saturating drink.
<s>Bhallātaka</s> nuts are sharp, ripening, and like fire;
when used according to rule, they become like nectar.
These ten kinds of applications of them have been proclaimed.
One who knows disease, constitution, and suitability should prescribe those applications.

children.text: kaphajo na sa rogo'sti na vibandho'sti kaścana
children.translated_text: There is no disease born of <s>kapha</s>, nor any obstruction at all,
which <s>bhallātaka</s>, quickly increasing intellect and digestive fire, would not destroy.
In ancient times the aged great seers, <s>Cyavana</s> and the others, desiring life,
became of immeasurable lifespan through these auspicious <s>rasāyana</s>s.
Having accumulated brahmanic austerity, celibacy, spiritual knowledge, and meditation,
they, long-lived as they wished, went to the third heaven.
Therefore, for the increase of life, those who desire vitality and seek happiness,
being well concentrated, should follow the procedure of <s>rasāyana</s> according to rule.
The combinations of <s>rasāyana</s>s, perfected by the one who seeks the welfare of beings,
have been taught by the great sage in the thirty-seven verses of the section called <s>Prāṇakāmīya</s>.

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte cikitsāsthāne rasāyanādhyāye prāṇakāmīyo nāma rasāyanapādo dvitīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s> and revised by <s>Caraka</s>, in the section on therapeutics, in the chapter on <s>rasāyana</s>, the second quarter on <s>rasāyana</s>, called <s>Prāṇakāmīya</s>, is completed.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of fever.
Thus indeed spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.
Free from fever himself, <s>Agniveśa</s>, with joined hands, asked <s>Punarvasu</s> about the subject of fever,
as he was sitting in a secluded, peaceful place.
Fever, tormenting body, senses, and mind, first-born of all diseases and powerful,
was formerly declared by the blessed one to be foremost among diseases.
Of that constant enemy of living beings, at its destruction and arising,

children.text: prakṛtiṃ ca pravṛttiṃ ca prabhāvaṃ kāraṇāni ca ||
children.translated_text: its nature, manifestation, power, and causes,
its prodromal signs, seat, strength, time, intrinsic character,
and, in detail and according to differences of method, the form of fever when separately divided,
the signs of unripe and mature fever, the sequence of treatment together with medicines,

children.text: vimuñcataḥ praśāntasya cihnaṃ yacca pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: and the separate signs of fever when it is leaving and when it has subsided,
how long one released from fever should be protected, and from what factors,
and by what causes a fever that has subsided returns again,
and also what treatments pacify it when it has recurred:
for the welfare of the world, blessed one, you ought to state all this.
Having heard that speech of <s>Agniveśa</s>, the teacher said,

children.text: jvarādhikāre yadvācyaṃ tat saumya nikhilaṃ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: 'Gentle one, hear in full what is to be said concerning fever.

children.text: jvaro vikāro rogaśca vyādhirātaṅka eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Jvara</s>, disorder, illness, disease, and affliction:
one single meaning is expressed by these various synonymous names.
Its nature is said to be the bodily and mental <s>doṣa</s>s,

children.text: dehinaṃ na hi nirdoṣaṃ jvaraḥ samupasevate ||
children.translated_text: for fever does not attack an embodied being who is without <s>doṣa</s>.
Wasting, darkness, fever, evil, and death are said to have the nature of <s>Yama</s>,
because they are causes of the five-elemental dissolution of people tormented by their own action.
Thus its nature has been stated. Its manifestation, however, comes from appropriation,
as was previously stated in the section on causes, and from the terrible anger of <s>Rudra</s>.
For in the second age the demons attacked <s>Śarva</s>,
who was established in a vow of freedom from anger, for a divine thousand years,
destroyers of austerity, in order to make an obstacle to the austerity of that great soul.
Seeing this and being able to act, <s>Dakṣa</s> <s>Prajāpati</s> remained indifferent.
Again, <s>Dakṣa</s> <s>Prajāpati</s> did not assign the fixed share belonging to <s>Maheśvara</s>
in the sacrifice, even though urged by the gods.
The verses belonging to <s>Paśupati</s>, and the oblations pertaining to <s>Śiva</s>,
which grant the success of the sacrifice, he performed the rite without them.
Then the god, his vow completed, knowing <s>Dakṣa</s>'s transgression,
<s>Rudra</s>, having set before himself the fierce state of his self-knowing self,

children.text: sṛṣṭvā lalāṭe cakṣurvai dagdhvā tānasurān prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: created an eye on his forehead; and after the lord had burned those demons,
he produced a child, heated by the fire of anger, for the destruction of the sacrifice.

children.text: tato yajñaḥ sa vidhvasto vyathitāśca divaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that sacrifice was destroyed, and the dwellers in heaven were distressed;
the hosts of beings, afflicted by burning pain, wandered confused through the directions.
Then the host of gods, together with the seven seers, approached the mighty lord,

children.text: tam ṛgbhir astuvan yāvacchaive bhāve śivaḥ sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and praised him with <s>ṛc</s> verses until <s>Śiva</s> stood in a benevolent state.

children.text: śivaṃ śivāya bhūtānāṃ sthitaṃ jñātvā kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing <s>Śiva</s>, auspicious for the beings, to be established in auspiciousness, with joined hands,
through fear, ash for his weapon, three-headed and nine-eyed,
fierce, covered with a garland of flames, with short shanks and belly, step by step,
the fire of anger said to the god, 'What shall I do for you?'
The lord said to that anger, 'You will be fever in the world.
At birth, at death, and amid occasions of misconduct you will arise.
Burning, loss of taste, thirst, pain together with aching of the limbs, and distress in the heart:
at birth and at death, the power of fever is very great.
Its nature, manifestation, and power have been shown.
In the section on causes, eight causes were previously stated separately.

children.text: ālasyaṃ nayane sāsre jṛmbhaṇaṃ gauravaṃ klamaḥ
children.translated_text: Laziness, tearful eyes, yawning, heaviness, exhaustion,
and uncertain aversion to fire, heat, wind, water, and food,
indigestion, bad taste in the mouth, and loss of strength and complexion,
and a slight alteration of conduct: this is the foremost symptom of fever.'
Only the body, together with the mind, is said to be the seat of fever.
But strength and season have been shown in the section on causes.
The sign specific to fever is heating of the body and mind.

children.text: jvareṇāviśatā bhūtaṃ na hi kiṃcinna tapyate ||
children.translated_text: For there is no being that, when entered by fever, is not heated at all.
By difference of classification, fever is twofold: bodily and mental.

children.text: punaśca dvividho dṛṣṭaḥ saumyaścāgneya eva vā ||
children.translated_text: And again it is seen as twofold: <s>saumya</s> (cool or soma-natured) and fiery.
It is further said to be twofold: with inward force and with outward force.
It is also natural or abnormal, and curable or incurable.
Again, from the strength and weakness of <s>doṣa</s> and season, it is seen as fivefold:
<s>saṃtata</s> (continuous), <s>satata</s> (constant), alternate-day, third-day, and fourth-day fever.
Again, by difference of seat among the <s>dhātu</s>s (tissue elements), it is regarded as sevenfold.
Divided by difference of cause, fever is again eightfold.

children.text: śārīro jāyate pūrvaṃ dehe manasi mānasaḥ
children.translated_text: Bodily fever first arises in the body, and mental fever in the mind.
Derangement, lack of delight, and languor are marks of heating of the mind.
And disturbance of the senses is to be known as a mark of such heating.
When fever is of the nature of <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, it desires cold; when it is of the nature of <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, it desires heat.
A fever whose signs are mixed desires both of these.
For <s>vāyu</s>, supremely a carrier in combination, brings about both effects.
Joined with fire it produces burning; depending on soma, it produces cold.
Excessive inner burning, thirst, delirious speech, difficult breathing, dizziness,
pain in the joints and bones, lack of sweating, and suppression of <s>doṣa</s> and feces:
these should be recognized as the signs of fever with inward force.
Greater external heat, and mildness of thirst and the other symptoms,
are the signs of fever with outward force, and also its easy curability.
A natural fever, easy to cure, is one arising in spring or autumn.
<s>Pitta</s>, increased in the hot season by heat, is aggravated in autumn.
And <s>kapha</s>, accumulated in the cold season, is likewise stirred up in spring.
In the rains, by waters and herbs that have sour post-digestive effect,
accumulated <s>pitta</s>, swollen up by the sun's heat in autumn,
quickly produces fever, and <s>kapha</s> acts as its secondary force.
There, because it is naturally a season of release, there is no danger from not fasting.
And <s>kapha</s>, accumulated by waters, herbs, and sweet substances,
is heated by the sun in winter and becomes aggravated in spring.
Therefore fever arises in spring through <s>śleṣman</s> (kapha).
Even for that fever, in the middle of the period of taking-in, <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> follow after.

children.text: ādāvante ca madhye ca buddhvā doṣabalābalam ||
children.translated_text: At the beginning, the end, and the middle, having understood the strength and weakness of the <s>doṣa</s>s,
the learned physician should treat fever in autumn and spring.
Natural fever has been defined with reference to the nature of the season.
In other seasons, abnormal fever is generally <s>vāta</s>-based and difficult.
Its various causes have been shown in the section on causes.
A fever is curable when the patient is strong, the <s>doṣa</s>s are slight, and there are no complications.
A fever born from many causes, from strong causes, and having many symptoms,
and one that brings life to an end and quickly destroys the senses,
after seven days, or after ten days, or likewise after twelve days,
a sharp fever accompanied by delirious speech, dizziness, and difficult breathing kills a person.
A deep fever that is long-lasting in one who is wasted or swollen,
and a powerful fever that parts the hair at the seam of the head, is incurable.
Heavy <s>doṣa</s>s, spread through the channels that carry <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid),
pervading the whole body and immobilized, produce continuous fever.

children.text: daśāhaṃ dvādaśāhaṃ vā saptāhaṃ vā suduḥsahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For ten days, or twelve days, or seven days it is very hard to bear.

children.text: sa śīghraṃ śīghrakāritvāt praśamaṃ yāti hanti vā
children.translated_text: Because it acts quickly, it quickly comes to pacification or kills.
For when a <s>doṣa</s> is equal to the season, the morbid substrate, and the constitution, it is continuous.
Lacking an antagonist, it acts; therefore it should be known as very hard to bear.
Just as <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣa</s>s affect the <s>dhātu</s>s, so too they affect urine and feces.
And in continuous fever they necessarily enter them all at once.

children.text: sa śuddhyā vāpyaśuddhyā vā rasādīnām aśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether through complete purification or through non-purification of <s>rasa</s> and the others,

children.text: saptāhādiṣu kāleṣu praśamaṃ yāti hanti vā
children.translated_text: at times beginning with seven days it either subsides or kills.

children.text: yadā tu nātiśudhyanti na vā śudhyanti sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when they are not very much purified, or are not purified in every respect,
then these twelve seats of the continuous fever are taught.
After making an obscure release on the twelfth day,
it continues for a long time, with pacification hard to obtain.

children.text: iti buddhvā jvaraṃ vaidya upakrāmettu saṃtatam ||
children.translated_text: Having understood continuous fever in this way, the physician should begin treatment,
properly engaged in the order of therapies, generally first with reducing measures.
A <s>doṣa</s> mostly seated in the blood <s>dhātu</s> produces constant fever,
having an antagonist, and characterized by increase and decrease over time.
Constant fever follows two times in a day and night,
only after gaining strength from one among season, constitution, and morbid substrate.
An alternate-day fever is produced when a <s>doṣa</s> obstructs the channels that carry fat,
and, having an antagonist, generates one attack in a day and night.
A <s>doṣa</s> gone into bone and marrow produces third-day and fourth-day fevers.
The movement of the <s>doṣa</s> every second day and every third day is described otherwise by others.
It may produce alternate-day fever even by resorting to blood.
Following the channels of flesh, it produces a third-day fever.
And the <s>doṣa</s>, resorting to the pathway of fat, also produces a fourth-day fever.
The alternate-day fever comes every day; the third-day fever skips one day.

children.text: dinadvayaṃ yo viśramya pratyeti sa caturthakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The one that rests for two days and returns is the fourth-day fever.

children.text: adhiśete yathā bhūmiṃ bījaṃ kāle ca rohati
children.translated_text: As a seed lies upon the ground and sprouts at the proper time,

children.text: adhiśete tathā dhātuṃ doṣaḥ kāle ca kupyati ||
children.translated_text: so a <s>doṣa</s> lies in a <s>dhātu</s> and becomes aggravated at the proper time.

children.text: sa vṛddhiṃ balakālaṃ ca prāpya doṣastṛtīyakam
children.translated_text: That <s>doṣa</s>, having gained increase, strength, and its proper time, makes a tertian fever
and also a quartan one, because the opposing force has been weakened.

children.text: kṛtvā vegaṃ gatabalāḥ sve sve sthāne vyavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: After producing an attack, the humors, their strength gone, settle in their own places;

children.text: punarvivṛddhāḥ sve kāle jvarayanti naraṃ malāḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, increased again at their own time, the impurities bring fever upon a person.
The tertian fever that seizes the sacral region arises from <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>; that seizing the back is of the nature of <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>;
and that seizing the head arises from <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>. Thus tertian fever is threefold.
Quartan fever shows a twofold manifestation:
the phlegmatic one first appears from the shanks, and the one born of wind from the head.
Another irregular fever is the reverse of quartan fever,
which each of the three humors produces when situated in one tissue or in two tissues.
Fever is generally seen as fivefold through combined disturbance,

children.text: sannipāte tu yo bhūyān sa doṣaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in combined disturbance whichever <s>doṣa</s> is stronger is so designated.
According to the strength or weakness of seasons, day and night, the humors, and the mind,
and according to time and circumstance, fever assumes this or that form.
Heaviness, misery, agitation, weakness, vomiting and loss of appetite,
external heat, aching of the limbs, and yawning occur when fever is situated in <s>rasa</s>.
Red and hot eruptions, thirst, repeated spitting mixed with blood,
burning, redness, giddiness, intoxication, and delirious speech occur when it is situated in the blood.
Internal burning, thirst and stupor, fatigue, looseness of stool,
bad smell, and jerking of the limbs occur when fever is situated in the flesh.
Sweating, intense thirst, delirious speech, and frequent vomiting,
inability to bear one's own smell, fatigue and loss of appetite occur when it is situated in fat.
Both purging and vomiting, cracking together with pain in the bones,
tossing of the limbs, and dyspnea occur in fever that has gone to the bones.
Hiccup, dyspnea, cough, and excessive seeing of darkness,
cutting pain in the vital spots, external coldness, and internal burning occur when it has gone to the marrow.
When it has reached the seat of semen, after causing discharge of semen and destroying it,
that powerful fever departs with life, together with <s>vāyu</s>, fire, and soma.
Fever resting in <s>rasa</s> and blood is curable, and so is that which has gone to fat and flesh;
that which has gone to bone and marrow is difficult, and that situated in semen is not successfully treated at all.
Fever was previously stated to be eightfold by causes and symptoms;
now hear in detail the symptoms of what was taught in brief.

children.text: śiroruk parvaṇāṃ bhedo dāho romṇāṃ praharṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Headache, splitting pain in the joints, burning, horripilation,
dryness of throat and mouth, vomiting, thirst, fainting, giddiness, and loss of appetite,
loss of sleep, excessive speech, and yawning are the form of fever from <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: śītako gauravaṃ tandrā staimityaṃ parvaṇāṃ ca ruk ||
children.translated_text: Chill, heaviness, drowsiness, rigidity, and pain in the joints,
constriction of the head, coryza, cough, and failure of sweating to occur,
together with heat and a moderate attack, are the form of fever from <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>.
Repeated burning and repeated cold, repeated obstruction of sweat,
stupor, cough, loss of appetite, and thirst indicate the activity of <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
A coated and bitter mouth and drowsiness are the form of fever from <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
These are declared to be the fevers born of paired humors; the one born of combined disturbance is now described.
Next, regarding the thirteenfold fever of combined humoral disturbance,

children.text: prāksūtritasya vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇaṃ vai pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: which was previously outlined, I shall state the symptoms separately, one by one.
Giddiness, thirst, burning, heaviness, and excessive pain of the head
should be known as the sign in fever where <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> are predominant and <s>kapha</s> is weak.
Coldness, cough, loss of appetite, drowsiness, thirst, burning, pain, and distress
are known as the signs in a disease where <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> are predominant and <s>pitta</s> is lower.
Vomiting, coldness, repeated burning, thirst, stupor, and bone pain
are determined as the signs when <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s> are predominant and <s>vāta</s> is weak.
Pain in the joints, bones, and head, delirious speech, heaviness, and giddiness
occur when <s>vāta</s> is predominant and the other two follow it, together with thirst and dryness of the throat and mouth.
Blood in stool and urine, burning, sweating, thirst, loss of strength,

children.text: mūrcchā ceti tridoṣe syālliṅgaṃ pitte garīyasi ||
children.translated_text: and fainting: these are the signs in a three-humor condition when <s>pitta</s> is the weightier factor.
By laziness, loss of appetite, nausea, burning, vomiting, aversion, and giddiness,
and also by drowsiness and cough, one should identify a combined fever in which <s>kapha</s> is predominant.
Coryza, vomiting, laziness, drowsiness, loss of appetite, and weakness of digestive fire
are regarded as the signs when <s>vāta</s> is deficient, <s>pitta</s> is middling, and <s>śleṣman</s> is excessive.
Yellowness of urine and eyes, burning, thirst, giddiness, and loss of appetite
are regarded as the signs when <s>vāta</s> is deficient, <s>kapha</s> is middling, and <s>pitta</s> is excessive.
Headache, trembling, dyspnea, delirious speech, vomiting, and loss of appetite
are the signs when <s>pitta</s> is deficient, <s>kapha</s> is middling, and <s>māruta</s> is excessive.
Chill, heaviness, drowsiness, delirious speech, and excessive pain in the bones and head
are known as the signs when <s>pitta</s> is deficient, <s>vāta</s> is middling, and <s>śleṣman</s> is excessive.
Dyspnea, cough, coryza, dryness of the mouth, and excessive pain in the side
are regarded as the signs when <s>kapha</s> is deficient, <s>pitta</s> is middling, and <s>vāta</s> is excessive.
Looseness of stool, weakness of digestive fire, thirst, burning, and quick giddiness
are known as the signs when <s>kapha</s> is deficient, <s>vāta</s> is middling, and <s>pitta</s> is excessive.
After the fever of combined humoral disturbance, I shall now state the symptom pattern:
at one moment there is burning, at one moment cold, with pain in the bones, joints, and head;

children.text: sāsrāve kaluṣe rakte nirbhugne cāpi darśane
children.translated_text: the sight is with discharge, turbid, red, and also contracted;
the ears are noisy and painful, and the throat is as if covered with bristles;
there are drowsiness, stupor, delirious speech, cough, dyspnea, loss of appetite, and giddiness;
the tongue is scorched and rough to the touch, and there is extreme looseness of the limbs;
there is spitting of blood and <s>pitta</s>, mixed with <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: śiraso loṭhanaṃ tṛṣṇā nidrānāśo hṛdi vyathā ||
children.translated_text: Rolling of the head, thirst, sleeplessness, and pain in the heart;
the appearance of sweat, urine, and feces only after a long time and in small quantity;
not excessive emaciation of the limbs, and constant gurgling in the throat;
the appearance of dark-red eruptions and circular patches;
muteness, inflammation of the channels, and heaviness of the abdomen;
delayed maturation of the <s>doṣa</s>s, and the form of <s>sannipāta-jvara</s> (fever from all doṣas);
when the <s>doṣa</s> is obstructed, the digestive fire destroyed, and all the symptoms are complete,
<s>sannipāta-jvara</s> is incurable; otherwise it is curable with difficulty.
In the section on causes, the form of fever was said to be threefold when described separately;
by that, the specific signs of combined and <s>sannipāta</s> fevers have also been stated.
But the eighth, the extrinsic fever, is taught as fourfold:
from trauma, from affliction or possession, from sorcery, and from a curse.
By weapons, clods, whips, sticks, fists, forearms, palms, teeth,
and similar things, when the body is struck, fever is caused by trauma.
In traumatic fever, <s>vāyu</s> (wind) generally vitiates the blood,
and produces a painful fever with pain, swelling, and discoloration.
The fever of one afflicted by desire, grief, fear, or anger
is to be known as fever from affliction; so too is that arising from possession by beings.
From desire, grief, and fear, <s>vāyu</s> is aggravated; from anger, <s>pitta</s>; and the three wastes
are aggravated by possession by beings, bearing symptoms corresponding to the possessing being.
Its eightfold set of signs has been explained in the section on beings.
From contact with poisonous trees, poisonous wind, and other poison-born things,
some also call the fever of an afflicted person a fever from affliction.

children.text: cikitsayā viṣaghnyaiva sa śamaṃ labhate naraḥ
children.translated_text: That person obtains relief from it only by poison-counteracting treatment.
The terrible <s>sannipāta-jvara</s> that arises through sorcery or a curse by accomplished persons
should be known as extremely hard to endure.
The sign that has been stated for <s>sannipāta-jvara</s> is remembered for that one too,
as are many other afflictions of the mind, senses, and body.

children.text: prayogaṃ tvabhicārasya dṛṣṭvā śāpasya caiva hi ||
children.translated_text: But by seeing the performance of sorcery or of a curse,
by hearing it oneself, by inference, or by its pacification, it is recognized.
Because sorcery and curses are diverse, in a fever of that nature
the symptom will be varied in different ways according to the rite performed.
Much brooding and sighing are remembered as the sign in fever from desire;
in one born from grief there are many tears, and in fear-fever terror predominates.
In one born from anger there is much agitation; in possession by beings there is behavior beyond the human;
in one arising from poison there is mostly fainting, confusion, intoxication, and exhaustion.

children.text: keṣāṃcid eṣāṃ liṅgānāṃ saṃtāpo jāyate puraḥ ||
children.translated_text: In some of these, burning heat arises before the signs;
in some cases among these fevers beginning with desire, it is the same afterward.
The distinctive mark that has been indicated for fevers born from desire and the rest
is remembered also for other diseases born from desire and the rest.
When the mind has first been struck by desire and the like, fever does not gain such strength
from <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣa</s>s until the body is vitiated.

children.text: dehe cābhihate pūrvaṃ vātādyairna tathā balam ||
children.translated_text: And when the body has first been struck by <s>vāta</s> and the others, fever does not gain such strength

children.text: jvaraḥ prāpnoti kāmādyair mano yāvanna dūṣyati
children.translated_text: from desire and the like until the mind is vitiated.
These extrinsic fevers are at first isolated, but afterward have symptoms mixed with endogenous fevers,
and they are distinguished by their causes and medicines.
The wastes, aggravated in combination, in <s>sannipāta</s>, or separately,
reach the tissue called <s>rasa</s> and drive digestion from its place;

children.text: svena tenoṣmaṇā caiva kṛtvā dehoṣmaṇo balam ||
children.translated_text: with their own heat and with that, having strengthened the body's heat,
they block the channels and, having reached only the body in excessive force,
produce excessive heat in the body. Then a person
becomes very hot in every limb, and because of that is called fevered.
Because the channels are obstructed, he does not obtain sweat;
and, in a fresh fever, the digestive fire is usually displaced from its own seat.
Loss of taste, indigestion, heaviness of the abdomen,
impurity or distress of the heart, drowsiness, and laziness;
a strong fever that does not disperse, non-movement of the <s>doṣa</s>s,
flowing saliva, nausea, loss of hunger, and a tasteless mouth;
stiffness, numbness, and heaviness of the limbs, and abundant urination;

children.text: na viḍ jīrṇā na ca glānirjvarasyāmasya lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: no stool, no digestion, and no relief from languor: these are the signs of unripe fever.
A stronger surge of fever, thirst, delirious speech, difficult breathing, dizziness,
movement of the wastes, and nausea are the signs of one that is being matured.

children.text: kṣut kṣāmatā laghutvaṃ ca gātrāṇāṃ jvaramārdavam ||
children.translated_text: Hunger, leanness, lightness of the limbs, and mildness of the fever,
movement of the <s>doṣa</s>s, and the eighth day are signs of fever free from <s>āma</s> (unprocessed morbidity).
In a new fever one should avoid day-sleep, bathing, oil massage, food, and sexual intercourse,
as well as anger, exposure to wind, exercise, and astringent substances.
In fever, <s>laṅghana</s> (lightening or fasting therapy) is prescribed at the very beginning, except in fever
arising from wasting, <s>vāyu</s>, fear, anger, desire, grief, or fatigue.
When the <s>doṣa</s> has been reduced by <s>laṅghana</s> and the digestive fire has been kindled,
freedom from fever, lightness, and hunger arise for him.
One should treat him with <s>laṅghana</s> that does not oppose the vital breaths,
for health rests on strength, and this therapeutic sequence has that as its purpose.
<s>Laṅghana</s>, sweating, time, thin gruel, and the bitter taste
are digestive measures for unmatured <s>doṣa</s>s in fresh fever.
If he is thirsty, warm water should be given in fever from <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>;

children.text: madyotthe paittike cātha śītalaṃ tiktakaiḥ śṛtam
children.translated_text: but in fever arising from alcohol and in <s>paittika</s> fever, cool water boiled with bitter substances should be given.

children.text: dīpanaṃ pācanaṃ caiva jvaraghnamubhayaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: It both kindles digestion and digests, and indeed it destroys fever in both ways.
It cleanses the channels, strengthens, produces relish and sweat, and is wholesome.
With <s>musta</s>, <s>parpaṭaka</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, sandalwood, <s>udīcya</s>, and dry ginger,
one should give water that has been boiled and cooled, for the calming of thirst and fever.
Having recognized the <s>doṣa</s>s that cause fever, kapha-predominant, not excessively stirred up, and situated in the stomach,
at the proper time he should remove by emetics those that are fit to be vomited out.
Vomiting in a fresh fever, when the <s>doṣa</s>s have not yet become available for expulsion,
strongly produces heart disease, dyspnea, abdominal distension, and stupefaction.
<s>Doṣa</s>s that pervade the whole body, are mixed with <s>āma</s>, lodged in the tissues, and hard to remove quickly,
are dangerous, like the juices of unripe fruits.
One who has been made to vomit and has fasted at the proper time should be treated with <s>yavāgū</s> gruels,
prepared with the appropriate medicines, beginning first with thin gruel-water.
A discerning physician should do this until the fever has become mild, or for six days;
by these gruels his digestive fire is kindled, like fire by fuel-sticks.
Because of their combination with medicines and because they are light, they kindle the digestive fire,
and they set <s>vāta</s>, urine, feces, and the <s>doṣa</s>s moving downward in the proper way.
Because they are liquid and warm they promote sweating; because they are fluid they calm thirst;
because they have the nature of food they sustain life, and because they move along readily they bring lightness.
They remove fever because they are suitable to fever; therefore the intelligent physician should first treat fevers with drinkable gruels,
except for fever arising from liquor.
In alcoholic disorder, in one habituated to liquor, in summer, when pitta and kapha are excessive,

children.text: ūrdhvage raktapitte ca yavāgūrna hitā jvare
children.translated_text: and in upward-moving <s>raktapitta</s>, <s>yavāgū</s> is not beneficial in fever.
In those cases, at first a nourishing drink should be administered, made with parched-grain flour,
mixed with fever-removing fruit juices, honey, and sugar.
Then, taking account of habituation and strength, he should feed him after that nourishing drink has been digested,
with thin mung-bean soup or with the meat broth of animals from dry country.
At meal times tooth-cleaning too should be prescribed for him,
with whatever is opposite to the taste in his mouth and is pleasing.
That brings clarity to his mouth and desire for food and drink,
and it makes him aware of the particular qualities of tastes.
After cleansing the mouth with the tips of tree twigs and rinsing it repeatedly,
he should take whey, sugarcane juice, liquor, and the like, according to the food regimen.
The physician should give a digestive or palliative <s>kaṣāya</s> (decoction)
to the fever patient after six days have passed, once he has been fed light food.
In a fresh fever, <s>doṣa</s>s bound by an astringent decoction become obstructed, do not digest,
and, because they are made rigid, produce irregular fever.
But decoction as a preparation is not being prohibited;
what is to be avoided in a fresh fever is a decoction that is strongly astringent.
With soups, sour or not sour, or with beneficial broths of dry-country animals,
he should eat light food for ten days, for the calming of fever.

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ kaphe mande vātapittottare jvare ||
children.translated_text: After that, when kapha is weak, in a fever dominated by <s>vāta</s> and pitta,
and when the <s>doṣa</s>s are fully matured, drinking ghee is like nectar.
Even before ten days, if the physician knows the condition to be kapha-predominant and not lightened,
he should not give ghee to drink; he should treat that patient with decoctions.
Until lightness is reached he should give food, and also with meat broth,

children.text: balaṃ hyalaṃ nigrahāya doṣāṇāṃ balakṛcca tat
children.translated_text: for strength is sufficient to restrain the <s>doṣa</s>s, and that broth produces strength.
A fever dominated by <s>vāta</s> and pitta in one overcome by burning and thirst,
or one in which the <s>doṣa</s>s are bound or have moved down, if free from <s>āma</s>, should be conquered with milk.

children.text: kriyābhirābhiḥ praśamaṃ na prayāti yadā jvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: When fever does not come to calm through these treatments,
if strength, flesh, and digestive fire are not depleted, he should pacify it with purgatives.

children.text: jvarakṣīṇasya na hitaṃ vamanaṃ na virecanam ||
children.translated_text: For one weakened by fever, vomiting is not beneficial, nor is purgation;

children.text: kāmaṃ tu payasā tasya nirūhairvā harenmalān
children.translated_text: but, if desired, his wastes may be removed by milk or by evacuative enemas.

children.text: nirūho balam agniṃ ca vijvaratvaṃ mudaṃ rucim ||
children.translated_text: An evacuative enema, when applied after the <s>doṣa</s>s have fully matured,
quickly brings strength, digestive fire, freedom from fever, gladness, and appetite.

children.text: pittaṃ vā kaphapittaṃ vā pittāśayagataṃ haret ||
children.translated_text: A laxative removes pitta or kapha-pitta that has gone to the seat of pitta;
an enema removes the three wastes that are situated in the large intestine.
In an old and wasting fever, when kapha and pitta remain, when digestive fire is firm,
and when the feces are dry and bound, an unctuous enema should be given.
When there is heaviness of the head, pain, and obstruction in the sense faculties,
in chronic fever he should perform head-purgation, which restores relish.
Oil massages, anointing poultices, sprinklings, and immersions,
divided according to whether cold or hot measures are required, should be done by the physician in chronic fever.
By these, fever that has gone to the external pathway quickly comes to calm;
the limbs obtain comfort, and strength and complexion increase.
Through fumigation and collyrium formulas, chronic fevers also come to calm,
as do those in which only the skin-level remnant remains and there is an association with an external cause.
Thus the established treatment sequence that destroys fever has been explained;
now hear further the substances to which this sequence belongs.
Old red <s>śāli</s> rice and the like are recommended, together with <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice,
for gruel, cooked rice, and parched grain for fever patients, since they remove fever.
A fever patient who is hungry and whose digestive fire is weak should first drink parched-grain gruel, easy to digest,
boiled with long pepper and dry ginger, for it removes fever.
If he desires sourness, he should drink that same gruel made sour with pomegranate and furnished with dry ginger;

children.text: sṛṣṭaviṭ paittiko vātha śītāṃ madhuyutāṃ pibet
children.translated_text: or, if he is pitta-dominant and has passed stool freely, he should drink it cold, mixed with honey.
Or, in pain of the side, bladder, or head, he should drink a gruel of red <s>śāli</s> rice,
cooked with <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s> and <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>, which removes fever.

children.text: jvarātisārī peyāṃ vā pibet sāmlāṃ śṛtāṃ naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or a man with fever and diarrhea should drink a sour gruel, boiled
with <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>bilva</s>, dry ginger, blue lotus, and coriander.
A man should drink gruel boiled with the vidārīgandhādi group, stimulating digestion and inducing sweating,

children.text: kāsī śvāsī ca hikkī ca yavāgūṃ jvaritaḥ pibet
children.translated_text: when he has cough, dyspnea, hiccup, or fever.
If his feces are obstructed, he should drink gruel boiled with barley, pippalī, and āmalaka,
mixed with ghee, a drink for the fever patient that moves the <s>doṣa</s>s downward.

children.text: koṣṭhe vibaddhe saruji pibet peyāṃ śṛtāṃ jvarī ||
children.translated_text: When the bowel is blocked and painful, the fever patient should drink gruel boiled with
raisins, pippalī root, cavya, āmalaka, and nāgara.

children.text: pibet sabilvāṃ peyāṃ vā jvare saparikartike ||
children.translated_text: Or, in fever with cutting pains, he should drink gruel with bilva,
boiled with balā, vṛkṣāmla, kolāmla, and kalaśī-dhāvanī.
One distressed by lack of sweating, sleeplessness, and thirst should drink gruel with sugar,
prepared with nāgara and āmalaka, fried in ghee, and removing fever.
For soups, one should prescribe mudga beans, lentils, chickpeas, horse gram, and samakuṣṭaka
to fever patients for whom soup is suitable.
Patola leaf together with its fruit, kulaka, pāpacelikā,

children.text: karkoṭakaṃ kaṭhillaṃ ca vidyācchākaṃ jvare hitam
children.translated_text: karkoṭaka, and kaṭhilla should be known as vegetables beneficial in fever.
Lāva quails, kapiñjala partridges, eṇa deer, cakora birds, and upacakraka birds,
kuraṅga antelopes, kālapuccha deer, hariṇa deer, pṛṣata deer, and hares,
a discerning physician should give, as fever-removing meats, to a fever patient accustomed to meat,

children.text: īṣadamlān anamlān vā sarān kāle vicakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: slightly sour or not sour, juicy, at the proper time.
Some physicians do not recommend fowl, peacocks, tittiri, krauñca, and vartaka
in fever, because they are heavy and hot.
If, through fasting, the strength of <s>vāta</s> becomes excessive in fever,
a physician who knows variations of dose and time may give even those.
He should give warm water as an after-drink to one who is thirsty,
or wine to one accustomed to wine, according to the <s>doṣa</s> and according to strength.
In new fever, foods that are heavy, hot, unctuous, sweet,
and astringent should generally be avoided, for the maturation of the <s>doṣa</s>s.
The established fever-destroying sequence of food and drink has been explained.
From here onward, fever-destroying decoctions will be stated.
One should drink musta and parpaṭaka, either hot-prepared or as a cold infusion,
or drink parpaṭaka with nāgara, or with durālabhā.
For the pacification of fever, one may drink kirātatikta, musta, guḍūcī, viśvabheṣaja,
pāṭhā, and uśīra together with udīcya.
These decoctions remove fever, kindle digestion, and digest the <s>doṣa</s>s;
they relieve thirst and loss of appetite and remove bad taste in the mouth.
Kaliṅgaka, leaf of paṭola, and kaṭukarohiṇī;
paṭola, sārivā, musta, pāṭhā, and kaṭukarohiṇī;
nimba, paṭola, triphalā, raisins, musta, and vatsaka;
kirātatikta, amṛtā, sandalwood, and viśvabheṣaja;
guḍūcī, āmalaka, and musta: these, ending at each half-verse,
are five decoctions and quickly pacify the five kinds of fever,
namely constant, continuous, quotidian, tertian, and quartan fever.
Vatsaka, āragvadha, pāṭhā, ṣaḍgranthā, kaṭurohiṇī,
mūrvā, ativisā, nimba, paṭola, and dhanvayāsaka,

children.text: vacāṃ mustamuśīraṃ ca madhukaṃ triphalāṃ balām
children.translated_text: vacā, musta, uśīra, madhuka, triphalā, and balā:
a man should drink this, hot-prepared or as a cold infusion, as a fever-removing decoction.
Madhuka, musta, raisins, kāśmarya fruits, and parūṣaka,
trāyamāṇā, uśīra, triphalā, and kaṭurohiṇī:
after drinking these when they have stood overnight, a person is quickly freed from fever.
Jāti, āmalaka, and musta, and likewise dhanvayavāsaka:
a fever patient with obstructed <s>doṣa</s>s should drink the decoction with jaggery.
Triphalā, trāyamāṇā, raisins, and kaṭurohiṇī:
this decoction removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, and it promotes downward movement.
Combined with trivṛt and sugar, it removes fever caused by <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>.
The two bṛhatīs, vatsaka, musta, devadāru, and mahauṣadha,
together with kolavallī: this formula removes <s>sannipāta</s> fever.

children.text: śaṭī puṣkaramūlaṃ ca vyāghrī śṛṅgī durālabhā
children.translated_text: Śaṭī, puṣkaramūla, vyāghrī, śṛṅgī, and durālabhā,
guḍūcī, nāgara, pāṭhā, kirāta, and kaṭurohiṇī:
this group beginning with śaṭī removes <s>sannipāta</s> fever.
It is recommended for cough, seizure in the heart, pain in the side, dyspnea, and stupor.

children.text: bṛhatyau pauṣkaraṃ bhārgī śaṭī śṛṅgī durālabhā
children.translated_text: The two bṛhatīs, pauṣkara, bhārgī, śaṭī, śṛṅgī, and durālabhā,
the seeds of vatsaka, paṭola, and kaṭurohiṇī:
this group beginning with bṛhatī is said to remove <s>sannipāta</s> fever.

children.text: kāsādiṣu ca sarveṣu dadyāt sopadraveṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: It should be given in all conditions beginning with cough, and in those accompanied by complications.
Decoctions and gruels that destroy thirst and fever
have been specified in the chapter on medicines; the physician should employ those also.
For fevers which are not pacified by decoctions, emetics, fasting therapies, and light foods

children.text: rūkṣasya ye na śāmyanti sarpisteṣāṃ bhiṣagjitam ||
children.translated_text: in a dry patient, ghee is the physician's victorious remedy.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ tejo jvarakaraṃ tejasā rūkṣitasya ca
children.translated_text: Dry heat produces fever; and in one dried out by heat,

children.text: yaḥ syādanubalo dhātuḥ snehavadhyaḥ sa cānilaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the subsidiary <s>dhātu</s> that arises is <s>vāta</s>, and it is to be overcome by unction.

children.text: kaṣāyāḥ sarva evaite sarpiṣā saha yojitāḥ
children.translated_text: All these decoctions, combined with ghee,
should be used for the pacification of fever; they kindle <s>agni</s> and are wholesome.
Pippalī, sandalwood, musta, uśīra, and kaṭurohiṇī,
kaliṅgaka, tāmalakī, sārivā, ativisā, and sthirā,
raisins, āmalaka, bilva, trāyamāṇā, and nidigdhikā:
ghee prepared with these at once dispels chronic fever.
It checks wasting, cough, headache, pain in the side, halīmaka,
burning in the shoulders, and irregular <s>agni</s>.
Vasā, guḍūcī, triphalā, trāyamāṇā, and yavāsaka

children.text: paktvā tena kaṣāyeṇa payasā dviguṇena ca ||
children.translated_text: After cooking it with that decoction and with twice as much milk,
with long pepper, musta, grapes, sandalwood, blue lotus, and dry ginger
made into a paste, one should cook the ghee, which removes chronic fever.

children.text: balāṃ śvadaṃṣṭrāṃ bṛhatīṃ kalasīṃ dhāvanīṃ sthirām
children.translated_text: Bala, śvadaṃṣṭrā, bṛhatī, kalasī, dhāvanī, sthirā,
neem, parpaṭaka, musta, trāyamāṇā, and durālabhā:
after making a decoction from these, for the paste one should add tāmalakī and śaṭī,
grapes, puṣkaramūla, medā, and āmalakī fruits.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ payaśca tat siddhaṃ sarpirjvaraharaṃ param
children.translated_text: Ghee and milk cooked with that become an excellent fever-removing ghee;
it removes wasting, cough, headache, side pain, and burning in the shoulders.
For patients with fever and many aggravated <s>doṣa</s>s, both upward and downward, the wise physician
should administer cleansing therapy at the proper time, as will be taught in the section on preparations.
Madana, or else [madana] combined with long peppers, kaliṅga, or licorice,
should be drunk with warm water as an emetic for the pacification of fever.
With honey-water, with sugarcane juice, or with salt water,

children.text: jvare pracchardanaṃ śastaṃ madyairvā tarpaṇena vā ||
children.translated_text: induced vomiting is recommended in fever, or with wines or with a nourishing drink.
One may drink the expressed juice of grapes or āmalakī as a purgative,
or the juice of āmalakī fruits fried in ghee, which removes fever.
Or one should lick powdered trivṛt mixed with honey and ghee;
or one should drink triphalā juice with honey added and with ghee.

children.text: āragvadhaṃ vā payasā mṛdvīkānāṃ rasena vā
children.translated_text: A fever patient may drink āragvadha with milk or with the juice of grapes,

children.text: trivṛtāṃ trāyamāṇāṃ vā payasā jvaritaḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: or trivṛt or trāyamāṇā with milk.
Having drunk abhayā together with grapes, one is freed from fever;
or a man, after drinking grape juice with warm milk as the after-drink,
is released from cough, dyspnea, headache, side pain, and chronic fever
when the fever patient drinks milk boiled with the five roots.
By drinking milk decocted with castor root, one is freed from fever with griping pain;
the same applies when it is cooked with unripe bilva fruits.
Milk prepared with trikaṇṭaka, bala, vyāghrī, jaggery, and dry ginger
removes obstruction of feces and urine, and removes swelling and fever.
Milk boiled with dry ginger, grapes, ghee, honey, sugar,
and dates destroys thirst and fever.
Milk boiled with four times as much water removes fever,

children.text: dhāroṣṇaṃ vā payaḥ sadyo vātapittajvaraṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: or milk warm straight from the udder immediately conquers fever from <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
For all chronic fevers, milk is the supreme pacifier;

children.text: peyaṃ taduṣṇaṃ śītaṃ vā yathāsvaṃ bheṣajaiḥ śṛtam ||
children.translated_text: it should be drunk warm or cold, according to the case, boiled with the appropriate medicines.
One should apply fever-removing evacuative enemas and oil enemas

children.text: pakvāśayagate doṣe vakṣyante ye ca siddhiṣu ||
children.translated_text: when the <s>doṣa</s> has gone to the large intestine; those will also be described in the sections on successful treatment.
Leaves of paṭola and ariṣṭa, uśīra, caturaṅgula,

children.text: hrīberaṃ rohiṇī tiktā śvadaṃṣṭrā madanāni ca ||
children.translated_text: hrībera, rohiṇī, tiktā, śvadaṃṣṭrā, and madana fruits,

children.text: sthirā balā ca tat sarvaṃ payasyardhodake śṛtam
children.translated_text: and sthirā and bala: all this is boiled in milk with half as much water;
when only the milk remains, the decoction is combined with honey and ghee,
with pastes of madana, musta, long pepper, licorice,
and vatsaka, and one should administer it as a <s>basti</s> (enema) that removes fever.

children.text: śuddhe mārge hṛte doṣe viprasanneṣu dhātuṣu
children.translated_text: When the channels have been cleansed, the <s>doṣa</s> removed, and the bodily constituents made clear,
the patient, whose limb pain has gone and whose body feels light, quickly becomes free from fever.
One should prepare a decoction of āragvadha, uśīra, the fruit of madana,
