and the four parṇinī plants.
Priyaṅgu, madana, musta, śatāhvā, and licorice
are the paste; ghee, jaggery, and honey make the best fever-destroying enema.

children.text: guḍūcīṃ trāyamāṇāṃ ca candanaṃ madhukaṃ vṛṣam
children.translated_text: Guḍūcī, trāyamāṇā, sandalwood, licorice, vṛṣa,

children.text: sthirāṃ balāṃ pṛśniparṇīṃ madanaṃ ceti sādhayet ||
children.translated_text: sthirā, bala, pṛśniparṇī, and madana: these should be prepared.
The physician should use the juice of the meat of wild animals, together with the juice,
with a paste of pippalī fruit, musta, and licorice.
Mixed properly with a little salt and with honey and ghee as a <s>nirūha</s> (evacuative enema),
he should administer it to pacify fever and to give strength, sweat, and appetite.

children.text: jīvantīṃ madhukaṃ medāṃ pippalīṃ madanaṃ vacām
children.translated_text: Jīvantī, licorice, medā, long pepper, madana, vacā,

children.text: ṛddhiṃ rāsnāṃ balāṃ viśvaṃ śatapuṣpāṃ śatāvarīm ||
children.translated_text: ṛddhi, rāsnā, bala, viśva, śatapuṣpā, and śatāvarī:

children.text: piṣṭvā kṣīraṃ jalaṃ sarpistailaṃ ca vipacedbhiṣak
children.translated_text: after grinding them, the physician should cook milk, water, ghee, and oil with them.
One should know this unctuous preparation for an <s>anuvāsana</s> (oil enema) as one that removes fever.
An unctuous preparation boiled with paṭola, picumarda,
guḍūcī, licorice, and madana fruits is a fever-destroying oil enema.
An unctuous preparation cooked with sandalwood, aguru, kāśmarya, paṭola, licorice, and blue lotus,
removes fever and is recommended as an unctuous enema.
The head-purgation that was described in the chapter on medicines, in the section on disease and medicine,
should be performed by one who understands proper application; it removes fever.
And the oil for nasal administration and the smoking wicks that were previously
specified in the chapter on suitable quantities should also be applied in fevers.
He should have massages, ointments, and affusions carried out,
dividing fever into its two kinds, cold and hot, according to the patient's need.
The physician should administer ghee washed a thousand times, or oil beginning with sandalwood,
as an anointing that pacifies burning fever.

children.text: atha candanādyaṃ tailamupadekṣyāmaḥ candanabhadraśrīkālānusāryakālīyakapadmāpadmakośīrasārivāmadhukaprapauṇḍarīka nāgapuṣpodīcyavanyapadmotpalanalinakumudasaugandhikapuṇḍarīkaśatapatrabisamṛṇāla śālūkaśaivālakaśerukānantākuśakāśekṣudarbhaśaranalaśālimūlajambuvetasavānīragundrākakubhāsanāśvakarṇasyandana vātapothaśālatāladhavatiniśakhadirakadarakadambakāśmaryaphalasarjaplakṣavaṭakapītanodumbarāśvattha nyagrodhadhātakīdūrvetkaṭaśṛṅgāṭakamañjiṣṭhājyotiṣmatīpuṣkarabījakrauñcādanabadarīkovidārakadalīsaṃvartakāriṣṭaśataparvāśītakumbhikā śatāvarīśrīparṇīśrāvaṇīmahāśrāvaṇīrohiṇīśītapākyodanapākīkālābalāpayasyāvidārījīvakarṣabhakamedāmahāmedā madhurasarṣyaproktātṛṇaśūnyamocarasāṭarūṣakabakulakuṭajapaṭolanimbaśālmalīnārikelakharjūramṛdvīkāpriyālapriyaṅgudhanvanātmaguptāmadhūkānām anyeṣāṃ ca śītavīryāṇāṃ yathālābhamauṣadhānāṃ kaṣāyaṃ kārayet
children.translated_text: Now we shall teach the oil called <s>Candanādya</s>, beginning with sandalwood. One should prepare a decoction, as available, from sandalwood and the many cooling substances listed here: lotus and water-lily varieties, vetiver, sārivā, madhuka, nāgapuṣpa, aquatic roots and stalks, grasses, reeds, cool tree-barks and fruits, mañjiṣṭhā, śatāvarī, jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, medā, mahāmedā, and other medicines of cooling potency.

children.text: tena kaṣāyeṇa dviguṇitapayasā teṣāmeva ca kalkena kaṣāyārdhamātraṃ mṛdvagninā sādhayettailam
children.translated_text: With that decoction, with twice as much milk, and with a paste of those very substances, in a measure equal to half the decoction, one should cook the oil over a gentle fire.
This oil, when used for anointing, immediately removes <s>dāhajvara</s> (burning fever).
With these same medicines, ground smooth and made very cold, one should prepare a poultice.
Water boiled with these same medicines and then cooled should be used for immersion and affusion.
Thus ends the oil called <s>Candanādya</s>.
Affusions and immersions with honey, sour gruel, milk, curd, ghee, and water immediately remove burning fever, because they are cool to the touch.
And here there are verses:
On very cool lotus-pools, and on leaves of lotus and blue-lotus,

children.text: kadalīnāṃ ca patreṣu kṣaumeṣu vimaleṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: on leaves of plantain, and on clean linen,
cooled with sandal-water, or even in a cool shower-house,
the person afflicted by burning should lie comfortably in a room sprinkled with icy water.
He should touch the pleasant contacts of gold, conch-shell, coral, gems,
and pearls, all cooled with sandal-water.
With garlands, blue lotuses, lotuses, and various fans,
he should be fanned by things that bring cool breezes and shower sandal-water.
Rivers, ponds, lotus-pools, and lakes with clear water
are beneficial for immersion, removing burning, thirst, exhaustion, and fever.
Beloved women, acting favorably, sprinkled with sandal,
and adorned with jewels and pearls, should soothe him with the highest pleasures.
Cold foods and drinks, cool groves,
winds, and moonbeams are cool and remove burning fever.

children.text: athoṣṇābhiprāyiṇāṃ jvaritānām abhyaṅgādīn upakramān upadekṣyāmaḥ agurukuṣṭhatagarapatranaladaśaileyadhyāmakahareṇukāsthauṇeyaka kṣemakailāvarāṅgadalapuratamālapatrabhūtīkarohiṣasaralaśallakī devadārvagnimanthabilvasyonākakāśmaryapāṭalāpunarnavā vṛścīrakaṇṭakārībṛhatīśālaparṇīpṛśniparṇīmāṣaparṇīmudgaparṇīgokṣurakairaṇḍaśobhāñjanakavaruṇārkacirabilvatilvaka śaṭīpuṣkaramūlagaṇḍīrorubūkapattūrākṣīvāśmantakaśigrumātuluṅgapīlukamūlakaparṇītilaparṇīpīluparṇīmeṣaśṛṅgī hiṃsrādantaśaṭhairāvatakabhallātakāsphotakāṇḍīrātmajaikeṣīkākarañjadhānyakājamodapṛthvīkāsumukhasurasakuṭherakakālamālakaparṇāsakṣavakaphaṇijjhaka bhūstṛṇaśṛṅgaverapippalīsarṣapāśvagandhārāsnāruhārohāvacābalātibalāguḍūcī śatapuṣpāśītavallīnākulīgandhanākulīśvetājyotiṣmatīcitrakādhyaṇḍāmlacāṅgerītilabadarakulatthamāṣāṇām evaṃvidhānām anyeṣāṃ coṣṇavīryāṇāṃ yathālābhamauṣadhānāṃ kaṣāyaṃ kārayet tena kaṣāyeṇa teṣāmeva ca kalkena surāsauvīrakatuṣodakamaireyamedakadadhimaṇḍāranālakaṭvaraprativinītena tailapātraṃ vipācayet
children.translated_text: Now we shall teach procedures such as anointing for fever-patients who desire warmth. One should prepare a decoction, as available, from medicines of hot potency such as aguru, kuṣṭha, tagara, leaf of nalada, śaileya, dhyāmaka, hareṇukā, sthauneyaka, devadāru, agnimantha, bilva, the bṛhat-pañcamūla and laghu-pañcamūla groups, castor, śobhāñjana, varuṇa, arka, śaṭī, puṣkaramūla, śigru, mātuluṅga, pīlu, sesame, hiṃsrā, bhallātaka, karañja, coriander, ajamodā, pṛthvīkā, surasa, ginger, long pepper, mustard, aśvagandhā, rāsnā, vacā, balā, atibalā, guḍūcī, śatapuṣpā, citraka, sour greens, sesame, jujube, horse-gram, black gram, and other such substances. With that decoction, with a paste of those same drugs, and with surā, sauvīraka, tuṣodaka, maireya, medaka, curd-whey, āranāla, and kaṭvara as modifying liquids, one should cook a vessel of oil.

children.text: tena sukhoṣṇena tailenoṣṇābhiprāyiṇaṃ jvaritamabhyañjyāt tathā śītajvaraḥ praśāmyati etaireva cauṣadhaiḥ ślakṣṇapiṣṭaiḥ sukhoṣṇaiḥ pradehaṃ kārayet etaireva ca śṛtaṃ sukhoṣṇaṃ salilamavagāhanārthaṃ pariṣekārthaṃ ca prayuñjīta śītajvarapraśamārtham ||
children.translated_text: With that comfortably warm oil one should anoint a fever-patient who desires warmth; in this way <s>śītajvara</s> (cold fever) subsides. With these same medicines, ground smooth and made comfortably warm, one should prepare a poultice. Water boiled with these same medicines and made comfortably warm should be used for immersion and affusion, in order to pacify cold fever.
And here there are verses:
The thirteenfold <s>sveda</s> (sudation) was shown in the chapter on sudation;
when applied by one who knows the proper measure and time, it removes cold fever.

children.text: sā kuṭī tacca śayanaṃ taccāvacchādanaṃ jvaram
children.translated_text: That hut, that bed, and that covering quickly pacify
cold fever, as do dense incenses made from aguru.
Young women with lovely, well-developed limbs, through the warmth of youth,
quickly pacify cold fever by embracing him.
Fomentations, foods, and drinks that remove <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>
quickly conquer cold fever through the force of their proper combination.

children.text: vātaje śramaje caiva purāṇe kṣataje jvare
children.translated_text: In fever caused by <s>vāta</s>, in fever caused by exertion, and likewise in chronic fever and fever caused by injury,
One should know that <s>laṅghana</s> (fasting therapy) is not beneficial, and should treat them with pacifying remedies.
For after displacing the heat of the stomach, the <s>doṣa</s>s go into the <s>rasa</s> of men,
and produce fever; from that the strength of <s>agni</s> diminishes.
Just as a blazing fire, even when supplied with fuel beneath a cooking pot,
does not cook the rice properly if it is driven outward by wind,
so too, when the bodily heat is driven outward from the place of digestion by the <s>doṣa</s>s,

children.text: na pacatyabhyavahṛtaṃ kṛcchrāt pacati vā laghu ||
children.translated_text: it does not digest what has been eaten, or digests only light food with difficulty.
Therefore, for the protection of the strength of <s>agni</s>, the regimen beginning with <s>laṅghana</s> is beneficial.
For the impurities that have entered the seven <s>dhātu</s>s are digested in seven days.
For this reason fever is generally said to be free from <s>āma</s> on the eighth day.
But a man whose <s>doṣa</s>s are excited and whose <s>agni</s> is weak, if he eats heavy food especially,

children.text: mucyate sahasā prāṇaiściraṃ kliśyati vā naraḥ
children.translated_text: is suddenly released from his life-breaths, or else suffers for a long time.
For this reason, even in a <s>vāta</s> fever at the beginning, a learned physician

children.text: nāti gurvati vā snigdhaṃ bhojayet sahasā naram
children.translated_text: should not suddenly feed a man food that is too heavy or unctuous.
In fever born of <s>māruta</s>, however, at the start, even without regard for the usual sequence,
he should perform measures such as oil massage when there is no complicating association.
After making the patient drink a decoction, he should feed him with meat-soup nourishment,
and should carry out every measure that removes chronic fever.
For patients rich in <s>śleṣman</s> and not affected by <s>vāta</s>, when the fever is not hot and <s>kapha</s> predominates,
it does not reach maturation even in seven days in those whose heat is mild.
Treating that fever gradually in the manner stated, with <s>laṅghana</s>, little food, and the like,
up to the tenth day, one should then treat it with decoctions and other remedies.

children.text: sāmā ye ye ca kaphajāḥ kaphapittajvarāśca ye ||
children.translated_text: In those fevers that are with <s>āma</s>, and those that are born of <s>kapha</s>, and those fevers born of <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>,

children.text: laṅghanaṃ laṅghanīyoktaṃ teṣu kāryaṃ prati prati
children.translated_text: the <s>laṅghana</s> described for those requiring <s>laṅghana</s> should be applied in each case.
With emetics, with purgatives, and with enemas, each in its proper order,
a wise physician should treat fevers arising from <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>anila</s>.
Having understood fevers that are combined or <s>saṃnipāta</s> fevers, whether by unequal degrees or equal degrees,
he should overcome them with the medicines already stated, taking account of the order of the <s>doṣa</s>s.
A <s>saṃnipāta</s> fever should be overcome by increasing a single <s>doṣa</s>, or by reducing the one that is elevated,
or else by following the successive order of the seats of <s>kapha</s>.
At the end of a <s>saṃnipāta</s> fever, at the root of the ear, a very severe
swelling arises; because of it only an occasional person is freed.
One should quickly overcome it by bloodletting and by drinking ghee,
by applications that counter <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, by nasal medicines, and by mouthful gargles.
When a person's fever is not pacified by cold, hot, unctuous, dry, and similar measures,
and follows the branches of the body, it is pacified through the letting of blood.
When fever is caused by <s>visarpa</s> (spreading inflammation), by injury, or by eruptions,

children.text: tatrādau sarpiṣaḥ pānaṃ kaphapittottaro na cet
children.translated_text: one should begin there with drinking ghee, unless <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s> are predominant.
When an old fever persists because of weakness of the bodily <s>dhātu</s>s,

children.text: balyaiḥ saṃbṛṃhaṇais tasmād āhārais tam upācaret
children.translated_text: one should therefore treat it with strengthening and nourishing foods.
One should abandon the ordinary treatment in tertian and quartan fevers,
for in intermittent fever there is generally an association with an external factor.
One should pacify <s>vāta</s>-predominant intermittent fever with ghee and with enemas including unctuous enemas,
and with unctuous, hot foods and drinks.
One should overcome <s>pitta</s>-predominant intermittent fever by purgation, by milk, by prepared ghee,
and by bitter and cooling remedies.
Emesis, digestive treatment, dry food and drink, and further fasting,

children.text: kaṣāyoṣṇaṃ ca viṣame jvare śastaṃ kaphottare
children.translated_text: as well as hot decoction, are recommended in intermittent fever when <s>kapha</s> predominates.
Further excellent formulations that destroy intermittent fever will be taught.
A discerning physician should use them after distinguishing the <s>doṣa</s>s and the other factors.
<s>Surā</s> with its sediment is to be used for drinking; for eating, the cock,
the partridge, and the peacock are to be employed in intermittent fever.
Or one should drink six <s>pala</s>s of ghee, or use <s>abhayā</s>,

children.text: triphalāyāḥ kaṣāyaṃ vā guḍūcyā rasameva vā
children.translated_text: or a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>, or simply the juice of <s>guḍūcī</s>.
One should drink <s>nīlinī</s>, <s>ajagandhā</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, and <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>
appropriately at the onset of fever, after being prepared with oleation and sweating.

children.text: sarpiṣo mahatīṃ mātrāṃ pītvā vā chardayet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, after drinking a large dose of ghee, one should vomit again.
Or, after taking abundant food and drink, one should again expel it upward.

children.text: sānnaṃ madyaṃ prabhūtaṃ vā pītvā svapyājjvarāgame ||
children.translated_text: Or, after drinking abundant wine together with food, one should sleep at the onset of fever.
In intermittent fever one should administer either a decoction enema or a sustaining enema.
On that same day one should drink, with milk, the dung of a <s>vṛṣadaṃśa</s>,
or that of a bull with curd whey, or with <s>surā</s> and rock salt.
The use of <s>pippalī</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, curd, buttermilk, ghee,
<s>pañcagavya</s>, and milk is prescribed in intermittent fever.
Taking garlic with oil before the meal,
and eating nourishing meats of hot potency, are also prescribed.

children.text: hiṅgutulyā tu vaiyāghrī vasā nasyaṃ sasaindhavā ||
children.translated_text: The fat of a tigress, equal in amount to <s>hiṅgu</s> and mixed with rock salt, is a nasal medicine;
old ghee and the fat of a lion are used in the same way, mixed with rock salt.
Rock salt, grains of <s>pippalī</s>, and realgar,
ground with oil as eye-salve, are recommended in intermittent fever.
<s>Palaṅkaṣā</s>, leaves of <s>nimba</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>harītakī</s>,
mustard seeds with barley and ghee make a fever-destroying fumigation.

children.text: ye dhūmā dhūpanaṃ yacca nāvanaṃ cāñjanaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: Whatever smokes, fumigation, nasal medicine, and collyrium
have been prescribed for mental disorder should be applied in intermittent fever.
By wearing jewels, herbs, auspicious objects, and poisons,
and by using anti-poison remedies, fever does not arise.
the god <s>Soma</s> with his attendants, and <s>Īśvara</s> together with the host of Mothers...
Worshipping with purity and concentration, one is quickly freed from irregular fever,
praising <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the thousand-headed, all-pervading lord of moving and unmoving beings,
with a thousand names; he drives away all fevers.
Worshipping <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Indra</s>, the oblation-eater, and the <s>Himālaya</s>,
and <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the hosts of <s>Maruts</s> with sacrifice, one conquers fevers.

children.text: bhaktyā mātuḥ pituścaiva gurūṇāṃ pūjanena ca ||
children.translated_text: Through devotion to one's mother and father, and through worship of teachers,
through celibacy, austerity, truthfulness, and restraint,
through recitation, oblation, giving, and hearing the <s>Vedas</s>,
and through seeing good people, one is quickly freed from fever.
When fever is located in the <s>rasa</s>, one should prescribe emesis and fasting.
When it is located in the blood, sprinkling, anointing, and pacifying measures are likewise used.
Purgation together with fasting is beneficial when it is located in flesh and fat.
When it has gone into bone and marrow, decoction enemas should be given, together with oil enemas.
For a fever that comes from a curse, sorcery, or possession by beings,
all medicine there is held to be divine-dependent therapy.
Fever from injury disappears through drinking and anointing with ghee,
through bloodletting, wines, and suitable meat broths with rice.
For those accustomed to wine and affected by distension, it is treated with wine, broths, and food.
For those injured and wounded, it is treated by the therapy for injuries and wounds,
and through reassurance, attainment of what is desired, and pacification of <s>vāyu</s>.
Fevers born from desire, grief, and fear come to calm through things that gladden,
through desired and pleasing objects, and also through measures that counter <s>pitta</s>.
Fever arisen from anger comes to calm through good words.
A fever of anger comes to destruction through desire, and one born from desire through anger;
one arisen from fear or grief goes away through both of these.

children.text: jvarasya vegaṃ kālaṃ ca cintayañjvaryate tu yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A person who becomes feverish while contemplating the force and timing of the fever,
at the release from fever makes sounds, vomits, and moves about.
Breathing hard, discolored, with sweating limbs, he trembles and repeatedly collapses.
He talks deliriously with all his limbs hot, and may also become cold-limbed.
Unconscious and afflicted by the force of fever, he appears as if angry.
Liquid stool, accompanied by <s>doṣa</s> and sound, flows out forcefully.
The discerning person should recognize these signs at the release from fever.
A strong, usually new fever with abundant <s>doṣa</s>,
if it releases through proper treatment and the maturation of the <s>doṣa</s>, does so very violently.
Those fevers of long duration which, after producing an attack under the influence of the <s>doṣa</s>,
gradually subside have a release that is not violent.
One should know a person to be free from fever when fatigue and heat have gone,
when he is without pain, his senses are clear, and he is joined with his natural mental strength.
Whether still feverish or freed from fever, one should avoid foods and drinks
that are burning, heavy, unsuitable, or mutually incompatible.
One should avoid sexual intercourse, excessive activity, bathing, and overeating.

children.text: tathā jvaraḥ śamaṃ yāti praśānto jāyate na ca ||
children.translated_text: Thus fever goes to calm, and once pacified it does not arise again.

children.text: vyāyāmaṃ ca vyavāyaṃ ca snānaṃ caṅkramaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: One who has been freed from fever should not engage in exercise, sexual intercourse, bathing, or walking about

children.text: jvaramukto na seveta yāvanna balavān bhavet ||
children.translated_text: until he has become strong.
But if a man freed from fever, before his strength has arisen, engages in
these things that are to be avoided, his fever returns.

children.text: durhṛteṣu ca doṣeṣu yasya vā vinivartate
children.translated_text: Or when the <s>doṣa</s>s have been badly removed and fever ceases for someone,
it turns back again even through a slight lapse in regimen.
When it returns, it quickly kills a person who has long been afflicted,
who is weak and deficient in vital brilliance.
Or else the impurities may gradually reach ripening within the <s>dhātu</s>s themselves
without producing fever; even then they do harm.
They cause dejection, swelling, exhaustion, pallor, and lack of desire for food,
and itching, wheals, and pustules; they also make the digestive fire weak.
In this way other diseases too return again,
when the <s>doṣa</s>s have not been expelled, even through small unwholesome acts in people.
Therefore, even when fever has ceased, according to the condition, strength,
and vitality, one should remove the <s>doṣa</s>, or bring it to calm by treatments.
Purification by gentle purgative measures is beneficial, as are sustaining enemas.
Light soups and broths made from the meat of animals of dry land are beneficial.
Oil massage, powder rubbing, bathing, fumigation, and collyria
are beneficial in fever that has recurred, as are bitter ghees.
When fever has returned because of eating heavy, clogging, and unsuitable foods,
the procedure beginning with fasting and warm treatment should be performed as before.
Kirātatiktaka, tiktā, musta, parpaṭaka, and amṛtā,
when drunk repeatedly, destroy recurrent fever.
In each particular state of fever patients, the discerning physician,
attending to the proper sequence of fever treatment, should carry out the appropriate therapy.
Fever, king of diseases, terrible and bringing an end to all beings,
therefore should especially be striven against by the physician for its pacification.
Here is the summary verse:
The treatment of fever has been stated in due order and according to the questions
by <s>Ātreya</s> to <s>Agniveśa</s>, out of desire for the welfare of beings.
Now then, we shall explain the treatment of <s>raktapitta</s>.
Thus indeed spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.
While <s>Punarvasu</s>, self-controlled, was staying at <s>Pañcagaṅga</s>,
<s>Agniveśa</s>, free from delusion and fiery in brilliance, bowed and spoke to him:
"Blessed one, the cause of <s>raktapitta</s> has been stated together with its symptoms.

children.text: vaktavyaṃ yat paraṃ tasya vaktumarhasi tadguro ||
children.translated_text: Whatever further about it should be spoken, please speak that, teacher."
The teacher said:
One should treat <s>raktapitta</s>, a great disease, very forceful, acting swiftly like fire,
after quickly discerning its causes and symptoms.

children.text: tasyoṣṇaṃ tīkṣṇamamlaṃ ca kaṭūni lavaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: Its causes, as stated earlier, are hot, sharp, sour things, pungent and salty foods,
heat, and the burning caused by food.
Provoked by those causes, <s>pitta</s> passes into the blood;

children.text: tadyonitvāt prapannaṃ ca vardhate tat pradūṣayat ||
children.translated_text: and, since blood is its source, after entering it, it increases while corrupting it.
By its heat the liquid constituent flows from one <s>dhātu</s> (tissue element) to another <s>dhātu</s>;
through that sweating it again obtains further increase.
Because of conjunction and corruption, and because of commonality in smell and color,
the wise call the blood's <s>pitta</s> '<s>raktapitta</s>'.
It abides depending upon the spleen and the liver,
for the blood-carrying channels of embodied beings have those as their roots.

children.text: sāndraṃ sapāṇḍu sasnehaṃ picchilaṃ ca kaphānvitam
children.translated_text: When joined with <s>kapha</s>, it is thick, somewhat pale, unctuous, and slimy;

children.text: śyāvāruṇaṃ saphenaṃ ca tanu rūkṣaṃ ca vātikam ||
children.translated_text: when governed by <s>vāta</s>, it is dark reddish-brown, frothy, thin, and dry.
<s>Raktapitta</s> that belongs to <s>pitta</s> is astringent-looking, black, like cow's urine,
resembling dark green, smoke from a house, or collyrium.
From combination it has mixed signs; when all three signs are present it is due to all three <s>doṣa</s>s.
That which follows one <s>doṣa</s> is curable; that with two <s>doṣa</s>s is said to be manageable.
That which has all three <s>doṣa</s>s is incurable, as is that which occurs in one of weak digestive fire and excessive force,
or in a body wasted by diseases, in an old person, or in one who does not eat.
The course of <s>raktapitta</s> has been shown as upward and downward.
The upward course has seven kinds of openings, while the downward course has two openings.

children.text: sapta chidrāṇi śirasi dve cādhaḥ sādhyamūrdhvagam
children.translated_text: There are seven apertures in the head and two below; the upward-moving type is curable,

children.text: yāpyaṃ tvadhogaṃ mārgau tu dvāvasādhyaṃ prapadyate ||
children.translated_text: while the downward-moving type is manageable; but when it takes both paths it becomes incurable.

children.text: yadā tu sarvacchidrebhyo romakūpebhya eva ca
children.translated_text: But when it proceeds from all apertures and even from the hair follicles,

children.text: vartate tām asaṃkhyeyāṃ gatiṃ tasyāhur āntikīm ||
children.translated_text: they call that innumerable course its terminal one.
That which flows excessively by both routes,
with blood very black and like the smell of a corpse,

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭaṃ kaphavātābhyāṃ kaṇṭhe sajati cāpi yat
children.translated_text: mixed with <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, and which sticks in the throat,
and that which is overwhelmed by all the complications described,
afflicted with yellow, blue, green, and coppery colors,

children.text: kṣīṇasya kāsamānasya yacca tacca na sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: or which occurs in a wasted person who is coughing, does not succeed in treatment.
That which follows two <s>doṣa</s>s, or which, after becoming calm, repeatedly flares up,

children.text: mārgānmārgaṃ caredyadvā yāpyaṃ pittamasṛk ca tat ||
children.translated_text: or which moves from one route to another, is manageable, both the <s>pitta</s> and the blood.
<s>Raktapitta</s> of a single route, in a strong person, not too violent, newly arisen,
and free from complications, is curable in a favorable season.
Unctuous and hot things are the cause of upward <s>raktapitta</s>; hot and dry things are usually the cause
of the downward type, the latter in one case and the former in the upward type.
The upward-moving type is mixed with <s>kapha</s>; the downward-moving type follows <s>māruta</s> (vāta).
The two-routed type is connected with both <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
When <s>raktapitta</s> occurs in one whose strength and flesh are not diminished and who is eating,
being vitiated and stirred up by the <s>doṣa</s>s, it does not at first deserve restraining treatment.
If restrained at the beginning, it would cause constriction of the throat, foul smell in the nose, fainting, restraint, loss of taste, fever,
abdominal tumor, enlargement of the spleen, abdominal distension, <s>kilāsa</s> (leucoderma), and difficult urination,
skin diseases, hemorrhoids, <s>visarpa</s> (spreading erysipelas), loss of complexion, fistula,
and obstruction of intellect and senses.
Therefore one who desires success, considering strength and <s>doṣa</s>,
should at first disregard the increased <s>raktapitta</s> in a strong person.
For in embodied beings, through provoked immature <s>doṣa</s>, <s>pitta</s> and blood usually
go to increase; therefore at first it should be treated with fasting.

children.text: mārgau doṣānubandhaṃ ca nidānaṃ prasamīkṣya ca
children.translated_text: After carefully considering the routes, the connection with <s>doṣa</s>s, and the causative factor,
one should employ fasting at the beginning of <s>raktapitta</s>, or else nourishing drink.
Water boiled with hrībera, sandalwood, uśīra, musta, and parpaṭaka,
or simply boiled and cooled water, should be given to one who is thirsty.
In upward-moving disease, nourishment should be given first; in downward-moving disease, thin gruel first.
One who knows time, habituation, and associated factors, and knows the constitution and preparation, should give it.
Water boiled with dates, raisins, madhūka, and parūṣaka,
cooled after boiling, should be used with sugar for the purpose of nourishment.
One should have nourishment administered with ghee and honey, using powdered parched grain;

children.text: ūrdhvagaṃ raktapittaṃ tat pītaṃ kāle vyapohati ||
children.translated_text: when drunk at the proper time, it removes that upward-moving <s>raktapitta</s>.
For one of weak digestive fire who is accustomed to sour taste, the learned physician may prepare that also with sourness,
and should afterward give pomegranate and āmalaka for the sake of sour taste.
Śāli rice, ṣaṣṭika rice, nīvāra, koradūṣa, praśāntikā,
śyāmāka, and priyaṅgu are food for those with <s>raktapitta</s>.
Mudga beans, lentils, chickpeas, sama, kuṣṭha, and āḍhakī beans,
prepared for soups and broths, are praised for those with <s>raktapitta</s>.
Paṭola, neem, tender cane shoots, plakṣa, vetasa leaves,
kirātatiktaka vegetable, gaṇḍīra, and kaṭhillaka,
the flowers of kovidāra, and also of kāśmarya and śālmalī,
and whatever other vegetable, in the regimen of food and drink, removes <s>raktapitta</s>,
that is recommended as vegetable fare for those with <s>raktapitta</s> who are accustomed to vegetables,

children.text: svinnaṃ vā sarpiṣā bhṛṣṭaṃ yūṣavadvā vipācitam ||
children.translated_text: whether boiled, fried in ghee, or cooked like soup.
Pārāvata doves, pigeons, quails, red-eyed vartakas,
hares, kapiñjala birds, antelopes, deer, and black-tailed animals,
should be known as beneficial in <s>raktapitta</s>; their meat broths should be used.
slightly sour, not salty or only slightly salty, fried in ghee, and with sugar.
When <s>kapha</s> follows, one should give pulse soup and greens; when <s>vāta</s> follows, meat broth.
In <s>raktapitta</s>, the preparation of gruels will now be explained.
The filaments of lotus and blue lotus, <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>

children.text: jale sādhyā rase tasmin peyā syādraktapittinām ||
children.translated_text: should be cooked in water; in that decoction a drinkable gruel is suitable for patients with <s>raktapitta</s>.
Likewise, it may be made in a decoction of <s>candana</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>lodhra</s>, with <s>nāgara</s>,
and likewise also in one of <s>kirātatiktaka</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>musta</s>.
Or it may be boiled in a decoction of <s>dhātakī</s>, <s>dhanvayāsa</s>, <s>ambu</s>, and <s>bilva</s>,
or in one of <s>masūra</s> and <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>, or else in a decoction of <s>sthirā</s> and <s>mudga</s>.
Or it may be prepared in a decoction of <s>hareṇukā</s>, with ghee, or in a decoction of <s>balā</s>,

children.text: siddhāḥ pārāvatādīnāṃ rase vā syuḥ pṛthakpṛthak ||
children.translated_text: or separately in the broths of pigeon and other birds.
Thus have been stated cooling gruels that remove <s>raktapitta</s>, with honey and sugar;
and this same method of preparation should also be applied to meat broths.
Rabbit with <s>vāstuka</s> is recommended for patients with <s>raktapitta</s> when there is constipation.
When <s>vāta</s> is predominant, partridge cooked in a decoction of <s>udumbara</s> should be used.
Peacock is beneficial in a decoction of <s>plakṣa</s>, and chicken in one of <s>nyagrodha</s>;
<s>vartaka</s> and <s>krakara</s> are beneficial in a decoction of <s>bilva</s>, <s>utpala</s>, and the like.

children.text: tṛṣyate tiktakaiḥ siddhaṃ tṛṣṇāghnaṃ vā phalodakam
children.translated_text: For one who is thirsty, water prepared with bitter drugs, or fruit-water that removes thirst,
or water prepared with <s>vidārigandhā</s> and the like, or water that has been boiled and cooled, may be given.
Having understood the <s>doṣa</s>, the accompanying <s>doṣa</s>, the strength, and the diet,
one should give water to the thirsty person, even little by little, according to the discharge.
Whatever cause of <s>raktapitta</s> has been set forth,
patients with <s>raktapitta</s> who desire life and health should not resort to that.
Thus the food and drink that remove <s>raktapitta</s> have been set out in order.

children.text: vakṣyate bahudoṣāṇāṃ kāryaṃ balavatāṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: Now the treatment for those with abundant <s>doṣa</s> and strong bodies will be stated.
For one whose strength and flesh are not depleted, whose <s>raktapitta</s>
has arisen from over-nourishment, is rich in <s>doṣa</s>, and belongs to a strong-bodied person,
and who, at the proper time, is fit for purification, one should remove it without complication,
by purgation when it is in the upper part, and by emesis when it moves downward.
The wise physician should employ <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, the fruits of <s>āragvadha</s>,
<s>trāyamāṇā</s>, the root of <s>gavākṣī</s>, or <s>āmalaka</s>s,
as a purgative, with abundant honey and sugar.
Their juice is especially praised in <s>raktapitta</s>.
For emesis, there is a <s>mantha</s> mixed with <s>madana</s>, with honey and sugar,

children.text: saśarkaraṃ vā salilamikṣūṇāṃ rasa eva vā ||
children.translated_text: or water with sugar, or simply sugarcane juice.

children.text: vatsakasya phalaṃ mustaṃ madanaṃ madhukaṃ madhu
children.translated_text: The fruit of <s>vatsaka</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>madana</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and honey:
this is said to be the best emetic when <s>raktapitta</s> flows downward.
For one with an upward course, whose bowel has been purified, the regimen beginning with <s>tarpaṇa</s> is beneficial.
When it goes downward, gruel and the like are beneficial, unless <s>vāta</s> is strong.
One depleted in strength and flesh, emaciated by grief, burden, and travel,
scorched by fire or sun, or depleted by other diseases,
a pregnant woman, an old person, a child, one who is dry, or one who eats little and in measured quantity,
whom one sees as a patient with <s>raktapitta</s> not fit for emesis or not fit for purgation,

children.text: śoṣeṇa sānubandhaṃ vā tasya saṃśamanī kriyā
children.translated_text: or one whose condition is accompanied by wasting and complications: for that person, palliative treatment
is praised as supreme for <s>raktapitta</s>. Now that will be explained.
A decoction of <s>aṭarūṣaka</s>, <s>mṛdvīkā</s>, and <s>pathyā</s>, with sugar,
mixed with honey, removes dyspnea, cough, and <s>raktapitta</s>.
In a decoction of <s>aṭarūṣaka</s>, having mixed <s>priyaṅgu</s>, clay, collyrium,

children.text: vinīya lodhraṃ kṣaudraṃ ca raktapittaharaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: <s>lodhra</s>, and honey, one should drink it as a remover of <s>raktapitta</s>.
<s>padmaka</s>, lotus filament, <s>dūrvā</s>, <s>vāstūka</s>, <s>utpala</s>,

children.text: nāgapuṣpaṃ ca lodhraṃ ca tenaiva vidhinā pibet ||
children.translated_text: <s>nāgapuṣpa</s>, and <s>lodhra</s> should be drunk by the same method.
<s>prapauṇḍarīka</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and honey in the juice of horse dung,
or the root of <s>yavāsa</s> and <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> in the juice of cow dung,
having been mixed with rice-water, should be drunk as a remover of <s>raktapitta</s>.
Or, combined with honey and ghee, one should lick the juice of cow or horse dung.
The flower powders of <s>khadira</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>kovidāra</s>, and <s>śālmalī</s>
a man with <s>raktapitta</s> should lick with honey.
The powders of <s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s>, parched grain, <s>musta</s>, and date,
and also of lotus filaments, he should lick with honey.
He should lick with honey the blood of dry-land deer and birds.

children.text: sakṣaudraṃ grathite rakte lihyāt pārāvataṃ śakṛt ||
children.translated_text: When the blood is clotted, he should lick pigeon dung with honey.
<s>uśīra</s>, <s>kālīyaka</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>kaṭphala</s>, conch, and red ochre,
each separately in an amount equal to sandalwood, with sugar, and soaked in rice-washing water,

children.text: raktaṃ sapittaṃ tamakaṃ pipāsāṃ dāhaṃ ca pītāḥ śamayanti sadyaḥ
children.translated_text: when drunk, immediately pacify blood with <s>pitta</s>, <s>tamaka</s> (asthmatic oppression), thirst, and burning.

children.text: kirātatiktaṃ kramukaṃ samustaṃ prapauṇḍarīkaṃ kamalotpale ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>kirātatikta</s>, <s>kramuka</s> together with <s>musta</s>, <s>prapauṇḍarīka</s>, lotus, and blue lotus,
roots of <s>hrībera</s>, leaves of <s>paṭola</s>, <s>durālabhā</s>, <s>parpaṭaka</s>, and lotus stalk,
<s>dhanañjaya</s>, bark of <s>udumbara</s> and <s>vetasa</s>, bark of <s>nyagrodha</s>, <s>śāleya</s>, and <s>yavāsaka</s>,
<s>tugā</s>, <s>latā</s>, <s>vetasa</s>, <s>taṇḍulīya</s>, with <s>sārivā</s>, <s>mocarasa</s>, and <s>samaṅgā</s>,

children.text: pṛthak pṛthak candanayojitāni tenaiva kalpena hitāni tatra ||
children.translated_text: each separately joined with sandalwood, are beneficial there by the same preparation.

children.text: niśi sthitā vā svarasīkṛtā vā kalkīkṛtā vā mṛditāḥ śṛtā vā
children.translated_text: Whether kept overnight, made into fresh juice, made into paste, crushed, or boiled,

children.text: ete samastā gaṇaśaḥ pṛthagvā raktaṃ sapittaṃ śamayanti yogāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these preparations, all together, in groups, or separately, pacify blood with <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: mudgāḥ salājāḥ sayavāḥ sakṛṣṇāḥ sośīramustāḥ saha candanena
children.translated_text: <s>mudga</s>s with parched grain, barley, and <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, with <s>uśīra</s> and <s>musta</s> together with sandalwood,

children.text: balājale paryuṣitāḥ kaṣāyā raktaṃ sapittaṃ śamayantyudīrṇam ||
children.translated_text: kept overnight in <s>balā</s>-water as astringent decoctions, pacify aggravated blood with <s>pitta</s>.
Of waters prepared with <s>vaidūrya</s>, pearls, gems, red ochre, clay, conch shell, gold, and <s>āmalaka</s>...
By drinking honey-water and also sugarcane juice, <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorder) subsides.

children.text: uśīrapadmotpalacandanānāṃ pakvasya loṣṭasya ca yaḥ prasādaḥ
children.translated_text: The clear infusion of uśīra, lotus, blue lotus, sandalwood, and baked clay,
mixed with sugar and honey and made very cold, should be given for calming excessive bleeding.
Water prepared with priyaṅgu, kācandana, lodhra, sārivā, madhūka, mustā, abhaya, and dhātakī,

children.text: samṛtprasādaṃ saha yaṣṭikāmbunā saśarkaraṃ raktanibarhaṇaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: together with clear earth-infusion and licorice water, and with sugar, is supreme for stopping blood.
When, after the digestive fire has been kindled and <s>kapha</s> has been overcome, <s>raktapitta</s>

children.text: yadraktapittaṃ praśamaṃ na yāti tatrānilaḥ syādanu tatra kāryam ||
children.translated_text: does not come to calm through the various decoction formulas stated above, then <s>vāta</s> is involved, and the treatment should be directed to that.

children.text: chāgaṃ payaḥ syāt paramaṃ prayoge gavyaṃ śṛtaṃ pañcaguṇe jale vā
children.translated_text: Goat's milk is the best for use; or cow's milk boiled in five times its quantity of water,
with sugar and honey added, or boiled with the group beginning with vidārigandhā, should be used.

children.text: drākṣāśṛtaṃ nāgarakaiḥ śṛtaṃ vā balāśṛtaṃ gokṣurakaiḥ śṛtaṃ vā
children.translated_text: Milk boiled with grapes, or boiled with nāgara, or boiled with balā, or boiled with gokṣura,

children.text: sajīvakaṃ sarṣabhakaṃ sasarpiḥ payaḥ prayojyaṃ sitayā śṛtaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: with jīvaka and sarṣabhaka, with ghee, or boiled with sugar, should be administered.

children.text: śatāvarīgokṣurakaiḥ śṛtaṃ vā śṛtaṃ payo vāpyatha parṇinībhiḥ
children.translated_text: Or milk boiled with śatāvarī and gokṣura, or milk boiled with the parṇinī herbs,

children.text: raktaṃ nihantyāśu viśeṣatastu yanmūtramārgāt sarujaṃ prayāti ||
children.translated_text: quickly destroys bleeding, especially that which passes painfully through the urinary tract.

children.text: viśeṣato viṭpathasampravṛtte payo mataṃ mocarasena siddham
children.translated_text: Especially when it proceeds by the path of the feces, milk cooked with mocarasa is approved,
or milk cooked with banyan aerial roots or banyan shoots, or with hrībera, blue lotus, and nāgara.

children.text: kaṣāyayogān payasā purā vā pītvānu cādyāt payasaiva śālīn
children.translated_text: Or, after first drinking the decoction formulas with milk, one should eat śāli rice only with milk afterward.
Or, in excessive discharge, one should drink ghee cooked with these decoction formulas.

children.text: vāsāṃ saśākhāṃ sapalāśamūlāṃ kṛtvā kaṣāyaṃ kusumāni cāsyāḥ
children.translated_text: Having made a decoction of vāsā together with its branches, leaves, and roots, and also its flowers,

children.text: pradāya kalkaṃ vipacedghṛtaṃ tat sakṣaudramāśveva nihanti raktam ||
children.translated_text: one should add the paste and cook ghee with it; taken with honey, it quickly stops blood.
Thus the vāsā-ghee.
Ghee cooked with the expressed juice of palāśa stalks, with a paste of that same plant, and with honey-liquid
should be licked; likewise ghee cooked with vatsaka paste, and likewise ghee cooked with samaṅgā, blue lotus, and lodhra.
This same procedure applies to trāyamāṇā, also to udumbara, and to paṭola leaf.

children.text: sarpīṃṣi pittajvaranāśanāni sarvāṇi śastāni ca raktapitte ||
children.translated_text: All these ghees destroy <s>pittajvara</s> (pitta fever) and are recommended in <s>raktapitta</s>.
Oil applications, sprinklings, affusions, immersions, beds, and dwellings,

children.text: śīto vidhirbastividhānamagryaṃ pittajvare yat praśamāya diṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: the cooling regimen, and the foremost procedure of <s>basti</s> (enema), which are prescribed for pacifying <s>pittajvara</s>,

children.text: tadraktapitte nikhilena kāryaṃ kālaṃ ca mātrāṃ ca purā samīkṣya
children.translated_text: should be carried out completely in <s>raktapitta</s>, after first considering the season and the dose.

children.text: sarpirguḍā ye ca hitāḥ kṣatebhyaste raktapittaṃ śamayanti sadyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Ghee, jaggery, and the things beneficial for wounds immediately pacify <s>raktapitta</s>.

children.text: kaphānubandhe rudhire sapitte kaṇṭhāgate syādgrathite prayogaḥ
children.translated_text: When blood, along with <s>pitta</s> and with an association of <s>kapha</s>, has reached the throat and is clotted, the application should be
of honey and ghee, properly combined, and also of the alkali made from blue-lotus stalk.
Likewise, alkalis of lotus stalks, lotus and blue-lotus filaments, and of palāśa and priyaṅgu,

children.text: tathā madhūkasya tathāsanasya kṣārāḥ prayojyā vidhinaiva tena ||
children.translated_text: and also of madhūka and asana, should be used according to that same rule.
Śatāvarī, pomegranate, tintiḍīka, kākolī, medā, madhuka, and vidārī,

children.text: piṣṭvā ca mūlaṃ phalapūrakasya ghṛtaṃ pacet kṣīracaturguṇaṃ jñaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the root of phalapūraka should be ground; the knowledgeable physician should cook ghee with four times as much milk.
That ghee destroys cough, fever, distension, constipation, colic, and <s>raktapitta</s>.

children.text: yat pañcamūlairatha pañcabhirvā siddhaṃ ghṛtaṃ tacca tadarthakāri ||
children.translated_text: Ghee prepared with the five roots, or with another set of five, serves that same purpose.
Thus the śatāvarī-group ghee.

children.text: kaṣāyayogā ya ihopadiṣṭāste cāvapīḍe bhiṣajā prayojyāḥ
children.translated_text: The decoction formulas taught here should also be used by the physician as <s>avapīḍa</s> (pressed nasal application),

children.text: ghrāṇāt pravṛttaṃ rudhiraṃ sapītaṃ yadā bhavenniḥsṛtaduṣṭadoṣam ||
children.translated_text: when blood flowing from the nose, accompanied by <s>pitta</s>, appears after the vitiated <s>doṣa</s> has come out.
For when the blood is vitiated, if the <s>avapīḍa</s> is obstructed, corrupt catarrh and disorders of the head arise.

children.text: raktaṃ sapūyaṃ kuṇapaśca gandhaḥ syād ghrāṇanāśaḥ kṛmayaśca duṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is blood with pus, a corpse-like smell, loss of smell, and harmful worms.
Blue lotus combined with red ochre and conch, together with sandalwood, should be used with sugar-water as a nasal medicine.
So too mango-stone juice, samaṅgā, and preparations with dhātakī, mocarasa, and lodhra.
Nasal medicine may be made from grape juice, sugarcane juice, milk, or the expressed juice of dūrvā,
and also from roots of yavāsa, onion root, or water of pomegranate flowers.

children.text: priyālatailaṃ madhukaṃ payaśca siddhaṃ ghṛtaṃ māhiṣam ājikaṃ vā
children.translated_text: Priyāla oil, madhuka, and milk, or ghee prepared from buffalo or goat milk,

children.text: āmrāsthipūrvaiḥ payasā ca nasyaṃ sasārivaiḥ syāt kamalotpalaiśca ||
children.translated_text: may serve as nasal medicine; so may the substances beginning with mango-stone, with milk, and with sārivā, lotus, and blue lotus.

children.text: bhadraśriyaṃ lohitacandanaṃ ca prapauṇḍarīkaṃ kamalotpale ca
children.translated_text: Bhadraśriyā, red sandalwood, prapauṇḍarīka, lotus, and blue lotus,
uśīra, vāṇīra water, lotus stalk, sahasravīryā, madhuka, and payasyā,
roots of śāli and sugarcane, roots of yavāsa and gundrā, and roots of reeds, kuśa, and kāśa,
kucandana, śaivala, anantā, kālānusārī, grass roots, and ṛddhi,

children.text: mūlāni puṣpāṇi ca vārijānāṃ pralepanaṃ puṣkariṇīmṛdaśca
children.translated_text: the roots and flowers of water-born plants, and mud from a lotus pond as a coating,
and udumbara, aśvattha, madhūka, lodhra, astringent trees, and all cool substances:
in the preparation of poultices, in sprinkling, in immersion, and in medicated ghee and oil,

children.text: raktasya pittasya ca śāntimicchan bhadraśriyādīni bhiṣak prayuñjyāt ||
children.translated_text: the physician who desires the pacification of blood and <s>pitta</s> should use the group beginning with bhadraśriyā.

children.text: dhārāgṛhaṃ bhūmigṛhaṃ suśītaṃ vanaṃ ca ramyaṃ jalavātaśītam
children.translated_text: A water-cooled pavilion, an underground room that is very cool, and a pleasant forest cooled by water and wind,
and, in burning sensation, the touch of vessels made of vaidūrya, pearl, and jewel, cooled by cold water, are beneficial.

children.text: patrāṇi puṣpāṇi ca vārijānāṃ kṣaumaṃ ca śītaṃ kadalīdalāni
children.translated_text: Leaves and flowers of water-born plants, cool linen cloth, and plantain leaves are also cooling.

children.text: pracchādanārthaṃ śayanāsanānāṃ padmotpalānāṃ ca dalāḥ praśastāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For covering beds and seats, leaves of lotuses and blue lotuses are recommended.
Also recommended in burning are the touches of beloved, beautiful women smeared with <s>priyaṅgu</s> and sandalwood,

children.text: dāhe praśastāḥ sajalāḥ suśītāḥ padmotpalānāṃ ca kalāpavātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and moist, very cool breezes from clusters of lotuses and blue lotuses.
Rivers, lakes, caves of the Himalaya, moonrises, and lotus ponds,

children.text: mano'nukūlāḥ śiśirāśca sarvāḥ kathāḥ saraktaṃ śamayanti pittam ||
children.translated_text: and all cool conversations pleasing to the mind calm <s>pitta</s> along with blood.
Here are two verses:

children.text: hetuṃ vṛddhiṃ saṃjñāṃ sthānaṃ liṅgaṃ pṛthak praduṣṭasya
children.translated_text: The cause, increase, definition, seat, and signs of separately vitiated <s>raktapitta</s>,
its two routes, what is curable, incurable, and manageable, and the sequence of treatment,

children.text: pānānnamiṣṭameva ca varjyaṃ saṃśodhanaṃ ca śamanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: as well as desirable food and drink, what is to be avoided, purification, and pacification,
the teacher has stated exactly in the treatment of <s>raktapitta</s>.
Now then, we shall explain the treatment of <s>gulma</s>.
Thus indeed spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.
<s>Punarvasu</s>, like a father and a refuge for all creatures, lord of what has been and what will be,

children.text: cikitsitaṃ gulmanibarhaṇārthaṃ provāca siddhaṃ vadatāṃ variṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the best of speakers, proclaimed the accomplished treatment for the removal of <s>gulma</s>.
Because of excessive discharge of stool, phlegm, or bile, or because of pressure by those same humors when increased,
or because urges, when risen, are obstructed downward, or because of external blows and excessive pressure,
or because dry foods and drinks have been overused, because of grief, or because of wrong treatment,

children.text: viceṣṭitairvā viṣamātimātraiḥ koṣṭhe prakopaṃ samupaiti vāyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: or because of irregular or excessive bodily activities, <s>vāyu</s> becomes aggravated in the alimentary tract.

children.text: kaphaṃ ca pittaṃ ca sa duṣṭavāyuruddhūya mārgān vinibadhya tābhyām
children.translated_text: That vitiated <s>vāyu</s>, stirring up <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s> and blocking the channels with them,
causes pain in the heart region, navel, sides, belly, and bladder; then, with its path obstructed, it does not move.

children.text: pakvāśaye pittakaphāśaye vā sthitaḥ svatantraḥ parasaṃśrayo vā
children.translated_text: Situated in the colon or in the seat of <s>pitta</s> or <s>kapha</s>, either independent or dependent on another,
because it is compacted and perceptible to touch, the <s>gulma</s> receives its name according to the <s>doṣa</s>.

children.text: bastau ca nābhyāṃ hṛdi pārśvayorvā sthānāni gulmasya bhavanti pañca
children.translated_text: The bladder, navel, heart, and the two sides are the five locations of <s>gulma</s>.

children.text: pañcātmakasya prabhavaṃ tu tasya vakṣyāmi liṅgāni cikitsitaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: I shall state the origin, signs, and treatment of that fivefold disorder.
Dry food and drink, irregular or excessive quantity, improper activity, and suppression of urges,
grief, trauma, excessive depletion of feces, and fasting are the causes of <s>vāta-gulma</s>.
That which produces variations in location, shape, and pain, obstruction of stool and flatus, and dryness of the throat and mouth,
dark-reddish coloration, cold fever, and pain in the heart, abdomen, sides, shoulders, and head,

children.text: karoti jīrṇe 'bhyadhikaṃ prakopaṃ bhukte mṛdutvaṃ samupaiti yaśca
children.translated_text: which becomes more aggravated when digestion is complete and becomes softer after food has been eaten,

children.text: vātāt sa gulmo na ca tatra rūkṣaṃ kaṣāyatiktaṃ kaṭu copaśete ||
children.translated_text: is a <s>gulma</s> due to <s>vāta</s>; in that condition dry, astringent, bitter, and pungent things are not suitable.
Pungent, sour, sharp, hot, burning, and dry things, anger, excessive liquor, sun, and fire,

children.text: āmābhighāto rudhiraṃ ca duṣṭaṃ paittasya gulmasya nimittamuktam ||
children.translated_text: trauma during indigestion and vitiated blood are said to be the causes of <s>pitta-gulma</s>.

children.text: jvaraḥ pipāsā vadanāṅgarāgaḥ śūlaṃ mahajjīryati bhojane ca
children.translated_text: Fever, thirst, redness of the face and limbs, severe pain, and distress while food is digesting,

children.text: svedo vidāho vraṇavacca gulmaḥ sparśāsahaḥ paittikagulmarūpam ||
children.translated_text: sweating, burning, and a <s>gulma</s> like an ulcer, intolerant of touch, are the form of a <s>paittika gulma</s>.

children.text: śītaṃ guru snigdhamaceṣṭanaṃ ca saṃpūraṇaṃ prasvapanaṃ divā ca
children.translated_text: Cold, heavy, and unctuous things, inactivity, overfilling, sleep, and sleeping by day

children.text: gulmasya hetuḥ kaphasaṃbhavasya sarvastu diṣṭo nicayātmakasya ||
children.translated_text: are the causes of a <s>gulma</s> arising from <s>kapha</s>; all these are also indicated for one consisting of accumulation.
Stiffness, cold fever, lassitude of the body, nausea, cough, anorexia, and heaviness,

children.text: śaityaṃ rugalpā kaṭhinonnatatvaṃ gulmasya rūpāṇi kaphātmakasya ||
children.translated_text: coldness, slight pain, and hardness with elevation are the forms of a <s>kapha</s>-type <s>gulma</s>.
Having observed the causes and signs in <s>gulma</s>, and the strength or weakness of the <s>doṣa</s>s in one involving two <s>doṣa</s>s,
one should diagnose the other three mixed <s>gulma</s>s by their combined signs, for the purpose of preparing medicines.
A <s>gulma</s> that is extremely painful, surrounded by burning, stone-like, dense and raised, rapidly suppurating, and terrible,
and that takes away mental strength, bodily strength, digestive fire, and vitality, should be declared incurable and arising from all three <s>doṣa</s>s.
In a woman, during the season because of lack of food, fear, drying measures, and suppression of urges,
and because of obstructive measures, emetics, and disorders of the womb, a blood-born <s>gulma</s> arises.

children.text: yaḥ spandate piṇḍita eva nāṅgaiścirāt saśūlaḥ samagarbhaliṅgaḥ
children.translated_text: That which pulsates while being a compact mass, not with limbs, which is long-standing, painful, and has all the signs of pregnancy,

children.text: sa raudhiraḥ strībhava eva gulmo māse vyatīte daśame cikitsyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is the blood-born <s>gulma</s> occurring in women; after the tenth month has passed, it should be treated.
Now I shall explain the established sequence of treatment that destroys <s>gulma</s>s in patients with <s>gulma</s>,
and, after that, formulas that remove <s>gulma</s>.
A <s>vātika gulma</s>, produced by dryness and exercise and having intense pain,
with stool and flatus obstructed, should first be treated with oleation.
With foods, oil massage, drinks, evacuative enemas, and accompanying unctuous enemas,
when he has been made unctuous, fomentation should be performed by the physician for the pacification of <s>gulma</s>.
After making the channels soft and overcoming the violent <s>vāta</s>,
fomentation, in one who has been oleated, breaks the obstruction and removes the <s>gulma</s>.
Drinking unctuous substances is beneficial in <s>gulma</s>, especially when it is above the navel;
when it has gone to the colon, enema is beneficial, and when it is lodged in the abdomen, both are beneficial.
When the digestive fire is kindled in <s>vātika gulma</s>, and stool and flatus are obstructed,
one should administer nourishing foods and drinks that are unctuous and warm.
Again and again, drinking unctuous substances, evacuative enemas, and oil enemas
should be used in <s>vāta-gulma</s>s, while guarding against <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: kapho vāte jitaprāye pittaṃ śoṇitameva vā
children.translated_text: If, when <s>vāta</s> has mostly been conquered, <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, or blood

children.text: yadi kupyati vā tasya kriyamāṇe cikitsite ||
children.translated_text: becomes aggravated during the treatment being performed for him,
then the physician should perform a treatment that conquers the <s>doṣa</s> which is predominant there.

children.text: ādāvante ca madhye ca mārutaṃ parirakṣatā ||
children.translated_text: One who protects <s>māruta</s> (vāta) at the beginning, end, and middle should proceed thus.
If, in vāta-gulma, increased <s>kapha</s> has destroyed the digestive fire and appetite,
and causes nausea, heaviness, and drowsiness, he should make the patient vomit it out.
In pains, distension, and constipation, and in gulma dominated by vāta and kapha,
suppositories, pills, and powders that remove kapha and vāta are beneficial.

children.text: pittaṃ vā yadi saṃvṛddhaṃ saṃtāpaṃ vātagulminaḥ
children.translated_text: Or if increased <s>pitta</s> produces burning heat in one with vāta-gulma,
he should be purged with unctuous medicines that direct vāta downward.
If a gulma produced by anila and the other <s>doṣa</s>s, though properly treated by the physician,
does not subside, it subsides through the letting of blood.
In a pitta-type gulma stirred up by unctuous and hot causes, a mild evacuative is beneficial;

children.text: rūkṣoṣṇena tu sambhūte sarpiḥ praśamanaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: but when it has arisen from dry and hot causes, ghee is the supreme pacifying remedy.

children.text: pittaṃ vā pittagulmaṃ vā jñātvā pakvāśayasthitam
children.translated_text: When he has recognized pitta, or a pitta-gulma, as located in the large intestine,
one who knows the proper time should at once remove it with bitter milk-enemas.
Or the physician should purge him with pleasantly warm milk mixed with bitter drugs,
or with tailvaka ghee, while considering the strength of his digestive fire.
In thirst, fever, intense burning, pain, sweating, weakness of digestive fire,
and also anorexia in patients with gulma, he should let blood alone.

children.text: chinnamūlā vidahyante na gulmā yānti ca kṣayam
children.translated_text: When their root has been cut, gulmas do not become inflamed and go on to destruction.

children.text: raktaṃ hi vyamlatāṃ yāti tacca nāsti na cāsti ruk ||
children.translated_text: For the blood becomes excessively sour; when that is absent, pain too is absent.
When the <s>doṣa</s>s have been removed, and the patient is wasted but has been nourished with soups of dry-land animals,
and has recovered, though some pain remains, he should again be made accustomed to ghee.
If, because blood and pitta are greatly increased and no other treatment is available,

children.text: yadi gulmo vidahyeta śastraṃ tatra bhiṣagjitam ||
children.translated_text: the gulma suppurates, surgery is the physician's approved treatment there.
A gulma that is heavy, hard in form, lodged hidden within the flesh,
unchanged in color, and fixed is said to be unripe.
One should know a gulma to be suppurating when there is burning, pain, distress, agitation, sleeplessness, restlessness, and fever;
that gulma should be treated with poultices.
When a gulma has signs of suppuration, protrudes outward, and is raised up,
is dark, bordered with redness, and on touch resembles a bladder,
rises again when pressed, is rigid and numb, and because of pressure on its side
the pain gathers at that very place, one should declare the gulma to be fully suppurated.
There, in the procedure of treatment, the authority belongs to the followers of <s>Dhanvantari</s>,
to physicians trained in puncturing, cleansing, and healing.
This also is the sign of one located internally as it is suppurating:
swelling in the cardiac and epigastric region and a movement out toward the side.
When ripe, it moistens the channels and moves either upward or downward.
If that <s>doṣa</s> begins to flow out by itself, he should observe it with wholesome foods.
For ten or twelve days the physician should guard against complications;

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ hitaṃ pānaṃ sarpiṣaḥ saviśodhanam ||
children.translated_text: after that, drinking ghee together with a purifying measure is beneficial.
For one who has been purified, bitter ghee with honey is recommended as a course of treatment.
When a kapha-type gulma has arisen from cold, heavy, and unctuous causes,
if the patient is unfit for emesis and has little body and weak digestive fire, he should first be made to fast.
The patient whose digestive fire is weak, whose pain is mild, and whose abdomen is heavy and sluggish,
with nausea and anorexia, is a gulma patient fit for emesis.
After emesis and fasting have been performed, he should be treated only with hot measures.
A gradual diet should be joined with medicines that are pungent and bitter.
Seeing a gulma with distension and constipation, hard and raised up,
the physician should first foment it properly; when it has been fomented, he should soften and dissolve it.
When fasting, emesis, and fomentation have been performed and the digestive fire has been kindled,
the patient with kapha-gulma should at the proper time drink ghee mixed with alkali and pungent drugs.
When he has recognized that the kapha-gulma has moved from its place,
he should cleanse it with purgatives or with unctuous enemas prepared with <s>daśamūla</s>.
When the digestive fire is weak, vāta is obstructed, and the receptacle is known to need unction,
pills, powders, and decoctions should be prescribed for patients with kapha-gulma.
A kapha-produced gulma that is deeply rooted, a great mass, hard, sluggish, and heavy
should be overcome with alkalis, fermented preparations, and cauterization.
In a kapha-predominant case, after understanding the conjunction of <s>doṣa</s>, constitution, gulma, and season,
and knowing the patient's strength and the measure of the <s>doṣa</s>s, the physician should apply alkali to the gulma.

children.text: ekāntaraṃ dvyantaraṃ vā tryahaṃ viśramya vā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He may do so every other day, every third day, or again after resting for three days,
being skilled in increasing or reducing the strength of the body and of the <s>doṣa</s>s.
For one who eats sweet, unctuous foods, meat, milk, and ghee, alkali cuts apart
the kapha again and again from its receptacle and, by its caustic nature, drains it downward.
When the digestive fire is weak and there is anorexia, for those accustomed to wine and eating with unction,
fermented preparations should be used in kapha-gulma to clear the channels.
If, through fasting, emesis, fomentations, drinking ghee, purgations,
enemas, and groups of pills, powders, alkalis, and fermented preparations,
a phlegmatic gulma does not subside because it has become deeply rooted,
cauterization after blood has been removed, with arrow-heads, iron instruments, and the like, is beneficial for him.
By its heat and sharpness, fire pacifies kapha and vāta in gulma;
and from the pacification of those two, the aggregate of the gulma breaks apart.
In cauterization here too, the strength of physicians lies with the followers of <s>Dhanvantari</s>;
in the application of alkali, the strength of physicians lies with those who know the science of alkalis.
When the <s>doṣa</s>s are mixed, this very course of treatment is to be mixed.
Now I shall state proven formulations for removing gulma.
With <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>, <s>triphala</s>, dhānya, viḍaṅga, cavya, and citraka,
made into a paste, ghee cooked together with milk removes vāta-gulma.
Thus ends the <s>Tryūṣaṇādi Ghṛta</s>.

children.text: eta eva ca kalkāḥ syuḥ kaṣāyaḥ pañcamūlikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And these same pastes may be used, with a decoction of <s>pañcamūla</s>.
Or with <s>dvipañcamūla</s>; that ghee is supreme for removing <s>gulma</s>.
Thus another <s>Tryūṣaṇādi-ghṛta</s>.
Or he should drink six <s>palas</s> of the ghee that was prescribed for <s>rājayakṣman</s>.

children.text: prasannayā vā kṣīrārthaṃ surayā dāḍimena vā
children.translated_text: Or ghee should be prepared with clear liquor, with <s>surā</s> in place of milk, with pomegranate,

children.text: dadhnaḥ sareṇa vā kāryaṃ ghṛtaṃ mārutagulmanut ||
children.translated_text: or with the watery portion of curd; it removes <s>māruta-gulma</s>.
Ghee cooked with asafoetida, <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, cumin, <s>viḍa</s> salt, pomegranate, <s>dīpyaka</s>,
<s>puṣkara</s>, the three pungents, coriander, alkali of <s>vetasa</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
with <s>śaṭī</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>ajagandhā</s>, cardamom, and <s>surasa</s>,
and with curd, removes colic and distension in those who have <s>anila-gulma</s>.
Thus the ghee beginning with asafoetida and <s>sauvarcala</s>.
One should cook ghee with <s>hapuṣā</s>, the three pungents, <s>pṛthvīkā</s>, <s>cavya</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and rock salt,
together with cumin, root of long pepper, and <s>dīpyaka</s>.
It should include the juice of <s>kola</s> and radish, and milk, curd, and pomegranate.
That is supreme for destroying <s>vāta-gulma</s> and for releasing colic and distension.
This ghee removes disorders of the womb, piles, disorders of the <s>grahaṇī</s>, dyspnea, cough, anorexia, and fever,
as well as pain in the bladder, heart, and side.
Thus the ghee beginning with <s>hapuṣā</s>.
There should be one and a half <s>picus</s> of long pepper, two <s>palas</s> of pomegranate, one <s>pala</s>
of coriander, five <s>palas</s> of ghee, one <s>karṣa</s> of dry ginger, and four times as much milk.
Ghee prepared with these immediately removes <s>vāta-gulma</s>,
pain in the womb, headache, piles, and irregular fever.
Thus the ghee beginning with long pepper.
The groups of herbs for ghee that have been taught here

children.text: te cūrṇayogā vartyastāḥ kaṣāyāste ca gulminām ||
children.translated_text: are also to be used as powder formulas, suppositories, and decoctions for those with <s>gulma</s>.
They should be drunk with <s>kola</s>, pomegranate, hot water, the upper part of <s>surā</s>, sour gruel,
or with citron juice; they remove colic and distension.
Or powders soaked with the juice of citron
should be made into suppositories and pills for calming the pain of <s>gulma</s> and distension.
Asafoetida, the three pungents, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>hapuṣā</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, <s>śaṭī</s>,
<s>ajamodā</s>, <s>ajagandhā</s>, tamarind, and sour <s>vetasa</s>,
pomegranate, <s>puṣkara</s>, coriander, cumin, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>vacā</s>,

children.text: dvau kṣārau lavaṇe dve ca cavyaṃ caikatra cūrṇayet ||
children.translated_text: the two alkalis, the two salts, and <s>cavya</s> should be powdered together.
This powder should be used, without harm, in foods and drinks,
or it should be drunk before meals with liquor or hot water.
It is used for pain in the side, heart, and bladder, for <s>gulma</s> caused by <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>,

children.text: ānāhe mūtrakṛcchre ca śūle ca gudayonije ||
children.translated_text: for distension, difficult urination, and pain arising in the anus or womb,
for disorders of the <s>grahaṇī</s> and piles, splenic disease, anemia, and anorexia,
for obstruction in the chest, hiccup, cough, dyspnea, and constriction of the throat.
Or this powder, soaked with the juice of citron
many times, should be made into pills; they will be still more effective.
Thus the asafoetida powder and pill.
Citron juice, asafoetida, pomegranate, <s>viḍa</s> salt, and rock salt
should be drunk with the upper part of <s>surā</s>; this removes the pain of <s>vāta-gulma</s>.
One should prepare powder from <s>śaṭī</s>, <s>puṣkara</s>, asafoetida, sour <s>vetasa</s>, alkali, and <s>citraka</s>,

children.text: dhānyakaṃ ca yavānīṃ ca viḍaṅgaṃ saindhavaṃ vacām ||
children.translated_text: as well as coriander, <s>yavānī</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, rock salt, and <s>vacā</s>,
with <s>cavya</s>, root of long pepper, <s>ajagandhā</s>, and pomegranate,

children.text: ajājīṃ cājamodāṃ ca cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: and also cumin and <s>ajamodā</s>, and should administer it.
After soaking it again with citron juice or with honey-vinegar,
one should grind it well and make it into pills the size of <s>kola</s> fruits.
This pill removes <s>gulma</s>, splenic disease, distension, dyspnea, cough, anorexia,
hiccup, heart disease, piles, and various pains of the head,
anemia, agitation of <s>kapha</s>, and all kinds of dysentery,
as well as pain in the side, heart, and bladder.

children.text: nāgarārdhapalaṃ piṣṭvā dve pale luñcitasya ca
children.translated_text: Having ground half a <s>pala</s> of dry ginger, and two <s>palas</s> of hulled
sesame with one <s>pala</s> of jaggery, he should drink it with warm milk.
It destroys <s>vāta-gulma</s>, upward movement of <s>vāta</s>, and pain in the womb.
He should drink castor oil mixed with the upper part of <s>vāruṇī</s>.
A man with <s>vāta-gulma</s> should drink that same oil with milk.
It is beneficial first when phlegm is secondary, and best when bile is secondary.
One should cook four <s>palas</s> of clean, dried garlic
in milk and water increased eightfold, and he should drink it when only the milk remains.
That milk quickly cures <s>vāta-gulma</s>, upward movement of <s>vāta</s>, sciatica, irregular fever,
heart disease, abscess, and swelling.
Thus garlic milk.
Oil, clear liquor, cow urine, sour gruel, and the first part of barley
when drunk together cure <s>gulma</s>, abdominal enlargement, and distension.
Thus the group of five oils.
He should drink <s>śilājatu</s> with an alkaline decoction of <s>pañcamūla</s>.
By using it, he is freed from <s>vāta-gulma</s>.
Thus the use of <s>śilājatu</s>.
After eating unctuous cakes with long-pepper soup
or with the juice of radishes, one is freed from upward movement of <s>vāta</s> and from <s>vāta-gulma</s>.
One should foment the patient with <s>vāta-gulma</s> who is afflicted by colic, distension, and obstruction,
with the fomentations taught in the section on fomentation: tubular, slab, and mixed fomentations.
One should know <s>basti</s> therapy to be supreme in destroying <s>gulma</s>, for after first conquering <s>māruta</s>

children.text: sve sthāne prathamaṃ jitvā sadyo gulmamapohati ||
children.translated_text: in its own place, it immediately removes <s>gulma</s>.
Therefore <s>gulma</s>s arising from <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s> are pacified
when they are treated repeatedly with evacuative enemas and with accompanying unctuous enemas.

children.text: gulmaghnā vividhā diṣṭāḥ siddhāḥ siddhiṣu bastayaḥ
children.translated_text: Various accomplished enemas that destroy <s>gulma</s> have been prescribed in the sections on successful treatment,
and oils that destroy <s>gulma</s> will be taught in the section on <s>vāta</s> disorders.
When those oils are used in <s>māruta</s>-born <s>gulma</s> for drinking, massage, and unctuous enema,
they quickly succeed, for oil is supreme in conquering <s>anila</s>.
The very ghee mentioned before, mixed with powder of <s>nīlinī</s>,
should be given to one with accumulated impurity; it is a cleansing remedy for a patient with <s>vāta-gulma</s>.
For purification, ghee should be given with <s>nīlinī</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, and <s>kampillaka</s>,
together with <s>biḍa</s> salt, alkali, and dry ginger.
One should cook <s>nīlinī</s>, <s>triphala</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>kaṭukarohiṇī</s>,
<s>viḍaṅga</s>, and <s>vyāghrī</s>, one pala each, in one āḍhaka of water.
When that has been reduced to one quarter, one should cook one prastha of ghee with it,
combining it with one prastha of curds and one pala of the milky juice of <s>sudhā</s>.
Then one should give a pala of the ghee mixed with the thin gruel-water of <s>yavāgū</s>;
when it is digested and the patient has been well purged, one should feed him a meal with meat-soup.
This ghee removes <s>gulma</s>, skin disease, abdominal enlargement, discolored patches, swelling, anemia, fever,
leucoderma, spleen disease, and insanity.
Thus ends the ghee beginning with <s>nīlinī</s>.
Fowls, peacocks, partridges, cranes, and quails,
rice, wine, and ghee are successfully used by physicians for <s>vāta-gulma</s>.
Food that is hot, liquid, and unctuous is beneficial for patients with <s>vāta-gulma</s>,
as is drinking <s>vāruṇī</s> together with gruel-water, or water boiled with coriander.

children.text: mande 'gnau vardhate gulmo dīpte cāgnau praśāmyati
children.translated_text: When the digestive fire is weak, <s>gulma</s> increases; when the digestive fire is strong, it subsides.
Therefore one should practice neither excessive satiety nor excessive fasting.
In every case of <s>gulma</s>, when oleation and fomentation have first been properly applied,

children.text: yā kriyā kriyate siddhiṃ sā yāti na virūkṣite ||
children.translated_text: whatever treatment is performed succeeds, not when the patient has been dried out.
Having understood the urgency, the physician should treat <s>pitta-gulma</s>
with purgative-prepared ghee or with bitter ghee.
The bark of <s>rohiṇī</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, neem, <s>madhuka</s>, and <s>triphala</s>,
one karṣa each, along with <s>trāyamāṇā</s>, and one pala each of <s>paṭola</s> and <s>trivṛt</s>,
and two palas of lentils are to be boiled in eight times as much water.
From the remaining decoction, equal in quantity to the ghee, one should prepare four palas of ghee.

children.text: pibet saṃmūrchitaṃ tena gulmaḥ śāmyati paittikaḥ
children.translated_text: One should drink it when it is well blended with that decoction; a <s>paittika gulma</s> is pacified by it,

children.text: jvarastṛṣṇā ca śūlaṃ ca bhramo mūrcchārucistathā ||
children.translated_text: as are fever, thirst, pain, dizziness, fainting, and anorexia.
Thus ends the ghee beginning with <s>rohiṇī</s>.
Four palas of <s>trāyamāṇā</s> should be cooked in ten times as much water.
When it remains as one fifth and has been strained, it should be combined with pastes of one karṣa each:
<s>rohiṇī</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>trāyamāṇā</s>, and <s>durālabhā</s>,
and with pastes of <s>tāmalakī</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, sandalwood, and blue lotus.

children.text: rasasyāmalakānāṃ ca kṣīrasya ca ghṛtasya ca
children.translated_text: Adding eight palas each of the juice of <s>āmalaka</s>, milk, and ghee,
one should cook it properly.
This excellent ghee destroys <s>gulma</s> arising from <s>pitta</s> and blood, erysipelas, <s>paittika</s> fever,
heart disease, jaundice, and skin disease.
Thus ends the ghee beginning with <s>trāyamāṇā</s>.
One should cook a quarter-part of ghee with the juices of <s>āmalaka</s> and sugarcane.
One should drink the ghee prepared with a quarter-part of <s>pathyā</s>; it removes <s>pitta-gulma</s>.
Thus ends the ghee beginning with <s>āmalaka</s>.
Grapes, <s>madhūka</s>, dates, <s>vidārī</s> together with <s>śatāvarī</s>,
<s>parūṣaka</s> fruits, and <s>triphala</s>, each in the measure of a pala, should be boiled.
When one āḍhaka of water has been reduced to a quarter, one should add juice of <s>āmalaka</s>,
ghee, sugarcane juice, milk, and a quarter-part paste of <s>abhayā</s>.
One should cook that ghee; when it is prepared, it should have a quarter-part each of sugar and honey added.
By use, it destroys <s>pitta-gulma</s> and removes all disorders of <s>pitta</s>.
Thus ends the ghee beginning with grapes.
Having pounded <s>vṛṣa</s> with its root, one should cook it in eight times as much water.
When one eighth remains, one should add a paste of its own flowers.

children.text: tena siddhaṃ ghṛtaṃ śītaṃ sakṣaudraṃ pittagulmanut
children.translated_text: Ghee prepared with that and taken cold with honey removes <s>pitta-gulma</s>;
it destroys bleeding disorder, fever, dyspnea, cough, and heart disease.
Thus ends <s>vāsā-ghṛta</s>.
Two palas of <s>trāyamāṇā</s>, boiled in two prasthas of water,
strained when one eighth remains, should be drunk warm with an equal quantity of milk.
After it, one should drink warm milk alone, according to strength.
By this, when the <s>doṣa</s>s have been expelled, a <s>paittika gulma</s> is pacified.
In <s>paittika gulma</s>, one should drink grape and <s>abhayā</s> juice with jaggery,
or lick <s>kampillaka</s> with honey as a liquid for the sake of purgation.
For patients with <s>pitta-gulma</s>, massage with ghee pacifies burning,
or massage with sandalwood oil, or with oil of <s>madhuka</s>.
The milk enemas that remove <s>pitta</s>-fever and contain bitter substances

children.text: hitāste pittagulmibhyo vakṣyante ye ca siddhiṣu ||
children.translated_text: are beneficial for those with <s>pitta-gulma</s>, as are those that will be taught in the section on successful therapies.

children.text: śālayo jāṅgalaṃ māṃsaṃ gavyāje payasī ghṛtam
children.translated_text: Rice, meat from animals of dry land, cow's and goat's milk, ghee,
dates, <s>āmalaka</s>, grapes, pomegranate, and <s>parūṣaka</s>
should be used as food; for drinking, boiled water
prepared with <s>balā</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, and fragrant herbs is the treatment for <s>pitta-gulma</s>.
When undigested material is associated with <s>pitta-gulma</s>, or when <s>kapha</s> or <s>vāta</s> is accompanied by such material,
after fasting, the digestive fire should be kindled with gruels, sour broths, and soups.
The pacification and aggravation of all <s>doṣa</s>s depend on the digestive fire.
Therefore one should always protect the digestive fire and avoid the causes.
For one fit for emesis, one should administer emesis in <s>kapha-gulma</s>,
when the body has been oleated and fomented and looseness has come into the <s>gulma</s>.
Wrapping blazing strands of <s>balvaja</s> grass, or else <s>kuśa</s> grass,
the physician should place them in a pot and set the <s>gulma</s> at the mouth of the pot.
When the <s>gulma</s> has been gripped, he should then remove the pot.
Then, placing a cloth between, the expert should break up the <s>gulma</s>.
With improvised instruments such as a goat's hoof or a mirror, according to availability, he should press it,
and should knead that <s>gulma</s> alone, but should not touch the intestines or the heart.
After smearing it with sesame, castor, flaxseed, and mustard seed,
the physician should foment the patient with kapha-type <s>gulma</s> using comfortably warm iron vessels.
Ghee cooked with <s>daśamūla</s>, with <s>tryūṣa</s>, alkali, and salt,
together with asafoetida, <s>biḍa</s> salt, and pomegranate, quickly overcomes kapha-type <s>gulma</s>.
Thus ends the <s>Daśamūlī Ghṛta</s>.
Two <s>palas</s> of <s>bhallātaka</s> and <s>pañcamūla</s> measured by the <s>pala</s>
should be cooked, after pounding, together with the group beginning with <s>vidārīgandhā</s>, in one <s>āḍhaka</s> of water.

children.text: pādaśeṣe rase tasmin pippalīṃ nāgaraṃ vacām
children.translated_text: When one quarter of that decoction remains, the physician should grind long pepper, dry ginger, sweet flag,

children.text: viḍaṅgaṃ saindhavaṃ hiṅgu yāvaśūkaṃ biḍaṃ śaṭīm ||
children.translated_text: <s>viḍaṅga</s>, rock salt, asafoetida, <s>yāvaśūka</s>, <s>biḍa</s> salt, and <s>śaṭī</s>,

children.text: citrakaṃ madhukaṃ rāsnāṃ piṣṭvā karṣasamaṃ bhiṣak
children.translated_text: <s>citraka</s>, licorice, and <s>rāsnā</s>, each in the amount of a <s>karṣa</s>,

children.text: prasthaṃ ca payaso dattvā ghṛtaprasthaṃ vipācayet ||
children.translated_text: and, adding one <s>prastha</s> of milk and one <s>prastha</s> of ghee, should cook it down.
This <s>Bhallātaka Ghṛta</s> is supreme for removing kapha-type <s>gulma</s>.
It destroys splenic disease, anemia, dyspnea, disease of the <s>grahaṇī</s>, and cough.
Thus ends the ghee beginning with <s>bhallātaka</s>.
With long pepper, long-pepper root, <s>cavya</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and dry ginger,
each one <s>pala</s>, together with barley-alkali, one <s>prastha</s> of ghee should be cooked.

children.text: kṣīraprasthaṃ ca tat sarpir hanti gulmaṃ kaphātmakam
children.translated_text: With one <s>prastha</s> of milk, that ghee destroys kapha-natured <s>gulma</s>.
It cures <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder and anemia, and removes splenic disease, cough, and fever.
Thus ends the <s>Kṣīraṣaṭpalaka Ghṛta</s>.
<s>Trivṛt</s>, <s>triphala</s>, <s>dantī</s>, and <s>daśamūla</s>, each measured at one <s>pala</s>,
should be cooked in four times their quantity of water until the decoction remains at one fourth.
Ghee, castor oil, and milk should be prepared together with it.
When perfected, this mixed unctuous preparation, taken with honey, destroys kapha-type <s>gulma</s>.
In obstructions from kapha and vāta, in skin disease, splenic disease, and abdominal enlargement,
and especially in pains of the female genital tract, the mixed unctuous preparation should be prescribed.
Thus ends the mixed unctuous preparation.
The purgative <s>Nīlinī Ghṛta</s> that was stated as destroying vāta-type <s>gulma</s>
