should be prescribed in double quantity for the purpose of purgation in patients with kapha-type <s>gulma</s>.
Powder of <s>trivṛt</s>, well impregnated in the liquid latex of <s>sudhā</s>,
in the measure of a <s>karṣa</s>, when licked with honey and ghee, purges well.
Twenty-five <s>abhayā</s> fruits should be cooked in one <s>droṇa</s> of water,

children.text: dantyāḥ palāni tāvanti citrakasya tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: along with as many <s>palas</s> of <s>dantī</s>, and likewise of <s>citraka</s>.
When one eighth remains, the strained decoction should be poured in.
Purified jaggery equal to the <s>dantī</s> should be added there, along with those <s>abhayā</s> fruits.
Also half a <s>kuḍava</s> of oil and four <s>palas</s> of powdered <s>trivṛt</s> should be added,
and one <s>pala</s> of long pepper and <s>viśvabheṣaja</s>.
That should be cooked to the consistency of an electuary; when it is cool, honey equal to the oil should be added,
as well as one <s>pala</s> of powder made from cinnamon bark, cardamom, bay leaf, and saffron.

children.text: tato lehapalaṃ līḍhvā jagdhvā caikāṃ harītakīm
children.translated_text: Then, after licking one <s>pala</s> of the electuary and eating one <s>harītakī</s> fruit,
the uncted patient is purged comfortably, expelling a <s>prastha</s> of <s>doṣa</s> without distress.
When used, this removes <s>gulma</s>, swelling, hemorrhoids, anemia, anorexia,
heart disease, disorder of the <s>grahaṇī</s>, jaundice, intermittent fever,
skin disease, splenic enlargement, and abdominal distension.
Its follow-up regimen is harmless: liquids, meat broth, and boiled rice.
Thus ends <s>Dantī-Harītakī</s>.
The successful decoction-enemas for patients with kapha-type <s>gulma</s> will be described in the sections on successful treatments,
and proven fermented formulations will be described in the treatments for <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder and hemorrhoids.
The powders and pills that were prescribed for patients with vāta-type <s>gulma</s>,
when prepared with double alkali, asafoetida, and sour <s>vetasa</s>, are beneficial in kapha.
The very alkalis that are used in disorder of the <s>grahaṇī</s>
are proven, harmless, and recommended for patients with kapha-type <s>gulma</s>; cauterization is praised at the end.
Very old grains and meat from wild animals and birds,
soups of horse gram and mung beans, and soups seasoned with long pepper and dry ginger,
soup of dried radish, and soups of <s>bilva</s> and <s>varuṇa</s>,
of shoots of <s>cirabilva</s>, and of <s>yavānī</s> and <s>citraka</s>,
with citron, asafoetida, sour <s>vetasa</s>, alkali, and pomegranate,
should be prepared as relishes with buttermilk, oil, and ghee.
A patient with kapha-type <s>gulma</s> should drink, at the proper time, water boiled with <s>pañcamūla</s>, old <s>vāruṇī</s> liquor,
or aged <s>mādhvīka</s> wine.
He should drink buttermilk powdered with <s>yavānī</s> and salted with <s>biḍa</s> salt;
it kindles digestion and restores the downward movement of vāta, kapha, and urine.
A <s>gulma</s> that has accumulated gradually, occupies a large seat,
has established roots, is bound by vessels, and rises like a tortoise,
when accompanied by weakness, anorexia, nausea, cough, vomiting, malaise, fever,
thirst, drowsiness, and coryza, is not curable.
When it seizes the patient with fever and dyspnea, and he is afflicted by vomiting and diarrhea,
swelling in the heart-region, navel, hands, and feet wastes away the patient with <s>gulma</s>.
For raudhira <s>gulma</s>, when the time of pregnancy has passed,
one should give an unctuous purgation to the woman whose body has been oleated and fomented.
Cooking two measures of <s>palāśa</s> alkali and two measures each of oil and ghee,
one should administer a dose that causes loosening of the <s>gulma</s>.
If it does not break open in this way, one should give a cleansing treatment for the female genital tract:

children.text: kṣāreṇa yuktaṃ palalaṃ sudhākṣīreṇa vā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a meat paste mixed with alkali, or again with the latex of <s>sudhā</s>.
Or one should place pungent fish, impregnated with either of these two, in the vagina,
or lac preparations thoroughly impregnated with the bile of boar and fish.
Or one may use preparations impregnated with downward-moving and upward-moving evacuants, together with honey,
or ferment mixed with jaggery and alkali, as a cleansing treatment for the female genital tract.
She should lick an alkali that checks raktapitta, together with honey and ghee,
and she should be given garlic, sharp wine, and fish.
An enema prepared with milk, cow urine, alkali, and <s>daśamūla</s>
When no blood is seen, one should perform the opening of the <s>gulma</s>.
When blood is flowing, one should give rice cooked with meat broth,
and anointing with ghee and oil, and young surā wine for drinking.
But when blood flows excessively, measures that remove <s>raktapitta</s> should be carried out,
and, for a woman afflicted by pains of <s>vāta</s>, again all measures that remove <s>vāta</s>.
One should use sprinklings with ghee and oil, and the meat of partridges and cocks,

children.text: surāṃ samaṇḍāṃ pūrvaṃ ca pānamamlasya sarpiṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: surā wine together with its sediment, and first the drinking of sour ghee.
Or afterwards one should administer ghee prepared with the life-promoting group of drugs.
When blood is flowing excessively, an unctuous enema with bitter drugs should be given.
Here are the verses:
Unction, fomentation, ghee, enema, powders, nourishing treatment, and pills,
emesis and purgation, and evacuation, are for the blood-born condition and for those with <s>vāta</s>-type <s>gulma</s>.
Ghee prepared with bitter drugs, milk, a laxative, and decoction enemas,
and also bloodletting, reassurance, and pacifying applications are for the blood condition.
A poultice and surgery are for one that is ripe and has burst internally.
Purification and pacification are for a <s>gulma</s> arising from <s>pitta</s>.
Unction, fomentation, incision, fasting, emesis, and purgation,
ghee, enema, pills, powders, and alkaline fermented preparations
and, at the end, cauterization are for a phlegmatic <s>gulma</s>; first, blood should be removed.
The order of treatment has been stated for blood-born <s>gulma</s> and for <s>gulma</s> arising in women.
The use of wholesome food and drink, and avoidance of causes according to each case,
constant restoration of digestive fire, and all procedures after oleation, are prescribed.

children.text: heturliṅgaṃ siddhiḥ kriyākramaḥ sādhyatā na yogāśca
children.translated_text: The cause, signs, success, order of treatment, curability, and formulations:
this much has been declared as <s>Agniveśa</s>'s compendium on the treatment of <s>gulma</s>.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of thirst.
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.
The son of <s>Atri</s>, renowned for knowledge, tranquility, and austerity, devoted to the welfare of the world,
taught the treatment for pacifying the five kinds of thirst.
From agitation, fear, exertion, grief, anger, fasting, and liquor,
and from taking alkaline, sour, salty, pungent, hot, rough, and dry foods,
from wasting of the tissues, emaciation by disease, excessive use of emesis and the like, and exposure to the heat of the sun,

children.text: pittānilau pravṛddhau saumyān dhātūṃś ca śoṣayataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>pitta</s> and wind, when increased, dry up the watery tissues.
Having dried the channels that carry <s>rasa</s>, and the root of the tongue, throat, palate, and kloman,
these two, very powerful in the bodies of men, produce thirst.

children.text: pītaṃ pītaṃ hi jalaṃ śoṣayatastāvato na yāti śamam
children.translated_text: Though water is drunk again and again, they dry it up, and it does not come to pacification.
In those emaciated by dreadful diseases, that thirst arises as a secondary complication.
The prodromal sign is dryness of the mouth; the defining symptom is the constant desire for water.
In all kinds of thirst, lightening and disappearance of the signs is the favorable indication.
Thirst produces dryness of the mouth, change of voice, dizziness, burning heat, delirious speech, stiffness,
roughness of the palate, lips, throat, and tongue, and loss of consciousness.
It causes protrusion of the tongue, anorexia, deafness, pain in the vital points, and exhaustion.

children.text: tṛṣṇodbhūtā kurute pañcavidhāṃ liṅgataḥ śṛṇu tām ||
children.translated_text: Thirst is fivefold in origin; hear of it according to its signs.

children.text: abdhātuṃ dehasthaṃ kupitaḥ pavano yadā viśoṣayati
children.translated_text: When aggravated wind dries up the water element situated in the body,
when that is dry, the weak man dries up, and, drying up, becomes thirsty.

children.text: nidrānāśaḥ śiraso bhramastathā śuṣkavirasamukhatā ca sroto'varodha iti ca syālliṅgaṃ vātatṛṣṇāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sleeplessness, dizziness of the head, a dry and tasteless mouth, and obstruction of the channels are the signs of <s>vāta</s>-type thirst.

children.text: pittaṃ matamāgneyaṃ kupitaṃ cet tāpayaty apāṃ dhātum
children.translated_text: <s>Pitta</s> is considered fiery; if aggravated, it heats the water element.

children.text: saṃtaptaḥ sa hi janayettṛṣṇāṃ dāholbaṇāṃ nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: When that has been heated, it produces in men a thirst in which burning is predominant.
A bitter taste in the mouth, burning in the head, delight in cold things, and fainting,
with yellowness of the eyes, urine, and feces, are the form of <s>pitta</s>-type thirst.
The thirst that arises from <s>āma</s> is also fiery, because it is produced by <s>āma</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
Its signs are anorexia, abdominal distension, and excess discharge of kapha.

children.text: deho rasajo'mbubhavo rasaśca tasya kṣayācca tṛṣyeddhi
children.translated_text: The body is born of <s>rasa</s> and is water-born; through the depletion of that <s>rasa</s>, one becomes thirsty.
There is a feeble voice, faintness, and dryness of the heart, throat, and palate.

children.text: bhavati khalu yopasargāttṛṣṇā sā śoṣiṇī kaṣṭā
children.translated_text: The thirst that occurs as a complication is indeed wasting and severe,
in the bodies of those afflicted by fever, urinary disorders, consumption, wasting disease, dyspnea, and the like.
All thirsts that are excessively persistent in those emaciated by disease and in those with persistent vomiting,
and that are joined with dreadful complications, should be known as leading to death.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of poison.
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.
First, its origin, qualities, sources, stages, signs, and treatments
of poison, as I speak of them properly, hear from me, <s>Agniveśa</s>.
When the ocean was being churned by gods and asuras for the sake of nectar,
before the arising of nectar there was born a being terrible to behold.
He was blazing in splendor, four-fanged, tawny-haired, and fire-eyed.
Seeing him, the world became despondent; therefore he was given the name poison.
<s>Brahmā</s> assigned it to the two sources, mobile and immobile.
Because it is water-born, it is therefore twofold and like fire.
It has eight stages, ten qualities, and twenty-four treatments.
Because it has water as its source, in the rainy season it becomes moist, like jaggery.
It spreads when the rain clouds have gone, and <s>Agastya</s> destroys it.
Therefore poison becomes weak in potency when the mass of clouds has passed away.
Snakes, insects, rats, spiders, scorpions, and house lizards,
leeches, fish, frogs, kaṇabhas, sakṛkaṇṭakas,
dogs, lions, tigers, jackals, hyenas, mongooses, and others are mobile sources.

children.text: daṃṣṭriṇo ye viṣaṃ teṣāṃ daṃṣṭrotthaṃ jaṅgamaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: The poison of creatures that have fangs is regarded as animal poison, arising from the fang.
<s>mustaka</s>, <s>pauṣkara</s>, <s>krauñca</s>, <s>vatsanābha</s>, and <s>balāhaka</s>,
<s>karkaṭa</s>, <s>kālakūṭa</s>, and the one called <s>karavīraka</s>,
<s>pālakendrāyudha</s>, oil, <s>meghaka</s>, and <s>kuśapuṣpaka</s>,
<s>rohiṣa</s>, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, and <s>lāṅgalakyañjanābhaka</s>,
<s>saṅkoca</s>, <s>markaṭa</s>, <s>śṛṅgīviṣa</s>, and likewise <s>hālāhala</s>,
these and other such substances, produced from roots and stationary in nature, are plant poisons.
Another poison is produced by a combination of <s>gara</s>; it is called <s>gara</s> and produces disease.
Because it ripens only after an interval of time, it does not take away life immediately.

children.text: nidrāṃ tandrāṃ klamaṃ dāhaṃ sapākaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Animal poison produces sleep, drowsiness, fatigue, burning with suppuration, horripilation,
swelling as well, and diarrhea.

children.text: sthāvaraṃ tu jvaraṃ hikkāṃ dantaharṣaṃ galagraham
children.translated_text: Plant poison, however, produces fever, hiccup, tingling of the teeth, constriction of the throat,
foamy vomiting, anorexia, dyspnea, and fainting.
Animal poison belongs to the lower part of the body, while root-born poison belongs to the upper part.

children.text: tasmāddaṃṣṭrāviṣaṃ maulaṃ hanti maulaṃ ca daṃṣṭrajam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore fang-poison counteracts root-poison, and root-poison counteracts fang-born poison.
In the first impulse, thirst, bewilderment, tingling of the teeth, salivation, vomiting, and fatigue occur,
because the <s>rasa</s> is vitiated; but in the second impulse, because the blood is vitiated,
there are discoloration, dizziness, trembling, fainting, yawning, tingling in the limbs, and darkness before the eyes.
In the third impulse, from corrupted flesh, there are circular eruptions, itching, swelling, and urticarial patches.
In the fourth there are conditions beginning with those of vāta, burning, vomiting, bodily pain, fainting, and the like.
In the fifth impulse there is the perception of blue and other colors, and of darkness.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe hikkā bhaṅgaḥ skandhasya tu saptame 'ṣṭame maraṇam
children.translated_text: In the sixth there is hiccup; in the seventh, breaking pain of the shoulder; in the eighth, death.
For humans the poison-impulses are eight, for quadrupeds fourfold, and for birds threefold.

children.text: sīdatyādye bhramati ca catuṣpado vepate tataḥ śūnyaḥ
children.translated_text: In the first impulse a quadruped sinks down and reels; after that it trembles and becomes vacant,

children.text: mandāhāro mriyate śvāsena hi caturthavege tu ||
children.translated_text: eats little, and in the fourth impulse dies through dyspnea.

children.text: dhyāyati vihagaḥ prathame vege prabhrāmyati dvitīye tu
children.translated_text: A bird broods in the first impulse, and in the second it whirls about;
with its limbs slackened, in the third poison-impulse it goes to death.

children.text: laghu rūkṣamāśu viśadaṃ vyavāyi tīkṣṇaṃ vikāsi sūkṣmaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Light, dry, swift, clear, diffusive, sharp, spreading, subtle,
hot, and of indeterminable taste: poison is said by those who know it to possess these ten qualities.
By its dryness it provokes vāta; because it is not cooling, pitta; by its subtlety, the blood.
Because its taste is indistinct, it follows kapha and the nutrient fluid of food quickly.
Because it is diffusive, it quickly pervades the entire body by itself.
Because it is sharp it injures the vital points; because it spreads, it destroys life.
Because it is light it is difficult to treat, and because it is clear its movement through the <s>doṣa</s>s is unobstructed.
Having reached one or another of the <s>doṣa</s>-sites and bodily constitutions, it excites it.
In a vāta-type person, when it is in a vāta-site, there may also be slight signs of kapha and pitta:
thirst, bewilderment, restlessness, fainting, constriction of the throat, vomiting, foam, and the like.
In a pitta-type person, when poison is situated in the pitta receptacle, the same applies regarding kapha and vāta.
There are thirst, cough, fever, vomiting, fatigue, burning, darkness before the eyes, diarrhea, and the like.
When it has gone to a kapha-region in a kapha-type person, it should show slight signs of vāta and pitta too:
dyspnea, constriction of the throat, itching, salivation, vomiting, and the like.
Chronic latent poison has signs of blood-vitiation: wounds, skin eruptions, and urticarial patches.
In this way poison, vitiating each <s>doṣa</s> one by one, takes away life.

children.text: kṣarati viṣatejasāsṛk tat khāni nirudhya mārayati jantum
children.translated_text: The blood flows out because of the fiery power of poison; obstructing the channels, it kills the creature.

children.text: pītaṃ mṛtasya hṛdi tiṣṭhati daṣṭaviddhayordaṃśadeśe syāt ||
children.translated_text: When poison has been drunk, it remains in the heart of the dead; in those bitten or pierced, it is at the place of bite.
Blue lips, looseness of the teeth, falling of the hair, breaking and convulsions of the body,
no horripilation from cold applications, and no rod-like streak when struck,
and blood from a wound not issuing from the wound: these are signs of death.
When the signs differ from these, the patients are to be treated; now hear from me their procedures of treatment.
Mantras, protective ligatures, cutting out, squeezing, suction, cautery, and affusions,
immersion, bloodletting, emesis, purgation, and applications beneath or around the affected part,
protection of the heart, collyrium, nasal medication, smoke, linctus, and medicines for pacification,
rubbing applications, antidote, restoration of consciousness, and poultice,
and even revival of the dead: these are twenty procedures plus four.

children.text: syurupakramā yathā ye yatra yojyāḥ śṛṇu tathā tān ||
children.translated_text: Hear now how those procedures are to be applied, each where it is appropriate.
If the poison from a bite has not yet spread in the bitten person, the physician should bind a ligature,
squeeze the bite strongly, or cut it out, while avoiding vital points.
Or he should suck that bite with his mouth filled with barley flour and dust.
Then the blood should be made to flow by scarification, horn, leeches, and puncturing.
When the blood is corrupted by poison, the bodily constitution is corrupted; after that the person gives up life.
Therefore, by vigorous rubbing and the like, blood that is not flowing should be made to flow.
<s>trikaṭu</s>, house-soot, turmeric, the five salts, <s>rocanā</s>, together with <s>vārttāka</s>,
are used for rubbing; when bleeding is excessive, a cooling poultice with banyan and similar substances is used.
For blood is the receptacle of poison, as wind is of fire; with cold poultices and affusions,

children.text: śītaiḥ skandati tasmin skanne vyapayāti viṣavegaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that blood coagulates; when it has coagulated, the impulse of poison passes away.
From the impulses of poison arise intoxication, fainting, despondency, and agitation of the heart.
One should check them with cold measures, and the patient should be fanned so long as horripilation does not occur.
As a tree does not grow when its root is cut, poison does not increase when the bite is cut out.
Suction draws it out; protective ligatures are like a dam for water.

children.text: tvaṅmāṃsagataṃ dāho dahati viṣaṃ srāvaṇaṃ harati raktāt
children.translated_text: Cautery burns poison that has gone into the skin and flesh; draining removes it from the blood.
Poison that has been drunk should be removed at once by emetics, but in the second stage by purgatives.
At the outset the heart should be protected; as a covering for it, one should drink whatever is available:
preparations of honey, ghee, and marrow, or sugarcane juice, or the juice of cow dung.

children.text: ikṣuṃ supakvamathavā kākaṃ niṣpīḍya tadrasaṃ varaṇam
children.translated_text: Or one may drink well-ripened sugarcane; or, squeezing a crow, its juice as the protective covering,
or the blood or ash of goats and the like, or clay, should quickly be drunk.
In the third stage, the alkaline antidote is used; scraping treatment with swelling-removing drugs, together with honey-water, is prescribed.
In the fourth impulse, cow-dung juice is used, together with <s>kapittha</s>, honey, and ghee.
In the fifth, drops, collyrium, and nasal medication should be made from the fresh juices of <s>kākāṇḍa</s> and <s>śirīṣa</s>.
Then, in the sixth, restoration of consciousness must be performed.
There should be a drink of <s>rajanī</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, black pepper, and long pepper, mixed with cow bile.
For those bitten after drinking poison, poison-drinking is prescribed, and, at the end, biting in return.
For those as if dead, an antidote of <s>palāśa</s> seed mixed with half as much peacock bile is excellent,
or <s>vārtāku</s>, treacle, house-smoke soot, cow bile, and <s>nimba</s>.
Pills prepared with cow bile, <s>surasā</s>, <s>granthi</s>, the two <s>rajanī</s>s, <s>madhuka</s>, and <s>kuṣṭha</s>,
are praised as equal to <s>amṛta</s>; or they may be made with the juices of <s>śirīṣa</s> flowers and <s>kākāṇḍa</s>.
With <s>kākāṇḍa</s>, <s>surasā</s>, <s>gavākṣī</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>vāyasī</s>, and fruits of <s>śirīṣa</s>,
there are applications, fumigations, nasal medications, and drinks for those dead from hanging, poison, water, or earth.
<s>Spṛkkā</s>, <s>plava</s>, <s>sthauṇeyaka</s>, <s>kāṃkṣī</s>, <s>śaileya</s>, <s>rocanā</s>, and <s>tagara</s>,
<s>dhyāmaka</s>, saffron, <s>māṃsī</s>, <s>surasā</s>, <s>aguru</s>, cardamom, and <s>kuṣṭha</s>,
<s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>śirīṣa</s> flower, <s>śrīveṣṭaka</s>, lotus, <s>cāraṭī</s>, and <s>viśālā</s>,
deodar, lotus filaments, <s>sāvaraka</s>, realgar, and <s>kauntya</s>,
the juices of jasmine and arka flowers, the two <s>rajanī</s>s, asafoetida, long pepper, and lac,
water, <s>mudgaparṇī</s>, sandalwood, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>madana</s>, and <s>sindhuvāra</s>,
<s>śampāka</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, peacock scent, fragrant fruits, <s>nākulī</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s>:

children.text: puṣye saṃhṛtya samaṃ piṣṭvā guṭikā vigheyāḥ syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: having collected them under the <s>Puṣya</s> asterism, one should grind them equally and make them into pills.
It destroys all poisons, brings victory, revives those dead from poison, and removes fever.
It acts by smelling, anointing, wearing, inhaling the smoke, and keeping it in the house.
It destroys beings, poison, creatures, misfortune, sorcery, spells, powerful missiles, and enemies.
It removes bad dreams, faults affecting women, untimely death, dangers from water and thieves, and fear.
It brings success in wealth, grain, and undertakings, and increases prosperity, nourishment, and lifespan; it is auspicious.
This reviver of the dead was formerly ordained by <s>Brahmā</s> as <s>amṛta</s>.
Thus ends the antidote called <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvana</s>, 'Reviver of the Dead.'
Binding the arteries with mantras, wiping away the poison, and self-protection should be performed.

children.text: doṣasya viṣaṃ yasya sthāne syāttaṃ jayetpūrvam ||
children.translated_text: Whichever seat of a <s>doṣa</s> the poison occupies, that should first be overcome.
When it is in a vāta seat, fomentation is used, and a drink of curd with a paste of <s>nata</s> and <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
When it is in a pitta seat, ghee, honey, milk, water-drinking, immersion, and sprinkling are used.
When it has gone to a kapha seat, the alkaline antidote, fomentation, and venesection are used.
Then, for latent poison, when it is situated in the blood, the fivefold procedure on the vessels is used.
Thus the learned physician, having always determined everything, should plan the medicine.
For one should first overcome the seat, and what is located in a seat should be treated with what is not opposed to that seat.
When the path of kapha is contaminated by poison and vāta is blocked by obstruction of the channels,
a person may breathe as if dead, yet be free from signs of incurability.
A paste made from the decoction of hide, the size of a <s>bilva</s>, should be placed on his head in the shape of a crow's foot,
and powder of <s>kaṭabhī</s>, <s>kaṭuka</s>, and <s>kaṭphala</s> should be blown into him.

children.text: chāgaṃ gavyaṃ māhiṣaṃ vā māṃsaṃ kaukkuṭameva vā
children.translated_text: Goat, bovine, or buffalo meat, or even chicken meat,
should be placed on that crow-foot mark; then the poison passes into it.
When there is obstruction of the nose, eyes, ears, tongue, or throat, nasal treatment should be performed
with ground <s>vārtāku</s> seed, <s>bījapūra</s>, <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, and similar drugs.
When the eyes are obstructed, collyrium should be applied, ground with goat urine,
using deodar, the three pungents, turmeric, oleander, <s>karañja</s>, <s>nimba</s>, and <s>surasā</s>.
White <s>vacā</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, asafoetida, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, rock salt, garlic,
mustard, the pith of <s>kapittha</s>, and the seeds of <s>ṭuṇṭuka</s> and <s>karañja</s>,

children.text: vyoṣaṃ śirīṣapuṣpaṃ dvirajanyau vaṃśalocanaṃ ca samam
children.translated_text: the three pungents, <s>śirīṣa</s> flower, the two <s>rajanī</s>s, and bamboo silica, in equal parts,
should be ground with goat urine and then, for seven days, with cow and horse bile.

children.text: vyatyāsabhāvito 'yaṃ nihanti śirasi sthitaṃ viṣaṃ kṣipram
children.translated_text: Prepared by alternating these impregnations, this quickly destroys poison lodged in the head.
It also destroys all fevers, possession by beings and <s>grahas</s>, <s>visūcikā</s>, chronic fainting disorders,
insanity, epilepsy, cataract, film over the eye, blue discoloration, and disorders of the head,
dry inflammation of the eyes, <s>pilla</s>, tumors, <s>arma</s>, itching, and disorders of darkness of vision,
wasting, weakness, intoxication after drink, anemia, and delusions, through its use as collyrium.
When applied, it also destroys poison from poisoned wounds, from licking, biting, and drinking poison.
For hemorrhoids and distension there should be an application to the anus, and for women an application to the vagina.
When the fetus is obstructed or spoiled, and in coryza, there should be an application to the forehead.
In enlargement, <s>kiṭima</s>, skin disease, vitiligo, <s>ṛvicarchikā</s>, and the like, it is used as an application.
Like an elephant destroying trees, this <s>Gandhahastin</s> antidote destroys diseases caused by poison.
Thus ends the antidote named <s>Gandhahastin</s>.
Leaves, <s>aguru</s>, <s>musta</s>, oil, five resins, sandalwood, and <s>spṛkkā</s>,
bark, <s>nalada</s>, blue lotus, <s>bālaka</s>, <s>hareṇuka</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>vanyanakha</s>,
deodar, gold, saffron, <s>dhyāmaka</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, and <s>tagara</s>,
the five parts of <s>śirīṣa</s>, the three pungents, orpiment, realgar, and cumin,
white <s>kaṭabhī</s> and <s>karañja</s>, <s>rakṣoghnī</s>, <s>sindhuvārikā</s>, and <s>rajanī</s>,
<s>surasā</s>, collyrium, red ochre, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, and resins of <s>nimba</s>,
bamboo bark, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, asafoetida, <s>dadhittha</s>, sour <s>vetasa</s>, and lac,
honey, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>somarājī</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>ruhā</s>, <s>rocanā</s>, and <s>tagara</s>.
This <s>agada</s> (antidote), taught to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> by <s>Tryambaka</s>, has sixty components;
it is famous as <s>Mahāgandhahastin</s>, with an efficacy that cannot be obstructed.

children.text: pittena gavāṃ peṣyo guṭikāḥ kāryāstu puṣyayogena
children.translated_text: It should be ground with the bile of cows, and pills should be made under the conjunction of <s>Puṣya</s>.
By drinks, collyria, and external applications it brings all its actions to success.

children.text: pillaṃ kaṇḍūṃ timiraṃ rātryāndhyaṃ kācamarbudaṃ paṭalam
children.translated_text: By constant use it destroys pilla, itching, dimness of sight, night-blindness, cataract, tumor, and film over the eye
in people who eat what is wholesome, measured, and suitable.
It destroys intermittent fevers, indigestions, ringworm, itching, cholera, and scabies,
and the poison of all mice, spiders, and serpents;

children.text: āśu viṣaṃ nāśayati samūlajamatha kandajaṃ sarvam ||
children.translated_text: it quickly destroys every poison born from roots and also from bulbs.

children.text: etena liptagātraḥ sarpān gṛhṇāti bhakṣayecca viṣam
children.translated_text: With his body smeared with this, a man may seize snakes and may eat poison;
even if overtaken by death, he lives always free from distress.
In constriction there is an application to the anus, and for women with an obstructed fetus there is an application in the vagina;
in fainting and pain, they say that smearing it on the forehead is most important.
Having smeared kettledrums, mṛdaṅga drums, war-drums, umbrellas, banners, and pennants with this,
a wise man should sound them and display them for the driving away of snake poison.

children.text: yatra ca sannihito 'yaṃ na tatra bālagrahā na rakṣāṃsi
children.translated_text: Where this is present, there are no child-seizing spirits and no demons;

children.text: na ca kārmaṇavetālā vahanti nātharvaṇā mantrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: no sorcery, vetālas, or Atharvan spells operate there.

children.text: sarvagrahā na tatra prabhavanti na cāgniśastranṛpacaurāḥ
children.translated_text: All seizing spirits have no power there, nor do fire, weapons, kings, or thieves;
and prosperity attends the place where <s>Mahāgandhahastin</s> is present.
And while it is being ground, one should utter this perfected mantra:

children.text: mama matā jayā nāma jayo nāmeti me pitā ||
children.translated_text: "My mother is named <s>Jayā</s>; my father is named <s>Jaya</s>.
I am the son of <s>Jaya</s> and <s>Jayā</s>; I am <s>Vijaya</s>, and I conquer.
Homage to <s>Puruṣasiṃha</s>, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the maker of the universe,
to the eternal one, to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, to <s>Bhava</s>, and to <s>Vibhava</s>.
May the power of <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> be present, and the power of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Yama</s>.
Just as I know of no defeat of <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
nor of the taking of the mother's hand, nor of the drying up of the ocean,
by this true utterance may this <s>agada</s> be perfected.
Touched by hilimili, protect, O best of all medicines; svāhā."
Thus ends the <s>agada</s> named <s>Mahāgandhahastin</s>.
<s>Ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, blue lotus, coriander, saffron, and ajājī,
with sugar, giri, and the pith of jujube, are drink preparations that remove dyspnea, fever, and the like.
Asafoetida joined with black pepper, with the juice of kapittha, and the best salt
should be drunk with honey and sugar; they destroy fever, hiccup, dyspnea, and cough.
For vomiting, there is an electuary made with jujube kernels, añjana, parched grain, lotus, milk, and ghee;
and a fumigation-wick made from the two <s>bṛhatī</s> plants and āḍhakī leaves destroys hiccup.
Peacock feathers, crane bones, mustard seeds, and sandalwood, combined with ghee,
are recommended as a poison-destroying smoke for houses, beds, seats, clothes, and the like.
<s>Nata</s> and <s>kuṣṭha</s> mixed with ghee, together with the serpent-king's head and śirīṣa flowers,
are remembered as a smoke-antidote that destroys every poison and removes swelling.
Lac, sevya leaves, guggulu, bhallātaka, kakubha flowers, and sarja resin,
together with the white substance, make an excellent smoke for driving away snakes, mice, insects, and cloth-worms.
One should strain fresh palāśa alkali and cook it together with equal parts of powdered ingredients:
red earth, the two kinds of turmeric, white surasa blossoms, and madhuka;
lac, rock salt, māṃsī, hareṇu, asafoetida, the two sārivās, and kuṣṭha;
with the pungent triad and saffron, until it coats the ladle.
They remove every poison, swelling, <s>gulma</s> masses, skin disorders, hemorrhoids, fistula, and diseases of the spleen,
as well as edema, epilepsy, worms, spirit-possession, hoarseness, and anemia,
and they destroy sluggish digestion, cough, and insanity in men
when used as pills dried in the shade, each equal in size to a jujube.
Thus ends <s>Kṣārāgada</s>.
This has been prescribed for those who have drunk poison, been bitten, been pierced, or been smeared with poison.
Having given the general instruction, now hear the detailed instruction separately, just as it is.

children.text: ripuyuktebhyo nṛbhyaḥ svebhyaḥ strībhyo 'thavā bhayaṃ nṛpateḥ
children.translated_text: For a king there may be danger from men allied with enemies, from his own people, or from women,
arising through food and regimen; therefore he should examine his servants.
A man who is excessively apprehensive, very talkative or else speaking little, and bereft of luster,
having undergone a change from his natural state, should be known as the poison-giver.

children.text: dṛṣṭvaivaṃ na tu sahasā bhojyaṃ kuryāttadannamagnau tu
children.translated_text: Seeing this, one should not eat the food at once, but should place that food in the fire;
for when poisoned food reaches the fire, the fire undergoes many changes.
Its flames are variegated like peacock feathers, sharp-looking, and accompanied by dry smoke that smells like a corpse;

children.text: sphuṭati ca saśabdamekāvarto vihatārcirapi ca syāt ||
children.translated_text: it crackles aloud, has a single whirl, and its flame may also be checked.

children.text: pātrasthaṃ ca vivarṇaṃ bhojyaṃ syānmakṣikāṃśca mārayati
children.translated_text: Food placed in a vessel becomes discolored and kills flies;
it makes crows weak-voiced and makes the eye of the cakora lose its brightness.

children.text: pāne nīlā rājī vaivarṇyaṃ svāṃ ca nekṣate chāyām
children.translated_text: In drink there is a blue streak and discoloration, and a man does not see his own reflection;
or he sees it distorted, and when salt is added there is a garland of foam.
From the smell of poisoned drink and food there are headache, pain in the heart, and fainting;
from touching it there are swelling of the hand, numbness, burning and pricking of the fingers, and splitting of the nails.

children.text: mukhagetvoṣṭhacimicimā jihvā śūnā jaḍā vivarṇā ca
children.translated_text: When it has entered the mouth, there are tingling of the lips, and the tongue is swollen, numb, and discolored;
there are a setting-on-edge of the teeth, stiffness of the jaw, burning in the mouth, salivation, and disorders of the throat.
When it has entered the stomach, there are discoloration, sweating, collapse, and nausea;
vision and the heart are obstructed, and the body becomes covered with hundreds of spots.
But when it has gone into the lower bowel, there are fainting, intoxication, delusion, burning, and loss of strength.

children.text: tandrā kārśyaṃ ca viṣe pāṇḍutvaṃ codarasthe syāt ||
children.translated_text: In the case of poison situated in the abdomen, there will be drowsiness, emaciation, and pallor.
When the tooth-cleaning brush is poisoned, its bristled end falls apart, and there is swelling of the teeth, lips, and gums.
With a poisoned head-anointing there is falling of the hair, headache, and nodules on the head.
When collyrium is corrupted, there are burning of the eyes, discharge, excessive coating, swelling, and redness.
With corrupted foods the bowel is affected first; with corrupted things that touch the body, the skin is vitiated.
Through corrupted bathing, anointing, rubbing substances, garments, ornaments, and cosmetics,
there arise itching, pustular eruptions, wheals, pimples, horripilation, tingling, and swellings.
These are accompanied by burning and piercing pain in the hands and feet, fatigue, and indigestion,
when shoes, horses, elephants, armor, banners, beds, and seats have been poisoned.
A garland becomes odorless and withers; it produces headache and horripilation.

children.text: stambhayati khāni nāsāmupahanti darśanaṃ ca dhūmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Smoke obstructs the channels, injures the nose, and also impairs sight.
Water from wells, ponds, and the like becomes foul-smelling, turbid, and discolored.

children.text: pītaṃ śvayathuṃ koṭhān piḍakāśca karoti maraṇaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: When drunk, it causes swelling, wheals, pimples, and death.
At the outset, when poison has gone to the stomach, the physician should administer emesis; when it is in the skin, applications, affusions, and the like,

children.text: kuryādbhiṣak cikitsāṃ doṣabalaṃ caiva hi samīkṣya ||
children.translated_text: and he should carry out treatment after considering the strength of the <s>doṣa</s>s as well.
Thus the specific root-poisons have been described. Now hear about animate poison.
First, the specific treatment for it is stated, beginning with that for snakes.
Here snakes are of three kinds: <s>darvīkara</s>, <s>maṇḍalī</s>, and <s>rājimān</s>.
In that order they provoke vāta, pitta, and śleṣman.
The <s>darvīkara</s> should be known as hooded; the <s>maṇḍalī</s> has a circular hood.
The serpent whose body is variegated with spots and lines is the <s>rājimān</s>.
Their poisons, respectively, are especially dry and pungent, sour and hot, and sweet and cold.
Therefore they provoke vāta and the others in that same order.
The bite made by a <s>darvīkara</s> has fine fang-marks, is black,
has obstructed blood, is tortoise-like, and is considered to produce vāta disorders.
The bite made by a <s>maṇḍalī</s> is broad-set and swollen;
it is yellowish, with yellow blood, and produces all pitta disorders.
The bite made by a <s>rājimān</s> is slimy and produces a firm swelling;
it is oily and pale, with thick blood, and it stirs up śleṣman disorders.
A male snake has rounded coils, a large body, hisses, looks upward,
has a large head and even limbs; a female is the reverse of this.
A neuter snake has a defective female-like form, looks downward, is without voice, and trembles.

children.text: striyā daṣṭo viparyastairetaiḥ puṃsā naro mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: A person bitten by a female, and one bitten by a male, is understood from these opposite signs.
But when these signs are mixed, one should say that the person has been bitten by a neuter snake.
This has been stated as the indication of female, male, and neuter among snakes.
One bitten by a pregnant female has a pale face; one bitten by a recently delivered female has swollen lips and black eyes,
is afflicted with yawning, anger, and pain under the tongue, and has bloody urine.
The snake called <s>gaudheraka</s> is a four-footed one born from a monitor lizard.
It is equal to a black snake, and there are many mixed-born varieties.
Hidden, fully inflicted, round, pressed, hanging and embedded,

children.text: sarpitaṃ ca bhṛśābādhaṃ daṃśā ye 'nye na te bhṛśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and creeping bites cause severe distress; the other bites are not severe.
Young black snakes, old <s>gonasa</s> snakes,
and middle-aged <s>rājimān</s> snakes are like deadly venomous serpents.
Snakes have four fangs; of them, the lower left is white,
the upper left fang is yellow, and the lower and upper right fangs are red and dark.
The measure of a drop that falls from a cow's hair lifted out of water
is the measure of a serpent's poison in the lower left fang.
In the succeeding fangs the portions of poison increase by one, two, three, and four, respectively.
Bites made by fangs of those colors contain increasingly much poison and are very severe.

children.text: sarpāṇām eva viṇmūtrāt kīṭāḥ syuḥ kīṭasaṃmatāḥ
children.translated_text: From the feces and urine of snakes themselves arise creatures recognized as insects.
They possess latent poison and take life: this is the brief account.

children.text: gātraṃ raktaṃ sitaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ śyāvaṃ vā piḍakānvitam
children.translated_text: A limb may become red, white, black, or dark, and covered with pimples,
with itching, burning, spreading inflammation, suppuration, and decay as well.
Now hear the fatal sign in one bitten by insects with latent poison.
As in snakebite, swelling increases, and the blood has a strong foul odor.
At the bite there is heaviness of the eyes, fainting, and pain; the distressed person also breathes with difficulty.
He is overcome by thirst and loss of appetite, afflicted by latent poison.

children.text: daṃśasya madhye yat kṛṣṇaṃ śyāvaṃ vā jālakāvṛtam
children.translated_text: Where the middle of the bite is black or dark and covered with a net-like pattern,
burnt in appearance, greatly suppurating, and accompanied by moisture, swelling, and fever,
one should identify him as bitten by spiders with latent poison.
Now the sign in the bites of all of those spiders is stated.

children.text: śophaḥ śvetāsitā raktāḥ pītā vā piḍakā jvaraḥ
children.translated_text: There is swelling, pimples that are white, black, red, or yellow, and fever.
Breathlessness may become fatal, and there are burning, hiccup, and stiffness of the head.
In one afflicted by mouse latent poison, pale blood comes from the bite, with circular marks, fever, and loss of appetite,
as well as horripilation and burning.
With incurable mouse bites there are fainting, swelling of the limbs, discoloration, moisture, failure to hear sounds, and fever,
heaviness of the head, salivation, blood, and vomiting.
When bitten by <s>kṛkalāsa</s> lizards, there may be dark coloration, blackness,
or many-coloredness, as well as confusion and looseness of stool.
At first scorpion poison burns like fire, and afterward it quickly seems to split upward.

children.text: vṛścikasya viṣaṃ yāti daṃśe paścāttu tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: It moves in the bite, but afterward it remains there.
A person bitten in an incurable way, whose sight, smell, and taste are impaired,
with flesh falling away and extreme pain, gives up his life.
Spreading inflammation, swelling, colic pain, fever, and vomiting as well
are the signs when bitten by <s>kaṇabha</s> insects, and the bite itself disintegrates.
When bitten by an <s>ucciṭiṅga</s>, with his hairs bristling and the mark becoming stiff, he suffers intensely;
he thinks that his limbs have been sprinkled as if with cold water.

children.text: ekadaṃṣṭrārditaḥ śūnaḥ saruk syāt pītakaḥ satṛṭ
children.translated_text: One injured by a single fang becomes swollen, painful, yellowish, and thirsty;
vomiting and sleepiness are the signs of being bitten by poisonous frogs.
Poisonous fish cause burning, swelling, and pain,

children.text: kaṇḍūṃ śothaṃ jvaraṃ mūrcchāṃ saviṣāstu jalaukasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and poisonous leeches cause itching, swelling, fever, and fainting.
The house-lizard produces burning, piercing pain, sweating, and swelling;
centipede poison causes sweating, pain, and burning at the bite.
A mosquito bite is itchy, with slight swelling and mild pain;
a mosquito wound resembling that of an incurable insect is incurable.
At a fly bite there is a pustule, immediately oozing, dusky,
and accompanied by burning, fainting, and fever; among them the <s>sthagikā</s> is harmless.
Those bitten in a cremation ground, shrine, anthill, sacrificial place, hermitage, or temple,
at the junctures of fortnights, at midday, at midnight, or on eighth lunar days,

children.text: na sidhyanti narā daṣṭāḥ pāṣaṇḍāyataneṣu ca
children.translated_text: and also in the shrines of heretics, do not recover;
likewise those affected by the poisons of <s>āśīviṣa</s> snakes through sight, breath, excrement, or touch.
Those bitten in any of the vital points quickly perish when the poison has reached them,

children.text: yena kenāpi sarpeṇa saṃbhavaḥ sarva eva ca ||
children.translated_text: and this can occur from any snake whatever.
Poison increases in one who is frightened, intoxicated, weak, overheated, hungry, thirsty, or distressed.
When it meets a matching constitution and season, poison becomes strong; otherwise it is slight.
Snakes whose force has been checked by water, that are exhausted, frightened, defeated by a mongoose,

children.text: vṛddhā bālāstvaco muktāḥ sarpā mandaviṣāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: old, young, or newly freed from their skin are remembered as having weak poison.
From anger a snake releases poison that is lodged throughout its whole body;
but for the sake of feeding, or from fear, it does not release that same poison fully.
The poisons of <s>ucciṭiṅga</s>s and scorpions are generally dominated by <s>vāta</s>;
insects are dominated by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, while <s>kaṇabha</s> and the like are phlegmatic.

children.text: yasya yasya hi doṣasya liṅgādhikyāni lakṣayet
children.translated_text: Whichever <s>doṣa</s>'s signs one observes as predominant,
for that very one he should apply treatment with medicines of opposite qualities.
Pressure in the heart, upward movement of wind, stiffness, stretching of the veins, pain in the bones and joints,
dizziness, twisting, and dark discoloration of the limbs occur in vāta-type poison.
Loss of consciousness, hot breath, burning in the heart, a pungent taste in the mouth,
tearing open of the bite, and swelling that is red and yellow occur in pitta-type poison.
By vomiting, anorexia, nausea, salivation, oppression, and heaviness,
together with coldness and sweetness in the mouth, one should know that poison is dominated by <s>śleṣman</s>.
In vāta-type poison, a wound-poultice with <s>khaṇḍa</s> and oil massage are appropriate;
sweating by tube, hot grain-poultices, and the like, and a nourishing regimen, are beneficial.
Pitta-type poison should be checked with very cold affusions and poultices;
phlegmatic poison should be overcome by scraping, cutting, sweating, and emesis.
Even among all poisons, and when they have gone to all bodily sites,
except in scorpion and <s>ucciṭiṅga</s> poison, a cooling procedure is generally beneficial.
In scorpion poison one should apply sweating, massage with ghee and salt,

children.text: sekāṃścoṣṇān prayuñjīta bhojyaṃ pānaṃ ca sarpiṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: warm affusions, and food and drink consisting of ghee.
The same should be used also for <s>ucciṭiṅga</s> poison, along with rubbing against the hair with dust,
warm pleasant water, and thick coverings.
A dog, because of aggravation of all three <s>doṣa</s>s and derangement of the bodily tissues,
becomes afflicted in the head, drools, and has its face turned downward.
Other beasts of this same kind are considered to aggravate <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>,
causing pain in the heart and head, fever, stiffness, thirst, and fainting.
Itching, pricking pain, discoloration, numbness, moistness, drying,
burning, redness, pain, suppuration, swelling, and contraction of knots,
tearing open of the bite, blisters, raised knobs, and circular patches,

children.text: jvaraśca saviṣe liṅgaṃ viparītaṃ tu nirviṣe ||
children.translated_text: as well as fever, are the signs of a poisonous bite; in a non-poisonous bite the opposite signs occur.
There all the procedures previously stated should be applied according to the condition;
now hear me tell correctly another procedure as well.
When there is burning in the heart or salivation, purgation and emesis should be strongly applied
according to the condition; when the patient has been purified, the sequence of restorative diet should be used.
When poison has gone to the head, the wise physician should prepare a nasal medicine from the roots
of <s>bandhujīva</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>surasa</s>, and <s>asita</s>.
The flesh and blood of the cock, crow, and peacock should be placed on a wound in the head:
on the head for one bitten below, and on the feet for one bitten above.
<s>Pippalī</s>, black pepper, alkali, <s>vacā</s>, rock salt, and <s>śigru</s>,
ground with <s>rohita</s> bile and applied as collyrium, destroy poison that has reached the eye.
For poison in the throat, one should lick unripe <s>kapittha</s> with sugar and honey;
when it has gone to the stomach, one should lick a <s>pala</s> of powdered <s>nata</s> with those two.
When poison has gone to the large intestine, a person should drink <s>pippalī</s>, the two <s>rajanī</s>s,

children.text: mañjiṣṭhāṃ ca samaṃ piṣṭvā gopittena naraḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: and <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, ground in equal quantity with cow bile.

children.text: raktaṃ māṃsaṃ ca godhāyāḥ śuṣkaṃ cūrṇīkṛtaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: Dried flesh and blood of the monitor lizard, made into powder, is beneficial
as a drink with <s>kapittha</s> juice when poison has gone to the nutrient fluid.
When it has gone to the blood, he should drink the roots, bark, and shoots of <s>śelu</s>,
<s>badara</s>, <s>udumbara</s>, and <s>kaṭabhī</s>; when it has gone to the flesh, he should drink
<s>khadira</s> decoction with honey, and <s>kuṭaja</s> root with water.

children.text: sarveṣu ca bale dve tu madhūkaṃ madhukaṃ natam ||
children.translated_text: In all cases, two kinds of <s>balā</s>, <s>madhūka</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>nata</s>,
<s>pippalī</s>, dry ginger, and alkali, mixed with fresh butter, may be used.
But when <s>kapha</s> is increased, the physician should prescribe rubbing inside the mouth.
<s>Māṃsī</s>, saffron, leaves, bark, the two <s>rajanī</s>s, <s>nata</s>, and sandalwood,
together with realgar, <s>vyāghranakha</s>, and <s>surasa</s>, ground with water,
as drinks, nasal medicines, collyria, and poultices remove all swelling and poison.

children.text: candanaṃ tagaraṃ kuṣṭhaṃ haridre dve tvageva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>candana</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, the two kinds of turmeric, and bark too,

children.text: manaḥśilā tamālaśca rasaḥ kaiśara eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>manaḥśilā</s>, <s>tamāla</s>, and resin, likewise <s>kaiśara</s>,
and a tiger’s claw, all well ground with rice-water,
destroy all poisons, just as Indra’s thunderbolt destroys the asuras.
White pepper steeped for seven days in the juice of <s>śirīṣa</s> flowers
is useful for those bitten by snakes as nasal medication, drink, and collyrium.
Two palas each of <s>nata</s> and <s>kuṣṭha</s>, with four palas each of ghee and honey:
this drink gives relief even to those bitten by <s>Takṣaka</s>.

children.text: sindhuvārasya mūlaṃ ca śvetā ca girikarṇikā ||
children.translated_text: The root of <s>sindhuvāra</s>, white <s>girikarṇikā</s>,
and <s>pākala</s> with honey are a drink, and also a nasal medication, when one is bitten by hooded snakes.
<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>madhuyaṣṭī</s>, <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, sugar,
<s>kāśmarya</s>, and banyan shoots are a drink for the poison of maṇḍalin snakes.
<s>vyoṣa</s>, with <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, house-soot, and <s>hareṇukā</s>,

children.text: tagaraṃ kaṭukā kṣaudraṃ hanti rājīmatāṃ viṣam
children.translated_text: <s>tagara</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, and honey destroy the poison of rājīmat snakes.
House-soot, the two kinds of turmeric, and <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> with its root:
even one bitten by <s>Vāsuki</s> should drink it soaked in honey and ghee.
An application of the bark of milky trees, when purified, removes insect poison.
An application of pearls is best; it removes swelling, burning pain, piercing pain, and fever.
<s>candana</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>śirīṣa</s>, and <s>sindhuvārikā</s>,
<s>kṣīraśuklā</s>, <s>nata</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>pāṭalā</s>, <s>udīcya</s>, and <s>sārivā</s>:
this, ground with the fresh juice of <s>śelu</s>, is generally effective against spiders.
It should be used as appropriate, after consideration, for applications and the like.
<s>madhūka</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>udīcya</s>, and <s>pāṭalā</s>,
with neem, <s>sārivā</s>, and honey, are a drink that removes spider poison.
<s>kusumbha</s> flower, cow’s tooth, <s>svarṇakṣīrī</s>, pigeon dung,
<s>dantī</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, and rock salt cause the falling away of the ear in those two cases.
The barks of <s>kaṭabhī</s>, <s>arjina</s>, <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>śelu</s>, and milky trees,
as decoctions, pastes, and powders, remove wounds caused by insects and spiders.

children.text: tvacaṃ ca nāgaraṃ caiva samāṃśaṃ ślakṣṇapeṣitam
children.translated_text: Bark and dry ginger, in equal portions, finely ground,
should all be drunk with warm water; it removes the poison of mice.
The ground fruit of <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>jālamālinī</s>,
and bitter <s>ikṣvāku</s>: this preparation, by drinking, insufflation, and the like,
removes the poison of scorpions, mice, spiders, and snakes.
It is equal to nectar and also destroys indigestion from artificial poison.
All antidotes should be employed according to the <s>doṣa</s> in the case of the chameleon.
Pigeon dung, citron, and the juice from <s>śirīṣa</s> flowers,

children.text: śaṅkhinyārkaṃ payaḥ śuṇṭhī karañjo madhu vārścike
children.translated_text: <s>śaṅkhinī</s>, milk of <s>arka</s>, dry ginger, <s>karañja</s>, and honey are used for scorpion poison.
The ground fruit of <s>śirīṣa</s>, with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>, is used for frog poison.
The roots of white <s>bhaṇḍī</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, and ghee are used for fish poison.
All treatments for insect bites are the same for leeches.
A treatment that removes vāta and pitta is also generally recommended.
The scorpion antidote applies to the <s>ucciṭiṅga</s>, and the mouse antidote to the <s>kaṇabha</s>.
<s>vacā</s>, bamboo bark, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>nata</s>, flower clusters of <s>surasa</s>,

children.text: dve bale nākulīṃ kuṣṭhaṃ śirīṣaṃ rajanīdvayam ||
children.translated_text: the two <s>balā</s>s, <s>nākulī</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>śirīṣa</s>, the two <s>rajanī</s>s,
<s>guhā</s>, <s>atiguhā</s>, white <s>ajagandhā</s>, and <s>śilājatu</s>,
<s>kattṛṇa</s>, <s>kaṭabhī</s>, alkali, house-soot, and <s>manaḥśilā</s>:
when ground with the bile of a <s>rohītaka</s>, this is the supreme antidote.
It is useful in nasal medication, collyrium, applications, and the like, for <s>viśvambhara</s> and similar poisons.
Alkali from <s>svarjikā</s> and goat dung, with <s>surasā</s> and <s>chathākṣipīḍaka</s>,
mixed with the scum of liquor, is beneficial for centipede poison.
<s>kapittha</s>, <s>akṣipīḍa</s>, seeds of <s>arka</s>, and <s>trikaṭuka</s>,

children.text: karañjo dve haridre ca gṛhagodhāviṣaṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: <s>karañja</s>, and the two kinds of turmeric overcome the poison of the house-lizard.
<s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> combined with the juice of <s>kākāṇḍa</s> is foremost against poisons;
with peacock bile it is the same, and likewise <s>vāyasa</s> and <s>pīluka</s>.
With equal parts of the fruit, root, bark, flowers, and leaves of <s>śirīṣa</s>,
this fivefold <s>śirīṣa</s> is the best, the foremost in killing poisons.
Thus ends the fivefold <s>śirīṣa</s> antidote.
A wound made by claw or tooth, whether by a quadruped or a biped,
swells, suppurates, flows, and also causes fever.
<s>somavalka</s>, <s>aśvakarṇa</s>, <s>gojihvā</s>, and <s>haṃsapadī</s>,
the two turmerics, and red ochre form an application that removes claw-and-tooth poison.
When someone has been pierced in deep darkness and suspects poison from something,
because of the agitation of poison-fear, fever, vomiting, fainting, burning, or other symptoms may arise.
Languor, bewilderment, and diarrhea too: this is considered poison caused by suspicion.
The wise physician should treat it while reassuring the patient.

children.text: sitā vaigandhiko drākṣā payasyā madhukaṃ madhu
children.translated_text: Sugar, <s>vaigandhika</s>, grapes, <s>payasyā</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and honey
are a drink; water purified with mantras is for sprinkling, along with consolation and cheering.
<s>śāli</s> rice, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, <s>koradūṣa</s>, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>
are recommended for food, and rock salt for salt.
<s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>, <s>jīyantī</s>, eggplant, and <s>suniṣaṇṇaka</s>,

children.text: cucūrmaṇḍūkaparṇī ca śākaṃ ca kulakaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>cucū</s>, <s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, and the vegetable <s>kulaka</s> are beneficial.
<s>dhātrī</s> and pomegranate are useful for sourness; soups with mung beans and <s>hareṇu</s> are beneficial.
Meat broths of antelope, peacock, porcupine, quail, partridge, and spotted deer are beneficial.
Meat broths and soups prepared together with poison-destroying herbs,
and foods that do not cause burning, are the physician’s successful treatment for those afflicted by poison.
Even after being freed from poison, one should avoid incompatible food, overeating, anger,
hunger, fear, exertion, sexual intercourse, and especially daytime sleep.
Repeated laying-on of the head, swelling, and drooping of the lips and ears
Fever, rigidity of the eyes and body, trembling of the jaw, and aching of the limbs,
loss of hair, exhaustion, aversion, trembling, and dizziness
are the signs here in four-footed animals that have been bitten.
<s>Devadāru</s>, the two <s>haridrā</s>s, <s>sarala</s>, sandalwood, and <s>aguru</s>,
<s>rāsnā</s>, <s>gorocanā</s>, <s>ajājī</s>, <s>guggulu</s>, <s>vikṣurasa</s>, and <s>nata</s>,
made into a powder with rock salt and <s>anantā</s>, combined with cow's bile and honey,
is an <s>agada</s> (antidote) of universal effect for bitten four-footed animals.
For the sake of good fortune, women give sweat, menstrual blood, and impurities born from various limbs,
and also <s>gara</s> (artificial poisons) employed by enemies, mixed with food.
By these a man becomes pale, thin, and weak in digestion, and <s>gara</s> arises in him.
There may be distress in the vital parts, distension, and swelling of the hands and feet,

children.text: jaṭharaṃ grahaṇīdoṣo yakṣmā gulmaḥ kṣayo jvaraḥ
children.translated_text: abdominal disease, disorder of the <s>grahaṇī</s>, wasting disease, abdominal tumor, emaciation, and fever;
it may show the signs of this kind of disease and of others as well.
In dreams he generally sees cats, jackals, wild beasts, mongooses, and monkeys,
as well as rivers and the like dried up, along with trees.
A dark man sees himself fair in a dream, and a fair man sees himself dark;
or, with his senses impaired, he sees himself without ears or nose.

children.text: tamavekṣya bhiṣak prājñaḥ pṛcchet kiṃ kaiḥ kadā saha
children.translated_text: Having examined him, a wise physician should ask, 'What was eaten, by whom, when, and with whom?'
After quickly ascertaining what was eaten, the physician should administer emesis.
For him, fine copper dust with honey is a purifier of the heart.

children.text: śuddhe hṛdi tataḥ śāṇaṃ hemacūrṇasya dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: When the heart has been purified, he should then be given a <s>śāṇa</s> measure of gold powder.
Gold quickly removes all poisons and <s>gara</s> poisons.
Poison does not cling to a body touched by gold, just as water does not cling to a lotus leaf.
Buffalo ghee cooked with <s>nāgadantī</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>dravantī</s>, the latex and fruits of <s>snuk</s>,
and with an <s>āḍhaka</s> of cow's urine is beneficial
for pacifying those afflicted by serpent and insect poison, and those afflicted by <s>gara</s>.
<s>Śirīṣa</s> bark, <s>trikaṭu</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, sandalwood, and the two lotuses,
the two <s>balā</s>s, <s>sārivā</s>, <s>āsphoṭā</s>, <s>surabhī</s>, <s>nimba</s>, and <s>pāṭalā</s>,
<s>bandhujīva</s>, <s>āḍhakī</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, <s>surasā</s>, and <s>vatsaka</s>,
<s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>aṅkola</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, root of <s>arka</s>, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, and <s>padmaka</s>,
<s>viśālā</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, lac, <s>kovidāra</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,
<s>kaṭabhī</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>, and <s>rasāñjana</s>,
<s>śvetabhaṇḍā</s>, <s>aśvakhuraka</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>dāru</s>, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>,
<s>vidārī</s>, the essence of <s>madhuka</s>, and the fruit and bark of <s>karañja</s>,
the two <s>rajanī</s>s, <s>lodhra</s>, and an <s>akṣa</s> portion should be ground up, and an <s>āḍhaka</s> of ghee cooked with them.
Cooked with an equal amount of water and three <s>āḍhaka</s>s of goat and cow urine, it removes those poisons.
By drinking, anointing, and nasal administration it destroys epilepsy, wasting, insanity, possession by spirits, <s>gara</s>, abdominal disease,
pallor, worms, abdominal tumors, spleen disease, stiffness of the thighs, jaundice,
and disorders such as stiffness of the jaw and shoulders.
It also revives men who have died from poisoning and strangulation.
This best of ghees, named <s>Amṛta</s>, is for all poisons.
Thus the <s>Amṛta</s> ghee.
And here there are verses:
One carrying an umbrella and a rattle in the hand should move about by night and by day;
snakes, frightened by their shadow and sound, quickly disappear.

children.text: daṣṭamātro daśedāśu taṃ sarpaṃ loṣṭameva vā
children.translated_text: As soon as he has been bitten, he should quickly bite that snake, or else a clod of earth;
he should tie a band above the bite, and should cut and burn the bite.
Diamond, emerald, <s>sāra</s>, <s>picuka</s>, <s>viṣamūṣikā</s>,
<s>karketana</s>, serpent-jewel, <s>vaidūrya</s>, and elephant pearl
should be worn, along with <s>garamaṇi</s> gems and excellent herbs that remove poison,
and birds such as mynahs, cranes, peacocks, geese, parrots, and the like should be kept.
On this there is a verse:
Thus this treatment for the disease of the twofold poison, of many kinds, has been stated in detail.

children.text: adhītya vijñāya tathā prayojayan varjedviṣāṇāmaviṣahyatāṃ budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having studied it, understood it, and applied it properly, a wise man should avoid the incurability of poisons.

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte cikitsāsthāne viṣacikitsitaṃ nāma tryoviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s> and redacted by <s>Caraka</s>, in the Section on Therapeutics, the twenty-third chapter, named the Treatment of Poison, is complete.
Now, then, we shall explain the treatment of disorders of the <s>yoni</s> (female reproductive tract).
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.
On a holy slope of <s>Himavat</s>, possessing divine bathing places and medicinal herbs, with variegated minerals and rocks,
sacred and frequented by gods, siddhas, and seers,
while <s>Punarvasu</s>, self-controlled and seeing the true object through austerity and yoga, was dwelling there,
<s>Agniveśa</s> asked him again.

children.text: bhagavan yadapatyānāṃ mūlaṃ nāryaḥ paraṃ nṛṇām
children.translated_text: 'Blessed one, women are the chief root of offspring for men;
that root is injured by diseases located in their <s>yoni</s>.
Therefore I wish to hear the arising of those diseases, the symptoms of those that have arisen,
and their remedies, from the desire to benefit living beings.'
Questioned thus by his pupil, the best of seers, the son of <s>Atri</s>, spoke:
'Twenty disorders of the <s>yoni</s> were specified in the Compendium of Diseases.
They arise in women from improper conduct, from corrupted menstrual blood,

children.text: jāyante bījadoṣācca daivācca śṛṇu tāḥ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: from defect of the seed, and from fate. Hear them individually.
In a woman whose diet and activity are <s>vāta</s>-provoking, and who is herself prone to <s>vāta</s>, the wind,
increased and lodging in the <s>yoni</s>, produces piercing pain of the <s>yoni</s> with suffering,
stiffness, a sensation as if ants were crawling, and roughness,
as well as numbness, fatigue, and other <s>vāta</s>-born disorders.
That disorder is marked, through <s>vāyu</s>, by menstrual flow that is noisy, painful, frothy, scanty, and dry.
A <s>pitta</s>-born disorder arises from pungent, sour, salty, alkaline, and similar substances.
The <s>yoni</s> affected by <s>pitta</s> has burning, suppuration, fever, heat, and menstrual blood that is blue, yellow, or black,
with a discharge that is extremely hot and corpse-smelling.
If <s>kapha</s>, increased by obstructive substances, should vitiate a woman's <s>yoni</s>,
It makes the <s>yoni</s> (female reproductive tract) slimy, cold, seized by itching, and with little pain.
It is pale in color and likewise carries pale, slimy menstrual discharge.
When all tastes are eaten indiscriminately, the three <s>doṣas</s>, after vitiating all the humors,
remain in the <s>yoni</s> and womb and afflict the <s>yoni</s> with their own symptoms.
That condition becomes afflicted with burning and pain and carries a white, slimy discharge.
In a woman using things that provoke blood and <s>pitta</s>, the blood, vitiated by <s>pitta</s>,
flows excessively in the <s>yoni</s>, even when conception has occurred, accompanied by blood.
If <s>pitta</s> situated in the <s>yoni</s> and womb should vitiate the blood,
that is considered <s>sārajaskā</s>, greatly producing emaciation and discoloration.
From failure to wash the <s>yoni</s>, creatures arise and cause itching.
That condition is <s>acaraṇā</s>; because of that itching she longs excessively for friction.
Through excessive intercourse, aggravated <s>vāta</s> causes swelling, numbness, and pains

children.text: karoti kupito yonau sā cāticaraṇā matā ||
children.translated_text: in a woman's <s>yoni</s>; this is considered <s>aticaraṇā</s>.
From intercourse with a girl who is too young, <s>vāyu</s>, causing pain in the back, waist, thighs, and groins,

children.text: rujan dūṣayate yoniṃ vāyuḥ prākcaraṇā hi sā ||
children.translated_text: vitiates the <s>yoni</s>; this is indeed <s>prākcaraṇā</s>.
In a pregnant woman, because of habitual use of phlegm-producing things and from restraining vomiting and breath,
angered <s>vāyu</s> brings <s>kapha</s> to the <s>yoni</s> and vitiates it.

children.text: pāṇḍuṃ satodamāsrāvaṃ śvetaṃ sravati vā kapham
children.translated_text: It discharges a pale flow with pricking pain, or discharges white <s>kapha</s>.
A <s>yoni</s> pervaded by <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> disease is <s>upaplutā</s>.
In a woman of pitta constitution, through intercourse and from suppressing sneezing and belching,
<s>vāyu</s> combined with <s>pitta</s> vitiates the woman's <s>yoni</s>.
Swollen, unable to bear touch, and painful, it discharges dark-blue and yellow blood.
When she is afflicted with pain in the pelvis, groins, and back and with fever, it is <s>pariplutā</s>.
From suppression and upward turning of natural urges, <s>anila</s> causes the <s>yoni</s> to turn upward.
Afflicted with pain, she releases menstrual blood that is obstructed and difficult to pass.

children.text: ārtave sā vimukte tu tatkṣaṇaṃ labhate sukham
children.translated_text: But when that menstrual flow is released, she immediately obtains relief.
Because of the upward movement of the menses, the wise know it as <s>udāvartinī</s>.
In a woman carrying at an improper time, <s>anila</s>, obstructed by the fetus,
mixed with <s>śleṣman</s> and blood, produces a fleshy knob in the <s>yoni</s>.
Because that obstructs the path of blood, she is considered <s>karṇinī</s> by reason of it.
When, because of dryness, <s>vāyu</s> destroys each fetus as soon as it arises,

children.text: duṣṭaśoṇitajaṃ nāryāḥ putraghnī nāma sā matā
children.translated_text: arising from vitiated blood in the woman, that condition is called <s>putraghnī</s>.
In a woman over-sated with intercourse, who has intercourse while oppressed by food,
<s>vāyu</s>, lodged in the channel of the <s>yoni</s> while her body is wrongly positioned,
bends the mouth of the <s>yoni</s>, with pains of bone, flesh, and <s>vāta</s>.
Greatly painful and unable to have intercourse, the <s>yoni</s> is considered <s>antarmukhī</s>.
When a woman is still in the womb, <s>vāyu</s>, through dryness, vitiates her <s>yoni</s>.
Because of a maternal fault it makes the opening minute; that is <s>sūcīmukhī</s>.
When a woman suppresses natural urges at the time of intercourse, aggravated <s>anila</s>
causes retention of feces and urine, pain, and drying of the mouth of the <s>yoni</s>.
After six days or seven nights, when semen has gone to the womb,

children.text: sarujaṃ nīrujaṃ vāpi yā sravet sā tu vāminī
children.translated_text: the woman who discharges it, with pain or without pain, is <s>vāminī</s>.
Because of a defect of the seed, her receptacle is struck by <s>māruta</s> while she is in the womb.
She becomes man-hating, without breasts, and sterile; she is not amenable to treatment.
Through intercourse on an uneven and painful bed, aggravated <s>anila</s>
stiffens the mouth of the woman's womb and <s>yoni</s>.
It has an unclosed mouth, is painful, and carries a rough, foamy discharge.
A great <s>yoni</s> has protruding flesh and pain in the joints and groins.
With these symptoms, twenty diseases born in the <s>yoni</s> have been taught.
Afflicted by these <s>doṣas</s>, the <s>yoni</s> does not retain semen.

children.text: tasmādgarbhaṃ na gṛhṇāti strī gacchatyāmayān bahūn ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the woman does not conceive and goes on to many diseases.
She suffers from <s>gulma</s>, piles, <s>pradara</s>, and the like, and from severe oppression by <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: āsāṃ ṣoḍaśa yāstvantyā ādye dve pittadoṣaje ||
children.translated_text: Of these, sixteen are the later ones; the first two arise from a fault of <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Pariplutā</s> and <s>vāminī</s> are held to be of the nature of <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Karṇinī</s> and <s>upaplutā</s> arise from <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>; the remaining ones are born of <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣas</s> afflict their bodies with their own signs.
In conditions born of <s>vāta</s>, one should perform oleation, sweating, <s>basti</s>, and the like, which remove <s>anila</s>.
In those produced by <s>pitta</s>, one should perform cool treatment that counteracts blood and <s>pitta</s>.
In those born of <s>śleṣman</s>, the discerning physician should apply drying and hot procedures.

children.text: sannipāte vimiśraṃ tu saṃsṛṣṭāsu ca kārayet
children.translated_text: In a combined disorder, and in mixed conditions, he should apply a mixed treatment.
Having oleated and fomented the woman, he should set right again a badly positioned <s>yoni</s>.
With the hand he should bend a crooked one back, and should enlarge a constricted one.
He should insert one that has protruded and turn back one that is too open.

children.text: yoniḥ sthānāpavṛttā hi śalyabhūtā matā striyāḥ
children.translated_text: For a woman, a <s>yoni</s> displaced from its place is considered like a foreign body.
For every disordered <s>yoni</s>, through gentle procedures beginning with emesis,
he should treat the oleated and fomented woman with the five purificatory measures.
When she has been well purified in every way, the remaining treatment is prescribed.
Treatment that removes <s>vāta</s> disease is always beneficial for those afflicted by <s>vāta</s>.
With meat from aquatic and marshy animals, with milk, and with rice mixed with sesame,
he should treat her by tube-sweats and pot-sweats using <s>vāta</s>-pacifying herbs.
Anointed with salt and oil, and along with heated stones and slabs,
fomented, with her limbs sprinkled with lukewarm water, she should be fed with <s>vāta</s>-pacifying broths.
In two <s>droṇas</s> of decoction of <s>balā</s>, one should cook one <s>āḍhaka</s> of ghee and oil
with pastes of <s>sthirā</s>, <s>payasyā</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, and <s>jīvaka</s>,
with <s>śrāvaṇī</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, <s>mudgaparṇī</s>, <s>pīlu</s>, and <s>māṣaparṇī</s>,

Prepared with the pastes in four times the quantity of milk, it should be drunk according to one's strength.

children.text: vātapittakṛtān rogān hatvā garbhaṃ dadhāti tat
children.translated_text: It eliminates diseases caused by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, and enables conception.
With <s>kāśmarya</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, grapes, <s>kāsamarda</s>, and <s>parūṣaka</s>,
with <s>punarnavā</s>, the two <s>rajanī</s> herbs, <s>kākanāsā</s>, and <s>sahācara</s>,

<s>Pippalī</s>, <s>kuñcikā</s>, <s>ajājī</s>, <s>vṛṣaka</s>, rock salt, and <s>vacā</s>,
as well as alkali of barley, <s>ajamodā</s>, sugar, and <s>citraka</s>,

This is for the removal of pain in the yoni and flanks, heart disease, abdominal tumors, and piles.
One should drink <s>vṛṣaka</s>, roots of citron, and <s>madayantikā</s>

In colic pain one should drink milk boiled with <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, and <s>vṛṣaka</s>.
One should also bathe the part with decoctions of <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and <s>dantī</s>.

children.text: saindhavaṃ tagaraṃ kuṣṭhaṃ bṛhatī devadāru ca ||
children.translated_text: Rock salt, <s>tagara</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, and <s>devadāru</s>
are made into pastes in equal parts and cooked into oil; this oil, retained there, removes pain.
With <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>mālatī</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
and with <s>nidigdhikā</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, and <s>yūthikā</s>, each in a <s>karṣa</s> measure,

children.text: tailaprasthaṃ gavāṃ mūtre kṣīre ca dviguṇe pacet ||
children.translated_text: one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of oil in cow urine and twice as much milk.

children.text: śītāḥ pittaharāḥ kāryāḥ snehanārthaṃ ghṛtāni ca ||

children.text: siddhe śīte ca madhunaḥ pippalyāśca palāṣṭakam ||
children.translated_text: When it has been prepared and cooled, eight <s>pala</s> measures each of honey and <s>pippalī</s>
should be mixed with ten <s>pala</s> measures of sugar; then one should lick a palmful of it.
It removes disorders of the yoni, blood, and semen; it is aphrodisiac and promotes male conception.

children.text: kṣataṃ kṣataṃ raktapittaṃ kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ halīmakam
children.translated_text: It conquers wounds and injuries, bleeding disorders, cough, dyspnea, and <s>halīmaka</s>,
jaundice, <s>vātarakta</s>, spreading skin inflammation, and seizure of the heart and head.
It overcomes insanity, restlessness, and epilepsy that are of <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> nature.
Thus, the great <s>śatāvarī</s> ghee.

is conception-producing and physician-approved for yonis affected by <s>pitta</s>.

Barley flour soaked in the milk of <s>arka</s>, together with rock salt,

A <s>droṇa</s> of young <s>udumbara</s> fruits, together with a <s>droṇa</s> of water,

With lac, exudates from the bark of <s>dhava</s> and <s>palāśa</s>, and with <s>śālmalī</s>,

children.text: piṣṭaiḥ siddhasya tailasya picuṃ yonau nidhāpayet ||

From sesame seeds steeped six times in the milk-sap of <s>udumbara</s>,

With <s>dhātakī</s>, leaves of <s>āmalakī</s>, <s>srotoja</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and blue lotus,

With decoctions of <s>karīra</s>, <s>dhava</s>, neem, <s>arka</s>, bamboo, <s>kośāmra</s>, and <s>jambu</s>,

children.text: tilacūrṇaṃ dadhi ghṛtaṃ phāṇitaṃ śaukarī vasā ||
children.translated_text: Sesame powder, curd, ghee, molasses, and pig fat

<s>bāhlīka</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>bilva</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>lodhra</s> with red ochre,
<s>kaṭvaṅga</s>, black pepper, dry ginger, raisins, red sandalwood,
<s>kaṭphala</s>, <s>vatsaka</s>, <s>anantā</s>, <s>dhātakī</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and <s>arjuna</s>:

It destroys bleeding that is discharged in piles and diarrhea,

children.text: doṣāgantukṛtā ye ca bālānāṃ tāṃśca nāśayet ||

It forcibly turns back women's disorders of the vagina, disorders of menstrual blood, white, blue, yellowish,

This powder, called <s>Puṣyānuga</s>, is beneficial and was praised by <s>Ātreya</s>.
Thus the <s>Puṣyānuga</s> powder.
The root of <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>, with honey, should be taken with rice-water.

children.text: rasāñjanaṃ ca lākṣāṃ ca chāgena payasā pibet
children.translated_text: One should drink <s>rasāñjana</s> and lac with goat's milk.
The pastes of the leaves of <s>rājādana</s> and <s>kapittha</s>, fried in ghee,

children.text: madhukaṃ triphalāṃ lodhraṃ mustaṃ saurāṣṭrikāṃ madhu ||
children.translated_text: <s>madhuka</s>, <s>triphala</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>musta</s>, alum, and honey,
or neem and <s>guḍūcī</s> with liquors, should be drunk in kapha-type <s>asṛgdara</s>.
In pitta-type <s>asṛgdara</s>, one should take purgation with the <s>Mahātikta</s> preparation.
And what has been prescribed as beneficial for discharge of the fetus should also be done.
Ghee prepared with a decoction of <s>kāśmarya</s> and <s>kuṭaja</s>, given as an upper enema,
is beneficial for bloody vaginal disorders, amenorrhea, and <s>putraghnī</s>.
A woman without menstruation should drink a preparation cooked with the blood of deer, goat, sheep, and boar, curds, sour fruits, and ghee,

children.text: arajaskā pibet siddhaṃ jīvanīyaiḥ payo 'pi vā
children.translated_text: or milk cooked with the life-promoting herbs.
In <s>karṇinī</s>, <s>acaraṇā</s>, dry vagina, <s>prākcaraṇā</s>,
and in kapha-vāta conditions, oil should be given by upper enema.
Linen steeped twenty-one times in cow bile or fish bile,

That cleanses the channels and removes itching, moisture, and swelling.
For <s>prāgaticāriṇī</s>, with vāta-pacifying oils cooked a hundred times,
she should be given evacuative and unctuous enemas and should be fomented with vāta-subduing substances,
and treated appropriately with unctuous substances, foods, and poultices.
A retaining gruel is prescribed with <s>śatāhvā</s>, barley, wheat, yeast, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>,
<s>balā</s>, <s>ākhuparṇikā</s>, and <s>śryāhvā</s>.
For <s>vāminī</s> and <s>upaplutā</s>, the regimen beginning with oleation and sweating
should be carried out; after that there should be an oil tampon, and then nourishment.
An oil tampon cooked in astringent decoctions of the barks of <s>śallakī</s>, <s>jiṅginī</s>, <s>jambu</s>, <s>dhava</s>,
and the five barks removes <s>viplutā</s>.
In <s>karṇinī</s>, a wick made with <s>kuṣṭha</s>, long pepper, tips of <s>arka</s>, and rock salt,
prepared in goat's urine, should be held; and all kapha-expelling measures should be used.
Oleation with <s>traivṛta</s>, sweating, and meat broths of domestic, marsh, and aquatic animals,
and milk enemas with <s>daśamūla</s>, are for upward-moving vāta and vāta pains.
She should also be given an unctuous enema with <s>traivṛta</s> and the enema called upper enema.
This very same treatment is prescribed for <s>mahāyoni</s> and for prolapse.
The fat of bears and boars, and ghee cooked with sweet herbs,
should be used to fill the enlarged vagina, and it should be bound with linen strips.
Having anointed a prolapsed vagina with ghee, warmed it with milk-steam, and replaced it,
one should bind it with a lump of <s>veśavāra</s> until the time for urination.
And whatever procedure has been stated for vāta disorders should be carried out
by the wise physician in all vaginal disorders, especially in <s>mahāyoni</s>.
For without vāta the vagina of women does not become thoroughly disordered.
After pacifying it, one should apply the remedy for the other <s>doṣa</s>.
In pale <s>asṛgdara</s>, one should drink paste of <s>rohītaka</s> root with water,
or paste of <s>āmalakī</s> seed with sugar and honey.
With honey, one may have her lick powder of <s>āmalakā</s>, or its juice.
Then she should drink paste of <s>lodhra</s> with a decoction of banyan bark.

children.text: āsrāve kṣaumapaṭṭaṃ vā bhāvitaṃ tena dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: For discharge, she should hold a linen band soaked in that,

With the vagina anointed with oil, a wick of <s>lodhra</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, or <s>madhuka</s>,
