children.translated_text: mixed with honey, should be held, and likewise all astringent wicks.
To cut off discharge, after anointing it, one may fumigate with ghee-soaked
<s>sarala</s>, <s>guggulu</s>, barley, oil, pungent substances, and fish products.
Green vitriol, <s>triphala</s>, <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, <s>samaṅgā</s>, mango stone, and <s>dhātakī</s>,
as a powder combined with honey, produce clarity in sliminess.
A paste of the barks of <s>palāśa</s>, <s>sarja</s>, and <s>jambu</s>, with <s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>moca</s>, and <s>dhātakī</s>,
is desired as a styptic for conditions that are slimy and excessively wet.
For those that are stiff and rough, a softening treatment should be done.
She should hold <s>veśavāra</s>, or milk-rice, and likewise <s>kṛśarā</s>.

children.text: durgandhānāṃ kaṣāyaḥ syāttauvaraḥ kalka eva vā ||
children.translated_text: For foul-smelling conditions there should be a decoction of <s>tauvara</s>, or else a paste,
or a powder of all fragrant substances, to remove putrid smell.

children.text: evaṃ yoniṣu śuddhāsu garbhaṃ vindanti yoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the vaginas have thus been purified, women obtain pregnancy,
provided that the seed is unimpaired and natural and the living principle enters.
The generative organ also of a man purified by the five procedures
should be examined by the colors of the <s>doṣa</s>s; if vitiated, it should be treated with remedies that counteract them.
And here there are verses.
The disorders of the <s>yoni</s> (female reproductive tract), with their signs, causes, and treatment,
have been stated properly and in detail by the virtuous seer of truth.
Then <s>Agniveśa</s> again asked the best of physicians,
approaching <s>Ātreya</s>: 'Blameless one, the semen disorders
of men, eight in all, were fully enumerated by you in the chapter on diseases.
O best of physicians, state their causes, the appearance of corrupted and uncorrupted semen,

children.text: cikitsitaṃ ca kārtsnyona klaibyaṃ yacca caturvidham ||
children.translated_text: their treatment in full, and also the fourfold <s>klaibya</s> (impotence),
and the <s>pradara</s> (excessive discharge) that was mentioned among complications of disorders of the <s>yoni</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ nidānaṃ liṅgaṃ ca cikitsāṃ caiva tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tell their causes, signs, and treatment truly,
both in summary and in detail, O best of physicians.'
To him, eager to hear, the foremost sage spoke.
'Since the seed that arises from sexual intercourse, from excitement and the <s>yoni</s>,
is called male <s>śukra</s> (semen), therefore I shall explain it; listen.
Just as a seed spoiled by untimely water, worms, insects, or fire

children.text: na virohati saṃduṣṭaṃ tathā śukraṃ śarīriṇām ||
children.translated_text: does not sprout, being corrupted, so too is the semen of embodied beings.
From excessive intercourse, from exercise, from using what is unsuitable,

children.text: akāle vāpyayonau vā maithunaṃ na ca gacchataḥ ||
children.translated_text: or from intercourse at the wrong time, in an improper <s>yoni</s>, or from not engaging in intercourse,
from using foods that are dry, bitter, astringent, excessively salty, sour, or hot,
from going to women who do not know the sexual sentiment, and also from old age,
from anxiety, grief, lack of trust, injury by knife, alkali, or fire, and mental disturbance,
from fear, anger, sorcery, and in one emaciated by diseases,
from suppressing natural urges, from wounds, and from the severe corruption of the bodily tissues,

children.text: doṣāḥ pṛthak samastā vā prāpya retovahāḥ sirāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>doṣa</s>s, separately or together, reaching the channels that carry semen,
quickly corrupt the <s>śukra</s>; I shall explain that according to its divisions.

children.text: phenilaṃ tanu rūkṣaṃ ca vivarṇaṃ pūti picchilam ||
children.translated_text: It is frothy, thin, dry, discolored, foul-smelling, slimy,
mixed with other bodily tissues, and, as the eighth, sinking downward.

children.text: phenilaṃ tanu rūkṣaṃ ca kṛcchreṇālpaṃ ca mārutāt ||
children.translated_text: Semen impaired by <s>māruta</s> (vāta) becomes frothy, thin, and dry,
and is discharged with difficulty and in small quantity; it is not fit for conception.
When corrupted by <s>pitta</s>, semen is bluish or yellow, excessively hot and foul-smelling,
and it comes out burning the penis.
When affected by <s>śleṣman</s> (kapha), its channel is obstructed and it becomes extremely slimy.
From excessive intercourse with women, from blows, or from wounds,
the semen of a person generally comes forth mixed with blood.
Because of suppression of urges, semen, obstructed in its path by <s>vāyu</s>,
passes with difficulty, clotted; the eighth type is the sinking kind.
Thus the eight disorders of semen have been described together with their signs.

children.text: snigdhaṃ ghanaṃ picchilaṃ ca madhuraṃ cāvidāhi ca ||
children.translated_text: One should know pure <s>retas</s> (semen) to be unctuous, thick, slimy, sweet, non-burning,
white, and like crystal.
When semen has become corrupted, it should then be treated
with those agreeable and beneficial applications of aphrodisiac formulations,

children.text: duṣṭaṃ yadā bhavecchukraṃ tadā tat samupācaret ||
children.translated_text: with formulations that remove <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding pitta disorder), and also with those used for disorders of the <s>yoni</s>.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ ca jīvanīyaṃ yaccyavanaprāśa eva ca
children.translated_text: The life-promoting ghee, and <s>Cyavanaprāśa</s> as well,
and the use of <s>girija</s> remove defects of semen.
For semen affected by <s>vāta</s>, decoction enemas together with oil enemas are beneficial;
for a <s>pitta</s> condition, the <s>Abhayāmalakīya</s> rejuvenative is recommended.
The rejuvenative made of <s>māgadhī</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, iron, and <s>triphala</s>,
and that made of <s>bhallātaka</s>, destroys semen disorder arising from <s>kapha</s>.
If semen is mixed with another bodily tissue, then, after examining it with reasoning,
one should apply treatment according to the <s>doṣa</s>, as taught by physicians skilled in <s>doṣa</s>s and tissues.
Ghee, milk, meat soups, <s>śāli</s> rice, barley, wheat, and <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice
are recommended for semen disorders, and especially enema therapy.
Thus the treatment of the eight semen disorders has been stated by the sage.
Since <s>klaibya</s> arising from semen disorder is cured precisely through purification of it,
therefore I shall explain it to you properly and exactly, O <s>Agniveśa</s>.
From injury to the seed, injury to the standard, old age, and depletion of semen,
<s>klaibya</s> arises. Hear its general sign.
Though constantly inclined toward imagining it, and though the woman is dear and obedient,

children.text: na yāti liṅgaśaitthilyāt kadācidyāti vā yadi
children.translated_text: he does not approach her because of slackness of the penis; or if he sometimes does approach,
he is afflicted with breathlessness, his limbs sweat, and his intention and effort are futile.
His penis is withered and he is seedless: this is the sign of <s>klaibya</s>.

From food that is cold, dry, scanty, spoiled, incompatible, or undigested,
from grief, anxiety, fear, terror, and excessive intercourse with women,
from sorcery, lack of trust, and wasting of <s>rasa</s> and the other tissues,
from derangement of <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣa</s>s, likewise from fasting and exertion,
from women's lack of knowledge of sexual pleasure, and from improper use of the five therapies,
there arises the type due to injury of the seed; the man becomes pale-colored and very weak,
with little vitality and little sexual excitement toward women.
He is afflicted by heart disease, pallor, darkness before the eyes, jaundice, and exhaustion,
and tormented by vomiting, diarrhea, colic, cough, and fever.
That is <s>klaibya</s> born of injury to the seed. Hear the one caused by breaking of the standard.
From food that is too sour, salty, alkaline, incompatible, or unsuitable,
from excessive drinking of water, from irregular eating, and from eating flour preparations and heavy foods,
from using curds, milk, and meat of marshy animals, and from excessive emaciation,
from intercourse with virgins and also from intercourse in an improper <s>yoni</s>,
with a woman suffering from a long disease, one long abandoned, and likewise a menstruating woman,
with a foul-smelling woman, one with a corrupted <s>yoni</s>, and likewise one having a discharge,
If, through delusion, a man delighted by desire approaches such a woman,
or because of intercourse with a quadruped and injury to the penis,
or from not washing the penis, from wounds made by weapons, teeth, or nails,
from blows or crushing by wood, and from excessive use of irritating applications,
and from obstruction of semen, <s>dhvajabhaṅga</s> begins.
Swelling, pain in the penis, and redness are observed.
Severe blisters arise, and suppuration of the organ may occur.

The discharge resembles water from washed rice and has a dark reddish color.
It may become ring-shaped, and the lesion is hard to grasp or confine.
Fever, thirst, dizziness, fainting, and vomiting arise in him.
Blood may flow out, black, blue, turbid, and reddish.

children.text: agnineva ca dagdhasya tīvro dāhaḥ savedanaḥ
children.translated_text: As in one burned by fire, there is intense burning with pain,
either in the bladder, the testicles, the perineal seam, or the groins.
At times there is also a slimy or pale discharge.
A dull, stiff swelling arises, with scanty outflow.

children.text: cirācca pākaṃ vrajati śūghraṃ vātha pramucyate
children.translated_text: It ripens after a long time, or else it is quickly discharged.
Worms also arise, and it becomes moist and foul-smelling.
His glans, penis, and even testicles disintegrate.
This is said to be impotence caused by <s>dhvajabhaṅga</s>.
Some declare this <s>dhvajabhaṅga</s> to be of five kinds.
Now I shall explain impotence produced by old age; listen to that.
Age is said to be threefold: inferior, middle, and superior.
In men of very advanced age, semen generally wastes away
because of the depletion of <s>rasa</s> and the other tissues, and likewise because of not using aphrodisiacs,
and because strength, virility, and the senses gradually decline,
because life itself declines, and because of lack of food, exertion, and fatigue.
For men, impotence born of old age arises from these causes.
Because of it, he becomes exceedingly depleted in tissue and very weak.
Discolored, weak, and miserable, he soon comes under disease.
This is the old-age-born type; now hear the fourth, the one born of wasting.
From excessive brooding, from grief, anger, and fear,
and from jealousy, longing, intoxication, and agitation, when a man is constantly overcome,
or when, being emaciated, he uses dry food, drink, and medicine,
and if he is of weak constitution and without food,
or from unwholesome eating, the <s>rasa</s> established in the heart,
which is the foremost tissue, quickly wastes away in men.
Then the bodily tissues beginning with blood also waste away in him.
Among these, ending with semen, semen is regarded as the supreme abode.
If, through excessive exhilaration of mind, he engages too much in intercourse,

children.text: tasyāśu kṣīyate śukraṃ tataḥ prāpnoti saṃkṣayam
children.translated_text: his semen is quickly depleted; then he reaches wasting.

children.text: ghoraṃ vyādhimavāpnoti maraṇaṃ vā sa gacchati ||
children.translated_text: He obtains a terrible disease, or he goes to death.
Therefore semen should be especially guarded by one who desires health.
Thus impotence has been described in four forms by causes and signs.
But some say that two forms of impotence are incurable: those arising from <s>dhvajabhaṅga</s> and from wasting,
as well as that caused by cutting off the penis and by removing the testicles.
Because of a defect in the seed of the mother and father, and through inauspicious acts of one whose self is unpurified,

children.text: garbhasthasya yadā doṣāḥ prāpya retovahāḥ sirāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when, in the fetus, the <s>doṣas</s> reach the channels that carry semen,
they quickly dry them up; through their destruction the semen too is damaged.
In that case, though complete in all limbs, he is a male who is not a man.
These have been explained as incurable because of the accumulation of combined <s>doṣas</s>.
Now hear the treatment in brief and in detail from this point onward.
The medicine which I have prescribed for disorders of semen, O sinless one,
should be used for calming impotence, along with whatever is beneficial for depletion and injury.
Enemas, milk, ghee, and the aphrodisiac formulas that are accepted,
and rasayana applications: all these should be employed.
The physician who knows medicine and timing should examine the body, the <s>doṣas</s>, digestive fire, and strength.
In impotence caused by sexual intercourse and also by derangement of the bodily tissues,
one should also use divine therapy, and medicine in that caused by sorcery.
This, in brief, has been stated as treatment for the pacification of impotence.
Again I shall explain in detail the medicine for the forms of impotence.
For one whose body has been well fomented and oleated, an unctuous purgation should be given.
Then one should prescribe eating of food, or again a non-unctuous enema.
The wise physician should administer it, and afterward should give him an unctuous enema.
Then he should give a non-unctuous enema with <s>palāśa</s>, castor, <s>mustā</s>, and the like.
The aphrodisiac formulas which were previously described

children.text: bhiṣajā te prayojyāḥ syuḥ klaibye bījopaghātaje
children.translated_text: should be employed by the physician in impotence caused by injury to the seed.
Having recognized impotence caused by <s>dhvajabhaṅga</s>, he should perform its treatment.
He should apply poultices and sprinklings, or perform bloodletting.

children.text: snehapānaṃ ca kurvīta sasnehaṃ ca virecanam ||
children.translated_text: He should also undertake drinking of unctuous substances and an unctuous purgation.
Then he should perform an unctuous enema, or again a non-unctuous enema.
In that condition, the skilled physician should carry out all procedures as for a wound.
In impotence born of old age and also in that born of wasting, he should arrange
a cleansing treatment with unctuous substances, beneficial for one prepared with oleation and fomentation.
Milk, ghee, aphrodisiac formulas, and sustaining enemas,
and rasayana applications are said to be the treatment for both of them.
This treatment for the forms of impotence has been stated by me in detail.

children.text: yaḥ pūrvamuktaḥ pradaraḥ śṛṇu hetvādibhistu tam ||
children.translated_text: That <s>pradara</s> which was mentioned earlier: hear about it with its causes and the rest.
When a woman consumes to excess foods that are salty, sour, and heavy,
and also pungent, burning, unctuous foods and meats,
meats of domestic and aquatic animals, fatty foods, <s>kṛśarā</s>, milk-rice, curd,
<s>śukra</s>, whey, liquor, and the like, her <s>anila</s> becomes aggravated.
Having taken blood beyond its proper measure, and entering the vessels situated in the womb,
the menstrual channels, it takes up the blood and that menstrual fluid.
Because it quickly increases that flow through a disturbance of the nutritive fluid and through excess,
therefore those skilled in the treatise call this <s>asṛgdara</s>.

children.text: rajaḥ pradīryate yasmāt pradarastena sa smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Because the menstrual fluid is torn forth, it is therefore remembered as <s>pradara</s>.
The cause and the sign have thus been stated in general.
In detail it is fourfold: from <s>vāta</s> and the other doṣas, and from their combined aggravation.
After this I shall explain its causes, forms, and medical treatment.
<s>Māruta</s>, aggravated by dry substances and the like, takes up blood as before

children.text: kupitaḥ pradaraṃ kuryāllakṣaṇaṃ tasya me śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: and produces <s>pradara</s>; hear from me its symptom.

children.text: phenilaṃ tanu rūkṣaṃ ca śyāvaṃ cāruṇameva ca
children.translated_text: It is frothy, thin, dry, dark, and also reddish,
like water colored by <s>kiṃśuka</s>; it may be painful or without pain.
In the waist, groin, heart region, flanks, back, and hips, <s>māruta</s>
causes severe pain; they know this as the <s>vāta</s>-type.
When <s>pitta</s> is aggravated by sour, hot, salty, and alkaline things,

children.text: pūrvavat pradaraṃ kuryāt paittikaṃ liṅgataḥ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: it produces <s>pradara</s> as before; hear the <s>pitta</s>-type by its signs.
Blue, or else yellow, very hot, and also blackish,
extremely red blood flows again and again, accompanied by pain.
Joined with burning, redness, thirst, delusion, fever, and dizziness,
it is <s>paittika asṛgdara</s>; now the phlegmatic type will be described.
<s>Kapha</s>, aggravated as before by causes such as heavy substances,

children.text: pradaraṃ kurute tasya lakṣaṇaṃ tattvataḥ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: produces <s>pradara</s>; hear its symptom in truth.

children.text: picchilaṃ pāṇḍuvarṇaṃ caguru snigdhaṃ ca śītalam
children.translated_text: The blood flows slimy, pale-colored, heavy, unctuous, and cold,
mixed with phlegm, thick, and producing slight pain.
It is accompanied by vomiting, anorexia, nausea, dyspnea, and cough.
Here the general cause of the defects of milk will be stated.
The very same cause that belongs to the three-doṣa form of <s>pradara</s>
should be understood for <s>asṛgdara</s> joined with all three signs and not having only one condition.
But when a woman is excessively afflicted and her blood is depleted,
then, because she has followed all the causes, <s>anila</s> becomes greatly increased.
Through the blood-path it drives forth <s>kapha</s>, strong in an opposing way,
foul-smelling, slimy, yellow, and scorched by the heat of <s>pitta</s>.
Taking up fat and adipose tissue as far as it can, the forceful one
sends it out through the birth-passage, resembling ghee, marrow, and fat.
It flows constantly as a discharge, and she is affected with thirst, burning, and fever.
Her blood is depleted and she is weak; one should reject her as incurable.
Menstrual fluid that appears monthly, free from sliminess, burning, and pain, and continuing for five nights,
neither very abundant nor very scanty, should be declared pure.
Menstrual fluid the color of the <s>guñjā</s> fruit, and resembling lotus and lac-dye,
like an <s>indragopaka</s> insect, should be declared pure.
Whatever treatment has been stated here for yonis of the <s>vātala</s> and other types,

children.text: caturṇāṃ pradarāṇāṃ ca tat sarvaṃ kārayedbhiṣak ||
children.translated_text: the physician should perform all of that for the four kinds of <s>pradara</s>.
And what has been prescribed for those with bloody diarrhea, likewise for those with <s>śoṇitapitta</s>,

children.text: raktārśasāṃ ca yat proktaṃ bheṣajaṃ tacca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: and what has been taught for bleeding piles, that treatment too should be performed.
The excellence of the nurse, breast, and breast milk was explained before in detail,
as was the production of breast milk and also the purification of breast milk.

children.text: vātādiduṣṭe liṅgaṃ ca kṣīṇasya ca cikitsitam
children.translated_text: The signs when it is vitiated by <s>vāta</s> and the other doṣas, and the treatment of diminished milk,
all that has been stated; but the eight defects of milk that have been taught
should be understood by the best physician, whose eye is the treatise, as included under <s>vāta</s> and the rest.
Since pupils are of three kinds, I shall therefore explain them at length.
From indigestion, unsuitable, irregular, incompatible, or excessive eating,
and from using salty, sour, pungent, alkaline, and moistening substances,
from distress of mind and body, sleeplessness at night, and brooding,
from suppressing urges that have arisen and from forcing those that have not arisen,
from sweet rice prepared with molasses, <s>kṛśarā</s>, curd, and <s>mandaka</s>,
from obstructive meats, and from domestic, marsh, and aquatic animals,
from repeatedly eating and then sleeping by day, and from excessive use of liquor,
from lack of exertion, from injury, from anger, and from wasting illnesses,

children.text: doṣāḥ kṣīravahāḥ prāpya sirāḥ stanyaṃ pradūṣya ca
children.translated_text: the doṣas reach the milk-carrying vessels and corrupt the breast milk.
They again make it eightfold according to doṣa; learn that from me.
In the <s>anila</s>-type there are bad taste, accumulation of foam, and dryness.
From <s>pitta</s> come discoloration and foul smell; from <s>kapha</s>, unctuousness, sliminess, and heaviness.
<s>Anila</s>, aggravated by its own dry and similar provokers,
becomes enraged, reaches the receptacle of milk, and corrupts the nutritive fluid of the breast milk.
Mixed with <s>vāta</s>, it becomes tasteless; the child who drinks it grows thin.

children.text: na *cāsya svadate kṣīraṃ kṛcchreṇa ca vivardhate ||
children.translated_text: Nor does the milk please him, and he grows only with difficulty.
Likewise, aggravated <s>vāyu</s>, churning the breast milk within,
makes an accumulation of foam, and that milk flows only with difficulty.
Because of it, the child has a wasted voice and obstruction of feces, urine, and wind,
and he develops a <s>vātika</s> disease of the head or coryza.
As before, <s>anila</s>, aggravated in the breast milk, dries up its unctuousness.
When the child drinks that dry milk, because of its dryness a loss of strength arises.
Pitta, angered by hot and similar factors, floods the receptacle of breast milk,
and causes discoloration of the milk, making it bluish, yellowish, blackish, and the like.
The infant becomes discolored in body, sweaty, thirsty, and has loose stool,
with a body that is always hot, and does not relish that breast.
When pitta is aggravated as before, the milk acquires a foul smell,
and a child who drinks it may develop pallor and jaundice.
Kapha, angered by heavy and similar factors and lodged in the woman's milk-receptacle,
because of its unctuousness makes that milk excessively oily.
Because of it the child becomes vomiting, retching, and drooling,
with the channels constantly coated, and accompanied by sleepiness and fatigue.
He is afflicted with dyspnea and cough, and beset by salivation and darkness of vision.

children.text: abhibhūya kaphaḥ stanyaṃ picchilaṃ kurute yadā ||
children.translated_text: When kapha overpowers the breast milk, it makes it slimy.
An infant who drinks that milk becomes drooling, with swollen face and eyes, and sluggish.
Kapha lodged in the milk-receptacle, because of heaviness, produces heaviness of the milk.
It makes it heavy; after drinking that heavy milk, the child contracts heart disease,
and it may produce various other diseases dependent on milk.
When milk is corrupted by vāta and the other doṣas, disorders of the same nature arise.
There, first, for the purification of breast milk, the wet nurse should be prepared with oleation,
properly fomented, and then the physician should prepare her by emesis.
With pastes of <s>vacā</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, the herb called <s>yaṣṭī</s>, <s>phala</s>, <s>vatsaka</s>, and mustard,
and with salted decoctions of neem and <s>paṭola</s>, she should be made to vomit.
After she has vomited properly and has undergone the prescribed post-emesis diet,
then, considering the doṣa, season, and strength, one should oleate her and administer purgation.
One should give <s>trivṛt</s> or <s>abhayā</s> combined with the juice of <s>triphalā</s>,
mixed with honey; or one may give <s>abhayā</s> alone.
Or, for the purpose of purgation, the knower of the treatise should give it mixed with urine.
When she has been properly purged, the intelligent physician should again put her through the post-purgation diet,
and then treat her with foods and drinks that destroy the remaining doṣas.

children.text: śālayaḥ ṣaṣṭikā vā syuḥ śyāmākā bhojane hitāḥ
children.translated_text: Rice grains, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, and <s>śyāmāka</s> millet are beneficial as food,
as are <s>priyaṅgu</s> grain, <s>koradūṣa</s>, barley, and bamboo barley.
Bamboo, cane, and peas, prepared with fat, should be used as vegetables.
One should prepare green gram, lentils, and horse gram for soups.
Soups boiled with neem, cane-shoots, <s>kulaka</s>, <s>vārtāka</s>, and <s>āmalaka</s>,
mixed with <s>vyosha</s> and rock salt, should be given as purifiers of breast milk.
One should also give properly prepared hare, <s>kapiñjala</s> partridge, and antelope meat.
For purification of milk one should give water boiled with <s>śārṅgeṣṭā</s>, <s>saptaparṇa</s> bark, and <s>aśvagandhā</s>,
or else water boiled with <s>rohiṇī</s> for the purification of breast milk.
One may also give a decoction of <s>amṛtā</s> and <s>saptaparṇa</s> bark with dry ginger,
or a decoction of <s>kirātatiktaka</s>; one should drink these three decoctions stated in quarter-verses
for the purification of breast milk. This is the general treatment
declared for disorders of breast milk; now hear the separate treatment for each.
For a woman whose milk is tasteless, one should give raisins, licorice, and <s>sārivā</s>,
and <s>payasyā</s>, finely ground and mixed in pleasant water, to drink.
With <s>pañcakola</s> and horse gram, ground into a paste, one should plaster the breasts.
When dry, one should wash them and milk them out; in this way the breast milk is purified.
A woman whose milk is like a mass of foam should be made to drink
<s>pāṭhā</s>, dry ginger, <s>śārṅgeṣṭā</s>, and <s>mūrvā</s>, ground with pleasant water.
Collyrium, dry ginger, deodar, bilva root, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>
should be applied to the breasts as before, as a milk-purifying plaster.
The physician should boil <s>kirātatiktaka</s> and dry ginger together with <s>amṛtā</s>,
and should give that decoction to the wet nurse to drink, as a remover of breast-milk disorder.
He should also plaster the breasts with ground barley, wheat, and mustard.
Using the breast-milk-purifying medicines taught in the chapter on the six purgative groups,

children.text: *rūkṣakṣīrā pibet kṣīraṃ tairvā siddhaṃ ghṛtaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: a woman with dry milk should drink milk, or drink ghee prepared with those medicines.
As before, the <s>jīvaka</s> group and the five roots
should be made into a pleasantly warm milk-purifying plaster for the breasts.
Licorice, raisins, <s>payasyā</s>, and <s>sindhuvārikā</s>
should be drunk as a paste with cold water; it removes discoloration of milk.
Her breasts should also be plastered with a paste of raisins and licorice,
then washed with water and milked out again and again.
One should drink <s>viṣāṇikā</s>, <s>ajaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, turmeric, and <s>vacā</s>,
ground with cold water, as a remover of foul smell in milk.
Or the wet nurse, while eating wholesome food, may lick powder of <s>abhayā</s>,
mixed with <s>vyosha</s> and soaked in honey, for the removal of foul smell in milk.
With <s>sārivā</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, madder, <s>śleṣmātaka</s>, and small sandalwood,
and with leaf-water, sandalwood, and <s>uśīra</s>, her breasts should be plastered.
A woman with unctuous milk, after grinding deodar, <s>musta</s>, and <s>pāṭhā</s> with pleasant water,
and drinking them with rock salt, quickly obtains purification of milk.
A woman with slimy milk should be given <s>śārṅgeṣṭā</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, and <s>vacā</s> to drink.
<s>Musta</s>, dry ginger, and <s>pāṭhā</s>, when drunk, are purifiers of breast milk.
She may also drink the buttermilk ferment that was prescribed as removing hemorrhoids.
Her breasts should also be plastered with <s>vidārī</s>, bilva, and licorice.
A woman with heavy milk should quickly drink a decoction boiled with <s>trāyamāṇā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, neem, <s>paṭola</s>, and <s>triphalā</s>,
for the purification of breast-milk disorder.
Or she should drink <s>pippalī</s> root, <s>cavya</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and dry ginger,
and plaster the breasts with <s>balā</s>, dry ginger, <s>śārṅgeṣṭā</s>, and <s>mūrvā</s>.
One should smear her breasts with <s>pṛśniparṇī</s> and <s>payasyā</s>.
These eight defects of milk, with their causes, signs, and remedies,
have been specified; and certain diseases arising from milk defects have likewise been described.
The <s>doṣa</s>s, the affected tissues, the wastes, and whatever major diseases there are,

children.text: ta eva *sarve bālānāṃ mātrā tvalpatarā matā
children.translated_text: all these also occur in children, but the dose is considered to be much smaller.
Considering the avoidance of emesis and the other procedures, their mildness, and their dependence on others,
and the incapacity of children in speech and activity, one versed in the śāstra
should administer medicine in a small dose, according to the disease.
Sweet, astringent, milk-containing, and mild medicines
a wise physician should administer to a child, with proper measure and without carelessness.
Medicine, drink, and food that are excessively unctuous, dry, hot, sour, pungent in postdigestive effect,
and heavy are condemned for children.
In summary, this treatment for all diseases in children
has been taught; a physician versed in the śāstra should apply it after careful discrimination.
And here there are verses:
Thus this treatment of all disorders has been stated.
For this section of the treatise is the supreme and highest secret.

children.text: asmin saptadaśādhyāyāḥ kalpāḥ siddhaya eva ca
children.translated_text: In this treatise, the seventeen chapters, the <s>Kalpa</s>s and the <s>Siddhi</s>s,
are not found in the tantra of <s>Agniveśa</s> as redacted by <s>Caraka</s>.
<s>Dṛḍhabala</s>, descendant of <s>Kapilabala</s>, made these remaining chapters
for the sake of completing this treatise of great meaning, just as it was.
Even those diseases not mentioned here by name and form, because of their multitude,
should have this very treatment too, after one has examined the <s>doṣa</s>s and the rest.
What is opposite to the <s>doṣa</s>, the affected tissue, and the cause is certainly beneficial.
Properly applied, it restrains all diseases, both stated and unstated.
For place, time, measure, and also what is suitable and unsuitable,
there must be proper application; otherwise even what is wholesome may become otherwise.
Medicine given through the mouth quickly destroys diseases situated in the stomach, and through the nose those situated in the head;
given through the anus, it quickly destroys those situated in the large intestine.
In eruptions arising in parts of the body, such as <s>visarpa</s> and <s>piḍakā</s>,
local applications and the like, according to the site, are especially pacifying.
Observation of the day, the patient, the medicine, the disease, the signs of digestion, and the season
should be known as timing; regard for the day is, for example, emesis in the forenoon.
Regard for the patient is as follows: a strong person, fasting in the morning, should drink
the medicine, while a weak person should take it with light and wholesome food.
The times for medicine are at the beginning of a meal, in the middle, afterward, repeatedly,
in the <s>sāmudga</s> manner, mixed with food, and between morsels; these are ten.
When <s>apāna</s> is disordered, it is given before the meal; when <s>samāna</s> is disordered, in the middle of the meal.
For <s>vyāna</s>, it is given after the morning meal, and for <s>udāna</s>, after the meal.
When <s>prāṇa-vāyu</s> is disturbed, it is to be used between morsels.
But in dyspnea, cough, and thirst, it should be administered again and again.
For hiccup it should be given in the <s>sāmudga</s> manner, combined with light food.
In loss of appetite, medicine eaten together with various foods is beneficial.
In fever, drinks, decoctions, milk, ghee, and purgation

children.text: ṣaḍahe ṣāḍahe deyaṃ kālaṃ vīkṣyāmayasya ca ||
children.translated_text: should be given on the sixth day or at six-day intervals, after considering the time and the disease.
The release of the urge of hunger, lightness, and purification are signs of digestion.
Then medicine should be taken; otherwise it would act like a <s>doṣa</s>.

children.text: cayādayaśca doṣāṇāṃ varjyaṃ sevyaṃ ca yatra yat
children.translated_text: The accumulation and other states of the <s>doṣa</s>s, what is to be avoided and what is to be used,
and whatever procedure is to be considered in each season have all been stated before.
The performance of therapeutic measures and the reason for their prohibition
have been explained with attention to weak patients and to the available alternatives.
By repeatedly observing the condition of diseases and of the patient,
the physician does not become confused in treatment.
Thus, if applied by a physician without regard for the sixfold time,
treatment would be harmful, like untimely rain for a crop.
The distinction that varies according to diseases, seasons, day and night, ages, and food

children.text: viśeṣo bhidyate yastu kālāvekṣaḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: is called regard for time.

children.text: vasante śleṣmajā rogāḥ śaratkāle tu pittajāḥ
children.translated_text: In spring, diseases born of <s>śleṣman</s> generally arise; in autumn, those born of <s>pitta</s>;
and in the rainy season, those of <s>vāta</s> generally arise.

children.text: niśānte divasānte ca varṣānte vātajā gadāḥ
children.translated_text: At the end of night, at the end of day, and at the end of the rains, there are <s>vāta</s>-born diseases.
In the morning and at the beginning of night there are <s>kapha</s>-born diseases, and between those times, <s>pitta</s>-born diseases.
In the last, middle, and first periods of life, diseases of <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>
respectively become strong by the natural course of human age.

children.text: jīrṇānte vātajā rogā jīryamāṇe tu pittajāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vāta</s>-born diseases gain strength at the end of digestion, and <s>pitta</s>-born diseases while food is being digested.

children.text: śleṣmajā bhuktamātre tu labhante prāyaśo balam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣman</s>-born diseases generally gain strength immediately after eating.
Too little medicine does not destroy a disease, just as a little water does not put out a great fire.
And an excessive dose becomes faulty, just as too much water is for a crop.
Therefore, having considered the strength of the disease and of the medicine,
one should administer treatment neither in too great nor in too small an amount.

children.text: aucityādyasya yat sātmyaṃ deśasya puruṣasya ca
children.translated_text: That which, through suitability, is <s>sātmya</s> for a particular region and person,
even if generally unwholesome, does not bring comfort when it is wholly abandoned.
The <s>Vāhlīka</s>s, <s>Pahlava</s>s, <s>Cīna</s>s, <s>Śūlīka</s>s, <s>Yavana</s>s, and <s>Śaka</s>s
are accustomed to meat, wheat, <s>mādhvīka</s> wine, weapons, and fire.
The eastern peoples are similarly accustomed to fish, and the <s>Saindhava</s>s to milk.
Oil and sour substances are said to be suitable for the <s>Aśmaka</s>s and <s>Avantika</s>s.
One should know bulbs, roots, and fruits to be suitable for the inhabitants of <s>Malaya</s>.
In the south, thin gruel is suitable, and in the northwest, <s>mantha</s>.
In the middle country, barley, wheat, and products of cow's milk are suitable.
For them one should prescribe medicines that are joined with what is suitable to their habituation.

children.text: sātmyaṃ hyāśu balaṃ dhatte nātidoṣaṃ ca bahvapi
children.translated_text: For <s>sātmya</s> (habitual suitability) quickly confers strength, and even in large amount it does not cause excessive disorder.
A physician who treats by formulae alone, not knowing place and the other factors, commits an error.
For many distinctions are recognized, such as age, strength, and body.
So too there are distinctions in the <s>doṣa</s>s that move hidden within the inner joints and pathways.
Sometimes even a procedure thought to be contrary may have to be done.
Hidden <s>pitta</s> lodged inside is brought outward by hot sudation, pouring, and poultices.
For by hot measures heat is led outward, and those same hot measures pacify heat.
And by external cold applications, such as pouring, heat, being pressed, goes inward.

children.text: so 'ntargūḍhaṃ kaphaṃ hanti śītaṃ śītaistathā jayet
children.translated_text: It destroys <s>kapha</s> hidden inside; likewise cold should be overcome by cold measures.
Even a smooth, thick paste of sandalwood can produce burning.
That is because it blocks heat located in the skin; otherwise, when not heavy, it produces coolness.
Fly excrement stops vomiting, but a fly itself may cause vomiting.
In substances that are cooked and eaten, transformation occurs even in those very same substances.
Therefore, after truly examining the ten factors, including <s>doṣa</s> and medicine,
the wise physician should undertake treatment, not merely by formulae alone.
Even when a disease has ceased, it returns from a slight cause

children.text: kṣīṇe mārgīkṛte dehe śeṣaḥ sūkṣma ivānalaḥ
children.translated_text: if a remnant remains, like a subtle fire, in a body that is depleted and whose channels have been opened.
Therefore one should follow it up with a course of treatment that does not lapse,
for the sake of securing the success of a medicine already applied, even when that medicine has succeeded.
Because of hardness or insufficiency, a great <s>doṣa</s> aggravated within
may, when brought by wholesome regimen to softness and smallness, become mild in producing disease.
Therefore, when disease arises even in someone eating wholesome food,
knowing this, one should cause its increase or its habituation accordingly.
When wholesome food has become disliked because it is constant or because of its naturally pleasant taste,
one should make it pleasing again by those various methods of preparation.
For from objects favorable to the mind arise satisfaction, nourishment, appetite, strength,
and pleasant enjoyment; from that there is a loss of the disease's strength.
As for the appetite that arises from craving, from depletion of the <s>doṣa</s>s, or from opposition to the disease,
among such cases there should be wholesome management; in the first case one should vary it by a formulation.
Here are the summary verses.
The twenty disorders of the <s>yoni</s> (female reproductive tract), their cause, and their sign,
and also their treatment have been taught out of desire for the pupils' welfare.
Likewise the eight disorders of semen have been taught with their causes, forms, and medicines,
as well as the four kinds of <s>klaibya</s> (impotence) and the four kinds of <s>pradara</s> (abnormal discharge).

children.text: teṣāṃ nidānaṃ liṅgaṃ ca bhaiṣajyaṃ caiva kīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: Their cause, sign, and medicine have been stated.
Likewise the eight defects of breast milk have been described by cause, sign, and physician's treatment.
The mark of purity of semen and of menstrual blood has also been stated.
Treatment of what has been stated and what has not been stated, and proper compounding,

children.text: deśādiguṇaśaṃsā ca kālaḥ ṣaḍvidha eva ca ||
children.translated_text: the praise of qualities beginning with place, and the sixfold time,

children.text: deśe deśe ca yat sātmyaṃ yathā vaidyo 'parādhyati
children.translated_text: what is suitable in each region, and how a physician commits error,
and treatment for <s>doṣa</s>s that move hidden have also been taught.

children.text: yo hi samyaṅna jānāti śāstraṃ śāstrārthameva ca
children.translated_text: One who does not properly know the treatise and the meaning of the treatise

children.text: na kuryāt sa kriyāṃ citramacakṣuriva citrakṛt ||
children.translated_text: should not perform a complex procedure, like a painter without eyes making a picture.

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte 'prāpte dṛḍhabalasaṃpūrite cikitsāsthāne yonivyāpaccikitsitaṃ nāma triṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s>, revised by <s>Caraka</s>, and supplemented in the incomplete portions by <s>Dṛḍhabala</s>, in the Cikitsāsthāna, the thirtieth chapter, called Treatment of Disorders of the <s>Yoni</s>, is complete.
Now then, we shall explain the Madana Kalpa.
Thus spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: atha khalu vamanavirecanārthaṃ vamanavirecanadravyāṇāṃ sukhopabhogatamaiḥ sahānyairdravyairvividhaiḥ kalpanārthaṃ bhedārthaṃ vibhāgārthaṃ cetyarthaḥ tadyogānāṃ ca kriyāvidheḥ sukhopāyasya samyagupakalpanārthaṃ kalpasthānam upadekṣyāmo'gniveśa ||
children.translated_text: Now, for the purpose of emesis and purgation, in order to prepare, distinguish, and classify the emetic and purgative drugs together with various other substances that make them easiest to consume, and in order to properly devise the easy method of action for those combinations, we shall teach the Kalpasthāna, O <s>Agniveśa</s>.

children.text: tatra doṣaharaṇamūrdhvabhāgaṃ vamanasaṃjñakam adhobhāgaṃ virecanasaṃjñakam ubhayaṃ vā śarīramalavirecanād virecanasaṃjñāṃ labhate ||
children.translated_text: There, removal of <s>doṣa</s>s by the upward route is called <s>vamana</s> (emesis), and by the downward route is called <s>virecana</s> (purgation); or both receive the name <s>virecana</s> because they evacuate the bodily wastes.

children.text: tatroṣṇatīkṣṇasūkṣmavyavāyivikāśīnyauṣadhāni svavīryeṇa hṛdayamupetya dhamanīranusṛtya sthūlāṇusrotobhyaḥ kevalaṃ śarīragataṃ doṣasaṃghātamāgneyatvād viṣyandayanti taikṣṇayādvicchindanti sa vicchinnaḥ pariplavan snehabhāvite kāye snehāktabhājanasthamiva kṣaudram asajjannaṇupravaṇabhāvād āmāśayam āgamyodānapraṇunno 'gnivāyvātmakatvād ūrdhvabhāgaprabhāvād auṣadhasyordhvam utkṣipyate salilapṛthivyātmakatvād adhobhāgaprabhāvāccauṣadhasyādhaḥ pravartate ubhayataścobhayaguṇatvāt
children.translated_text: There, medicines that are hot, sharp, subtle, penetrating, and diffusive reach the heart by their own potency, follow the vessels, and, from the gross and subtle channels, liquefy the mass of <s>doṣa</s>s located in the body because of their fiery nature and cut it apart because of their sharpness. Once cut apart, that mass floats in a body prepared with oil, like honey in an oil-smeared vessel, without sticking; because of its tendency toward minuteness it comes to the stomach, and, impelled by <s>udāna</s>, it is thrown upward because of the medicine's fiery and airy nature and upward effect. Because of the medicine's watery and earthy nature and downward effect it proceeds downward; it moves both ways when it has both sets of qualities.
This is the statement of the definitions.

children.text: tatra phalajīmūtakekṣvākudhāmārgavakuṭajakṛtavedhanānāṃ śyāmātrivṛccaturaṅgulatilvakamahāvṛkṣasaptalāśaṅkhinīdantīdravantīnāṃ ca nānāvidhadeśakālasaṃbhavāsvādarasavīryavipākaprabhāvagrahaṇād dehadoṣaprakṛtivayobalāgnibhaktisātmyarogāvasthādīnāṃ nānāprabhāvavattvācca vicitragandhavarṇarasasparśānām upayogasukhārtham asaṃkhyeyasaṃyogānāmapi ca satāṃ dravyāṇāṃ vikalpamārgopadarśanārthaṃ ṣaḍvirecanayogaśatāni vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, because <s>phala</s>, <s>jīmūtaka</s>, <s>ikṣvāku</s>, <s>dhāmārgava</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s>, and <s>kṛtavedhana</s>, and also <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>caturaṅgula</s>, <s>tilvaka</s>, <s>mahāvṛkṣa</s>, <s>saptalā</s>, <s>śaṅkhinī</s>, <s>dantī</s>, and <s>dravantī</s>, must be understood according to their various places and times of origin, tastes, potencies, post-digestive effects, and specific powers, and because body, <s>doṣa</s>, constitution, age, strength, digestion, liking for food, habituation, disease stage, and the rest have varied effects, we shall explain six hundred evacuative formulations. These are for the ease of using substances of varied smell, color, taste, and touch, and also for showing alternative methods among countless combinations of drugs.

children.text: tāni tu dravyāṇi deśakālaguṇabhājanasaṃpadvīryabalādhānāt kriyāsamarthatamāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: But those substances become most capable of action through the excellence of place, season, qualities, vessel, potency, and strength.

children.text: trividhaḥ khalu deśaḥ jāṅgalaḥ ānūpāḥ sādhāraṇaśceti
children.translated_text: There are indeed three kinds of region: <s>jāṅgala</s> (dry upland), <s>ānūpa</s> (marshy), and <s>sādhāraṇa</s> (ordinary or intermediate).

children.text: tatra jāṅgalaḥ paryākāśabhūthiṣṭhaḥ tarubhirapi ca kadarakhadirāsanāśvakarṇadhavatiniśaśallakīsālasomavalkabadarītindukāśvatthavaṭāmalakīvanagahanaḥ anekaśamīkakubhaśiṃśapāprāyaḥ sthiraśuṣkapavanabalavidhūyamānapranṛtyattaruṇavitpaḥ pratatamṛ gatṛṣṇikopagūḍhatanukharaparuṣasikatāśarkarābahulaḥ lāvatittiricakorānucaritabhūmibhāgaḥ vātapittabahulaḥ sthirakaṭhinamanuṣyaprāyo jñeyaḥ athānūpo hintālatamālanārikelakadalīvanagahanaḥ saritsamudraparyantaprāyaḥ śiśirapavanabahulaḥ vañjulavānīropaśobhitatīrābhiḥ saridbhir upagatabhūmibhāgaḥ kṣitidharanikuñjopaśobhitaḥ mandapavanānuvījitakṣitiruhagahanaḥ anekavanarājīpuṣpitavanagahanabhūmibhāgaḥ snigdhatarupratānopagūḍhaḥ haṃsacakravākabalākanandīmukhapuṇḍarīkakādambamadgubhṛṅgarājaśatapatramattakokilānunāditataruviṭapaḥ sukumārapuruṣaḥ pavanakaphaprāyo jñeyaḥ anayoreva dvayor deśayor vīrudvanaspativānaspatyaśakunimṛgagaṇayutaḥ sthirasukumārabalavarṇasaṃhananopapannasādhāraṇaguṇayuktapuruṣaḥ sādhāraṇo jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among these, the <s>jāṅgala</s> region should be known as mostly open to the sky and firm in ground, dense even with trees such as <s>kadara</s>, <s>khadira</s>, <s>āsana</s>, <s>aśvakarṇa</s>, <s>dhava</s>, <s>tiniśa</s>, <s>śallakī</s>, <s>sāla</s>, <s>somavalka</s>, <s>badarī</s>, <s>tinduka</s>, <s>aśvattha</s>, <s>vaṭa</s>, and <s>āmalakī</s>; abounding in many <s>śamī</s>, <s>kakubha</s>, and <s>śiṃśapā</s> trees; having young branches of trees constantly shaken and made to dance by the force of steady dry winds; largely covered with thin, harsh, rough sand and gravel, with extended mirage-like tracts; its ground frequented by quail, partridge, and <s>cakora</s> birds; predominating in wind and bile; and mostly inhabited by firm, hard-bodied people. The <s>ānūpa</s> region, on the other hand, should be known as dense with groves of <s>hintāla</s>, <s>tamāla</s>, coconut, and plantain; generally bounded by rivers and the sea; rich in cool winds; with stretches of land reached by rivers whose banks are adorned with <s>vañjula</s> and cane; adorned with mountain thickets; with dense trees fanned by gentle winds; with areas of ground thick with many rows of blossoming forest trees; covered over by unctuous tree-creepers; with tree branches resounding with swans, <s>cakravāka</s> birds, cranes, <s>nandīmukha</s> birds, <s>puṇḍarīka</s> birds, <s>kādamba</s> birds, divers, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> birds, <s>śatapatra</s> birds, and intoxicated cuckoos; producing delicate people; and predominating in wind and phlegm. The <s>sādhāraṇa</s> region should be known as one that has the qualities common to those two regions, with people endowed with firmness and delicacy, strength, complexion, and compactness, and with groups of creepers, forest trees, fruit trees, birds, and animals belonging to both those regions.

children.text: tatra deśe sādhāraṇe jāṅgale vā yathākālaṃ śiśirātapapavanasalilasevite same śucau pradakṣiṇodake śmaśānacaityadevayajanāgārasabhāśvabhrārāmavalmīkoṣaravirahite kuśarohiṣāstīrṇe snigdhakṛṣṇamadhuramṛttike suvarṇavarṇamadhuramṛttike vā mṛdāvaphālakṛṣṭe 'nupahate 'nyair balavattarair drumair auṣadhāni jātāni praśasyante ||
children.translated_text: In such a region, whether ordinary or <s>jāṅgala</s>, medicinal plants born in a place served in due season by cold, heat, wind, and water, level, clean, with water flowing clockwise, free from cremation grounds, shrines, temples, houses, assembly halls, pits, parks, anthills, and saline soil, covered with <s>kuśa</s> and <s>rohiṣa</s> grass, having unctuous, black, sweet soil or golden-colored, sweet soil, soft, not ploughed by a plough, and not overpowered by other stronger trees, are praised.

children.text: tatra yāni kālajātānyupāgatasaṃpūryapramāṇarasavīryagandhāni kālātapāgnisalilapavanajantubhiranupahatagandhavarṇarasasparśaprabhāvāṇi pratyagrāṇyudīcyāṃ diśi sthitāni teṣāṃ śākhāpalāśamaciraprarūḍhaṃ varṣāvasantayor grāhyaṃ grīṣme mūlāni śiśire vā śīrṇaprarūḍhaparṇānāṃ śaradi tvakkandakṣīrāṇi hemante sārāṇi yathartu puṣpaphalamiti maṅgalācāraḥ kalyāṇavṛttaḥ śuciḥ śuklavāsāḥ saṃpūjya devatā aśvinau gobrāhmaṇāṃśca kṛtopavāsaḥ prāṅmukha udaṅmukho vā gṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: Among them, those that are born in the proper season, have attained fullness of measure, taste, potency, and smell, whose smell, color, taste, touch, and specific power have not been damaged by season, sun, fire, water, wind, or creatures, that are fresh and situated in the northern direction, should be taken as follows: recently sprouted branches and leaves in the rainy season and spring; roots in summer or winter from plants whose old leaves have fallen and new ones have sprouted; bark, bulbs, and latex in autumn; heartwood in winter; flowers and fruits according to their season. A person of auspicious conduct, good behavior, purity, and white clothing, having worshipped the deities, the <s>Aśvins</s>, cows, and brahmins, and having fasted, should gather them while facing east or north.

children.text: gṛhītvā cānurūpaguṇavadbhājanasthānyāgāreṣu prāgudagdvāreṣu nivātapravātaikadeśeṣu nityapuṣpopahārabalikarmavatsu agnisalilopasvedadhūmarajomūṣakacatuṣpadāmanabhigamanīyāni svavacchannāni śikyeṣvāsajya sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: And after gathering them, he should place them in storehouses suited to vessels of corresponding quality, with doors facing east and north, in places partly free from wind and partly ventilated, where daily offerings of flowers, oblations, and bali offerings are made; inaccessible to fire, water, moisture, smoke, dust, mice, and quadrupeds; well covered; and hung on slings.

children.text: tāni ca yathādoṣaṃ prayuñjati surāsauvīrakatuṣodakamaireyamedakadhānyāmlaphalāmladadhyamlādibhir vāte mṛdvīkāmalakamadhumadhukaparūṣakaphāṇitakṣīrādibhiḥ pitte śleṣmaṇi tu madhumūtrakaṣāyādibhirbhāvitānyāloḍitāni ca ityuddeśaḥ
children.translated_text: And he applies them according to the doṣa: in disorders of wind, after they have been infused and stirred with liquor, <s>sauvīraka</s>, sour gruel-water, <s>maireya</s>, <s>medaka</s>, grain-sour, fruit-sour, sour curd, and the like; in bile, with raisins, <s>āmalaka</s>, honey, licorice, <s>parūṣaka</s>, molasses, milk, and the like; and in phlegm, with honey, urine, decoctions, and the like. This is the concise statement.
We shall explain that in detail, after distinguishing substances, bodies, doṣas, suitability, and so on.
They say that the fruits of <s>madana</s> are the very best among emetic substances because they are free from danger.

children.text: tāni vasantagrīṣmayorantare puṣyāśvayugbhyāṃ mṛgaśirasā vā gṛhṇīyānmaitre muhūrte
children.translated_text: One should gather them between spring and summer, under the lunar mansions <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Aśvayuj</s>, or <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, at the friendly muhūrta.

children.text: yāni pakvānyakāṇānyaharitāni pāṇḍūnyakrimīṇyapūtīnya athāta uttarabastisiddhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those which are ripe, not hollow, not green, pale, worm-free, and not foul: now, therefore, we shall explain the successful procedure for the upper enema.
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.
Now the physician should carefully protect a patient who has been cleansed by emesis and the other therapies,
who is weak, emaciated, has little digestive fire, and whose joints and bindings are loosened;
whose wind, feces, urine, phlegm, and bile have been drawn out, whose internal receptacle is depleted,
whose body is empty, and who cannot endure countermeasures.

children.text: yathāṇḍaṃ taruṇaṃ pūrṇaṃ tailapātraṃ yathaiva ca
children.translated_text: As one would protect a tender egg, or a vessel full of oil,
and as a staff-bearing cowherd protects cows, so should he protect him from every improper action.
For the sake of kindling the digestive fire, the physician skilled in sequence
should first treat him gradually with thin gruel and the rest, followed by meat soup and similar nourishing foods.
Then he should use unctuous, sour, sweet, and pleasant foods, then the sour and salty tastes,
then again the sweet and bitter, and after that the astringent and pungent.
By using, in alternation, tastes that oppose one another,
and likewise unctuous and dry substances, the physician should bring him back to his natural condition.
One should know that he has returned to his natural condition when he can tolerate everything, is free from contact with incompatible regimen, takes pleasure in food and activity, has steady senses,
is strong, and is endowed with mental firmness.
Until he has attained this natural condition, he should avoid all things that are to be avoided,
and especially these eight that produce great harm:
speaking loudly, jolting in a chariot, excessive walking and sitting still,
eating during indigestion and eating unwholesome food, sleeping by day, and sexual intercourse.
From these there arise, in due order, disorders born from affliction of the upper body, the whole body, the lower body, and the middle body, from faulty intoxication,
as well as disorders born from <s>śleṣman</s> and those born from wasting.
I shall explain in full the signs of each of them and the remedy for each,
and also the successfully prepared <s>bastis</s> and the sustaining <s>yāpana</s> bastis, just as they are.

There, from speaking loudly and speaking excessively, there occur burning in the head, piercing pain in the temples and ears, obstruction of hearing, dryness of the mouth, palate, and throat, dimness of vision, thirst, fever, darkness before the eyes, stiffness of the jaw, rigidity of the neck, spitting, pain in the chest and sides, breaking of the voice, hiccup, dyspnea, and the like.

From jolting in a carriage there occur looseness of the joints and articulations, pain and stabbing in the jaw, nose, ears, and head, agitation of the abdomen, gurgling and rumbling of the intestines, distension, obstruction of the heart and senses, pain in the buttocks, sides, groins, testicles, waist, and back, weakness of the joints, shoulders, and neck, burning throughout the limbs, swelling of the feet, numbness, horripilation, and the like.

From excessive walking there occur pain in the feet, shanks, thighs, knees, groins, hips, and back, debility and stabbing pain in the thighs, cramping of the calves, aching of the limbs, burning in the shoulders, tingling in the veins and arteries, dyspnea, cough, and the like.
From sitting too long there occur the same disorders as those born from jolting in a carriage, such as pain in the buttocks, sides, groins, testicles, waist, and back.

From indigestion and eating again before the previous meal is digested there occur dryness of the mouth, distension, pain, stabbing, thirst, exhaustion of the body, vomiting, diarrhea, fainting, fever, straining, depression from <s>āma</s>, and the like.

From irregular and unsuitable eating there occur lack of desire for food, weakness, discoloration, itching, skin eruptions, bodily languor, and disorders such as those of <s>grahaṇī</s> and hemorrhoids produced by the aggravation of <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣas</s>.

From sleeping by day there occur anorexia, indigestion, loss of digestive fire, wet heaviness, pallor, itching, skin eruptions, burning, vomiting, aching of the limbs, stiffness of the heart, dullness, drowsiness, excessive sleep, formation of swellings, weakness, and reddishness or coating of the urine, eyes, skin, and palate.

children.text: vyavāyādāśubalanāśorusādaśirobastigudameḍhravaṃkṣaṇorujānujaṅghāpādaśūlahṛdayaspandananetrapīḍāṅgaśaithilyaśukramārgaśoṇitāgamana kāsaśvāsaśoṇitaṣṭhīvanasvarāvasādakaṭīkaurbalyaikāṅgasarvāṅgarogamuṣkaśvayathuvātavarcomūtrasaṅgaśukravisargajāḍyavepathubādhiryaviṣādādayaḥ syuḥ avalupyata iva gudaḥ tāḍyata iva meḍhram avasīdatīva mano vepate hṛdayaṃ pīḍyante sandhayaḥ tamaḥ praveśyata iva ca
children.translated_text: From sexual intercourse there occur rapid loss of strength, weakness of the thighs, pain in the head, bladder, anus, penis, groins, thighs, knees, shanks, and feet, palpitation of the heart, eye pain, looseness of the limbs, flow of blood through the semen-channel, cough, dyspnea, spitting of blood, weakness of the voice, weakness of the waist, disease in one limb or all limbs, swelling of the scrotum, obstruction of flatus, feces, and urine, discharge of semen, dullness, trembling, deafness, despondency, and the like. It is as if the anus is being torn away, as if the penis is being beaten, as if the mind is sinking; the heart trembles, the joints are afflicted, and it is as if one is being entered by darkness.
Thus these complications arise from these eight forms of improper conduct.

Their successful treatment is as follows. For those born from loud speaking and excessive speaking, all procedures that remove <s>vāta</s> are to be used: oil massage, fomentation, poultices, smoking, nasal therapy, drinking unctuous substances after meals, meat soup, milk, and the like, and also silence.

children.text: rathakṣobhāticaṅkramaṇātyāsanajānāṃ snehasvedādi vātaharaṃ karma sarvaṃ nidānavarjanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: For those born from carriage-jolting, excessive walking, and sitting too long, all <s>vāta</s>-removing measures such as unction and fomentation are to be used, and the causes are to be avoided.

children.text: ajīrṇādhyaśanajānāṃ niravaśeṣataśchardanaṃ rūkṣaḥ svedo laṅghanīyapācanīyadīpanīyauṣadhāvacāraṇaṃ ca
children.translated_text: For those born from indigestion and overeating before digestion, complete vomiting, dry fomentation, and the administration of medicines that promote fasting, digestion, and kindling of the digestive fire are prescribed.
For those born from irregular and unsuitable eating, therapies removing the respective <s>doṣas</s> are to be used.

For those born from daytime sleep, one should use smoking, fasting, emesis, purgation of the head, exercise, dry foods, <s>ariṣṭa</s> preparations, and digestive medicines; and all <s>śleṣman</s>-removing procedures such as rubbing, kneading, and sprinkling are to be used.

children.text: maithunajānāṃ jīvanīyasiddhayoḥ kṣīrasarpiṣorupayogaḥ tathā vātaharāḥ svedābhyaṅgopanāhā vṛṣyāścāhārāḥ snehāḥ snehavidhayo yāpanābastayo 'nuvāsanaṃ ca mūtravaikṛtabastiśūleṣu cottarabastirvidārīgandhādigaṇajīvanīyakṣīrasaṃsiddhaṃ tailaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: For those born from sexual intercourse, one should use milk and ghee prepared with life-promoting drugs; likewise <s>vāta</s>-removing fomentations, oil massages, and poultices, aphrodisiac foods, fats and oleation procedures, <s>yāpana-bastis</s>, and unctuous enemas. In urinary disorders and pain of the bladder, an <s>uttara-basti</s> should be used, and oil prepared with the <s>vidārīgandhādi</s> group, the life-promoting group, and milk is suitable.

children.text: yāpanāśca bastayaḥ sarvaphālaṃ deyāḥ tānupadekṣyāmaḥmustośīrabalāragvadharāsnāmañjiṣṭhākaṭurohiṇītrāyamāṇāpunarnavābibhītakaguḍūcīsthirādipañcamūlāni palikāni khaṇḍaśaḥ klṛptānyaṣṭau ca madanaphalāni prakṣālya jalāḍhake parikvāthya pādaśeṣo rasaḥ kṣīradviprasthasaṃyuktaḥ punaḥ śṛtaḥ kṣīrāvaśeṣaḥ pādajāṅgalarasastulyamadhughṛtaḥ śatakusumāmadhukakuṭajaphalarasāñjanapriyaṅgukalkīkṛtaḥ sasaindhavaḥ sukhoṣṇo bastiḥ śukramāṃsabalajananaḥ kṣatakṣīṇakāsagulmaśūlaviṣamajvarabradhnaauvardhmajhkuṇḍalodāvartakukṣiśūlamūtrakṛcchrāsṛgrajovisarpapravāhikāśirorujājānūrujaṅghābastigrahāśmaryunmādārśaḥpramehādhmānavātaraktapittaśleṣmavyādhiharaḥ sadyo balajanano rasāyanaśceti
children.translated_text: And <s>yāpana</s> bastis, fruitful in all cases, should be given; we shall teach them. One <s>pala</s> each of <s>musta</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>āragvadha</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>, <s>trāyamāṇā</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>bibhītaka</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, and the five roots beginning with <s>sthirā</s>, cut into pieces, and eight <s>madana</s> fruits, are washed and boiled in an <s>āḍhaka</s> of water until one quarter remains. The decoction, combined with two <s>prasthas</s> of milk, is boiled again until only the milk remains; it is mixed with a quarter part of meat soup from animals of dry land, with equal honey and ghee, made into a paste with <s>śatakusumā</s>, licorice, <s>kuṭaja</s> fruit, <s>rasāñjana</s>, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>, and with rock salt. Used pleasantly warm as a <s>basti</s>, it produces semen, flesh, and strength, removes injury, wasting, cough, abdominal tumor, pain, irregular fever, scrotal and inguinal swellings, upward movement of wind, abdominal pain, dysuria, disorders of blood and menstrual flow, erysipelas, dysentery, headache, pain in the knees, thighs, and shanks, gripping of the bladder, stone, insanity, hemorrhoids, <s>prameha</s>, distension, and diseases of <s>vāta</s>, blood, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s>; it immediately produces strength and is a rejuvenative.

children.text: eraṇḍamūlapalāśāt ṣaṭpalaṃ śāliparṇīpṛśniparṇī bṛhatī kaṇṭakārikā rokṣurako rāsnāśvagandhā guḍūcī varṣābhūrāragvadho devadārviti palikāni khaṇḍaśaḥ klṛptāni phalāni cāṣṭau prakṣālya jalāḍhake kṣīrapāde pacet
children.translated_text: Six <s>palas</s> of <s>eraṇḍa</s> root and <s>palāśa</s>, and one <s>pala</s> each of <s>śāliparṇī</s>, <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>kaṇṭakārikā</s>, <s>gokṣuraka</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>āragvadha</s>, and deodar, cut into pieces, together with eight fruits, should be washed and cooked in an <s>āḍhaka</s> of water with one quarter milk.

children.text: pādaśeṣaṃ kaṣāyaṃ pūtaṃ śatakusumākuṣṭhamustapippalīhapuṣābilvavacāvatsakaphalarasāñjanapriyaṅguyavāniprakṣepakalkitaṃ madhughṛtatailasaindhavayuktaṃ sukhoṣṇaṃ nirūhamekaṃ dvau trīn vā dadyāt
children.translated_text: When a quarter remains, the decoction is strained, made into a paste with the added powders of <s>śatakusumā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, <s>hapūṣā</s>, bilva, <s>vacā</s>, <s>vatsaka</s> fruit, <s>rasāñjana</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, and <s>yavānī</s>, combined with honey, ghee, oil, and rock salt, and given pleasantly warm as one, two, or three evacuative <s>nirūha</s> enemas.

It is praised for all, and especially for those who are refined and delicate, those exhausted by intercourse with women, the wasted, the injured, the aged, those long afflicted with piles, and those desiring offspring.
In the same way, it may be prepared with milk cooked with <s>sahacara</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>darbha</s> root, and <s>sārivā</s>.

Likewise, a <s>basti</s> should be given as before with milk decocted with <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>, <s>śatāvarī</s>, and <s>chinnaruhā</s>, and with a paste of <s>madhuka</s>, <s>madana</s>, and <s>pippalī</s>.

children.text: tathā balātibalāvidārīśāliparṇīpṛśniparṇībṛhatīkaṇṭakārikādarbhamūlaparūṣakakāśmaryabilvaphalayavasiddhena payasā madhukamadanakalkitena madhughṛtasaivarcalayuktena kāsajvaragulmaplīhārditastrīmadyakliṣṭānāṃ sadyobalajanano rasāyanaśca
children.translated_text: Likewise, milk cooked with <s>balā</s>, <s>atibalā</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>śāliparṇī</s>, <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>kaṇṭakārikā</s>, <s>darbha</s> root, <s>parūṣaka</s>, <s>kāśmarya</s>, bilva fruit, and barley, mixed with a paste of <s>madhuka</s> and <s>madana</s>, and joined with honey, ghee, and <s>saindhava</s> and <s>sauvarcala</s> salts, immediately generates strength and acts as a <s>rasāyana</s> for those afflicted by cough, fever, abdominal tumor, enlarged spleen, facial paralysis, and by women and wine.

children.text: balātibalārāsnāragvadhamadanabilvaguḍūcīpunarnavairaṇḍāśvagandhāsahacarapalāśadevadārudvipañcamūlāni palikāni yavakolakulatthadviprasṛtaṃ śuṣkamūlakānāṃ ca jaladroṇasiddhaṃ nirūhapramāṇāvaśeṣaṃ kaṣāyaṃ pūtaṃ madhukamadanaśatapuṣpākuṣṭhapippalīvacāvatsakaphalarasāñjanapriyaṅguyavānīkalkīkṛtaṃ guḍaghṛtatailakṣaudrakṣīramāṃsarasāmlakāñjikasaindhavayuktaṃ sukhoṣṇaṃ bastiṃ dadyācchukramūtravarcaḥsaṅge 'nilaje gulmahṛdrogādhmānabradhnapārśvapṛṣṭhakaṭīgrahasaṃjñānāśabalakṣayeṣu ca
children.translated_text: One should give a comfortably warm <s>basti</s> for obstruction of semen, urine, and feces, and for wind-born abdominal tumors, heart disease, distension, scrotal swelling, stiffness of the flanks, back, and waist, loss of consciousness, and loss of strength: a decoction of one-pala portions of <s>balā</s>, <s>atibalā</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>āragvadha</s>, <s>madana</s>, bilva, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, castor, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>sahacara</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, and the two groups of five roots, together with two prasṛtas each of barley, jujube, and horse gram and also dry radishes, cooked in a droṇa of water until the decoction remains in the measure for a decoction-basti, strained, made with pastes of <s>madhuka</s>, <s>madana</s>, <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>vatsaka</s> fruit, <s>rasāñjana</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, and <s>yavānī</s>, and combined with jaggery, ghee, oil, honey, milk, meat broth, sour gruel, and rock salt.

children.text: hapuṣārdhakuḍavo dviguṇārdhakṣuṇṇayavaḥ kṣīrodakasiddhaḥ kṣīraśeṣo madhughṛtatailalavaṇayuktaḥ sarvāṅgavisṛtavātaraktasaktaviṇmūtrastrīkheditahito vātaharo buddhimedhāgnibalajananaśca
children.translated_text: Half a kuḍava of <s>hapuṣā</s>, with twice as much half-crushed barley, cooked in milk and water until only the milk remains, and mixed with honey, ghee, oil, and salt, is beneficial when <s>vāta</s> and blood have spread through the whole body, when feces and urine are stuck, and for one wearied by women; it removes <s>vāta</s> and generates understanding, intelligence, digestive fire, and strength.

children.text: hrasvapañcamūlīkaṣāyaḥ kṣīrodakasiddhaḥ pippalīmadhukamadanakalkīkṛtaḥ saguḍaghṛtatailalavaṇaḥ kṣīṇaviṣamajvarakarśitasya bastiḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>basti</s> for one wasted by irregular fever consists of the decoction of the small five roots, cooked with milk and water, made with pastes of <s>pippalī</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and <s>madana</s>, and containing jaggery, ghee, oil, and salt.

A decoction of eight palas each of <s>balā</s>, <s>atibalā</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, and <s>ātmaguptā</s>, with a handful of half-crushed barley, joined with jaggery, ghee, oil, and salt, is a <s>basti</s> as above and is most wholesome for the aged, the weak, and those whose semen and blood are depleted.

children.text: balāmadhukavidārīdarbhamūlamṛdvīkāyavaiḥ kaṣāyamājena payasā paktvā madhukamadanakalkitaṃ samadhughṛtasaindhavaṃ jvarārtebhyo bastiṃ dadyāt
children.translated_text: After cooking a decoction of <s>balā</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>darbha</s> root, raisins, and barley with goat's milk, one should give to those afflicted by fever a <s>basti</s> made with a paste of <s>madhuka</s> and <s>madana</s> and containing honey, ghee, and rock salt.

children.text: śāliparṇīpṛśniparṇīgokṣurakamūlakāśmaryaparūṣakakharjūraphalamadhūkapuṣpairajākṣīrajalaprasthābhyāṃ siddhaḥ kaṣāyaḥ pippalīmadhukotpalakalkitaḥ saghṛtasaindhavaḥ kṣīṇendriyaviṣamajvarakarśitasya bastiḥ śastaḥ
children.translated_text: A decoction cooked with <s>śāliparṇī</s>, <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>, <s>gokṣuraka</s> root, <s>kāśmarya</s>, <s>parūṣaka</s>, date fruit, and <s>madhūka</s> flowers, in one prastha each of goat's milk and water, made with pastes of <s>pippalī</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and blue lotus, and containing ghee and rock salt, is recommended as a <s>basti</s> for one whose faculties are depleted and who has been wasted by irregular fever.

children.text: sthirādipañcamūlīpañcapalena śāliṣaṣṭikayavagodhūmamāṣapañcaprasṛtena chagaṃ payaḥ śṛtaṃ pādaśeṣaṃ kukkuṭāṇḍarasasamamadhughṛtaśarkarāsaindhavasauvarcalayukto bastirvṛṣyatamo balavarṇajananaśca
children.translated_text: A <s>basti</s> made from goat's milk boiled down to a quarter with five palas of the five roots beginning with <s>sthirā</s> and five prasṛtas of rice, sixty-day rice, barley, wheat, and black gram, and then mixed with an equal amount of chicken-egg fluid, honey, ghee, sugar, rock salt, and <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, is most aphrodisiac and generates strength and complexion.
Thus the twelve sustaining <s>basti</s>s are given.
This same procedure may also be applied in broths of peacock, <s>gonarda</s>, goose, crane, and egg.

children.text: satittiriḥ samayūraḥ sarājahaṃsaḥ pañcamūlīpayaḥsiddhaḥśatapuṣpāmadhukarāsnākuṭajamadanaphalapippalīkalko ghṛtatailaguḍasaindhavayukto bastirbalavarṇaśukrajanano rasāyanaśca
children.translated_text: A <s>basti</s> prepared with partridge, peacock, and royal goose, cooked in milk with the five roots, made with pastes of <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>madana</s> fruit, and <s>pippalī</s>, and combined with ghee, oil, jaggery, and rock salt, generates strength, complexion, and semen and is a <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: dvipañcamūlīkukkuṭarasasiddhaṃ payaḥ pādaśeṣaṃ pippalīmadhukarāsnāmadanakalkaṃ śarkarāmadhughṛtayuktaṃ strīṣvatikāmānāṃ balajanano bastiḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>basti</s> for those excessively desirous of women, generating strength, consists of milk cooked with the two groups of five roots and chicken broth, reduced to a quarter, with pastes of <s>pippalī</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, and <s>madana</s>, and mixed with sugar, honey, and ghee.

children.text: mayūramapittapakṣapādāsyāntraṃ sthirādibhiḥ palikaiḥ sajale payasi paktvā kṣīraśeṣaṃ madanapippalīvidārīśatakusumāmadhukakalkīkṛtaṃ madhughṛtasaindhavayuktaṃ bastiṃ dadyāt strīṣvatiprasaktakṣīṇendriyebhyo balavarṇakaram
children.translated_text: One should cook a peacock, with its bile, feathers, feet, mouth, and entrails removed, in watery milk together with one-pala portions of the roots beginning with <s>sthirā</s>; when only the milk remains, one should make it with pastes of <s>madana</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>śatakusumā</s>, and <s>madhuka</s>, add honey, ghee, and rock salt, and give it as a <s>basti</s> to those whose faculties have been depleted by excessive attachment to women, for producing strength and complexion.

children.text: kalpaścaiṣa viṣkirapratudaprasahāmbucareṣu syāt akṣīro rohitādiṣu ca matsyeṣu
children.translated_text: This same procedure applies among birds of the <s>viṣkira</s>, <s>pratuda</s>, <s>prasaha</s>, and water-going classes, and, without milk, among fish such as <s>rohita</s>.

children.text: godhānakulamārjāramūṣikaśallakamāṃsānāṃ daśapalān bhāgān sapañcamūlān payasi paktvā tatpayaḥpippalīphalakalkasaindhavasauvarcalaśarkarāmadhughṛtatailayukto bastirbalyo rasāyanaḥ kṣīṇakṣatasya sandhānakaro mathitoraskarathagajahayabhagnavātabalāsakaprabhṛtyudāvartavātasaktamūtravarcaśśukrāṇāṃ hitatamaśca
children.translated_text: Parts of ten palas each of the meats of iguana, mongoose, cat, mouse, and porcupine, together with the five roots, should be cooked in milk; that milk, combined with a paste of <s>pippalī</s> fruit, rock salt, <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, sugar, honey, ghee, and oil, is a strengthening <s>basti</s>, a <s>rasāyana</s>, a healer of wasting and injury, and extremely beneficial for men whose chests have been crushed, for those broken by chariots, elephants, or horses, and for disorders such as <s>udāvarta</s>, <s>vāta</s>, and <s>balāsaka</s>, and for obstructed urine, feces, and semen.

Milk cooked with the flesh of any one of tortoise and similar animals, mixed with the fluid of the testicles of bull, elephant, horse, and crocodile, with goose and chicken egg fluid, honey, ghee, sugar, rock salt, and pastes of <s>ikṣuraka</s> and <s>ātmaguptā</s> fruit, is a <s>basti</s> that generates strength even in the aged.

children.text: karkaṭakarasaścaṭakāṇḍarasayuktaḥ samadhughṛtaśarkaro bastiḥ ityete bastayaḥ paramavṛṣyāḥ uccaṭakekṣurakātmaguptāśṛtakṣīrapratibhojanānupānāt strīśatagāminaṃ naraṃ kuryuḥ
children.translated_text: Crab broth joined with sparrow-egg fluid, with honey, ghee, and sugar, is a <s>basti</s>. These <s>basti</s>s are supremely aphrodisiac; by using as post-meal drinks milk boiled with <s>uccaṭa</s>, <s>ikṣuraka</s>, and <s>ātmaguptā</s>, they would make a man able to go to a hundred women.

A <s>basti</s>, slightly salted, is made from milk cooked with the testicles of bull, goat, boar, and ram, with crab and sparrow, and combined with <s>uccaṭa</s>, <s>ikṣuraka</s>, <s>ātmaguptā</s>, honey, ghee, and rock salt.

children.text: daśamūlamayūrahaṃsakukkuṭakvāthāt pañcaprasṛtaṃ tailaghṛtavasāmajjacatuṣprasṛtayuktaṃ śatapuṣpāmustahapuṣākalkīkṛtaḥ salavaṇo bastiḥ pādagulphorujānujaṅghātrikavaṅkṣaṇabastivṛṣaṇānilarogaharaḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>basti</s> made with five <s>prasṛtas</s> from a decoction of <s>daśamūla</s>, peacock, goose, and cock, joined with four <s>prasṛtas</s> of oil, ghee, fat, and marrow, made into a paste with <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, <s>musta</s>, and <s>hapuṣā</s>, and containing salt, removes disorders of wind in the feet, ankles, thighs, knees, shanks, sacral region, groins, bladder, and testicles.
<s>Bastis</s> for deer, ground-scratching birds, marsh animals, and burrow-dwelling animals should be given according to this same procedure.

A <s>basti</s> consisting of two <s>prasṛtas</s> each of honey and ghee, an equal amount of warm water, half a <s>pala</s> of <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, and half an <s>akṣa</s> of rock salt is supremely aphrodisiac and removes dysuria, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: sadyoghṛtatailavasāmajjacatuṣprasthaṃ hapuṣārdhapalaṃ saindhavārdhākṣayukto bastirvṛṣyatamo mūtrakṛcchrapittavyādhiharo rasāyanaḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>basti</s> with four <s>prasthas</s> consisting of fresh ghee, oil, fat, and marrow, half a <s>pala</s> of <s>hapuṣā</s>, and half an <s>akṣa</s> of rock salt is supremely aphrodisiac, removes dysuria and disorders of <s>pitta</s>, and is a <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: madhutailaṃ catuḥprasṛtaṃ śatapuṣpārdhapalaṃ saindhavārdhākṣayukto bastirdīpano bṛṃhaṇo balavarṇakaro nirupadravo vṛṣyatamo rasāyanaḥ krimikuṣṭhodāvartagulmārśobradhnaplīhamehaharaḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>basti</s> of four <s>prasṛtas</s> of honey and oil, half a <s>pala</s> of <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, and half an <s>akṣa</s> of rock salt kindles digestion, nourishes, produces strength and complexion, is free from complications, is supremely aphrodisiac, is a <s>rasāyana</s>, and removes worms, skin disease, upward movement of wind, abdominal tumor, hemorrhoids, inguinal swelling, spleen disease, and <s>meha</s>.

children.text: tadvanmadhughṛtābhyāṃ payastulyo bastiḥ pūrvakalkena balavarṇakaro vṛṣyatamo nirupadravo bastimeḍhrapākaparikartikāmūtrakṛcchrapittavyādhiharo rasāyanaśca
children.translated_text: Similarly, a <s>basti</s> with honey and ghee and an equal amount of milk, prepared with the former paste, produces strength and complexion, is supremely aphrodisiac, is free from complications, removes inflammation of the bladder and penis, cutting pain, dysuria, and disorders of <s>pitta</s>, and is also a <s>rasāyana</s>.

Similarly, a <s>basti</s> with honey and ghee and an equal amount of meat juice, containing <s>musta</s> and <s>akṣa</s>, prepared as before, removes <s>vāta</s>, <s>balāsa</s>, tingling in the feet, abdominal tumor, and contractions of the sacral region, thighs, knees, and legs, and removes pain in the bladder, testicles, penis, sacral region, and back.

A <s>basti</s> of seven <s>prasṛtas</s> consisting of liquor, <s>sauvīraka</s>, horse gram, meat juice, honey, ghee, and oil, made into a paste with <s>musta</s> and <s>śatāhvā</s> and containing salt, removes all diseases of <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: dvipañcamūlatriphalābilvamadanaphalakaṣāyo gomūtrasiddhaḥ kuṭajamadanaphalamustapāṭhākalkitaḥ saindhavayāvaśūkakṣaudratailayukto bastiḥ śleṣmavyādhibastyāṭopavātaśukrasaṅgapāṇḍurogājīrṇavisūcikālasakeṣu deya iti ||
children.translated_text: A <s>basti</s> whose decoction is made from the two sets of five roots, <s>triphalā</s>, bilva, and <s>madana</s> fruit, prepared with cow urine, made into a paste with <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>madana</s> fruit, <s>musta</s>, and <s>pāṭhā</s>, and joined with rock salt, barley awn, honey, and oil, should be given in disorders of <s>śleṣman</s>, rumbling in the bladder, obstruction of wind and semen, anemia, indigestion, choleraic diarrhea, and <s>alasaka</s>.
After this we shall describe the most aphrodisiac unctuous preparations.

children.text: śatāvarīguḍūcīkṣuvidāryāmalakadrākṣākharjūrāṇāṃ yantrapīḍitānāṃ rasaprasthaṃ pṛthagekaikaṃ tadvadghṛtatailagomahiṣyajākṣīrāṇāṃ dvau dvau dadyāt jīvakarṣabhakamedāmahāmedātvakkṣīrīśṛṅgāṭakamadhūlikāmadhukoccaṭāpippalīpuṣkarabījanīlotpalakadambapuṣpapuṇḍarīkakeśarakalkān pṛṣatatarakṣumāṃsakukkuṭacaṭakacakoramattākṣabarhijīvañjīvakuliṅgahaṃsāṇḍarasavasāmajjādaṃśca prasthaṃ dattvā sādhayet
children.translated_text: One should take separately one <s>prastha</s> of the pressed juices of <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, sugarcane, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, grapes, and dates; likewise two <s>prasthas</s> each of ghee, oil, and the milk of cow, buffalo, and goat; add pastes of <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>mahāmedā</s>, <s>tvakkṣīrī</s>, water chestnut, <s>madhūlikā</s>, licorice, <s>uccaṭā</s>, long pepper, lotus seed, blue lotus, kadamba flower, and white lotus filaments; and add one <s>prastha</s> of the juices of the meat, fat, and marrow, and the egg juices, of spotted deer, hyena, cock, sparrow, partridge, <s>mattākṣa</s>, peacock, <s>jīvañjīva</s> bird, <s>kuliṅga</s> bird, and goose; then it should be cooked.

children.text: brahmaghoṣaśaṅkhapaṭahabherīninādaiḥ siddhaṃ sitacchatrakṛtacchāyaṃ gajaskandhamāropayedbhagavantaṃ vṛṣadhvajamabhipūjya taṃ snehaṃ tribhāgamākṣikaṃ maṅgalāśīḥstutidevatārcanairbastiṃ gamayet
children.translated_text: When it has been prepared amid the recitation of Vedic sound and the sounds of conches, drums, and kettledrums, it should be placed on an elephant's shoulder under the shade of a white parasol; after worshipping the blessed <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>, one should administer that unctuous preparation as a <s>basti</s>, with one third honey, accompanied by auspicious blessings, praises, and worship of the deities.

children.text: nṛṇāṃ strīvihāriṇāṃ naṣṭaretasāṃ kṣatakṣīṇaviṣamajvarārtānāṃ vyāpannayonīnāṃ vandhyānāṃ raktagulminīnāṃ mṛtāpatyānāmanārtavānāṃ ca strīṇāṃ kṣīṇamāṃsarudhirāṇāṃ pathyatamaṃ rasāyanamuttamaṃ valīpalitanāśanaṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: It should be known as most wholesome for men who consort with women, for those whose semen has been lost, and for those afflicted by injury, wasting, and irregular fever; and for women with disordered wombs, barren women, women with blood tumors, women whose children have died, women without menstruation, and women whose flesh and blood are depleted. It is an excellent <s>rasāyana</s> and destroys wrinkles and gray hair.
