children.text: balāgokṣurakarāsnāśvagandhāśatāvarīsahacarāṇāṃ śataṃ śatamāpothya jaladroṇaśate prasādhyaṃ tasmin jaladroṇāvaśeṣe rase vastrapūte vidāryāmalakasvarasayorbastamahiṣavarāhavṛṣakukkuṭabarhihaṃsakāraṇḍavasārasāṇḍarasānāṃ ghṛtatailayoścaikaikaṃ prasthamaṣṭau prasthān kṣīrasya dattvā candanamadhukamadhūlikātvakkṣīrībisamṛṇālanīlotpalapaṭolātmaguptānnapākitālamastakakharjūramṛdvīkātāmalakīkaṇṭakārījīvakarṣabhakakṣudrasahāmahāsahāśatāvarīmedāpippalīhrīberatvakpannakalkāṃśca dattvā sādhayet
children.translated_text: One should crush one hundred each of <s>balā</s>, <s>gokṣuraka</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>śatāvarī</s>, and <s>sahacara</s>, cook them in one hundred <s>droṇas</s> of water, and, when one <s>droṇa</s> of water remains, strain that juice through cloth. Into it one should put one <s>prastha</s> each of the fresh juices of <s>vidārī</s> and <s>āmalaka</s>, of the meat juices and egg juices of goat, buffalo, boar, bull, cock, peacock, goose, and <s>kāraṇḍava</s>, and of ghee and oil, together with eight <s>prasthas</s> of milk; then add pastes of sandalwood, licorice, <s>madhūlikā</s>, <s>tvakkṣīrī</s>, lotus fiber, lotus stalk, blue lotus, <s>paṭola</s>, <s>ātmaguptā</s>, <s>annapākī</s>, palmyra pith, dates, raisins, <s>tāmalakī</s>, <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>, <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>kṣudrasahā</s>, <s>mahāsahā</s>, <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>medā</s>, long pepper, <s>hrībera</s>, and bark, and cook it.
One should administer the prepared <s>basti</s> according to the procedure beginning with Vedic recitation.

children.text: tena strīśataṃ gacchet na cātrāste vihārāhārayantraṇā kācit
children.translated_text: By means of it he may go to a hundred women, and there is no restriction at all here on regimen or diet.

children.text: eṣa vṛṣyo balyo vṛṃhaṇa āyuṣyo balīpalitanut kṣatakṣīṇanaṣṭaśukraviṣamajvarārtānāṃ vyāpannayonīnāṃ ca pathyatamaḥ
children.translated_text: This is aphrodisiac, strength-giving, nourishing, life-promoting, removing wrinkles and gray hair, and most wholesome for those afflicted by injury, wasting, loss of semen, irregular fever, and disordered wombs.

children.text: sahacarapalaśatamudakadroṇacatuṣṭaye paktvā droṇaśeṣe rase supūte vidārīkṣurasaprasthābhyāmaṣṭaguṇakṣīraṃ ghṛtatailaprasthaṃ balāmadhukamadhūkacandanamadhūlikāsārivāmedāmahāmedākākolīkṣīrakākolīpayasyāgurumañjiṣṭhāvyāghranakhaśaṭīsahacarasahasravīryāvarāṅgalodhrāṇāmakṣamātrairdviguṇaśarkaraiḥ kalkaiḥ sādhayet
children.translated_text: One should cook one hundred <s>palas</s> of <s>sahacara</s> in four <s>droṇas</s> of water until one <s>droṇa</s> remains; in the well-strained juice, with one <s>prastha</s> each of <s>vidārī</s> juice and sugarcane juice, eight times as much milk, one <s>prastha</s> each of ghee and oil, and pastes, in one-<s>akṣa</s> measures, of <s>balā</s>, licorice, <s>madhūka</s>, sandalwood, <s>madhūlikā</s>, <s>sārivā</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>mahāmedā</s>, <s>kākolī</s>, <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>, <s>payasyā</s>, aloe-wood, madder, <s>vyāghranakha</s>, <s>śaṭī</s>, <s>sahacara</s>, <s>sahasravīryā</s>, <s>varāṅga</s>, and <s>lodhra</s>, together with twice as much sugar, it should be cooked.
One should administer the prepared <s>basti</s> according to the procedure beginning with Vedic recitation.

This <s>rasāyana</s> removes all diseases and is best for the delicate and for women dwelling in the inner apartments; with one third honey, it removes pain from injury, wasting, <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, dyspnea, and cough, removes wrinkles and gray hair, and increases complexion, beauty, strength, flesh, and semen.

children.text: ityete rasāyanāḥ snehabastayaḥ sati vibhave śatapākāḥ sahasrapākā vā kāryā vīryabalādhānārthamiti ||
children.translated_text: Thus these <s>rasāyana</s> unctuous <s>bastis</s>, when there is sufficient wealth, should be made with a hundred cookings or with a thousand cookings, for the sake of imparting potency and strength.
And here there are verses:
Thus these <s>bastis</s> and unctuous preparations have been taught under the name <s>yāpana</s>.
They are not incompatible for the healthy, for the sick, or for the aged.
For those habitually given to excessive sexual intercourse, they bestow semen, flesh, and strength.
They pacify all diseases and are suitable in all seasons.
They bestow offspring on women who have not borne children and also on men without progeny.
They are seen to accomplish both purposes, as unctuous <s>bastis</s> and as <s>nirūhas</s>.

children.text: vyāyāmo maithunaṃ madyaṃ madhūni śiśirāmbu ca
children.translated_text: Exercise, sexual intercourse, liquor, honey-drinks, cold water,
eating together with incompatible foods, and jolting in a chariot are condemned during these <s>bastis</s>.
On this there are verses:
Three <s>bastis</s> are prepared with eggs of peacock, wild cow, and swan, in the manner of the cock.
Twenty are prepared with pecking birds, thirty with striking birds, and nine with beasts of prey.
Likewise there are twenty and twenty-seven with water-moving creatures,
and nine with fish and the rest; these are the <s>bastis</s> according to the peacock model.
Ten <s>bastis</s> are prepared with crabs and the rest, according to the tortoise-paste model.
Seventeen with deer, nineteen with pecking birds, and ten
with marshland animals, in the manner of the cock and peacock, and fourteen with earth-dwelling animals:
these are twenty-nine in all, together with the unctuous preparations, in summary.

children.text: proktā vistaraśo bhinnā dve śate ṣoḍaśottare
children.translated_text: Explained in detail with their distinctions, they are two hundred and sixteen.
These, when combined with honey, make a man exceedingly virile.

children.text: nātiyogaṃ na vāyogaṃ stambhitāste ca kurvate
children.translated_text: They produce neither over-application nor under-application; when retained,
because of their mildness, they do not return in the person to whom they have been administered.
Such a person should at once be given an evacuative <s>āsthāpana</s> with sharp <s>bastis</s> containing urine.
Swelling, loss of digestive fire, pallor, pain, hemorrhoids, fissuring pain,
fever, and diarrhea arise from excessive use of <s>yāpana</s>.
In that case, stimulating treatment with <s>ariṣṭa</s>, milk, <s>sīdhu</s>, and the like is desired.
Therefore one should use <s>yāpana</s> according to proper judgment, not from attachment or overuse.
Thus the complications, together with their treatment, of the therapies beginning with loud speaking
have been explained separately and in detail; one should always protect a person from them.
The section in which the means of accomplishing success are stated for the dangers caused by improper performance
of procedures such as emesis is called the Siddhisthāna.
Thus the hundred and twenty chapters, spoken by the sage <s>Ātreya</s>,
were taught by the wise <s>Agniveśa</s> for the welfare of living beings.
Long life, fame, health, abundant fulfillment of the three aims of life,

children.text: siddhiṃ cānuttamāṃ loke prāpnoti vidhinā paṭhan
children.translated_text: and unsurpassed success in the world are obtained by one who studies it according to rule.
The editor expands what has been stated briefly and condenses what has been too extensively stated.

children.text: saṃskartā kurute tantraṃ purāṇaṃ ca punarnavam
children.translated_text: He makes the ancient treatise newly renewed.
Therefore this supreme treatise was redacted by the very intelligent <s>Caraka</s>,
complete in truth and marked by three divisions.
Having propitiated <s>Śaṅkara</s>, lord of beings, <s>Dṛḍhabala</s> completed it
with its meaning unbroken; he was born in the city of <s>Pañcanada</s>.
Having gathered a special gleaning, like picking grain from many treatises,
he filled it out with the seventeen chapters on pharmaceutics and the Siddhi and Kalpa sections.
This treatise is not deficient in word or meaning and is free from defects of composition.
It is adorned with the twenty-six various <s>tantrayuktis</s> (methods of systematic exposition).
Among them are topic, combination, reasoned meaning, the meaning of a word,
specification, indication, definition, remainder of a sentence, purpose,
instruction, citation, extension, implication, and determination;
context, the absolute, the non-absolute, exception, and reversal;
objection, statement of rule, assent, explanation, and doubt;
consideration of past and future, technical designation, inference, and aggregation;
example, etymological explanation, restriction, and option;
rebuttal, extraction, and possibility: these are the <s>tantrayuktis</s>.
In a treatise stated both concisely and expansively, all these are present in full.
In one stated concisely, they are seen only in part.
As the sun is for a lotus-pond, and as a lamp is for a house,
so are the systematic devices of a treatise for awakening understanding and giving light.
A person whose intellect has gained a place here in even one science
quickly understands another science too, because he knows the methods of reasoning.
Even while studying the sciences, a physician without <s>tantrayukti</s>
does not grasp the meanings of the science, just as wealth is not gained when fortune has declined.
A badly grasped science destroys an ignorant man, like a weapon.

children.text: sugṛhītaṃ tadeva jñaṃ śāstraṃ śastraṃ ca rakṣati ||
children.translated_text: That very science, well grasped, protects the knowledgeable man, as does a weapon.
Therefore these will be explained again in detail in the later section,
for the sake of knowing the truth of this very treatise, with its merits and defects.
The person who has studied all this completely, reflects on the meanings correctly, is attentive, and is constant in practice,
becomes a giver of happy life to human beings, increased in firmness, memory, intellect, and <s>dharma</s>.
He in whose heart the twelve-thousand-verse <s>saṃhitā</s> abides
is a knower of meanings, a knower of analysis, and skilled in treatment.

children.text: rogāṃsteṣāṃ cikitsāṃ ca sa kimarthaṃ na budhyate
children.translated_text: What would he not understand about diseases and their treatment?
The treatment taught by <s>Agniveśa</s> is directed to what is wholesome and unwholesome for the healthy and the sick.
What is here is found elsewhere; what is not here is nowhere at all.
In the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s> and redacted by <s>Caraka</s>,
when the eighth Siddhisthāna had not been obtained, then by <s>Dṛḍhabala</s>
the Siddhisthāna was concisely completed for the sake of its own successful completion.

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte 'prāpte dṛḍhabalasampūrite siddhisthāne uttarabastisiddhirnāma dvādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s>, redacted by <s>Caraka</s>, and completed by <s>Dṛḍhabala</s> where it had not been obtained, in the Siddhisthāna, the twelfth chapter, named the Successful Procedure for the Upper Basti, is finished.
Now then we shall explain the rasayana section called Karapraciti.
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: karapracitānāṃ yathoktaguṇānām āmalakānāmuddhṛtāsthnāṃ śuṣkacūrṇitānāṃ punarmāghe phālgune vā māse triḥsaptakṛtvaḥ svarasaparipītānāṃ punaḥ śuṣkacūrṇīkṛtānām āḍhakam ekaṃ grāhayet atha jīvanīyānāṃ bṛṃhaṇīyānāṃ stanyajananānāṃ śukrajananānāṃ vayaḥsthāpanānāṃ ṣaḍvirecanaśatāśritīyoktānām auṣadhagaṇānāṃ candanāgurudhavatiniśakhadiraśiṃśapāsanasārāṇāṃ cāṇuśaḥ kṛttānām abhayāvibhītakapippalīvacācavyacitrakaviḍaṅgānāṃ ca samastānāmāḍhakamekaṃ daśaguṇenāmbhasā sādhayet tasminnāḍhakāvaśeṣe rase supūte tāny āmalakacūrṇāni dattvā gomayāgnibhir vaṃśavidalaśaratejanāgnibhir vā sādhayed yāvad apanayādrasasya tam anupadagdham upahṛtyāyasīṣu pātrīṣvāstīrya śoṣayet suśuṣkaṃ tat kṛṣṇājinasyopari dṛṣadi ślakṣṇapiṣṭam ayaḥsthālyāṃ nidhāpayet samyak taccūrṇam ayaś cūrṇāṣṭabhāgasamprayuktaṃ madhusarpirbhyām agnibalam abhisamīkṣya prayojayediti ||
children.translated_text: Of hand-gathered <s>āmalaka</s> fruits having the qualities described, with their stones removed, dried, powdered, then saturated twenty-one times with their own juice in the month of <s>Māgha</s> or <s>Phālguna</s>, and again dried and powdered, one should take one <s>āḍhaka</s>. Then one should take one <s>āḍhaka</s> in all of the life-promoting, nourishing, breast-milk-producing, semen-producing, and age-sustaining drug groups taught in the chapter on the six hundred purgatives, together with the heartwood, cut fine, of <s>candana</s>, <s>aguru</s>, <s>dhava</s>, <s>tiniśa</s>, <s>khadira</s>, <s>śiṃśapā</s>, and <s>āsana</s>, and also of <s>abhayā</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>cavya</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s>. He should cook them in ten times as much water. When one <s>āḍhaka</s> of the well-strained liquid remains, he should put in those <s>āmalaka</s> powders and cook them with fires of cow-dung or with fires of split bamboo, reed, <s>śara</s>, and <s>tejana</s>, until the liquid is gone. Removing it before it is burnt, he should spread it out in iron vessels and dry it. When it is thoroughly dry, he should grind it smooth on a stone over a black antelope skin and place it in an iron pan. That powder, properly combined with one eighth part iron powder, should be administered with honey and ghee after considering the strength of the digestive fire.
Formerly <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
<s>Jamadagni</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and other such knowers
used this rasayana with discipline and were freed from the danger of fatigue, disease, and old age.
By its power, greatly strong, they practiced austerity for as long as they wished.
<s>Brahmā</s> made this rasayana, lasting a thousand years,
pacifying old age and disease and bestowing intellect, senses, and strength.
Through austerity, celibacy, knowledge, tranquility,
the rasayana regimen, and a lifespan joined to the proper time,

children.text: sthitā maharṣayaḥ pūrvaṃ nahi kiṃcid rasāyanam
children.translated_text: the great seers of old remained steadfast. No rasayana
succeeds without self-discipline for people of village life who are occupied with other affairs.
For a year one should live continually among cows, subsisting on milk,
meditating mentally on the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, celibate and with senses restrained.

children.text: saṃvatsarānte pauṣīṃ vā māghīṃ vā phālgunīṃ tithim
children.translated_text: At the end of the year, on a lunar day in <s>Pauṣa</s>, <s>Māgha</s>, or <s>Phālguna</s>,
having fasted for three days, he should enter an <s>āmalakī</s> grove in the bright fortnight.
Climbing a tree rich in large fruits, he should take in his hand a fruit on a branch
and stand there reciting from the teaching of <s>Brahman</s> and immortality.
For at that moment immortality necessarily dwells in the <s>āmalaka</s>.
Through contact with immortality they become like sugar and honey, unctuous and soft.
As many of those fruits as he eats,
for that many thousands of years he lives with his youth returned.
Having reached satiation with them, he becomes like an immortal,

children.text: svayaṃ cāsyopatiṣṭhante śrīr vedā vākca rūpiṇī ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Śrī</s>, the <s>Vedas</s>, and Speech personified attend upon him of their own accord.

children.text: triphalāyā rase mūtre gavāṃ kṣāre ca lāvaṇe
children.translated_text: In the juice of <s>triphalā</s>, in the urine of cows, in saline alkali,
and then successively in <s>iṅgudī</s> alkali and <s>kiṃśuka</s> alkali,
one should heat plates of sharp iron until they are fire-colored.
They should be four finger-breadths long and thin, with the thickness of sesame seeds.
Knowing them to be like collyrium, one should make them into fine powders.
Those powders, combined with honey and with the juice of <s>āmalaka</s>,
should be kept like a linctus in a jar smeared with ghee,
and deposited for a year in a heap of barley.
The wise man should stir it every month, stirring it throughout.
At the end of the year its use is with honey and ghee,

children.text: prātaḥ prātarbalāpekṣī sātmyaṃ jīrṇe ca bhojanam
children.translated_text: morning after morning, with regard for strength; when it has been digested, suitable food is to be taken.

children.text: eṣa eva ca lauhānāṃ prayogaḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This very procedure has been proclaimed for preparations of iron.
He is not to be overpowered by blows, by illness, by old age, or by death;
he becomes one with the life-force of an elephant and always has exceedingly strong senses.
A man who uses the iron rasayana for a full year
becomes intelligent, famous, successful in speech, retentive of what he has heard, and very wealthy.
By this same method a proven preparation of gold and silver
extends life and removes all diseases.
<s>Aindrī</s>, that called <s>matsyākhyaka</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>brahmasuvarcalā</s>,

children.text: pippalyo lavaṇaṃ hema śaṅkhapuṣpī viṣaṃ ghṛtam ||
children.translated_text: <s>pippalī</s>, salt, gold, <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, poison, and ghee:
of these, except for gold, ghee, and poison, the portions should be three barley-grains each.

children.text: dvau yavau tatra hemnastu tilaṃ dadyādviṣasya ca ||
children.translated_text: There one should give two barley-grains of gold and one sesame-grain of poison,
and one <s>pala</s> of ghee; he should administer that as one combined preparation.
When it has been digested, food rich in ghee and accompanied by honey is praised.
It pacifies old age and disease, is supreme for producing memory and intelligence,
promotes life, nourishment, and prosperity, and clarifies voice and complexion.
This proven <s>Aindra</s> rasayana is a supreme producer of vital essence.

children.text: nainat prasahate kṛtyā nālakṣmīrna viṣaṃ na ruk ||
children.translated_text: No sorcery overpowers it, nor misfortune, nor poison, nor pain.

children.text: śvitraṃ sakuṣṭhaṃ jaṭharāṇi gulmāḥ plīhā purāṇo viṣamajvaraśca
children.translated_text: White leprosy together with <s>kuṣṭha</s>, abdominal enlargements, <s>gulma</s> tumors, splenic disease, chronic irregular fever,
diseases that remove intelligence, memory, and knowledge, and exceedingly strong winds are pacified by this.

children.text: maṇḍūkaparṇyāḥ svarasaḥ prayojyaḥ kṣīreṇa yaṣṭīmadhukasya cūrṇam
children.translated_text: The fresh juice of <s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s> should be used; the powder of <s>yaṣṭīmadhuka</s> with milk;

children.text: raso guḍūcyāstu samūlapuṣpyāḥ kalkaḥ prayojyaḥ khalu śaṅkhapuṣpyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the juice of <s>guḍūcī</s> together with its root and flowers; and the paste of <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s> should indeed be used.
They bestow life, destroy disease, and increase strength, digestive fire, complexion, and voice.

children.text: medhyāni caitāni rasāyanāni medhyā viśeṣeṇa ca śaṅkhapuṣpī ||
children.translated_text: And these <s>rasāyanas</s> (rejuvenatives) are intellect-promoting; <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s> is especially intellect-promoting.
Five, eight, seven, or ten <s>pippalīs</s>, with honey and ghee,
should be used for a full year by one who seeks the qualities of a <s>rasāyana</s>.
Three at a time in the forenoon, after eating, and before the meal,
<s>pippalīs</s> infused with alkali of <s>kiṃśuka</s> and fried in ghee
should be used, mixed with honey, by one who desires the qualities of a <s>rasāyana</s>,

children.text: jetuṃ kāsaṃ kṣayaṃ śoṣaṃ śvāsaṃ hikkāṃ galāmayān ||
children.translated_text: in order to conquer cough, wasting disease, consumption, dyspnea, hiccup, and diseases of the throat,
hemorrhoids, disorder of <s>grahaṇī</s>, pallor, irregular fever,
hoarseness, nasal catarrh, swelling, abdominal tumor, and <s>vātabalāsaka</s>.
By gradual increase over ten days, he should increase the daily amount up to ten <s>pippalīs</s>,
together with milk, and then reduce it again in the same way.

children.text: jīrṇe jīrṇe ca bhuñjīta ṣaṣṭikaṃ kṣīrasarpiṣā
children.translated_text: Whenever the previous dose has been digested, he should eat <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk and ghee.
This regimen of a thousand <s>pippalīs</s> is a <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: piṣṭās tā balibhiḥ sevyāḥ śṛtā madhyabalair naraiḥ
children.translated_text: They should be taken pounded by strong persons, boiled by men of middling strength,
and, for those of slight strength, they should be administered powdered, against the <s>doṣas</s> and diseases.
The regimen of ten <s>pippalīs</s> is best; the regimen of six is declared middling.

children.text: prayogo yas triparyantaḥ sa kanīyān sa cābalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The regimen that goes only up to three is the lesser one, and it is for the weak.
The <s>rasāyana</s> of <s>pippalīs</s> is nourishing, good for the voice, life-promoting, destructive of spleen and abdominal disease,
age-stabilizing, and intellect-promoting.
At the end of digestion he should take one <s>abhayā</s>; before food, two <s>vibhītakas</s>;
and after eating, four <s>āmalakas</s> with honey and ghee.
Using this <s>triphala</s> <s>rasāyana</s> for a full year,
one would live a complete hundred years, free from old age and disease.
One should smear a new iron vessel with a paste of <s>triphala</s>.
That coating, left for a day and night, he should drink when moistened with honey-water.
When it has been digested, food rich in unctuous substance is recommended there.

children.text: ajaro 'ruk samābhyāsāj jīvec caiva samāḥ śatam ||
children.translated_text: Through a year's repeated practice, he becomes free from old age and disease and lives a hundred years.
With <s>madhuka</s>, <s>tugākṣīrī</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, honey, ghee,

children.text: triphalā sitayā cāpi yuktā siddhaṃ rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: and also sugar, <s>triphala</s> is combined into a perfected <s>rasāyana</s>.
With all metals, with gold, with <s>vacā</s>, honey and ghee,
with <s>viḍaṅga</s> and <s>pippalī</s>, and with salt, <s>triphala</s> is combined.
By use for a year it grants intelligence, memory, and strength;
it becomes life-giving, auspicious, and a remover of old age and disease.

children.text: anamlaṃ ca kaṣāyaṃ ca kaṭu pāke śilājatu
children.translated_text: <s>Śilājatu</s> is non-sour, astringent, and pungent in digestion.
It is neither excessively hot nor cold, and it arises from four minerals.
From gold, from silver, from copper, from the excellent one, black iron,
that substance is a <s>rasāyana</s> according to the proper procedures; it is aphrodisiac and it removes disease.
When well impregnated with decoctions that remove <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>,
it attains supreme excellence of potency, either with all of them or with each one separately.

children.text: prakṣiptoddhṛtam apy enat punas tat prakṣiped rase
children.translated_text: Even after it has been put in and taken out, one should again put it into the decoction,
warm, for seven days; by this procedure its impregnation is accomplished.
According to the procedure stated before, together with powdered metals,
when drunk with milk it should grant long life accompanied by happiness.
It calms old age and disease and is supremely strengthening for the body;
it produces intelligence and memory and is auspicious; one living on milk should use it.
Its course of use is seven weeks, three weeks, or one week;
its threefold use is prescribed as superior, middling, and inferior.

children.text: palamardhapalaṃ karṣo mātrā tasya tridhā matā
children.translated_text: Its measure is regarded as threefold: one <s>pala</s>, half a <s>pala</s>, or one <s>karṣa</s>.
Next I shall explain its particular varieties and their proper procedure.
The mountain minerals beginning with gold, heated by the sun, exude.
That soft, resin-like, clear earthy exudation is <s>śilājatu</s>.
That which is sweet and slightly bitter, and resembles the hibiscus flower,
pungent in digestion and cooling, is the exudation of gold.

children.text: rūpyasya kaṭukaḥ śvetaḥ śītaḥ svādu vipacyate
children.translated_text: The exudation of silver is pungent, white, cooling, and sweet in digestion.
That of copper resembles a peacock's neck, is bitter and hot, and digests as pungent.
But that which has the appearance of <s>guggulu</s>, is somewhat bitter and joined with salt,
pungent in digestion and cooling, is the one from iron, and it is the best of all.
All have the smell of cow's urine and are suitable for all therapeutic actions.
In <s>rasāyana</s> applications, however, the last is especially distinguished.
In due order, for <s>vāta</s> with <s>pitta</s>, for <s>śleṣman</s> with <s>pitta</s>, for <s>kapha</s>, and for all three,
the exudations born from the minerals beginning with gold are especially praised.
In regimens of <s>śilājatu</s>, one should avoid foods that cause burning and foods that are heavy;
at all times one should especially avoid <s>kulattha</s>.

children.text: te hy atyantaviruddhatvād aśmano bhedanāḥ param
children.translated_text: For because of their extreme incompatibility, they are seen in the world
to split stones completely; therefore their use is prohibited.

children.text: payāṃsi takrāṇi rasāḥ sayūṣās toyaṃ samūtrā vividhāḥ kaṣāyāḥ
children.translated_text: Milks, buttermilks, meat juices, soups with pulse broth, water, urines, and various decoctions

children.text: āloḍanārthaṃ girijasya śastās te te prayojyāḥ prasamīkṣya kāryam ||
children.translated_text: are praised for stirring the mountain-born substance; each should be used after carefully considering the intended action.

children.text: na so 'sti rogo bhuvi sādhyarūpaḥ śilāhvayaṃ yaṃ na jayet prasahya
children.translated_text: There is no disease on earth, if it is of curable form,

children.text: tat kālayogairvidhibhiḥ prayuktaṃ svasthasya corjāṃ vipulāṃ dadāti ||
children.translated_text: that the substance called <s>śilā</s>, applied with proper timing and procedures, would not forcibly conquer; and it gives abundant energy to a healthy person.

children.text: karapracitike pāde daśa ṣaṭ ca maharṣiṇā
children.translated_text: In the <s>Karapracitika</s> section, ten and six
combinations of perfected <s>rasāyanas</s> have been set forth by the great seer.

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte cikitsāsthāne rasāyanādhyāye karapracitīyo nāma rasāyanapādastṛtīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s> and redacted by <s>Caraka</s>, in the <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s>, in the chapter on <s>rasāyana</s>, the third <s>rasāyana</s> quarter, named <s>Karapracitīya</s>, is completed.
Now then we shall explain the <s>rasāyana</s> section called "The Arising of Ayurveda."
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: ṛṣayaḥ khalu kadācicchālīnā yāyāvarāśca grāmyauṣadhyāhārāḥ santaḥ sāmpannikā mandaceṣṭā nātikalyāśca prāyeṇa babhūvuḥ
children.translated_text: Once, indeed, the sages, both settled and wandering, were taking village-grown herbs and food; they had become well provided for, sluggish in activity, and, for the most part, not very healthy.

children.text: te sarvāsām itikartavyatānām asamarthāḥ santo grāmyavāsakṛtamātmadoṣaṃ matvā pūrvanivāsam apagatagrāmyadoṣaṃ śivaṃ puṇyam udāraṃ medhyam agamyam asukṛtibhir gaṅgāprabhavam amaragandharvakiṃnarānucaritam anekaratnanicayamacintyādbhutaprabhāvaṃ brahmarṣisiddhacāraṇānucaritaṃ divyatīrthauṣadhiprabhavam atiśaraṇyaṃ himavantam amarādhipatiguptaṃ jagmur bhṛgvaṅgiro'trivasiṣṭhakaśyapāgastyapulastyavāmadevāsitagautamaprabhṛtayo maharṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Being unable to perform all that had to be done, and thinking that the fault in themselves had been caused by village-dwelling, the great sages, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Agastya</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Asita</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and others, went to their former abode, <s>Himavant</s>: free from the faults of village life, auspicious, holy, noble, pure, inaccessible to the impious, sprung from the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, frequented by immortals, gandharvas, and kiṃnaras, filled with masses of many jewels and of inconceivable, wondrous power, frequented by brahmarṣis, siddhas, and cāraṇas, the source of divine sacred fords and herbs, exceedingly protective, and guarded by the lord of the immortals.

children.text: tān indraḥ sahasradṛg amaragurur abravītsvāgataṃ brahmavidāṃ jñānatapodhanānāṃ brahmarṣīṇām
children.translated_text: To them <s>Indra</s>, the thousand-eyed teacher of the immortals, said: "Welcome to the brahmarṣis, knowers of brahman, whose wealth is knowledge and austerity.

children.text: asti nanu vo glānir aprabhāvatvaṃ vaisvaryaṃ vaivarṇyaṃ ca grāmyavāsakṛtam asukham asukhānubandhaṃ ca grāmyo hi vāso mūlam aśastānāṃ tat kṛtaḥ puṇyakṛdbhir anugrahaḥ prajānāṃ svaśarīramavekṣituṃ kālaḥ kālaścāyamāyurvedopadeśasya brahmarṣīṇām ātmanaḥ prajānāṃ cānugrahārtham āyurvedamaśvinau mahyaṃ prāyacchatāṃ prajāpatiraśvibhyāṃ prajāpataye brahmā prajānām alpam āyur jarāvyādhibahulam asukham asukhānubandham alpatvād alpatapodamaniyamadānādhyayanasaṃcayaṃ matvā puṇyatamam āyuḥprakarṣakaraṃ jarāvyādhipraśamanam ūrjaskaram amṛtaṃ śivaṃ śaraṇyamudāraṃ bhavanto mattaḥ śrotumarhatāthopadhārayituṃ prakāśayituṃ ca prajānugrahārthamārṣaṃ brahma ca prati maitrīṃ kāruṇyam ātmanaś cānuttamaṃ puṇyamudāraṃ brāhmamakṣayaṃ karmeti ||
children.translated_text: Surely there is weariness, loss of power, weakness of voice, and loss of complexion among you, caused by village-dwelling, and this is unpleasant and followed by unpleasantness; for village-dwelling is the root of unwholesome things. Therefore your coming here, meritorious ones, is a favor to living beings. It is time to look after your own bodies, and this too is the time for the instruction of Ayurveda. For the sake of favoring the brahmarṣis themselves and living beings, the Aśvins gave Ayurveda to me, Prajāpati gave it to the Aśvins, and Brahmā gave it to Prajāpati. Considering that the life of creatures is short, full of old age and disease, unpleasant and followed by unpleasantness, and, because of its shortness, with little accumulation of austerity, self-restraint, observance, giving, and study, you should hear from me, retain, and reveal for the favor of living beings this most holy teaching, which lengthens life, pacifies old age and disease, gives energy, is deathless, auspicious, protective, and noble. This will also be friendship and compassion toward the seers and brahman, and for yourselves an unsurpassed, holy, noble, brahmanic, imperishable act."

children.text: tacchrutvā vibudhapativacanam ṛṣayaḥ sarva evāmaravaram ṛgbhis tuṣṭuvuḥ prahṛṣṭāśca tadvacanamabhinananduśceti ||
children.translated_text: Hearing this speech of the lord of the gods, all the sages praised the best of the immortals with Ṛg verses, and joyfully approved his words.

children.text: athendras tadāyurvedāmṛtam ṛṣibhyaḥ saṃkramyovāca etatsarvamanuṣṭheyam ayaṃ ca śivaḥ kālo rasāyanānāṃ divyāścauṣadhayo himavatprabhavāḥ prāptavīryāḥ tadyathā aindrī brāhmī payasyā kṣīrapuṣpī śrāvaṇī mahāśrāvaṇī śatāvarī vidārī jīvantī punarnavā nāgabalā sthirā vacā chattrā aticchatrā medā mahāmedā jīvanīyāścānyāḥ payasā prayuktāḥ ṣaṇmāsāt paramāyurvayaśca taruṇamanāmayatvaṃ svaravarṇasampadam upacayaṃ medhāṃ smṛtimuttamabalam iṣṭāṃścāparān bhāvān āvahanti siddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Indra</s>, having transmitted that nectar of Ayurveda to the sages, said: "All this is to be practiced, and this is an auspicious time for <s>rasāyana</s> treatments. The divine herbs born in <s>Himavant</s> have attained their potency. They are, namely: <s>aindrī</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, <s>payasyā</s>, <s>kṣīrapuṣpī</s>, <s>śrāvaṇī</s>, <s>mahāśrāvaṇī</s>, <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>nāgabalā</s>, <s>sthirā</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>chattrā</s>, <s>aticchattrā</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>mahāmedā</s>, and other life-promoting herbs. When successfully prepared and used with milk, after six months they bring the highest lifespan, youthful age, freedom from disease, excellence of voice and complexion, bodily increase, intelligence, memory, supreme strength, and other desired states.

children.text: brahmasuvarcalā nāmauṣadhir yā hiraṇyakṣīrā puṣkarasadṛśapattrā ādityaparṇī nāmauṣadhiryā sūryakāntā iti vijñāyate suvarṇakṣīrā sūryamaṇḍalākārapuṣpā ca nārīnāmauṣadhiḥ aśvabalā iti vijñāyate yā bilvajasadṛśapattrā kāṣṭhagodhā nāmauṣadhir godhākārā sarpānāmauṣadhiḥ sarpākārā somo nāmauṣadhirājaḥ pañcadaśaparvā sa soma iva hīyate vardhate ca padmā nāmauṣadhiḥ padmākārā padmaraktā padmagandhā ca ajānām auṣadhiḥ ajaśṛṅgī iti vijñāyate nīlā nāmauṣadhistu nīlakṣīrā nīlapuṣpā latāpratānabahuleti āsāmoṣadhīnāṃ yāṃ yāmevopalabheta tasyās tasyāḥ svarasasya sauhityaṃ gatvā snehabhāvitāyām ārdrapalāśadroṇyāṃ sapidhānāyāṃ digvāsāḥ śayīta tatra pralīyate ṣaṇmāsena punaḥ sambhavati tasyājaṃ payaḥ pratyavasthāpanaṃ ṣaṇmāsena devatānukārī bhavati vayovarṇasvarākṛtibalaprabhābhiḥ svayaṃ cāsya sarvavācogatāni prādurbhavanti divyaṃ cāsya cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ ca bhavati gatir yojanasahasraṃ daśavarṣasahasrāṇy āyur anupadravaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: There is an herb named <s>brahmasuvarcalā</s>, which has golden milk and leaves like lotus leaves; there is an herb named <s>ādityaparṇī</s>, known as <s>sūryakāntā</s>, with golden milk and flowers shaped like the solar disk; the herb named <s>nārī</s> is known as <s>aśvabalā</s>, and has leaves like those of the bilva; the herb named <s>kāṣṭhagodhā</s> is lizard-shaped; the herb of serpents is serpent-shaped; <s>soma</s>, the king of herbs, has fifteen joints, and it wanes and waxes like the moon; the herb named <s>padmā</s> is lotus-shaped, lotus-red, and lotus-scented; the herb of goats is known as <s>ajaśṛṅgī</s>; and the herb named <s>nīlā</s> has blue milk, blue flowers, and many spreading vine-shoots. Of these herbs, whichever one he obtains, after drinking its fresh juice to satiety, he should lie naked in a covered trough of fresh palāśa wood that has been soaked with oil. There he dissolves, and after six months he comes into being again. Goat's milk is his restorative regimen. In six months he becomes like a deity in age, complexion, voice, form, strength, and radiance; all forms of speech arise spontaneously for him, his sight and hearing become divine, his range of movement is a thousand yojanas, and his life lasts ten thousand years without affliction.
The power of the divine herbs can be endured by people such as you;
but it cannot be endured by those whose selves have not been prepared.

children.text: oṣadhīnāṃ prabhāveṇa tiṣṭhatāṃ sve ca karmaṇi
children.translated_text: Through the power of the herbs, while you remain in your own proper work,
every kind of complete welfare will indeed come to you.
For forest-dwellers and householders who are purified and self-controlled,

children.text: śakyā oṣadhayo hy etāḥ sevituṃ viṣayābhijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these herbs, born in their own regions, can indeed be used.
But those herbs which, because of the qualities of their ground and because of a middling action,

children.text: mṛduvīryatarās tāsāṃ vidhirjñeyaḥ sa eva tu ||
children.translated_text: are milder in potency, should be understood to have this same procedure.

children.text: paryeṣṭuṃ tāḥ prayoktuṃ vā ye 'samarthāḥ sukhārthinaḥ
children.translated_text: For those who seek well-being but are unable to search for them
or to use them, this other <s>rasāyana</s> procedure is praised.

children.text: balyānāṃ jīvanīyānāṃ bṛṃhaṇīyāś ca yā daśa
children.translated_text: Of the ten that are strengthening, life-promoting, and bulk-promoting...
and of the age-sustaining substances, and of <s>khadira</s> and <s>āsana</s>;
of dates, <s>madhūka</s>, <s>mustā</s>, and <s>utpala</s>;
of raisins, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>vacā</s>, and <s>citraka</s>;
of <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>payasyā</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>joṅgaka</s>;
of <s>ṛddhi</s>, <s>nāgabalā</s>, <s>dvāradā</s>, and <s>dhava</s>;
of <s>triphalā</s>, <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, and sandalwood;
of sugarcane, roots of reed, <s>śrīparṇī</s>, and <s>tiniśa</s>;

children.text: rasāḥ pṛthak pṛthag grāhyāḥ palāśakṣāra eva ca
children.translated_text: their juices should be taken separately, and also the alkali of <s>palāśa</s>.

children.text: eṣāṃ palonmitān bhāgān payo gavyaṃ caturguṇam ||
children.translated_text: Of these, portions measured by a <s>pala</s> should be taken, along with cow's milk in fourfold quantity;

children.text: dve pātre tilatailasya dve ca gavyasya sarpiṣaḥ
children.translated_text: two vessels of sesame oil and two of cow's ghee;

children.text: tat sādhyaṃ sarvam ekatra susiddhaṃ snehamuddharet ||
children.translated_text: all that should be cooked together, and when the unctuous preparation is well prepared, it should be removed.
Into it an <s>āḍhaka</s> of <s>āmalaka</s> powder, processed one hundred times,
with its own fresh juice, should be added, along with fresh honey;
and one <s>prastha</s> vessel of powdered sugar should be added.

children.text: tugākṣīryāḥ sapippalyāḥ sthāpyaṃ saṃmūrchitaṃ ca tat ||
children.translated_text: Together with <s>tugākṣīrī</s> and <s>pippalī</s>, that should be set aside after being thoroughly blended,
in a very clean earthen jar smeared with ghee, for half a month.
Thereafter one should use a dose of it equal to one's digestive fire.
Of gold, copper, coral, iron, and crystal,
of pearls, beryl, conch, and silver powders,
having added a sixteenth part, and avoiding exertion and sexual intercourse,

children.text: jīrṇe jīrṇe ca bhuñjīta ṣaṣṭikaṃ kṣīrasarpiṣā ||
children.translated_text: whenever it has been digested, one should eat <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk and ghee.
It pacifies all diseases, is aphrodisiac, and is excellent for longevity;
it gives strength to mind, memory, body, digestive fire, intellect, and senses.
It is supremely energy-producing, and likewise improves complexion and voice;
it pacifies poison and misfortune, and bestows everything connected with speech.

children.text: siddhārthatāṃ cābhinavaṃ vayaśca prajāpriyatvaṃ ca yaśaśca loke
children.translated_text: Success in undertakings, fresh youth, popularity among people, and fame in the world
are to be sought by using properly this <s>Brāhma</s> rasāyana, of noble potency.
For those who are capable, free from disease, intelligent, and self-controlled,
entering the cottage is beneficial, provided they have time and the necessary equipment.

children.text: ato'nyathā tu ye teṣāṃ sauryamārutiko vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: But for those otherwise situated, there is the solar-and-wind procedure;

children.text: tayoḥ śreṣṭhataraḥ pūrvo vidhiḥ sa tu suduṣkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: of the two, the former procedure is superior, but it is very difficult to perform.
If diseases arise from a lapse in the rasāyana regimen,
their appropriate medicine should be administered, leaving off the rasāyana.
One should know as a perpetual rasāyana the man who is truthful, free from anger, abstinent from liquor and sexual intercourse,
nonviolent, not overexerting himself, calm, and pleasant in speech;
devoted to recitation and purity, firm, constantly generous, austere,
delighting in honoring gods, cows, brahmins, teachers, gurus, and elders;
always devoted to compassion, always sensitive to mercy,
regular in waking and sleeping, and constantly eating milk and ghee;
knowing place, time, and measure, knowing reasoned application, free from arrogance,
of approved conduct, unmixed in habits, with his senses turned toward the self;
serving elders, believers, and self-controlled people,
and devoted to the dharmaśāstras.

children.text: guṇair etaiḥ samuditaiḥ prayuṅkte yo rasāyanam
children.translated_text: Whoever, endowed with these qualities all together, uses rasāyana,
obtains all the benefits of rasāyana just as they have been stated.
Without eliminating, as appropriate, the bodily and mental <s>doṣas</s>,
a person is never joined to the benefits of rasāyana.
For formulations intended to extend life and remove old age and disease
succeed for those whose mind and body are purified and whose self is disciplined.
Therefore all this should not be spoken of to people whose selves are ruined,
to unsuitable or crooked persons, to non-twice-born persons, or to those in whom there is no obedience.
Those rasāyana combinations, and those aphrodisiac formulations that are recognized,
and whatever medicine there is for disorders, all of that depends on the physician.
Therefore the wise man should honor, as his life-teacher, an intelligent man who has mastered the Veda,
with the utmost of his power, just as <s>Devendra</s> honored the two <s>Aśvins</s>.
The two <s>Aśvins</s> are remembered as the divine physicians and bearers of the sacrifice;
for the severed head of the sacrifice was restored by them.

children.text: praśīrṇā daśanāḥ pūṣṇo netre naṣṭe bhagasya ca
children.translated_text: The fallen teeth of <s>Pūṣan</s>, and the lost eyes of <s>Bhaga</s>,
and the paralysis of the thunder-bearer's arm were treated by them alone.
The cool-rayed one, seized by <s>rājayakṣmā</s> (consumption), was treated;
<s>Candra</s>, afflicted through <s>Soma</s>, was made well again by them.

children.text: bhārgavaścyavanaḥ kāmī vṛddhaḥ san vikṛtiṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: The lustful <s>Cyavana</s> of the <s>Bhṛgu</s> line, old and deformed,
bereft of complexion and voice, was made young again by them.
By these and many other deeds, the two best physicians
became greatly worthy of honor among the great-souled ones beginning with <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: grahāḥ stotrāṇi mantrāṇi tathā nānāhavīṃṣi ca
children.translated_text: Planetary rites, hymns, mantras, and various oblations,
as well as smoky-colored animals, are prescribed for them by twice-born ritualists.
In the morning pressing, <s>Śakra</s> drinks Soma together with the <s>Aśvins</s>;
and in the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> rite the Blessed One rejoices together with the <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: indrāgnī cāśvinau caiva stūyante prāyaśo dvijaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and the <s>Aśvins</s> are very often praised by twice-born priests;

children.text: stūyante vedavākyeṣu na tathānyā hi devatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they are praised in Vedic utterances; other deities are not praised in the same way.
Thus, by ageless, deathless, steadfast gods together with their lords,
the <s>Aśvins</s> are honored with discipline as physicians.
How much more, by mortals subject to death, disease, and old age, mostly full of suffering and desirous of happiness,

children.text: kiṃ punarbhiṣajo martyaiḥ pūjyāḥ syur nātiśaktitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should physicians be honored with the utmost of one's power?
A twice-born physician who is virtuous, intelligent, competent, and versed in śāstra
He should be honored by living beings like a guru, for he is remembered as a teacher of life.
At the completion of his learning, a physician is said to have a second birth;

children.text: aśnute vaidyaśabdaṃ hi na vaidyaḥ pūrvajanmanā ||
children.translated_text: for he obtains the word <s>vaidya</s>; he is not a <s>vaidya</s> by his former birth.
At the completion of learning, either a brahmanic or even a seerly essence

children.text: dhruvam āviśati jñānāt tasmād vaidyo dvijaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: surely enters him through knowledge; therefore a <s>vaidya</s> is remembered as twice-born.
One should not envy him, nor abuse him, nor do anything harmful

children.text: prāṇācāryaṃ budhaḥ kaścid icchann āyur anitvaram ||
children.translated_text: toward the teacher of life, if any wise person desires enduring life.
But a man who, having been treated, whether after promising or without promising,
does not render service to the physician, has no expiation here.
The physician too, careful, should protect all patients like his own sons

children.text: ābādhebhyo hi saṃrakṣed icchan dharmam anuttamam ||
children.translated_text: from afflictions, if he desires unsurpassed <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).
<s>Āyurveda</s>, for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, and for the sake of wealth and pleasure,
was revealed by the great seers, who were devoted to <s>dharma</s> and desired the imperishable state.
The one who engages in treatment neither for wealth nor for pleasure, but out of compassion for beings,
surpasses everything.
But those who, for the sake of livelihood, make treatment a commodity for sale
abandon a heap of gold and attend upon a heap of dust.
For those being dragged by terrible diseases to the abode of <s>Vaivasvata</s>,

children.text: chittvā vaivasvatān pāśān jīvitaṃ yaḥ prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: the one who cuts the nooses of <s>Vaivasvata</s> and grants life
has no equal here as a giver of <s>dharma</s> and wealth.

children.text: na hi jīvitadānāddhi dānam anyad viśiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: For no other gift is superior to the gift of life.

children.text: paro bhūtadayā dharma iti matvā cikitsayā
children.translated_text: The one who, thinking that compassion for beings is the highest <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: vartate yaḥ sa siddhārthaḥ sukham atyantam aśnute ||
children.translated_text: engages in treatment, has accomplished his aim and obtains complete happiness.
The origin of <s>Āyurveda</s>, the auspicious procedure for divine medicines,
the perfected jewel-like <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenant), whose qualities are little short of nectar,
which the lord of immortals spoke to the perfected celibates,
all that has been fully set forth in the origin of <s>Āyurveda</s>.

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte cikitsitasthāne rasāyanādhyāye āyurvedasamutthānīyo nāma rasāyanapādaścaturthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s> and redacted by <s>Caraka</s>, in the section on treatment, in the chapter on <s>rasāyana</s>, the fourth <s>rasāyana</s> quarter, named the origin of <s>Āyurveda</s>, is completed.
Now then we shall explain the <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> quarter named <s>Saṃyogaśaramūlīya</s>.
So spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.
A self-possessed man should always seek <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> (virility therapy),

children.text: tadāyattau hi dharmārthau prītiśca yaśa eva ca ||
children.translated_text: for <s>dharma</s> and wealth depend on that, as do affection and fame.
For this is the basis of a son, and these qualities rest upon a son;

children.text: vājīkaraṇam agryaṃ ca kṣetraṃ strī yā praharṣiṇī ||
children.translated_text: and the foremost <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>, the field, is a woman who is joyful.

children.text: iṣṭā hy ekaikaśo 'py arthāḥ paraṃ prītikarāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Objects desired even one by one are remembered as giving supreme delight;

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ strīśarīre ye saṃghātena pratiṣṭhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: how much more those that are established together in a woman's body.
For the aggregation of the objects of the senses is found among women and nowhere else.
For the sense-object that depends on a woman produces especially great delight.
Among women delight is especially established; among women offspring is established.

children.text: dharmārthau strīṣu lakṣmīśca strīṣu lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Among women <s>dharma</s> and wealth, fortune, and the worlds are established.
She who is beautiful, settled in youth, and adorned with auspicious marks,

children.text: yā vaśyā śikṣitā yā ca sā strī vṛṣyatamā matā
children.translated_text: who is compliant and trained, that woman is considered the most virilifying.
But because of the various inclinations of people, and because of the fated conjunction of women,

children.text: taṃ taṃ prāpya vivardhante naraṃ rūpādayo guṇāḥ
children.translated_text: qualities such as beauty grow in each case on reaching one man after another.
The woman who, by age, beauty, speech, and gestures, is supreme for a particular man

children.text: praviśatyāśu hṛdayaṃ daivād vā karmaṇo 'pi vā
children.translated_text: quickly enters his heart, whether through fate or through karma.
She who has the form of a festival for the heart, who has the same mental disposition,

children.text: samānasattvā yā vaśyā yā yasya prīyate priyaiḥ
children.translated_text: who is of the same nature, compliant, and dear to him through qualities dear to him,
who, by surpassing qualities, becomes a snare for all the senses,

children.text: yayā viyukto nistrīkam aratir manyate jagat
children.translated_text: separated from whom he thinks the world is womanless and without delight,

children.text: yasyā ṛte śarīraṃ nā dhatte śūnyam ivendriyaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: without whom a man does not sustain his body, as if it were empty of the senses,
on seeing whom he is not overcome by grief, agitation, aversion, or fear,

children.text: yāti yāṃ prāpya visrambhaṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣyatyatīva yām ||
children.translated_text: on reaching whom he comes to confidence, and on seeing whom he is exceedingly delighted,
whom he approaches again and again as if she were unprecedented, with a rush of excessive joy,

children.text: gatvā gatvāpi bahuśo yāṃ tṛptiṃ naiva gacchati ||
children.translated_text: and to whom, even after going many times, he never comes to satiety:

children.text: sā strī vṛṣyatamā tasya nānābhāvā hi mānavāḥ
children.translated_text: that woman is the most virilifying for him, for human dispositions are various.
A healthy man desiring offspring should approach a woman of a different lineage, virilifying, joyful, and free from trouble,
pure and bathed.

children.text: acchāyaś caikaśākhaś ca niṣphalaśca yathā drumaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As a tree is without shade, with one branch, and fruitless,
with an unpleasant smell and solitary, so too is a man without offspring.
He is to be considered a painted lamp, a dried-up pond, a non-mineral that resembles a mineral,
a bundle of straw in human form, if he is without progeny.
A man without offspring should be considered without foundation, naked, empty, and having only one sense,
and indeed inactive.
One with abundant offspring has many forms, many faces, many arrays, and many actions;
he has many eyes, much knowledge, many selves, and many progeny.
"This man is auspicious, this man is praiseworthy, this man is fortunate, this man is vigorous,
this man has many branches"; thus a man with abundant offspring is praised.

children.text: prītirbalaṃ sukhaṃ vṛttir vistāro vipulaṃ kulam ||
children.translated_text: Affection, strength, happiness, livelihood, expansion, and an extensive family,
fame, worlds with happy results, and satisfaction depend upon offspring.
Therefore, desiring offspring and the qualities that depend upon offspring,
and desiring the pleasures of love, one should be constantly devoted to <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>;
also the perfected pleasures of enjoyment that increase virility and offspring.
Next I shall explain the aphrodisiac combinations.
The roots of <s>śara</s> and of sugarcane, sugarcane stalk, and sugarcane shoots,
<s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>payasyā</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, and <s>kaṇṭakārikā</s>,

children.text: jīvantī jīvako medā vīrā carṣabhako balā ||
children.translated_text: <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, and <s>balā</s>,
<s>ṛddhi</s>, <s>gokṣuraka</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>ātmaguptā</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>:

children.text: eṣāṃ tripalikān bhāgān māṣāṇām āḍhakaṃ navam ||
children.translated_text: of these one should take portions of three <s>palas</s> each, and a fresh <s>āḍhaka</s> of black gram.
He should cook them in a <s>droṇa</s> of water and leave one quarter remaining.

children.text: tatra peṣyāṇi madhukaṃ drākṣā phalgūni pippalī ||
children.translated_text: Into that, the ingredients to be ground are <s>madhuka</s>, grapes, <s>phalgūni</s>, and <s>pippalī</s>,
<s>ātmaguptā</s>, <s>madhūka</s> fruits, dates, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,
and separately the juices of <s>vidārī</s>, emblic myrobalan, and sugarcane.

children.text: sarpiṣaś cāḍhakaṃ dadyāt kṣīradroṇaṃ ca tadbhiṣak
children.translated_text: The physician should add an <s>āḍhaka</s> of ghee and a <s>droṇa</s> of milk.
He should cook it until only the ghee remains, strain it well, and then combine it again
with powders of sugar and <s>tugākṣīrī</s>, each measured at one <s>prastha</s>,

children.text: palaiś caturbhir māgadhyāḥ palena maricasya ca ||
children.translated_text: with four <s>palas</s> of <s>māgadhī</s>, and with one <s>pala</s> of black pepper,
and with powders of cinnamon, cardamom, and saffron, each measured at half a <s>pala</s>.
The physician should prepare it with two <s>kuḍavas</s> of honey.
When thickened, he should make pills of one <s>pala</s> each and administer them according to the digestive fire.

children.text: eṣa vṛṣyaḥ paraṃ yogo bṛṃhaṇo balavardhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is an excellent aphrodisiac formula, nourishing and strength-increasing.
By means of it, a strong man, excited like a stallion, can apply his sexual organ.
One should take a fresh <s>āḍhaka</s> of black gram and of the seeds of <s>ātmaguptā</s>,
along with <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>ṛddhi</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,
as well as <s>madhuka</s> and <s>aśvagandhā</s>, each measured by a <s>kuḍava</s>, and cook them.

children.text: rase tasmin ghṛtaprasthaṃ gavyaṃ daśaguṇaṃ payaḥ
children.translated_text: In that decoction one should put one <s>prastha</s> of cow ghee and ten times as much cow's milk,
one <s>prastha</s> of the juice of <s>vidārī</s>, and one <s>prastha</s> of sugarcane juice.
Having cooked it over a gentle fire, he should store the prepared ghee.
Into it he should add separate portions of sugar, <s>tugākṣīrī</s>, and honey,
each of four <s>palas</s>, and he should add one <s>pala</s> of <s>pippalī</s>.
After first licking one <s>pala</s> of this, he should then take food.

children.text: ya icchedakṣayaṃ śukraṃ śephasaś cottamaṃ balam
children.translated_text: This is for one who desires inexhaustible semen and excellent strength of the penis.
With sugar, split black gram, <s>tugākṣīrī</s>, milk, and ghee,
with wheat flour as the sixth ingredient, one should cook an <s>utkārikā</s> in ghee.

children.text: tāṃ nātipakvāṃ mṛditāṃ kaukkuṭe madhure rase ||
children.translated_text: While it is not overcooked, it should be crushed and put into warm, sweet chicken broth,

children.text: sugandhe prakṣiped uṣṇe yathā sāndrībhaved rasaḥ
children.translated_text: fragrant, so that the broth becomes thick.
This thickened lump-broth is aphrodisiac, nourishing, and strength-increasing.
By means of it, a strong man, excited like a stallion, can apply his sexual organ.
In the same way, the lump-broth of peacock, partridge, and goose is recognized.
Through it a man becomes virile, and it produces strength, complexion, and voice.
One should cook ghee, black grams, and goat testicles in buffalo meat broth.
He should fry that strained broth, made sour with fruit, in fresh ghee.
It should be slightly salted and joined with coriander, cumin, and dry ginger.
This excellent broth is aphrodisiac, strengthening, and nourishing.
He should prepare sparrows in partridge broth, partridges in chicken broth,
chickens in peacock broth, and peacock likewise in goose broth.
He should make these broths heated in fresh ghee and soured with fruit,
or sweet, according to suitability, fragrant, and strength-increasing.
When a man has eaten sparrow meat to satiety and drinks milk afterward,

children.text: na tasya liṅgaśaithilyaṃ syānna śukrakṣayo niśi ||
children.translated_text: he will have neither slackness of the penis nor loss of semen at night.
One who, after eating <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice rich in ghee with black-gram soup,

children.text: payaḥ pibati rātriṃ sa kṛtsnāṃ jāgarti vegavān
children.translated_text: drinks milk, stays awake for the whole night, full of impulse.

children.text: na nā svapiti rātriṣu nityastabdhena śephasā
children.translated_text: He does not sleep during the nights, his penis being constantly stiff.
When satisfied with chicken meat roasted in crocodile semen,
one should drain off the juice of fish eggs and eat it fried in ghee.
In the same way, one should eat the eggs of geese, peacocks, and cocks.

children.text: srotaḥsu śuddheṣvamale śarīre vṛṣyaṃ yadā nā mitamatti kāle
children.translated_text: When the channels are purified and the body is stainless, and when a man eats a measured aphrodisiac at the proper time,

children.text: vṛṣāyate tena paraṃ manuṣyas tadbṛṃhaṇaṃ caiva balapradaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: through it he becomes supremely virile; it is also nourishing and strength-giving.

children.text: tasmāt purā śodhanameva kāryaṃ balānurūpaṃ na hi vṛṣyayogāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore purification must first be performed according to one's strength, for aphrodisiac formulas

children.text: sidhyanti dehe maline prayuktāḥ kliṣṭe yathā vāsasi rāgayogāḥ ||
children.translated_text: do not succeed when applied in an impure body, just as dye preparations do not succeed on a soiled cloth.

children.text: vājīkaraṇasāmarthyaṃ kṣetraṃ strī yasya caiva yā
children.translated_text: The power of vājīkaraṇa, the woman as the field, and the woman belonging to each man,

children.text: ye doṣā nirapatyānāṃ guṇāḥ putravatāṃ ca ye ||
children.translated_text: the defects of the childless and the qualities of those who have sons,
and the fifteen combinations that increase virility and offspring
have been stated in the <s>Śaramūlīya</s> quarter; they give nourishment and strength.

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte cikitsāsthāne vājīkaraṇādhyāye saṃyogaśaramūlīyo nāma vājīkaraṇapādaḥ prathamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s> and redacted by <s>Caraka</s>, in the <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s>, in the chapter on vājīkaraṇa, the first vājīkaraṇa quarter, named <s>Saṃyogaśaramūlīya</s>, is completed.
Now, then, we shall explain the vājīkaraṇa quarter called <s>Āsiktakṣīrika</s>.
So indeed spoke the Blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.
One should take pure <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, filled with poured milk and not dried,
pound it well in a mortar, and press it out after kneading it with milk.

children.text: gṛhītvā taṃ rasaṃ pūtaṃ gavyena payasā saha
children.translated_text: Taking that strained juice together with cow's milk,
and with the seeds of <s>ātmaguptā</s> and the broth of grain and black gram,
with <s>balā</s>, <s>śūrpaparṇī</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, and <s>jīvaka</s>,
with <s>ṛddhi</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>kākolī</s>, <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, and <s>madhuka</s>,
and also with <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, grapes, and dates,
the physician should cook it, combined in proper measure, and should add to it
powders of <s>tugākṣīrī</s>, black gram, rice, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s>,

children.text: godhūmānāṃ ca cūrṇāni yaiḥ sa sāndrībhavedrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and wheat, by which that broth becomes thick.
and he should make it concentrated, with abundant honey and sugar.
The pills should be equal in size to jujube fruits, and he should fry them in ghee.
Using them according to his digestive fire, while eating milk and meat broth,
even an old man sees abundant offspring, sons of his own, inexhaustible.
Of sparrows, haṃsas, cocks, and peacocks likewise,
and of the <s>śiśumāra</s> and the crocodile, the physician should collect the semen.
Cow's ghee, and also the fat of the boar and the <s>kuliṅga</s> bird,

children.text: ṣaṣṭikānāṃ ca cūrṇāni cūrṇaṃ godhūmakasya ca ||
children.translated_text: powders of <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, and powder of wheat,
with these, small cakes should be made, as well as <s>śaṣkulī</s> cakes and rolls,

children.text: pūpā dhānāś ca vividhā bhakṣyāścānye pṛthagvidhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: cakes, parched grains, and various other kinds of foods separately.
Through the use of these foods, with the penis firm and filled with semen,
a man goes to women like a stallion, for as long as he wishes.
He should boil seeds of <s>ātmaguptā</s>, black gram, dates, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,
water chestnuts and raisins, measured by <s>prasṛta</s>s,
with a <s>prastha</s> of milk and a <s>prastha</s> of water, until one <s>prastha</s> remains.

children.text: śuddhena vāsasā pūtaṃ yojayet prasṛtais tribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Strained through a clean cloth, it should be combined with three <s>prasṛta</s>s each
of sugar, <s>tugākṣīrī</s>, and fresh ghee.

children.text: tat pāyayet sakṣaudraṃ ṣaṣṭikānnaṃ ca bhojayet ||
children.translated_text: He should make him drink that with honey, and should feed him <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice.
Even a man beset by old age and weak, through this preparation, obtains

children.text: naro'patyaṃ suvipulaṃ yuveva ca sa hṛṣyati ||
children.translated_text: very abundant offspring, and rejoices like a young man.
The head of the date-palm, black gram, <s>payasyā</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,
dates, <s>madhūka</s> fruits, raisins, and <s>ajaḍā</s> fruit,
each measured by a <s>pala</s>, the wise man should boil in an <s>āḍhaka</s> of water.
When that has been reduced to one quarter, he should cook it with a <s>prastha</s> of milk.
When only the milk remains, he should eat <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice rich in ghee with it.

children.text: saśarkareṇa saṃyoga eṣa vṛṣyaḥ paraṃ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This combination, with sugar added, is remembered as supremely aphrodisiac.
<s>Jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, the two <s>śrāvaṇī</s>s,
dates, <s>madhuka</s>, grapes, long pepper, and dry ginger,

children.text: śṛṅgāṭakaṃ vidārīṃ ca navaṃ sarpiḥ payo jalam
children.translated_text: water chestnut and <s>vidārī</s>, fresh ghee, milk, and water:
when cooked until only the ghee remains, with one quarter each of sugar and honey,
it should be used with <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice according to one's strength.

children.text: vṛṣyaṃ balyaṃ ca varṇyaṃ ca kaṇṭhyaṃ bṛṃhaṇam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: It is aphrodisiac, strengthening, complexion-promoting, good for the throat, and an excellent bulk-promoter.
The essence of curds, resembling the autumn moon and free from faults,
the wise man should combine, in proper measure, with sugar, honey, peppers, and <s>tugākṣīrī</s>,

children.text: yuktyā yuktaṃ sasūkṣmailaṃ nave kumbhe śucau paṭe
children.translated_text: together with finely powdered cardamom, in a new vessel and with a clean cloth.
Having cleansed it, he should place it, cold, into <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice rich in ghee.
He should drink a measure of <s>rasālā</s> after eating that <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice.
By this a man, endowed with complexion, voice, and strength, becomes virile.
Using <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, like moonbeams, prepared with milk and rich in ghee,
combined with sugar and honey, he becomes virile.
A crocodile egg mixed with a rooster's egg in hot ghee,
combined with <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> flour and fresh ghee,
should be cooked into small cakes; a man should eat them with the scum of <s>vāruṇī</s> liquor,

children.text: ya icchedaśvavad gantuṃ prasektuṃ gajavac ca yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if he wishes to go like a horse and to discharge like an elephant.
By these applications, performed according to rule, a handsome man, endowed with virility and furnished with strength and complexion,

children.text: harṣānvito vājivad aṣṭavarṣo bhavet samarthaśca varāṅganāsu ||
children.translated_text: filled with excitement, becomes like an eight-year-old stallion and capable among excellent women.

children.text: yadyacca kiṃcin manasaḥ priyaṃ syādramyā vanāntāḥ pulināni śailāḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever is dear to the mind, pleasant forest retreats, sandbanks, mountains,

children.text: iṣṭāḥ striyo bhūṣaṇagandhamālyaṃ priyā vayasyāśca tadatra yogyam ||
children.translated_text: desired women, ornaments, perfumes, garlands, and beloved companions, all that is suitable here.
The preparations that have been proclaimed in the <s>Āsiktakṣīrika</s> quarter
are eight; they should be used by those desiring offspring and seeking manly power.

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte cikitsāsthāne vājīkaraṇādhyāye āsiktakṣīriko nāma vājīkaraṇapādo dvitīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s> and redacted by <s>Caraka</s>, in the <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s>, in the chapter on <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>, the second <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> quarter, named <s>Āsiktakṣīrika</s>, is completed.
Now then we shall explain the <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> quarter called <s>Māṣaparṇabhṛtīya</s>.
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.
A wise man should maintain a well-nourished, first-calved cow, fed on <s>māṣaparṇa</s>, with four teats,
whose calf is of the same color and alive,
red or black, with upward-pointing horns, not fierce,

children.text: ikṣvādām arjunādāṃ vā sāndrakṣīrāṃ ca dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: feeding on sugarcane or feeding on <s>arjuna</s>, and having thick milk.

children.text: kevalaṃ tu payastasyāḥ śṛtaṃ vāśṛtameva vā
children.translated_text: Her milk alone, whether boiled or even unboiled,
combined with sugar, honey, and ghee, is an excellent aphrodisiac.
Milk cooked separately with semen-producing, life-promoting,
bulk-promoting, strength-increasing, and milk-producing substances,
combined with wheat flour and with ghee, honey, and sugar,
should be used in alternation by one who desires inexhaustible semen.
<s>Medā</s>, <s>payasyā</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>kaṇṭakārikā</s>,
<s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, <s>kṣīrikā</s>, black gram, wheat, <s>śāli</s> rice, and <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice,
each one <s>karṣa</s>, should be cooked in milk with half as much water, in an <s>āḍhaka</s> measure.
When only the milk remains, he should remove it; strained, it should be combined with honey and ghee.

children.text: yuktaṃ saśarkaraṃ pītvā vṛddhaḥ saptatiko 'pi vā
children.translated_text: After drinking it with sugar added, even an old man, even one seventy years old,

children.text: vipulaṃ labhate'patyaṃ yuveva ca sa hṛṣyati ||
children.translated_text: obtains abundant offspring and rejoices like a young man.
The milk of that same cow, boiled with discs of gold,
prepared with ghee, honey, and sugar, is effective for generating offspring.
Thirty long peppers, well pounded, in a <s>prakuñca</s> of oil and ghee...
fried, mixed with sugar and honey, and drenched with a stream of milk.
Having drunk according to his strength, and afterward having eaten <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk and ghee,

children.text: bhuktvā na rātrim astabdhaṃ liṅgaṃ paśyati nā kṣarat ||
children.translated_text: at night he does not find his organ flaccid, nor does it leak.
In the juice of <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s> and <s>vidārī</s>, with four times as much milk,
a porridge of <s>māṣa</s> and <s>ṣaṣṭika</s>, rich in ghee, is cooked; it is aphrodisiac.
There should be a <s>kuḍava</s> measure of powdered fruits that are life-promoting, unctuous, and appetite-stimulating,
and also of the fruit of <s>svayaṃguptā</s>.

children.text: kuḍavaścaiva māṣāṇāṃ dvau dvau ca tilamudgayoḥ
children.translated_text: There should also be a <s>kuḍava</s> of <s>māṣa</s>, and two each of sesame and <s>mudga</s>,
and of powders of wheat and <s>śāli</s> rice there should be a <s>kuḍava</s> each.
There should also be one <s>kuḍava</s> of ghee. After kneading all that with milk,

children.text: paktvā pūpalikāḥ khāded bahvyaḥ syur yasya yoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should cook small cakes and eat them, if one has many women.
One should cook ghee containing <s>śatāvarī</s> in ten times as much milk.
Mixed with sugar, <s>pippalī</s>, and honey, that is the best aphrodisiac.
He who uses one <s>karṣa</s> of <s>madhuka</s> powder, mixed with equal parts ghee and honey,

children.text: prayuṅkte yaḥ payaścānu nityavegaḥ sa nā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and drinks milk afterward, does not lose his regular impulse.
A man whose food is ghee and milk, fearless, free from disease, always active, and young,
constantly intent on desire, becomes virile among women.
Those who have accomplished their one task, whose aims are fulfilled, and who conform to one another,

children.text: kalāsu kuśalāstulyāḥ sattvena vayasā ca ye ||
children.translated_text: who are equally skilled in the arts and equal in character and age,
who are endowed with family nobility, greatness, courtesy, conduct, and purity,

children.text: ye kāmanityā ye hṛṣṭā ye viśokā gatavyathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: who are always amorous, delighted, free from sorrow, and free from pain,

children.text: ye tulyaśīlā ye bhaktā ye priyā ye priyaṃvadāḥ
children.translated_text: who are of similar character, devoted, dear, and pleasant-spoken:

children.text: tair naraḥ saha visrabdhaḥ suvayasyair vṛṣāyate ||
children.translated_text: with such good companions a man, trusting and at ease, becomes virile.
By oiling, rubbing, bathing, perfumes, garlands, and ornaments,
by the comforts of house, bed, and seat, and by unworn, agreeable garments,
by pleasing bird calls and by the jingling of women's ornaments,
and by massages from excellent, desired women, he becomes virile.
Water places with lotuses, frequented by intoxicated bees,
and cool inner chambers scented with jasmine and blue lotuses,
rivers wearing foam as an upper garment, and mountains with blue slopes,
the rising mass of dark clouds, and nights lovely with moonrise,
winds pleasant to the touch and fragrant with beds of night-lotuses,
nights fit for the enjoyment of love, dear through close embrace and aloe fragrance,

children.text: sukhāḥ sahāyāḥ parapuṣṭaghuṣṭāḥ phullā vanāntā viśadānnapānāḥ
children.translated_text: pleasant companions, places resounding with cuckoo calls, blossoming forest-edges, and clear food and drink,

children.text: gāndharvaśabdāśca sugandhayogāḥ sattvaṃ viśālaṃ nirupadravaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: music, fragrant preparations, and a broad mind free from disturbance:

children.text: siddhārthatā cābhinavaśca kāmaḥ strī cāyudhaṃ sarvamihātmajasya
children.translated_text: success, fresh desire, and a woman are here the whole means for producing a son.

children.text: vayo navaṃ jātamadaśca kālo harṣasya yoniḥ paramā narāṇām ||
children.translated_text: Fresh youth, a season in which passion has arisen, and the right time are the supreme source of joy for men.

children.text: praharṣayonayo yogā vyākhyātā daśa pañca ca
children.translated_text: Ten and five combinations that are sources of exhilaration have been explained,
in this quarter called <s>Māṣaparṇabhṛtīya</s>, which bestow <s>śukra</s> and strength.

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte cikitsāsthāne vājīkaraṇādhyāye māṣaparṇabhṛtīyo nāma vājīkaraṇapādastṛtīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s> and redacted by <s>Caraka</s>, in the <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s>, in the chapter on <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>, the third <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> quarter, named <s>Māṣaparṇabhṛtīya</s>, is completed.
Now then we shall explain the <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> quarter beginning with 'a man whose strength has arisen.'
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: pumān yathā jātabalo yāvadicchaṃ striyo vrajet
children.translated_text: How a man, with strength arisen, may go to women as much as he wishes,

children.text: yathā cāpatyavān sadyo bhavet tad upadekṣyate ||
children.translated_text: and how he may quickly become possessed of offspring: that will be taught.

children.text: na hi jātabalāḥ sarve narāś cāpatyabhāginaḥ
children.translated_text: For not all men whose strength has arisen share in offspring.
There are large-bodied, strong men who are weak with women.
And there are men of small frame who are strong with women and have many children.
Some are weak by nature, and some are weak because of illness.
Some men go to a woman many times like a <s>caṭaka</s> bird,
and some ejaculate like an elephant but do not go many times.
Some have strength through the suitability of time; some are constant through practice.
Some are shown to be virile through efforts, and some are so by nature.
Therefore we shall state applications that give strength to the weak,
make enjoyment pleasant for the strong, and further increase strength.
First, after bodies have been purified by non-unctuous enemas together with unctuous enemas,
one who seeks strength should employ applications that increase <s>śukra</s> and offspring.
Enemas mixed with ghee, oil, meat juice, milk, sugar, and honey
should be prepared for those whose diet is milk and meat broth.
Having ground boar meat and added pepper and rock salt,
one should make pills the size of jujubes and roll them in hot ghee.
When they have been firmed by rolling, they should be put into chicken broth,
rich in ghee, fragrant, and containing curds and pomegranate juice.

children.text: yathā na bhindyād gulikās tathā taṃ sādhayed rasam
children.translated_text: One should cook that broth in such a way that the pills do not break.

children.text: taṃ piban bhakṣayaṃs tāśca labhate śukramakṣayam ||
children.translated_text: Drinking that broth and eating those pills, he obtains inexhaustible <s>śukra</s>.
In this same way the physician should make pills from other nourishing meats;
their use together with their juices increases <s>śukra</s>.
Clean sprouted <s>māṣa</s> beans, dehusked and together with <s>ājaḍā</s> fruits,
should be put into buffalo broth rich in ghee, with curds and pomegranate juice.
In proper measure, with coriander, cumin, and dry ginger,

children.text: bhuktaḥ pītaśca sa rasaḥ kurute śukramakṣayam ||
children.translated_text: that broth, eaten and drunk, makes <s>śukra</s> inexhaustible.
Fresh fish meat, or well-fried <s>śapharī</s> fish,

children.text: tapte sarpiṣi yaḥ khādetsa gacchet strīṣu na kṣayam ||
children.translated_text: if one eats them in hot ghee, he does not become exhausted among women.
<s>Rohita</s> fish, fried in ghee, in goat broth with fruit essence...
One who desires offspring should use them as unctuous preparations, with broths drunk afterward.
A minced preparation of fish and meat, with asafoetida, rock salt, and coriander,
combined with wheat flour, should be cooked in ghee as small <s>pūpalikā</s> cakes.

children.text: māhiṣe ca rase matsyān snigdhāmlalavaṇān pacet
children.translated_text: Fish should be cooked in buffalo-meat broth, made unctuous, sour, and salty;
when the broth has penetrated it, he should pound the meat, and into it he should add

children.text: maricaṃ jīrakaṃ dhānyamalpaṃ hiṅgu navaṃ ghṛtam
children.translated_text: black pepper, cumin, coriander, a little asafoetida, and fresh ghee.
That should be prepared as the filling for <s>māṣa</s> cakes.
These two recipes for <s>pūpalikā</s> cakes are bulk-promoting and strength-increasing;
they give excitement and good fortune, produce sons, and are supremely semen-increasing.
Flour made from <s>māṣa</s>, <s>ātmaguptā</s>, wheat, <s>śāli</s> rice, and <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice,
together with powder of sugar, <s>vidārī</s>, and <s>ikṣuraka</s>,

children.text: saṃyojya masṛṇe kṣīre ghṛte pūpalikāḥ pacet
children.translated_text: should be combined in smooth milk, and <s>pūpalikā</s> cakes should be cooked in ghee.
Taken with milk as the after-drink, they quickly produce supreme virility.
There should be one <s>tulā</s> of sugar and one of cow's ghee,

children.text: prastho vidāryāścūrṇasya pippalyāḥ prastha eva ca ||
children.translated_text: one <s>prastha</s> of <s>vidārī</s> powder, and likewise one <s>prastha</s> of long pepper,
and half an <s>āḍhaka</s> each of <s>tugākṣīrī</s> and fresh honey.
All this, thoroughly blended, should stand in an earthen vessel used for ghee.
Morning after morning, he should use a dose of it suited to his digestive fire.

children.text: eṣa vṛṣyaḥ paraṃ yogo balyo bṛṃhaṇa eva ca ||
children.translated_text: This is an excellent aphrodisiac preparation, strengthening and also bulk-promoting.
Of <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, and likewise of <s>māṣa</s> and <s>ātmaguptā</s>,
and of <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, he should prepare decoctions separately in water.
Having cooked a <s>prastha</s> of ghee with them, again in eight times as much milk,
one who desires offspring should use that preparation mixed with sugar and honey.
He should cook a vesselful of ghee in a hundredfold quantity of <s>vidārī</s> juice;

children.text: siddhaṃ punaḥ śataguṇe gavye payasi sādhayet ||
children.translated_text: when it is prepared, he should again cook it in a hundredfold quantity of cow's milk.
It should be combined with quarter-parts of sugar, <s>tugākṣīrī</s>, honey, <s>ikṣuraka</s>,
long pepper, and <s>sājaḍā</s>.
The physician should make pills as large as a stout <s>udumbara</s> fruit.
From using them, a man becomes excited like a <s>kuliṅga</s> bird.
One hundred <s>palas</s> of sugar candy, half that amount of fresh ghee,
combined with a quarter-part of honey, should be cooked with a quarter-part of water.
When it is thick, a quarter-part of wheat flour should be scattered on a clean, smooth stone slab,
and he should prepare it by kneading.
Pure <s>utkārikā</s> cakes should be made, resembling the disk of the moon.
By using them, a man satisfies women like an elephant.

children.text: yat kiṃcin madhuraṃ snigdhaṃ jīvanaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ guru
children.translated_text: Whatever is sweet, unctuous, life-promoting, bulk-promoting, and heavy,
and whatever gladdens the mind, all of that is called aphrodisiac.
Therefore, prepared with substances of this kind, he should approach a woman,
impelled by his own urge and delighted by feminine charms.

children.text: gatvā snātvā payaḥ pītvā rasaṃ vānu śayīta nā
children.translated_text: After intercourse, having bathed and drunk milk or meat broth, the man should then sleep.

children.text: tathāsyāpyāyate bhūyaḥ śukraṃ ca balameva ca ||
children.translated_text: In that way his semen and strength increase still further.
Just as the fragrance of a flower in bud is not perceived,

children.text: labhyate tadvikāśāttu tathā śukraṃ hi dehinām ||
children.translated_text: but is perceived when it opens, so indeed is the semen of embodied beings.

children.text: narte vai ṣoḍaśād varṣāt saptatyāḥ parato na ca
children.translated_text: Not before the sixteenth year, and not after seventy,
should a man who desires long life undertake union with women.
For a very young boy, whose bodily constituents are not yet fully complete, if he approaches a woman,
would suddenly dry up like a pond with little water.

children.text: śuṣkaṃ rūkṣaṃ yathā kāṣṭhaṃ jantudagdhaṃ vijarjaram
children.translated_text: As dry, rough wood, eaten by insects, burned, and decayed,

children.text: spṛṣṭamāśu viśīryeta tathā vṛddhaḥ striyo vrajan ||
children.translated_text: falls apart as soon as it is touched, so is an old man when he approaches women.
Semen wastes away through old age, worry, diseases, and exhaustion from work,
through fasting, and through excessive indulgence in women.
Through wasting, fear, lack of trust, grief, seeing defects in women,
ignorance of women's pleasures, lack of judgment, and lack of practice,
even for one who is otherwise satisfied, the capacity to approach women does not arise.
Excitement and capacity depend on the body, vitality, and strength; capacity is born from excitement.

children.text: rasa ikṣau yathā dadhni sarpistailaṃ tile yathā
children.translated_text: As juice is in sugarcane, ghee in curds, and oil in sesame,
so semen pervades the whole body and is present at contact.
In the union of woman and man, because of activity, intention, and pressure,
semen slips from its place like water from a wet cloth.
Because of excitement, longing, fluidity, sliminess, and also heaviness,
because it is subtle and prone to flow, and because of the swiftness of wind,

children.text: aṣṭābhya ebhyo hetubhyaḥ śukraṃ dehāt prasicyate
children.translated_text: for these eight reasons semen is discharged from the body.
It is called the formative substance of a moving being of manifold forms.

children.text: bahalaṃ madhuraṃ snigdham avisraṃ guru picchilam
children.translated_text: Semen that is thick, sweet, unctuous, not foul-smelling, heavy, slimy,
and white is fruitful, without doubt.
That by which a man obtains capacity among women like a stallion,
and by which he approaches them with greater vigor, is precisely <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>.
The reason for teaching these preparations, and the twelve excellent preparations,

children.text: yat pūrvaṃ maithunāt sevyaṃ sevyaṃ yanmaithunād anu ||
children.translated_text: what should be used before intercourse and what should be used after intercourse,

children.text: yadā na sevyāḥ pramadāḥ kṛtsnaḥ śukraviniścayaḥ
children.translated_text: when women are not to be approached, and the entire ascertainment of semen,
together with definition and explanation, have been set forth here in the section beginning with 'a man of newly acquired strength.'

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte cikitsāsthāne vājīkaraṇādhyāye pumāñjātabalādiko nāma vājīkaraṇapādaścaturthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s> and redacted by <s>Caraka</s>, in the <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s>, in the chapter on <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>, the fourth <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> quarter, called <s>Pumāñjātabalādika</s>, is completed.
And this second chapter on <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> is completed.
